units.tr: ...to be built by the Branch [צמח] (Germine) is distinguished from the Temple of Zerubbabel, Zech. 6.13. But that is not the third Temple built for Israel's own benefit, which is promised there and also by Ezekiel. That Temple is not in Zion and the tribe of Judah, Ezek. 45.1, 4, 5, 6, 7; 48.8, 9, 10. Nor, for the same reason, is that third Temple the one to which the Messiah had to come, since he had to come to Zion, Ps. 2.6; 78.68; 132.13, 17. Finally, the purpose of God in giving this oracle must above all be considered. That purpose was to console Daniel and, with him, all the faithful, and to nourish their expectation and rouse their patient endurance [ὑπομονή]. With that purpose it did not fit to command the godly to count and calculate the years, since, apart from a few days of distress, the outcome would be not a great and inestimable good but an unspeakable evil and ruin: the scattering of the people, lasting so long that no fixed end could be found. Did God then wish the years of a little prosperity to be counted, but not the years of so great a calamity coming in exile? What more need be said? The obstinacy and unbelief of the Jews are written in the clear light of day, since they have forbidden, under a curse, anyone to think that times are fixed in such prophecies. For in the tractate Sanhedrin, ch. 11, this is read: "Let the spirit of those who compute the ends be broken" [תפח רוחן של מחשבי קצין] (Rumpatur spiritus eorum, qui computant terminos). And R. Lipman, in the Nizzachon, n. 334: "Let their spirit perish in Gehenna, those who compute the ends" [תפח נשמתם בגהנם של מחשבי הקיצים] (Pereat spiritus eorum in gehenna, qui terminos computant). Moreover, the masters say that the Chaldee interpreter was divinely forbidden to compose a paraphrase of the prophet Daniel, tractate Megillah, ch. 1: "because in it is contained the end of the Messiah" [דאית ביה קיף המשיח] (quia in eo finis Messiæ continetur).

units.la: CXXI. Inane verò & illud κρησφύγετον est, quòd prædictiones de Messiæ adventu non absolutas, sed conditionatas, adeóque non impletas, nisi impleta conditione, pœnitentia vi-delicet, seu conversione ad Deum à peccatis, fingunt; & vel revelationem Messiæ jam exhibiti, sed latentis: vel exhibitionem ejusdem destinato tempore prædicti peccatis populi impediri nugantur. Quomodo Magistri Traditioni domus Elianæ; quòd mundus bis mille annos sub Lege duraturus sit, in Avodah Sarah asseruunt, propter peccata populi longum tempus super bis mille annos exactum iri. Cæterùm non à conditione ulla oracula hactenus allata, quibus & præcedentia & comitantia adventum Messiæ, & articulum temporis, quo is adventare debuit, prænuntiata diximus, pendent. Prædictiones quippe, non promissiones duntaxat iis continentur. Eas inter hæc differentia intercedit, quòd illæ conditionem respuunt, hæ solæ admittere possunt. Periit prædictionum, imò & promissionum vis omnis, cùm à conditione incerta, & pro arbitrio voluntatis mutabili suspenduntur. Nulla uspiam Messiæ prædictio vel promissio conditionata extat, vel à Judæis producta hactenus est. Sicut porro Messiæ promissio merè gratuita fuit, ita ejusdem exhibitio gratuita etiam sufflaminari à peccatis eorum, quibus is promissus est, nullatenus potuit. Ego Jehova vocavi te in justitia (ut veniens adducas justitiam) & apprehendam manum tuam, & custodiam te, ac dabo te in fœdus populi, & in lucem gentium, Esaj.XLII.6. Ecce ego seco fœdus: coram toto toto populo tuo faciam mirabilia ; quae non sunt creata in tota terra, & omnibus gentibus. Et videbit totus populus, in cujus medio es, opus Jehovae, Exod.XXXIV.10. Molitionem molietur in diebus vestris, non credetis, cum narrabitur, Habac.I. 5. Tantum vero abest, ut peccata hominum Messiae adventum remoratura fuerint, ut potius eum provocaverint Nam adventare debuit defectionem coercitypus, peccatum consummaturus, & pravitatem expiaturus, Dan.IX.24. Peccata bajulaturus & sublaturus, Esaj.LIII.3.4. Eo die erit fons apertus domui Davidis, & habitanti Hierosolymam pro peccato & omni menstruo, Zach.XIII.1. Unde ipsi Hebraei Messiam איש כפר Virum placatorem appellant. Sicut peccata populi non impedierunt, quo minus Deus ex Aegypto & Babylone forti manu eum liberaret: ita nec ejusdem populi peccata obstare redemptioni ejus spirituali potuerunt. Futurum enim alias erat, ut nunquam Messias mitteretur, quia peccatorum moles nunquam non eundem populum caecitate percussum, & cordis duritie infamem semper, premit, premetque quandiu Salvatorem verum non agnoverint. Ita hominum infidelitas Dei fidem irritam reddet. quod velut ingens ἄτοπον merito gentium Doctor, Rom.III.3.4. respuit. Facit huc disceptatio, quae ex Thalmude Cod.Sanhedr.cap.Holec citari solet, duos inter Rabbinos celebres, R.Eliezerem & R. Josue, quorum ille adventum Messiae ob peccata populi disseri asseruit, hic negavit. Scriptum est, inquiebat R.Eliezer: Convertimini filii rebelles, & sanabo vos a vestris rebellionibus. Sed inquit R. Josue: Dictum quoque est: Venditi estis ob rem nihili, (idololatriam) & fine argento (bonis operibus vestris) redimemini. At vero inquit R. Eliezer, dictum est: Convertimini ad me, & ego me convertam ad vos. Sed enim, ait R.Josue, habemus & illud. Accepi vos in uxorem, veluti mulierem, & capiam vos, unam ex una urbe, & duas ex una tribu &c. & introducam vos in Sion. Instat R. Eliezer: Dictum est: In quiete & tranquillitate salvabimini. Et apud Esajam quoque, inquit R. Josue, scriptum est: sic dicit Sanctus Redemptor Israelis, ad animam contemptibilem, & ad gentem abominabilem, &c. Tandem inquit R. Eliezer: Quid ergo sibi vult Jeremias: Si convertaris Israel, &c. cum modus illeloquendi fit conditionalis? Imo regerit R. Josue: Quid sibi Daniel (cap.x 11.7.) Audivi virum illum indutum lineis vestibus, qui erat supra aquas fluminis, & elevavit dextram suam & sinistram suam ad Coelum, & juravit per viventem in secula, quod ad tempus, tempora & dimidium temporis. Cumque compleverit, &c. Ad hunc locum R.Eliezer obmutuit. Qui magnorum Rabbinorum punctim se ferientium conflictus veritatem adversus domus Elianae glossam luculenter confirmat. Denique edisserant illi, ecquodnam ingens illud, populo Judaico proprium peccatum sit, quod Messiae adventum retardavit hactenus? Primum Templum propter idololatriam, luxum, homicidia, eversum ajunt. At non defuerunt Prophetae in exilio Babylonico, qui populum consolationum fomentis mulcerent. Cur tam longo seculorum decursu, quo omni idololatria abstinent, & Legi impense vacant, & a luxu homicidiisque temperant magis, nemo stupentes solatur, erigit? Cumque etiam itante secun-
units.tr: CXXI. Equally empty is that refuge [κρησφύγετον] by which they pretend that the predictions about the Messiah's coming are not absolute but conditional, and therefore not fulfilled unless the condition, namely repentance, that is, conversion to God from sins, has been met. They also trifle that either the Messiah, already given, is hidden and not revealed, or that his manifestation at the time foretold is prevented by the sins of the people. So the Masters of the tradition of the house of Elijah assert, in Avodah Sarah, that the world will endure for two thousand years under the Law, because of the sins of the people a long time beyond two thousand years will pass. Yet the oracles so far cited, which we have said foretold both the events preceding and accompanying the Messiah's coming and the moment of time when he was to come, depend on no condition. For these contain not merely promises but predictions. There is this difference between them: predictions reject any condition, while promises alone can admit one. All the force of predictions, and indeed of promises too, is lost when they are suspended on an uncertain condition, changeable at the will of the one who wills. Nowhere is there any conditional prediction or promise of the Messiah, and the Jews have to this day produced none. Just as the promise of the Messiah was purely gratuitous, so its fulfilment could in no way be hindered by the sins of those to whom he was promised. I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness (so that, coming, you might bring righteousness), and will hold your hand, and keep you, and give you for a covenant of the people, and for a light of the Gentiles, Isa. 42.6. Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will do marvels, which have not been created in all the earth, nor among all nations. And all the people among whom you are shall see the work of the LORD, Exod. 34.10. He will work a work in your days which you will not believe when it is told, Hab. 1.5. So far are the sins of men from having delayed the Messiah's coming that they rather provoked it. For he was to come to finish the transgression, to make an end of sin, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, Dan. 9.24. He was to bear and carry away sins, Isa. 53.3, 4. On that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness, Zech. 13.1. Hence the Hebrews themselves call the Messiah [איש כפר] a man of atonement. As the sins of the people did not prevent God from freeing them from Egypt and Babylon with a mighty hand, so neither could the sins of the same people stand in the way of his spiritual redemption. For otherwise the Messiah would never have been sent, since the mass of sins, which has always struck that people with blindness and kept them infamous for hardness of heart, never ceases to weigh them down, and will continue to do so as long as they do not acknowledge the true Saviour. Thus the unbelief of men will not make the faithfulness of God void, which the teacher of the Gentiles, Rom. 3.3, 4, rightly rejects as a huge absurdity [ἄτοπον]. To this point belongs the dispute, which is usually cited from the Talmud, Cod. Sanhedr., chap. Holec, between two famous rabbis, R. Eliezer and R. Joshua, of whom the former asserted that the coming of the Messiah was deferred because of the sins of the people, while the latter denied it. It is written, said R. Eliezer, "Turn back, rebellious children, and I will heal you of your rebellions." But R. Joshua said: "It is also said, 'You were sold for nothing' (that is, for idolatry), 'and you will be redeemed without silver' (that is, by your good works)." But R. Eliezer replied, "It is said, 'Turn to me, and I will turn to you.'" But, said R. Joshua, we also have this: "I took you as a wife, as a woman, and I will take you, one from a city and two from a tribe, etc., and I will bring you into Zion." R. Eliezer pressed on: "It is said, 'In quietness and in confidence you shall be saved.'" And in Isaiah too, said R. Joshua, it is written: "Thus says the Holy One, the Redeemer of Israel, to the despised soul, and to the abhorred nation," etc. At last R. Eliezer said: "What then does Jeremiah mean: 'If you return, Israel,' etc.?" since the form of speech is conditional. But R. Joshua answered: "What then does Daniel mean? I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, and he lifted his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives for ever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time. And when he has finished," etc. At this point R. Eliezer fell silent. This conflict of great rabbis, striking one another with points, clearly confirms the truth against the gloss of the house of Elijah. Finally let them explain what great sin peculiar to the Jewish people has so far delayed the coming of the Messiah. They say that the First Temple was overthrown on account of idolatry, luxury and murders. But there were not lacking prophets in the Babylonian exile who soothed the people with the balm of consolations. Why, through so long a course of ages, during which they have abstained from all idolatry, devoted themselves diligently to the Law, and refrained more from luxury and murders, does no one console or raise up the astonished people?

units.la: do Templo adeo ab idololatria abhorruerint, ut novissima quaeque pati, quam sinere, ut Imperatoris statua, vel aquila Romana in Templum induceretur, maluerint, quid causae esse potuit, ut Messias pridem, uti ajunt, natus, sese in conspectum non dederit, imo tot tantisque miseriis ex eo tempore cumulatos & poene obrutos neglexerit? Nequicquam illi vitulum in deserto ante aliquot annorum chiliadas adoratum causantur, cum utique populus in flagranti delicto poenas luerit, & multoties exinde oppressus liberatusque fuerit. Alii sceleris sibi ignoti poenas se luere ajunt. Quod si vero crimen non norunt, nec utique agnoscere possunt: & si nec agnoscere, frustra etiam poenitentiam instituunt; sicuti ex facto solennes poenitentias subinde indixerunt. Quandoquidem vero poena adeo universalis, longe extrema est, crimen etiam ejusmodi sit oportet. Et quia, uti illi asseruunt, idololatria & injustitia per primi Templi excidium expiatae fuerint, gravior causa aliqua secundi Templi excidium, longumque adeo & tot concatenatis malis & calamitatibus exercitum, nulla meliorum spe affulgente, accelerare debuit, quae infidelitas illa est, qua Jesum verum Messiam, Rupem salutis suae ינבלי pro stulta & scelerata tractarunt, & hanc Dei, sed versus se, sententiam provocarunt: Abscondam faciem meam ab iis. Videbo quid in novissimo eorum futurum sit. Generatio enim perversa sunt, בנים לא אמן בם filii, in quibus nulla fides est, Deut.XXXII.1 s.20.
units.tr: do Temple, since they recoiled so much from idolatry under the Second Temple that they preferred to suffer the worst rather than allow an image of the Emperor, or the Roman eagle, to be brought into the Temple, what cause could there have been why the Messiah, long since born, as they say, did not show himself, but indeed neglected a people so heaped with and almost overwhelmed by such great miseries from that time? It is in vain that they blame the calf worshipped in the wilderness many thousands of years ago, since surely the people have paid the penalty for that offence in the very act, and have many times since been oppressed and delivered. Others say they are paying penalties for a crime unknown to them. But if they do not know the crime, they certainly cannot acknowledge it; and if they cannot acknowledge it, they institute repentance in vain, just as they have from time to time appointed solemn repentances for particular events. Since, however, the punishment is so universal and so far extended, the crime too must be of the same kind. And because, as they assert, idolatry and injustice were expiated by the destruction of the First Temple, some graver cause ought to have hastened the destruction of the Second Temple, and the long exile vexed with so many linked evils and calamities, with no hope of better things shining forth. That cause is the unbelief by which they treated Jesus, the true Messiah, the Rock of their salvation [ינבלי] as foolish and wicked, and so provoked that sentence of God, directed against themselves: I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be. For they are a perverse generation, children in whom is no faith, Deut. 32.1, 20 [בנים לא אמן בם].

units.la: CXXII. Habent vero Recutiti etiam folia ficulnea, quibus infidelitatem suam palliant; & in errore abnegati adventus Messiae se ipsi obfirmant: Praecipua R.Isaac filius Abrahami in stygio illo ספר חזק אמונה Libro, Munimen fidei dicto, & a Celeb. Wagenseilio ex MS. Africano aliquot abhinc annis, una cum Versione Latina edito, complexus est; sed glacie quavis frigidiora. Nam quod Messiae adventus promittitur באחרית הימים in novissimo illorum dierum, Esaj.II.2. non in fine demum mundi, sed in novissimo illorum dierum, qui tum fluebant, puta in fine dierum V.T. quem ἐσχατον ἡμερων etiam S.Paulus Prophetico stylo utens, Hebr.I. 1. appellat, eum venturum arguit. Aliquando enim אחרית הימים novissimum dierum finem מועד illius, quae visioni & politiae carnali populi Israelitici constituta est, & tempus eum sequens notat. Aliquando Hos.III.5. ubi filii Israel ad Jehovam Deum suum, & Davidem Regem suum convertendi באחרית הימים in novissimo dierum dicuntur, finis N.T. & mundi ipsius significatur. Nam ibi in praecedentibus de modo indurationis Judaeorum sub Regno Christi dictum est. Sicut nempe duplex in mundo seculum memoratur, עולם הזה αἰὼν ὁ νῦν seu ἐνεστηκὼς seculum praesens, quo Prophetae prophetabant, & העולם הבא αἰὼν μέλλων seculum futurum, quo alia rerum facies & complementum Prophetiarum futurum erat: ita duplex etiam seculi, unus prioris, alter posterioris finis est. In novissimo illo dierum prioris seculi mons domus Jehovae explanandus in capite montium & extollendus praecollibus, Esaj.II.2. dicitur. quod nondum impletum nequicquam illi caussantur. Non enim exaltatio montis domus Jehovae, Moriah naturanaturalis & localis: (nam Messiam naturam mutaturum, Hebraeorum doctissimi, nominatim Majmonides in Hilkot Melachim cap. ult. negant;) sed spiritualis in eo consistens, quòd majori gloria illustrabitur, quàm ullus unquam mons, ne ipso quidem monte Sinai excepto; notatur. De qua gloria etiam Scriptura Psal.CII.17.Esaj.XL.5.Hagg.II.9. loquitur. Impleta ea exaltatio est, quando tum Filius Dei ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν habitavit inter nos, & suam Majestatem in carne conspiciendam dedit, ut gloriam Unigeniti à Patre, plenus gratia & veritate, Joh.I.14. cum post effusionem Spiritus S. in Apostolos, Evangelium ex Sione exivit, & in mundo praedicari, confluentibus ad montem illum undequaque gentibus, coeptum est. Et monti quidem Templi, non aliis locis, quos aequè Christus calcavit, gloria haec adscribitur; quia Christus, postquam eo in loco confessionem edidisset, ibi effuso Spiritu S. gloriam suam primò publicè manifestavit, Act.II.33.36. Neque spiritualem ejusmodi significatum rejicere ipsi Judaei ausint, utpote qui passim regulam hanc decantant, quòd ea, quae de Messiae Regno Prophetae praedicunt אלהי ולא גשמו spiritualiter, non corporaliter intelligenda sint. Quòd porro eadem Prophetia subjicit: Et fluent ad illum omnes gentes. Et ibunt populi multi, & dicent: Agite, ascendamus in montem Jehovae, domum Jacobi, ut doceat nos de viis suis, & ambulemus in itineribus ejus, Esaj.II.2.3. non arguit, simul semelque omnes populos ad Messiam confluxuros, & unam in mundo fidem extituram, simul atque ille venerit. quod nondum impletum iidem objectant. Non enim Scriptura dicit, statim omnia Christo subjecta fore, & omnes sine exceptione homines Messiae obedituros; sed dicit: eum regnaturum inter hostes, Psal.CX.1.2. quos etiam sceptro ferreo confracturus, ibid.II.9. praedicitur. Et Esaj.LVI.8. Ait Dominus Jehova colligens depulsos Israelis: Adhuc colligam ad ipsum ultra collectos ejus. Non ergo simul semelque etiam semen Israelis collecturus erat. Cùm ergo Prophetia habet כל הגוים omnes gentes ad montem domus Jehovae confluxuras, sensus est, nullam fore διαστολὴν distinctionem gentium, Rom.III.22. X.11.12. XI.31.32. & in consummatione ac πληρώματι gentes exceptum non iri, juxta Psal.LXXXVI.9. Dan.VII.27. denique affluxum gentium continuatum iri, ut aliae post alias gentes veniant, & nunquam desinant accedere gentes, donec plenitudo gentium intraverit, Rom.XI.25. Ex quo tamen concludere non licet, gente affluente, singulos in gente ea homines affluxuros, quia in hac locutione est Synecdoche, qua superstites & vocati gentium juxta Joel.II.32. Amos.IX.12. seu τὰ ἔθνη τῶν σωζομένων gentes eorum qui salvantur, Apoc.XXI.24. intelliguntur. Ideo particula כל omnes, v.2. adhibita, mox, v.3. in רבים multas mutatur; ut significetur initium affluxus omnium gentium ad montem sanctum, dum scil. in magnis & multis Regnis & Rebuspublicis plurimi excitabuntur ad accedendum & alios cohortandum. Omnes populi ambulabunt quisque in nomine Dei sui. Nos autem ambulabimus in nomine Jehovae Dei nostri in seculum & ultra, Mich.IV.5. Quomodo verò quovis Regni Messiae tempore unam fore fidem illi sustinebunt, cùm Prophetia praedixerit, architectos Lapidem angularem rejecturos, Psal.CXVIII.22. Messiam futurum lapidem offendiculi, & petram scandali duabus domibus Israelis, laqueum civibus Hierosolymae, Esaj. VIII.14? Neque magis Judaeorum causam juvant vaticinia, quibus alta pax sub Regno Messiae statuitur. Cudent populi gladios suos in ligones, & hastas suas in falces. Non feret gens in gentem gladium, & non discent amplius bellum, Esaj.II.4. Egredientur habitatores urbium Israel, & succendent atque comburent arma, & scuta & clypeos, arcus & sagittas, &c. Ezech.XXXIX.9. Succidam quadrigas de Ephraim, & equos de Jerusalem, excidentúrque arcus bellici, & loquetur pacem gentibus, &c. Zach.IX.10. Sive enim vaticinia ejusmodi praesagiunt pacem Civilem universalem; talis imperante & Templum Jani claudente Augusto; sub quo Jesus natus est; in mundo toto altissima floruit: sive Ecclesiasticam finem imponentem idololatrarum, persecutorum furoribus, talis à Constantino Jesu Christo nomen dante mundo vindicata, & non semel aliâs data est, dabitúrque porro usque dum nemo amplius bellum discat, de qua pace Ecclesiae etiam, Mich.V.4.5. sermo est: sive Spiritualem vel gentium seu populorum, gentium inimicitia; & distinctio Judaei & Graeci sub Jesu cessavit: vel conscientiae pacatae, & Deo suo in solidum reconciliatae, eadem in Jesu eodem piis & credentibus obtigit. Paradigma שלמנו Pacis nostrae super ipso erat.Esaj. LIII.5. Si quaevis pax sub quovis Messiae tempore florebit, quid ergo de bello adversus Gogum & Magogum, quod à Messiis suis cernendum illi scisc unt, & in quo priorem Messiam occubiturum somniant, fiet? Praeterea etiam religionis Christianae à bellis temerè movendis & inferendis abhorrentis genium vaticinia ejusmodi describunt, cui Pseudochristianorum bellis inhiantium impietas non praejudicat. Jam & cohabitatio lupi cum agno, pardi cum haedo, vituli & agni cum leone rapace, vaccae cum ursa pascuum habentis, leonis cum bove foenum comedentis, lactentis, apud foramen aspidis ludentis, &c. ibid.XI.6.7.8. praedicta non ad literam, sed emblematicè de pace Ecclesiastica populorum & hominum sub Regno Messiae, quorum alii cum mansuetis animalibus comparati fideles, regenitos, sanctificatos; alii feris & venenatis bestiis assimilati homines Spiritu Dei destitutos, hostes Christi, sed ipsi tamen & Ecclesiae mentientes, Deut.XXXIII.29. Psal.XVIII.45. LXVI.3. LXXXI.16. hoc est, ad Ecclesiam Christi, sed sine Spiritu Christi, accedentes, vel animum etiam mutantes, significant, explicanda sunt. Si autem καὶ ἐντὸν intelligi haec deberent, Messias venire debuisset naturam ipsam immutatum. quod ipsi Rabbini inficiantur; Majmonides enim Hilk. Mel. cap. ult. praefatus, quòd mundus במנהגו in natura sua semper mansurus sit, subjicit statim, verba illa Esaiae dicta esse משל וחידה parabolicè & aenigmaticè. & omnia ejusmodi dicta de diebus Messiae משלים metaphorica esse. Idem Majmonides Moreb Nevoch. part. II I. vaticinium illud impleri tum, cùm cognoscitur veritas, perit odium, invidia & contentio, quibus se invicem homines proscindunt, docet. Quòd verò etiam sub eodem Regno Messiae Lux Lunae ut lux Solis, & lux Lunae septupla, tanquam lux septem dierum futura, Esaj.XXX.26. dicitur, citur, figurate cognitionem Dei & mysterio- rum ac Prophetiarum ejus sub Mefsia,nec quo- vis, sed postremo Regni ejus tempore, quod venturum Ecclesia expectat, significat. Com- pungetur Luna,& pudefiet Sol, cum Regnum capef- siverit Dominus in monte Sion & Hierosolyma, & coram senioribus ipsius erit gloria, Esaj.XXIV.23. Eveniet quandoque ut inimicae potestates,quae fe Lucem & Solem mentiuntur, vero Soli justi- tiae cedant, & tantum sonet verbum Dei, atque secundum illud solum Ecclesia fratres a non fratribus discernat. De Templi tertii quasi ma- nu humana sub Mefsia struendi praejudicio non semel diximus. Revera enim Vir [Hebrew] Germen aedificabit Templum Domini, Zach. VI.12. non ta- men manufactum illud, utpote in quo Deus non habitat, Esaj.LXVI.1. sed verum illud, in quo Deus habitet in seculum, adeoque spiritua- le. Nam Mefsias venire debuit ad unctionem San- ctii Sanctorum, sive veri adyti, stante Templo, quod destruendum erit, Dan.IX.25.26. Et in Templo eo Mefsias Sacerdos erit, Zach.VI.13. At in Templo materiali Mefsias Sacerdos esse, vel victimas terrestres & brutas, offerre non potest, quia eas abolendas esse Prophetae, Esaj. LXVI.3.Psal.XL.7. Dan.IX.26. praenuntiarunt. Aedificatio vero Templi spiritualis est sanctifi- catio animarum & corporum nostrorum ad inhabitationem Dei, per victimam sanguinis, & effusionem Spiritus S. inde ab initio Ecclesiae ad finem usque ejus; sed peculiari tamen ratio- ne & Greek sub Novo Testamento. In qua aedificatione ipse Christus Lapis est, Zach.III.9. & aedificationis ejusdem consilium est perpendi- culum in manu Zorobabelis. utpote pignus missio- nis Christi, & illuminationis gentium,ibid.cap. IV.10. Inter Rabbinos ipse Alschech in Hagg.II. 10. Templum isthoc [Hebrew] spirituale, & muros ac parietes ejus [Hebrew] spirituales, pios Dei cul- tores, interpretatur. De praelio eo, quod Messi- am adversus Gogum & Magogum gesturum Judaei fabulantur, & propter quod nondum gestum Mefsiae adventum abnegant, supra dixi- mus. Denique nec reductio populi in terram Canaan, quam per Mefsiam successuram iidem arguunt,adventum ejusdem dubium reddit. Si- ve enim reductio populi in terram Canaan pas- sim promissa tum impleta est, cum Babylone reversi sunt, nihil id ad tempora Mefsiae facit: sive implenda demum eo tempore est, quo ante finem mundi Judaei ad Christum converteн- tur,ne sic quidem Mefsiae adventus infringi po- test, quia quod in ultimis Regni ejus tempori- bus eveniet, praecedentem ejus adventum non tollit. Non enim vel paucorum dierum & an- norum,vel paucorum facinorum Regnum Mef- siae erit.
units.tr: CXXII. The Jews also have fig leaves with which to cover their unbelief, and by refusing the coming of the Messiah they harden themselves in their error. The chief of these is R. Isaac son of Abraham, whose book called Munimen fidei (Bulwark of Faith), in that Hebrew text ספר חזק אמונה, was published a few years ago by the distinguished Wagenseil from an African manuscript, together with a Latin version. But it is colder than any ice. For the prophecy that the Messiah's coming is promised באחרית הימים in the latter days, Isa. 2.2, does not refer to the end of the world, but to the latter part of those days that were then passing, that is, to the end of the days of the Old Testament, which the Apostle Paul also, using prophetic style, calls ἐσχατον ἡμερων the last of the days (Heb. 1.1), and thereby proves that he is to come. For sometimes אחרית הימים the latter of the days denotes the end of that dispensation and political order of the Israelite people, which was established for the sight of the flesh, and the time that follows it. Sometimes, as in Hos. 3.5, where the children of Israel are to return to Jehovah their God and to David their King באחרית הימים in the latter days, the end of the New Testament and of the world itself is signified. For there, in the preceding verses, the manner of the hardening of the Jews under the reign of Christ has been described. Just as there are two worlds mentioned, עולם הזה αἰὼν ὁ νῦν, the present age, in which the prophets prophesied, and העולם הבא αἰὼν μέλλων, the age to come, in which another state of things and the fulfilment of the prophecies were to take place; so also there are two ends of the age, one of the former and one of the latter. It is said: In the latter part of the days of the former age the mountain of the house of Jehovah shall be made firm on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills, Isa. 2.2. The Jews vainly argue that this has not yet been fulfilled. For the exaltation of the mountain of the house of Jehovah, Moriah, is not natural and local (for the most learned of the Hebrews, Maimonides by name, in Hilkot Melachim, last chapter, deny that the Messiah will change nature), but spiritual, consisting in this, that it would be made illustrious with a greater glory than any mountain ever was, not excepting Mount Sinai itself. Scripture also speaks of this glory, Ps. 102.17; Isa. 40.5; Hag. 2.9. That exaltation was fulfilled when the Son of God ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, dwelt among us, and gave his majesty to be seen in the flesh, full of grace and truth, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, John 1.14, when, after the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Apostles, the Gospel went forth from Zion and began to be preached in the world, with the nations flowing to that mountain from every side. And this glory is ascribed to the mountain of the Temple, and not to other places, which Christ equally trod, because Christ, after he had made his confession in that place, there first publicly manifested his glory when the Holy Spirit was poured out (Acts 2.33, 36). Nor dare the Jews themselves reject this spiritual meaning, since they everywhere chant this rule, that what the prophets foretell about the kingdom of the Messiah is to be understood אלהי ולא גשמו, spiritually, not corporeally. Further, that the same prophecy adds: And all the nations shall flow to it. And many peoples shall go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, to the house of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways, and we may walk in his paths, Isa. 2.2, 3, does not imply that all peoples will flock to the Messiah at once and together, and that one faith will arise in the world as soon as he comes. This too the Jews object as unfulfilled. For Scripture does not say that all things will be subjected to Christ at once, and that all men without exception will obey the Messiah; it says that he will reign in the midst of his enemies, Ps. 110.1, 2, and it is foretold that he will break them with a rod of iron, ibid. 2.9. And Isa. 56.8: The Lord Jehovah, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, says: I will gather others to him, besides those already gathered. So he was not going to gather the seed of Israel all at once and together. Therefore, when the prophecy has כל הגוים all the nations flowing to the mountain of the house of Jehovah, the sense is that there will be no distinction (διαστολὴν) of nations (Rom. 3.22; 10.11, 12; 11.31, 32), that the nations will not be excluded at the consummation and fullness (πληρώματι), according to Ps. 86.9 and Dan. 7.27, and finally that the flow of the nations will be continuous, so that one nation after another comes, and the nations never cease to come, until the fullness of the nations has come in, Rom. 11.25. Yet it does not follow from this that, while a nation flows in, each individual man of that nation will flow in as well, because this is a synecdoche, by which the survivors and the called of the nations, according to Joel 2.32 and Amos 9.12, or the nations of those who are saved (Rev. 21.24), are understood. Therefore the particle כל all, used in v. 2, is soon changed in v. 3 to רבים many; so that the beginning of the flow of all nations to the holy mountain is signified, namely while in the great and many kingdoms and commonwealths very many are stirred up to come and to urge others on. All the peoples will walk each in the name of his god. But we will walk in the name of Jehovah our God forever and ever, Mic. 4.5. But how can they hold that there will be one faith throughout every time of the Messiah's kingdom, when the prophecy has foretold that the builders will reject the cornerstone, Ps. 118.22, and that the Messiah will be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to the two houses of Israel, and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Isa. 8.14? Nor do the prophecies that establish deep peace under the Messiah's kingdom help the Jewish cause any more. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, and they shall learn war no more, Isa. 2.4. The inhabitants of the cities of Israel shall go out and kindle and burn the weapons, both shields and bucklers, bows and arrows, etc., Ezek. 39.9. I will cut off the chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be broken, and he shall speak peace to the nations, etc., Zech. 9.10. For whether such prophecies foretell a universal civil peace, such as flourished in the highest degree throughout the world under Augustus, who closed the temple of Janus, and under whom Jesus was born; or an ecclesiastical peace, putting an end to the fury of the persecutors and idolaters, such as was granted to the Church by Constantine, when the world took the name of Jesus Christ, and such as has been given more than once since, and will be given further until no one any more learns war, of which peace of the Church also Mic. 5.4, 5 speaks; or a spiritual peace, in which the enmity between the nations ceased, and the distinction between Jew and Greek ceased under Jesus; or the peace of a quieted conscience, fully reconciled to its God, which in Jesus has fallen to the lot of the pious and believing: The chastisement of our peace was upon him (Isa. 53.5). If some peace will flourish under every time of the Messiah, what then will become of the war against Gog and Magog, which the Jews imagine their Messiahs will see and in which they dream that the former Messiah will perish? Moreover, prophecies of this kind also describe the character of the Christian religion, which shrinks from waging and inflicting wars rashly; the impiety of pseudo-Christians who lust after war does not prejudice this. Again, the cohabitation of the wolf with the lamb, the leopard with the kid, the calf and the lion with the young ox, the cow with the bear that has pasture, the lion with the ox eating straw, the suckling playing by the hole of the asp, etc., ibid. 11.6, 7, 8, are foretold not literally but emblematically, of the ecclesiastical peace of peoples and men under the Messiah's reign. Of these, some, compared to tame animals, are believers, regenerated and sanctified; others, likened to wild and venomous beasts, are men destitute of the Spirit of God, enemies of Christ, yet still lying to the Church (Deut. 33.29; Ps. 18.45; 66.3; 81.16); that is, they approach the Church of Christ but without the Spirit of Christ, or even change their minds, and these things must be explained accordingly. But if these things were to be understood καὶ ἐντὸν, literally, the Messiah would have had to come with nature itself changed. This the Rabbis themselves deny; for Maimonides, in the aforementioned Hilk. Mel. last chapter, after saying that the world will always remain in its own course (במנהגו, in its nature), immediately adds that those words of Isaiah are spoken as a parable and riddle (משל וחידה, parabolically and enigmatically), and that all such sayings about the days of the Messiah are metaphorical (משלים). The same Maimonides, in Moreh Nevukhim part II, teaches that the prophecy is fulfilled when the truth is known and hatred, envy and strife, by which men tear one another apart, perish. As for what is said of the same kingdom of the Messiah, that the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the moon sevenfold, like the light of seven days, Isa. 30.26, it figuratively signifies the knowledge of God and of his mysteries and prophecies under the Messiah, and not under any Messiah but in the last time of his kingdom, which the Church expects to come. The moon shall be confounded and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and his glory shall be before his elders, Isa. 24.23. It will happen at some time that the hostile powers, which falsely pass themselves off as light and sun, will give way to the true Sun of righteousness, and the word of God alone will sound, and by that alone the Church will distinguish brothers from non-brothers. We have more than once spoken of the prejudice that the third Temple is to be built by human hands under the Messiah. In truth, the man whose name is the Branch shall build the temple of the Lord, Zech. 6.12, yet not that made by hands, since God does not dwell in it (Isa. 66.1), but the true temple in which God will dwell forever, and which is therefore spiritual. For the Messiah was to come for the anointing of the Holy of Holies, that is, of the true sanctuary, while the Temple still stood, which was to be destroyed (Dan. 9.25, 26). And in that Temple the Messiah will be Priest (Zech. 6.13). But in a material Temple the Messiah cannot be priest or offer earthly and brute victims, since the prophets foretold that these were to be abolished (Isa. 66.3; Ps. 40.7; Dan. 9.26). The building of the spiritual temple, however, is the sanctification of our souls and bodies for the indwelling of God, through the sacrifice of blood and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, from the beginning of the Church to its end; but in a peculiar manner and Greek under the New Testament. In this building Christ himself is the Stone (Zech. 3.9), and the plumb line of this building is the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel, as a pledge of the mission of Christ and of the enlightenment of the nations (ibid., ch. 4.10). Among the Rabbis, Alshech on Haggai 2.10 interprets this temple as spiritual, and its walls and partitions as spiritual, pious worshippers of God. Concerning the battle that the Jews fable the Messiah will wage against Gog and Magog, and on account of which they deny that the Messiah has come since it has not yet been fought, I have spoken above. Finally, neither does the return of the people to the land of Canaan, which the same Jews argue will take place through the Messiah, make his coming doubtful. For if the return of the people to the land of Canaan, promised everywhere, was fulfilled when they came back from Babylon, that has nothing to do with the time of the Messiah; but if it is still to be fulfilled at that time, when before the end of the world the Jews will be converted to Christ, not even so can the Messiah's coming be overturned, because what will happen in the last times of his kingdom does not remove his earlier coming. For the kingdom of the Messiah will not be one of a few days or years, or of a few deeds.

units.la: CXXIII. Quae argumenta Mefsiae adven- tum confirmant, eadem Jesum esse Christum, seu Mefsiam adstruunt.
units.tr: CXXIII. The arguments that confirm the coming of the Messiah also establish that Jesus is the Christ, that is, the Messiah.

units.la: Nam quae Mefsiae ad- ventum praecedere debuerunt, eadem Jesu ad- ventum praecesserunt: & quae Mefsia apparente extare debuerunt, Jesu adventante extiterunt, aut mox extare debuerunt: & quod tempus Mefsiae adventui & morti a Daniele praefixum est, illud Jesu moriente effluxit, & tam bene in Jesum convenit,ut Magister Hebraeus Nehemi- as,qui quinquaginta annis eum praecesit,aper- te jam tum dixerit, non posse ultra annos eos quin- quaginta tempus Messiae a Daniele praesignificatum protrahi. Vel igitur alius Mefsias circa ea tem- pora ostendi debet; quod ne ipsi quidem Judaei sustinent; vel Prophetiae fefellerunt; quod di- ctu blasphemum est; vel Jesus noster Mefsias est. Et revera eum verum Mefsiam esse argu- mentum habemus promptissimum; evidentis- simumque, quodque iis, qui in Christum credunt, omnibus obvium & necessarium cognitu est, nempe quod ipse Jesus, Dei Sapientia, com- mendavit discipulis Johannis Baptistae interro- gantibus, numquid ipse esset, qui venturus erat, an alius expectandus? Profecti, inquit, renunciate Johanni, quae auditis, & quae videtis. Caeci vident, & claudi ambulant, leprosi purgantur, & surdi audi- unt, mortui excitantur, & pauperibus Evangelium praedicatur. Et beatus est, qui in me non offenditur, Matth.XI.4.5.6. Hoc argumentum validum & Greek est. Si enim Jesu apparente ea visa sunt, quae videri debuerunt, & audita, quae audiri debuerunt, Christo apparente, quin & Mefsias venerit, & Jesus Mefsias ille sit, dubitari non potest. Quoad Greek visa. Jesus opera fecit, quae Mefsiam decuerunt. Nemo ante vel post Jesum, eo miraculis illustrior apparuit, uti supra ostendimus. Promiserat autem Deus Prophetam parem Mosi, hoc est, Mose non inferio- rem; eumque audiri jusserat, Deut.XVIII.18. Sanatione morborum Israelis se sanatorem pec- catorum, quae miseriae omnis causa sunt, de- monstravit. Ita potentia unctus fuit a Deo, hoc est,demonstratum est,eum a Deo esse,& Regem constitutum esse, Act.II.22. X.28. Esaj.LXI.1. Accedunt & illa opera, quae per Apostolos fecit, de quibus dictum est: Ecce ego, & pueri, quos mihi dedisti in signum & prodigium in medio Israe- lis a Jehova, qui habitat in monte Sion, ibid.VIII. 18. Tum & ipsa humilitas Jesu, quae adeo Ju- daeos offendit,inter visa illa, Mefsiam ostenden- tia referri meretur. Debuit enim esse minor An- gelis,Psal.VIII.6. Vermis,& non vir,ibid.XXII.7. Cui nulla species, nullum decus, nulla spectabilis, ap- petibilis forma; spretus & deficiens virorum, vir do- lorum & notus infirmitate, & ut res tecta facie a- versanda prae nobis, contemptibilis, & non reputan- dus,Esaj.LIII.2.3. Non clamare,non efferre se, non facere audiri foris vocem suam, ibid. XLII.2. nihil denique facere, quod terrenam Majestatem re- siperet, & acerbissima, ad mortem usque, pati. Quae scandalo licet sint iis, qui alta sapiunt & quaerunt, tamen & obedientiam & charitatem Sacerdote dignam demonstrant. Quibus & alia post mortem ejus visa succenturiari debent; supplicia populo Judaico rebelli & refra- ctario, juxta praedictionem ipsius Jesu, & disci- pulorum ejus,Divinitus inflicta; praedicatio ejus in gentibus; idololatriae & cultus daemo- num extirpatio: apostasia Ecclesiae; ejusdem inter seductionum & violentiae omnis certami- na, & martyria mirabilis conservatio. quae cun- cta juxta praedictiones Prophetarum, Jesu & A- postolorum ejus evenerunt hactenus & eveni- re non desinunt. Accedunt visis hisce etiam Greek audita. Nam Jesus noster Evangeli- um praedicavit pauperibus. Ad hoc enim mit- tendus erat Messias, ut evangelizaret [Hebrew] mansuetis vel pauperibus, humilibus, non sua justitia, sapientia, viribus nixis, sed justitiae Dei se subji- cientibus, & eandem esurientibus, sitientibus, Esaj.
units.tr: For the things that ought to have preceded the Messiah's coming did precede Jesus' coming, and the things that ought to have existed when the Messiah appeared did exist when Jesus came, or were soon to exist. The time that Daniel fixed for the Messiah's coming and death ran out at Jesus' death, and it fits Jesus so well that the Hebrew teacher Nehemiah, who lived fifty years before him, openly said already that the time of the Messiah foretold by Daniel could not be extended beyond those fifty years. Therefore either another Messiah must be shown to have appeared around that time, which even the Jews themselves do not maintain; or the prophecies have failed, which is blasphemous to say; or Jesus our Lord is the Messiah. And indeed we have a most ready, most evident argument that he is the true Messiah. It is obvious to those who believe in Christ and necessary for them to know. Jesus himself, the Wisdom of God, pointed to it when the disciples of John the Baptist asked whether he was "the one who is to come, or should we look for another?" He answered: "Go and report to John what you hear and see. The blind see, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the gospel is preached to the poor. And blessed is the one who is not offended in me" (Matt. 11:4-6). This argument is strong and clear. For if, at Jesus' appearing, those things were seen that ought to be seen, and those things were heard that ought to be heard, and if at Christ's appearing the Messiah has come, then there can be no doubt that Jesus is that Messiah. As to the things seen: Jesus performed works that befit the Messiah. No one before or after Jesu has appeared more illustrious in miracles, as we have shown above. God had promised a prophet like Moses, that is, not inferior to Moses, and had commanded that he be heard (Deut. 18:18). By healing the diseases of Israel, he showed himself the healer of sins, which are the cause of all misery. Thus he was "anointed by God with power," that is, it was shown that he was from God and appointed King (Acts 2:22; 10:38; Isa. 61:1). To these are added the works he did through the apostles, of which it was said: "Behold, I and the children whom God has given me are for signs and wonders in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion" (Heb. 2:13; Isa. 8:18). Moreover, Jesus' very humility, which so offended the Jews, deserves to be counted among the things seen that point to the Messiah. For he was to be "lower than the angels" (Ps. 8:5), "a worm and not a man" (Ps. 22:6), "one who had no form or comeliness, no beauty that we should desire him; despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with infirmity, and as one from whom men hide their faces, despised, and not esteemed" (Isa. 53:2-3); one who would "not cry out, nor lift up his voice, nor make his voice heard in the street" (Isa. 42:2); who would do nothing that savoured of earthly majesty, and would suffer the most bitter things, even to death. Though these things are a stumbling block to those who think highly and seek lofty things, they nonetheless show an obedience and a love worthy of the Priest. To these must be added the things seen after his death: punishments divinely inflicted on the rebellious and stubborn Jewish people, according to the prediction of Jesus himself and his disciples; the preaching of his gospel among the nations; the extirpation of idolatry and the worship of demons; the apostasy of the Church; the struggles of the Church against all kinds of seductions and violence, and its wonderful preservation under martyrdom. All these things have happened, according to the predictions of the prophets, of Jesus, and of his apostles, and they have not ceased to happen to this day. To these visible things are added the things heard. For our Jesus preached the gospel to the poor. Indeed the Messiah was sent for this purpose, "to preach good news to the meek or poor, the humble, who rely not on their own righteousness, wisdom, or strength, but submit themselves to the righteousness of God, and hunger and thirst for it," (Isa. 61:1).

units.la: Jesum Messiam esse tum iisdem argumentis, quibus Mefsiae adventus confirmatur: tum ex iis, quae Jesu apparente visa & audita sunt: tum ex hereditate Esaj.LXI.1.Luc.IV.18. Debuit igitur mansuetis & pauperibus annuntiari bonum. Neque aliud bonum illis, qui sub jugo & lege gemebant, annuntiari majus poterat, quàm quòd justitia parata & adducta esset. Quae annuntiatio fieri nisi ab eo, qui à Deo missus erat, non poterat, tum quia Scripturae nihil de Pseudo-prophetis Evangelium falsò annuntiaturis praedixerunt: tum quia Pseudo-prophetae justitiam Dei ignorant, & eam praedicare non possunt: tum quia is, qui Evangelium annuntiat, etiam facit & patitur ea, quae ad confirmationem annuntiatae justitiae pertinent. Ea verò Dominus Jesus fecit & passus est; utpote qui in tota vita Legi Dei obedivit, in passionibus charitatem Sacerdote dignam ostendit, & Legem Dei & gratiam ejus praedicavit. Praeterea etiam praeconium resurrectionis è mortuis, ascensionis in Coelum non sine accedente robore testium [Greek] circumstantiarum & operum, qualia sunt, quòd Spiritum S. in discipulos suos effudit, & ii, qui ante erant delapsi, & dissidebant, & metu ac terrore perculsi erant, magna vi testimonium illud Judaeis & Gentibus praedicarunt; & potentiam suam inter hostes exercuit, ex quibus Saulem praedatus ministrum suum fecit, & velut in triumpho egit, & ea, quibus olim frustra saevierant, abolevit; sufficientibus argumentis, in mundo percrebuit. Data mox etiam est haereditas gentium, & simul impletae sunt promissiones Noae & Abrahamo & populo Israelis factae: Pelliciet Deus Japhetum, &c. Gen.IX.27. In Semine tuo benedicent sibi omnes familiae terrae, ibid. XII.3. XXII.18. Ad Legem ejus insulae sperabunt, Esaj.XLII.4. Creditus enim in mundo Jesus est non obstantibus gravissimis obstaculis respectu tum Christi, humilis adeò & tot opprobriis, execrabili imprimis crucifixione mactati; tum doctrinae ejus omnibus mundi doctrinis, carni inprimis & sanguini hostiliter adversantis: tum praeconii Christi, quibus rudibus piscatoribus tot Academiae, tot Philosophorum agmina, tot ingeniorum acumina, tot tribunalia & sceptra cesserunt; tum modi docendi, qui non elaboratus, curiosus, lenociniis sermonis & verborum ampullis ornatus, sed simplex, rudibus pariter atque eruditis obvius, nec dolo nec vi ulla munitus fuit. Et qua ratione fides Jesu in mundo plantata, eadem conservata & propagata haetenus est. Accedit, quòd ii, qui Mosi & Prophetis credunt, & eorum sermonem probè intelligunt, idem in sermone Christi & Apostolorum recognoscunt, quod in sermone Mosis & Prophetarum legunt, atque sic dubitare non possunt, quin cor unum cum Patribus habeant, & doctrina Apostolorum ex Coelo sit. Suffragatur quin etiam argumentum à Prophetia petitum. Nam & Prophetia Christi & Apostolorum sic haetenus impleta est, ut quae in Ecclesia Christiana gesta sunt, à Christo & Apostolis praedicta reperiantur: Et Prophetia Christi & Apostolorum eadem est cum Prophetia Mosis & Prophetarum reliquorum: & Jesus apparuit talis, tali tempore, & temporis charactere, quali Messiam apparituram Prophetae praedixerunt.
units.tr: That Jesus is the Messiah is shown both by the same arguments by which the coming of the Messiah is confirmed, and by those things which were seen and heard when Jesus appeared, and by the inheritance (Isa. 61:1; Luke 4:18). Good news therefore had to be announced to the meek and the poor. Nor could a greater good be announced to those who groaned under the yoke and the law than that righteousness had been prepared and brought near. This announcement could not be made except by one who had been sent by God. This is so because the Scriptures foretold nothing about false prophets who would falsely announce the gospel; because false prophets do not know the righteousness of God and cannot preach it; and because one who announces the gospel also does and suffers those things that pertain to the confirmation of the righteousness announced. The Lord Jesus did and suffered these things, since he obeyed the Law of God throughout his whole life, showed in his sufferings a love worthy of the Priest, and preached the Law of God and his grace. Moreover, the proclamation of the resurrection from the dead and of the ascension into heaven was not without the added strength of the testimony of witnesses and of circumstances and works. Such were the effusion of the Holy Spirit on his disciples, and the fact that those who had earlier fallen away and were divided, and had been struck with fear and terror, then proclaimed that testimony to Jews and Gentiles with great power. He also exercised his power among his enemies: from among them he took Saul, made him his minister, and led him as in a triumph; and he abolished those things against which they had raged in vain. With sufficient arguments, this spread through the world. Soon afterwards the inheritance of the nations was also given, and at the same time the promises made to Noah, to Abraham, and to the people of Israel were fulfilled: "God shall enlarge Japheth" (Gen. 9:27); "In your seed all the families of the earth shall bless themselves" (Gen. 12:3; 22:18); "The islands shall wait for his law" (Isa. 42:4). For Jesus has been believed in the world, although there were very grave obstacles, on the side of Christ himself, who was so humble and was struck with so many reproaches, above all by the detestable death of the cross; on the side of his doctrine, which stands in hostile opposition to all the doctrines of the world, above all to the flesh and blood; on the side of the preaching of Christ, to which so many academies, so many companies of philosophers, so many keen minds, so many tribunals and sceptres yielded, while the preachers were rude fishermen; and on the side of his manner of teaching, which was not laboured, curious, adorned with the enticements of speech and the bombast of words, but simple, accessible alike to the untutored and the learned, and fortified by neither deceit nor any violence. And by the same means by which the faith of Jesus was planted in the world, it has been preserved and propagated up to the present. In addition, those who believe Moses and the prophets, and understand their words rightly, recognise in the speech of Christ and of the apostles the same thing they read in the speech of Moses and the prophets. Thus they cannot doubt that they have one heart with the fathers, and that the doctrine of the apostles is from heaven. Even the argument drawn from prophecy lends support. For the prophecy of Christ and of the apostles has been fulfilled up to now in such a way that the things done in the Christian Church are found foretold by Christ and the apostles. The prophecy of Christ and of the apostles is the same as the prophecy of Moses and the other prophets; and Jesus appeared such a person, at such a time, and with such marks of the time, as the prophets foretold the Messiah would appear.

units.la: CXXIV. Longum foret paralleliam inter ea, quae de Jesu nostro historia praedicat, & à Prophetis praedicta sunt, instituere. [Greek]
units.tr: CXXIV. It would be long to draw a parallel between the things that the history tells about our Jesus and the things foretold by the prophets.

units.la: Lower column continues with the right-hand text, from "ζεν & summa rerum capita delibare sufficiet. Prodromum Jesus habuit Johannem, qui virtute & spiritu Elias fuit, juxta Esaj.XL.3. Malach.III.1. IV.1. Natus est ex Semine Abrahami, Judae, Davidis, Gen.XII.1,3. XXII.18. XLIX.10." and continues to "Latus ejus mortuus est" in the right column. tui perfossum est, Zach.XII.10. Corpus ejus à divitibus pollinctum & sepultum est, Esaj.LIII. 9. Tertio die ex morte revixit, Psalm.XVI.10. XLIX.16.Hos.VI.2.XIII.14.In Coelum ascendit, Psalm.XXIV.7. XLVII.6. LXVIII.5. Prov. XXX.4.Esaj.LII.13.Ad dextram Dei Patris consedit,Psal.XVI.10.11. CX.1.Spiritum S. discipulis misit, Esaj.XLIV.3. LIX.21. Ezech.XXXVI. 26.27. Joel,II.28.29. Taceo reliqua, quae deinceps in Ecclesia per Apostolos gesta sunt, & hactenus in eadem evenerunt, juxta testimonia clarissima Mosis & Prophetarum. quae cùm innumera fere sint, ad compendium ponimus.
units.tr: ...and it will suffice to touch on the main heads. Jesus had John as his forerunner, who was Elijah in power and spirit, according to Isa. 40:3; Mal. 3:1; 4:1. He was born of the seed of Abraham, Judah and David, Gen. 12:1, 3; 22:18; 49:10. ...his side was pierced, Zech. 12:10. His body was anointed by the rich and buried, Isa. 53:9. On the third day he rose again from death, Ps. 16:10; 49:16; Hos. 6:2; 13:14. He ascended into heaven, Ps. 24:7; 47:6; 68:5; Prov. 30:4; Isa. 52:13. He sat down at the right hand of God the Father, Ps. 16:10, 11; 110:1. He sent the Holy Spirit to his disciples, Isa. 44:3; 59:21; Ezek. 36:26, 27; Joel 2:28, 29. I pass over the rest, which have since been done in the Church through the Apostles and have happened in it up to now, according to the very clear testimonies of Moses and the Prophets. Since these are almost innumerable, I set them down in summary.

units.la: CXXV. Testimoniis illis clarissimis nequicquam obscuriora quaedam, & figurata Judaei opponunt, ut in Jesu non evenisse omnia, quae in Messia eventura Prophetae praedixerunt, evincant. Quae supra §. CXXII. discussimus. Idem vero qui supra R. Isac. Fil.Abraham in eodem libro מנשה פין dicto ratiunculas etiam alias putidissimas corrasit, quibus Jesum non esse Messiam comprobare conatus est, sed infelice & vanissimo successu. Nam quae Deitati Jesu, nec non nativitati ex Virgine, genealogiae, miraculis & Regno spirituali ejusdem ex libris N.T. oppositum, cum iis conveniunt, quae supra, ubi de Deitate Christi, ejusdem nativitate ex Virgine, genealogia, miraculis & Regno spirituali egimus, adversus hostes Deitatis Jesu, Judaeos inprimis, dicta sunt. Neque operam ludere vacat. At nec melioris commatis sunt, quae doctrinae & vaticiniis Jesu idem objectat. Inimicorum dilectionem, fateor, Jesus suasit. At Legi Mosis eandem congruere, supra nos quoque confirmavimus. Non pacem, sed gladium in terram se attulisse, & divisionem inter conjunctissimos instituisse, Jesus Matth.X.34. profitetur; ne videlicet Evangelicam pacem externa & civili pace discipuli ejus metirentur, quasi,quod Judaeorum, ex male intellectis vaticiniis pacem sub Messia promittentibus εἰρήνην erat; Messias externam pacem stabiliturus, & divisionem hominum sublaturus in carnem venisset. Sed venit ille βαλὼν in medium jacturus non pacem, sed bellum; non tamen instituto proprio, sed eventu, quia homines maleferiatos persecuturos esse eos, qui piè in mundo vivere volunt, noverat, juxta praedictionem Divinam: Ne credatis in amico, ne confidatis familiari: a cubante in sinu tuo custodi ostia oris tui. Nam filius flagitium facit in patre: filia surgit in matrem suam; nurus in socrum suam: inimici cujusque domestici ejus sunt, Mich.VII.5.6. Eodem sensu Messiam lapidem offendiculi & petram scandali duabus domibus Israelis futurum,Esaj.VIII.14. praedictum fuit. Neque etiam Jesus religionem patrum mutavit vel abolevit, sed luculentius explicavit, & veritate atque corpore pro ascititiis figuris & umbris, veritati & corpori semper cedentibus, substituto plenissime perfecit. de quo in loco plura etiam diximus. Interiora Religionis, promissio, Christus, beneficia ejus spiritualia & coelestia, sacrificia spiritualia, lotiones & circumcisio cordis, quoad rem eadem semper fuerunt & sunt, licet modò cortice figurarum velata, modò revelata plenius. Quòd Jesus cedenti maxillam dextram, alteram etiam objiciendam, Matth.V.39. dixit, privatae vindictae, non publicae oppositum est. Sensus enim est, novas etiam super veteres injurias ferendas esse potius, quàm ut privatam ultionem exequāre. Non peccavit autem adversus Legem hanc vel Jesus, cùm Pontificis servo maxillam unam cedenti alteram non objecit, Joh.XVIII.22. vel S. Paulus cùm Pontifici colaphum infligenti oblocutus est; Act.XXIII.2. Nam Jesus Pontificis famulum dehortatus licet à petulanti insectatione, se ipsum tamen verberibus multiplicatis, imò morti ipsi totum patienter objicere, quàm se ipsum ulcisci maluit, Matth. XXVI. 68. Esaj.L.6. De S. Pauli verò facto supra egimus. Non ille privatae vindictae studio, sed Spiritus Dei Zelo judici injustè judicanti imprecatus est. Illud quoque dilutum est, quod ex eo, quòd Jesus pro crucifigentibus ipsum Deum, ut remittat iis ignorantibus peccatum, cujus se reatui obstrinxerunt, precatus est, vel irritam ejus intercessionem fuisse, vel crucifixionem Jesu non esse causam exilii & calamitatum, quas sustinent, colligunt. Intercessionis enim Jesu efficacia statim se in conversione Centurionis, & eorum qui cum ipso erant, Matth.XXVII.54. aliisque pluribus Petri concione compunctis, Act.II.23-40.41.47.nec non sacerdotibus, ibid. VI.7.exeruit. Alia ratio eorum erat, qui Jesum petulanter crucifixerant, & in corde suo sibi benedixerant, dicentes: Pax mihi erit, etiamsi in duritie cordis mei ambulavero: de quo Moses: Non vult Jehova illi parcere, quia tum fumabit furor Jehovae, &c.Deut.XXIX.19.20. Non peccavit contra Legem idem Jesus, cùm adversus adulteram sententiam mortis ferre renuit, Joh.VIII.11. quia cùm judex non fuerit, eam ferre non potuit. Idem enim in simili casu dixit: Homo, quis me constituit ἀκαςτὴν judicem? Luc.XII.14. Divortia porro temeraria Judaeorum graviter Jesus, Matth.XIX.8.9. increpuit, sed fretus authoritate Mosis, Gen.II.24. & Malach.II.14: non vel Mosi, vel Prophetis obloquens. De quo etiam in loco plura diximus. Mandatum porro à Jesu diviti juveni latum, ut venderet sua, & pauperibus daret, Matth.XIX.21. non commune & simplex, sed personale & causae singulari, puta manifestandae infirmitati hominis sibi in justitia sua nimium placentis, innixum fuit. Idem Jesus ciborum & dierum discrimen sustulit, perinde ut cerimonias reliquas, quia ex mente Dei Legislatoris interdictum ad certum tempus durare, non semper vigere debuit. quod ipsum etiam supra veritati dedimus. Nihil ergo in doctrina Jesu apparet, quod Messiam dedeceat.
units.tr: CXXV. The Jews set against these very clear testimonies certain passages that are obscure and figurative, in order to prove that not everything that the Prophets foretold of the Messiah came to pass in Jesus. We have discussed these above in §. CXXII. The same man who above, in the same book called Menasseh Pin [מנשה פין], was cited as R. Isaac son of Abraham, also heaped together other very foolish little arguments, by which he tried to prove that Jesus is not the Messiah, but with an unhappy and very vain result. For the objections, drawn from the New Testament, against the Deity of Jesus, and likewise against his birth from a Virgin, his genealogy, his miracles and his spiritual Kingdom, agree with what we have said above, where we treated of the Deity of Christ, his birth from a Virgin, his genealogy, his miracles and his spiritual Kingdom, against the enemies of the Deity of Jesus, chiefly the Jews. Nor is there time to waste on these. Nor are the objections which he raises against the teaching and prophecies of Jesus of any better quality. I admit that Jesus taught the love of enemies. But that this agrees with the Law of Moses we have also confirmed above. Jesus declares, that he came not to send peace upon the earth but a sword, and to set up division between those who are closest, Matt. 10:34. He says this so that his disciples would not measure the Gospel peace by external and civil peace, as though the peace which the Jews, from misunderstood prophecies, expected under the Messiah were the peace [εἰρήνην] that the Messiah would establish as an external peace and remove the division among men, had he come in the flesh. But he came, [βαλὼν] casting into the midst, to bring not peace but war; not however by his own purpose but by the outcome, since he knew that wicked men would persecute those who wish to live godly in the world, according to the Divine prediction: Do not trust in a friend, do not place confidence in a companion; guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom. For the son dishonours the father, the daughter rises against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own household, Mic. 7:5, 6. In the same sense the Messiah was foretold as a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to the two houses of Israel, Isa. 8:14. Nor did Jesus change or abolish the religion of the fathers, but explained it more clearly, and by the truth and the body fully completed what was put in place of the added figures and shadows, which always give way to truth and body. I have said more about this in its place. The inner things of religion, the promise, Christ, his spiritual and heavenly benefits, spiritual sacrifices, the washings and circumcision of the heart, have always been and still are the same in substance, although at one time veiled under the bark of figures and at another revealed more fully. That Jesus said, to one who strikes the right cheek, offer the other also, Matt. 5:39, is opposed to private revenge, not to public justice. For the sense is that new injuries, even on top of old ones, are rather to be borne than that one should carry out private vengeance. Nor did Jesus sin against this Law when he did not offer the other cheek to the servant of the High Priest who struck one, John 18:22; nor did St. Paul when he spoke against the High Priest who ordered him struck, Acts 23:2. For Jesus, while he dissuaded the High Priest's servant from wanton abuse, preferred to suffer himself many blows, and even to give himself wholly to death patiently, rather than to avenge himself, Matt. 26:68; Isa. 50:6. As for St. Paul's deed, we have treated it above. He did not invoke curses on the unjustly judging judge out of a desire for private vengeance, but out of the zeal of the Spirit of God. This too has been answered: from the fact that Jesus, on behalf of those who crucified him, asked God to forgive them the sin in which they were bound through their ignorance, they conclude either that his intercession was in vain, or that the crucifixion of Jesus was not the cause of the exile and calamities which they suffer. For the efficacy of Jesus' intercession was shown at once in the conversion of the Centurion and of those who were with him, Matt. 27:54, and in the many others pricked in heart by Peter's sermon, Acts 2:23-40, 41, 47, and likewise in the priests, ibid. 6:7. Their own explanation is that of those who had wantonly crucified Jesus and had blessed themselves in their hearts, saying: I shall have peace, even if I walk in the stubbornness of my heart. Of them Moses says: The Lord will not be willing to spare him, for then the anger of the Lord will smoke, etc., Deut. 29:19, 20. Nor did this same Jesus sin against the Law when he refused to pass sentence of death upon the adulteress, John 8:11, because, since he was not a judge, he could not pass it. For in a similar case he said: Man, who has made me a [ἀκαςτὴν] judge? Luke 12:14. Moreover, Jesus sharply rebuked the rash divorces of the Jews, Matt. 19:8, 9, but relying on the authority of Moses, Gen. 2:24, and Mal. 2:14, and not speaking against Moses or the Prophets. I have also said more about this in its place. Further, the command which Jesus gave to the rich young man, to sell his possessions and give to the poor, Matt. 19:21, was not a common and simple command but a personal one, resting on a particular cause, namely to reveal the weakness of a man who was too pleased with his own righteousness. Jesus likewise removed the distinction of foods and days, just as the other ceremonies, because by the mind of God the Lawgiver the prohibition ought to last only for a fixed time and not to be always in force. This too we have already conceded to the truth above. Nothing therefore appears in the teaching of Jesus which is unworthy of the Messiah.

units.la: CXXVI. At nec merito in vaticiniis ejus tale quid Judaeus alter Lusitanus in Colloquio Mittelburgensi, aliique notant. Nam quòd Jesus Evangelium Regni sui ante excidium urbis in toto mundo praedicatum iri, Matth.XXIV.14. praedixit, fidem planè invenit, & inveniet ampliùs. Discipuli enim ejus profecti in omnibus locis praedicarunt, Marc.XVI.20. In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, & in totum mundum verbum eorum, Rom.X.18. Et suo tempore intrabit plenitudo gentium, ibid.XI.25. Hierosolyma enim calcabitur à gentibus, donec impleantur tempora gentium, Luc.XXI.24. Neque illud obstat, quod multae gentes in Asia, Africa & Europa olim ad Jesum conversae ab eodem ad Muhammedem & Antichristum defecerint. Nam & praedictum semel est,
units.tr: CXXVI. Nor, rightly, does another Portuguese Jew at the Colloquy of Middelburg, or others, note anything of this kind in his prophecies. For when Jesus foretold that the Gospel of his Kingdom would be preached in the whole world before the destruction of the city, Matt. 24:14, he has certainly found and will find faith more widely. For his disciples, having gone out, preached in all places, Mark 16:20. Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the whole world, Rom. 10:18. And in its own time the fullness of the Gentiles will come in, ibid. 11:25. For Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, Luke 21:24. Nor does it stand in the way that many nations in Asia, Africa and Europe, once converted to Jesus, have since fallen away from him to Muhammad and the Antichrist. For it has also been foretold once that...

units.la: Tum vide est, Deum vindicaturum esse eum,qui non obedierit verbis Dei, quæ positurus erat in ore Messiæ, magni illius Prophetæ, Deut.XVIII.18.19. Et Christus ipse omnia, quæ futura erant,explicavit, monens discipulos, ne deciperentur, vel conturbarentur. Inprimis Apocalypsis omnium tentationum ordinem exhibuit. Et in illis ipsis terris, in quibus defectio à Jesu facta est, Ecclesiarum reliquiæ nonnullæ manserunt, juxta prædictionem Dei: Erit in die illa,addet Dominus secundò manum suam, ut acquirat in reliquum populi sui; quod reliquum erit ab Assyria & Ægypto, & Pathros(Thebaide Habeilinorum Regno) & Cusch (Æthiopia & Arabia) & Elam (Persia) & Sinear (Babylonia) & Chamath (terris, quæ sunt ad septentrionem Palæstinæ) & insulis maris (Occidente, sive Europa, & quod ultra est,) Esaj.XI.11.Hæc in diebus Messiæ futura palam est, quia surculus ex radicibus Jesse procedens,ibid.v.1.sine dubio Messias est. Licèt verò Ecclesiæ in Oriente & Occidente imminutæ sint, tamen id factum est per judicium, quo Christus Regnum suum vindicavit, hypocritas punivit,& in gentibus glorificatus est. De quo pluribus, ibid.LVI.8.&c. agitur. Non etiam prædictionis ejusdem, Luc.XXI.24. de Hierosolyma à gentibus conculcanda,donec plenitudo gentium intraverit, fidem illud minuit, quod Hierosolyma non semper sub gentium, sed aliquando etiam sub Christianorum, Constantini M.&Bullionæi potestate fuit. Nam per ἐθνη gentes non infideles duntaxat, sed fideles etiam oppositè ad Judæos, intelliguntur. Utrique Hierosolymam calcarunt, non in potestatem suam redigendo duntaxat, sed in pace etiam eidem dominando. Ac licèt etiam Ecclesia Christiana horrendum in modum à gentilibus Imperatoribus,Turca & Antichristo diutissimè pressa fuerit, nunquam tamen ita oppressa fuit, vel opprimetur, ut non amplius constet fides prædictioni Christi, quòd portæ Inferorum eì supra Petram ædificatæ prævalitura non sint,Matth. XVI.18. Nam idem Jesus,qui Ecclesiæ suæ constantiam promisit, etiam angustias & tribulationes eidem obventuras passim, velut Matth. IX.15.Joh.XV.18.21.XVI.2.3. &c. prædixit:& ejusdem Apostoli certamina illa luculentiùs prænunciarunt. Ad constantiam Regni Christi satis est, quòd nunquam illud in mundo desinit, sed inter gravissima certamina & conflictationes non in uno jam monte Sionis, sed in multis montibus hinc inde durat. Deus nobis est receptus & robur, auxilium in angustiis promptum valde. Iccirco non timemus,cùm movetur terra,& cùm Lapsant montes in cor marium. Strepant, turbentur aquæ ejus,&c. Deus est in medio ejus,non movetur. Auxiliatur ei Deus appetente matutino, &c. Psal.XLVI.2-8. Id,si quodammodo etiam de Ecclesia in V.T. in monte Sionis structa,at casibus miris identidem turbata & jactata, adeò ut quandoque filia Sion fuerit ut tugurium in vinea,ut casa in cucumerano,ut urbs obsessa, Esaj.I.8. dici potuit: quomodo non etiam de Ecclesia Jesu super petram ædificata,sed perpetuæ tamen conflictationi obnoxia dici potest? Movetur illa, sed non commovetur; turbatur, sed non perturbatur: premitur, sed non opprimitur. Frustra iidem flagellant velut incerta, imò falsa verba illa Christi: Nunc judicium est hujus
units.tr: Moreover, it is clear that God will avenge himself on the one who does not obey the words of God, which he was to put in the mouth of the Messiah, that great Prophet, Deut. 18:18, 19. And Christ himself explained all that was to come, warning the disciples not to be deceived or disturbed. Above all, the Apocalypse set out the order of all the temptations. And in those very lands in which the falling away from Jesus took place, some remnants of the Churches have remained, according to the prediction of God: In that day the Lord will again put forth his hand to gain the remnant of his people, which will be left from Assyria and Egypt, and Pathros (the Thebaid, the kingdom of the Habeilini), and Cush (Ethiopia and Arabia), and Elam (Persia), and Shinar (Babylonia), and Hamath (the lands which are to the north of Palestine), and the islands of the sea (the West, or Europe, and what lies beyond), Isa. 11:11. That these things are to be in the days of the Messiah is plain, because a shoot coming forth from the roots of Jesse, ibid. v. 1, is without doubt the Messiah. Although indeed the Churches in East and West have been diminished, this has nonetheless happened through the judgment by which Christ vindicated his Kingdom, punished the hypocrites, and was glorified among the nations. Many things are said about this in more detail, ibid. 56:8, etc. Nor does that prediction, Luke 21:24, that Jerusalem would be trodden down by the Gentiles until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, lose its credibility because Jerusalem has not always been under the power of the Gentiles, but at times also under that of the Christians, of Constantine the Great, and of Godfrey of Bouillon. For by ἐθνη [the Gentiles] are understood not only unbelievers but also believers, in contrast to the Jews. Both trod down Jerusalem, not merely by bringing it under their power, but also by ruling over it in peace. And although the Christian Church has been most dreadfully and for a very long time pressed by the heathen Emperors, the Turks and the Antichrist, it has never been so crushed, nor will it be, that the faith in Christ's prophecy is no longer assured, that the gates of Hell shall not prevail against the Church built upon the rock, Matt. 16:18. For the same Jesus who promised the constancy of his Church also foretold everywhere that distresses and tribulations would come upon it, as in Matt. 9:15; John 15:18, 21; 16:2, 3, etc.; and his Apostle foretold those conflicts still more clearly. For the constancy of Christ's Kingdom it is enough that it never ceases in the world, but amid the most grievous struggles and conflicts it endures, not now on one mountain of Zion but on many mountains here and there. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear when the earth is moved, and when the mountains are carried into the heart of the seas. Its waters roar and are troubled, etc. God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved. God shall help her at the dawning of the morning, etc. Ps. 46:2-8. If this could in some measure be said of the Church in the Old Testament, built on the mountain of Zion, yet repeatedly shaken and tossed by wondrous misfortunes, so that at times the daughter of Zion was like a booth in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city, Isa. 1:8, why could it not also be said of the Church of Jesus, built upon the rock, yet exposed to perpetual conflict? She is moved, but not overthrown; she is troubled, but not thrown into confusion; she is pressed, but not crushed. Those who scourge these words of Christ as uncertain, or rather false, do so in vain: Now is the judgment of this

units.la: mundi: nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicitur foras: Et ego cùm elatus fuero ex terra, omnes trahàm post me,Joh.XII.31.32. Numquid enim, inquiunt, jam tum judicium processit; Sathanas foro cessit, & Christus omnes homines ad se pellexit? Sed facilis responsio est.Non enim de novissimo judicio agitur,sed de eo,quodDeus in Judæos induratos, & gentes patienter hactenus toleratas, sed longanimitate Dei efferatas, & Christi Evangelium repudiantes exercere incipiebat. De quo judicio etiam Moses, Deut.XXIX.23.&c. XXXII.36. David, Psalm.L. Malachias capp. II. III. loquuntur. Sed & Princeps hujus mundi, expiato in morte Christi peccato, quod eum principem mundi fecit ,ejectus semel est meritò, at ejici coepit & usque perrexit meriti ejusdem efficacia, donec non amplius in eo habebit locum, & Serpens non amplius nocebit in toto monte Sancto, Esaj.LXV.25. Ultima Sathanæ extrusio erit abolitio omnis potestatis, dominationis & ipsius mortis, 1.Cor.XV.24.25.55.56. Idem verò exaltatus ad se traxit omnes Judæos & gentes, utrosque sine discrimine, propositus in signum populorum,ad quod omnes confugiant, Esaj.XI.10. Perseverat & perseverabit ea tractio, donec & plenitudinem gentium attrahat, & Judæos, jam sub inobedientiam inclusos, salvet,Rom.XI.25.26. Quid prædictioni huic falsi,& non in Prophetis ipsis testimonium habentis inest?
units.tr: of this world: now the prince of this world is cast out; and I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me, John 12:31-32. For they object: Was judgment not then already passed? Was Satan not driven from the field, and did Christ not draw all men to himself? The answer is easy. The passage speaks not of the last judgment but of that judgment which God had begun to execute on the hardened Jews, on the nations he had hitherto patiently endured, but who had become savage through the forbearance of God, and on those who rejected the Gospel of Christ. Moses (Deut. 29:23ff.; 32:36), David (Ps. 50) and Malachi (chs. 2-3) speak of this judgment. And the Prince of this world, though his sin was expiated in the death of Christ, which made him prince of the world, was rightly cast out once for all; yet the effect of that merit began to cast him out and has continued to do so, until he shall no longer have a place in it, and the serpent shall no longer harm in all my holy mountain, Isa. 65:25. The final expulsion of Satan will be the abolition of all power, dominion and death itself, 1 Cor. 15:24-25, 55-56. Moreover, Christ, having been lifted up, drew all Jews and Gentiles to himself, both without distinction, set forth as a sign to the peoples, to which all may flee, Isa. 11:10. That drawing continues and will continue, until it has drawn in the fullness of the Gentiles and saved the Jews, who are now shut up in disobedience, Rom. 11:25-26. What is false in this prediction, which has its testimony in the Prophets themselves?

units.la: CXXVII. Sed audent etiam Jesu nostri vitam omnis labis scelerisque purissimam maledictis proscindere, & in crimen vocare.
units.tr: CXXVII. But they also dare to tear apart the life of our Jesus, most pure from every stain and crime, with slanders and to bring it into accusation.

units.la: Nam Majores suos Sacerdotes,viros probos & sapientes inprimis, pessimè de Christo, tanquam Samaritano, blasphemo, seductore & daemonium habente sensisse, objiciunt. Sed similia, saltim pessima quæque Judæos quosdam Mosi,& Aharoni, Num.XVI.3. Mosi,ibid.v.13.14. Achabum & Jezabelem Eliæ, 1.Reg.XVIII.17. Michæ,ibid.XXII.8. Amaziam Amosò, Amos.VII.10. Pontificem Paschurum Jeremiæ, Jer.XX.7.8. alios aliis innocentissimis impegisse crimina quis ignorat? Etenim si accusare sufficit, quis innocens erit? Samaritanus Christus non fuit,quia verum Deum Abrahami,Isaci & Jacobi,non peregrinum coluit.docuitque. Blasphemus non fuit, licèt se Filium Dei dixerit. Nam & Filius Dei fuit, & se esse operibus demonstravit. Neque ad alienos Deos colendos seduxit, sed corda filiorum ad corda Patrum flectendo, eundem Deum suasit, quem Patres coluerunt. Praeterea se daemonia non per Beelzebulem, sed per Spiritum Dei ejicere,ipse Matth.XII.25.&c. potenter & ad ἐχεμυθίαν usque Judæorum convicit. Quales insuper Christi accusatores fuerunt? Inimici ejus, invidiae oestro perciti, internecino ejus odio flagrantes, non ob scelus Christi, sed ob zelum ejus, quo hypocrisin & nequitiam eorundem in apricum produxit; denique simul judices & testes in causa propria. Neque illud obstat, quòd ne fratres quidem Christi in eum crediderunt,Joh.VII.5.Nam & ipsos carnali praejudicio terrestris Regni à Jesu erigendi laborasse, satis consilium illud, quo Christo,ut abiret in Judæam,& se mundo manifestaret, atque ita ἐν παῤῥησίᾳ in publico exisseret, suasemunt, v.3.4. prodidit. Cogitationes easdem, quas & reliqui Judæi, foverunt; fore scilicet,ut
units.tr: For they object that his elders, the priests, men of good character and above all wise, thought the worst of Christ, that he was a Samaritan, a blasphemer, a seducer, and a man possessed by a demon. But similar charges, at least the very worst, were brought by certain Jews against Moses and Aaron (Num. XVI.3), against Moses (ibid. v.13.14), Ahab and Jezebel against Elijah (1 Kings XVIII.17), against Micaiah (ibid.
