And since no one can call Jesus Lord except by the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 12:3), it is nevertheless clear that David called Christ his Lord (Ps. 110:1). Just as they believed through the Holy Spirit the promise that the Holy Spirit would be poured out, so through the same Holy Spirit they longed for the coming of Christ and the outpouring of the Spirit. Therefore the same Spirit kindled the thirst that he quenched. But although the covenant of grace is one and the same in substance, the economy of the covenant of grace differs in degree and in fulfilment. Hence it is expressly said that, under the economy of that time, before Christ was glorified, the Spirit was not yet (John 7:39), because he had not yet been given in the degree and fulfilment of operation that belongs to the Spirit of pure promise and adoption. For that Spirit, who in the fathers of the Old Testament worked faith in the testimony of God with hope of the coming Christ, was about to work in believers, now that Christ was glorified, faith in the already accomplished Christ, and indeed with perfect joy and perfect love as children of God. Just as in the children of God under the Law there was the Spirit of adoption or sonship, not pure but mixed with servitude, which is simply called the Spirit of bondage (Rom. 8:15), because it was given to children who were heirs and lords of all but who, being infants [νήπιοι] and subject to stewards and governors, differed in no way from servants (Gal. 4:1–3); so, when Christ was glorified, the Spirit was to be given purely and wholly as the Spirit of grace and of supplication for grace (Zech. 12:10), or the Spirit of adoption [πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας], that is, of sonship or adoption (Rom. 8:15). This Spirit is called, pre-eminently, the Spirit of God [πνεῦμα Θεοῦ] and the Spirit of the Son of God [πνεῦμα υἱοῦ Θεοῦ] (Rom. 8:9; 1 Cor. 2:12; 3:16; Gal. 4:6), and so on.

units.la: XLV.Præci-
units.tr: XLV. Chief-

units.la: Proximum N.T. bonum est donatio Spiritus Promissionis.
units.tr: The chief good of the New Testament is the gift of the Spirit of promise.

units.la: Differentia œconomiæ V.&N.T. quoad donationem Spiritus.
units.tr: The difference between the economy of the Old and New Testaments with regard to the gift of the Spirit.

units.la: XLV. Praecipuum igitur opus Spiritus Promissionis dati est υἱοθεσία Filiatio, seu Adoptio eorum, qui Evangelio credunt. Qui Spiritu Dei aguntur, hi sunt filii Dei. Non enim accepistis Spiritum servitutis iterum ad metum, sed accepistis πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας Spiritum Filiationis, in quo clamamus Abba, Pater. Idem ille Spiritus attestatur Spiritui nostro, quod sumus filii Dei. Si verò filii, etiam haeredes, haeredes quidem Dei, coharedes autem Christi, Rom.VIII.14–17. Misit Deus Filium suum, &c. ut eos, qui sub lege sunt, redimeret, ut υἱοθεσίαν filiationem adipisceremur. Quia verò estis filii, misit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda vestra, clamantem, Abba, Pater, Gal.IV.4.5.6. Praedestinavit nos εἰς υἱοθεσίαν ad adoptionem per Iesum Christum in ipsum, Ephes. I.5. Tum vero Spiritum hunc promissum Filiationis fideles accipiunt, cum Spiritum fidei erga Evangelium accipiunt, ut in Christum credant, & in eo, velut perfecte justificati, sibi benedicant & glorientur; denique affectum talem, qualis filiorum adultorum à paedagogorum austeritate liberatorum, erga parentes flagrat, induunt. Fuerunt etiam filii Dei credentes ante Christum, & eorundem Pater Deus fuit, Exod. IV.22. Deut.XIV.1. Malach.1.6. Hebr.II.10. Nonne Jehova est אביך pater tuus, קניך פשך ויכננך qui possedit te, fecit te, & praeparavit te? Deut.XXXII.6. Eorum fuit υἱοθεσία filiatio, seu adoptio, Rom.IX.4. Ideo comparantur cum filio familias, qui puer etiamsi sit Dominus omnium, sub paedagogis habetur, & eatenus nihil à servis differt, Gal.IV.1.2. Unde liquet, eos ejusmodi filios fuisse, ut & servi quodammodo fuerint; & ejusmodi filiationem, adoptionem habuisse, quae δουλείαν servitutem non exclusit, sed inclusit. Dabatur Israelitis nomen Filiorum in commune, quatenus ad haereditatem terrae, quae pignoris loco erat, vocabantur, & inter eos erant regeniti per Spiritum fidei ad spem haereditatis Coelestis, qui in reliquo mundo non inveniebantur, nisi quòd pauci Proselyti ad eos accedebant; in qua adoptione pro tempore mundi elementis serviebant, facta tamen promissione, fore, ut aliquando pleniori jure filiorum gauderent. Erit in loco, ubi dictum est iis: Non populus meus vos, ibi vocabuntur υἱοὶ Θεοῦ ζῶντος· Filii Dei viventis, Rom.IX.26. tum nempe, cum Deus in plenitudine temporum mittet Filium, &c. ut eos, qui sub Lege sunt, redimeret, ut filiationem accipiamus, Gal.IV.4.5. Hoc autem Spiritus Adoptionis filiorum, κατ' ἐξοχὴν, emphaticè, & in aetate non puerili & servili, sed virili talium, operatur, quod consentaneum est in iis agi vel fieri, dum à conditione servili vindicati, & ut filii à Deo adoptati habentur. Pertinent huc notitia omnium intellectus aenigmatum, sapientia & prudentia, fides passionis & glorificationis Christi, παρρησία, ἀπεκδοχὴ ... fiducia, accessus in confidentia, spes melior, per quam proximè sine Sacerdote, altari, victima, tabernaculo, lustrationibus typicis) ad Deum accedimus, Hebr. IV.16. VII.19. X.34.
units.tr: XLV. The chief work, then, of the Spirit of promise, who has been given, is the sonship, or adoption, of those who believe the Gospel. Those who are led by the Spirit of God are the sons of God. For you did not receive the spirit of bondage to fear again, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father." The same Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God. And if children, then heirs: heirs indeed of God, and fellow heirs with Christ (Rom. 8:14–17). God sent his Son, etc., that he might redeem those who are under the law, that we might receive adoption [υἱοθεσία]. And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, "Abba, Father" (Gal. 4:4–6). He predestined us to adoption [εἰς υἱοθεσίαν] through Jesus Christ for himself (Eph. 1:5). Believers then receive this promised Spirit of sonship when they receive the spirit of faith in regard to the Gospel, so that they believe in Christ and, in him as perfectly justified, rejoice in and glory in themselves; and finally they put on that disposition which burns towards parents in grown children freed from the harshness of tutors. There were also believing children of God before Christ, and God was their Father (Exod. 4:22; Deut. 14:1; Mal. 1:6; Heb. 2:10). Is not the LORD your father [אביך], who has possessed you, made you, and prepared you? (Deut. 32:6). Adoption or sonship belonged to them (Rom. 9:4). Therefore they are compared to a child of a household who, although he is lord of all, while a boy is under tutors and in this respect differs in no way from servants (Gal. 4:1–2). From this it is clear that they were such sons that they were in a certain way also servants, and that their sonship or adoption did not exclude servitude [δουλεία] but included it. The name of sons was given to the Israelites in common, insofar as they were called to the inheritance of the land, which was a pledge; and among them were those reborn through the Spirit of faith to the hope of a heavenly inheritance, who were not found in the rest of the world, except that a few proselytes came to them. In this adoption they served, for the time of the world, under the elements; yet a promise was made that at some time they would enjoy the rights of sons in fuller measure. In the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," there they will be called "sons of the living God" (Rom. 9:26). That will be when God, in the fullness of time, sends his Son, etc., to redeem those under the Law, that we might receive sonship (Gal. 4:4–5). Now the Spirit of adoption works this, pre-eminently and emphatically, and in a mature rather than a childish and servile age of such persons; which is fitting, since it is done or effected in them while they are freed from servile condition and are regarded as adopted by God as sons. To this belong the knowledge of all the mysteries of the intellect, wisdom and prudence, faith in the passion and glorification of Christ, boldness [παρρησία], expectation [ἀπεκδοχή] ... confidence, access in assurance, a better hope, through which, almost without priest, altar, victim, tabernacle, or typical purifications, we draw near to God (Heb. 4:16; 7:19; 10:34).

units.la: XLVI. Hoc adoptionis Spiritu pollentes Deum Abba, Patrem compellant, Rom.VIII.15. secus quàm olim servi Hebraei לא קורא אבותם non vocantes vel adscitentes sibi Abba, Patrem, perinde ut liberi patrem sibi adsicere poterant. De quo Loc, XVI, §.56. diximus. Erat etiam Ve-
units.tr: XLVI. Possessing this Spirit of adoption, they address God as Abba, Father (Rom. 8:15). This is unlike the Hebrew servants of old, who did not call or claim Abba [לא קורא אבותם] as their father, although free men could claim a father for themselves. Concerning this we spoke in Chapter XVI, §56.

units.la: teribus Deus Pater, sicut illi Filii, Deum etiam Patrem suum nuncupantes, Deut.XXXII.6. Esaj.LXIII.16. Jer.III.19. Mal.1.6. Erat Pater, sed qui eos ἄχεα ... ad definitum à Patre tempus subjecit paedagogis, qui de Patris bonitate & haereditate expectanda aliquid pueris dicebant, bona Patris procul ostentabant: Regnum & Regni gloriam promittebant; interim eosdem crepundiis, elementis mundi distringebant, & intendere pignori haereditatis, figuris veritatis jubebant. Ita Deum nec merum Patrem, nec merum Dominum ciebant. Nam peccabant etiam, qui Deum considerabant non ut ullo modo patrem, sed ut merum Dominum, qui ad mercedem vocaret sub conditione operis, & ei dicebant בעלי Baali, Hos.II.16. Pater erat, quia eos genuit, & patris affectu, ad tempus licet occultato nonnihil, dilexit. Dominus, quia paedagogis eos subjiciens ad tempus servilitèr habuit. At ubi Christus consummatus & glorificatus est, non amplius Deus fideles paedagogis subjicit. Veniente fide non amplius estis sub paedagogo. Omnes enim filii Dei estis per Iesum Christum. Gal.III.25.26. Ipsam nunc imaginem rerum, Hebr.X.1. intuemur in Christo, qui mortuus est, & resurrexit, & ascendit in Coelum, & nos fecit Sacerdotes & Reges, Apoc.I.6.V.10. 1.Pet.II.9. Sacerdotes, ut in Christo proxime, sine ullo velo interjecto, accedamus, & per fidem Deo offeramus sanguinem ipsius; tanquam nostrum; Reges, ut à nemine amplius in servitutem redigamur, & omnia, etiam haereditas mundi, nostra sint. Non prius, quàm Christus glorificatus est, Spiritus S. animum credentium laetitia & amore perfecto implere potuit, evincendo, omnia ad justitiam & salutem patrandam necessaria facta & consummata esse. Hoc enim, quia per Evangelium fit, & Spiritus, ut Evangelio credamus, efficit, in eo utique clamamus Abba, Pater. Credere enim Evangelio est affirmare & obsignare, quod Deus sit verax, Joh.III.33, hoc est, quòd nobis factus sit in Deum, nos per sanguinem Filii sui & Spiritum suum, ut Regni sui participes simus, regeneraverit; Christo nos conjunxerit & inseruerit, ut in eo justi & haeredes simus: quòd nos cum ipso vivificaverit, resuscitaverit, & in supracoelestibus collocaverit; Denique nobis in Christo Pater consummatus factus sit.
units.tr: To the ancients God was also Father, just as they were sons, and they called God their Father too (Deut. 32:6; Isa. 63:16; Jer. 3:19; Mal. 1:6). He was Father, but he subjected them, for a time fixed by the Father, to tutors, who spoke to the children of the Father's goodness and of the inheritance to be expected, and showed the goods of the Father only from a distance; they promised the kingdom and the glory of the kingdom, yet meanwhile held them bound to trinkets and the elements of the world, and ordered them to attend to the pledge of the inheritance and to the figures of the truth. Thus they called God neither merely Father nor merely Lord. For they also erred who regarded God not as Father in any way, but only as Lord, who called them to a reward under the condition of works, and called him "my Baal" (Hos. 2:16). He was Father because he begot them and loved them with a father's affection, though for a time it was somewhat hidden; he was Lord because, subjecting them to tutors for a time, he held them in servitude. But when Christ was consummated and glorified, God no longer subjects believers to tutors. Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor. For you are all sons of God through Jesus Christ (Gal. 3:25–26). Now we look upon the very image of things, in Christ, who died, rose again, and ascended into heaven, and has made us priests and kings (Rev. 1:6; 5:10; 1 Pet. 2:9). We are priests, so that in Christ, with no veil interposed, we may draw near and offer to God his blood through faith as our own; we are kings, so that we may no longer be reduced to servitude by anyone, and so that all things, even the inheritance of the world, may be ours. Not until Christ was glorified could the Holy Spirit fill the minds of believers with joy and perfect love, by showing that all things necessary for accomplishing righteousness and salvation have been made and completed. For since this happens through the Gospel, and the Spirit brings it about that we believe the Gospel, in it we surely cry, "Abba, Father." For to believe the Gospel is to affirm and seal that God is true (John 3:33); that is, that he has become our God, has regenerated us through the blood of his Son and his Spirit so that we may be partakers of his kingdom, has joined and grafted us to Christ so that in him we may be righteous and heirs, has quickened us together with him, raised us up, and seated us in the heavenly places; and finally, that in Christ the Father has become fully ours.

units.la: XLVII. Proxima Spiritus Adoptionis operatio est Revelatio plenior & Sapientia fidelium N.T. multis parasangis Sapientiam Veterum superans. Nam Spiritus S. est Spiritus sapientiae & prudentiae, consilii & fortitudinis, Spiritus cognitionis & timoris Jehovae, Esaj.XI.2. Sicut ergo Spiritus S. sub N.T. ampliore mensura donatur, ita etiam tum revelatio ipsa, tum revelationis cognitio, quam Spiritus S. in fidelibus operatur, longè sub Evangelio, quàm ante illud, amplior & exuberantior est. Quoad Revelationem enim, nunc ἡμέρᾳ dies est, Rom.XIII.12. בקר mane, Esaj.XXI.12. Sicut lux mane, cum exortus est Sol, mane, inquam, absque nubibus. 2.Sam. XXIII.4. Et par cognitionis ratio est. De utraque clarissimae praedictiones extant. Plena erit terra cognitione Jehovae, ut aquis mare operientibus, Esaj.XI.9. Propterea cognoscet populus שמי Nomen meum in die illo; quod ego, qui loquebar, ecce ad-
units.tr: XLVII. The next work of the Spirit of adoption is a fuller revelation and the wisdom of the faithful under the New Testament, which surpasses the wisdom of the Ancients by many parasangs. For the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Jehovah (Isa. XI.2). Just as the Holy Spirit is given under the New Testament in a larger measure, so also both the revelation itself and the knowledge of it which the Spirit works in the faithful are far fuller and more abundant under the Gospel than before it. As to revelation, it is now "day" [ἡμέρα] (Rom. XIII.12), "morning" [בקר] (Isa. XXI.12), like the light of morning once the sun has risen, morning, I say, without clouds (2 Sam. XXIII.4). The case of knowledge is the same. Most clear predictions of both exist: "The earth shall be full of the knowledge of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea" (Isa. XI.9). "Therefore my people shall know my name in that day; that I who spoke, behold, I am here" (...

units.la: Ejusdem Spiritus Promissionis operatio est Revelatio plenior, eximia sapientia fidelium sub N.T. quae jam olim praedicta & promissa. ce adsum, ibid.LII.6. Ponam כרכר שמשתיך Cadcod, seu gemmam pellucidam speculapия tua (clarissimam lucem vobis impertiar) & portas tuas in lapidem carbunculi; (Christus,qui porta,via est, Joh.X.9. XIV.6. vobis erit lux & amor) Et omnes filii tui (nullo discrimine doctorum & discipulorum) erunt לומדי יהוה discipuli Jehovæ, (non amplius hominum,sed Jehovæ, qui verbo & Spiritu suo vos intus docebit & potenter illuminabit, ut Deo credatis, & ad veram sapientiam proficiatis,) Esaj.LIV.12.13. Non exister amplius puer diebus, & senex, qui non impleat dies suos,sed puer centenarius morietur, & peccator centum annos maledicetur. q. d. sufficientia omnibus & singulis erunt discendi & proficiendi media, cum vel puer tantum cogniturus sit,quantum alius, qui centum annos vixit; & nemo etiam peccator, moriturus sit, quin occasionem habeat id statim & parvo labore discendi, quod aliàs centum annis non fuisset cognitum, ibid. LXV.20. Surge, luce,quia venit lux tua,& gloria Domini super te exorta est. Ambulabunt gentes ad lucem tuam,& Reges ad splendorem tuum, ibid. LX.1.3. Proin etiam Animalia illa quatuor, Ecclesiæ N. T. figuræ, עינים סביב מלאת γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν plena oculis a parte anteriore & posteriore, Ezech.I.18. Apoc. IV.6. repræsentantur. Nam etiam inter Bona N.T. eximia illud refertur: Non docebunt amplius quisquam proximum suum, & quisquam fratrem suum,dicendo, Cognoscite Jehovam. Nam ipsi cognoscent me,non minus parvus ipsorum,quam magnus ipsorum,ait Jehova, Jer.XXXI.34. Absconde verba illa, & obsigna librum usque ad tempus finis, quo multi scrutabuntur, & cognitio multiplicabitur, Dan.XII.4. Et erit dies unus, ille noscetur Jehovâ,non dies, & non nox. Et erit, tempore vespere erit lux,Zach.XIV.7.
units.tr: The same Spirit of promise works a fuller revelation, the eminent wisdom of the faithful under the New Testament, which was foretold and promised long ago: "...I am here" (ibid. LII.6). "I will make your pinnacles [כרכר שמשתיך, Cadcod] of pellucid gem, a clear mirror (I will bestow on you the brightest light), and your gates of carbuncle stone" (Christ, who is the gate and the way, John X.9, XIV.6, will be light and love to you). "And all your sons" (without distinction between teachers and disciples) "shall be disciples of Jehovah" [לומדי יהוה] (not of men any longer, but of Jehovah, who will teach you inwardly by his Word and Spirit and mightily enlighten you, so that you believe God and advance to true wisdom) (Isa. LIV.12–13). "There shall no longer be an infant of days, nor an old man who does not fill his days, for the child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner, being a hundred years old, shall be accursed." That is to say, there will be sufficient means of learning and advancing for all and each, so that even a child will learn as much as another who lived a hundred years, and no sinner, however near death, will lack the opportunity to learn in a short time and with little labour what otherwise would not have been known in a hundred years (ibid. LXV.20). "Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. The nations shall walk by your light and kings by the brightness of your rising" (ibid. LX.1, 3). Therefore also those four living creatures, figures of the Church of the New Testament, "full of eyes before and behind" [עינים סביב מלאת / γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν], are set forth (Ezek. I.18; Rev. IV.6). For among the excellent blessings of the New Testament this also is reckoned: "They shall no longer teach each one his neighbour, or each his brother, saying, Know Jehovah; for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says Jehovah" (Jer. XXXI.34). "Shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end, when many shall search and knowledge shall be increased" (Dan. XII.4). "And there shall be one day, which shall be known to Jehovah, neither day nor night; but at evening time there shall be light" (Zech. XIV.7).

units.la: XLVIII.
units.tr: XLVIII.

units.la: Fata sic prædicta viam invenerunt. Nam ante omnia Christus evangelizans occultata hactenus, & in thesauris Sapientiæ Dei recondita,apertam in lucem protulit. Aperuit ille os suum in parabolis, scaturiginis instar effudit חידות מני קדם κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου abscondita ab origine mundi,Psal LXXVIII.2. Matth.XIII.35. Evangelium & præconium Christi factum est secundum revelationem mysterii (magni illius pietatis, I.Tim.III.16.) temporibus saecularibus taciti,nunc vero manifestati, & per Scripturas Propheticas secundum præceptum Dei æterni, ad obedientiam fidei,in omnes gentes notificati, Rom.XVI.25-26. Ideo Christus gratias Domino Cœli & terræ agit, quòd hæc occultavit à sapientibus & intelligentibus, & revelavit νηπίοις pueris, Matth.XI.25. Non adhuc dico vos servos, quia servus non novit,quid faciat suus Dominus. Vos autem dixi amicos, quia omnia (totum decretum de salute, justitia, Regno) quæ audivi à Patre meo, vobis notificavi,Joh.XV.15.q.d.Non amplius illud tempus est, ut filius hæres nihil amplius à servo differt,Gal.IV.1.2. Jam pueritiæ spatia finita sunt; pædagogi cessant, quando fides venit, ibid.III.25. Olim magna in hæredibus pueris inscitia erat. Multa ignorabant, quæ non audiebant à doctoribus dici: quædam nondum patefacta erant. Servile est,non scire omnia, quæ herus facit, amicorum scire. At vos non amplius servi estis,sed filii,amici estis,admissionis intimæ,quibus arcana cordis reserari, & in sinum deponi
units.tr: The predicted fates found their way. For first of all Christ, preaching the Gospel, brought into the open light what had hitherto been hidden and laid up in the treasuries of the wisdom of God. He opened his mouth in parables and poured them out like a spring: "riddles of old" [חידות מני קדם], "things hidden from the foundation of the world" [κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου] (Ps. LXXVIII.2; Matt. XIII.35). The Gospel and the proclamation of Christ was made according to the revelation of the mystery (of that great godliness, 1 Tim. III.16), kept silent through the ages of the world but now made manifest, and through the prophetic Scriptures, according to the command of the eternal God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith (Rom. XVI.25–26). Therefore Christ gives thanks to the Lord of heaven and earth that he hid these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to babes [νηπίοις] (Matt. XI.25). "I no longer call you servants, for a servant does not know what his lord does; but I have called you friends, for all things (the whole decree concerning salvation, righteousness and the kingdom) that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you" (John XV.15). That is to say: this is no longer the time when the heir differs nothing from a servant (Gal. IV.1–2). Now the years of childhood are finished, and the tutors cease, since faith has come (ibid. III.25). Formerly there was great ignorance among the child-heirs. They knew many things they had not heard from teachers, and some things had not yet been disclosed. It is servile not to know everything that the master does; but you are no longer servants, but sons and friends, admitted to intimacy, to whom the secrets of the heart are unlocked and entrusted to the bosom.

units.la: solent. Tanquam fratres sedebitis unâ coram Deo Patre meo & vestro,& me Domino & Præceptore vestro, Psal.CXXXIII.1. non servi,sed liberti, I.Cor.VII.22. imo filii, Gal.IV.7. In oratione sua sacerdotali: Ἐγνώρισα, inquit, ἀνθρώποις τὸ ὄνομά σε ,notum iis feci Nomen tuum,Joh.XVII.26. q. d. Et verbis & factis, obedientia inprimis mea usque ad mortem effeci, ut cognoscerent mei,te esse Jehovam, Deum Abrahami, misericordem & gratiosum,qui non utatur ἀθωώσει, nocentem non absolvat,Exod.XXXIV.6.7. In Christo enim demum Lex Dei vera est. Novum mandatum scribo vobis ὃ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ἐν αὐτῷ quod verum est in ipso, I.Joh.II.8. Nomen illud Dei sunt cùm omnes virtutes,quas Deus Mosi patefecit, Exod.XXXIV.7: tum inprimis justitia & misericordia à Christo, quà Propheta declaratione Legis, patefactione voluntatis Dei universæ, obedientiæ, exemplo, demonstratione missionis suæ ad expiationem peccati & salutem, & ostensione unici medii apprehendendæ salutis; quod fides est: quà Sacerdote obedientia mortis, quà Rege victoria mortis, ascensione in Cœlum & sessione ad dextram Dei,illustrata. Est enim Christus imago Dei invisibilis, Col.I.15. quia cùm sit unum cum Patre, consequens est, ut in demonstratione virtutum Filii, & voluntatis ejus, manifestandi Dei justitiam & misericordiam, voluntas Patris certissimè & plenissimè cognosceretur, cùm una sit utriusque voluntas; nec fieri possit, ut Filius à se ipso quicquam dicat vel faciat,Joh.V.19.20.In hac revelatione explicatio ænigmatum à seculo consistit; Psal.LXXVIII.2. Indicatio Salutis & revelatio justitiæ Dei coram omnibus gentibus, Psal.XCVIII.2. γνωρισμὸς πολυποικίλης σοφίας notificatio multifariæ sapientiæ Dei, Ephes.III.10. thesaurorum in Christo abscondidorum referatio,Col.II.3.adeò ut qui Christum didicerit, ad omnes divitias certitudinis intelligentiæ, ad cognitionem mysterii Dei & Patris & Christi pervenerit,ibid.v.2. Accedit Paracletus Filii.Spiritus S.qui ab eodem missus fideles omnia docere debuit, Joh.XIV.26. Est enim Spiritus σοφίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως Sapientiæ & Revelationis, qui illuminat oculos mentis ad cognoscendum, quæ spes vocationis nostræ sit,Ephes.I.17. 18.Ille effusus fecit prophetare filios & filias, Joel. II.28.& nôsse omnia,I.Joh.II.20.
units.tr: "As brothers you shall sit together before God, my Father and yours, and me, your Lord and Teacher" (Ps. CXXXIII.1). Not servants but freedmen (1 Cor. VII.22), indeed sons (Gal. IV.7). In his priestly prayer he says: "I made known to men your name" [Ἐγνώρισα ... ἀνθρώποις τὸ ὄνομά σου] (John XVII.26). That is to say: both by word and by deed, chiefly by my obedience even to death, I have caused those who are mine to know that you are Jehovah, the God of Abraham, merciful and gracious, who does not acquit [ἀθωώσει] and does not absolve the guilty (Exod. XXXIV.6–7). For in Christ at last the Law of God is true. "I write to you a new commandment, which is true in him" [ὃ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ἐν αὐτῷ] (1 John II.8). That name of God consists of all the virtues that God revealed to Moses (Exod. XXXIV.7); above all, justice and mercy, made known by Christ: as Prophet, by the declaration of the Law, by the disclosure of the whole will of God for obedience, by example, by showing the purpose of his mission for the expiation of sin and salvation, and by pointing out the sole means of laying hold of salvation, which is faith; as Priest, by the obedience of his death; as King, by victory over death, illustrated by his ascension into heaven and his sitting at the right hand of God. For Christ is "the image of the invisible God" (Col. I.15), because, since he is one with the Father, it follows that in the display of the virtues of the Son and of his will, by which the justice and mercy of God are manifested, the will of the Father is known most certainly and most fully, since the will of both is one; nor can it happen that the Son says or does anything of himself (John V.19–20). In this revelation the explanation of the enigmas, which has stood from the beginning of the age (Ps. LXXVIII.2), consists; the indication of salvation and the revelation of God's righteousness before all the nations (Ps. XCVIII.2); the "making known" [γνωρισμὸς] of the "manifold wisdom" [πολυποικίλης σοφίας] of God (Eph. III.10); the unfolding of the treasures hidden in Christ (Col. II.3), so that whoever has learned Christ attains to all the riches of the assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ (ibid. II.2). To this is added the Paraclete of the Son, the Holy Spirit, who was sent by him to teach the faithful all things (John XIV.26). For he is the Spirit of wisdom and revelation [σοφίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως], who enlightens the eyes of the mind to know what is the hope of our calling (Eph. I.17–18). Poured out, he made sons and daughters prophesy (Joel II.28) and know all things (1 John II.20).

units.la: XLIX. Commemorabilis hæc Novi Testamenti supra Vetus præcellentia est. In Veteri umbræ & figuræ rerum futurarum dominabantur. In Novo Corpus Christi, Col.II.17. & εἰκών τῶν πραγμάτων imago rerum,Hebr.X.1. obtinet. Ibi sapientia plena velata: hic revelata & & consummata est. Ibi erat κάλυμμα velamen simile illi, quod Mosis faciei circumpositum erat, ne ejus gloriam oculis inconnivis intuerentur: Hic in Christo illud amovetur,tollitur. Unde facie revelata gloriam Domini (virtutes Dei, & admirabilem misericordiam, per quam Deus peccatorem justificat) καταπτιζόμενοι velut in speculo contemplantes (nullo medio, velut ad expiationem peccati necessario, nullo magistro, legislatore, brabeuta,nullo verbo,interprete authentico,præter Deum, interposito) ad eandem imaginem transformamur à gloria in gloriam, (renovatione nostra magis magisque procedente, donec ad imaginem Christi perveniamus, & Christi gloria spiritualis, illam Mosis gloriam carnalem oculis corpo-
units.tr: XLIX. This pre-eminence of the New Testament over the Old is worth remembering. In the Old, shadows and figures of things to come held sway. In the New, "the body of Christ" (Col. II.17) and "the image of the things" [εἰκὼν τῶν πραγμάτων] (Heb. X.1) prevails. There the wisdom was full but veiled; here it is revealed and perfected. There was a "veil" [κάλυμμα], like that which lay upon the face of Moses, lest the children of Israel should look steadfastly on his glory; here in Christ this is removed and taken away. Hence, with the face unveiled, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord (the virtues of God and his wonderful mercy, by which God justifies the sinner) [καταπτιζόμενοι], with no intermediary (such as would be necessary for the expiation of sin), no teacher, lawgiver or arbiter, no word, authentic interpreter, standing between us and God, we are transformed into the same image from glory to glory (our renewal proceeding more and more until we attain the image of Christ, and the spiritual glory of Christ is that carnal glory of Moses that...

units.la: Et per Christum Mysteria Regni Coelorum recludentem praestita est.
units.tr: And it has been bestowed through Christ, who unlocks the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Comparatio quoad bonum ipsum Veteris & Novi Testamenti. corporalibus conspicabilem, multis parasangis superans, in nobis splendescat,) 2.Cor.III.13-18. Ibi nondum Jehova in Deum populo suo factus, secundum nomen & virtutes suas plenè cognosci non potuit. Hic in Christo in carne manifestato in Deum factus, secundum nomen & virtutes suas, misericordiam inprimis & justitiam plenissimè, quantum in vita hac fieri pote, cognoscitur. Pater justè, mundus (Judæi & gentes execcatæ) te (ex luce conscientiæ, operibus, beneficiis, judiciis, verbo toties repetito & inculcato) non cognovit. Ego verò te cognovi, (namavi, glorificavi, voluntatem tuam implevi; & ideo) hi (quoque) cognoverunt, quod tu misteris me (in mundum, ad salvandos homines) & notum feci iis Nomen tuum, (effeci verbis & factis, ut Nomen tuum, Exod.XXXIV.6.7. declamatum penitus cognoscerent) & notum faciam (tum iis, quibus jam notum feci ad notitiam uberiorem, ne unquam nominis mei oblivisceantur, tum iis, quibus nondum notum feci, & quos mihi, ut Te iis manifestarem, dedisti) Joh.XVII.25.26. Ibi à notitia veri Dei exclusi sunt tum Israelitæ carnales, carne circumcisi, at corde præputiati, quibus Deus non dedit cor ad cognoscendum, Deut. XXIX.4. quorum cordi velum Mosis incubuit, 2.Cor.III.15. tum gentes. Hic omnes cognoscunt à minimo usque ad maximum, Jer.XXXI.34. Non enim amplius est διαστολὴ distinctio, Rom.III.22. An Judæorum tantùm Deus est? Annon etiam gentium? Utique & gentium, ibid.v.29. Non est distinctio Judæi & Græci. Idem enim est Deus omnium, dives erga omnes, qui eum invocant, ibid X.12. In Christo Jesu nihil circumcisio, vel præputium valet, sed fides per charitatem operans, Gal.V.6. Neque alii nunc Christi nescii & expertes sunt, quàm σοφοὶ καὶ συνετοὶ sapientes & intelligentes (qui fiducia propriæ sapientiæ & intelligentiæ inflati, se Deo erudiendos non committunt, Matth.XI.25. quorum infidelium mentes Deus hujus seculi excæcavit, ut iis non illucescat splendor Evangelii gloriæ Christi, 2.Cor.IV.4. Ibi docebat quisque proximum suum, dicendo: Cognoscite me. Quia enim, quæ Deus de se cognosci, credi & expectari voluit ad gloriam suam, in ænigmatibus abscondita erant, opus erat unum alteri dicere: Cognosce Jehovam; hoc est, ei ænigmata & figuras involutas evolvere. Id ipse Moses εἰς μαρτύριον ἐαν τῷ λαλημένων in testimonium eorum, quæ dicenda erant, Hebr.III.5. & post Mosen, aliis licet verbis, alio stylo & methodo; manente in verbis Mosis doctrinæ radice & canone; Prophetæ, quin & Christus, Propheta maximus omnium, eique suffragantes Apostoli; cùmòti illi tum prænuntii futurorum, tum præsentium monitores, & rudium doctores præstiterunt, authoritate principali ipsius Dei usi, sic præfantes: Sic dicit, Dominus Zebaoth, Israelis, Jerem.XLIV.2. Ezech.XX.5. Jer.XXXI.1. Esaj.I.11. Hos.I.1. 2.&c. Et quia nondum omnia verba dicta erant, expectandus erat Propheta Mosi similis, qui verba Dei omnia perfectè loqueretur. Hic utrumque, & ænigmatum enodatio atque penjiculatio, & Prophetæ talis expectatio cessat. Nam non docebit amplius quisquam proximum suum, &c. Omnes enim ipsi cognoscent me, à minimo usque ad maximum, Jer.XXXI.34. Postquam enim omnia verba Dei per Christum & Apostolos ejus palam dicta sunt, & Christus scatebrae
units.tr: Comparison as to the good itself of the Old and New Testaments. (2 Cor. 3:13-18.) It shines within us, surpassing by many parasangs the glory that was visible to the bodily eyes. There, Jehovah had not yet become God to his people, so his name and powers could not be fully known. Here, in Christ made manifest in the flesh, God has become God, and his name and powers, above all his mercy and justice, are known as fully as is possible in this life. Righteous Father, the world (the blind Jews and Gentiles) did not know you, though you showed yourself by the light of conscience, by works, benefits, and judgments, and by the word so often repeated and inculcated. But I have known you, (I have loved you, glorified you, and fulfilled your will), and therefore these (also) have known that you sent me into the world to save men, and I have made known to them your name (by my words and deeds I have made your name, Exod. 34:6-7, thoroughly known to them), and I will make it known (both to those to whom I have already made it known, for a fuller knowledge, that they may never forget my name, and to those to whom I have not yet made it known, and whom you have given me so that I may reveal you to them). John 17:25-26. There, both the carnal Israelites, circumcised in the flesh but uncircumcised in heart, to whom God has not given a heart to know (Deut. 29:4), and the Gentiles, were shut out from the knowledge of the true God. Over their heart the veil of Moses lay (2 Cor. 3:15). Here all know me, from the least to the greatest (Jer. 31:34). For there is no longer any distinction (Rom. 3:22). Is God the God of the Jews only? Is he not also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also (ibid. v. 29). There is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, rich to all who call upon him (ibid. 10:12). In Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but faith working through love (Gal. 5:6). Nor are those now ignorant of Christ and without experience of him other than the wise and understanding (who, puffed up with confidence in their own wisdom and understanding, do not entrust themselves to be taught by God, Matt. 11:25), whose unbelieving minds the god of this age has blinded, so that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ does not shine on them (2 Cor. 4:4). There, each one taught his neighbour, saying: Know me. For since the things God wished to be known, believed, and expected of him for his glory were hidden in riddles, it was necessary for one to say to another: Know Jehovah; that is, to unfold the riddles and wrapped-up figures. Moses himself did this for a testimony of the things that were to be spoken (Heb. 3:5), and after Moses, the prophets, and Christ himself, the greatest of all prophets, and the apostles who supported him, did so in other words, in another style and method, the root and rule of Moses' doctrine remaining in his words. Those men, using the principal authority of God himself and speaking thus, Thus says the Lord of hosts, God of Israel (Jer. 44:2; Ezek. 20:5; Jer. 31:1; Isa. 1:11; Hos. 1:1-2, etc.), served both as forecasters of future things, as monitors of present things, and as teachers of the untaught. And because not all the words had yet been spoken, a prophet like Moses had to be awaited, who would speak all the words of God perfectly. Here both the unfolding and interpretation of riddles, and that expectation of such a prophet, cease. For no one shall teach his neighbour any more, etc. For they shall all know me, from the least to the greatest (Jer. 31:34). For once all the words of God have been openly spoken through Christ and his apostles, and Christ has poured out, as a fountain,

units.la: more effudit ænigmata ab antiquo, Psal.LXXVIII.2. quin & Johannes canonem verborum Dei clausit his verbis: Si quis addiderit verbis Prophetiæ hujus, addet super eum Deus plagas, Apoc.XXII.18. non opus est homine alio, qui demum ænigmata extricet, involutas notiones evolvat, & nucleum eruat; cùm is nucleus, qui fundamentum fidei est, omnibus & parvis (pueris in Christo 1.Cor.III.1.) & magnis (adultis, perfectis, in quibus verbū crucis est sapientia, ibid.II.6. notus sit, neque ultra expectandus sit, qui quid hactenus indictum dicat. Quia enim Lex omnibus publicata cordi inscribitur; nihil à quoquam ad fidem dici potest, quod non per verba omnibus prædicata doceatur is; qui in cognitione Dei proficit. Minimus in Regno Cœlorum nunc major Prophetis est, Matth.XI.11. Tametsi ergo nunquam Ecclesiæ defuturi sunt διδάσκαλοι doctores, Ephes.IV.11. potentes in doctrina sana, Tit.I.9. laborantes ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ in verbo & doctrina, I.Tim.IV.17. tamen novis Prophetis, Apostolis; Doctoribus, qui revelationem augeant, non dictum & non revelatum antehac dicant, vel revelent, Prophetiam multiplicent; opus non est. Hac fiducia Johannes dicit, eos, qui in Filium credunt, & habere unctionem à Sancto; quæ ipsos de omnibus docet, & novisse omnia, 1. Epist.II.20. Non tantum enim verbum, quod principium fidei est, perfectum tenent, sed etiam ejusdem mentem non aliunde, quàm ex eodem verbo, & per eandem unctionem discunt; & clavim, quæ iis ad omnia mysteria no cenda aditum facit, habent. Et potuit olim clavis illa γνώσεως cognitionis occultari; & occultata non semel est ab illis, quorum erat illa uti; & mysteria referare. Væ vobis Legis peritis, quia sustulistis clavim cognitionis; Vos non intratis, & intrare volentes prohibuistis, Luc.XI.52. Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi hypocritæ, quia κλείετε claudetis Regnum Cœlorum, &c. Matth.XXIII.13. Nunc verò clavi cognitionis in publico posita, quæ occultari amplius nequit, non adimus montem vel Sionis, vel Tarpejum, vel alium, ut inde ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν à quoquam νομοθέτη velut privilegium absque errore interpretandi habente, petamus. Ibi necesse erat, ut in Cathedra Mosis sederent Doctores, qui ingeminarent identidem אֵת יְהוָה Cognoscite Dominum, Jer.XXXI.34. Populus enim puer erat durae cervicis; paedagogi metu coercendus. Hic non pueri, sed filii cùm simus, talibus non indigemus. Spiritus Filiationis, Doctor & Paracletus, Joh.XIV.26. מוֹרֶה Index noster, Zach.IX.12. est.
units.tr: riddles of old in the manner of a spring (Ps. 78:2), and John himself closed the canon of God's words with these words: If anyone adds to the words of this prophecy, God will add to him the plagues (Rev. 22:18), there is no need for another man who would at last disentangle riddles, unfold wrapped-up notions, and bring out the kernel. For that kernel, which is the foundation of faith, is known both to the little ones (babes in Christ, 1 Cor. 3:1) and to the great (the adults, the perfect, among whom the word of the cross is wisdom, 1 Cor. 2:6), and no one is to be awaited any longer to say anything new. For since the Law is published to all and written on the heart, nothing can be said by anyone as a matter of faith that is not taught by words proclaimed to all who make progress in the knowledge of God. The least in the kingdom of heaven is now greater than the prophets (Matt. 11:11). Although, therefore, there will never be lacking teachers in the Church (Eph. 4:11), able in sound doctrine (Titus 1:9), labouring in word and doctrine (1 Tim. 4:17), yet there is no need for new prophets, apostles, or teachers to speak what has not been spoken or revealed before, or to reveal it, and so multiply prophecy. With this confidence John says that those who believe in the Son have an anointing from the Holy One, which teaches them about all things, and they know all things (1 John 2:20). For they hold not only the Word, which is the beginning of faith, perfectly, but they also learn its meaning from nothing other than the same Word and through the same anointing, and they have the key which gives them access to unlock all mysteries. And that key of knowledge could once be hidden, and was hidden more than once by those whose office it was to use it and open the mysteries. Woe to you lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter, and you hindered those who wished to enter (Luke 11:52). Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you shut the kingdom of heaven, etc. (Matt. 23:13). But now the key of knowledge is set out in public, and can no longer be hidden; we need not climb Mount Sion, or the Tarpeian rock, or some other mountain, to seek from anyone who claims to be a lawgiver, as if he had the privilege of interpreting without error, his own explanation. There it was necessary for teachers to sit in the chair of Moses and repeatedly urge Know the Lord (Jer. 31:34), for the people were a child with a hard neck, to be restrained by fear of the tutor. Here, since we are not children but sons, we have no need of such things. The Spirit of adoption is Teacher and Paraclete (John 14:26), our Guide (Zech. 9:12).

units.la: L. Sapientiæ hujus exuberantioris comes σοφίας τέρπος Fiducia, Dilectio & Sanctitas est. Spiritus enim ei sicut cognitionis, ita etiam timoris Dei Spiritus est, Esaj.XI.2. Quò enim notitia Dei amplior, hoc ejusdem amor, timor, & erga eum fiducia intensior est. Sicut ignoti nulla cupido est: ita rei bonæ notissimæ cupido omnium maxima est. Et cognoscere quidem Dominum Jer. XXXI.34. non tantum est ejus Nomen compertum & exploratum habere; sed etiam eum respicere, intueri, ante oculos habere, quod est in eum credere, ei confidere, eum quærere, revereri & amare. Facit huc promissio: Do Legem meam in medio ipsorum, & super corde eorum inscribam eam, ibid. v.33. Deus inscribens Legem fidei & justitiæ in cor id efficit, ut fœderati eam liben-
units.tr: L. The companion of this more abundant wisdom is the sweetness of wisdom: confidence, love, and holiness. For the Spirit is, as he is of knowledge, so also the Spirit of the fear of God (Isa. 11:2). For the fuller the knowledge of God, the more intense is the love of him, the fear of him, and confidence in him. As there is no desire for what is unknown, so the greatest of all desires is for a good thing that is best known. And to know the Lord (Jer. 31:34) is not merely to have his name learned and examined, but also to regard him, to look upon him, to keep him before one's eyes, which is to believe in him, to trust in him, to seek him, to revere him, and to love him. To this the promise applies: I will put my law in their midst, and write it on their heart (ibid. v. 33). God, by writing the law of faith and righteousness on the heart, brings it about that those in covenant willingly

units.la: ȷ libenter recipiant, ea impensè delectentur, ejus non obliviscantur amplius. Convenit promissio circumcidendi cordis, Deut. XXX. 6. Puta non tantum ab amore vanitatis & injustitiæ, à Regno peccati (quomodo & veterum credentium cor Deus circumcidit) sed etiam à conscientia peccati & reatus nondum expiati, & à servitute, reliquisque hujus effectibus amori perfecto Dei obstantibus. Et verbum quidem Legis ex Sina pronuntiatum, lapidibus insculptum fuit, 2. Cor. III. 7. Sed Lex hæc melior inscribitur [Greek] tabulis lapideis, sed [Greek] tabulis cordis carneis, ibid. 3. Scripsit Deus in lapidibus, docens se etiam scribere in cordibus. In lapidibus scribere haud obscurè lapideum cor Israeli exprobravit. Rumpens lapides, fœderis rupti significationem edidit. Jubens secundas tabulas sculpi, Exod. XXXIV. 1. innuit, experiri se velle, quantum ministerium mortis lapidibus insculptum apud peccatorem valeat. Exitus docuit, nihil omnino valuisse. Nemo enim Israelitarum ex mero Legis auditu salutem adeptus est. Nunc verò meliora obtinent: Inscriptio legis justitiæ & fidei non amplius in tabulis lapideis simul, & utcunque etiam in corde credentium; sed, abolito ministerio mortis, in tabulis cordis longè pretiosioribus solis, & quidem plenè, ad amorem & obedientiam merè filialem', cessante servitute omni ætatis puerilis. Nam pueri pædagogis subjecti minus quam filii ab iisdem soluti diligunt. Et planè amor & obedientia illa, sic à Spiritu S. in corde fœderatorum plantata, spontanea est, sicut populus ipse fœderatus [Hebrew] populus spontaneitatum est, Psal. CX. 3. perinde ac si non legibus jussa, sed charitate Dei nos diligentis extorta esset. Nam charitas Christi, morte ejus manifestata [Greek] constringit nos, 2. Cor. V. 14. & viva quædam veluti Lex loquensque est. Estque amor ille vehementissimus erga Soteratorem nostrum, Christum, per passiones consummatum, & Deum in Christo planissimè placatum vis illa, quæ Regno Cœlorum, quod [Greek] violenti rapturi-unt, infertur, Mat. XI. 12. Vis enim quædam est, subigere carnem, superare concupiscentiam, se ipsum & omnia, quæ in mundo sunt, abnegare. Sed vim hanc ultro, qui Christum diligunt, & Regni Cœlorum virtutes gustant, sibi inferunt. Demonstravit enim Deus [Greek] omni cognitione superiorem charitatem suam erga nos, (Ephes. III. 19.) mittendo Filium unigenitum, & tradendo eum morti pro nobis. Mittentem ergo Patrem, & Filium missum ardentissimo omnium amore completi decet. Denique præceptum Christi licèt vetus sit, & ab antiquo, quatenus promissio jam in Paradiso facta jam vim habuit præcepti, jubentis amare Deum tanquam justitiam nostram & Sanctificatorem nostrum, & Sathanam cum operibus ejus odio habere; pro quo præcepto nullum aliud novum substitui potest: tamen illud ipsum præceptum quadantenus [Greek] novum est, quatenus idem ille sermo antiquitus auditus [Greek] in Christo & nobis est, 1. Joh. II. 7. 8. Veritas enim promissionis in Christo & ab eo præstitæ & extantis, & ejusdem obedientia, velut novum quoddam vinculum, & novo quodam jure, potentius nos ad amorem Dei, & odium Diaboli obligat. Eàdemque verificatio promissionis in nobis per sanctificationem nostram ad fidem, quæ jam non tantùm promissioni, sed etiam [Greek] veritati habetur, fit nobis Lex Spiritus S. ad Deum enixissimè amandum & Sathanam perfectissimo odio habendum.
units.tr: receive it, delight in it greatly, and no longer forget it. The promise of circumcision of the heart (Deut. 30:6) agrees with this: that is, God circumcises the heart not only from the love of vanity and injustice, from the kingdom of sin (as he also circumcised the hearts of the believers of old), but also from the consciousness of sin and of guilt not yet expiated, and from slavery, and the other effects which stand in the way of perfect love of God. Indeed, the word of the Law, proclaimed from Sinai, was engraved on stones (2 Cor. 3:7). But this Law is written in a better way, not on tablets of stone, but on tablets of fleshly hearts (ibid. v. 3). God wrote on stones, teaching that he would also write on hearts. To write on stones was a clear reproach to Israel for having a stony heart. By breaking the stones he showed the meaning of a broken covenant. By commanding the second tablets to be carved (Exod. 34:1), he signified that he wished to test how much the ministry of death engraved on stones could prevail with a sinner. The outcome taught that it had no effect at all. For none of the Israelites obtained salvation from the bare hearing of the Law. But now they obtain better things: the writing of the law of righteousness and faith is no longer on tablets of stone, merely and in some fashion, even on the heart of believers; rather, with the ministry of death abolished, it is written on the tablets of the heart, far more precious, fully and solely, for a love and obedience that is purely filial, with all the servitude of childhood ceased. For children subject to tutors love less than sons freed from them. And that love and obedience, so planted by the Holy Spirit in the hearts of those in covenant, are plainly spontaneous, just as the covenant people themselves are a people of free will (Ps. 110:3), as if they were not commanded by laws, but drawn out by the charity of God who loves us. For the love of Christ, made manifest in his death, constrains us (2 Cor. 5:14), and is a kind of living law that speaks. And that most vehement love toward our Saviour Christ, consummated through his sufferings, and that force by which God, fully reconciled in Christ, is entered into the kingdom of heaven, which the violent take by force (Matt. 11:12), is that power. For there is a certain force in subduing the flesh, overcoming concupiscence, and denying oneself and all things that are in the world. Yet those who love Christ and taste the powers of the kingdom of heaven willingly apply this force to themselves. For God has shown his love toward us, a love surpassing all knowledge (Eph. 3:19), by sending his only-begotten Son and giving him up to death for us. It is fitting, therefore, that those who love the sending Father and the sent Son should be filled with the most ardent love of all. Finally, although the command of Christ is old and from the beginning, insofar as the promise made already in Paradise had the force of a command, bidding us love God as our righteousness and our Sanctifier, and hate Satan with his works, for which command no other new one can be substituted, yet that same command is in some respect new, insofar as that same word, heard of old, is true in Christ and in us (1 John 2:7-8). For the truth of the promise, in Christ and performed by him and standing in him, and his obedience, bind us more powerfully to the love of God and the hatred of the devil, as a kind of new bond and by a kind of new right. And the same verification of the promise in us, through our sanctification to faith, which is now held not only as a promise but as truth, becomes for us the law of the Holy Spirit, to love God most earnestly and to hate Satan with the most perfect hatred.

units.la: LI. Proximum hisce bonum Libertas Novi Testamenti est. Nam ubi Spiritus Domini (datus non ex mensura, filiationis, adeoque in emphasi) est, ibi [Greek] Libertas, 2. Cor. III. 17. quæ servituti opponitur. Triplex autem servitus est, una Peccati, altera Dei & justitiæ, ultima Legis. Libertas servituti primæ opposita omni tempore credentibus data est. Nam credere in Christum, & per fidem hanc in Christum justificari, & peccato velut dominanti servire, [Greek] sunt. Etiam Libertas servitudi Dei & justitiæ opposita peccati & Diaboli servitus, & non tam vera libertas, quàm licentia violandi legem Dei, nullis ullius temporis credentibus, sed solis Diaboli filiis competit. Nam liberati à peccato servi fiunt Dei, Rom. VI. 22. Cùm fuistis servi peccati, fuistis [Greek] liberi justitiæ, ibid. v. 20. Servire Deo, regnare est. Denique libertas legis servituti opposita bonum [Greek] Novi Testamenti est. Deus misit Filium, &c. ut adoptionem acciperemus. Quia verò estis filii, misit Spiritum Filii sui in corda vestra, &c. Itaque non amplius es servus, sed filius: si verò filius, etiam hæres Dei per Christum, Gal. IV. 47. Quod de certo servitutis genere intelligitur. Nam servi quidem Dei semper sumus: sed servi hominum & elementorum mundi fuerunt fideles ante Christum: non sunt amplius fideles post Christum, sub Evangelio: quia filii meri sunt, non amplius servorum similitudinem habent. Non enim Spiritum servitutis acceperunt rursus ad metum, sed Spiritum Filiationis, Rom. VIII. 15. Libertate igitur, qua Christus vos liberavit, state, & ne rursus jugo servitutis implicamini, Gal. V. 1. Si Filius vos liberos fecerit, revera liberi eritis, Joh. VIII. 36. puta non tantum à servitute peccati, sed ab ea etiam servitute, cui obnoxii quondam erant filii, quandiu in domo Patris versantes, & pædagogis subjecti, omnium licèt hæredes, parùm tamen à servis differebant. Hierosolyma quæ sursum est, (cœlestis, non terrestris, utpote succedens Sanctis non jam amplius in carne servientibus, sed in cœlum translatis, cum iis communionem status consummationis habens, & è cœlo descendens, Apoc. III. 12. XXI. 2. 10. pomoeriis justitiæ, libertatis & lætitiæ in terram usque porrectis) [Greek] libera est (ab accusatione, reatu peccati, servitute elementorum mundi, & dominatione vindicum Legis,) Gal. IV. 26.
units.tr: LI. The next good is the liberty of the New Testament. For where the Spirit of the Lord is (given not by measure, but in the spirit of sonship, and so in emphasis), there is [ἐλευθερία] liberty, 2 Cor. 3:17, which is opposed to slavery. There is a threefold slavery: the first is to sin, the second to God and righteousness, and the last to the Law. The liberty opposed to the first slavery has been given to believers at all times. For to believe in Christ, to be justified through faith in him, and to serve sin as its master, are [mutually exclusive] things. The slavery of sin and the Devil, which is opposed to the service of God and righteousness, is not true liberty but rather licence to violate the law of God; it belongs to no believers of any age, but only to the sons of the Devil. For those who have been freed from sin become servants of God, Rom. 6:22. When you were slaves of sin, you were [ἐλεύθεροι] free from righteousness, ibid. v. 20. To serve God is to reign. Finally, the liberty opposed to the slavery of the Law is a good [belonging to the] New Testament. God sent his Son, etc., that we might receive adoption. And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, etc. So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then also an heir of God through Christ, Gal. 4:47 [as printed]. This is understood of a certain kind of slavery. For we are indeed always servants of God, but the faithful before Christ were servants of men and of the elements of the world; after Christ, under the Gospel, the faithful are no longer such, because they are simply sons and no longer bear the likeness of servants. For they have not received again the spirit of slavery to fear, but the Spirit of sonship, Rom. 8:15. Stand firm, therefore, in the liberty with which Christ has made you free, and do not be entangled again in the yoke of slavery, Gal. 5:1. If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed, John 8:36; that is, free not only from the slavery of sin but also from that slavery to which the sons once were bound, as long as they lived in their Father's house and were subject to guardians; although they were all heirs, they differed little from slaves. The Jerusalem which is above (heavenly, not earthly, as it succeeds the saints who no longer serve in the flesh but have been translated into heaven, having with them a fellowship of the state of consummation, and descending from heaven, Rev. 3:12; 21:2, 10, with the boundaries of righteousness, liberty and joy extended even to the earth) is free (from accusation, the guilt of sin, the slavery of the elements of the world, and the dominion of the executors of the Law), Gal. 4:26.

units.la: LII. Tria enim in universum sunt, in quibus libertatis illius, fidelibus N. T. eximiæ [Greek] consistit; nimirum immunitas tum ab execratione Legis, & exorto inde timore mortis; tum à servitute Legis præceptorum in placitis, tum à dominatione vindicum Legis. Nam omnem illam veterum servitutem, omnemque ejus imaginem & speciem longissimè removet. Et Immunitas quidem ab execratione oratione Legis in eo consistit, quòd morte Christi effectum est, non tantùm, ne Lex peccati impediret sanctificationem, & immunitatem ab æterna execratione Seminis, quod etiam in hæredibus prioris temporis obtinuit, sed etiam, ne lex amplius irrogare posset iræ, à maledictione suppullulantis, quandam speciem. Quod demum morte Christi olim valuit. Nam prius quàm Sponsor moreretur, potuit peccatum, ejusque reatus adhuc dum extans, commemorari, accusari, & ad servitutem temporalem imputari: potuit chirographum postulari, praescribi. Quicunque ex operibus Legis sunt, sub execratione sunt. Scriptum enim est: Maledictus omnis, qui non manet in omnibus, quæ scripta sunt in libro Legis, ut faciat ea, Gal. III. 10. De quo plura Loc. XIII. 37. diximus; demonstrantes, quòd talia cum grano salis & œconomicè intelligenda sint. Postquam verò Christus, hæres omnium, mortem obiit, eum oportuit, ut Dominum, sibi vindicare, & sic in libertatem afferere redemptos suos, nec relinquere eos in conditione eorum, qui se tenentur accusare; sed potiùs eos in eam conditionem vindicare, ut pro redemptione & justificatione sua gratias Deo agere, & non amplius peccato accusanti, sed Domino vindicanti vivere possint. Christus nos emit, ut liberi essemus ab execratione Legis, dum pro nobis execratio factus est, ibid. v. 13. Immunitas hæc post se trahit liberationem à metu mortis temporalis, cui per omnem vitam obnoxii veteres fuerunt: & qui non ultima pars servitutis legalis fuit. Ut liberaret eos, qui per totum vitæ tempus timori mortis obnoxii erant, à servitute: vel, qui propter timorem mortis per omne vitæ tempus obnoxii erant servituti, Hebr. II. 15. Timenda ita mortis, non æternæ illius (à cujus timore promissio Dei omnes fœderatos semper liberavit & communivit) sed temporalis, causa fuit, quòd mors accelerata, & afflictiones hujus vitæ transgressoribus Legis sub facie & specie pœnæ propositæ sunt, atque adeò, quòd illæ præmio temporali, vitæ longævæ & benedictæ in possessione hæreditatis terræ Canaan, quam Lex cetį pignus & figuram cœlestis hæreditatis, fœderatis proponebat, non parùm adversarentur. Placuit enim Deo, nondum exhibita vera justitia in populo carnali ostendere, quid omnis doctrina, disciplina & temporalis retributio in hominibus carnalibus ad conversionem valeat; atque interim expectationem meliorum hisce terrestribus, tanquam in puericia Ecclesiæ solari & sustentare. Cùmque & afflictiones temporales, & mors ipsa non parùm terrestria hæc perturbaverint, eorum amittendorum metus, & addicta iisdem terrestribus servitus mirè eos per totam vitam exercuit. Ubi verò justitia exhibita, & per eandem conscientiæ absolutio data est, necesse erat velum, quod in externo sanctuario, & terra in secretam hæreditatem data erat, tolli. Sic timor afflictionum & mortis unà cum omni servitute legali cessavit, & ejusdem loco libertas filiorum Dei incessit. Cum qua cohæret immunitas à servitute Legis præceptorum in placitis, potissima Libertatis Evangelicæ species. Postquam enim fides venit non amplius sub lege, sed sub gratia sumus, Rom. VI. 14. Lex enim, quatenus subintravit domi-nio, pædagogico suo throno cedere, & gratiæ atque justitiæ infservire jussa est. Nos cùm essemus pueri, in servitutem redacti sumus elementorum mundi, &c. Nunc autem cognoscentes Deum, magis etiam à Deo cogniti, quomodo convertimini rursus ad infirma & egena elementa, &c? Gal IV. 3. 9. Delevit subscriptionem manus in placitis nobis subcontrariam, & eam sustulit ex medio, eam clavis affigens cruci, Col. II. 14. Ne quis igitur vos judicet in cibo aut potu, aut in parte festi, aut noviluniii, aut Sabbathorum; quæ sunt umbra futurorum, corpus autem Christi est, ib. v. 16. 17. Pro quo cultu carnali nunc merè spiritualis & rationalis Deo placet. Spiritus Deus est; & adorantes eum in Spiritu & veritate adorare oportet. Joh. IV. 24. Adhortor vos, fratres, per miserationes Dei, ut corpora vestra sistatis victimam vivam, sanctam, placentem Deo, rationalem cultum vestrum, Rom. XII. 1. Omnibus ergo placitis circa res medias sublatis, illarum usus ingenuæ charitatis & prudenti judicio scli nunc relinquitur. Si propter escam frater tuus tristitia afficitur, non amplius secundum charitatem ambulas. Ne esca tua illum perde, pro quo Christus mortuus est, ibid. XIV. 15. Nemo vos dijudicet in cibo & potu, vel in parte festi, vel neomeniæ, vel Sabbathorum, Col. II. 16. Connexa eidem libertati est immunitas & emancipatio è manu vindicum Legis Divinitus constitutorum. Cujusmodi olim fuerunt Ἐπίτροποι καὶ οἰκονόμοι Tutores & Curatores, nec non pædagogi, quibus Israelitæ in ætate infantili ad tempus correctionis usq; subjecti fuerunt, Gal. III. 24. IV. 2. A talibus enim populi prisci puericiam, quæ inconsiderata ut plurimum & imprudens fuit, regi Deus voluit, qui & Νομοθέται Legislatorum, hoc est, Legum & statutorum renovatorum, inculcatorum ἐργοδιώκται, qui potestatem habebant leges ad cultum pertinentes condendi, & eas simul cum Divinis vigidissimè, & quàdam carnis castigatione urgendi & exercendi; nomine Genef. XLIX. 10. veniunt. Tales Christus ἀπο- εκδυσάμενος exuit suo dominatu, vel etiam se Regem populi sui, illis tanquam velo hactenus sibi circumpositò, exuit, ἀπεγμάτισεν ἐν παρρη- σίᾳ ostentui habuit, velut invalidas & impotentes, & velut subactos, in triumpho egit in semet ipso. Col. II. 15. Contrà Christus nos fecit Sacerdotes & Reges, Apoc. V. 10. illud, ut accederemus ad Deum in fiducia filiali in nomine Filii, Joh. XIV. 15. 16. Hebr. X. 19. 20. hoc, quia nobis omnia in Christo subjecta sunt, I. Cor. III. 21. 22. 23. Ephes. I. 22. II. 6. Vos estis genus electum, Regale Sacerdotium, gens sancta, &c. I. Pet. II. 9. Neque alium posthac in fide Dominum & magistrum nisi solum Deum agnoscimus. Jehova judex noster, Jehova Legislator noster, Jehova Rex noster est. Esai. XXXIII. 22. Scriptum est: Perdam sapientiam sapientum. Ubi sapiens? Ubi scriba? ubi inquisitor hujus seculi? I. Cor. I. 19. Sapientiam loquimur in perfectis; Sapientiam autem non hujus seculi, neque Principum seculi hujus abolendorum, ibid. II. 6. Christo autem omnis potestas in cœlo & terra data est. Matth. XXVII. 18.
units.tr: LII. There are three things in general in which that liberty, singular to the faithful of the New Testament, consists: namely, immunity from the curse of the Law and the fear of death arising from it; freedom from slavery to the Law's precepts concerning matters of indifference; and freedom from the dominion of the executors of the Law. For it removes far away all that old slavery, and every image and species of it. The immunity from the curse of the Law consists in this: it was effected by the death of Christ, not only so that the law of sin should not hinder sanctification, and that there should be immunity from the eternal curse of the Seed, which also held good for the heirs of the earlier time, but also so that the Law could no longer inflict on wrath a certain appearance of the curse that was then growing up. This was at last made effective by the death of Christ. For before the Surety died, sin and its guilt, still remaining, could be recalled, accused, and imputed to a temporal slavery; the handwriting could be demanded and charged against us. All who rely on works of the Law are under a curse; for it is written, Cursed is everyone who does not abide by all things written in the book of the Law, to do them, Gal. 3:10. I have said more about this in Locus 13, §37, where I showed that such things must be understood with a grain of salt and in an economic sense. But after Christ, the heir of all, had died, it was fitting that he claim his people as Lord, and so set his redeemed free, and not leave them in the condition of those who are held to be accusers; rather, he should claim them into that condition in which they could give thanks to God for their redemption and justification, and live no longer for the accusing sin but for the Lord who claims them. Christ bought us, that we might be free from the curse of the Law, since he became a curse for us, ibid. v. 13. This immunity carries with it deliverance from the fear of temporal death, to which the ancients were subject throughout their whole life; and this was not the least part of legal slavery. That he might deliver those who through fear of death were subject to slavery all their lives, or who because of the fear of death were subject to slavery all their life, Heb. 2:15. The fear of death that had to be feared was the cause, not of that eternal death (from the fear of which the promise of God always freed and fortified all who were in covenant), but of temporal death; the cause was that death was accelerated, and the afflictions of this life were set before the transgressors of the Law under the face and appearance of punishment, and so they opposed quite strongly the temporal reward proposed by the Law to those in covenant: a long and blessed life in possession of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which the Law then offered as a pledge and figure of the heavenly inheritance. For it pleased God, before true righteousness had been revealed, to show to a carnal people what all doctrine, discipline and temporal retribution might accomplish for conversion among carnal men; and meanwhile, to comfort and sustain the Church in its childhood with the expectation of better things than these earthly ones. And since temporal afflictions and death itself had greatly disturbed these earthly things, the fear of losing them, and the slavery bound to these earthly things, wonderfully exercised them all their life. But when righteousness was revealed, and by it absolution of conscience was given, it was necessary that the veil which hung in the external sanctuary, and the land given as a secret inheritance, be taken away. So the fear of afflictions and death ceased along with all legal slavery, and in its place the liberty of the sons of God came in. Bound up with this is immunity from slavery to the Law's precepts concerning matters of indifference, the chief species of Evangelical liberty. For after faith came, we are no longer under the law, but under grace, Rom. 6:14. The Law, insofar as it entered in as a guardian, was ordered to yield its pedagogical throne and to serve grace and righteousness. When we were children, we were enslaved to the elements of the world, etc. But now, knowing God, or rather being known by God, how do you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elements?, etc., Gal. 4:3, 9. He blotted out the handwriting of requirements that was against us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to the cross, Col. 2:14. Let no one therefore judge you in food or drink, or with regard to a festival, a new moon, or Sabbaths; these are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ, ibid. v. 16, 17. In place of this carnal worship, now purely spiritual and rational worship pleases God. God is Spirit, and those who worship him must worship in Spirit and truth, John 4:24. I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, your rational worship, Rom. 12:1. With all the requirements concerning things indifferent removed, the use of them is now left entirely to free charity and prudent judgment. If your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking in love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died, ibid. 14:15. Let no one judge you in food or drink, or with regard to a festival, or a new moon, or Sabbaths, Col. 2:16. Connected with this same liberty is immunity and emancipation from the hand of the executors of the Law, instituted by God. Of such kind were formerly the epitropoi and oikonomoi [ἐπίτροποι καὶ οἰκονόμοι], tutors and curators, and also the pedagogues, to whom the Israelites were subject in their infancy until the time of correction, Gal. 3:24; 4:2. For God willed that the childhood of the ancient people, which for the most part was thoughtless and imprudent, be ruled by such guardians; these are named nomothetai [νομοθέται] (legislators, that is, makers of laws and statutes), and ergodiōktai [ἐργοδιώκται] (the urgers and enforcers of renewed and inculcated statutes), who had power to enact laws pertaining to worship, and to enforce them together with the Divine laws most vigorously, and with a certain chastisement of the flesh; see Gen. 49:10. Christ, having stripped off (ἀπεκδυσάμενος), put off his dominion over such men, or even himself as King of his people, stripped them, as with a veil hitherto placed around him; he made a public show of them [ἀπεδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ] as weak and powerless, and as subdued, and led them in triumph in himself, Col. 2:15. On the contrary, Christ has made us priests and kings, Rev. 5:10: the former, so that we might approach God in filial confidence in the name of the Son, John 14:15, 16; Heb. 10:19, 20; the latter, because all things are subject to us in Christ, 1 Cor. 3:21–23; Eph. 1:22; 2:6. You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, etc., 1 Pet. 2:9. Nor do we henceforth acknowledge in faith any Lord and teacher except God alone. The LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king, Isa. 33:22. It is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise. Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the inquirer of this age?, 1 Cor. 1:19. We speak wisdom among the perfect; yet not the wisdom of this age, nor of the rulers of this age who are being brought to nothing, ibid. 2:6. But all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Christ, Matt. 28:18.

units.la: LIII. Neque tamen Libertas, in quam Christus morte sua nos asseruit, in eo plenè planè- que consummati r, quòd non circumcidimur, non censemus alia pura, alia impura, tempora non discernimus, elementa non tractamus, hominibus, sive dominis, sive pædagogis non subjicimur; sed in eo potius, quod abdicatis umbris & dominis aliis, & servitute omni legali soluta, Christum Dominum agnoscimus, ei servimus, jugum ejus, quod χρηστὸν suave est, Matth. XI. 29. libentes volentésque suscipimus, in Christo gloriamur, & ad Deum, tanquam Deum nostrum, & Patrem nostrum cum omni fiducia accedimus, eíque pro liberatione nostra à servitute, & maximè à reatu gratias agere satagimus; Denique ab eo omnium benedictionum spiritualium in Coelestibus fluenta expetimus. Hæc illa ἀληθεια veritas est, quæ nos ἐλευθερώσει liberabit, Joh. VIII. 32. Hac potissima & maxima ἐλευθερία Libertate, qua Christus nos liberavit, stamus, ne iterum jugo servitutis nos innodari patiamur, Gal. V. 1. Nam qui jugo servitutis post liberationem ab eodem per Christum iterum se innodari patitur, is lætitiam, quæ in Regno Dei est; & præcipuum charitatis fomentum est, abjicit. Perfecta charitas timorem foras pellit, 1. Joh. IV. 18.
units.tr: LIII. Yet the liberty into which Christ by his death has set us free is not fully and completely realised in this, that we are not circumcised, that we do not regard some things as clean and others as unclean, that we do not observe times, that we do not handle the elements, and that we are not subject to men, whether masters or tutors. It consists rather in this: having put aside the shadows and other lords, and having been released from all legal servitude, we acknowledge Christ as our Lord and serve him. We willingly and gladly take up his yoke, which is sweet [χρηστὸν] (Matt. 11:29). We glory in Christ, and we come to God, as our God and our Father, with all confidence, and we take pains to give thanks to him for our deliverance from bondage, and above all from guilt. Finally, from him we seek the streams of all spiritual blessings in heavenly places. This is the truth [ἀληθεια] that will make us free [ἐλευθερώσει] (John 8:32). We stand in this chief and greatest liberty [ἐλευθερία], with which Christ has made us free, lest we allow ourselves to be held again in the yoke of bondage (Gal. 5:1). For whoever, after being freed by Christ, allows himself to be bound again in the yoke of servitude, casts away the joy that is in the kingdom of God and the chief nourishment of love. Perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18).

units.la: LIV. Libertatem hanc Pax, Novi Testamenti Bonum, sequitur. Nam Regnum Dei etiam Pax est, Rom. XIV. 17. non tantum cum Deo, de qua est ibid. V. 1. & quæ consummata ira, quam Lex operabatur, opponitur, sed etiam cum gentibus, quæ in V. T. ceu futurum bonum prædicta est. In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes, Gen. XXII. 18. &c. Ei, Schiloni erit obedientia populorum, ibid. XLIX. 10. Afferent montes Pacem populo, Psal. LXXII. 3. Habitabit lupus cum agno, & pardus cum hædo cubabit, & vitulus, catulus leonis & bubalus simul, & puer parvus eos ducet. Vacca & ursa unâ pascentur, simul cubabunt nati earum, & leo sicut bos paleam comedet. Et ludet lactens apud foramen aspidis, & in cavernam basilisci ablactatus manum projiciet. Non malefacient, neq; perdent in toto monte Sancto meo; sed plena erit terra cognitione Jehovæ, ut aquis mare operientibus, Esai. XI. 6-9. Pluribus ita verbis exposuit Esaias, quod paucis apud Hoseam Deus vaticinans: Faciam illis fœdus cum bestiis agri, Hos. II. 18. Non tamen sine emphasi sic animalia distinxit, per mansueta animalia, agnum, hœdum, vitulum, vaccam & pullos ejus Ecclesiam & homines regenitos, per lupum, pantheram, juvenes leones, aspidem, basiliscum, eos qui sunt extra Ecclesiam, irregenitos & carnales figurans; & utraque, pro diversitate operationum Spiritus S. in Ecclesia, nec non Dei hujus seculi in iis, qui sunt extra Ecclesiam per certos coalituræ pacis gradus & processus distinguens, de quo nunc dicere supersedemus. Idem apud Haggæum prædictum est, Deo promittente: Major fiet gloria domus hujus posterioris, quàm prioris, dixit Jehova, Deus exercituum: & in loco hoc dabo שלום Pacem, ait Jehova, Deus exercituum, Hagg. II. 9. Erit consilium Pacis inter utrumque Jehovam & Sacerdotem Jehovæ, in throno Jehovæ sedentem, Zach. VI. 13. Excindam currum ab Ephraim, & equum ab Hierosolyma. Et excindetur arcus belli: & loquetur pacem gentibus, & dominatio ipsius erit à mari ad mare, & à fluvio ad terminos terræ, ibid. IX. 10. Ideo Christus שר שלום Princeps Pacis, Esai. IX. 6. appellatur, quia iram omnem & maledictionem, peccati commemoratio-
units.tr: LIV. The liberty is followed by peace, the good of the New Testament. For the kingdom of God is also peace (Rom. 14:17), not only with God, of which Paul speaks in Rom. 5:1, and which is set against the wrath that the Law worked, but also with the nations, which in the Old Testament was foretold as a future good. In your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed (Gen. 22:18), and so on. To him shall be the obedience of the peoples (Gen. 49:10). The mountains shall bring peace to the people (Ps. 72:3). The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them. The cow and the bear shall feed; their young shall lie down together; and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. The nursing child shall play at the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the viper's den. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; but the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea (Isa. 11:6-9). Isaiah set this out in more words than Hosea, where God, prophesying in a few words, says: I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field (Hos. 2:18). Yet it is not without meaning that he distinguishes the animals in this way. By the gentle animals, the lamb, the kid, the calf, the cow and her young, he signifies the Church and regenerate men; by the wolf, the leopard, the young lions, the asp and the basilisk, those who are outside the Church, unregenerate and carnal. Both are distinguished according to the diversity of the operations of the Holy Spirit in the Church, and of the god of this age in those who are outside the Church, through certain degrees and stages by which the peace is to be joined together. We may pass over this now. The same is foretold by Haggai, God promising: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than that of the former, says the LORD of hosts; and in this place I will give peace, says the LORD of hosts (Hag. 2:9). The counsel of peace shall be between them both, the LORD and the priest of the LORD, sitting upon the throne of the LORD (Zech. 6:13). I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; and the battle bow shall be cut off; and he shall speak peace to the nations; and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth (Zech. 9:10). Christ is therefore called the Prince of Peace [שר שלום] (Isa. 9:6), because he, by removing all wrath and curse, the remembrance of sin, the fear of death, whether arising from a conscience of sin not yet expiated or from the carnal testament, and the distinction between the nations as regards the covenant of grace, ought to bring peace to his people.

units.la: nem, metum mortis sive ex conscientia peccati nondum expiati, sive ex testamento carnali oriundum, & discrimen gentium, quoad fœdus gratiæ, tollendo, Pacem populo suo afferre debuit.
units.tr: ...nem, the fear of death arising either from a conscience of sin not yet expiated or from the carnal covenant, and the distinction between the nations as regards the covenant of grace, by removing these, he ought to bring peace to his people.

units.la: LV. Prædictionibus eventus respondit. Nam Christus factus est Pax nostra (tum inter homines omnes & Deum: tum inter hominum diversa genera, capitalibus inimicitiis hactenus divulsa) qui fecit utrumq; (Judæos & Gentes) unum (corpus in se velut capite) & intergerinum parietem solvit (Legem præceptorum in placitis constitentium, quæ Judæos à gentibus vehementer disterminabat, flagrante inimicitia inter utrosque, religionum è diametro oppositarum divortiis distractos, sustulit, atque ita ad pacem latam portam aperuit; eadem opera abolens) inimicitiam quæ in carne ejus (nondum fracta, velo nondum rupto, antequam fractuiram & rupturam, nondum præstita satisfactione Lex, ceu intergerinus ille paries, duravit, neque gentibus aditus ad Ecclesiam patuit) erat; dum Legem præceptorum in placitis constitentem ad nihilum redegit: ut duos illos crearet in se in unum hominem novum (gentes ceu noviter ex morte peccatorum & præputio carnis excitandas, & Judæos ipsos, sanctificatos licèt & credentes promissioni dato Spiritu filiationis velut novas creandas) faciens pacem; & reconciliaret utrosque in uno corpore Deo per crucem, interfecta inimicitia in se, Ephes. II. 14.15.16. Placuit Deo per ipsum (Christum) omnia reconciliare εἰς αὐτὸν ad se, pacem faciendo per sanguinem crucis ejus, per ipsum (tum obedientia, doloribus, opprobriis, morte, tum valore & dignitate personæ) tum quæ in cœlis sunt, tum quæ in terris sunt. (Angelos, beatos spiritus, & accedentes ad Deum in terra, Judæos & gentes) Et vos, qui aliquando eratis alienati, & inimici mente in operibus malis, nunc reconciliavit (ab ira, inimicitia liberavit) in corpore carnis suæ per mortem (per obedientiam suam usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis) ut vos sisteret sanctos, & sine vitio; & inculpatos coram se. Col. I. 20-23.
