Without this assurance, a person has no hope and belongs to those who are "without God in the world" [ἄθεοι] (Eph. 2:12). Without this hope and certainty, we easily forget [λήθην λαμβάνομεν] the purification of the sins committed long ago (2 Pet. 1:9). Finally, this doctrine is the nurse of piety. For it produces the fear of God, not the fear by which we flee from and shudder at God, but the fear by which we esteem him, as a Father, as uniquely lovable and desirable. We take earnest care not to receive the grace of God in vain (2 Cor. 6:1), and we labour to keep the light of his face, as of our Father, always shining in us. This fear of God is so far from making people uncertain and doubtful about grace and salvation that it is rather a treasury of salvations [אוצר ישועות], a guarded chest, as it were, of salvation and wisdom (Isa. 33:6), and a fountain of life [מקור חיים] (Prov. 14:27).

units.la: III. Et maximi igitur ad salutem æternam & consolationem nostram in ærumnosæ humjus vitæ fluctibus momenti, & necessaria non minùs, quàm quævis gratia Dei, Perseverantiæ Sanctorum & Certitudinis Gratiæ, Gratia est. De qua etiam distincta, seorsim & distinctè nobis agendum est. Utriusque quædam σχέσις firmitas est. Illa objecti, sive quoad rem, quæ indissolubilis
units.tr: III. Therefore the perseverance of the saints and the certainty of grace are of the greatest importance for eternal salvation and for our consolation amid the waves of this troubled life. They are no less necessary than any grace of God, and they too must be treated separately and distinctly. Each has a certain firmness. The first is the firmness of the object, or as regards the thing itself, which is indissoluble

units.la: ii dissolubili nexu causarum & effectuum, mediorum & finis, nititur: haec subjecti, sive καθ' ἡμᾶς quoad nos & assensum atque persuasionem nostram de gratia Dei, velut ad nos pertinente, qua novimus cui credidimus, πεπεισμαι γαρ persuasi sumus, quòd potens sit servare τὴν παραθήκην depositum in diem illum, 2. Tim. I. 12. Quod depositum salutis nostrae pignus est, de quo cum glorietur Apostolus, se non posse confundi, quia novit, cui crediderit, & certus sit, eum potentem beneficii semel collati custodem & conservatorem esse, id certè indicat, assensus fiducialis actum non tantum directum in rem promissam, sed etiam reflexum in credentis ipsius apprehensionem, & πίστεως persuasionem esse. Non enim tantum generalis illa Evangelii vox est: Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, salvabitur, Marc. XVI. 16. sed etiam sigillatim quisque fidelis, una cum omnibus fidelibus reliquis, in corde suo clamat & decantat: Nos accepimus Spiritum, qui ex Deo est, ut sciamus, quae à Deo nobis donata sunt, 1. Cor. II. 12. De utraque Firmitate, quantum poterimus, solida & salutaria dicemus: & prius de Firmitate objecti, seu Perseverantia Sanctorum, quae Firmitatis seu certitudinis subjecti veluti basis est. Nam haec illam supponit, & in ea velut fundatur: illa vero hanc infert; salvo tamen discrimine utriusque. Nam illa in se immota & semper aequalis est, neque gradus admittit, quia causis immutabilibus & perpetuis nititur. Haec suas patitur vices, nec eadem semper in animo fidelis est. Et tanto etiam accuratiorem doctrina de Perseverantia tractationem meretur, quantò validius illa ab omnibus fere Reformatorum adversariis impetitur. Verè enim illa puritatis Religionis Reformatae supra tot religionis Christianae sectas character & quoddam velut ἀληθοφυλλιμα est.
units.tr: bond of causes and effects, of means and end. The second is the firmness of the subject, or [καθ' ἡμᾶς] as regards us, concerning our assent and persuasion about the grace of God, as pertaining to us, by which we know whom we have believed, [for] we are persuaded that he is able to keep [τὴν παραθήκην] what has been committed to him until that day, 2 Tim. 1:12. This deposit is the pledge of our salvation. When the Apostle glories that he cannot be put to shame, because he knows whom he has believed and is sure that he is able to guard and preserve the benefit once bestowed, this clearly shows that an act of fiducial assent is directed not only at the promised thing, but also reflexively at the believer's own apprehension, and is the persuasion of faith. For the general voice of the Gospel is not the only one: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, Mark 16:16. Each faithful person, together with all the other faithful, also cries out and sings in his own heart: We have received the Spirit who is from God, that we may know the things freely given to us by God, 1 Cor. 2:12. Concerning both firmnesses we shall speak as solidly and usefully as we can, and first concerning the firmness of the object, or Perseverance of the Saints, which serves as the basis of the firmness or certainty of the subject. For the latter presupposes the former and is founded upon it, while the former infers the latter, though with a difference between the two. The former is in itself immovable and always the same, and admits no degrees, because it rests on unchangeable and perpetual causes. The latter undergoes its changes, and is not always the same in the mind of the believer. The doctrine of Perseverance deserves all the more careful treatment, because it is attacked more vigorously by nearly all the adversaries of the Reformed. Indeed, that doctrine is, above so many sects of Christian religion, a mark of the purity of the Reformed religion and a kind of touchstone of truth [ἀληθοφυλλιμα].

units.la: IV. Perseverantia in universum quaedam animi constantia cum severitate conjuncta, est. Unde ἐπερεμένης Ephes. VI. 18. dicitur, quae vox a simplici κάρτος pro κράτος robur derivatur. Ut ita perseverantia fortis quaedam & severa in re propósita constantia fit. Paucis verò Apostolus Perseverantiam Sanctorum ὑπομονὴν τῆς χάριτος permansionem in bonitate, vel gratia definit. Vide erga te bonitatem, ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι, si permanseris in bonitate, gratia, ei firmiter affixus fueris, adhaeseris, Rom. XI. 22. Persuaserunt eis, ἐπιμεῖναι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ ut permanerent in gratia Dei, Actor. XIII. 43. Idem perseverare definit τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς ὑπο-στάσεως μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν κατασχεῖν initium fidei, seu fiduciae, usque ad finem firmum retinere, Hebr. III. 14. Plenius verò Perseverantia Sanctorum definitur, quòd sit donum Dei, quo Deus ab aeterno electos, in tempore vocatos, seu per incorruptibile verbum Dei & gratiam Spiritus S. regenitos, per fidem justificatos & sanctificatos invicta constantia donat, ut certantes contra peccatum & aerumnas hujus seculi, vel etiam à lapsibus per resipiscentiam resurgentes, in semel donata gratia, usque in diem redemptionis suae permaneant, & aeternum salventur.
units.tr: IV. Perseverance in general is a certain constancy of mind joined with steadfastness. Hence it is called [προσκαρτέρησις] (Eph. 6:18), a word derived from the simple κάρτος, put for κράτος, strength. Thus perseverance is a certain strong and resolute constancy in the matter proposed. The Apostle briefly defines the perseverance of the saints as [ὑπομονὴν τῆς χάριτος], a remaining in goodness or grace. Behold the goodness of God: if you continue in his goodness [ἐὰν ἐπιμένῃς τῇ χρηστότητι], if you remain in goodness, and hold firmly to it, Rom. 11:22. They persuaded them [ἐπιμεῖναι τῇ χάριτι] to continue in the grace of God, Acts 13:43. The same Apostle defines perseverance as [τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς ὑποστάσεως μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν κατασχεῖν], to hold firm the beginning of confidence, or of trust, to the end, Heb. 3:14. More fully, the perseverance of the saints is defined as the gift of God by which God, with invincible constancy, grants to those whom he elected from eternity, called in time, or regenerated through the incorruptible word of God and the grace of the Holy Spirit, and justified and sanctified through faith, that they, striving against sin and the troubles of this age, or even rising again from falls through repentance, persist in the grace once given until the day of their redemption and are eternally saved.

units.la: V. Non ergo de Perseverantia quorumvis & quavis sermo nobis est. Non quorumvis hominum, quia non quivis electi, vocati, & justificati sunt, sed Christianorum per Baptismum, vel sine eo per solam fidem in Ecclesiam cooptatorum. Ac ne omnium quidem baptizatorum, Baptismo vel sola fide in Ecclesiam cooptatorum. Non infantum, qui nec peccata conscientiam vastantia committunt, nec liberi arbitrii usu gaudent, quo peccato obluctentur; sed adultorum. Ac ne horum quidem omnium, quia non omnes electi vel fideles sunt, licet verbum Dei praedicatum cum gaudio audientes, & eidem sic voluntate sua assentientes, ut ex fide tali dogmatica minimè simulata affectuum quaedam mutatio, & morum emendatio in iis oriatur, judicio charitatis pro electis & fidelibus censeri debeant.
units.tr: V. Therefore our discussion is not of the perseverance of any persons whatever. It is not of any men, since not all are elect, called, and justified, but of Christians, those received into the Church through baptism, or without it through faith alone. Nor is it even of all the baptized, those received into the Church by baptism or by faith alone. It is not of infants, who commit no sins that trouble the conscience, nor enjoy the use of free will by which they might struggle against sin, but of adults. Nor is it even of all adults, since not all are elect or faithful. Yet those who hear the preached Word of God with joy and assent to it with their will, so that from such faith, which is not feigned in doctrine, some change of affections and reform of morals arises in them, ought by the judgment of charity to be counted among the elect and faithful.

units.la: sed militantes huius vitae. nostri Jesu Christi, 1.Cor.I. 8. Et sic Dei donum est,ut non sit in homine habitus instar moralis seu ethici , crebris credendi obediendíque actibus comparati; qualem Remonstrantes faciunt ; sed supernaturalis, spiritualis & Theologici Spiritus S. virtute in perseverante producti. Planè enim habitus Divinitus donatus & infusus est. Timorem meum dabo in cor eorum, לבלתי מור מעלי ut non recedant à me, Jerem. XXXII. 40. Hoc est fœdus meum cum ipsis. Spiritus meus,qui super te est, & verba mea,quæ posui in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo, & ab ore Seminis tui, dicit Jehova, à nunc & in seculum, Esaj. LIX. 21. Persuasus hoc sum,quòd,qui in vobis incepit opus bonum, perfecturus illud sit, usque ad diem Jesu Christi, Phil. I. 6. Non ergo spiritualis illa qualitas & habitus perinde in humanis viribus est,atque habitus quivis moralis,qui crebris actibus acquiritur. Alias ipsa etiam fides & sanctitas actibus nostris acquireretur. Cùm tamen & fides sit donum Dei, Ephes. II. 8. & sanctitas sit ab ἁγιάσαντι sanctificante & τηρῶντι conservante Deo, 1. Thess. V. 23. Ac liceret etiam sic nobis de fide & perseverantia in eodem gloriari. Sed Dei donum est, ne quis glorietur, Ephes. II. 8. 9. Licèt enim credentes quotidianis fidei actibus & exercitiis augescant,& in fide confirmentur, non tamen ideo ipsi sibi perseverantiam acquirunt, quia non per suos actus, sed per gratiam Dei continuatam, & in iis bonum, quod cœpit, opus perficientem, Phil. I. 6. Hinc pro gratia perseverantiæ & precamur & gratias agimus. Fidelis est, qui vocat vos ὃς καὶ ποιήσει qui etiam efficiet, 1. Thess. V. 24. Gratias semper Deo pro vobis agere debemus, ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη, quòd superabundat fides vestra, & augescit charitas, 2. Thess. I. 3.
units.tr: but those who are fighting in this life, of our Lord Jesus Christ, 1 Cor. 1:8. And so it is a gift of God that there is not in a person a habit like a moral or ethical one, built up by frequent acts of believing and obeying, as the Remonstrants hold; rather it is a supernatural and spiritual habit, produced in perseverance by the power of the Holy Spirit and of theological virtue. Clearly the habit is divinely bestowed and infused. "I will put my fear in their heart, לבלתי מור מעלי, that they may not depart from me," Jer. 32:40. "This is my covenant with them. My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your seed, says the LORD, from now and for ever," Isa. 59:21. "I am persuaded of this, that he who began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Jesus Christ," Phil. 1:6. Therefore that spiritual quality and habit does not lie within human powers in the way any moral habit, acquired by frequent acts, does. Otherwise faith and holiness themselves would be acquired by our acts. Yet faith is "the gift of God," Eph. 2:8, and holiness comes from God, "sanctifying [ἁγιάσαντι] and preserving [τηρῶντι]," 1 Thess. 5:23. And then we could also boast of faith and perseverance in the same way. But "it is the gift of God, lest anyone should boast," Eph. 2:8-9. For although believers grow by the daily acts and exercises of faith and are confirmed in faith, they do not thereby acquire perseverance for themselves, because it comes not through their own acts but through the continued grace of God, who in them performs "the good work that he began," Phil. 1:6. Hence we both pray for and give thanks for the grace of perseverance. "Faithful is he who calls you, who also will do it [ὃς καὶ ποιήσει]," 1 Thess. 5:24. "We ought always to give thanks to God for you, because your faith grows exceedingly [ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη], and the love of each of you towards one another abounds," 2 Thess. 1:3.

units.la: VII. Perseverantiam magnum Dei donum
units.tr: VII. Perseverance is a great gift of God

units.la: etiam Tridentini Sess. VI. can. 16. appellant. Neque aliter Remonstrantes. Sed donum Dei sanè plane peregrino & heterodoxo appellant, asserentes, donum Dei esse tum quoad potentiam, quam Deus largiatur, ut possit homo perseverare, non quoad actum, ut reipsa perseveret : tum generale, omnibus vocatis paratum & expositum, per gratiam collatam sufficientem, seu resistibilem, non speciale, electorum proprium : tum ab arbitrio humano dependens, non morte Christi paratum. Quale δῶρον verè δωρον est,quia nihil,vel parum ad salutem & consolationem fidelium confert. Sed Scriptura disertè doni hujus vigorem non in potentia duntaxat,sed in actu & consummatione ipsa collocat. Circumcidet Jehova cor tuum, & cor Seminis tui, ut diligas Jehovam Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & tota anima tua, propter vitam tuam, Deut. XXX. 6. Spiritum meum dabo in medio cordis vestri,efficiámque,ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, & judicia mea custodiatis, & illa faciatis,Ezech. XXXVI. 27. Deus confirmabit vos usque ad finem inculpatos, 1. Cor. I. 8. Qui incepit in vobis opus bonum, ἐπιτελέσει perficiet usque in diem Jesu Christi, Phil. I. 6. Gratis datum vobis est,in Christum non tantùm credere, sed etiam pro eo pati,ibid. v. 29. Deus est in vobis operans καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν & velle & operari pro beneplacito, cap.II. 13. Neque etiam donum illud commune, sed singulare electorum est.
units.tr: The Council of Trent also calls it this, Sess. VI, can. 16. The Remonstrants do likewise. But they call it a "gift of God" in a quite foreign and heterodox sense, asserting that it is a gift of God in respect of the power which God bestows so that a person may persevere, but not in respect of the act itself, so that he actually perseveres; that it is a general gift, prepared and offered to all who are called, through a sufficient or resistible grace conferred, not a special gift proper to the elect; and that it depends on human choice, not being procured by the death of Christ. Such a "gift" [δῶρον] is truly a mere gift in name, since it contributes nothing, or very little, to the salvation and comfort of believers. But Scripture expressly places the force of this gift not merely in power, but in the act itself and its completion. "The LORD your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, for the sake of your life," Deut. 30:6. "I will put my Spirit in the midst of your heart, and I will cause you to walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them," Ezek. 36:27. "God will confirm you until the end, blameless," 1 Cor. 1:8. "He who began a good work in you will perfect it [ἐπιτελέσει] until the day of Jesus Christ," Phil. 1:6. "It has been given to you on Christ's behalf not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him," ibid. v. 29. "It is God who works in you both to will and to do [καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν] for his good pleasure," ch. 2:13. Nor is this gift a general one, but a special gift of the elect.

units.la: Nam quos præcognovit,&c. illos vocavit, justificavit, glorificavit; Rom. VIII. 28--31. Electio assequitur,cap. XI. 7. Illorum certè perseverantia est, quorum fides, quia fidei perseverantia est. At fides non est omnium,2.Thess.III.2. sed ἐκλεκτῶν electorum duntaxat,Tit. I. 1. Denique neque donum illud magis quàm cætera beneficia spiritualia & salutaria à liberi arbitrii usu pendet,sed morte Christi, ejusque merito nobis acquisitum est. Animam meam pono pro ovibus. Et ego do illis vitam æternam, Joh. X. 15. 28. Justificati sanguine ejus, servabimur per ipsum ab ira,&c. Rom. V. 9. Alias extra Christum foret salus, quæ nonnisi perseverantibus datur. Atqui in nullo alio salus est, & nullum sub Cœlo nomen datum hominibus, in quo nos salvari oporteat, Actor. IV. 12.
units.tr: For "whom he foreknew ... those he also called, justified, and glorified," Rom. 8:28-31. "The election obtained it," ch. 11:7. Certainly perseverance belongs to those whose faith it is, since perseverance is of faith. But "faith is not of all," 2 Thess. 3:2, but only of the elect [ἐκλεκτῶν], Titus 1:1. Finally, that gift, like the other spiritual and saving benefits, does not depend on the use of free will, but was acquired for us by the death of Christ and his merit. "I lay down my life for the sheep. And I give them eternal life," John 10:15, 28. "Being justified by his blood, we shall be saved through him from wrath," etc., Rom. 5:9. Otherwise there would be salvation outside Christ, which is given only to those who persevere. But "there is salvation in no other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved," Acts 4:12.

units.la: VIII. Sed ita Perseverantia Dei donum est, ut in eo producendo & efficiendo omnes tres Deitatis Personæ sigillatim, & diversimodè,pro variante earum œconomia,concurrant. Nam admirabili & sapientissima œconomia factum est, ut personæ S. S. Trinitatis maximum illud salutis nostræ opus velut inter se partirentur, ut, dum totam S. S. Triadem operi huic manum admovi{s}se, & singulas ejus personas peculiari ratione singulorum salutis nostræ graduum curam suscepisse intelligimus, fides & consolatio nostra magis confirmaretur. Filum enim triplicatum non citò rumpitur, Eccles. IV. 12. Ergo donum hoc Deus Pater æterna dilectione & electione, Deus Filius suscepta in novo fœdere gratiæ redemptione,jugique & efficacissima intercessione,denique Spiritus S. regeneratione, perpetua gubernatione & obsignatione operatur. Ab æterno in consilio Dei nobis destinatum,in tempore perChristum Mediatorem procuratum est,& à Spiritu S. regenerante & sanctificante confertur. His tribus de causis, pro personarum Divinarum œconomia variantibus certam esse Perseverantiam Scriptura docet, quando eam ἑτοιμίαν paratam appellat, atque ad triplex illud certitudinis fundamentum, tanquam ad triplicem salutis ἑτοιμασίαν præparationem digitum intendit. Nam & benedictis Patris βασιλείαν ἡτοιμασμένην regnum paratum esse à jacto mundi fundamento, Matth. XXV. 34. atque vasa misericordiæ προητοιμασμένα ante præparata ad gloriam,Rom. IX. 23. Scripturæ docent,& Christus suos consolaturus se proficisci ad Patrem ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ad parandum nobis locum Joh. XIV. 2. testatur: & Paulus nos esse conditos ad bona opera,quæ Deus προητοίμασεν antepræparavit (conferendo Spiritum S. qui in nobis operaretur & operari & perficere) ut ambularemus in iis,Eph. II. 10. confirmat. Hæc tria trium personarum ἐνεργήματα Perseverantiæ Sanctorum, ceu unius apotelesmatis,seu operis perfectissimi, inconcussa fundamenta deinceps explicanda sunt.
units.tr: VIII. But perseverance is a gift of God in such a way that all three Persons of the Deity concur in producing and effecting it, each separately and in different ways, according to their varying economy. For by a wonderful and most wise economy it has come about that the Persons of the Most Holy Trinity have, as it were, divided among themselves that greatest work of our salvation, so that, while we understand that the whole Most Holy Triad has laid hand to this work, and that each of its Persons has undertaken the care of the individual stages of our salvation in a particular manner, our faith and comfort may be the more strongly confirmed. "For a threefold cord is not quickly broken," Eccl. 4:12. Therefore God the Father works this gift by eternal love and election, God the Son by redemption undertaken in the new covenant of grace, by his constant and most effective intercession, and finally the Holy Spirit by regeneration, by perpetual governance and sealing. What was destined for us from eternity in the counsel of God has been procured in time through Christ the Mediator, and is conferred by the regenerating and sanctifying Holy Spirit. For these three reasons, owing to the varying economy of the Divine Persons, Scripture teaches that perseverance is certain, when it calls it "prepared" [ἑτοιμίαν], and directs our attention to this threefold foundation of certainty, as to the threefold preparation [ἑτοιμασίαν] of salvation. For Scripture teaches that the "kingdom prepared [ἡτοιμασμένην] from the foundation of the world" is for those blessed by the Father, Matt. 25:34, and the "vessels of mercy ... prepared [προητοιμασμένα] beforehand for glory," Rom. 9:23. Christ also testifies, when he is about to comfort his people by going to the Father, that he goes "to prepare [ἑτοιμάσαι] a place" for us, John 14:2. And Paul confirms that we are "created for good works, which God prepared beforehand [προητοίμασεν]" (by bestowing the Holy Spirit, who works in us both to will and to do, and to perform), "that we should walk in them," Eph. 2:10. These three operations [ἐνεργήματα] of the three Persons, as of one perfect work or accomplishment [apotelesmatis], concerning the perseverance of the saints, must now be set out as their unshakeable foundations.

units.la: IX. Primum Perseverantiæ fundamentum est operatio Dei PATRIS ab æterno nos diligentis & eligentis. Nam Deus Pater elegit nos in Christo ante fundationem mundi, Eph. I. 4. præcognovit & prædestinavit nos,Rom. VIII.29.30. ordinavit ad vitam æternam, Actor. XIII. 48. Hinc toties ἐκλεκτοὶ electi; & εὐλογημένοι benedicti Patris, Matth. XXV. 34. præparati ad gloriam, Rom. IX. 23. vocantur. Cùm igitur cercerta & immutabilis eadem fit, uti Loc. V. 49. 50. ostendimus, consequens est, electos nullos mutari, deficere, perire posse, quod diversis verbis Scriptura testatur, ajens possibile non esse, ut electi seducantur, Matth. XXIV. 24. electionem assequi, Rom. XI. 7. & praedestinatos glorificari, ibid. VIII. 30.
units.tr: IX. The first foundation of perseverance is the operation of God the FATHER, who loves and elects us from eternity. For God the Father "chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world," Eph. 1:4; he "foreknew and predestined us," Rom. 8:29-30; he "ordained us to eternal life," Acts 13:48. Hence they are so often called "elect" [ἐκλεκτοὶ], and "blessed of the Father," Matt. 25:34, "prepared for glory," Rom. 9:23. Since therefore this election is certain and unchangeable, as we have shown in Loc. V, pp. 49-50, it follows that none of the elect can be changed, fail, or perish. Scripture testifies to this in various words, saying that it is impossible for the elect to be led astray, Matt. 24:24; that they "obtain the election," Rom. 11:7; and that the predestined are glorified, ibid. 8:30.

units.la: X. Electionem non esse indefinitam conditionum & qualitatum, sed definitam certarum personarum in loco adversus Socinianos & asseclas eorum fusius etiam astruximus. At nec electio quorundam duntaxat, non omnium fidelium est, quasi alii fideles ad gloriam non electi, a fide totaliter & finaliter, alii ad gloriam electi totaliter, at non finaliter deficere possint; vel omnium fidelium ad gratiam & Ecclesiae consortium tantum, quorundam vero, puta praescitorum & in fide morientium ad salutem est; quae Augustanorum & Pontificiorum plerorumque ἐνσηµάτων sunt. Sicut enim fides non omnium, 2. Thess. III. 2. sed electorum tantum Tit. I. 1. est: ita fideles omnes electi sunt. Fideles enim a fide denominantur, ut quae fidei ratio est, eadem fidelium esse debeat. Neque alterum κεχηπωμένον de fidelium aliorum ad gratiam & consortium Ecclesiae, aliorum ad gloriam electione juvat. Unicam enim ad gratiam & gloriam electionem esse Loc. V. 39. ostendimus. Si igitur electi ad gratiam deficere possunt, etiam electi ad gloriam possunt. Tum fingere electionem ad gratiam & Ecclesiae consortium, quae non sit ad gloriam, est fingere electionem ad gratiam salutarem, quae non sit salutaris. Absurdum inprimis est statuere, quod electio ad gloriam ex praevisione status finalis, seu morientium in fide facta sit, tum quia Deus non morientes in fide, sed peccatores, seu mortuos in peccatis elegit: tum quia electio ab uno soloque Dei beneplacito pendens, nullam in homine causam vel dispositionem, quae ad eligendum moveat, invenit: tum quia Apostolus, Rom. VIII. 29. 30. electionem distincte fontem vocationis & justificationis, adeoque ipsius etiam fidei, quae vocatione datur & justificatione apprehenditur, statuit: tum denique, quia sic electio non praedestinatio, sed postdestinatio erit. Si enim Deus prius vidit hominem in fide perseverantem, quam eum ad vitam elegit, electio ad gloriam non tam electio, quam gloriae retributio erit. Praeterea nec consolatio ulla ab electione peti potest, si nec omnes fideles electi sunt, nec electio hominis viventis, sed demum morientis est. Insuper nec opus fuisset inculcari in Scripturis electionis & consilii Dei aeterni de salvandis quibusdam hominibus τὸ ἀµετάθετον seu immutabilitatem, si ex praevisione status finalis hominum pendet. Quis enim ambigat, eos, qui stadio confecto metam assecuti sunt, salvatum iri? Denique neque Christus dixisset, electos non posse seduci, Matth. XXIV. 24. Si electi fideles demum morientes sunt: quia nulli post mortem Pseudoprophetae erunt. Nil juvat cum Gerhardo dicere, electos a Christo nuncupari, quos Deus ad finem usque perseveraturos vidit, ut ita seductionis impossibilitas a praescientiae infallibilitate pendeat. Non enim infallibilitas praescientiae Dei rerum naturam mutat, quia praevisio non rei causa est, sed rem extra causas suas supponit. Si igitur seductio illa respectu omnium causarum contingens & possibilis foret, nec ulla perseverantiae fidelis causa necessaria daretur, Christus dixisset, electos non seducum iri, non, possibile non esse ut seducantur. Si nulla causa est voluntatem humanam necessario determinans, nulla etiam praescientia infallibilis esse potuit, utpote quae fundamento sciendi caruit. Neque parum sic nutabit consolatio Christi, qui causam, cur fideles seduci non possint, hanc reddidit, quod ἐκλεκτοί electi sint. Dicendum enim Christo fuisset, non, possibile non esse, ut electi seducantur, sed, si fideles non seducantur, atque id Deus praeviderit, eo casu illos electos fore. Quae hinc consolationis solidae materies?
units.tr: X. We have also argued more fully, against the Socinians and their followers, that election is not an indefinite election of conditions and qualities, but a definite election of certain persons in place. Nor is election of only some, and not of all believers, as if other believers, not elected to glory, could fall away totally and finally from faith, while others elected to glory could fall away totally but not finally; nor is it an election of all believers to grace and the fellowship of the Church only, and of some, namely the foreknown and those who die in faith, to salvation. These are the [ἐνσημάτων] tenets of most of the Augsburg Confessors and the Papists. For just as faith is not of all, 2 Thess. 3:2, but only of the elect, Titus 1:1, so all believers are elect. For believers are named from faith, and whatever is the ground of faith must be the same for believers. Nor does the other argument help, that there is one election to grace and the fellowship of the Church for some, and another to glory for others. For we have shown in Loc. V, p. 39, that there is one election to grace and glory. If therefore the elect can fall away from grace, the elect to glory can also fall away. Moreover, to imagine an election to grace and the fellowship of the Church that is not to glory is to imagine an election to saving grace that is not saving. It is above all absurd to hold that election to glory was made in view of the foreseen final state, that is, of those who die in faith, because God did not elect those dying in faith, but sinners, or those dead in sins. Also because election, depending on the sole good pleasure of God, finds no cause or disposition in man that moves him to elect. Also because the Apostle, Rom. 8:29-30, clearly sets election as the source of calling and justification, and so also of faith itself, which is given by calling and laid hold of by justification. And finally, because in that case election would not be predestination but postdestination. For if God saw a man persevering in faith before he elected him to life, election to glory would not be election at all, but a rewarding of glory. Besides, no comfort can be drawn from election if not all believers are elect, and if election is not of a living man, but only of one who is dying. Moreover, there would have been no need to inculcate in the Scriptures the immutability [τὸ ἀµετάθετον] of God's eternal counsel and election to save certain men, if it depended on the foreseen final state of men. For who doubts that those who have finished the race and reached the goal will be saved? Finally, Christ would not have said that the elect cannot be seduced, Matt. 24:24, if the elect were believers who are only elected at death, since after death there will be no false prophets. It does not help to say with Gerhard that those are called elect by Christ whom God saw would persevere to the end, so that the impossibility of seduction depends on the infallibility of foreknowledge. For the infallibility of God's foreknowledge does not change the nature of things, because foreknowledge is not the cause of the thing, but presupposes the thing outside its causes. If therefore such seduction were contingent and possible with respect to all causes, and no necessary cause of faithful perseverance were given, Christ would have said that the elect would not be seduced, not that it is impossible that they be seduced. If there is no cause necessarily determining the human will, then no infallible foreknowledge could exist either, since it would lack the ground of knowing. Nor would Christ's comfort be slight, when he gave as the cause why believers cannot be seduced that they are elect. For Christ would have had to say not that it is impossible for the elect to be seduced, but that if believers are not seduced, and God has foreseen this, then in that case they will be elect. What solid matter of comfort is there in this?

units.la: XI. Sed inprimis electionis aeternae efficacia & adamantinus cum caeteris gratiae beneficiis, electionis exequendae mediis, eodem electionis decreto definitis nexus Sanctorum perseverantiam potenter evincit. Deus enim non ad salutem & vitam duntaxat, sed etiam ad vitae & salutis media nos elegit, quod ipsum etiam Loc. V. 48. demonstravimus. Nam & Christum, principale salutis medium, Deus elegit, quia in Christo nos elegit, Ephes. I. 4. & quos elegit, eosdem in tempore tum vocat, potente tractu ad se pertrahit, regenerat, fidem iisdem, quae electorum, Tit. I. 1. & ordinatorum ad vitam aeternam, Actor. XIII. 48. est, quia ab electione & ordinatione ad vitam aeternam ab aeterno facta, ut causa unica fluit, donat: tum justificat, quia praecogniti sumus εἰς ῥαῦλησιν ad aspersionem sanguinis Jesu Christi, 1. Petr. I. 2. tum per Jesum Christum adoptat in filios, Ephes. I. 5. tum sanctificat, quia eligit nos ut simus sancti, ibid. v. 4. Facit huc inprimis arcana illa & providentissima omnium eventuum in bonum electorum directio, juxta quam vocati ex proposito electis, adeoque, quia vocati ex proposito, electi sunt, & ex eodem fonte Deum diligentibus omnia cooperari ad bonum dicuntur, Rom. VIII. 28. Admirabilem illum electionis & beneficiorum tum gratiae, tum gloriae nexum, catenatione quadam indissolubili, proponit Apostolus. Quos, inquiens, praecognovit, eos praedestinavit, ut conformes sint imagini Filii Dei. Quos vero praedestinavit, eos etiam vocavit. Et quos vocavit, eos etiam justificavit. Quos vero justificavit, illos etiam glorificavit, ibid. vers. 29. 30. Recte Augustinus de Praedest. 8. cap. 17. sic ἑνακφέναν illam ptemit: Non alios, sed quos praedestinavit, illos & vocavit. Nec alios, sed quos ita vocavit, ipsos etiam justificavit. Nec alios, sed quos praedestinavit, vocavit & justificavit, ipsos etiam glorificavit, illo utique sine, qui non habet finem. Electi ergo, quia electi sunt, & vocantur, & justificantur & glorificantur: adeoque nec a regeneratione & fide, quae in vocatione est, nec a justitia Christi, quae in justificatione est, nec a salute & gloria, quae in glorificatione est, excidere, vel perire, salva catenatione Apostoli, possunt. Neque enim Apostolus loquitur vel de praecognitis, ceu finaliter crediturus, quia Apostolus dicens; quos praecognovit, aperte innuit, non de qualitate fidei, sed de personis praecognitis, hoc est, ab aeterno dilectis, & ex proposito salvandis se loqui: vel de praecognitis, seu praedestinatis ad crucem, quia non is Apostoli scopus est, utpote cui propositum erat, rationem reddere, cur vocavocatis secundum propositum omnia ad bonum cooperentur, quia Deus vocatos secundum propositum salvare statuit. Id verò ut confirmet, efficaciam decreti electionis specialiter declarat, quòd ex eo vocatio, justificatio & glorificatio necessariò dependeant. Accedit, quòd terminus, ad quem Apostolus tendit, & in quo definit, non crux & afflictiones, sed glorificatio & salus est: quódque non simpliciter dicit, prædestinari nos, ut simus conformes Filio, sed, ut simus conformes imagini Filii, ut ille sit primogenitus inter multos fratres. Licet ergo etiam per crucem Christo conformemur, tamen ea est præcipua conformitas, quam Scriptura potiùs in sanctitate & gloria collocat. Transfiguramur in eandem imaginem à gloria in gloriam, sicut à Spiritu Domini, 2. Corinth. III. 18. Etiam in Cœlo Christo sine cruce similes erimus, 1. Joh. III. 2. & imaginem Adami cœlestis gestabimus, 1. Cor. XV. 49. Præterea nec justificatio vocationem ad crucem sequitur, sed potiùs præcedit. Plura eandem in rem Loc. XXI. 52. 53. dicta heic ad compendium ponimus.
units.tr: XI. But above all, the effectiveness of eternal election and its unbreakable connection with the other benefits of grace, the means of carrying out election, defined by the same decree of election, powerfully proves the perseverance of the saints. For God chose us not only to salvation and life but also to the means of life and salvation, which we have already demonstrated in Loc. V. 48. For God also chose Christ, the principal means of salvation, because he chose us in Christ (Eph. 1:4). Those whom he has chosen, he also calls in time, draws to himself by a powerful attraction, regenerates, and gives them faith, which belongs to the elect and to those ordained to eternal life (Titus 1:1; Acts 13:48), because it flows from the election and ordination to eternal life made from eternity, as its sole cause. He justifies them, because they are foreknown unto sprinkling by the blood of Jesus Christ (1 Pet. 1:2). He adopts them as sons through Jesus Christ (Eph. 1:5). He sanctifies them, because he chose us that we should be holy (ibid. v. 4). To this belongs especially that hidden and most provident direction of all events for the good of the elect, by which those called according to purpose are the elect, and so, because they are called according to purpose, they are the elect; and from the same source it is said that all things work together for good to those who love God (Rom. 8:28). The Apostle sets forth that wonderful connection of the benefits of grace and of glory, joined in a certain indissoluble chain. "Those whom he foreknew," he says, "he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son. And those whom he predestined, he also called. And those whom he called, he also justified. And those whom he justified, he also glorified" (ibid. vv. 29, 30). Augustine rightly expresses this chain in his book On Predestination, chapter 17: "Not others, but those whom he predestined, these he also called. Nor others, but those whom he so called, these he also justified. Nor others, but those whom he predestined, called and justified, these he also glorified, in that life which has no end." Therefore the elect, because they are elect, are also called, justified and glorified; and so, the chain of the Apostle being preserved, they cannot fall away or perish from regeneration and the faith which is in calling, nor from the righteousness of Christ which is in justification, nor from the salvation and glory which are in glorification. For the Apostle does not speak of the foreknown as those who would finally believe, since in saying "whom he foreknew" he clearly indicates that he speaks not of the quality of faith but of persons foreknown, that is, loved from eternity and destined to salvation by purpose. Nor does he speak of those foreknown or predestined to the cross, since this is not the Apostle's aim, whose purpose was to give the reason why all things work together for good for those called according to purpose: namely, because God has determined to save those called according to purpose. To confirm this, he specially declares the efficacy of the decree of election, from which calling, justification and glorification necessarily depend. Moreover, the goal toward which the Apostle tends and in which he ends is not the cross and afflictions but glorification and salvation; and he does not simply say that we are predestined to be conformed to the Son, but that we are predestined "to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers" (Rom. 8:29). Although we are therefore also conformed to Christ through the cross, yet the chief conformity is that which Scripture places rather in holiness and glory: "We are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord" (2 Cor. 3:18). We shall also be like Christ in heaven without the cross: "we shall be like him" (1 John 3:2), and "we shall bear the image of the heavenly Adam" (1 Cor. 15:49). Moreover, justification does not follow the call to the cross but rather precedes it. What has been said on the same matter in Loc. XXI. 52, 53 we set down here in brief.

units.la: XII. Secundum Perseverantiæ fundamentum operatio œconomica Filii, in se Mediatore inito Foedere Gratiæ electos à Deo Patre, & dilectos ab æterno, in tempore redimentis, est. Docet enim Scriptura, rupto foedere operum, & fractis primi Adami per peccatum ejusdem tabulis, Deum novum foedus Gratiæ in & cum Adamo secundo, Christo, & iis, qui cum eo communionem habituri erant, pepigisse; in quo iis, quorum personam gessit, non justitiam duntaxat & salutem, sed etiam fidem, & in eadem perseverantiam promisit; Christo vicissim Deo Patri suorum, seu sibi datorum redemptionem per meritum mortis suæ pollicitante & præstante. Si ergo Foedus Gratiæ Christo Mediatore initum promissionem fidei perseverantis habet, & Christus merito mortis suæ sibi datos redemit, certam & perseverantem gratiam omnium eorum, qui ad Novum Foedus Gratiæ & Mediatorem atque Sponsorem ejusdem, Christum, pertinent, esse consequitur. Alia enim planè Foederis operum & Foederis gratiæ ratio est. In illo Deus obedientiam præscripsit, vires obediendi suppeditavit, at actum obedientiæ non promisit, vel præstitit, sed liberæ voluntati hominis reliquit. In hoc conditionem foederis, quæ fides in Christum est, sic Deus præcipit, ut simul & vires & actum credendi promittat & conferat. In illo obedientia à mutabili voluntate hominis pendens nutare, deficere potuit. In hoc fides à gratia Dei unicè pendens deficere non potuit. Est enim donum Dei, Ephes. II. 8. non quoad potentiam duntaxat, sed etiam quoad actum credendi, uti supra ostendimus. Ego Jehova vocavi te cum justitia, & apprehendo manum tuam, & retinebo te, & dabo te in foedus populi, in lucem gentium, ut aperiantur oculi cæci, ad educendum ex claustro vinctum, ex carcere sedentes in tenebris, Esai. XLII. 6. 7. Surge, luce, quia venit lux tua, & gloria Domini super te exorta est. Et ambulabunt gentes ad lucem tuam, ibid. LX. 1. 3. Hoc est foedus, quod feriam cum domo Israel post dies illos; Dabo legem meam in medio eorum, & cordi eorum inscribam eam, &c. Cognoscent me à minimo usque ad maximum, Jerem. XXXI. 33. 34. Quibus
units.tr: XII. The second foundation of perseverance is the economic work of the Son, who, as Mediator, entered into the covenant of grace and in time redeems the elect, chosen by God the Father and loved from eternity. For Scripture teaches that, the covenant of works having been broken and the tables of the first Adam shattered through his sin, God made a new covenant of grace in and with the second Adam, Christ, and with those who were to have fellowship with him. In this covenant he promised to those whose person he bore not only righteousness and salvation but also faith, and perseverance in it; and in turn Christ promised and provided to God the Father the redemption of his own, or those given to him, through the merit of his death. If therefore the covenant of grace entered into with Christ as Mediator has the promise of persevering faith, and Christ has redeemed by the merit of his death those given to him, it follows that the grace of all those who belong to the new covenant of grace, and to its Mediator and Surety, Christ, is certain and persevering. For the manner of the covenant of works is entirely different from that of the covenant of grace. In the former, God prescribed obedience and supplied the strength to obey, but did not promise or provide the act of obedience; he left it to the free will of man. In the latter, God so commands the condition of the covenant, which is faith in Christ, that he at the same time promises and bestows both the strength and the act of believing. In the former, obedience depending on the changeable will of man could waver and fail. In the latter, faith, depending solely on the grace of God, could not fail. For it is the gift of God (Eph. 2:8), not only as to the power but also as to the act of believing, as we have shown above. "I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness, and will take hold of your hand, and will keep you, and give you as a covenant to the people, as a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoner from the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness from the prison" (Isa. 42:6, 7). "Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you. And nations shall walk by your light" (ibid. 60:1, 3). "This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days: I will put my law within them, and write it on their hearts," etc. "They shall all know me, from the least to the greatest" (Jer. 31:33, 34).

units.la: similibusque locis non tantùm potentia, sed ipse etiam actus Deum salutariter cognoscendi & credendi, Gratiæ Foederis Dei accepta fertur; neque quoad potentiam & suasionem duntaxat, sed etiam quoad actum, persuasionem & convictionem. Nam & certis duntaxat hominibus foederis filiis, & à Deo doctis, Esaj. LIV. 13. quibus brachium Jehovæ revelatur, ibid. LIII. 1. in medio eorum, & in corde ponendo, imò, ut constantiam, perennitatem & efficaciam agnoscamus, ei, veluti digito Dei, adeóque ab ipso Deo inscribendo, & individuo nexu cum reliquis novi Foederis ἀλεονεξίημαται, cujusmodi inprimis adoptio & remissio peccatorum, Jerem. XXXI. 33. 34. Timor Dei, & via una ad timendum Deum, ibid. XXXII. 38. 40. Spiritus Dei efficiens, ut in statutis Dei ambulemus, jura ejus observemus & ea faciamus, Ezech. XXXVI. 27. promittitur. Frustra enim talia de gratia sufficiente, illustriori quadam motione, imò efficaci etiam apud eos, qui non resistunt, vel obicem ponunt, explicari, abundè in loco, quo efficaciam gratiæ vocationis adversus ejusmodi χεηστόνυπτα vindicavimus, veritati à nobis datum est. Quis enim regeneranti, Joh. III. 5. 1. Petr. I. 23. potenter trahenti, Joh. VI. 44. & superexcellentem magnitudinem potentiæ Dei erga credentes secundum efficaciam roboris virium Dei, quas in Christo ex mortuis resuscitando exeruit, Eph. I. 19. 20. demonstranti Deo resistere, quis pessulum obdere, obicem ponere potis est?
units.tr: By these and similar passages there is ascribed to the grace of God's covenant not only the power but the very act of knowing and believing God savingly; and this not only as to power and persuasion but also as to the act, the persuasion and the conviction. For it is promised to those who are certain sons of the covenant and taught by God (Isa. 54:13), to whom "the arm of the LORD is revealed" (ibid. 53:1), that he will place it in their midst and in their heart, and indeed that, so that we may recognise its constancy, perpetuity and efficacy, he will write it upon them as with the finger of God, and so by God himself, and in indivisible connection with the other benefits of the new covenant, of which the chief are "adoption and forgiveness of sins" (Jer. 31:33, 34), "the fear of God" and "one way to fear God" (ibid. 32:38, 40), and "the Spirit of God working that we walk in God's statutes, observe his judgments and do them" (Ezek. 36:27). For it is in vain that such things are explained of a sufficient grace, with a certain more illustrious motion, indeed efficacious even among those who do not resist or place an obstacle; this has been amply answered in the place where we vindicated the efficacy of the grace of calling against such [fine-sounding talkers] [χρηστολόγους]. For who is able to resist him who regenerates (John 3:5; 1 Pet. 1:23), who powerfully draws (John 6:44), and who demonstrates "the surpassing greatness of his power toward those who believe, according to the working of the strength of his might, which he exerted in Christ when he raised him from the dead" (Eph. 1:19, 20)? Who can bolt the door against him, or place an obstacle in his way?

units.la: XIII. Neque tantùm fidem, sed etiam perseverantem fidem & obedientiam Foedus Gratiæ in Christo sancitum promittit. Nam ante omnia promittit inscriptionem legis fidei in cor foederatorum, Jerem. XXXI. 33. Quæ inscriptio præter fidei donationem etiam gratiæ foederalis vim perpetuam notat, quia in universum usus & scopus Scripturæ est, ut perennitati serviat, cùm contra volet irrevocabile verbum. Ideo Deus scribi jubet, quæ perpetua esse vult. Scribite vobis canticum istud, pone illud in ore eorum, ut sit mihi in testem contra filios Israel, Deut. XXXI. 19. Scribe in tabula, & in libro scribe eam, ut sit in die novissimo in testimonium usque in seculum, Esaj. XXX. 8. Et Jobus: Utinam aliquò scriberentur verba mea! Utinam in libro exararentur! Cum stylo ferreo & plumbo in perpetuum rupi inciderentur! Job. XIX. 23. 24. Alludit autem promissio illa foederalis ad legem tabulis lapideis inscriptam, ne unquam in oblivionem veniret; innuitque legem fidei in tabulis cordis inscriptam tandiu duraturam, quandiu cor ipsum. Misericordia & veritas ne deserant te. Liga eas ad guttur tuum, כתבם על לוח לבך scribe eas in tabula cordis tui, Prov. III. 3. Eodem sensu peccatum Juda scriptum stylo ferreo, & ungue adamantino, sculpta in tabula cordis eorum dicitur, Jerem. XVII. 1. Planè igitur habitus fidei à Deo donatus indelebilis, perseverans & perpetuus indicatur. Sic enim etiam cùm ἐγγαν νόμω opus legis manu Providentiæ Dei γεγραμμένον ἐν καρδίαις scriptum in cordibus hominum, Rom. II. 15. dicitur, ejusdem perpetuitas & constantia, atque indelebilis tenor significatur. Metaphoram in eodem argumento clarissimis verbis sic Deus ipse explicat: Dabo iis cor unum & viam unam, ut timeant me cunctis diebus.
units.tr: XIII. The covenant of grace sealed in Christ promises not only faith but also persevering faith and obedience. First of all it promises the inscribing of the law of faith in the hearts of the covenanted, Jer. 31:33. Besides the gift of faith, this inscribing also signifies the lasting force of the covenant of grace, since the whole use and purpose of Scripture is to serve permanence, just as an irrevocable word wills to be permanent. For this reason God orders things to be written that he wills to be perpetual: Write this song for yourselves, and put it in their mouth, that it may be a witness for me against the children of Israel, Deut. 31:19. Write it on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for a testimony in the last day for ever, Isa. 30:8. And Job says: Oh that my words were written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book! That with an iron pen and lead they were graven in the rock for ever!, Job 19:23-24. That covenant promise alludes to the law inscribed on tablets of stone, so that it should never fall into oblivion; and it implies that the law of faith, inscribed on the tablets of the heart, will last as long as the heart itself. Let mercy and truth not forsake you. Bind them about your neck; write them upon the tablet of your heart [כתבם על לוח לבך], Prov. 3:3. In the same sense the sin of Judah is said to be written with an iron pen and with a diamond point, graven upon the tablet of their heart, Jer. 17:1. Clearly, then, the habit of faith given by God is indicated as indelible, persevering and perpetual. So too, when the work of the law is said to be written [γεγραμμένον] in the hearts of men by the hand of God's providence, Rom. 2:15, its permanence and constancy and its indelible tenor are signified. God himself explains this metaphor in the same matter in the clearest words: I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me all their days.

units.la: Et quidem fidei atque obedientiæ perseverantis. Feriam quoque cum iis foedus perpetuum, quòd non aversurus sim me ab ipsis, ut benefaciam iis, & timorem meum dabo in corde eorum, ut non recedant à me, Jerem. XXXII. 39. 40. Quæ augustiora & difertiora longè sunt, quam ut de solo officio foederatorum, & intentione Dei explicari possint. Eventus enim, & opus ipsum clarissimè promittitur, neque vel respectu quorundam, sed omnium fidelium; vel vi præscientiæ Dei, providentis, multos perseveraturos, neque Deum deserturos, sed vi gratiæ infallibiliter operantis. Nam juxta foedus omnes cognoscent Deum à minimo usque ad maximum, & omnium horum peccatorum non recordabitur amplius, ib. XXXI. 34. Omnes ergo etiam foederati vi foederis gratiæ perseverabunt. Et Deus inscriptionem fidei, & inditionem timoris sui non prædicit ut opus alienum, sed promittit ut suum. Ac ne prædicere quidem, ceu præscitam potuit, quia extra gratuitam donationem ejus nulla præscientiæ causa, adeoque nec certitudo locum habere potuit. Præterea perseverantia verbis illis non ut verisimilis, sed ut certa promittitur, tum quia ipsa inscriptio in cor, & timoris datio promittitur: tum quia habituum, quales fides & timor Dei sunt, ea vis est, ut certò perdurent, præsertim ubi manu ipsius Dei inscribuntur: tum quia tale cor Deus promittit, ut reverituri sint Jehovam cunctis diebus, ut bene sit iis, & filiis eorum, tum quia ratio perpetuitatis foederis, quam Deus addit; quòd se non fit aversurus ab ipsis, quò minùs, ceu foederatus conjunctissimus iis benefaciat, & timorem cordi eorum inditurus sit, ne a se recedant; quibus verbis mutua foederatorum sibi indivulsè adhærentium conjunctio notatur, non verisimilem, sed certam perseverantiam postulat. Ideo subjungit Deus. Lætabor super eos benefaciendo iis, & plantabo eos in terra hac (mystica, Ecclesia N. T.) באמת in veritate, firmitudine, toto corde meo, & tota anima mea, ibid. XXXII. 41.
units.tr: And indeed this is the perseverance of faith and obedience. I will also make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them to do them good; and I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me, Jer. 32:39-40. These words are far too lofty and explicit to be explained as referring only to the duty of the covenanted or to God's intention. The outcome and the work itself is promised plainly, and not with respect to some only but to all the faithful. It is not that, by the force of God's foreknowledge, many are foreseen to persevere and not to forsake God, but that they are kept by the power of grace working infallibly. For according to the covenant all shall know God, from the least to the greatest, and he will remember their sins no more, ibid. 31:34. Therefore all the covenanted will persevere by the force of the covenant of grace. And God does not foretell the inscribing of faith and the implanting of his fear as another's work, but promises them as his own. Nor could he foretell them as foreseen, for outside his free gift there is no cause of foreknowledge, and so no certainty could have a place. Moreover, perseverance is promised in those words not as probable but as certain: partly because the inscribing in the heart and the giving of the fear are themselves promised; partly because such habits as faith and the fear of God have such a force that they certainly endure, especially where they are inscribed by the very hand of God; partly because God promises a heart such that they will revere Jehovah all their days, so that it may go well with them and their children; and partly because of the reason for the perpetuity of the covenant that God adds, namely that he will not turn away from them, so that, as a most closely joined covenant partner, he may do them good, and will put his fear in their hearts so that they do not depart from him. By these words the mutual conjunction of the covenanted, who cling inseparably together, is marked, and it requires not a probable but a certain perseverance. Therefore God adds: I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land [mystical, the Church of the New Testament] in truth [באמת], in firmness, with my whole heart and my whole soul, ibid. 32:41.

units.la: XIV. Neque aliam ob causam foedus ipsum gratiæ בריח עולם foedus æternum, perinde ut Testamentum, ex quo foedus gratiæ oritur, Διαθήκη αἰωνιος Testamentum æternum, Heb. XIII. 20. appellatur. Feriam vobiscum foedus æternum, בריח עולם ... gratias fideles Davidis, seu permanentes, Esaj. LV. 3. Feriam cum iis foedus æternum, Jerem. XXXII. 40. Dispo-nit enim de gratia firma & constante. In seculum custodiam ei misericordiam meam, & foedus meum ליעולם firmum erit ipsi, Psal. LXXXIX. 29. Quomodo verò foedus æternum dici potest, si gratia in eo promissa ab arbitrio hominis in horas mutabilis pendet, & vim suam æternam in cordibus foederatorum non explicat? Dilutum enim planè est, quòd æternum dici respectu Dei sub conditione fidei perseverantis, salutem promittentis, non respectu hominis, utpote qui non perseverans illud irritum facere possit. Nam formula foederis novum illud foedus à veteri distinguit, quòd Patres hoc irritum fecerint, Jerem. XXXI. 31. innuens, foederatos novi foederis neutiquam irritum illud facturos. Et promissiones foederis gratiæ ejusmodi sunt, ut æternitatem foederis etiam quoad foederatorum perseverantiam includant. Montes movebunt sese, & colles nutabunt. Mi-
units.tr: XIV. For no other reason the covenant of grace itself is called an everlasting covenant [בריח עולם], just as the Testament from which the covenant of grace arises is called an eternal Testament [Διαθήκη αἰωνιος], Heb. 13:20. I will make with you an everlasting covenant [בריח עולם], the sure mercies of David, that is, those that endure, Isa. 55:3. I will make with them an everlasting covenant, Jer. 32:40. For it disposes concerning a grace that is firm and constant. I will keep my mercy for him for ever, and my covenant shall stand fast with him [ליעולם], Ps. 89:29. But how can it be called an everlasting covenant if the grace promised in it depends on the will of man, which changes from hour to hour, and does not exert its eternal force in the hearts of the covenanted? It is plainly false to say that it is called eternal with respect to God, under the condition of persevering faith that promises salvation, but not with respect to man, who by not persevering could make it void. For the formula of the covenant distinguishes the new covenant from the old in that the Fathers made that one void, Jer. 31:31, implying that the covenanted of the new covenant will by no means make it void. And the promises of the covenant of grace are such that they include the eternity of the covenant also as regards the perseverance of the covenanted. The mountains shall depart, and the hills shall be removed; but my mercy shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, Isa. 54:10.

units.la: sericordia autem mea non recedet, & foedus pacis mea ... non nutabit, Esaj. LIV. 10. Quo fundamento nixus Apostolus dixit: Dona Dei gratuita & vocationem esse ἀμεταμέλητα sine pœnitentia, hoc est, nunquam mutari, Rom. XI. 29. Cujus immutabilitatis ratio est in ipsa rei natura, quia scilicet dona hæc à mera gratia, favore, proposito & beneplacito Dei, Eph. I. 9. 11. 2. Tim. I. 9. pendent. Nam quod Deus facit ex proposito, id mutari nisi eodem proposito & beneplacito mutato potest.
units.tr: On this foundation the Apostle rests when he says: The gifts and calling of God are without repentance [ἀμεταμέλητα], that is, never to be changed, Rom. 11:29. The reason for this immutability lies in the very nature of the matter, namely that these gifts depend on the mere grace, favour, purpose and good pleasure of God, Eph. 1:9, 11; 2 Tim. 1:9. For what God does from his purpose can be changed only if that same purpose and good pleasure is changed.

units.la: XV. Etiam modus ille, quo Deus juxta Foedus Gratiæ fidem confervat & perennem reddit, ejusdem Perseverantiam demonstrat. Consistit enim ille tum in continuo influxu gratiæ in foederatos: tum in protectione eorundem adversus causas destruentes. Nam quoad influxum continuum gratiæ, promittitur foederatis inhabitatio Spiritus S. in cordibus. Spiritum meum ponam in medio vestri, efficiamque, ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, Ezech. XXXVI. 27. hoc est, non ut ambulare possitis, si vultis, sed ut velitis. Nam ipsius voluntatis flexio includitur: & Deus dicit faciam, efficiam, hoc est, ἐνεργήσω efficaciter operabor, Phil. II. 13. ut ambuletis. Quod Deus se facturum promittit, illud certò fit, quia ejus vis infinita est. Consilium meum stabit, & omne beneplacitum faciam, Esaj. XLVI. 10. Neque nulla emphasis est in verbo quod & præteriti temporis rei certitudinem notat, & simul complementum operis significat, quia consummationem operis notat. Quievit Deus ab opere, quod creavit ad faciendum, seu perficiendum, Genes. II. 3. Opus Rupis nostræ est perfectum, Deut. XXXII. 4. Sed clarius etiam Deus dicit: Me quod attiner, hoc est foedus meum cum ipsis: Spiritus meus, qui est super te, & verba mea, quæ posui in ore tuo, non recedent ab ore tuo, & ab ore Seminis tui, & ab ore Seminis Seminis tui, à nunc & in seculum, Esaj. LIX. 21. Tam diserta & absoluta promissio hæc est, ut obscurari nullo modo possit. Quam etiam Christus ipse confirmavit, dicens: Et ego rogabo Patrem, & alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ἵνα μένῃ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ut maneat vobiscum in seculum, Joh. XIV. 16.
units.tr: XV. The very manner in which God, according to the covenant of grace, preserves faith and makes it lasting also demonstrates its perseverance. For it consists partly in a continuous inflow of grace into the covenanted, and partly in the protection of the same against causes that destroy it. As for the continuous inflow of grace, the covenanted are promised the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in their hearts: I will put my Spirit in the midst of you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, Ezek. 36:27. That is, not that you may be able to walk if you will, but that you will. For the very bending of the will is included, and God says I will cause, that is, I will work effectually [ἐνεργήσω], Phil. 2:13, that you may walk. What God promises that he will do certainly happens, because his power is infinite: My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure, Isa. 46:10. Nor is there no emphasis in the verb, which both signifies the certainty of a thing in the past tense and at the same time signifies the completion of the work, because it marks the consummation of the work. God rested from all his work which he had created to make, that is, to perfect, Gen. 2:3. The work of our Rock is perfect, Deut. 32:4. But God says even more clearly: As for me, this is my covenant with them: my Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your seed, nor out of the mouth of your seed's seed, from henceforth and for ever, Isa. 59:21. This promise is so plain and absolute that it can in no way be obscured. Christ himself also confirmed it, saying: And I will pray the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever [ἵνα μένῃ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα], John 14:16.

units.la: XVI. Protectionem foederatorum adversus Perseverantiæ hostes, seu causas destruentes, Christus his verbis docet: Oves meæ audiunt vocem meam, & ego cognosco eas, & me sequuntur. Et ego do ipsis vitam æternam, & non peribunt in æternum, & nemo eas rapiet ex manu mea. Pater meus; qui eas dedit mihi, major me est, & nemo potest eas rapere ex manu Patris. Pater & ego unum sumus, Joh. X. 27–30. Si nemo oves Christi & Patris ex manu utriusque, qui ἐν unum sunt, adeoque unam etiam manum & potentiam habent, rapere potest, custodiuntur igitur, & proteguntur, ut nemo eas rapiat, vel rapere possit. At qui fideles, per fidem oves Christi, & Pastorem hunc suum sequentes, mox deficere à fide, perire possunt, illi & rapi ex manu Patris & Filii possunt, & deficientes rapiuntur. Vanum est, quod Perseverantiæ adversarii regerunt, neminem raptum oves è manu Patris & Christi, quandiu per fidem sunt & manent oves Patris & Christi, & sponte sua è manu Pastoris non aufugiunt. giunt. Nam hoc ipsum negat Christus, ajens, non rapi, nec posse rapi oves è manu sua, adeóque nec fidem abjicere, & sponte aufugere. Nam qui hoc faciunt, eos Sathanas Tentator, & propria caro, quæ ceu hostis domesticus, ἀντικεῖται πνεύματι Spiritui repugnat, Gal. V. 17. & στρατεύεται πρὸς τὴν ψυχήν militat adversus animam, 1. Pet. II. 11. rapit è manu Patris & Christi. Est enim ἀρπαγμὸς raptus ille, interprete Christo, πλάνη seductio, Matth. XXIV. 24. Atqui quisque tentatur (seducitur) à propria concupiscentia extractus & inescatus, &c. Μὴ πλανᾶσθε Ne errate, seducimini, Jac. I. 13. 16. Ideo etiam τῇ ἀδικίᾳ injustitiæ, & τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ peccato Scriptura ἀπάτῃ seductionem tribuit, 2. Thessal. II. 10. Hebr. III. 13. Etiam reprobi sponte Diabolo se dedentes, & in castra ejus confugientes, rapiuntur ab eodem: & Adamus sponte peccans à Sathana, homicida ab initio, raptus Deóque ereptus est. Nullus enim carne, domestico hoste, periculosior hostis est, quia semper adversus Spiritum concupiicit, & fomes peccati est, suscipiens Sathanæ & mundi igniculos immissos, nil sine carne concupiscente valituros. Vel igitur Christus fideles suos consolaturus nihil iis promisit, vel promisit etiam, fore ut nec à propria carne transversi abripiantur. Neque tantùm Christus dixit: Nemo oves meas rapiet è manu mea: sed etiam; Ego do ipsis vitam æternam.
units.tr: XVI. Christ teaches the protection of the covenanted against the enemies of perseverance, or the destroyers of its causes, in these words: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. And I give unto them eternal life, and they shall never perish, and no one shall pluck them out of my hand. My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to pluck them out of the Father's hand. I and the Father are one, John 10:27–30. If no one can snatch the sheep of the Father and of Christ out of the hand of both, who are one and so have one hand and one power, then they are kept and protected so that no one snatches them or can snatch them. But if the faithful, who through faith are sheep of Christ and follow their Shepherd, can soon fall from faith and perish, then they can be snatched out of the hand of the Father and the Son, and those who fall away are snatched. What the adversaries of perseverance reply is vain, namely that no one snatches the sheep out of the hand of the Father and Christ as long as they are, and remain through faith, sheep of the Father and Christ, and do not of their own accord flee from the hand of the Shepherd. For Christ himself denies this, saying that no one snatches or can snatch his sheep out of his hand, and so neither do they cast off faith and flee of their own will. For those who do this, Satan the Tempter and their own flesh, which as a domestic enemy lusts against the Spirit, Gal. 5:17, and wars against the soul, 1 Pet. 2:11, snatch away from the hand of the Father and Christ. For that snatching is, in Christ's own interpretation, deception [πλάνη], seduction, Matt. 24:24. Yet each person is tempted (seduced) when drawn away and enticed by his own lust, etc. Do not err [Μὴ πλανᾶσθε], James 1:13, 16. Therefore Scripture also attributes seduction to unrighteousness [τῇ ἀδικίᾳ] and to sin [τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ], 2 Thess. 2:10; Heb. 3:13. Even the reprobate, who willingly give themselves over to the Devil and flee into his camp, are snatched by him; and Adam, sinning willingly, was snatched by Satan, a murderer from the beginning, and taken away from God. For no enemy is more dangerous than the flesh, the domestic enemy, because it always lusts against the Spirit, and it is the tinder of sin, receiving the sparks of Satan and the world cast into it, which would have no force without the lusting flesh. So either Christ, meaning to console his faithful, promised them nothing, or he promised also that they would not be carried off headlong by their own flesh. Nor did Christ say only: No one shall pluck my sheep out of my hand, but also: I give them eternal life.

units.la: XVII. Eandem Ecclesiæ totius, omniúmque adeò fidelium protectionem, & gratiam tum internè perficientem, tum externè protegentem Christus alibi quoque emphaticè promisit, dicens: Super hanc petram (me ipsum) ædificabo Ecclesiam, & portæ inferorum non prævalebunt ei, Matth. XVI. 18. Quod etiam Deus apud Prophetam his verbis promisit: Ecce fundo in Sion lapidem, lapidem explorationis, angulum pretiosissimi, fundati fundatissimi. Credens non præcipitabit πρὸς ὑπῳεία tanquam confusus, Esaj. XXVIII. 16. Et alibi: Ædificabitur Jehova Civitas, (Ecclesia) Non evelletur, nec destruetur ultra in seculum, Jerem. XXXI. 38 40. Cùm Ecclesia vocatorum fidelium cœtus sit, dubitari nequit, quin eadem fidelium omnium, quæ Ecclesiæ est, ratio sit. Si igitur Christus Ecclesiæ toti pro petra, & quidem invicta, cui inferorum portæ prævalere non possunt, est, singulis vocatis fidelibus talem se gerat oportet. Protegit ergo singulos adversus hostes spirituales omnes, ipsasque inferni portas, hoc est, vel inferni robur & ὀχυρώματα propugnacula, quia robur civitatis in portis ejus est, quibus apertis civitas ipsa victa est; vel inferni incolas, portis ejus velut inclusos, & qui ex iis egrediuntur; cujusmodi Sathanas, mundus & caro sunt; & ut alii interpretantur, mors ipsa, ultimus hostis, omnium præcedentium cumulus. Si fideles, quibus perpetua cum inferni portis, Sathana, mundo, carne & morte ipsa conflictatio est, à fide deficere, non perseverare, & perire possunt, inferorum portæ illis prævalent, & potentior infernus ad eos perdendum, quàm Deus ad protegendum est. Frivolum est, quòd promissionem illam cum conditione, si voluerit, intelligendam esse, Remonstrantes oggerunt. Non enim Christus dixit: Ædificabo Ecclesiam meam, si voluerit; & non prævalebunt ei portæ inferni, si voluerit. Sed totum ædificationis & invictæ constantiæ opus in solidum & absolutè uni soli que Christo, qui κατεσκεύασεν τὸν οἶκον constr uxit domum suam, Hebr. III. 3. acceptum fertur. Accedit tum architecti Christi omnipotentia, in cujus manu homines velut lapides pro beneplacito & summo robore ejus aptandi, & petræ superstruendi sunt: tum operis ipsius, constructionis Ecclesiæ, ceu ædificii spiritualis per collationem fidei, lapidum vivificationem, & cum Christo per fidem perseverantem unionem, ratio: tum operatio Christi, qui ipse sic Ecclesiam & fideles ædificat. Nec solida hæc ratio, nec certa promissio erit, si operationis illius eventus ex humano arbitrio suspenditur.
units.tr: XVII. Christ also elsewhere emphatically promised the same protection and grace of the whole Church, and indeed of all the faithful, both inwardly perfecting them and outwardly guarding them, saying: Upon this rock (myself) I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it, Matt. 16:18. God also promised this through the Prophet in these words: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious corner stone, a firmly founded foundation. He who believes shall not make haste [πρὸς ὑπῳεία], as one thrown into confusion, Isa. 28:16. And elsewhere: The LORD shall build the City (the Church); it shall not be plucked up nor destroyed any more for ever, Jer. 31:38–40. Since the Church is an assembly of called believers, there can be no doubt that the same reasoning holds for all the faithful who make up the Church. If, then, Christ is to the whole Church a rock, and indeed an unconquered one, against which the gates of hell cannot prevail, he must behave in the same way toward each called believer. He therefore protects each one against all spiritual enemies, and the very gates of hell. These gates are either the strength of hell and its strongholds (bulwarks), since the strength of a city lies in its gates, and once they are opened the city itself is conquered; or the inhabitants of hell, as it were shut in by its gates, and those who come out of them, such as Satan, the world and the flesh; and, as others interpret, death itself, the last enemy, the sum of all the preceding. If the faithful, who face perpetual conflict with the gates of hell, Satan, the world, the flesh and death itself, could fall from faith, not persevere, and perish, then the gates of hell would prevail over them, and hell would be stronger to destroy them than God is to protect them. The Remonstrants' objection, that the promise is to be understood with the condition "if he wills", is frivolous. For Christ did not say: I will build my Church, if he wills; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it, if he wills. Rather, the whole work of building and of invincible constancy is ascribed in full and absolutely to Christ alone, who has built the house [κατεσκεύασεν τὸν οἶκον], Heb. 3:3. Added to this is the reason drawn from the omnipotence of Christ the architect, in whose hand men are to be fitted like stones, at his good pleasure and by his supreme strength, and built upon the rock; then the reason drawn from the work itself, the construction of the Church as a spiritual edifice, through the bestowal of faith, the quickening of the stones, and union with Christ through persevering faith; and finally the working of Christ, who himself so builds the Church and the faithful. Nor will this reasoning be solid, nor this promise certain, if the outcome of that working depends on human choice.

units.la: XVIII. Potens illud præsidium, quo sic Deus credentes custodit & sustentat, ut ad salutem denique eluctentur, etiam S. Petrus sic explicat: Hæreditas incorruptibilis, &c. servata est in Cœlo nobis, qui potentia Dei (φρουρουμένοι) custodimur per fidem ad salutem, quæ parata est, ut reveletur in ultimo tempore, 1. Petr. I. 4. 5. Fidelium igitur spes viva fundatur in potentia Dei, quæ ipsorum φρουρά custodia, præsidium est, quo veluti circumvallantur, custodiuntur, & ad æternam vitam conservantur; & quidem διά πίστεως per fidem, per quam sentimus, experimur & δοκιμὴν accipimus, nos custodiri potentia Dei ad salutem. Non enim, quæ adversantium subtilis glossa est, hoc sibi vult S. Petrus, quando credimus, nostro scilicet arbitrio, tum nos accipere animum heroicum, & per eum custodiri, dummodo velimus; sed hoc potiùs, eos, qui sanctificati, & ad obedientiam regeniti sunt, potentiæ Dei præsidio custodiri & conservari in fide; & fidei hac conservatione in iisdem eos invictos, & ab omni malo tutos præstari, atque ad salutem custodiri, quod non fieret, si fides eorum excideret; denique eos per fidem custodiri, quia fides hanc Dei custodiam nobis conciliat. Sicut enim fides vincit mundum, 1. Joh. V. 4. 5. ita Dei præsidium nobis præstat. Nam quod justificat, etiam conservationem Dei conciliat. Deus eorum, quos justificat, clypeus est, & omne telum & linguam, quæ contra ipsos est, pudefacit, Esaj. LIV. 17. Fidei enim est dicere: Ecce Deus est salus mea, securus ero; & non pavebo. Nam robur meum & cantus est Jah Jehova: & factus est mihi salutì, ibid. XII. 2. Quæ gloriatio consentanea est dicto Dei: Tantùm in Jehova (de me dixit) justitiæ & robur. Ad illum accedet omnis, & pudefient omnes excandescentes in eum. In Jehova justificabuntur & gloriabuntur omne semen Israelis, ibid. XLV. 24. 25.
units.tr: XVIII. St Peter also explains that mighty protection by which God keeps and sustains believers, so that at last they struggle through to salvation: An inheritance incorruptible, etc., is reserved in heaven for us, who by the power of God are kept [φρουρουμένοι] through faith unto salvation, which is ready to be revealed in the last time, 1 Pet. 1:4, 5. The living hope of believers is therefore founded in the power of God, which is their guard [φρουρά], the defence by which they are, as it were, encircled, kept and preserved to eternal life. This is indeed through faith [διά πίστεως], through which we perceive, experience and receive proof [δοκιμήν] that we are kept by the power of God unto salvation. For St Peter does not mean, as the subtle gloss of the adversaries has it, that when we believe, by our own choice, we then receive a heroic spirit and are kept by it, provided we are willing. He means rather that those who have been sanctified and begotten again to obedience are guarded and preserved in faith by the protection of God's power; that by this preservation they are made invincible in faith and safe from every evil, and kept unto salvation, which would not happen if their faith fell away; and finally, that they are kept through faith, because faith secures for us this custody of God. For as faith overcomes the world, 1 John 5:4, 5, so it obtains God's protection for us. What justifies also secures God's preservation. God is the shield of those whom he justifies, and he puts to shame every weapon and tongue that is raised against them, Isa. 54:17. For it belongs to faith to say: Behold, God is my salvation; I shall be secure, and shall not fear; for the LORD JAH is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation, ibid. 12:2. This boasting agrees with God's word: Only in the LORD (he said of me) are righteousness and strength. To him shall all come, and all who are inflamed against him shall be put to shame. In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified and glory, ibid. 45:24, 25.

units.la: XIX. Fuerunt promissiones Fœderis Gratiæ Christo Mediatore initi, ex quibus Perseverantia Sanctorum stabilitur. Accedit promissionum earundem confirmatio gemina: prior in modo συγκριτικῷ comparativo, quo illæ in Scriptura proponuntur; posterior in Factis & Signis consistens. Quoad priorem, Scriptura imagines constantiæ fœderis & promissionum ejus ex terra & cœlo petit. Comparat enim illud cum iis dispositionibus, quæ in terra apud homines, & in Cœlo apud Deum perpetuam vim habent. In terra apud homines in pactis δι- αθηκαις seu mutuis nullum conjugio sanctius; in pactis verò μονο-διαθηκαις seu non-mutuis nullum TestaTestamento firmius est. Utroque emblemate Scriptura utitur, atque sic de indubitata foederis Gratiae constantia certos reddit.
units.tr: XIX. There were promises of the Covenant of Grace entered into with Christ the Mediator, and by these the perseverance of the saints is established. Two confirmations of these same promises are added. The first is comparative συγκριτικῷ [comparative], in the way Scripture sets them out; the second consists in Deeds and Signs. As to the first, Scripture draws its images of the constancy of the covenant and its promises from earth and heaven. It compares the covenant with those arrangements which have a perpetual force among men on earth and with God in heaven. On earth, among men, in δι- αθηκαις [covenants] that are mutual, nothing is more sacred than marriage; in μονο-διαθηκαις [covenants] that are not mutual, nothing is firmer than a testament. Scripture uses both emblems, and so makes us certain of the undoubted constancy of the covenant of grace.

units.la: XX. Cum conjugio enim foedus hoc diserte comparat. Pangam cum illis foedus &c. Et desponsabo te mihi in seculum ; & desponsabo te mihi in justitia & in judicio, & in gratia & in misericordia. Et desponsabo te mihi in fide, & cognosces Jehovam, Hos. II.18.19.20. Relinquet homo Patrem & matrem, & adhaerebit uxori suae, & erunt duo in unam carnem. Mysterium hoc magnum est. Ego vero dico in Christum, & in Ecclesiam, Ephes. V.31.32. Sanctissimum conjugale foedus est, quo sic conjuges conglutinantur, & in societatem individuam & indivulsam coalescunt, ut rebus integris sola morte vinculum dissolvi, & conjuges separari possint. Potest nihilominus corporale conjugium, violata matrimonii fide per adulterium, rumpi. Neque in potestate unius conjugis est, alterius fidem illibatam conservare. Sed diversa conjugii spiritualis ratio est, in quo pars altera, Deus, Christus sponsam suam, concessa veluti dote quadam & tessera perseverantiae gratia, conservare potest & vult, ne in spirituale adulterium incidens a se divelli & separari possit. Desponsat enim sibi fideles לעולם in seculum, adeoque promittit, quod eos, ceu uxorem suam sibi perpetim affixam conservaturus sit, & quod nullus filiorum Dei per ἐνέχυρον τῆς ἀπαλλαγῆς grassantem a conjugio eo abducendus sit. Et desponsat illos לי sibi uni soli que, non passurus, ut fiat conjux alterius, qui non est, quod ipse est. Et arrham, dotem atque tesseram conjugalem ei dat non bona terrestria, lanam, linum, & similia, sed longe majora, צדקה justitiam, remissionem peccatorum, & adoptionem in filios; משפט judicium, quo peccatum in Christo judicatum est, & tum Deus per ejus obedientiam demonstratus est peccati ofor, & justificatus est ut recte justificans impium in Filio; חסד gratiam, propositum & beneplacitum non tantum justificandi, sed etiam sanctificandi, conservandi & glorificandi, & רחמים miserationes, voluntatem consolandi in afflictionibus etiam per peccata accersitis, remunerandi omnem passionem pro nomine ejus, & ut poenitudine afficiatur super servis suis, Deut.
