XXXII.36. A parte Sponsae Ecclesiae est, אמונה fides, per quam justitia, judicium & gratia cognoscuntur, & per ὁμολογίαν Deo conjugium cum oblatione illarum dotum postulanti respondetur. Sicut enim per fidem conjugium cum Deo, Ecclesiae Sponso, contrahimus; ita per eandem participes fimus dotis justitiae, ut vitae aeternae haeredes ex gratia constituamur. Sed fidem illam non ex voluntate nostra, sed ex efficacia donationis Dei Ecclesiam habituram, Deus ipse significat, dicens: Desponsabo te mihi in fide; ubi non admonitio officii, a voluntate hominis suspensi & ejusdem exactio, sed prophetia & promissio continetur. Cujus etiam certum & indubitatum effectum statim Deus ipse promittit, dicens: Et cognosces Jehovam, ea videlicet notitia, in qua vita aeterna, Joh. XVII.3. collocatur. Neque etiam emphasi caret trina repetitio verborum, ארשתיך לי Desponsabo te mihi. Pondus addit, quod Deus in spirituali hoc matrimonio non tantum mariti, sed etiam factoris ἀγνόν induit. Ne timeas, quia non pudefies; & ne confundaris, quia non compungeris, sed pudoris adolescentiae tuae oblivisceris, & probri viduitatis tuae non recordaberis amplius בעליך Nam qui te in matrimonio habent, factores (creatores) tui sunt, Esai. LIV.4. Ubi plurali numero utitur ad innuendum mysterium Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. & insinuandam formationem non unam, velut Creatoris, Redemptoris & Sanctificatoris. Idem ergo maritus etiam עשה factor πλεωτής persector & consummator Sponsae est. Nam עשה Deo tributum consummationem operis significat, juxta superius dicta, & verba illa Dei: Omnem, qui nominatur a nomine meo בראתיו יצרתיו אף עשיתיו creavi eum, formavi eum, etiam feci, seu perfeci eum, Esai. XLIII.7. respondet ei vox Graeca καπηχάζεσθαι, qua utens Paulus Deum dicit καπηχαστικόν ἡμᾶς, hoc est, non tantum rem rudem & informem effingentem, expolientem, sed perficientem & absolventem, 2. Cor. V.5. Velle mihi adest, sed τὸ καλὸν ἐργάζεσθαι operari, perficere bonum non invenio, Rom. VII.18.
units.tr: XX. For it compares this covenant expressly with marriage: I will make a covenant with them, etc. And I will betroth you to me for ever [לעולם]; yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in judgement, and in grace and in mercies. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you shall know the LORD, Hos. 2:18-20. A man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery; but I speak concerning Christ and the Church, Eph. 5:31-32. Marriage is the most sacred covenant, by which spouses are so bound together and grow into a society so indivisible and inseparable that, with things remaining whole, the bond can be dissolved and the spouses parted only by death. Nevertheless, bodily marriage can be broken, when the faith of marriage is violated by adultery. Nor is it in the power of one spouse to keep the other's faith unimpaired. But the spiritual marriage is of a different kind, in which the other party, God, Christ, is able and willing to keep his bride, granting grace as a kind of dowry and pledge of perseverance, so that she, falling into spiritual adultery, cannot be torn and separated from him. For he betroths the faithful to himself in seculum [לעולם], for ever, and so promises that he will keep them, as his wife, fixed to himself perpetually, and that none of the sons of God is to be led away from that marriage by an ἐνέχυρον τῆς ἀπαλλαγῆς [pledge of release] roaming about. And he betroths them sibi [לי], to himself alone, not allowing that she become the spouse of another, who is not what he himself is. And he gives as earnest, dowry and marriage token to her not earthly goods, wool, linen and the like, but far greater things: justitiam [צדקה], righteousness, the forgiveness of sins and adoption as sons; judicium [משפט], judgement, by which sin was condemned in Christ, and God was then shown, through his obedience, to be just in punishing sin, and was justified as a righteous justifier of the ungodly in the Son; gratiam [חסד], grace, the purpose and good pleasure not only of justifying but also of sanctifying, preserving and glorifying; and miserationes [רחמים], mercies, the willingness to comfort in afflictions even those brought on by sins, and to reward every suffering for his name, and that he should be poenitudine afficiatur super servis suis [moved to repentance concerning his servants], Deut. 32:36. On the part of the bride, the Church, there is fides [אמונה], faith, through which righteousness, judgement and grace are known, and through ὁμολογίαν [confession] the marriage is answered to God, who asks for it with the offer of those dowries. For just as we contract marriage with God, the Church's Bridegroom, through fidem [faith], so through the same faith we become partakers of the dowry of righteousness, and are made heirs of eternal life by grace. But that fidem [faith] the Church will have not from our will but from the efficacy of God's gift, God himself declares, saying: I will betroth you to me in faith; where there is no reminder of duty, suspended on the will of man and demanding it, but prophecy and promise. And God himself promises at once a certain and undoubted effect of this, saying: And you shall know the LORD, namely with that knowledge in which vita aeterna [eternal life] is placed, John 17:3. Nor is the threefold repetition of the words ארשתיך לי [I will betroth you to me] without emphasis. It adds weight that God, in this spiritual marriage, puts on not only the character of mariti [husband], but also of factoris ἀγνόν [maker, pure]. Fear not, for you shall not be put to shame; neither be confounded, for you shall not be brought to reproach; but you shall forget the shame of your youth, and shall remember no more the reproach of your widowhood. For your husbands [בעליך] who have you in marriage are your makers (creators), Isa. 54:4. Where he uses the plural number, to hint at the mystery of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and to suggest a formation not single but as of Creator, Redeemer and Sanctifier. So the same maritus [husband] is also factor πλεωτής [maker, perfecter] and perfecter and consummator of the bride. For עשה [made] applied to God signifies the completion of a work, according to what was said above, and the words of God: Everyone who is called by my name, whom I have created, formed and also made, or perfected, him, Isa. 43:7. To this answers the Greek word καπηχάζεσθαι [to work out, to make to completion], which Paul uses when he says that God καπηχαστικόν ἡμᾶς [has made us for this very thing], that is, not merely shaping and polishing a rough and formless thing, but perfecting and completing it, 2 Cor. 5:5. To will is present with me, but to perform that which is good I find not, Rom. 7:18.

units.la: XXI. Dein etiam Foedus Gratiae non simplex, sed Testamentaria dispositio est, quia a Testamento aeterno gratiae oritur, & tum foedus, tum Testamentum eodem nomine ברית & διαθήκη venit, & κυρωσεως seu sanctio Foederis Gratiae talis est, qualis Testamenti est, scilicet per mortem Testatoris. Testamenti autem ratificati ea natura est, ut irritum fieri non possit. Fratres κατὰ ἄνθρωπον humanitus loquor; hominis Testamentum ratificatum ἀθετεῖ ἢ ἐπιδιαταττει nemo irritum facit, aut dispositione alia mutat, Gal. III.15. Ratificatum autem est Testamentum gratiae in morte Christi. Testamentum, in mortuis firmum est. Neque enim valet, quandiu testator vivit, Hebr. IX.17. In omni porro Testamento nominantur haeredes. Hi in foedere Gratiae Testamentario fideles sunt. Cum ergo Testamentum ratificatum irritum reddi, vel contraria dispositione mutari non possit, sequitur, neque haeredes in eo scriptos vel deleri, vel bonis, quae ipsis dispositia & delegata sunt, excidere & defraudari posse. Non enim in eo haeredes in genere tantum scribuntur ii, qui perseveranter crediturii sunt, fide eorum & perseverantia ab incertitudine arbitrii ipsorum suspensa; sed in individuo certi homines, quibus Testamento hoc certa haereditas promittitur. Alias ne Testamentum quidem foret.
units.tr: XXI. Next, the Covenant of Grace is not a simple arrangement but a testamentary disposition, because it arises from the eternal Testament of grace; and both covenant and testament are called by the same name, ברית [berith] and διαθήκη [diathēkē], and the κυρωσεως [ratification] or sanction of the covenant of grace is of the same kind as that of a testament, namely by the death of the testator. The nature of a ratified testament, however, is that it cannot be made void. Brothers, I speak after the manner of men: though it is only a man's covenant, yet when it is confirmed, no man disannulleth or addeth thereto, Gal. 3:15. The testament of grace, however, was ratified in the death of Christ. For a testament is of force after men are dead; otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth, Heb. 9:17. In every testament heirs are named. In the testamentary covenant of grace these are the faithful. Since therefore a ratified testament cannot be rendered void, nor changed by a contrary disposition, it follows that the heirs written in it can neither be erased nor cut off and defrauded of the goods which have been assigned and bequeathed to them. For in it the heirs are not written only in genere [in general], as those who will believe perseveringly, their faith and perseverance being left in suspense on the uncertainty of their own choice; but in the individuo [individually] certain men are named, to whom a certain inheritance is promised by this testament. Otherwise there would not even be a testament.

units.la: XXII. Sed conjugia & Testamenta humanae dispositiones sunt, quae qua tales, terrenae instabilitati obnoxiae sunt, nec satis immotam & inconcussam gratiae foederalis firmitatem adumbrant. Firmiores longe è Coelo, seu ex statutis Providentiae Divinae, quae ad consummationem usque mundi fixa & immota lege decurrunt, petitae sunt. Talia sunt tum lex in mundi creatione de perpetuo motu Solis ad lucem interdiu, & lunae ac stellarum noctu lata: tum decretum illud postdiluvianum de non immittendo amplius cataclysmo. Quae Providentiae Dei statuta eodem ברית foederis nomine, Gen. IX.11. Jerem. XXXIII.20. veniunt. De priore Jeremias: Sic dixit Jehova, qui dat Solem ad lucem diei, leges lunae & stellarum ad lucem noctis, &c. אם ימושו החקים האלה Si recedunt
units.tr: XXII. But marriages and testaments are human arrangements, which, as such, are subject to earthly instability, and do not sufficiently shadow forth the firm and unshaken stability of the covenant of grace. Far firmer things are sought è Coelo [from heaven], or from the ordinances of Providentiae Divinae [Divine Providence], which run on by a fixed and immovable law until the consummation of the world. Such are: the lex [law] laid down at the creatione [creation] of the world concerning the perpetual motion of the sun to give light by day, and of the moon and stars by night; and that decretum [decree] postdiluvianum [after the flood] not to send a cataclysm again. These ordinances of Divine Providence come under the same name of foederis [covenant], ברית [berith], Gen. 9:11; Jer. 33:20. Of the former Jeremiah says: Thus says the LORD, who gives the sun for a light by day, the ordinances of the moon and the stars for a light by night, etc. If these ordinances depart

units.la: Cum Testamento
units.tr: With the Testament

units.la: Cum stabilitate aeterna Providentia dunt statuta hæc à conspectu meo, ait Jehova, etiam semen Israelis (spirituale interna vocatione tale) cessabunt, ut non sint gens coram me, omnibus diebus, ibid. XXXI. 35. 36. Si irritum facere potestis Fœdus meum circa diem & noctem, ne sit tempus diurnum & nocturnum, etiam fœdus meum cum Davide servo meo irritum fiet, ne sit ei filius regnans in solio ejus, (germen illud, quod Davidi efflorescet vers. 15. & cui Deus daturus erat thronum Davidis Patris sui, Luc. I. 32.) & cum Levitis, Sacerdotibus, ministris meis (non typicis, sed spiritualibus, fidelibus, qui Sacerdotes justitia & salute induti, Psal. CXXXII. 16. & Sacerdotium Regale sunt, 1. Petr. II. 5.) Jerem. XXXIII. 20. 21. De posteriore sic Deus: בְּרִית נוֹחַ Aqua Noachi hoc mihi. Quemadmodum juravi, non transituras aquas Noachi terram: sic juravi, ne effervescam in te & increpem te. Nam montes decedent, & colles nutabunt, at gratia mea à te non recedet, & fœdus pacis mea non nutabit, ait miserator tuus Jehova, Esaj. LIV. 9. 10. Magni certè momenti modus ille est, quo collationes hæ institiuntur. Totus enim ad ingenerandam animis nostris ideam impossibilitatis exitii foederatorum compararatus est. Simili figura Poëtæ & Oratores utuntur; comparatione æquè impossibilium aliquid ἀτοπον vel ἀδύνατον arguentes. Eadem ratione Deus confirmat, tam impossibile esse, ut fideles & fœderati pereant, quàm impossibile est, ut ipse sua ipsius decreta rescindat, vel homo illa figere possit.
units.tr: With the eternal stability of Providence [...] these ordinances from before my face, says the LORD, then the seed of Israel also (spiritual, of such a kind by inward calling) shall cease, so that they shall not be a nation before me for all days, Jer. 31:35-36. If you can break my covenant of the day and my covenant of the night, so that there is not day and night in their season, then also my covenant with David my servant shall be broken, so that he shall not have a son to reign upon his throne (that branch which shall spring up for David, v. 15, and to whom God would give the throne of David his father, Luke 1:32), and with the Levites, the priests, my ministers (not typical, but spiritual, faithful ones, who are clothed with righteousness and salvation, Ps. 132:16, and are a royal priesthood, 1 Pet. 2:5), Jer. 33:20-21. Of the latter God speaks thus: בְּרִית נוֹחַ [the covenant of Noah] This is to me as the waters of Noah: as I have sworn that the waters of Noah shall no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be wroth with you nor rebuke you. For the mountains shall depart and the hills be removed, but my kindness shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, says the LORD your merciful one, Isa. 54:9-10. Certainly that manner by which these comparisons are instituted is of great weight. For it is wholly designed to engender in our minds the idea of the impossibility of the destruction of the covenanted. Poets and orators use a similar figure, arguing that something is ἀτοπον [absurd] or ἀδύνατον [impossible] by comparison with things equally impossible. In the same way God confirms that it is as impossible for the faithful and covenanted to perish as it is impossible for God to rescind his own decrees, or for man to fix them.

units.la: XXIII. Sequitur confirmatio promissionum fœderis Gratiæ ex Factis.
units.tr: XXIII. Follows the confirmation of the promises of the covenant of grace from deeds.

units.la: Deus enim amplissimam promissionibus suis fidem facturus, quicquid homines ad suarum promissionum, fœderalium inprimis, solenniorem corroborationem adhibent, cujusmodi Acta publica, Juramenta, Testes, Sacrificia, Monumenta sunt, ipse quoque adhibet. Acta publica quod attinet, solent promissiones fœderales inscribi Libris, Tabulis lapideis, æreis aliisque incidi. Etiam Deus leges Fœderis jussit scribi in Libro, qui inde Liber Fœderis, Exod. XXIV. 7. dicitur. Easdem digito suo tabulis lapideis inscripsit, quæ iccirco לוחות הברית tabulæ Fœderis, Deut. IX. 9. dicuntur. Triplex inprimis ille liber est, Scripturæ, Memoriæ, Vitæ vel Agni, & Cordis. In libro Scripturæ promissiones doni Perseverantiæ consignatæ sunt. Scribe tibi omnia verba, quibus alloquor te, in libro. Servient Jehovæ Deo suo. & Davidi Regi suo, quem excitabo ipsis. Eritis mihi populus: & ego ero vobis Deus, Jer. XXX. 2. 9. 22. In libro Memoriæ, Vitæ & Agni inscripsit nomina eorum, ad quos promissiones pertinent. Scriptum est בְּסֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן in libro memoriæ, seu commentario coram ipso, pro timentibus Jehovam, & cogitantibus de nomine ejus. Eruntque mihi, dicit Dominus exercituum, in die, qua ego facio, in peculium: & parcam iis, quemadmodum parcit quis filio suo servienti sibi, Malach. III. 16. 17. Hic liber Vitæ Phil. IV. 3. Apoc. XXI. 27. & liber vitæ Agni, ibid. XIII. 8. est, de quo alibi. Libro Cordis, seu tabulis carneis cordis, 2. Cor. III. 3. & conscientiæ Deus ipse legem suam inscribit, Jerem. XXXI. 34. qua de amore & cura ejus perpetua planè certi reddimur. Qui liber non literis, sed Divinis inspirationibus constat; non oculis legitur, sed corde sentitur, non atramento, sed Spiritu Dei vivi, 2. Cor. III. 3. testantis in corde fidelium eos esse filios Dei, heredes Dei, & coheredes Christi, Rom. VIII. 16. 17.
units.tr: God, who intends to give his promises the fullest assurance, also makes use of the means that men employ to strengthen their promises, especially covenant promises, such as public records, oaths, witnesses, sacrifices and memorials. As for public records, covenant promises are usually inscribed in books, on tablets of stone or bronze, and other such materials. God too commanded the laws of the covenant to be written in a book, which is therefore called the Book of the Covenant (Exod. 24:7). He inscribed them with his own finger on tablets of stone, which for that reason are called the tablets of the covenant [לוחות הברית] (Deut. 9:9). There are chiefly three such books: the book of Scripture, the book of memory, and the book of life or of the Lamb, and of the heart. In the book of Scripture the promises of the gift of perseverance are recorded: Write in a book all the words that I speak to you. They shall serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them. You shall be my people, and I will be your God (Jer. 30:2, 9, 22). In the book of memory, of life and of the Lamb, he has written the names of those to whom the promises belong: It is written in a book of remembrance [בְּסֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן], that is, a record kept before him, for those who fear the LORD and think upon his name. They shall be mine, says the LORD of hosts, on the day when I make them my own possession, and I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him (Mal. 3:16, 17). This is the book of life (Phil. 4:3; Rev. 21:27), and the book of life of the Lamb (ibid. 13:8), of which we speak elsewhere. In the book of the heart, or on the fleshy tablets of the heart (2 Cor. 3:3), and of conscience, God himself writes his law (Jer. 31:34), by which we are made utterly certain of his love and his unfailing care. This book consists not of letters but of divine inspirations; it is not read with the eyes but felt in the heart, not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God (2 Cor. 3:3), bearing witness in the hearts of believers that they are the children of God, heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ (Rom. 8:16, 17).

units.la: XXIV. Etiam juramento promissiones suas Deus confirmavit. Nam homines quidem per majorem jurant, & omnis ipsis controversiæ finis ad confirmationem, est jusjurandum. Qua in re ex abundante volens Deus ostendere immutabilitatem consilii sui heredibus promissionis, ἐμεσιτεύσατο ὅρκῳ juramento intercessit, ut per duas has res, quæ transponi non possunt, in quibus impossibile est mentiri Deum, validam inhortationem haberemus, qui confugimus ad illam spem expositam, Heb. VI. 16. 17. 18. Etenim non semel Deus juravit. Juravit enim Abrahamo. בִּי נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי Per me ipsum juravi, dixit Jehova, &c. Benedicendo benedicam tibi, & multiplicando multiplicabo semen tuum, &c. Genes. XXII. 16. 17. Etiam Davidi servo suo juravit, se in seculum stabilituruam semen ejus, &c. Psal. LXXXIX. 4. 5. Aquæ Noachi hoc mihi. Quemadmodum juravi, non transituras aquas terram: sic juravi ne effervescam in te, & increpem te, &c. Esaj. LIV. 9. Per me juravi. Prodiit ex ore meo justitia, verbum, quod non revocabitur. Mihi incurvabitur omne genu (electorum ex omnibus populis) & jurabit mihi omnis lingua. In Jehova justificabuntur & glorificabuntur totum semen Israel, ibid. XLV. 23. 25. Non potuisset verbis efficacioribus יִשְׁעִיהוּ עֵצָה consilium consultatum, ibid. XIV. 26. seu ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς immutabilitas consilii Dei exprimi. Jurat Deus, & per se maximum jurat; & ex ore jurantis verbum לֹא יָשׁוּב quod non revertetur, seu irrevocabile prodit, quòd omne (fidelium) genu non possit tantùm, si velit, sed certè se incurvaturum sit, atque sic ipso facto eos in Jehova justificatum & glorificatum iri. Si injuria est hominibus, qui flagitii nullius comperti sunt, jurantibus nolle credere, & propterea juramentum etiam humanum valet & firmitudinem habet, cùm tamen homo sit malus, mendax, nec Deum noverit, amet ac glorificet, sicut oportet; nulla supererit ratio dubitandi, quin Deo per se ipsum juranti, hoc est, nobis, ut credamus, vitam omnémque perfectionem suam commemoranti, & quasi obsidem veritatis suæ facienti & ostendenti, se eo, quod promisit, velle manifestum facere, quis ipse sit, & quæ ejus virtutes sint, sine omni exceptione credendum sit. Idque eò magis, quia nos jubet sibi juranti credere, & eo fine ut credamus ipsi, jurat. Denique quid jurata ab ipso Deo promissione firmius? Si igitur jurat, quòd certò Semini benedicere, adversus illud non effervescere velit, & quòd Semen illud sibi genu incurvaturum, justificandum & glorificandum sit, ejusdem perseverantia firmiori talo stare non posset.
units.tr: XXIV. God has also confirmed his promises with an oath. For men indeed swear by one greater than themselves, and an oath is for them the end of every dispute, as a confirmation. In this matter God, wishing to show more abundantly the immutability of his counsel to the heirs of the promise, interposed himself with an oath, so that through these two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we might have strong encouragement, we who have fled to lay hold of the hope set before us (Heb. 6:16–18). God did not swear only once. He swore to Abraham: By myself I have sworn, says the LORD, [בִּי נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי] that because you have done this... I will surely bless you and multiply your seed (Gen. 22:16, 17). He also swore to David his servant that he would establish his seed for ever (Ps. 89:3, 4). This is to me like the waters of Noah. As I swore that the waters of Noah would no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you (Isa. 54:9). By myself I have sworn; from my mouth has gone forth in righteousness a word that shall not return. To me every knee shall bow (that is, the elect from all peoples), and every tongue shall swear to me. In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified and glorified (ibid. 45:23, 25). The immutability of God's counsel could not have been expressed in more forceful words, [יִשְׁעִיהוּ עֵצָה] (ibid. 14:26), or the unchangeableness of his purpose [ἀμετάθετον τῆς βουλῆς]. God swears, and he swears by himself, the greatest being; and from the mouth of him who swears comes a word that will not return [לֹא יָשׁוּב], that is, an irrevocable word, that every knee (of believers) not only may bow, if he wishes, but certainly will bow, and thus by that very fact they will be justified and glorified in the LORD. If it is wrong for men to refuse to believe those who swear, men against whom no crime has been proved, and if for this reason even a human oath is valid and has firmness, although man is evil, a liar, and does not know God, love him and glorify him as he ought, then there will be no reason at all to doubt that we must believe without any exception God, who swears by himself, that is, to us, when he recalls his life and all his perfection, and, as a pledge of his truth, shows that by what he has promised he wishes to make manifest who he is and what his virtues are. And he swears all the more because he bids us believe him when he swears, and swears in order that we may believe him. Finally, what is firmer than a promise confirmed by an oath from God himself? If therefore he swears that he will surely bless the seed, that he will not be angry with it, and that this seed will bow the knee to him and be justified and glorified, then its perseverance could not stand on a firmer foundation.

units.la: XXV. Faciunt huc etiam promissionum Divinarum Testes, iisque ex Cœlo & ex terra. Ex Cœlo Deus ipse. In cœlis firmasti veritatem tuam. Semen ejus in seculum erit, & thronus ejus sicut Sol coram me. Sicut luna stabilietur in seculum בִּשְׁמַיִם נֶאֱמָן וְעֵד & testis in æthere fidelis, Psal. LXXXIX. 3. 37. 38. Sicut enim Deus juravit per se ipsum; ita suarum etiam promissionum testis fidelis & verax est. Testis dein Christus est. Feriam vobiscum pactum sempiternum, gratias Davidis fideles. Ecce עֵד לְאוּמִּים testem nationibus dedi.
units.tr: XXV. The witnesses of the divine promises also bear on this, both from heaven and from earth. From heaven, God himself: In the heavens you have established your truth. His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before me. Like the moon it shall be established for ever [בִּשְׁמַיִם נֶאֱמָן וְעֵד], a faithful witness in the sky (Ps. 89:37, 38, 3). For just as God swore by himself, so he is also a faithful and true witness of his own promises. Next, Christ is a witness: I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David. Behold, I have given him as a witness to the peoples [עֵד לְאוּמִּים].

units.la: aaa dedi eum, ducem & præceptorem populis, Esaj. LV. 3. 4. Denique etiam Spiritus S. qui in cordibus fidelium testatur, eos esse filios Dei, hæredes vitæ æternæ, Rom. VIII. 16. Ita tres sunt, qui testantur in Cœlo, Pater, Sermo & Spiritus S. 1. Joh. V. 7. Quorum hoc testimonium est, quòd Deus vitam æternam nobis dederit, ibid. v. 11. In terra testes fuerunt Prophetæ, Apostoli. Scripsi vobis, ut sciatis, vos habere vitam æternam; quæ sine perseverantia nemini datur; ibid. v. 13. Denique νέφος μαρτύρων, nubes testium nos circumstat, Hebr. XII. 1. quorum testimonium est, quòd justus fide vivat, adeoque ad vitam perseveret, ibid. X. 38.
units.tr: I have given him as a leader and commander to the peoples (Isa. 55:3, 4). Finally, the Holy Spirit also bears witness in the hearts of believers that they are the children of God and heirs of eternal life (Rom. 8:16). Thus there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit (1 John 5:7). Their testimony is that God has given us eternal life (ibid. v. 11). On earth the witnesses were the prophets and apostles: I have written to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, which is given to no one without perseverance (ibid. v. 13). Finally, a cloud of witnesses [νέφος μαρτύρων] surrounds us (Heb. 12:1), and their testimony is that the righteous shall live by faith, and so persevere unto life (ibid. 10:38).

units.la: XXVI. Fœdera humana sacrificiis confirmari solent. Romani porcum vel porcam cœdebant: Chaldæi fœdus pangentes victimas secabant, & inter segmenta transibant, significantes, eodem modo violatores fœderis dissecandos. Unde ברית כרת secare fœdus: & Latinorum fœdus icere, percutere. Sic Deus cum Abrahamo fœdus percutiens, & in eo spirituale & perseverans semen ei promittens, justit vitulam & capram dissectas, turturem & pullum sibi offerri, inter quorum segmenta cibanum fumantem & lampadem ardentem transmisit, Genes. XV. 10. Etiam fœdus Mosaicum non sine sanguine Testamenti dedicatum est, Exod. XXIV. 8. Hebr. IX. 18. Qui typus evidens fuit sacrificii Christi, quo Deus sancivit promissiones non tantum de salute credentibus danda, sed etiam de lege cordibus fidelium fœderatorum inscribenda, & peccatis in perpetuum iisdem remittendis, ibid. VIII. 10. 12. Unde sanguis Christi αἷμα τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης sanguis novi Testamenti, Matth. XXVI. 28. appellatur. Et Testamentum de hæreditate spirituali Semini Abrahæ conferenda ratificatum in Christo, Gal. III. 17. dicitur. Quin & fideles, כרתי ברית עלי זבח ferire fœdus super sacrificio, Psal. L. 5. dicuntur.
units.tr: XXVI. Human covenants are usually confirmed by sacrifices. The Romans slaughtered a boar or a sow. The Chaldeans, when making a covenant, cut the victims in pieces and passed between the pieces, signifying that violators of the covenant would be cut in pieces in the same way. Hence the Hebrew phrase [ברית כרת], to cut a covenant, and the Latin foedus icere, to strike a covenant. So God, when he struck a covenant with Abraham and promised him in it a spiritual and enduring seed, bade a heifer and a goat be cut in pieces, and a turtledove and a young pigeon be offered to him, and between their pieces he passed a smoking furnace and a burning lamp (Gen. 15:10). The Mosaic covenant too was dedicated not without blood (Exod. 24:8; Heb. 9:18). This was a clear type of the sacrifice of Christ, by which God ratified promises not only that salvation would be given to believers, but also that his law would be written in the hearts of the covenanted faithful, and that their sins would be forgiven them for ever (ibid. 8:10, 12). Hence the blood of Christ is called the blood of the new testament [αἷμα τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης] (Matt. 26:28). And the testament concerning the spiritual inheritance to be conferred on the seed of Abraham is said to be ratified in Christ (Gal. 3:17). Indeed the faithful are said to strike a covenant over a sacrifice [כרתי ברית עלי זבח] (Ps. 50:5).

units.la: XXVII. Ad perpetuam fœderum memoriam & sanctionem Monumenta etiam statui solent. Jacobus enim lapidem מצבה in statuam, seu testimonium fœderis cum Labane icti exrexit, Gen. XXXI. 45. Moses duodecim statuas, seu lapides, vel lapidum acervos, qui duodecim tribus repræsentabant, erexit, & altare, monimentum fœderis Deum inter & populum contracti, exstruxit, Exod. XXIV. 4. Deus ipse fœdus pangens, quo se non amplius terram inundaturum promisit, disposuit arcum suum in nube in signum fœderis ipsum inter & terram, ut eo viso recordetur fœderis sui, Genes. IX. 11. &c. Similia fœderis gratiæ & promissionum ejus confirmandarum monumenta Deus in terra & Cœlo statuit. In terra ipse Dei cultus passim, nequicquam hostibus ringentibus, publice institutus certum documentum præbet, Deum ibi fœderatos suos, quos potentissima vi gratiæ suæ in Cœlum perducturus sit, habere. Hæc enim illa מצבה statua, seu lapis erectus juxta terminum ejus Jehovæ, & מזבח altare in medio terræ Ægypti, seu mundi hujus tenebricosi, in signum & testem Jehovæ exercituum, quòd dabit Servatorem suis, & liberabit eos, & agnoscetur in Ægypto & cognoscent Jehovam Ægyptii die illo, & colent sacrificio & munere, & vovebunt votum Jehovæ, & solvent illud; Unde ipse Deus dicet: Benedictus populus meus, Esaj. XIX. 19. &c. In
units.tr: XXVII. Monuments are also customarily set up to keep a covenant in perpetual memory and to confirm it. Thus Jacob set up a stone as a pillar, or witness of the covenant struck with Laban, Gen. XXXI. 45. Moses erected twelve pillars, or stones, or heaps of stones, representing the twelve tribes, and built an altar, a monument of the covenant made between God and the people, Exod. XXIV. 4. God himself, making a covenant in which he promised that he would no longer flood the earth, set his bow in the cloud as a sign of the covenant between himself and the earth, so that on seeing it he would remember his covenant, Gen. IX. 11, etc. God has set up similar monuments in earth and heaven to confirm the covenant of grace and its promises. On earth, the worship of God, instituted publicly and everywhere, though enemies rage in vain, gives a sure proof that God has his covenanted people there, whom by the most powerful force of his grace he will bring into heaven. For this is that מצבה pillar, or stone set up beside the border of Jehovah, and the altar מזבח in the midst of the land of Egypt, that is, of this dark world, as a sign and witness to Jehovah of hosts, that he will send a Saviour to his people, and he will deliver them, and he will be recognised in Egypt, and the Egyptians will know Jehovah on that day, and they will worship with sacrifice and gift, and they will make a vow to Jehovah, and they will pay it; whence God himself will say: Blessed be my people, Isa. XIX. 19, etc. In

units.la: Cœlo Johannes vidit ἴρις κυκλόθεν ὁ θρόνος, arcum seu iridem circa thronum (Christi) similem smaragdo, Apoc. IV. 3. Quo symbolo fideles de perpetua benevolentia Christi certiores redduntur. Nam novum hunc mundum, & creaturas novas nunquam diluvio iræ Divinæ perituras significatur. Iris enim, thronum gratiæ circumdans, tonitrua, fulgura & densas nubes ac procellas maledictionis Divinæ serenitati æterni favoris Dei locum cessisse, manifestè docet. Ipse etiam Christus מצבה statua, & מזבח altare, seu perpetuum fœderis nobiscum initi monumentum est; ad quem Deus respiciens fœderis sui & ejus, qui in Cœlos, tanquam πρόδρομος præcursor noster intravit, Hebr. VI. 20. recordatur. In cujus denique resurrectione, ascensione & sessione ad dextram Patris Deus nos pignus perpetuitatis vitæ novæ futuræ resurrectionis & sessionis nostræ in throno Patris habere voluit, Col. III. 1. 1. Cor. XV. 15. Ephes. II. 6. Apoc. III. 21.
units.tr: Heaven John saw a rainbow [ἴρις κυκλόθεν ὁ θρόνος] round the throne, a bow like an emerald encircling the throne (of Christ), Rev. IV. 3. By this symbol the faithful are made more certain of Christ's perpetual goodwill. For it signifies that this new world and these new creatures will never perish in a flood of divine wrath. The rainbow, encircling the throne of grace, clearly teaches that thunder, lightning, dense clouds and storms of divine curse have given way to the calm of God's eternal favour. Christ himself is also the pillar מצבה and the altar מזבח, that is, the perpetual monument of the covenant entered into with us; looking to him, God remembers his covenant with him who, as our forerunner [πρόδρομος], entered into heaven, Heb. VI. 20. In his resurrection, ascension and sitting at the right hand of the Father, God wished us to have a pledge of the perpetuity of new life, of our future resurrection and of our sitting on the Father's throne, Col. III. 1; 1 Cor. XV. 15; Eph. II. 6; Rev. III. 21.

units.la: XXVIII. Cum factis his signa promissiones fœderales mirè confirmantia jungimus. Quæ non unius generis in humanis pactis confirmandis adhiberi consueverunt. Velut convivia, Genes. XXVI. 30. munera, 1. Sam. XVIII. 4. arrhabones in pacto conjugali; annuli exhibitio in jure hæreditatis vel dignitatis, Genes. XLI. 42. glebæ traditio ad obsignandam hæreditatis possessionem, & primitiæ ad fruitionem frugum; sigilla diplomatis addita in obsignanda gratia & privilegio Principis: Signum ad peculium ceu nostrum notandum, (ibid. IV. 15.) tesseræ hospitales, quibus jus hospitii confirmatur. Similia planè signa Deus promissionibus fœderis sui confirmandis adhibuit. Postquam enim fide ostium cordis nostri ipsi apertum est, ipse venit ad nos, & cœnat nobiscum, & nos cum ipso, Apoc. III. 20. Qua in Cœna gustus & promulsis illius cœnæ gloriosæ est, quæ in Cœlo nobis parata est, Matth. VIII. 11. Luc. XIV. 15. Etiam hic nos pascit manna occulto, Apoc. II. 17. cibat nos carne & sanguine suo, seu se ipso, qui vivus panis est, qui è Cœlo descendit, & quem qui comedit, vitam æternam habet, Joh. VI. 51. Ceu Sponsus noster Spiritum S. nobis donat arrhabonem, 2. Cor. I. 22. atque ita de nuptiis in Cœlo secuturis plenam nobis spem facit, Apoc. XIX. 7. & hæreditatem nobis promissam obsignat, Ephes. I. 13. 14. Ille ipse etiam σφραγίς sigillum, quo diploma remissionis peccatorum munitur, & filiorum Dei privilegia nobis confirmantur. Nam in ipso ἐσφραγισμένοι obsignati sumus in diem redemptionis, ibid. IV. 30. Qui etiam nobis datur tanquam calculus albus, quo de nostra coram tribunali Dei absolutione certi reddimur, Apoc. II. 17. & tanquam signum, quod Deus in iis, quos servatus est, posuit, Esaj. LXVI. 19. Qui cùm obsignati sint in frontibus sigillo Dei vivi, ab Angelo vastatore lædi non possunt, Apoc. VII. 23. Quin & tessera illa hospitalis est, quem Christus è terris discessurus nobis reliquit, & qua certos nos reddidit, quòd in cœlestè tabernaculum nos admissurus & ad se assumpturus est, ut ubi ille est, etiam nos simus, Joh. XIV. 3. Accedunt his testeris internis externa etiam signa, Sacramenta, promissionum fœderalium aspectabilia signa, quibus promissiones salutis validissimè corroborantur
units.tr: XXVIII. To these facts we add signs which greatly confirm the covenant promises. Such signs have customarily been used to confirm human agreements of more than one kind: for example, feasts, Gen. XXVI. 30; gifts, 1 Sam. XVIII. 4; earnests in a marriage contract; the handing over of a ring in matters of inheritance or dignity, Gen. XLI. 42; the handing over of a clod of earth to seal possession of an inheritance, and first fruits to secure the enjoyment of the crops; seals added to a prince's diploma to confirm a grace or privilege; a sign to mark property as our own, Gen. IV. 15; and hospitality tokens by which the right of hospitality is confirmed. God has used signs of exactly this kind to confirm the promises of his covenant. For once, by faith, the door of our heart has been opened to him, he comes to us and dines with us and we with him, Rev. III. 20. In this Supper there is a taste and foretaste of that glorious feast which is prepared for us in heaven, Matt. VIII. 11; Luke XIV. 15. Even here he feeds us with hidden manna, Rev. II. 17; he nourishes us with his flesh and his blood, that is, with himself, who is the living bread which came down from heaven, and whoever eats of him has eternal life, John VI. 51. As our Bridegroom, he gives us the Holy Spirit as a pledge [arrhabonem], 2 Cor. I. 22, and so assures us full hope of the marriage feast to follow in heaven, Rev. XIX. 7, and seals the inheritance promised to us, Eph. I. 13, 14. He himself is also the seal [σφραγίς] by which the diploma of the forgiveness of sins is secured and the privileges of the sons of God are confirmed for us. For in him we have been sealed for the day of redemption, Eph. IV. 30. He is given to us also as a white pebble by which we are assured of our absolution before the judgement-seat of God, Rev. II. 17, and as a sign which God has placed on those whom he has saved, Isa. LXVI. 19. Since they are sealed on their foreheads with the seal of the living God, they cannot be harmed by the destroying angel, Rev. VII. 2, 3. Indeed, he is that hospitality token which Christ, about to leave the earth, left us, and by which he has assured us that he will receive us into the heavenly tabernacle and take us to himself, that where he is we may also be, John XIV. 3. To these inward testimonies are added outward signs, the Sacraments, the visible signs of the covenant promises, by which the promises of salvation are most powerfully strengthened

units.la: {a} Sacrificium Christi. borantur & obsignantur, non sub conditione fidei perseverantis, uti οἱ ἐξ ἐνανλίας statuunt, sed eadem ratione, qua fœdus ipsum, cujus Sacramenta signacula sunt, fidem & perseverantiam in eadem fœderatis promittit. Nam signa testamentaria sunt, pro certis, non incertis, hæredibus institua, & promissiones fœderales, non à voluntatis humanæ arbitrio, sed à solo beneplacito Dei suspensas, ceu σφραγίδες signacula justitiæ fidei, Rom. IV. 11. non ad tempus, sed in perpetuum obtentæ, quippe iis, quorum μακαρισμὸς beatitudo est, ibid. v. 9. tum singulis fidelibus, ad fructum propriæ consolationis & fiduciæ; tum toti Ecclesiæ, ad fructum communis gaudii & fiduciæ, de ejus fœcunditate & stabilitate perpetua, quatenus signa communi efficativa & confirmativa sunt promissionum in eorum institutione de perpetua efficacia fœderis gratiæ in adducendis ad salutem electis, ad finem usque mundi, obsignant.
units.tr: {a} The sacrifice of Christ. and sealed. They are not, as those from Arminius [οἱ ἐξ ἐνανλίας] maintain, sealed under the condition of perseverance in faith; rather, they are sealed on the same ground on which the covenant itself, whose Sacraments are the seals, promises faith and perseverance to those in the covenant. For testamentary signs are appointed for certain heirs, not uncertain ones, and the covenant promises, which depend not on the decision of human will but solely on the good pleasure of God, are seals [σφραγίδες] of the righteousness of faith, Rom. IV. 11. They are obtained not for a time but for ever, since they belong to those whose blessedness [μακαρισμός] it is, ibid. v. 9. They serve, for individual believers, as a fruit of their own comfort and confidence; and for the whole Church, as a fruit of common joy and confidence in its fruitfulness and lasting stability. In so far as they are common signs that are effective and confirmatory of the promises, they seal, by their institution, the perpetual efficacy of the covenant of grace in bringing the elect to salvation, until the end of the world.

units.la: XXIX. Tam luculenter promissam & confirmatam Perseverantiam à Deo obnixis precibus fœderati expetunt, orantes quotidie: Ne nos inducas in tentationem, sed libera nos à malo, Matth. VI. 13. Etiam aliis eandem precantur: Deus pacis sanctificet vos totos, & integer spiritus vester, & anima, & corpus inculpatè conserventur usque ad adventum Christi, 1. Thess. V. 23. Indesinenter pro vobis precamur, ut Deus compleat omne beneplacitum bonitatis & opus fidei in potentia, 2. Thess. I. 11. Consoletur Deus corda vestra, 2. Thess. II. 17. Inprimis S. Paulus emphaticè precatur Ephesiis, ut corroborentur per Spiritum Dei quoad interiorem hominem, & in charitate radicentur & fundentur, Ephes. III. 16-19. Cùmque sic precatus fuerit, dubio omni procul, non dubitans vel similis fluctui maris à ventis agitato, Jac. I. 6. sed in fide, quæ mandato & promissione Dei innititur; imò alibi precum suarum & fiduciæ de earum exauditione rationem à fidelitate Dei in suis promissionibus petat, dicens: Fidelis est Deus, qui id efficiet, 1. Thess. V. 24. Fidelis est Dominus, qui confirmabit vos, & custodiet ab improbo illo, 2. Thess. III. 3. Fidelis est Deus, qui non sinet vos tentari supra id, quod poteritis, sed unà cum tentatione exitum præstabit, 1. Cor. X. 13. manifestum est, eum perseverantiam Sanctorum, ceu Divinitus promissam, à Deo petiisse, certámque illam esse. Quod ampliùs etiam inde colliquescit, quia Sancti pro dono perseverantiæ Deo gratias agunt. Paulus enim pœne in singulis epistolis Deo gratias agit, quòd fidelium fides augescat, & charitas crescat, 2. Thess. I. 3. coll. cum Phil. I. 3. Col. I. 3. 1. Thess. I. 2. Et Petrus Deo benedicit, quòd nos regeneravit, ad spem vivam, ad hæreditatem in cœlis servatam, 1. Pet. I. 3. 4. Judas quoque Deo gloriam tribuit, ceu δυναμένῳ φυλάξαι ἀπταίστους potenti custodire nos sine lapsu, & statuere in conspectu suo inculpatos, vers. 24. Denique Paulus, ubi ex miseriæ suæ sensu priùs exclamavit: Quis me liberabit ex isto corpore mortis? Mox velut de liberatione sua certus, & metam attingens subjicit: Gratias ago Deo per Jesum Christum, Rom. VII. 24. 25. solennémque trium-phum canit: In his omnibus ὑπερνικῶμεν plusquàm victores sumus, per eum, qui nos dilexit. Persuasus enim sum, quòd neque mors, neque vita, neque Angeli, neque Principatus; neque potentiæ, neque præsentia, neque futura; neque altitudo, neque profunditas, neque ulla creatura alia nos separare possit à charitate Dei, quæ est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, ibid. VIII. 37. 38. 39. Tantundem est ac si dixisset: Quæ res in mundo potest esse, quæ sit potentior amore Christi erga nos, à quo solo omnis justitia, spes & salus nostra pendet; quæque efficere possit, ut non simus in amicitia Christi, vel ut Christus amorem suum in odium irámque convertat. Quod planè significat, nos amore & potentia Christi tutos, extra periculi omnis aleam, quippe manu & virtute ejus φρουρούμενος, seu invicto velu præsidio circumvallatos, collocari, ut ab eo descisci non possimus, eúmque amare nunquam desinamus. Nulla ab amore Christi separatio est, nisi illa, qua ab amore ejus & fide in eum abducimur. Licèt enim prædictum sit, fore ut charitas refrigescat, Matth. XXIV. 12. nihilominus statim Christus ostendit habere Deum electos perseverantes, neque cum reliquis per ἀνομίαν deficientes; dicens: Qui verò perseveraverit usque ad finem, salvabitur, v. 13.
units.tr: XXIX. The covenanted seek from God, with earnest prayers, the perseverance so clearly promised and confirmed, praying daily: Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, Matt. VI. 13. They also pray the same for others: May the God of peace sanctify you wholly, and may your whole spirit, soul and body be kept blameless until the coming of Christ, 1 Thess. V. 23. We pray always for you, that God may fulfil every good pleasure of goodness and the work of faith in power, 2 Thess. I. 11. May God comfort your hearts, 2 Thess. II. 17. Above all, St Paul emphatically prays for the Ephesians that they may be strengthened by the Spirit of God in respect of the inner man, and be rooted and grounded in love, Eph. III. 16–19. And when he has so prayed, without any doubt, not doubting or like a wave of the sea driven by the winds, Jas. I. 6, but in faith, which rests on the command and promise of God, he seeks, elsewhere, the ground of his prayers and of his confidence that they will be heard from the faithfulness of God in his promises, saying: Faithful is God who will bring it to pass, 1 Thess. V. 24. Faithful is the Lord who will establish you and guard you from the evil one, 2 Thess. III. 3. Faithful is God, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, but with the temptation will provide the way out, 1 Cor. X. 13. It is clear that he sought the perseverance of the saints from God as something divinely promised, and that it is certain. This becomes even clearer from the fact that the saints give thanks to God for the gift of perseverance. Paul, in almost every epistle, gives thanks to God that the faith of believers grows and their love increases, 2 Thess. I. 3, compare Phil. I. 3, Col. I. 3, 1 Thess. I. 2. Peter also blesses God that he has regenerated us to a living hope, to an inheritance kept in heaven, 1 Pet. I. 3, 4. Jude too ascribes glory to God, who is able [δυναμένῳ] to keep us without stumbling [ἀπταίστους] and to present us blameless in his sight, v. 24. Finally, Paul, having first cried out from a sense of his wretchedness, Who will deliver me from this body of death? at once, as one certain of his deliverance and reaching the goal, adds: I thank God through Jesus Christ, Rom. VII. 24, 25, and sings a solemn triumph: In all these things we are more than conquerors [ὑπερνικῶμεν] through him who loved us. For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other creature, will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord, ibid. VIII. 37, 38, 39. This is as much as to say: What thing in the world can be stronger than the love of Christ towards us, on which alone all our righteousness, hope and salvation depend; and what can bring it about that we are not in friendship with Christ, or that Christ turns his love into hatred and anger? This plainly means that we, safe by the love and power of Christ, are placed beyond every risk of danger, indeed guarded [φρουρούμενος] by his hand and strength, or fenced round with an unconquered garrison, so that we cannot fall away from him and never cease to love him. There is no separation from the love of Christ except that by which we are drawn away from his love and from faith in him. For although it has been foretold that love will grow cold, Matt. XXIV. 12, nevertheless Christ at once shows that God has elect who persevere, and who do not fall away with the rest through lawlessness [ἀνομίαν]; saying: But whoever endures to the end will be saved, v. 13.

units.la: XXX. Eodem Fœderis Gratiæ causæ tum impulsiva, tum finalis, aurigantur. Impulsiva est amor Dei erga fœderatos, isque gradu summus, & duratione æternus. In hoc est charitas, non quòd nos Deum dilexerimus, sed quòd ipse nos dilexit, & misit Filium suum, placamentum pro peccatis nostris, 1. Joh. IV. 10. Deus fuit in Christo mundum sibi reconcilians, &c. 2. Cor. V. 19. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut dederit Filium sibi unigenitum, ut quisquis in eum credit, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam, Joh. III. 16. Commendat charitatem suam erga nos Deus, quòd, cùm peccatores adhuc essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est. Quanto magis justificati sanguine ejus σωθησόμεθα per ipsum ab ira. Si autem cùm hostes adhuc essemus, reconciliati sumus per mortem Filii ejus, quanto magis reconciliati servabimur in vita ejus? Rom. V. 8-11. Quanta verò illa charitas est, qua incitante Deus Filium suum unigenitum dedit in mortem, & dedit ad reconciliandos nos, ne peccata nobis imputarentur, 2. Cor. V. 19. ad justificandum, atque eapropter etiam regenerandum nos, ad justificatos ab ira salvandum, juxta illa: Qui nominaverit nomen Domini, salvabitur, Joel. II. 32. Denique ad omnino salvandum nos, & in statu eo collocandum, ut immunes simus ab omni miseria & periculo, quod in æterna vita continget? Revera invictus est, ut mors, hic amor, durus ut orcus, zelus, scintillæ ejus sunt scintillæ ignis, flamma Dei. Aquæ multæ non possunt amorem extinguere, & fluvii non inundabunt eum, Cant. VIII. 6. 7. Qui etiam perinde ut ipsum fœdus gratiæ, æternus cùm sit, nullum durationis suæ finem habet. Pangam vobiscum fœdus æternum, gratias fideles, constantes Davidis, Esaj. LV. 3. Misericordia æterna misereor tui, dixit assertor tuus, Jehova. Nam montes decedent, & colles nutabunt, at gratia mea à te non recedet, & fœdus pacis meæ non nutabit, ait Jehova miserator tuus, ibid. LIV. 8. 10. Ideo, quos Christus semel amat in mundo, eos εἰς πλῆθος ἀγάπης ad finem usque amat, Joh. XIII. 1. Finis Foederis Gratiae, manifestatio gloriae Gratiae Dei, eandem Perseverantiam postulat. Manifestare enim Deus voluit gloriam Gratiae suae non imperfectae, sed plenissimae & cumulatissimae; neque offerendo tantum vel procurando, sed etiam realiter conferendo gratiam & salutem foederatorum. Unde consequens est, Deum vi foederis omnia etiam media foederatis suis conferre, quibus ad salutem illi infallibiliter proveherentur. Quae inter maximè fides perseverans est. Necessario enim nexu voluntas, finis & mediorum cohaeret, ut qui ad finem, salutem, foederatos destinavit Deus, idem ad media etiam destinaverit. Inprimis cùm Scriptura in hoc negotio sapientiam & potentiam Dei, quibus consilium suum exequitur, magnopere commendet, Eph. I. 19. II. 10. Ideo Foedus Gratiae vocatur בְּרִית שָׁלוֹם foedus pacis, quo omnigena pax & benedictio confertur, Esaj. LIV. 10. Ezech. XXXIV. 25. & בְּרִית הַחַיִּים וְהַשָּׁלוֹם foedus vitarum seu vitae & pacis, Mal. II. 5. Et S. Paulus diserte hunc finem Dei declarat, dicens, eum pro scopo habuisse non simpliciter laudem gloriae, sed ἔπαινον δόξης χάριτος laudem gloriae gratiae seu gloriosae gratiae, quae se modo valde gloriosò & illustri, per communicationem gratiae & mediorum salutis, exerit, Ephes. I. 6. Non ergo qualiscunque vel dimidiata, sed plena, perfecta gratia est, quia alias gloriosa non esset. Ad gloriam meam creavi eum, formavi eum יְצַרְתִּיו וְעָשִׂיתִיו & perfeci eum (ad insinuandam executionem potentissimam) Esaj. XLIII. 7. Omnes justi in aeternum haereditatem accipient terram, virgultum plantationum mearum, opus manuum mearum, לְהִתְפָּאֵר ad glorificandum me, ibid. LX. 21. Qualis vero gloria illa Gratiae est, quam Perseverantiae adversarii intentam, at non certò conferendam, vel ad extremum sic conferendam, ut cum ea innumeri perire possint, imò etiam evenire possit, ut nemo unus salvetur, fingunt?
units.tr: XXX. The impulsive and final causes of the Covenant of Grace are set out in the same way. The impulsive cause is God's love toward those in the covenant, which is supreme in degree and eternal in duration. "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins" (1 John 4:10). "God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself," etc. (2 Cor. 5:19). "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life" (John 3:16). "God commends his love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved [σωθησόμεθα] from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life" (Rom. 5:8–11). And how great is that love by which God, moved by it, gave his only-begotten Son to death, and gave him to reconcile us, so that sins would not be imputed to us (2 Cor. 5:19); to justify us and therefore also to regenerate us; to save us, justified, from wrath, according to the words "Whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved" (Joel 2:32); and finally to save us completely and to place us in that state in which we are free from every misery and danger that could befall us in eternal life? Indeed, "this love is strong as death, its jealousy is cruel as the grave; its flashes are flashes of fire, the very flame of God. Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it" (Song 8:6–7). Just as the covenant of grace itself is eternal, so this love, being eternal, has no end to its duration. "I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David" (Isa. 55:3). "With everlasting kindness will I have mercy on you, says your Redeemer, the LORD. For the mountains shall depart and the hills be removed, but my kindness shall not depart from you, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, says the LORD who has mercy on you" (Isa. 54:8, 10). Therefore those whom Christ has loved once in the world he loves to the end, "into the full extent of love" [εἰς πλῆθος ἀγάπης] (John 13:1). The end of the covenant of grace, which is the manifestation of the glory of God's grace, demands the same perseverance. For God willed to display the glory of his grace not as imperfect but as most full and abundant, not merely by offering or procuring grace and salvation, but by actually conferring them on those in the covenant. Hence it follows that by virtue of the covenant God gives to his covenanted people all the means by which they would infallibly be carried on to salvation, and among these above all is persevering faith. For there is a necessary connection between will, end and means, so that God, who has appointed the covenanted people to salvation as their end, has also appointed them to the means. Especially since Scripture in this matter strongly commends the wisdom and power of God, by which he carries out his purpose (Eph. 1:19; 2:10). Therefore the covenant of grace is called "covenant of peace" [בְּרִית שָׁלוֹם], by which every kind of peace and blessing is conferred (Isa. 54:10; Ezek. 34:25), and "covenant of lives and peace" [בְּרִית הַחַיִּים וְהַשָּׁלוֹם] (Mal. 2:5). And St. Paul plainly declares this purpose of God, saying that he had as his aim not simply "the praise of glory," but "the praise of the glory of grace" [ἔπαινον δόξης χάριτος], that is, of glorious grace, which displays itself in a most glorious and illustrious way through the communication of grace and of the means of salvation (Eph. 1:6). Therefore grace is not of some ordinary or half-measure kind, but full and perfect, for otherwise it would not be glorious. "I created him for my glory, I formed him and made him" [יְצַרְתִּיו וְעָשִׂיתִיו], and "I perfected him" (to indicate the most powerful execution) (Isa. 43:7). "All your people shall be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified" [לְהִתְפָּאֵר] (Isa. 60:21). But what kind of glory of grace is it that the opponents of perseverance imagine as intended, yet not certainly to be conferred, or conferred only at the last in such a way that countless people may perish with it, and indeed that it may come about that not one person at all is saved?

units.la: XXXI. Fundamentum Foederis Gratiae Christus est. Nam in ipso Mediatore & Sponsore initum est. Deus enim fundavit in Sione lapidem, lapidem explorationis, angulum pretiosissimum, מוּסָד מוּסַד fundati fundatissimi, Esaj. XXVIII. 16. Hinc etiam Testamentum Dei προκεκυρωμένον ante ratificatum fuit à Deo εἰς Χριστὸν in Christum, adeóque Deo Christum respiciente, Gal. III. 17. Omnes enim promissiones in Christo sunt ita & Amen, quia in eo ut factae, impletae eodem per ναὶ ita affirmantur, & gratiarum actionem & glorificationem dicendo 'Αμὴν Amen postulant, 2. Cor. I. 20. Cúmque Christus Foederis gratiae fundus duobus modis considereтur, puta tum in susceptione officii Mediatorii, & in pacto, tum in ejusdem executione, & in facto, atque in susceptione officii, seu pacto ipse quidem Deo Patri obedientiam ad colligendum sibi peculiarem populum promiserit, adeóque eidem se servum & Mediatorem atque Sponsorem stiterit; vicissim Deus Pater Filio obedienti illum ipsum populum morte ejus acquisitum, ceu haereditatem, cujus caput & rex sit, promiserit, adeóque eum populi hujus haeredem, Caput & Regem constituerit: in executione verò officii, seu facto idem Christus homines redemerit, & Diabolum vicerit; singula certè haec, in Christo, Filio Dei quàm maximè conspicua Sanctorum perseverantiam & salutem in tutissima arce collocant. Quomodo enim deficere fides, & nutare salus eorum potest, in quorum gratiam Christus, Filius Dei, caro factus est, & se Deo Patri servum obedientem ad mortem usque crucis stitit; pro quibus, ceu Mediator spopondit; quos ipsi, ceu haeredi, Capiti, Regi Deus Pater haereditatem, corpus, populum promisit; quos denique vicło, debellato & triumphato Sathana, redemit, salvavit, suíque aeterni juris, beneficii & peculii fecit? Sed singula haec instituto nostro paulò amplius & pensiculatius applicemus.
units.tr: XXXI. The foundation of the covenant of grace is Christ. For it was made in the Mediator and Surety himself. For God "laid in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, firmly founded" [מוּסָד מוּסַד], "founded and most firmly founded" (Isa. 28:16). Hence also the "testament of God was previously ratified" [προκεκυρωμένον] by God "in Christ" [εἰς Χριστὸν] (Gal. 3:17), that is, with God regarding Christ. "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen," because they are fulfilled in him and are thereby affirmed as "yes" [ναὶ], and they call for thanksgiving and glorification, saying "Amen" ['Αμὴν] (2 Cor. 1:20). Since Christ, the foundation of the covenant of grace, is considered in two ways, namely in the undertaking of the office of Mediator and in the compact, and also in its execution and in the deed itself: in the undertaking of the office, or the compact, he promised obedience to God the Father so as to gather for himself a peculiar people, and so presented himself to him as servant, Mediator and Surety; and in turn God the Father promised the Son, when obedient, that very people acquired by his death, as an inheritance of which he would be head and king, and so appointed him heir, head and king of this people. In the execution of the office, or the deed itself, the same Christ redeemed men and conquered the Devil. Each of these, certainly, set the perseverance and salvation of the saints in Christ, the Son of God, in the most secure stronghold. For how can their faith fail and their salvation waver, for whose sake Christ, the Son of God, was made flesh, and presented himself as an obedient servant to God the Father "even unto death, the death of the cross"; for whom he undertook as Mediator; whom God the Father promised to him as heir, head and king, as inheritance and body and people; whom, finally, having conquered, subdued and triumphed over Satan, he redeemed and saved, and made his own by eternal right, benefit and possession? But let us apply each of these to our purpose a little more fully and carefully.

units.la: XXXII. Ante omnia Deus Pater Christum Servum fecit, & eidem servitium praestanti פּעֵלָה operae suae pretium, haereditatem populum promisit. Ecce servum meum, quem elegi, Esaj. XLIII. 10. Sacrificium & oblationem noluisti. Aures mihi perforasti, corpus mihi adaptasti, in quo tibi servirem, Ps. XL. 7. Heb. X. 5. Seipsum exinanivit, formam servi assumens, Phil. II. 7. In hoc servi officio obeundo id ipsi à Deo Patre negotii datum est, ut filios Dei dispersos in unum congregaret, Joh. XI. 52. Oves ex caula Judaeorum & gentium adduceret, ibid. X. 16. זֶרַע בְּרוּכֵי יְהוָה Semen benedictorum à Jehova, & germina eorum cum ipsis vivificaret, Esaj. LXV. 23. גְּאוּלֵי redemptos, vindicatos à se ibid. LXIII. 4. & datos sibi a Patre, Joh. XVII. 6. 12. salvaret; non utcunque eos docendo, vel Spiritus S. munere quopiam mactando, sed cæcos oculos aperiendo, vinctos è claustro, sedentes in tenebris educendo, Esaj. XLII. 7. atque sic è potestate tenebrarum liberando, & in Regnum Filii dilectionis ejus transferendo, Col. I. 13. denique id efficiendo, ut Deus haberet genus electum, Regale Sacerdotium, gentem sanctam, populum peculi praedicantem virtutes ejus, qui illum ex tenebris vocavit ad lucem admirabilem, 1. Petr. II. 9. domum spiritualem, Sacerdotium sanctum, ad offerendas victimas spirituales, ibid. v. 5. יְהוָה מַטַּע plantas Jehovæ, quibus ad glorificandum se uteretur; Esaj. LXI. 3. Quae Patris non inefficax voluntas, seu velleitas, sed θεληματος propositum efficientis omnia ex consilio voluntatis suae, fuit, Ephes. I. 11. Haec est voluntas Patris, ut, quicquid dedit mihi, nihil perdam ex eo, sed illud suscitem in ultimo illo die, Joh. VI. 39. Quod sic Filio suo injunxit Pater, quod sibi injunctum Filius suscepit, eventum ancipitem, vel omnino nullum habere non potuit. Obstant enim servi hujus tum zelus, non deferentis vadimonium, sed masculè obeuntis, & dicentis: Ecce venio, ut faciam voluntatem tuam חֶפְצִי delector ea, & lex tua in medio viscerum meorum est, Psal. XL. 8. 9. tum invicta roboris efficacia, qua, sicut Lazaro dixit: Exi foras, Joh. XI. 43. ita dicere vinctis spiritualibus, Exite; & jacentibus in tenebris: Manifestate vos, Esaj. XLIX. 9. potuit: tum fidelitas summa, quæ cingulum renum ejus est, Esaj. XI. 5. & per quam fidelis fuit Patri, qui ipsum constituit, Heb. III. 2. tum potentissima manus Patris servo suo opem praesentissimam promittentis: Ecce servus meus בְּוֹ אֶתְמֹךְ teneo illum (ipsi adsum potentia mea) electus meus, in quo acquiescit anima mea; dedi Spiritum meum super ipsum, judicium gentibus proferet, &c. Esaj. XLII. 1. Ego Jehova vocavi te (Servum) cum justitia, & אֶחָזְךָ.
units.tr: XXXII. Above all, God the Father made Christ a Servant, and to him, rendering service, he promised the worth of his labour, an inheritance, a people. "Behold my servant whom I have chosen" (Isa. 43:10). "Sacrifice and offering you did not desire; my ears you have opened; a body you have prepared for me" (in which I might serve you) (Ps. 40:6; Heb. 10:5). "He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant" (Phil. 2:7). In undertaking this office of servant, this task was given to him by God the Father: that he should "gather together in one the children of God who were scattered" (John 11:52); that he should "bring the sheep from the fold of Jews and Gentiles" (John 10:16); that he should make alive "the seed of the blessed of the LORD, and their offspring with them" (Isa. 65:23); and save "the redeemed, whom he has vindicated" (Isa. 63:4), and "those given to him by the Father" (John 17:6, 12). He would save them not merely by teaching them in some way, or by slaying them with some gift of the Holy Spirit, but "by opening blind eyes, by bringing out prisoners from the prison, and those sitting in darkness from the dungeon" (Isa. 42:7), and so by "delivering them from the power of darkness and transferring them into the kingdom of his beloved Son" (Col. 1:13); and finally by bringing it about that God should have "a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, to declare the virtues of him who called them out of darkness into his marvellous light" (1 Pet. 2:9); "a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices" (ibid., v. 5); "plants of the LORD" [יְהוָה מַטַּע] by which he might be used "to glorify himself" (Isa. 61:3). This was not an ineffective will or mere wish of the Father, but a "purpose" [θεληματος], that of one who "works all things according to the counsel of his will" (Eph. 1:11). "This is the will of the Father, that of all that he has given me I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day" (John 6:39). What the Father thus enjoined on his Son, and what the Son undertook as enjoined, could not have an uncertain outcome or none at all. For there stand in the way the zeal of this Servant, who does not decline the pledge but undertakes it manfully, saying, "Behold, I come to do your will, O God; I delight to do it, and your law is within my heart" [חֶפְצִי] (Ps. 40:8–9); and the unconquered power of his strength, by which, as he said to Lazarus, "Come out," so he could say to the spiritually bound, "Come out," and to those lying in darkness, "Show yourselves" (John 11:43; Isa. 49:9); and his supreme faithfulness, which is "the girdle of his loins" (Isa. 11:5), and by which he "was faithful to him who appointed him" (Heb. 3:2); and the most powerful hand of the Father promising his servant most present help: "Behold my servant, whom I uphold [בְּוֹ אֶתְמֹךְ]; I hold him (I am present with him in my power), my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him; he shall bring forth judgment to the nations," etc. (Isa. 42:1). "I the LORD have called you (the Servant) in righteousness, and I will hold your hand [אֶחָזְךָ]."

units.la: Tum ut servus Dei faetus, certissimam adducendorum ad Deum illorum, quorum in gratiam servi munus suscepit, promissionem accepit. [?] apprehendi manum tuam [Hebrew: ואחזך בידך] & retinebo te, & dabo te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium, &c. ibid. v. 6. Audite insulæ, &c. Jehova ab utero vocavit me, à visceribus matris meæ commemoravit nomen meum. Et posuit os meum, tanquam gladium acutum, & umbra manus suæ occultavit me, & posuit me telum electum, in pharetra sua abscondit me. Et dixit mihi, servus meus es tu, Israel (Christe unâ cum corpore tuo mystico) in quo condecorabor, ibid. XLIX. 1-4. Dedit enim Deus Christo potestatem in omnem carnem, ut quicquid dedit ipsi, ei det vitam æternam, Joh. XVII. 2. Unde etiam destinationem Christi ad tantum officium optatum successum habituram, prædictum est. Voluntas Dei in manu ejus (servi justi,) [Hebrew: ידוֹ יצליח] prosperabitur, ibid. LIII. 10. Ponet in terra judicium, & legem ejus insulæ expectabunt, ibid. XLII. 4. Ambulare faciam cæcos per viam, quam non noverant, & per semitas, quas non cognoverant, incedere eos faciam, ibid. v. 16. Festinabunt filii tui, &c. Dicesque in corde tuo; [Hebrew: מי ילד לי את אלה] Quis mihi genuit istos? ibid. XLIX. 17, 21. In his omnibus nihil ab arbitrio hominis suspenditur; quin potius illos, pro quibus Christus consilio Dei servivit, certò adductum & salvatum iri, asseritur.
units.tr: Then, as the servant of God was formed, he received a most certain promise of bringing to God those for whose sake he undertook the servant's office: [?] I have taken hold of your hand [Hebrew: ואחזך בידך] and will keep you, and will give you as a covenant of the people, a light to the nations, etc. ibid. v. 6. Listen, O islands, etc. The LORD called me from the womb; from my mother's bowels he made mention of my name. And he made my mouth like a sharp sword, and in the shadow of his hand he hid me; he made me a polished shaft, and in his quiver he hid me. And he said to me, You are my servant, Israel (Christ together with his mystical body), in whom I will be glorified, ibid. XLIX. 1-4. For God gave Christ power over all flesh, that whatever he gave him, he should give eternal life, John XVII. 2. Hence it was also foretold that Christ's appointment to so great an office would have the desired success: The pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand (of the righteous servant) [Hebrew: ידו יצליח], ibid. LIII. 10. He shall set judgment in the earth, and the isles shall wait for his law, ibid. XLII. 4. I will lead the blind in a way that they knew not, and in paths that they have not known I will make them walk, ibid. v. 16. Thy sons shall make haste, etc. And you shall say in your heart: Who has begotten these for me? [Hebrew: מי ילד לי את אלה], ibid. XLIX. 17, 21. In all these things nothing is made to depend on the choice of man; rather, it is asserted that those for whom Christ served according to God's counsel will certainly be brought in and saved.

units.la: XXXIII. Non tantum Servus Dei, sed etiam Mediator Deum inter & homines Christus est; & quidem Mediator non internuntius duntaxat, sed etiam fidejussor, Sponsor. Consilium enim illud, cui Christus inservivit fuit [Hebrew: עצת שלום] consilium pacis, Zach. VI. 13. atque illud cum hominibus hactenus rebellibus. Ideo [Greek: ἔγγυος] Sponsor melioris Testamenti, Hebr. VII. 22. appellatur. Existet dux ex ipso, &c. [Hebrew: והקריבתי] & faciam eum appropinquare, & accedet ad me. Nam quis ille est, [Hebrew: ערב את לבו לגשת אלי] qui in fidem suam recepit cor suum, ut ad me accedat; quis pro alio spondere animum suum induce t; dit Jehova? Jerem. XXX. 21. Est autem officium Sponsoris, ut in se præstationem conditionum fœderis recipiat. Pro quo igitur Christus ita spopondit, ejus salus certa est; nisi vel potentia ejus, qui [Greek: παντοκράτωρ] omnipotens est, Apoc. I. 8. vel fides ejusdem, qui vocatur [Greek: πιστὸς καὶ ἀληθινὸς] verax & fidelis, ibid. XIX. 11. nutare statuatur. Imò si illi, pro quibus Christus spopondit, fide & nova obedientia destituti, vel ab eodem deficere, & non salvari possent, Christus semel à Deo admissus Sponsor vadimonium deseruisse, imò & noxam contraxisse, dici deberet, juxta vulgatum illud: 'Εγγύα, παρὰ δ' ἀτη. Sponde, detrimentum est: & Solomonis illud: Si non sit tibi ad reddendum, cur creditor lectum tuum subter te tollet? Prov. XXII. 27. Vadimonium igitur deserere & perfidia est, & pœnæ obnoxium reddit; quorum utrumque à Christo alienissimum est. Nam quòd Christum spopondisse Deo satisfactionem, at non eorum, pro quibus satisfecit, fidem & novam obedientiam, eamque perseverantem, adversarii regerunt, oppidò absurdum est, sive is ceu Sponsor Dei apud homines, sive ceu Sponsor hominum apud Deum consideratur. Quatenus enim Sponsor Dei apud homines est, Sponsor utique ejus fœderis est, cujus principalis promissio nomine Dei est inscriptio legis in cor, Jerem. XXXI. 33. Hebr. VIII. 6. 10. VII. 22. quam perseverantis fidei esse, supra
units.tr: XXXIII. Christ is not only the Servant of God but also the Mediator between God and men; and indeed a Mediator not merely as go-between, but also as surety and sponsor. For that counsel which Christ served was [Hebrew: עצת שלום] the counsel of peace, Zech. VI. 13, and this was with men hitherto rebellious. Therefore he is called [Greek: ἔγγυος] surety of a better testament, Heb. VII. 22. A leader shall arise from him, etc. [Hebrew: והקרבתי] And I will make him draw near, and he shall approach me. For who is he [Hebrew: ערב את לבו לגשת אלי] who has pledged his heart to approach me; who has brought his mind to stand surety for another? says the LORD. Jer. XXX. 21. But the office of a surety is to take upon himself the performance of the conditions of the covenant. Therefore, for whom Christ has so stood surety, their salvation is certain, unless either his power, who is [Greek: παντοκράτωρ] almighty (Rev. I. 8), or the faithfulness of the same, who is called [Greek: πιστὸς καὶ ἀληθινὸς] faithful and true (ibid. XIX. 11), is supposed to waver. Indeed, if those for whom Christ stood surety could be destitute of faith and new obedience, or fall away from him and not be saved, then Christ, once admitted by God as Surety, would have to be said to have failed to honour his bond, and even to have incurred guilt, according to the common saying: [Greek: Ἐγγύα, παρὰ δ' ἀτη] Give a pledge, and ruin is at hand; and Solomon's: If you have nothing to repay, why should the creditor take away your bed from under you? Prov. XXII. 27. To desert a bond is therefore faithlessness and renders one liable to punishment; both of which are most alien to Christ. For our opponents object that Christ promised God satisfaction, but not faith and new obedience, and that persevering, for those for whom he made satisfaction; this is utterly absurd, whether he is considered as God's surety before men, or as men's surety before God. For insofar as he is surety of God before men, he is surely surety of that covenant whose principal promise, in God's name, is the writing of the law in the heart, Jer. XXXI. 33; Heb. VIII. 6, 10; VII. 22; which, as we have shown above, belongs to persevering faith.

units.la: ostendimus. Et hæc similesque promissiones fœderis gratiæ, ceu Propheta, verbo suo declaravit, ceu Sacerdos, sanguine suo obsignavit, & confirmavit, & ceu Rex, Dei nomine sic confert, ut sceptro suæ fortitudinis, & Spiritus S. efficacia corda ad novam obedientiam flectat. Quatenus verò etiam Sponsor hominum est apud Deum, fidem & novam obedientiam perseverantem Deo pro hominibus pariter spondit. Quod multa comprobant, inprimis objecti sponsionis designatio, non pars aliqua fœderis, sed totum fœdus, pro quo si spopondit, etiam fidem & obedientiam novam, fœderis illius partem Deo spoponderit, necesse est: tum Testamenti Filii, quod in sponsione illa includitur, ratio, quæ in voluntate absoluta bona gratiæ & gloriæ, adeòque etiam fidem, certis hæredibus morte sua acquisitam Hebr. IX. 16. 17. conferendi, non illa tenues in auras dissipandi consistit; tum scopus sponsionis, qui fuit salutis humanæ securitas per novæ obedientiæ in novo fœdere donationem, qua carens fœdus operum irritum planè cecidit: tum Sponsoris dignitas, qui ut hominum corda in sua manu habens, & ut rivos aquarum inclinans, quò vult, Prov. XXI. 1. spondendo [Greek: ἀνάδοχος] suam abnegare, & cùm Deo ab æterno sine nobis spoponderit, in tempore assensum in nobis non efficere non potuit. Sed & sponsio satisfactionis sine sponsione novæ obedientiæ tum planè [Greek: ἀνέγγυος] est, quia sic spopondisset satisfactionem pro nonnullis, qui reatu peccati obstricti manent, atque ita satisfecisset pro iis, pro quibus satisfactum non est, solvisset [Greek: λύτρον] nemine illud acceptante: tum planè [Greek: ἀλογος] quia nemo prudens absolutè spondet id, cujus incertus, & à mutabili ejus, pro quo spopondit, voluntate pendens eventus est, Id enim si oppido stultum est, quomodo sine impietate ita tribui Christo potest, ut dicamus, eum, qui [Hebrew: פלא יועץ] admirabilis consilio, Esaj. IX. 6. & magnus consilio, Jerem. XXXII. 18. est, voluisse Deo non qualiscunque rei, sed pretiosissimi sanguinis sui effusionem spondere, atque tantæ rei fructum à mutabili voluntate hominis suspendere; imò spondere pro iis, quos inferno damnatos vel damnandos ignorare non potuit? Neque enim adversarii Christo sponsionem moriendi conditionatam, utpote cum Christi universali, quam tuentur, redemptione, [Greek: ἀνάλογον] tribuere possunt. Posita enim sponsione moriendi conditionata, Christus pro solis credentibus mortuus censeri deberet, quia conditio nihil ponit in esse.
units.tr: And these and similar promises of the covenant of grace he declared by his word as Prophet, sealed and confirmed by his blood as Priest, and as King confers them in God's name, so that by the sceptre of his strength and the efficacy of the Holy Spirit he bends hearts to new obedience. But insofar as he is also surety of men before God, he likewise promised to God, on behalf of men, persevering faith and new obedience. Many things prove this, above all the designation of the object of the promise: not some part of the covenant but the whole covenant. If he stood surety for that, he must necessarily also have promised to God faith and new obedience, which are part of that covenant. Then there is the nature of the Son's Testament, included in that promise, which consists in the absolute will to bestow the goods of grace and glory, and thus also faith, acquired by his death for certain heirs (Heb. IX. 16, 17), and not in scattering those things into thin air. Then there is the aim of the promise, which was the security of human salvation through the granting of new obedience in the new covenant, without which the covenant of works utterly failed. Then there is the dignity of the Surety, who holds the hearts of men in his hand and turns them like streams of water wherever he wills (Prov. XXI. 1); by promising, he could not deny his own, and since he promised to God from eternity without us, he could not fail in time to effect our assent. But also a promise of satisfaction without a promise of new obedience would be [Greek: ἀνέγγυος] not a pledge at all, because he would thus have promised satisfaction for some who remain bound by the guilt of sin, and so would have satisfied for those for whom satisfaction was not made, and would have offered a [Greek: λύτρον] ransom with no one accepting it. It would also be [Greek: ἀλογος] unreasonable, because no prudent person absolutely promises something whose outcome is uncertain and depends on the changeable will of the one for whom he promised. If that is very foolish, how can it be attributed to Christ without impiety, so that we would say that he, who is [Hebrew: פלא יועץ] wonderful in counsel (Isa. IX. 6) and great in counsel (Jer. XXXII. 18), wished to promise God not some ordinary thing but the outpouring of his most precious blood, and made the fruit of so great a thing depend on the changeable will of man; indeed, promised for those whom he could not fail to know were condemned, or to be condemned, to hell? For our opponents cannot consistently ascribe to Christ a conditional promise to die, since that would fit only with the universal redemption they defend. For if the promise to die is conditional, Christ would have to be considered to have died only for believers, because a condition brings nothing into being.

units.la: XXXIV. Sicut Christus Deo Patri se Servum, Mediatorem & Sponsorem sistens, eorum, pro quibus se Deo Patri servum stitit & spopondit, salutem in tuta arce collocavit: ita Deus Pater vicissim ei populum, pro quo servi & sponsoris officium suscepit, in hæreditatem & peculium, cujus ipse hæres, Rex, caput; esset, promittens, illis qui ei ceu hæreditas & peculium cesserunt, salutem certissimam pariter reddidit. Sicut enim Christus Deo Patri serviens quasi-promisit gloriam Patris, Joh. XVII. 4. ita vicissim Pater gloriam Filii, ibid. VIII. 50. Cui ipse dixit: Pete à me. & dabo gentes hæreditatem tuam, & possessionem tuam terminos terræ, Psal. II. 8. Generationem ejus quis enarrabit? Si posuerit animam
units.tr: XXXIV. Just as Christ, presenting himself to God the Father as Servant, Mediator and Surety, placed in a secure stronghold the salvation of those for whom he presented himself as servant and surety, so God the Father, in turn, promised him the people for whom he undertook the office of servant and surety, to be his inheritance and peculiar people, of which he is heir, King and head; and to those who yielded to him as inheritance and peculiar people, he likewise rendered salvation most certain. For just as Christ, serving the Father, as it were promised the glory of the Father (John XVII. 4), so in turn the Father promised the glory of the Son (John VIII. 50).
