For by it there is signified and sealed: first, our natural depravity, which in Scripture is usually called the old man and the flesh, which we ought to put off, to which we ought to die, and whose filth must be washed away by pure water (Rom. VI. 3, 4; Col. II. 11, 12); then that pure water by which the filth of sin is expiated and washed away, namely Christ's most pure obedience and blood (John III. 5; Heb. X. 23; Ezek. XXXVI. 25); then the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, for completing redemption and abolishing sin and its guilt (Rom. VI. 4, 5); then the righteousness of Christ, imputed to us through faith, sprinkled with his blood by the Holy Spirit, of remission of sins and adoption (ibid. IV. 11; Acts II. 38; XXII. 16); then our communion with Christ's death, burial and resurrection, which comes to us in justification by imputation and in sanctification by our conformity with Christ and his image, through which both we are also subjected to him as our only Lord and Saviour, as his own people, a peculiar possession; then the Holy Spirit, through whom we are engrafted into Christ, his death is applied to us, and we are baptized into one body with him; then our glorification, that, dead with Christ, we will with certainty also revive with him, to be freed from the struggle of sin in death, and from the death of the body, the last enemy, in the resurrection (Rom. VI. 4, 5, etc.); then the earnest and pledge of all these given by God himself in the waters, and so the seal of our trust in God and Christ, in which is contained that appeal of a good conscience towards God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ (the firm ground of a good conscience through faith purified, to ask freely of God, and for which Christ rose from the dead to receive and to grant), 1 Pet. III. 21. Rightly, therefore, Baptism is called by Theodoret the earnest of future good things, and the figure of the resurrection to come, and the communion of the Lord's sufferings, and the participation in the Lord's resurrection.

units.la: XLII.
units.tr: XLII.

units.la: Sed haec beneficia Evangelii praestantissima Baptismus non nudè repraesentat, sed in legitimo usu iis, qui baptizantur, ceu ad eos ex tenore promissionum Foederis gratiae pertinentia,obsignat & exhibet; at non ut causa inhaerente vel assistente virtute efficiens,sed ut sigillum,arrhabo atque pignus certissimum de iis acceptis vel accipiendis fidem faciens. Procul enim omni dubio Baptismus perinde, ut alia Sacramenta,gratiae non causa efficiens, sed ejus effectae vel efficiendae signum & sigillum est. Successit enim Circumcisioni,ceu Sacramentum regenerationis simile & ei succenturiatum, Col. II. 11. 12. At Circumcisio fuit signum, Genes. XVII. 11. & sigillum justitiae, Rom. IV. 11. Tum Baptismus similis,& seu priori, aquis diluvii, respondens & conformis typus statuitur,1. Pet. III.21. Quomodo etiam Hebr. IX.24. simpliciter typum, figuram & signum notat. Quod etiam res ipsa docet,quia Baptismi aqua & ritus aliquid adumbrat & figurat,nempe regenerationem per meritum Christi & operationem Spiritus S. aliàque be-neficia Evangelica, uti fusius analogiam inter utraque illa exponentes ostendimus. Accedit, quòd baptizamur in nomen Patris,Filii & Spiritus S. Matth. XXVIII.19. hoc est, Baptismi Sacramento & velut sigillo atque arrhabone certi reddimur gratiae Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. atque hoc velut auctoramento eidem subjicimur : quòd baptizamur ad remissionem peccatorum,Actor. II.38. hoc est,ad & certitudinem de remissione peccatorum concipiendam : quòd gratia regenerationis & salus Baptismo, Eph. V.26. Tit. III.5. 1.Petr. III.21. non aliam ob causam adscribitur,quàm quia Baptismus arrhabo , pignus & sigillum, certissimam de iis fiduciam & gignit: quòd denique in Christum baptizamur,Gal. III.27. aliter atque in Mosen olim Israelitae baptizati, 1.Cor. X.2. dicuntur. Nam in Mosen baptizati sunt,ut ejus,ceu fidelis servi in domo Dei, doctrinam susciperent, praecepta observarent,& suo tempore Messiam,propter testimonium Mosis reciperent: In Christum nos baptizamur, quia Baptismus nobis signum & sigillum communionis cum Christo ceu Domino & Messia,in quo gaudium nostrum consummatur, ex institutione ipsius Christi administratur. Tale ergo signum & sigillum gratiae & salutis cùm sit Baptismus , simul ejusdem causa efficiens , seu physica & inhaerente, seu externa & assistente virtute operans,statui nullo modo potest. Nam sigilla non rem proprie efficiunt , sed effectae seu efficiendae certitudinem praestant. Neque dissimile exemplum ullum ostendi potest.
units.tr: But Baptism does not merely represent these most excellent benefits of the Gospel. In proper use it seals and exhibits them to those who are baptized, as things belonging to them under the terms of the promises of the covenant of grace. It does not do so as an efficient cause, operating by an inherent or assisting power, but as a seal, a pledge and a most certain token that makes us sure of the things received or to be received. For beyond all doubt Baptism, like the other sacraments, is not an efficient cause of grace but a sign and seal of the grace that has been or is to be effected. It succeeded circumcision, as a sacrament of regeneration similar to it and corresponding to it (Col. 2:11, 12). Circumcision was a sign (Gen. 17:11) and a seal of righteousness (Rom. 4:11). Then Baptism is set forth as a type that is similar to, and corresponds to, the former, the waters of the flood (1 Pet. 3:21). In the same way Heb. 9:24 simply denotes a type, figure and sign. The thing itself also teaches this, because the water and the rite of Baptism foreshadow and figure regeneration through the merit of Christ and the working of the Holy Spirit, and the other evangelical benefits, as we have shown at greater length when we set out the analogy between the two. Add to this that we are baptized into the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit (Matt. 28:19), that is, by the sacrament of Baptism, and as by a seal and pledge, we are made certain of the grace of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and by this, as by a sworn bond, we are bound to them. We are baptized for the remission of sins (Acts 2:38), that is, so that we may conceive certainty concerning the remission of sins. The grace of regeneration and salvation are ascribed to Baptism (Eph. 5:26; Tit. 3:5; 1 Pet. 3:21) for no other reason than that Baptism, as pledge and seal, both gives birth to and produces the most certain confidence in them. Finally, we are baptized into Christ (Gal. 3:27) in a different way from how the Israelites of old are said to have been baptized into Moses (1 Cor. 10:2). For they were baptized into Moses so that they would receive his teaching as that of a faithful servant in the house of God, observe his precepts, and in due time receive the Messiah on the testimony of Moses. We are baptized into Christ, because Baptism, by the institution of Christ himself, is administered to us as a sign and seal of communion with Christ as Lord and Messiah, in whom our joy is brought to completion. Since Baptism is such a sign and seal of grace and salvation, it cannot in any way be regarded as operating as the efficient cause of that grace, whether its physical cause by an inherent power or its external cause by an assisting power. For seals do not properly effect the thing, but give assurance of what has been or is to be effected. Nor can any similar example be shown.

units.la: XLIII.
units.tr: XLIII.

units.la: Praeterea sicut omnia Sacramenta non gratiae causae ex opere operato,vel operantis efficientes, sed effecta; & causae non existentiae gratiae , nisi quatenus unà cum verbo morali quadam ratione ad operandam eam concurrere possunt,sed & certitudinis ejus quoad nos sunt ; uti pluribus Loc. XI. 60. 61. demonstravimus : ita nec Baptismus gratiam ex opere operato, virtute sive inhaerente & physica,ut Thomas Aquinas,& Dominicanorum sequacium schola pertendit; sive assistente,uti Scotus & Franciscanorum eidem consentientium schola asserit; producit. Qui error non levis ex characteris a Baptismo impressi,& necessitatis ejusdem absolutae figmento pullulans elementa mundi & creaturas gratiae causas faciens Sacramenta in idola & magica quaedam carmina commutat. Cui utinam Augustani nuncium in solidum remitterent. Sacramenta gratiae vehicula,& velut manum quandam, qua Deus gratiam suam donet, statuentes. Nam Sacramenta vim talem sive inhaerentem, sive assistentem nec ex natura habent, quod ipsimet fatentur : nec supra naturam ex peculiari operatione Divina , qualis nulla uspiam revelata est.Tum Apostolus Rom. VIII.29. 30. causas salutis edisserens,nec Baptisini,nec ullius Sacramenti alterius meminit. Nam electos glorificari asserit. Atqui constat plures baptizatos nec electos esse, nec glorificari; ut plures non baptizatos tum electos esse, tum certò glorificari. Altiores longè salutis causae & media,quàm res terrestres,& elementa sunt ; aeterna praecognitio , praedestinatio conformandorum cum imagine Filii, meritum Christi,
units.tr: Moreover, just as all the sacraments are not causes of grace by the work worked, nor efficient by the agent who works, but effects, and are causes not of the existence of grace but only in so far as they can concur, together with the moral word and some moral reason, in producing it, and also of our certainty about it, as we have shown at length (Loc. 11, pp. 60, 61), so Baptism does not produce grace by the work worked, whether by an inherent and physical power, as Thomas Aquinas and the school of Dominican followers maintain, or by an assisting power, as Scotus and the school of Franciscans who agree with him assert. This is no small error, springing from the fiction of an indelible character impressed by Baptism and of an absolute necessity of the same, which makes the elements of the world and creatures causes of grace and turns the sacraments into idols and certain magical incantations. Would that the Augsburg Confession had repudiated this entirely, by setting up the sacraments as vehicles of grace and as a kind of hand by which God gives his grace. For sacraments do not have such a power, whether inherent or assisting, either from nature (as they themselves confess), or above nature by a peculiar divine operation, of which no instance has been revealed anywhere. Moreover, the Apostle, in setting out the causes of salvation (Rom. 8:29, 30), mentions neither Baptism nor any other sacrament. For he asserts that the elect are glorified. But it is plain that many who are baptized are neither elect nor glorified, just as many who are not baptized are both elect and certainly glorified. The causes and means of salvation are far higher than earthly things and elements: eternal foreknowledge, the predestination of those to be conformed to the image of the Son, the merit of Christ,

units.la: Simul sigillum & causa gratiae esse non potest. Christi, sanctificatio Spiritus ad obedientiam (fidei) & aspersionem sanguinis Jesu Christi, 1. Pet. I. 2. sunt. Nulla vel in V. vel in N. T. creatura salutis nostrae causa proprie dicta nominata est; neque alia creaturarum in negotio salutis occupatio est, quam ex institutione Divina eandem effectam & promissam similitudine quadam repraesentandi & obsignandi, vel morali quadam ratione, adeoque mediata, non immediata, & ex opere operato manante virtute, producendi. Cumque omnis causa proprie dicta prior sit effectu, gratia regenerationis, fidei, resipiscentiae, remissionis peccatorum & sanctificationis vel effecta vel promissa Baptismo prior, non, ceu effectus ejus, posterior est. Atque ideo Christiani baptizantur, quia Christiani, regeniti, fideles, justificati, sanctificati sunt, jam eo tempore, quo baptizantur; vel saltem promissionem gratiae illius tempore Deo placito per ejusdem immediatam operationem successuræ habere censentur. Quia enim eorum est Regnum Coelorum, ideo ad Christum venire, & de gratia ejus certiores esse jubentur, Marc. X. 14. Et adulti non credituri, & resipiscentiam acturi, sed per gratiam regenerationis jam credentes & resipiscentes, & promissionum Divinarum velut ad se pertinentium compotes, baptizandi sunt. Resipiscite & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Domini Jesu, ad remissionem peccatorum &c. Nam vobis & liberis vestris promissiones factae sunt, Act. II. 38. 39. Et fides igitur & resipiscentia, adeoque regeneratio etiam baptismum illum praecesserunt: & promissiones Foederis gratiae ad eos jam pertinentes fundamentum suscipiendi Baptismi, non Baptismus fundamentum promissionum earum statuitur. Ideo fidelium parentum liberos Sanctos Apostolus dicit, 1. Cor. VII. 14. non per naturam, sed per sanctificantem gratiam, quosdam sanctitate etiam inhaerente omnes relativa; non post Baptismum demum, sed etiam ante Baptismum, quia alias par ratio esset liberorum a sanctificatis & non sanctificatis parentibus natorum, qui post Baptismum utrique sancti sunt; cum tamen Apostolus liberorum a sanctificatis parentibus fatorum hanc prae illis, qui a parentibus infidelibus fati sunt, praerogativam statuerit, quod illorum, non horum liberi sancti sint. Quia enim & a parentibus fidelibus nati praerogativa foederis gaudent & sancti sunt, baptizari debent: non demum sancti fiunt, quia baptizantur, & postquam baptizati sunt. Praeterea nonnullorum etiam in utero materno sanctificatorum Scriptura meminit, velut Jacobi, Rom. IX. 11. 13. quem typum & exemplar electorum ibidem v. 10. Apostolus statuit: Jeremiae, Jerem. I. 5. Davidis, quem in utero matris gratia Dei texit, & oculi gratiosi ejusdem aspexerunt, Psal. CXXXIX. 13. 16. Johannis Baptistae in utero matris spiritu pleni & exilientis, Luc. I. 15. Sed & Spirtus S. supra Cornelium aliosque ipsi praesentes cecidisse etiam ante Baptismum Actor. X. 44. 48. commemoratur. Ne quid de Veteris Ecclesiae catechumenis, non prius baptizatis, quam fidem profiterentur, dicam. Clarissime S. Petrus: Baptismus nos salvat, inquit, non depositio sordium carnis, sed interrogatio bonae conscientiae in Deum, 1. Petr. III. 21. In Ba-
units.tr: A seal cannot at the same time be the cause of grace. Christ, the sanctification of the Spirit to obedience (of faith) and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ (1 Pet. 1:2). In neither the Old nor the New Testament is any creature named as the cause of our salvation in the proper sense. Nor is there any other role for creatures in the business of salvation than, by divine institution, to represent and seal that same grace which has been effected and promised, by a certain likeness, or by a moral reason, and so mediately, not immediately, and by producing it through a power flowing from the work worked. And since every cause properly so called is prior to its effect, the grace of regeneration, faith, repentance, remission of sins and sanctification, whether effected or promised, is prior to Baptism; it is not later than it as its effect. Therefore Christians are baptized because they are already Christians, regenerate, believers, justified and sanctified at the time when they are baptized; or at least they are regarded as having the promise of that grace, which will follow at a time pleasing to God through its immediate operation. For since theirs is the kingdom of heaven, they are bidden to come to Christ and to be assured of his grace (Mark 10:14). And adults, who are not going to believe and repent, but who already believe and repent through the grace of regeneration, and who possess the divine promises as belonging to them, are to be baptized. Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, for the remission of sins, etc. For the promises have been made to you and to your children (Acts 2:38, 39). So faith and repentance, and therefore regeneration too, precede that Baptism; and the promises of the covenant of grace, already belonging to them, are established as the foundation for receiving Baptism, not Baptism as the foundation of those promises. Therefore the Apostle calls the children of believing parents holy (1 Cor. 7:14), not by nature, but by sanctifying grace, some by inherent holiness, all by relative holiness; and this holiness belongs to them not only after Baptism but even before it. Otherwise there would be the same reason for the children of sanctified and unsanctified parents, who are both holy after Baptism. Yet the Apostle has set up this privilege of children born of sanctified parents above those born of unbelieving parents, that the former are holy and not the latter. For since children born of believing parents enjoy the privilege of the covenant and are holy, they ought to be baptized; they do not become holy only afterwards, because they are baptized and after they have been baptized. Moreover, Scripture also mentions some who were sanctified even in the mother's womb, such as Jacob (Rom. 9:11, 13), whom the Apostle sets forth in the same passage (v. 10) as the type and pattern of the elect; Jeremiah (Jer. 1:5); David, whom the grace of God wove in his mother's womb, and whose unformed substance his eyes saw, that is, with favour (Ps. 139:13, 16); John the Baptist, filled with the Spirit even in his mother's womb and leaping (Luke 1:15). And the Holy Spirit is recorded as having fallen upon Cornelius and others present with him even before Baptism (Acts 10:44, 48). Not to mention the catechumens of the early Church, who were not baptized until they had professed the faith. Most clearly St. Peter says: Baptism saves us, he says, not by the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but by the answer of a good conscience toward God (1 Pet. 3:21). In Baptism, however, water cleanses the filth of the flesh through the work worked, and in so far as it cleanses in this way, it is a figure and sacrament of salvation. Therefore it does not save by being a figure and sacrament of salvation, nor is it the efficient cause of salvation. But on the same point, more is found in Loc. 11, pp. 60…

units.la: ptismo autem aqua ex opere operato sordes carnis abluit; & quatenus sic abluit, figura & Sacramentum salutis est. Non ergo qua figura & Sacramentum salutis est, salvat, vel salutis causa efficiens est. Sed eandem in rem plura Loc. XI. 60. 61. diximus, ubi etiam adversantium argumenta diluimus.
units.tr: In baptism, however, the water washes away the defilements of the flesh by the work done (ex opere operato). And insofar as it washes in this way, it is a figure and sacrament of salvation. It does not save insofar as it is a figure and sacrament of salvation, nor is it the efficient cause of salvation. But we have said more on this same point at Loc. XI. 60, 61, where we also refuted the arguments of opponents.

units.la: XLIV. Neque probanda hic nobis uno vel utroque pollice videtur opinio Theologorum quorundam recentium, caetera doctissimorum & meritissimorum, qui sic Baptismi efficaciam explicant, ut ejus aeque ac caeterorum Sacramentorum signa cum miraculorum signis contendant, & Deum ordinarie gratiam suam eodem tempore, quo eam per signa repraesentat, conferre, nisi singularis ratio obstet; infantes foederatorum ante Baptismum esse filios irae, morti obnoxios, nec plene reconciliatos; per Baptismum reatum omnem peccati originalis tolli, ut nemo baptizatus propter peccatum originale damnetur, & de non baptizatorum, utpote peccati originalis culpa etiamnum adstrictorum salute spes certa nulla sit; licet Deus tales modo extraordinario, & velut miraculoso, a consueta providentiae & gratiae via multum recedente salvare possit, quomodo multos longo tempore sine cibo, & Danielis socios in mediis flammis incolumes servavit afferant. Quae & extollendae in majus Sacramentorum efficaciae, atque necessitati, & minuendae nonnihil consolationi piorum, & elementorum religioni augendae esse, & nonnihil errori Pontificiorum indulgere videntur. Quorum etiam sententiam argumenta non pauca Pontificiis oppositia feriunt. Cumque Sacramenta non sint miracula, quia nihil ardui & inusitati habent, nisi quod significatio eorum ex institutio Dei supernaturalis est, signa eorum cum signis miraculorum perperam comparari videntur. Quanquam isthoc Sacramentorum efficaciam ex adverso deprimeret, quia signa miraculorum exiguam vel nullam nisi praesentis, at nulla operatione miraculum adjuvantis symboli vim habent: at signa Sacramentalia, ceu sigilla & arrhabones, gratiae certitudinem quoad nos efficiunt. Sed & usu venire sic posset, ut infantes fidelium parentum nulla sua & propria, sed parentum culpa, vel necessitatis acri telo ἀξιώπλησις, irae filii & morti obnoxii manerent, cum tamen Deus declaraverit, animam, quae peccaverit, moriturum, Ezech. XVIII. 20. Illud vero gravius videtur, quod omnium baptizatorum peccatum originale baptismo remitti afferunt. Vix enim illi Simoni Mago baptizato κακίαν pravitatem cordis, nec non συνδέσμον ἀδικίας colligationem illam & vinculum injustitiae, fontem & originem peccatorum omnium, propter quam ipsi μερίς portio & κλῆρος fors nulla in sermone fuit, Act. VIII. 21. 22. 23. remissam esse sustinuerint. Neque illud cum Evangelio convenit, ut vel Christus alia peccata remittere, alia retinere, adeoque peccata remittenda secare & partiri dicatur; cum remissio vel retentio peccatorum omnium sine ulla ullorum exceptione semper praedicetur: aliorum quam electorum peccata qualiacunque illa in se suscepit: vel peccata ulla sine Christi pro illis satisfactione remittantur: vel in statum gratiae per baptismum
units.tr: XLIV. Nor does the opinion of certain recent theologians, otherwise most learned and deserving, seem to me to deserve approval, not even with one or both thumbs. They explain the efficacy of baptism in such a way that they set the signs of baptism, like those of the other sacraments, alongside the signs of miracles, and hold that God ordinarily confers his grace at the same time as he represents it through the signs, unless some special reason stands in the way. They hold that the infants of covenanted parents before baptism are children of wrath, liable to death, and not fully reconciled; that through baptism all guilt of original sin is removed, so that no one baptized is condemned on account of original sin; and that there is no certain hope of salvation for the unbaptized, since they remain bound by the guilt of original sin. They concede that God can save such persons in an extraordinary way, and as it were miraculously, departing far from the customary way of providence and grace, and they cite how he preserved many for a long time without food, and Daniel's companions unharmed in the midst of the flames. These views seem to me to exalt the efficacy and necessity of the sacraments beyond measure, to diminish somewhat the consolation of the godly, to increase superstitious reverence for the elements, and to indulge somewhat the error of the Papists. The arguments opposed to the Papists strike their opinion as well. And since the sacraments are not miracles, having nothing arduous or unusual about them except that their signification is supernatural by God's institution, their signs seem wrongly compared with the signs of miracles. Yet this would on the other hand lower the efficacy of the sacraments, because the signs of miracles have little or no force beyond that of the present sign, which does nothing to help the miracle by any operation; whereas sacramental signs, like seals and earnests, produce certainty of grace as far as we are concerned. It could also happen that infants of faithful parents, not through their own fault but through their parents' fault, or through the sharp dart of necessity [ἀξιώπλησις], remain children of wrath and liable to death, although God has declared that the soul that sins shall die, Ezek. 18:20. More serious still seems their claim that the original sin of all the baptized is remitted by baptism. For they could hardly allow that wickedness of heart [κακίαν], and that bond and chain of injustice [συνδέσμον ἀδικίας], the fountain and origin of all sins, on account of which Simon Magus, though baptized, had no portion [μερίς] or lot [κλῆρος] in the word, was remitted, Acts 8:21-23. Nor does it agree with the Gospel that Christ is said to remit some sins and retain others, and so to divide and apportion the sins to be remitted; for the remission or retention of all sins is always preached without any exception: whatever sins he took upon himself, they were those of the elect and of no others. Nor are any sins remitted without Christ's satisfaction for them, or is anyone brought into the state of grace through baptism

units.la: Circa efficaciam Baptismi recentium quorundam opinio expenditur. mum cooptatus denuo per succedentia peccata actualia in statum irae collabatur, atque ita Deum vocationis & gratiae suae poeniteat. Quae obiter, salva virorum maximorum veneratione, afferenda duxi, memor Aquilam & Priscillam etiam potenti illi in Scripturis Apollini viam Dei accuratius exquisitius indicasse, Act. XVIII. 21. 25. 26. Quod novissime etiam Celeber. Theologus Hermannus Witsius accurata diatriba edita pari eruditione & modestia praestitit.
units.tr: Concerning the efficacy of baptism, the opinion of certain recent writers is examined. ...once admitted, falls back into the state of wrath through subsequent actual sins, and so makes God regret his calling and his grace. I have thought it right to set these things out in passing, with all due respect to such great men, mindful that Aquila and Priscilla also more accurately and carefully showed the way of God to the powerful Apollos in the Scriptures, Acts 18:21, 25, 26. Most recently, the distinguished theologian Hermann Witsius has also treated this matter in an accurate dissertation, with equal learning and moderation.

units.la: XLV. Qui sic Baptismi efficaciam auxerunt, Pontificii, eandem deinceps mire, sublata per eum remissione peccatorum postbaptismalium, depressum iverunt. Nam Synodus Tridentina Sess. VII. de Bapt. Can. 10. anathemate eos perculit, qui dixerint, peccata, quae post Baptismum fiunt, sola recordatione & fide suscepti Baptismi remitti. Ad remissionem enim peccatorum post Baptismum commissorum non Baptismum, sed novum Sacramentum poenitentiae, ceu secundae post naufragium tabulae valere, asserunt. Sed peccata equidem per solam gratiam Dei in Christo remittuntur. Ejus vero remissionis Baptismus sigillum & Sacramentum est, cujus legitimo usu remissio peccatorum omnium praeteritorum & futurorum remissio obsignatur, non exclusa fide & poenitentia Evangelica, quae, ceu medium salutis nostrae Divinitus constitutum Baptismo suo loco coordinatur. Etenim talis in suo genere Baptismus est, quale est Foedus ipsum Gratiae, per quod Baptismus efficax est. Baptismus enim & foedus gratiae ad se mutuo ut signum & res signata, referuntur. Atqui foedus gratiae aeternum est, adeoque ad peccatorum omnium remissionem se extendit, Genes. XVII. 7. Ezaj. LV. 3. Hos. II. 19. Si ad remissionem peccatorum postbaptismalium foedus gratiae non sufficeret, secundum peccatorum numerum multiplicari illud deberet. Aliter quidem atque aliter remissio peccatorum fide apprehenditur, poenitentia demonstratur, Sacramentis Baptismi & Eucharistiae obsignatur. Sed nec sic peccata remittenda in partes secantur & discerpuntur, ut remissionem aliorum fides apprehendat, aliorum poenitentia demonstret, aliorum Baptismus, aliorum Eucharistia obsignet. Ideo Scriptura Baptismo remissionem peccatorum omnium & praeteritorum, quia est lavacrum regenerationis, Tit. III. 5. & praesentium, quia Baptismus salvat nos in praesentiarum, 1 Petr. III. 21. & futurorum, quia baptizatus salvatur. Marc. XVI. 16. salus autem sine omnium peccatorum remissione non constat. Baptizamur enim in mortem Christi, Rom. VI. 3. quae non praeterita duntaxat, sed futura etiam peccata expiat. Et sine omni indicata temporis & remittendorum peccatorum differentia sic Scriptura loquitur: Baptizabat Johannes in deserto, & praedicabat Baptismum resipiscentiae ad remissionem peccatorum, Marc. I. 4. Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Jesu Christi ad remissionem peccatorum. Act. II. 38. Cur sic indefinite Scriptura loquitur, neque uspiam praeterita a futuris peccatis distinguit, si alia in Baptismo, alia in aliis Sacramentis remittantur? Ubi lex non distinguit, neque nobis distinguere fas est. Cumque in Christum baptizamur, Gal. III. 27. eumque ut
units.tr: XLV. Those who have so increased the efficacy of baptism, the Papists, have afterwards diminished it remarkably, since by their account the remission of sins committed after baptism is abolished. For the Council of Trent, Session 7, On Baptism, Canon 10, anathematizes those who say that sins committed after baptism are remitted by the mere recollection and faith of the baptism received. They assert that for the remission of sins committed after baptism it is not baptism but the new sacrament of penance that avails, like a second plank after shipwreck. But sins are indeed remitted through the grace of God in Christ alone. Baptism is the seal and sacrament of this remission, and through its lawful use the remission of all sins, past and future, is sealed, not excluding faith and evangelical repentance, which, as a means of our salvation divinely established, is coordinated with baptism in its own place. For baptism is of such a kind in its own sphere as the covenant of grace itself is, through which baptism is efficacious. For baptism and the covenant of grace are referred to one another as sign and thing signified. But the covenant of grace is eternal, and so extends to the remission of all sins, Gen. 17:7; Isa. 55:3; Hos. 2:19. If the covenant of grace were not sufficient for the remission of sins committed after baptism, it would have to be multiplied according to the number of sins. Remission of sins is indeed apprehended by faith and demonstrated by repentance in different ways, and it is sealed by the sacraments of baptism and the Eucharist. But the sins to be remitted are not so cut up and torn into parts that faith apprehends the remission of some, repentance demonstrates the remission of others, baptism seals some and the Eucharist seals others. Therefore Scripture ascribes to baptism the remission of all sins, past because it is the washing of regeneration, Titus 3:5; present because baptism saves us now, 1 Pet. 3:21; and future because the baptized is saved, Mark 16:16. But salvation does not stand without the remission of all sins. For we are baptized into the death of Christ, Rom. 6:3, which atones not only for past sins but also for future ones. And Scripture speaks in this way without any distinction of time or of the sins to be remitted: John was baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, Mark 1:4; Let each one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, Acts 2:38. Why does Scripture speak so indefinitely, and nowhere distinguish past from future sins, if some are remitted in baptism and others in the other sacraments? Where the law makes no distinction, we are not permitted to make one.

units.la: Paracletum nostrum apud Deum, 1. Joh. II. 1. Divina potentia oves suas conservantem, Joh. X. 9. 1. Petr. I. 5. ejus gratia & potentia futura utique etiam peccata nobis remittuntur; ac pro in & Baptismus in Christum remissionem talem Christi obsignat. Per Baptismum enim salvamur, Marc. XVI. 16. Tit. III. 5. 1. Petr. III. 21. Ergo ejusdem efficacia ad futura etiam peccata se extendit, quia alias per sequentia Baptismum peccata salus a Baptismo obsignata incidi & impediri posset. Par enim, certe non inferior Baptismi quam Circumcisionis ratio est. Atqui hanc etiam in futurum valuisse, Scriptura 1. Sam. XIV. 6. XVII. 26. testatur. Utrumque Circumcisionis & Baptismi Sacramentum justitiae, adeoque etiam justificationis, sigillum, Rom. IV. 11. est. Atqui justitia Christi semel donata omnia peccata remittit.
units.tr: Since we are baptized into Christ, Gal. 3:27, and he is our Advocate with God, 1 John 2:1, keeping his sheep by divine power, John 10:9; 1 Pet. 1:5, by his grace and power our future sins too are certainly remitted to us; and baptism, which is into Christ, seals such a remission from Christ. For through baptism we are saved, Mark 16:16; Titus 3:5; 1 Pet. 3:21. Therefore its efficacy extends also to future sins, for otherwise the salvation sealed by baptism could be cut off and hindered by sins committed afterwards. The reason for baptism is equal, and certainly not inferior, to that for circumcision. But Scripture attests that circumcision too was valid for the future, 1 Sam. 14:6; 17:26. Both the sacrament of circumcision and that of baptism are a seal of righteousness, and so also of justification, Rom. 4:11. But the righteousness of Christ, once bestowed, remits all sins.

units.la: XLVI. Semel φωτισθέντας illuminatos, si prolabantur, renovari posse ad poenitentiam, Apostolus Hebr. VI. 4. &c. negat. At nec φωτισμός illi Baptismus est, quia ante Baptismum, in eo, & post eum illuminationi locus esse potest, nec παράπτωμα prolapsus quovis peccatum postbaptismale, sed peccatum in Spiritum S. plane irremissibile notat: nec poenitentia, quae illuminatis & prolapsis negatur, baptismalis, sed quaevis poenitentia est. S. Johannes quoque: Si confiteamur, inquiens, peccata nostra, fidelis & justus est, ut peccata nobis remittat, 1. Joh. I. 9. non peccatorum post Baptismum admissorum remissionem Confessioni Sacramentali acceptam refert, quia nec de Confessione Sacramentali, qualis nulla est, sed de Evangelica, eaque non vel Christi merito, vel Baptismo opposita, sed utrique subordinata, & in adultis etiam cum Baptismo conjuncta, Matth. III. 6. ipsi termo est: & praecipuum, imo unicum remissionis peccatorum remedium, ἱλασμὸν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν propitiationem pro peccatis nostris, quam in Baptismo obsignari supra ostendimus, facit. Quod sic aeque facile reconciliari posse ante Baptismum per ignorantiam, & post Baptismum per notitiam peccantes, atque id iniquum esse, tricantur: frivolum equidem est, tum quia, quid apud Deum aequum vel iniquum sit, ex verbo ejus, non ex humano cerebro definiri debet: tum quia gratuitam plane peccatorum remissionem ex peccatorum qualitate vel quantitate dimetiri non licet, cum abundante peccato, quod agnoscitur & deploratur, gratia superabundet, Rom. V. 20 tum quia qualiscunque peccatorum remissio est, sive facilis, sive difficilis, remissio certe est, & gratuita remissio est, neque alia est, quam quae in Baptismo promissa & obsignata est. Ac licet vetus Ecclesia post Baptismum lapsis difficilimos subinde labores, nimia quadam ἐκλογὴ imposuerit, non tamen imposuit, quod nullam Baptismum in futura peccata efficaciam exercere, vel pro peccatis post Baptismum admissis Deo per labores ejusmodi poenales satisfaciendum putaverit. Satisfieri enim per labores ejusmodi non Deo, sed Ecclesiae, peccatis offensae disertis verbis Augustinus Enchirid. cap. 65. & Hieronymus in Matth. cap. 6. testantur. Qui etiam passim poenitentiam secundam post naufragium tabulam insignientes, non poenitentiam tanquam Sacramentum Baptismo
units.tr: XLVI. The Apostle, Heb. 6:4 and following, denies that those once enlightened, if they fall away, can be renewed to repentance. But that enlightenment [φωτισμός] is not baptism, since there can be a place for enlightenment before baptism, in it, and after it; nor does falling away [παράπτωμα] denote any sin committed after baptism, but plainly a sin against the Holy Spirit that is irremissible; nor is the repentance which is denied to the enlightened and the fallen baptismal, but any repentance whatever. Likewise St John: If we confess, he says, our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, 1 John 1:9. He does not refer the remission of sins committed after baptism to sacramental Confession, since the term itself refers not to a sacramental confession, of which there is none, but to an evangelical one; and that is not opposed to Christ's merit or to baptism, but subordinate to both, and in adults is also joined with baptism, Matt. 3:6. It is the chief, indeed the only, remedy for the remission of sins, propitiation for our sins [ἱλασμὸν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν], which, as we have shown above, is sealed in baptism. Some object that it is equally easy for those who sin before baptism to be reconciled through ignorance and for those who sin after baptism through knowledge, and that this is unjust. This is trifling: first, because what is just or unjust before God must be defined by his word, not by the human brain; second, because one may not measure the wholly gratuitous remission of sins by the quality or quantity of sins, where sin abounds, which is acknowledged and lamented, grace superabounds, Rom. 5:20; third, because whatever the remission of sins may be, whether easy or difficult, it is certainly a remission, and a gratuitous remission, and it is no other than that which is promised and sealed in baptism. And although the ancient Church at times imposed very difficult labours, by a certain excessive choice [ἐκλογή], on those who had fallen after baptism, it did not impose them because it thought that baptism exercised no efficacy against future sins, or that satisfaction was to be made to God for sins committed after baptism by such penal labours. For Augustine, in plain words in the Enchiridion chapter 65, and Jerome on Matthew chapter 6, attest that satisfaction for such labours is made not to God but to the Church offended by the sins. They also repeatedly call repentance the second plank after shipwreck, not as a sacrament like baptism

units.la: Baptismus remissionem peccatorum etiam post Baptismum commissorum obsignat.
units.tr: Baptism seals the forgiveness of sins committed even after Baptism.

units.la: Objectiones Pontificiorum dissolvuntur. ptismo in foro Poli & Divino succenturiarunt, sed tantum ostendere voluerunt, in foro Soli & Humano jus communionis & synaxeos peccato enormi post Baptismum commisso, non aliter quàm poenitentia publica, seu canonica recuperari, secus quàm Novatiani, nullum poenitentiae ejusmodi canonicae post Baptismum lapsis relinquentes, censebant. Etenim qui post peccatum navi non tam gratiae, quàm sensus gratiae per Baptismum obsignatae excidit, & tantisper tentationum fluctibus percellitur, is secunda tabula non indiget, cùm navis ipsa infracta semper & salva maneat, ad quam proin Baptismo munitam & obsignatam sine novo Sacramento reverti, eámque, ut Hieronymi verbo utar, retentare integrum est.
units.tr: The Papists' objections are answered. They supply the reception of baptism in the court of heaven and by divine reckoning, but they meant only to show that in the court of earth and by human judgement, the right of communion and of the Lord's Supper lost through a grave sin committed after baptism can be recovered only by public or canonical repentance. This is unlike the Novatians, who thought that no such canonical repentance was left for those who had fallen after baptism. For the one who falls into sin after baptism does not lose so much the grace as the sense of the grace sealed in baptism, and is for a while beaten by the waves of temptation. Such a person does not need a second plank, since the ship itself remains unbroken and safe. Having been fortified and sealed by baptism, he may return to it without a new sacrament, and it is open to him, to use Jerome's word, to retain it whole.

units.la: XLVII. Baptismus efficaciam non nisi in legitimo usu exercet.
units.tr: XLVII. Baptism exerts its efficacy only in lawful use.

units.la: Non enim, quod Theologis etiam orthodoxis quibusdam, Pareo, Davenantio, Forbesio visum, quotquot baptizantur, regenerationis participes fiunt, vel Christo inseruntur, quod de Simone Mago aliisque baptizatis similibus ne cogitare quidem fas est. Licet enim Baptismus medium quoddam, quo gratiae Dei obsignatio ad animam hominis derivatur, sit, tamen non magis Sacramento, quàm verbo suo gratiam Deus alligavit. Sicut igitur promissiones Evangelii, Christus & beneficia ejus omnibus Ecclesiae membris praedicantur & offeruntur, neque tamen per verbi praeconium in omnium audientium animas derivantur, sed in eas demum, quorum auditus cum fide contemperatus est, Heb. IV.2. quíque adeò ad salutem ab aeterno electi sunt: ita Baptismus visibile illud verbum, omnibus Evangelium profitentibus & eorundem liberis administratur, quia, sicut praecones verbi, ita etiam Sacramentorum dispensatores, fideles ab hypocritis, triticum à palea distinguere non valent; neque tamen per visibilem Baptismum res significata, seu gratia invisibilis & spiritualis aliis quàm promissionum haeredibus ab aeterno electis obsignatur. Sacramenta enim sigilla sunt. Quid verò sigilla chartae purae & virgini, in qua nec haeres, nec haereditas scripta est, appensa efficiunt? Grave verò & illud est, quòd regenerationem & justificationem etiam pereuntibus sic tribuunt. Cùm tamen semen regenerationis semper maneat, & justitia Christi justitia seculorum sit, neque foedus Gratiae semel initum rescindi unquam possit. Fatendum equidem est, quòd Sacramenta non arcani consilii & propositi Dei sed Foederis Dei revelati sigilla sint. Cùm tamen foedus gratiae non sit nisi executio aeterni consilii Dei, & justitia fidei, cujus sigilla Sacramenta sunt, & quam Foedus Gratiae promittit, non sit nisi electorum, ad eos utique solos Foedus Dei revelatum pertinet, qui in aeterno & arcano consilio Dei, ceu futuri foederati, nominati & scripti sunt.
units.tr: For it is not the case, as some orthodox theologians such as Pareus, Davenant and Forbes have thought, that all who are baptized become partakers of regeneration or are grafted into Christ. Such a thing cannot even be imagined of Simon Magus and other similarly baptized persons. For although baptism is a certain means by which the sealing of God's grace is conveyed to the soul of man, God has bound his grace no more to the sacrament than to his word. Just as the promises of the gospel, Christ and his benefits are proclaimed and offered to all members of the Church, yet they are not conveyed by the preaching of the word into the souls of all who hear, but only into those whose hearing is joined with faith (Heb. 4.2), and who were chosen from eternity for salvation, so baptism, that visible word, is administered to all who profess the gospel and to their children. For just as the heralds of the word, so too the dispensers of the sacraments cannot distinguish the faithful from the hypocrites, or the wheat from the chaff. Yet the thing signified, that is, the invisible and spiritual grace, is not sealed through visible baptism to anyone other than the heirs of the promises, chosen from eternity. For sacraments are seals. But what effect do seals attached to blank, virgin paper have, on which neither heir nor inheritance is written? It is also a grave matter that they attribute regeneration and justification even to those who perish. Yet the seed of regeneration always remains, the righteousness of Christ is a righteousness of the ages, and the covenant of grace once entered into can never be rescinded. It must indeed be admitted that the sacraments are seals not of the secret counsel and purpose of God, but of the revealed covenant of God. Yet since the covenant of grace is nothing but the execution of the eternal counsel of God, and the righteousness of faith, of which the sacraments are seals and which the covenant of grace promises, belongs only to the elect, the revealed covenant of God pertains surely to those alone who, in the eternal and secret counsel of God, have been named and written down as future parties to the covenant.

units.la: XLVIII. Neque etiam heic se extricant, qui rite baptizatis saltem gratiam regenerationis potentialem & vitam novam, quae si in illis nutriatur & foveatur, discant illi succum & saporem gratiae fugendo ad se derivare: at suffocabilem tamen vitam illam, nisi fugendo confirmetur; conferri afferunt. Perinde, inquiunt, ac si quis quaerenti, cur infans post sex septem ve dies mortuus reperiatur (suppositò, quòd mater eum nutrire neglexerit) respondeat; non quòd non sit natus non vitalis & vivus, sed quòd lacte non sit enutritus. Vitam ergo talem in cunctis suffocabilem, in multis in adulta aetate, vel adolescentia, seu suo, seu parentum vitio statuunt. Verùm nunquam, qui in peccato moriuntur, vixerunt, vel nati ex Deo vivi & vitales sunt; sed tantisper citra vitam novam vitalem omnes pares sunt, donec illos Deus discernat, suppeditans quibusdam intus arcanam & solidam cum Christo agglutinationem, exarescentibus reliquis. Sicut enim in terrena agricolatione, facta insitione ramorum plurium, qui ab oleastro amputati sunt in oleam bonam, nullus illorum quidquam intrinsecum à manu agricolae, per quod oleastri naturam exuat, & sugendo succum oleae bonae in se derivet, atque cum ea in lignum unum coalescat, sed totum hoc Coelo expectandum à benedictione Dei, qui solus incrementum dat, 1. Cor. III.7. ita qui sacramentaliter Christo inseruntur, nihil à Baptismi aquae efficacia vitalis vitae accipiunt, quae cunctis communis sit, & in aliis suffocetur, in aliis non; atque ita tandem illos non gratia Dei in solidum, sed non positus pariter gratiae obex suo vel parentum vitio, discernat. Quin potius idem quoad cunctos expectandus eventus esset, ut ejecti foras arescerent, nunquam facti palmites Christo συμφυτοι, nisi insitionis operi Deus ἐν κεντρῷ in occulto manum admoveret, & hos prae illis φυτεῶν plantationem suam efficeret. Nam omnis plantatio, quam non plantavit Pater Coelestis, eradicabitur, Matth. XV.13. XLIX. Neque tamen nulla omnino baptizatorum non electorum supra non baptizatos praerogativa est. Nam & olim Circumcisio, etiam non electorum circumcisis praerogativam supra non circumcisos contulit. Τί τὸ περισσὸν ἢ ἡ ὠφελία; Quae praerogativa Judaei, aut quae utilitas circumcisionis est? Multa omni modo. Nam illis credita sunt eloquia Dei, Rom. III. 1. 2. Pari ratione communis quaedam gratia & favor Dei est, quo omnes baptizati, etiam non electi potiuntur, initiatio, & ἐγκέντρισις insitio in externum Ecclesiae corpus, cujus vi etiam pereuntes jus habent in nomen υἱῶν βασιλείας filiorum regni, & privilegiis externis foederatorum Dei fruuntur. Sicut enim Circumcisio non tantum sigillum justitiae fidei, sed etiam externae communionis tanquam paries intergerinus Israelem inter & gentes, fuit: ita etiam Baptismus quorumvis annulus velut quidam, criterion & sigillum externorum Ecclesiae membrorum est, quo Deus iisdem aditum ad verbi & sacramentorum, aliorumque Ecclesiae privilegiorum communium usum obsignat. Ideo etiam Ecclesia visibilis venit nomine Regni Dei, Matth. VIII.12. XIII.41. & priore loco etiam filii Regni, sic dicti, quia per circumcisionem jus ad externa Regni πλεονεκτήματα habuerunt, ejiciendi dicuntur. Quemadmodum alibi ramí ab olea vera, & palmites à vite vera defringi, ejici foras, & collecti in ignem abjici dicuntur, Joh. XV. 1-6. Rom. XI. 17-24. Hoc ergo etiam pereuntes à Baptismo habent, quia jus in nomen filiorum Regni & externa Regni Dei πλεονεκτήματα habent. Sed vestibulum {a} nat. flibulum, cortex & superficies sola hæc Baptismi est, cuius interiora non quibusvis baptizatis, sed solis baptizatis electis patent. Gratia externa communis, interna electorum propria.
units.tr: XLVIII. Nor do those extricate themselves here who say that to those rightly baptized there is conferred at least a potential grace of regeneration and a new life, which, if it is nourished and cherished in them, they learn to draw to themselves the juice and savour of grace by fleeing sin. But that life is capable of being suffocated unless it is strengthened by flight. They compare it, they say, to someone asked why an infant is found dead after six or seven days (supposing the mother neglected to nurse it). The answer is not that it was not born, not alive and not living, but that it was not nourished with milk. So they hold that such a life is in all capable of being suffocated, and in many, in adult age or adolescence, through their own or their parents' fault. But those who die in sin have never lived, nor are those who are born of God alive and living in a sense that is not already established. All of them are equally without new and living life for as long as God has not separated them, supplying to some within a hidden and firm union with Christ, while the rest wither. For just as in earthly husbandry, when many branches cut from a wild olive are grafted into a good olive, none of them has anything intrinsic, by the hand of the husbandman, by which it may strip off the nature of the wild olive, draw to itself the juice of the good olive, and grow together with it into one tree. Rather, all this is to be expected from heaven, from the blessing of God, who alone gives the increase (1 Cor. 3:7). So those who are grafted into Christ sacramentally receive nothing of living life from the efficacy of the water of Baptism, which would be common to all and be suffocated in some but not in others. Thus at last God does not discern them by grace poured out entirely, but by the obstacle that equally stands in the way of grace, owing to their own or their parents' fault. Indeed, the same outcome would be expected for all, that the ejected would wither outside, never having become branches united with Christ (sympheytoi), unless God laid his hand in secret upon the work of grafting, in the hidden centre (en kentro), and made his own planting (phyteōn plantationem) of these rather than those. For every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted up (Matt. 15:13). XLIX. Yet there is not altogether no advantage of the baptized non-elect over the unbaptized. For formerly circumcision also conferred an advantage on the uncircumcised non-elect over the uncircumcised. What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the profit of circumcision? Much in every way. For to them were committed the oracles of God (Rom. 3:1-2). By the same reasoning there is a certain common grace and favour of God, which all the baptized, even the non-elect, enjoy: initiation and engrafting (egkentrisis) into the external body of the Church, by the power of which even those who perish have a right to the name sons of the kingdom (huioi basileias), and enjoy the external privileges of the covenanted people of God. For just as circumcision was not only a seal of the righteousness of faith but also, like a dividing wall, a token of external communion between Israel and the nations, so Baptism is like a ring, a criterion and seal of the external members of the Church, by which God seals to them access to the use of the word, of the sacraments and of the other common privileges of the Church. Hence the visible Church also comes under the name Kingdom of God (Matt. 8:12; 13:41), and in the former place also sons of the Kingdom, who are said to be cast out, because through circumcision they had a right to the external advantages (pleonektēmata) of the Kingdom. In the same way elsewhere the branches of the true olive and the shoots of the true vine are said to be broken off and cast out, and gathered and thrown into the fire (John 15:1-6; Rom. 11:17-24). Therefore those who perish also have this from Baptism, that they have a right to the name sons of the Kingdom and the external advantages of the Kingdom of God. But this is the vestibule, the bark and the mere surface of Baptism, whose inner parts are open not to all the baptized but only to the baptized who are elect. External grace is common, internal grace belongs to the elect.

units.la: L. Et baptizantur quidem adulti & infantes. Adulti illi, qui infideles nati & educati Christum didicerunt, fidem in eundem publice confitentur, & desiderium obsignandarum Divinarum promissionum testantur: Infantes illi, qui in gremio Ecclesiæ parentibus fidelibus nati, sicut fœderis gratiæ, ita sigillorum, eiusdem jure gaudent. Quoad adultos, non omnibus illis baptismus externus interiorem gratiam obsignat, sed solis illis, qui fidem minimè simulatam in corde gerunt, & verbis confitentur. Dixit Philippus Eunucho: Si credis ex toto corde, licet baptizari. Respondens vero dixit: Credo Filium Dei esse Jesum Christum, Act. VIII. 37. Absurdum enim & ἄλογον plane foret gratiam Dei sine ejusdem fœdere utentibus sigillo polliceri. Fœdus autem Dei ad solos credentes pertinet. Quotquot enim eum receperunt, iis dedit potestatem, ut filii Dei fiant, iis, qui credunt in nomen ejus, Joh. I. 12. Neque etiam infantibus fidelium parentum liberis omnibus & singulis, sed solis electis Baptismus regenerationem & gratiam spiritualem univeriam obsignat. Licet enim de singulis ejusmodi infantibus judicio charitatis bene sperare fas piumque sit, de universis tamen non licet, neque ἀκαία κρίσις justum judicium est. At nec infantibus electis omnibus & singulis Baptismus regenerationem præsentem obsignat. Alia enim electorum in infantia morientium: alia vitam ad usum usque rationis & ultra prorogantium ratio est. Qui in infantia moriuntur, illis Baptismus gratiam regenerationis & insitionis in Christum tam certò obsignatur, quàm certò illorum corpus aqua conspergitur. Cum enim illi non modo ordinario per verbum & Spiritum, sed sine verbo per solum Spiritum, mortem Christi applicantem, regenerentur, nihil obstat, quò minùs vel in utero materno sic regenerentur, & sanctificentur, adeòque mox Baptismus regenerationem jam factam, & ad mortem usque perseverantem obsignet. Neque illud obstat, quòd infantes ejusmodi nec verbum Dei audire, nec credere in Christum possunt, quia etiam sine iis Spiritus S. Christi justitiam & mortem iis applicare potest. Fides manus est, justitiam Christi donatam apprehendens. At donare Spiritus S. etiam non apprehensam manu potest, & justificatio in applicatione justitiæ Christi, non præcisè in apprehensione per manum fidei consistit. Defectum fidei Deus Spiritu suo sanctificante, & quæ fidei sunt, sublimiore modo præstante, supplet, quod inprimis ex anima infantis Christi, per conceptionem ex Spiritu S. etiam sine fide actuali, qualis adultorum est, sanctificata liquet: Cumque peccatum Adami primi infantibus applicetur actu tali, qualis adultorum est, non cognoscentibus, quid & quomodo in se fiat; etiam justitia Adami secundi iisdem verbum Dei adultorum more non audientibus, cognoscentibus & credentibus applicari & donari potest. Nam & homines infantibus munera conferunt, ad quæ licet non adultorum more apprehensa, jus plenum habent, ...
units.tr: L. Both adults and infants are baptized. Those adults who were born and brought up as unbelievers and have learned about Christ publicly confess faith in him and testify to their desire to have the divine promises sealed to them. Those infants who are born to believing parents in the bosom of the Church enjoy the right of the covenant of grace and likewise of its seals. As for adults, the external baptism does not seal inner grace to all of them, but only to those who bear faith in their heart, not feigned, and confess it in words. Philip said to the eunuch: "If you believe with your whole heart, you may be baptized." And he answered: "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God" (Acts 8:37). For it would be absurd and plainly unreasonable to promise the grace of God by a seal to those who do not use the covenant of God. But the covenant of God pertains only to believers. For to as many as received him he gave the power to become sons of God, to those who believe in his name (John 1:12). Nor does Baptism seal regeneration and spiritual grace universally to all and each of the infants of believing parents, but only to the elect. For although it is lawful and pious, by the judgment of charity, to hope well of each such infant, it is not lawful to do so of all, nor is an unreasonable judgment a just judgment. Yet neither does Baptism seal present regeneration to all and each of the elect infants. For there is one reason for the elect who die in infancy, and another for those whose life is prolonged to the use of reason and beyond. Those who die in infancy are sealed by Baptism to have grace of regeneration and of engrafting into Christ as surely as their body is certainly sprinkled with water. For since they are regenerated not only in the ordinary way through the word and the Spirit, but without the word, through the Spirit alone applying the death of Christ, nothing prevents them from being regenerated and sanctified even in the mother's womb, so that Baptism seals a regeneration already accomplished and persisting until death. Nor does it hinder that such infants can neither hear the word of God nor believe in Christ, because the Holy Spirit can apply to them the righteousness and death of Christ even without these. Faith is the hand that grasps the righteousness given in Christ. But the Holy Spirit can also give what is not grasped by the hand, and justification consists in the application of Christ's righteousness, not precisely in its apprehension by the hand of faith. God supplies the lack of faith by his sanctifying Spirit, who performs in a more exalted way the things that belong to faith. This is made plain above all by the soul of the infant Christ, which was sanctified by conception from the Holy Spirit even without actual faith such as adults have. And since the sin of the first Adam is applied to infants by an act such as adults perform, though they do not know what or how it is done in them, so the righteousness of the second Adam can also be applied to and bestowed upon them, though they do not hear the word of God in the manner of adults, nor know or believe. For men also confer gifts upon infants, which, though they are not grasped in the manner of adults, they have full right to ...

units.la: cèt actu illud non exerceant. Qui de infantibus dixit, quòd illorum sit Regnum Cœlorum, optimè is novit, quomodo Regnum Cœlorum illis conferat & applicet. Dubitari igitur nullo modo potest, quin infantum ejusmodi electorum in infantia morientium animæ vel ante Baptismum, vel certè in Baptismo per Spiritum S. Christo inserantur, justitiæ Christi sacra veste induantur, titulo filiorum, vel filiarum per adoptionis gratiam insigniantur; & imagine Dei donatæ ad statum glorificationis perducantur. Alia ratio infantum electorum eorum est, qui vitam ad usum usque rationis & ultra prorogant. Licet enim Dei gratia & potentia limitibus nullis coarctanda, & tempora regenerationis talium temerè definienda non sint, tamen illis promiscuè omnibus per Baptismum gratiam & regenerationem præsentem obsignari, non sine temeritate, sine solida ratione certè quidam definiunt. Si enim per Baptismum illis habitus gratiæ sive infunderetur, sive obsignaretur, maturè satis se proderet, neque diu nimis ignis ille Spiritus S. sub cinere carnis sopitus delitesceret. Ubicunque est, ibi operatur. Neque in talibus Deus ordinem suum deserere videtur, in eo consistentem, quòd fides ex auditu gignitur, & justitia Christi per fidem, non sine ea, apprehenditur.
units.tr: yet they do not exercise that right in act. Whoever spoke of infants and said that the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to them knew very well how He confers and applies the Kingdom of Heaven to them. There can therefore be no doubt in any way that the souls of such elect infants as die in infancy are, either before Baptism or certainly in Baptism, joined to Christ through the Holy Spirit, clothed in the sacred robe of Christ's righteousness, marked with the title of sons or daughters through the grace of adoption, and, having been given the image of God, brought on to the state of glorification. The case of elect infants who prolong their life to the use of reason and beyond is different. For although the grace and power of God are not to be confined within any limits, and the times of regeneration must not be rashly fixed for such persons, nevertheless some define, not without rashness and certainly without solid reason, that present grace and regeneration are sealed to all of them indiscriminately through Baptism. For if a habit of grace were either infused or sealed to them through Baptism, it would reveal itself early enough, and that fire of the Holy Spirit would not lie hidden for long, smothered under the ashes of the flesh. Wherever it is, there it works. Nor does God seem to abandon His order in such cases, which consists in this: that faith comes by hearing, and the righteousness of Christ is apprehended through faith, and not without it.

units.la: LI. Neque tamen sic Baptismus infantum electorum, sive in infantia morientium, sive vitam prorogantium inanis figura & ceremonia ludrica est; quia illis gratiam præsentem & extraordinariam, sed ab iis non intellectam; his futuram & ordinariam obsignat. Præterquam enim quòd minister Baptismi furorum fatorum infantum minimè conscius ex præcepto Christi omnes baptizare tenetur, perinde ut omnibus, perituris etiam, verbum Dei prædicare tenetur, quia salvandorum & pereuntium differentiam ignorat; etiam Baptismus in infantia morientibus efficax gratiæ sigillum manet, licèt gratiam extraordinariam in Baptismo obsignatam non intelligant, neque per fidem sibi applicare valeant. Nam intellecturi & per fidem sibi applicaturi fuerant, si ad annos pervenissent, & in infantiâ morientibus ipsis intelligunt parentes, intelligit Ecclesia, cujus interest, ut de salute civium suorum certitudinem, nonnullam habeat. Denique ipsi etiam in Cœlo intelligunt, quantis beneficiis in terra Deus se mactaverit. Ac multò minus Baptismus ceremonia inutilis est illis, qui ad ætatem rationis usus comporem proficiunt, quia obsignatam in Baptismo gratiam ordinariam vera fide sibi applicant, ejusque sic obsignatæ fiduciam & certitudinem tum, cùm in Christum credunt, concipiunt. Sicut enim infans coronatus jus non inane & cassum, sed maximè reale habet ad Regnum, sed illud demum exercet, atque eo fruitur, quando administrandi Regni capacitatem adipiscitur: ita infans electus baptizatus jam tum jus communionis cum Christo, regenerationis & adoptionis eo velut sigillo sibi obsignatum habet; sed ætatis vitio & impotentia non ante illud exercet, atque eo fruitur, quàm Deus ei fidem operosam ad apprehendendum Christum; ejusque beneficia largiri dignatur. Plenum ergo Christo Sacramentum etiam infantii administratum est, non ceremonia otiosa & nuda; cujus utilitas summa tum durante infantia ad parentes & Ecclesiam, promissionibus Divinis sibi & semini suo factis confidentem: tum ad infantes ipsos, quando adoleverint, & Divina dignatione fidem in Christum acceperint, redundat. Tum enim maximè quæ sibi vagientibus facta sunt, pia meditatione recognoscunt, & Divinæ charitatis cum gratiarum actione recordantur, ut modò natos & à matre rubentes, è genetricis gremio in suas quasi ulnas solenniter deferri jusserit: ut canticum illud: Fecisti, ut securus agerem ad ubera matris mea: in te rejectus sum ex vulva, inde ab utero matris mea Deus meus es, Psal. XXII. 10. 11. ori suo indiderit, ut à teneris unguiculis sacratissimo fœderi suo se innexuerit, & bonis omnibus mactaverit: ut denique tesseram & sigillum impresserit, cujus fructus nunc lætus se profert, & lætissimus in æternitate exuberabit.
units.tr: LI. Yet the Baptism of elect infants, whether of those who die in infancy or of those who prolong their life, is not therefore an empty figure or a mocking ceremony; for it seals to them a present and extraordinary grace, though one they do not understand, and to the others a future and ordinary grace. For, apart from the fact that the minister of Baptism, ignorant of the fates of infants, is bound by Christ's command to baptize all, just as he is bound to preach the Word of God to all, even to those who will perish, since he does not know the difference between those who are to be saved and those who perish, Baptism also remains an effective seal of grace in infants who die, even though they do not understand the grace sealed in Baptism and cannot apply it to themselves through faith. For they would have understood and applied it through faith had they reached adulthood; and in the case of infants who die, the parents understand it, and the Church, whose concern it is, understands it, so that it may have some certainty about the salvation of its members. Finally, the infants themselves in heaven understand how great the benefits are with which God has blessed them on earth. Much less is Baptism a useless ceremony for those who advance to the age of reason, since they apply to themselves by true faith the grace ordinarily sealed in Baptism, and when they believe in Christ they conceive the confidence and certainty of that sealed grace. For just as an infant who has been crowned has a right to the kingdom that is not empty and void but most real, yet he does not exercise it or enjoy it until he attains the capacity to administer the kingdom, so the baptized elect infant already has the right of communion with Christ, of regeneration and of adoption, sealed to him by that seal; but because of the defect of his age and his inability he does not exercise or enjoy it until God deigns to grant him the working faith to apprehend Christ and His benefits. The Sacrament is therefore fully administered to infants also, not as an idle and bare ceremony; its greatest usefulness flows both during infancy to the parents and the Church, who trust in the divine promises made to them and to their seed, and afterwards to the infants themselves, when they have grown up and by divine favour have received faith in Christ. For then they most of all recall with pious meditation what was done for them while they were crying, and with thanksgiving remember the divine love, just as He ordered that those newly born and reddened from the mother be solemnly carried from the mother's lap into His arms, so that they might put on their lips that song: "Thou didst make me trust when I was on my mother's breasts; I was cast upon thee from the womb; from my mother's belly thou art my God" (Ps. 22:9-10), and that from their tender nails they might be bound to His most sacred covenant and endowed with all good things; and finally that He might impress the token and seal, whose fruit they now joyfully display and in eternity will abound in most joyfully.

units.la: LII. Baptismi effecta eximia sunt confirmatio fidei, & obligatio ad cultum veri Dei.
units.tr: LII. The chief effects of Baptism are the confirmation of faith and the obligation to the worship of the true God.

units.la: Sigillum enim gratiæ cùm sit, fidem gratiæ tum regenerationis, cujus lavacrum est, Tit. III. 5. tum remissionis peccatorum, utpote ad quam baptizamur, Actor. II. 38. tum unionis nostri cum Christo, quem in Baptismo induimus, Gal. III. 27. mirè confirmat, ejusque in nobis certitudinem munit. In nomen Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. cùm detur, ad colendum eum, & propter eum diligendum proximum obligat, & incitat. Quomodo verò fidem gratiæ Baptismus confirmet & excitet, obscurum esse non potest. Nam primò Deus Baptismum dans is est, qui per ministrum à nobis stipulatur, sive nos interrogat de veritate & sinceritate fidei & resipiscentiæ nostræ. Quæ stipulatio id efficit, ut nos ipsos excutiamus, & in conscientia ipsi experimenta Spiritus fidei investigemus, & cor nostrum coram Deo effundamus. Deinde idem in Baptismo alloquitur corda nostra, & testimonium nobis præbet, quòd sit Pater noster in Christo, imò nobis de gratiæ suæ constantia veluti jurat. Cui respondet ὁμολογία seu astipulatio gloriationis nostræ in Deo, & interrogationis ejus, sive commemorationis in precibus nostris promissionum ejus nobis factarum, cum conscientia pura & à peccatis absoluta. Ita salvat Baptismus, non depositio sordium carnis (seu dum corpus à sordibus peccati abluitur) sed interrogatio bonæ conscientiæ ad Deum (astipulatio & fiducia conscientiæ mundæ, quæ est fidei gloriantis in Deo, quæ nunquam confundit) 1. Petr. III. 21. Accedit visibilis repræsentatio gratiæ, quæ in Baptismo obsignatur, quæque unâ cum verbo fidem excitat & confirmat. Cùmque Baptismus signaculum fœderis gratiæ sit, non tantùm gratiam obsignat, sed etiam officium nostrum in fœdere gratiæ requisitum, fidem & novam obedientiam, adeóque amorem Dei & proximi stipulatur.
units.tr: For since it is a seal of grace, it powerfully confirms our faith in the grace of regeneration, of which it is the washing (Tit. 3:5), in the remission of sins, to which we are baptized (Acts 2:38), and in our union with Christ, whom we put on in Baptism (Gal. 3:27), and it strengthens our certainty of these in us. Since it is given in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, it binds and urges us to worship Him and to love our neighbour for His sake. How Baptism confirms and stirs up faith in grace cannot be unclear. For first, God, who gives Baptism, is the one who through the minister demands from us a pledge, that is, who questions us about the truth and sincerity of our faith and repentance. This demand brings it about that we examine ourselves, search within our conscience for the experiences of the Spirit of faith, and pour out our heart before God. Then, in Baptism, He addresses our hearts and bears witness to us that He is our Father in Christ; indeed He swears to us, as it were, the constancy of His grace. To this there answers the ὁμολογία [confession], or the joint pledge of our glorying in God, and of our answer to His question, or of our recalling in prayer the promises made to us, with a pure conscience absolved from sins. Thus "Baptism saves, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh (that is, the washing of the body from the filth of sin), but the appeal of a good conscience towards God" (1 Pet. 3:21): the pledge and confidence of a clear conscience, which is the faith that glories in God and never puts to shame. To this is added the visible representation of the grace sealed in Baptism, which together with the Word stirs up and confirms faith. And since Baptism is the sign and seal of the covenant of grace, it not only seals grace but also demands from us the duty required in the covenant of grace, namely faith and new obedience, and so stipulates the love of God and of neighbour.

units.la: LIII. Baptismi subjectum est Populus Dei fidelis, sive verè sit, sive censeatur talis ob externam fidei professionem, & cum fidelibus communionem absque omni gentis, sexus & ætatis distinctione. Gentis, quia licet initiò solis Judæis administrari debuerit, deinceps tamen mandante Christo omnibus gentibus administra-ri cœpit, Matth. XXVIII. 19. Sexus, quia utrique sexui communis est; sicut Philippus viros & mulieres, Actor. VIII. 12. Paulus Lydiam, ibid. XVI. 15. Stephanam, 1. Cor. I. 16. alias baptizarunt. Ætatis denique, quia adulti & infantes baptizari debent; ea tamen conditione, ut adulti priùs peccata sua confiteantur, & fidem in Christum profiteantur, Matth. III. 6. Actor. II. 41. VIII. 12. 37. Infantes verò parente fideli sive utroque, sive alterutro nati sint, ibid. II. 38. 39. 1. Cor. VII. 14. LIV. Sed Infantum Baptismum & Pelagiani veteres, & recentes Socinani atque Anabaptistæ improbant; Illi quòd infantes peccato originali carentes sacro lavacro non indigeant: Isti, quòd Baptismum in universum, nedum in infantibus, utpote Christum Servatorem ignorantibus, necessarium non esse, neque ulla Christi beneficia obsignari censeant: Hi, quòd institutio desit, & doctrinam Christi cognoscere non valeant. Audita est vox Mennonis, non homine sed bove digna, quòd Pædobaptismus nihil à campanarum baptismo differat, immutatio Divini ordinis, abusio nominis, & abominabile idolum fit. Eò væsaniæ ignorantia & obstinatio hominum processit. LV. Cæterum sicut Circumcisio toti Semini Abrahami, non tantùm adultis, sed etiam pueris, ad obsignandum iis fœdus gratiæ cum Abrahamo & toto semine ejus initum, data est: ita Baptismus, qui circumcisioni successit, Col. II. 10. 11. ab Ecclesia liberis fidelium æquè ac fidelibus adultis rectè confertur. Nam promissio Abrahamo & Semini ejus facta non imminuta fuit tum, cùm Christus revelatus est, sed sub N. T. per os Petri repetita est, dicentis: Baptizetur unusquisque vestrum, &c. Vestra enim est promissio & filiorum vestrorum, Act. II. 38. 39. Ponitur præceptum, ut unusquisque baptizetur, addita ratione per conjunctionem γὰρ enim, etiam, quòd & liberis (indefinitè sine ætatis discrimine) eorum facta sit promissio, & utrorumque, parentum & liberorum receptio intelligenda relinquitur ex prima fœderis pactione cum Abrahamo, patre omnium fidelium ex Judæis & Gentibus sancita, Rom. IV. 10. 11. ubi infantes censebantur ex conditione parentum, & masculi die octavo circumcidebantur. Unde consequens est, non minùs Israelitas vi promissionis liberis suis sub N. T. baptismum petere posse, quàm sub V. T. iisdem circumcisionem datam esse constabat. Porro Israelitæ, qui olim prope erant, & fideles ex gentibus, quæ olim μακρὰν procul erant, nullo discrimine sub N. T. habentur. Non est Judæus, neque Græcus. Non est servus, neque liber. Non est mas, neque fœmina. Omnes enim vos unus estis in Christo Jesu, Galat. III. 28. Unde etiam hominis fidelis gentilis, non præjudicante alterius conjugis infidelitate liberi ἅγιοι sancti sunt, 1. Cor. VII. 14. Quæ sanctitas non minor ea est, de qua S. Paulus: Si primitiæ sanctæ, & massa: si radix sancta & rami, Rom. XI. 16. Unde etiam semen Israelis sanctum, Esaj. VI. 13. Esr. IX. 2. appellatur; & in eadem etiam gentiles in fœdus assumpti cum Israelitis paria faciunt, quia & ipsi Semen Abrahami spirituale sunt. Cùm ergo æquè Baptismus atque Circumcisio credentibus dentibus obsignet id foedus, in quod recepti sanctos habent liberos, jure eodem Ecclesia infantibus impertitur Baptismum, quo etiam Circumcisionem olim impertita est. Neque illud obstat, quòd mandato Circumcisionis addita est comminatio excidii, Baptismo non item, & quòd Circumcisio solis masculis & octavo die administrata est; at Baptismus etiam foemellis administratur. Analogia enim utriusque Sacramenti, atque etiam successio eorum inter se, non in omnibus circumstantiis, sed in conditionibus principalibus, ad confirmationem foederis gratuiti relatis, & in N. T. declaratis, valet. At comminatio excidii circumstantia, politiae Israelis accommodata fuit. Ejusdem commatis est determinatio temporis, & sexus foeminei ceu Sacramenti illius quoad signum inhabilis, exclusio. Tum jussit discipulos suos Christus μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη Gentes discipulos facere & baptizare, Matth. XXVIII. 19. Qui in gremio Ecclesiae nascuntur & suscipiuntur, & quibus אב מוסר eruditio patris & אם תורה traditio matris est verbum Dei, quemadmodum & liberis Patriarcharum fuit, & qui capaces sunt institutionis, quae etiam in aetate infantili incipi debet, quis eos unà cum parentibus ad discipulatum Christi pertinere negaverit? Qualibus Christus etiam Regnum Coelorum promittit, Matth. XIX. 14. Marc. X. 13. Sed à symbolis communionis Sanctorum excludere eos, qui discipuli Christi sunt, & in gremio Ecclesiae existunt, & sancti, non ἀκάθαρτοι impuri sunt; 1. Cor. VII. 14. quos aeque ac liberos Israelitarum, ceu foederis sui participes, Deus non excindit, Genes. XVII. 10. 11. imò disertis verbis admittit, & in quibus quandoque sanctificationem etiam Spiritus peragit, nae illud immane nimis est. Neque profecto de nihilo est, quòd cùm Apostoli jussi fuerint baptizare τὰ ἔθνη Gentes integras, si integrae crediderint, & domos integras baptizasse non semel legantur, eodem plane loquendi modo, quo & gens Abrahamidarum circumcidi jubebatur, & totae domus circumcisae sunt, nulla tamen vel in mandato indefinito, vel in historia praxeos sacra restrictio ad solos adultos invenitur, quò minùs similibus similis obsignatio ejusdem promissionis, quae in V. T. fuit, fieri intelligeretur. Accedit, quòd cùm Baptismus sit sigillum foederis gratiae Dei & promissionis foederalis, Actor. II. 39. causa nulla reddi potest, cur infantibus non imprimatur. Nam etiam rebus inanimatis sigillum foederis sigillum impressum olim fuit. Iris in nube sigillum foederis fuit, Genes. IX. 13. Lex in altari insculpta pariter sigillum foederis fuit, Jos. VIII. 30. 31. Sanguis sparsus in duodecim columnas erectas duodecim tribus Israelis repraesentantes sigillum & vinculum foederis fuit, Exod. XXIV. 4. &c. Et quanto magis sigillum infantibus & animatis & ratione praeditis & foederis capacibus imprimi potest? Erat olim circumcisionis, & non deest nostris infantibus aequalis capacitas. Non dispositio recipientis, sed voluntas instituentis requiritur. Cùmque in Baptismo obligemur S. S. Trinitati ad obsequium, constat, etiam infantes, imò nondum natos haeredes, Deut. XXIX. 15. obligari. Nam id, ad quod
units.tr: LIII. The subject of baptism is the faithful people of God, whether they truly are such or are reckoned to be so because of an outward profession of faith, and who share in fellowship with the faithful, without any distinction of nation, sex or age. Nation: although it ought at first to have been administered only to the Jews, afterwards, at Christ's command, it began to be administered to all nations, Matt. 28:19. Sex: because it is common to both sexes; thus Philip baptized men and women, Acts 8:12; Paul baptized Lydia, ibid. 16:15, and Stephanas, 1 Cor. 1:16, and others. Age: finally, because both adults and infants ought to be baptized, though on this condition, that adults first confess their sins and profess faith in Christ, Matt. 3:6; Acts 2:41; 8:12, 37. Infants, however, whether born of a believing parent, both or only one, are to be baptized, ibid. 2:38, 39; 1 Cor. 7:14. LIV. But the Pelagians of old, and the Socinians and Anabaptists of more recent times, reject infant baptism. The former because infants, being free from original sin, have no need of the holy washing; the latter because they think baptism is not necessary at all, let alone in infants, who know nothing of Christ the Saviour, and that no benefits of Christ are sealed by it; and the Anabaptists because there is no institution for it and infants cannot know the doctrine of Christ. The words of Menno have been uttered, worthy not of a man but of an ox: that infant baptism differs in no way from the baptism of bells, a change of the divine order, an abuse of the name, and an abominable idol. To such a pitch has the ignorance and obstinacy of men gone. LV. Moreover, just as circumcision was given to the whole seed of Abraham, not only to adults but also to boys, to seal to them the covenant of grace made with Abraham and with his whole seed, so baptism, which has succeeded circumcision, Col. 2:10, 11, is rightly conferred by the Church on the children of believers just as on adult believers. For the promise made to Abraham and to his seed was not diminished when Christ was revealed, but under the New Testament it was repeated through the mouth of Peter, who said: "Let each one of you be baptized," etc. For the promise is yours and your children's, Acts 2:38, 39. A command is laid down that each one be baptized, with the reason added by the conjunction γὰρ, "for"; and that the promise was made also to their children (indefinitely, without distinction of age), and that the reception of both parents and children is to be understood, is left clear from the first covenant agreement with Abraham, the father of all believers from Jews and Gentiles, Rom. 4:10, 11, where infants were reckoned by the condition of their parents, and males were circumcised on the eighth day. Hence it follows that, by virtue of the promise, the Israelites could no less ask baptism for their children under the New Testament than it was evident that circumcision had been given to the same under the Old.
