Sedere ergo, dominari debuit in medio fidelium, Seniorum, Pastorum, Episcoporum, non ut alius Episcopus, Pastor, λαὸν Θεοῦ minister Dei, sed ut Deus. Quid ergo de Ecclesiæ externæ, quoad commixtam ejus partem deteriorem, infallibilitate, perpetuitate & sinceritate statuendum sit, abundè hinc colliquescit.
units.tr: crept in under the name of Christian, threatening, with the same words of the foundation, the profession of the Apostles' Creed on his lips and the Scriptures in his hand. He ought therefore to sit and rule in the midst of the faithful, the elders, the ministers and the bishops, not as another bishop or minister, a minister of God [λειτουργὸς Θεοῦ], but as God. From this it is abundantly clear what must be decided concerning the infallibility, perpetuity and sincerity of the external Church, as regards its mixed and worse part.

units.la: XLV. Sed commixtio illa deficientium, Exlegis Antichristi cum Ecclesia vera non semper fuit, sed aliquot post Christi mortem secuVerbatim omitted. demonstrationem ex Scripturis finirentur, odio potissimum novitatis, quasi omne novum, in quo est profectus cognitionis verbi Dei & fundamenti simpliciter rejiciendum esset; & eadem fraude sedes aliqua, apud quam certior traditionis successio esset, velut à Deo electa ad custodiam & conservationem veritatis extolleretur; ut inprimis de libero arbitrio, de justitia fidei & sacrificio Christi quaestiones commoverentur, atque illae minùs solidè illustratae multis occasionem errandi praeberent: ut Philosophi, Rhetores & Causidici ad Religionem Christianam conversi, & neophyti eloquentia & sapientia sua ad multa incautiùs dicenda & docenda, quae deinceps traditionis & humanae praeceptionis materies essent, abuterentur: ut unus caeteris Episcopus cum singulari potestate manus imponendi praeesset: ut controversiae & lites fidelium ad Episcopos deferrentur, eorumque sic cupiditas cum jurisdictione quadam assumpta aliis terrestrium ad instar principium dominandi augeretur, & eam alii ignorantes naturam Regni Coelorum augerent, eósque inprimis, qui caeteris Episcopis in magnis regionibus praerant, opibus amplis ditarent: ut Imperatores Episcopis jurisdictionem confirmarent, & officiales suos quenquam à judicio Episcopi avellere vetarent: ut πᾶσαι cathedrarum Patriarchalium, maximè Romanae sedis, ceu primae in Occidente, Synodica & Caesarea auctoritate stabilirent, & Imperatores Episcopi Romani sententias pro editis & legibus recipi mandarent. His aliisque sensim sine sensu provenientibus fieri potuit, ut, quamvis Episcopus Romanus dominium Ecclesiae externae sic adeptus cuncta ex praescripto verbi Dei gereret, (secus tamen plane factum est) plurimi tamen potius ipsius nomen, quàm verbi Divini authoritatem sequerentur, atque ea opinione imbuerentur, Deum eam sedem ad praeservandam Ecclesiam ab omni corruptione elegisse; atque ita in Ecclesia externa humanum nomen Divino praevaleret, & quidvis pro lubitu definiendi & dictandi, Monarchiam inprimis spiritualem erigendi, & tyrannidem in conscientias exercendi, quin & persequendi eos, qui in mundo piè vivere volunt, facultas esset. Et clanculum igitur in externa Ecclesia mysterium illud iniquitatis, seminibus ad apostasiam suo tempore maturandam jactis, operari; & tandem apostasia ipsa in externae Ecclesiae visceribus, & Templo Dei praevalere debuit.
units.tr: XLV. But this mixing of the failing with the true Church, of the lawless Antichrist, did not always exist, but some centuries after Christ's death it followed, ... demonstration from the Scriptures were brought to an end, chiefly from hatred of novelty, as if everything new, in which there is progress in the knowledge of the Word of God and of the foundation, were simply to be rejected; and by the same deceit some see, in which there was a more certain succession of tradition, was exalted as if chosen by God for the guarding and preserving of truth. Thus questions were raised especially about free will, the justice of faith and the sacrifice of Christ, and these, being less solidly explained, offered many an occasion for error. Philosophers, rhetoricians and lawyers converted to the Christian religion, and neophytes, abused their eloquence and wisdom to say and teach many things too carelessly, which afterwards became the matter of tradition and human precept. One bishop was set over the rest with a unique power of laying on hands. Disputes and quarrels of the faithful were referred to the bishops, and their desire to rule was increased, having assumed a certain jurisdiction, after the manner of earthly princes, and others, ignorant of the nature of the kingdom of heaven, increased it and enriched them with ample wealth, especially those who presided over the other bishops in large regions. Emperors confirmed jurisdiction for the bishops and forbade their officials to withdraw anyone from the bishop's judgment. The patriarchal sees, above all the Roman See as the first in the West, were established by synodical and imperial authority, and emperors ordered that the decrees of the Roman bishop be received as edicts and laws. By these and other things arising gradually and without notice, it could happen that, although the Roman bishop, having thus obtained dominion over the external Church, managed everything according to the prescription of the Word of God (though in fact it was done quite otherwise), yet most people followed his name rather than the authority of the Divine Word, and were imbued with the opinion that God had chosen that see to preserve the Church from all corruption. Thus in the external Church the human name prevailed over the Divine, and there was the power to define and dictate whatever one pleased, above all to set up a spiritual monarchy, to exercise tyranny over consciences, and even to persecute those who wish to live piously in the world. And so the mystery of iniquity, with the seeds of apostasy sown to ripen in its time, was secretly at work in the external Church; and at last apostasy itself was bound to prevail in the very bowels of the external Church and in the Temple of God.

units.la: XLVI. Cùm ergo Ecclesiam externam in quibusvis coetibus suis particularibus errare posse constet, & in eandem apostasiam, & in fidem dominationem hominis Adversarii & Exlegis introductum iri praedictum sit, quatenus cum ea Ecclesia sic errante vel inordinata fideles communionem colere possint, vel ab ea discessionem facere teneantur, disquirendum est.
units.tr: XLVI. Since it is established that the external Church can err in any of its particular assemblies, and since it has been foretold that the rule of the man of sin and the lawless adversary will be introduced into that same apostasy and into faith, it must be inquired whether the faithful may keep communion with that Church while it errs or is disordered, or whether they are bound to separate from it.

units.la: Atque id ante omnia constat, oportere, hoc est, ex voluntate & decreto Dei non posse non adeóque necessariò in Ecclesia haereses esse ut probi manifesti fiant, 1. Cor. XI. 19. Licèt enim Deus haereses non elegerit, ceu causas & media boni; tamen eas ordinavit & permittere decrevit, ceu occasionem manifestandae rectitudinis fidelium, ut per eas tententur & manifestentur. Deus enim hoc modo probos, rectos, pios, sinceros, veros fideles, qui soli Deo credunt, & fundamento fidei immobiliter adhaerent, & in bona conscientia fratres appellari possunt, manifestos facere, at hypocritas, Pseudapostolos, Pseudoprophetas confundere, imò etiam ab Ecclesiae suae communione abscindere statuit.
units.tr: Above all, this is established: heresies must arise in the Church, that is, by the will and decree of God they cannot but arise, and so necessarily, that the approved may be made manifest, 1 Cor. 11:19. For although God has not chosen heresies as causes or means of good, yet he has ordained them and decreed to permit them as an occasion for displaying the uprightness of the faithful, so that they may be tested and made manifest through them. For God has determined in this way to make manifest the upright, the righteous, the pious, the sincere, the true faithful, who trust in God alone, cling immovably to the foundation of faith, and can be called brothers with a good conscience; and to confound hypocrites, false apostles and false prophets, and even to cut them off from the communion of his Church.

units.la: Nam qui in externa Ecclesia probi sunt, veritati conservandae invigilant, se ipsos in fide sanctissima aedificant, errorum principiis, & iisdem invalescentibus se opponunt, agrum Ecclesiae à zizaniis, aream ejusdem à paleis purgare, hoedos ovili Christi exigere, graves lupos à grege abigere pro viribus studunt, atque ita zelum & probitatem suam demonstrant. Sed contingere tamen potest, ut & ipsi vel carnis infirmitate devincti, dormiant, & dormientibus iis inimicus zizania conserat, atque illa cum tritico crescentia serò deprehendantur, & cùm mala per longas invaluere moras, difficilius longè tollantur, imò, praecipiente Christo, non colligenda zizania, sed relinquenda sint, ne colligentes zizania simul cum iis triticum evellant, Matth. XIII. 28. 29. vel malo tollendo, & morbo praevalido sanando impares sint; imò à potentiore in Ecclesia factione premantur, & captivi velut in externo illo Ecclesiae malignantium ergastulo attineantur, & non paternè, sed paedagogicè regantur atque vexentur; cùm non desit mulier illa Jezabel, quae se Prophetissam (infallibilem fidei matrem & magistram Spiritum S. habentem ad docendum indemonstrabilia sine errore) dicit, & docet atque seducit Christi servos ad fornicandum & idolothyta edendum, (ad eandem cum idololatris mensam accedendum, & cum ipsorum factis communicandum) Apoc. II. 20.
units.tr: For those who are upright in the external Church watch over the keeping of the truth, build themselves up in most holy faith, and oppose the principles of error and those who advance them. They strive, as far as they can, to cleanse the field of the Church from tares and its threshing floor from chaff, to drive the goats from the fold of Christ and to drive grievous wolves from the flock, and so they show their zeal and uprightness. Yet it may happen that even they, overcome by the weakness of the flesh, fall asleep, and while they sleep the enemy sows tares, and these, growing up with the wheat, are detected too late; and when evils have grown strong through long delay, they are far harder to remove. Indeed, at Christ's command the tares are not to be gathered but left alone, lest in gathering the tares they pull up the wheat with them, Matt. 13:28, 29. Or they may be unequal to removing the evil and healing a strongly established disease. Indeed they may be oppressed by a more powerful faction within the Church, and held captive, as it were, in that external prison of the malignant in the Church, and governed and harassed not as a father governs but as a schoolmaster. For that woman Jezebel is not lacking, who calls herself a prophetess (the infallible mother and teacher of the faith, having the Holy Spirit to teach indemonstrable things without error), and teaches and seduces the servants of Christ to commit fornication and eat things sacrificed to idols (to approach the same table as idolaters and share in their deeds), Rev. 2:20.

units.la: Quam mulierem, quae sic finit, patitur Ecclesia, contra eam Christus se pauca habere, ibidem testatur. Quo in statu illi etiam ἅγιοι sancti sunt, quos à Bestia vinci ibid. XIII. 7. dicitur, quando per hostium Ecclesiae dominantium violentiam eas ad angustias res Sanctorum rediguntur, ut eorum laetitia & gaudium non parum minuatur, aedificatio & disciplina secundum verbum Dei impediatur, Sancti dissipentur, & in latebras adigantur, & communionis Sanctorum fructu priventur, inquinatis iis, cum quibus commercium esse potest, ut cogantur dicere: Defecit fidelis, Psal. XII. 2. adeóque se abscondere cogantur, pabulum animae purum putum Dei verbum, & solida ejus interpretatio iis subtrahatur; denique iis vita etiam eripiatur, quae tamen mors Sanctorum victoria, quam de Bestia reportant, est.
units.tr: Christ testifies against this woman, whom the Church suffers to act thus, that he has a few things against her, in the same place. In this state, too, there are the saints (ἅγιοι), whom the beast is said to overcome, Rev. 13:7, when, through the violence of the enemies who dominate the Church, the affairs of the saints are reduced to such straits that their joy and gladness are not a little diminished, their building up and discipline according to the Word of God are hindered, the saints are scattered and driven into hiding, and they are deprived of the fruit of the communion of the saints, since those with whom they could have fellowship are polluted, so that they are forced to say: "The faithful have failed," Ps. 12:2. Thus they are compelled to hide themselves, and the pure food of the soul, the Word of God and its solid interpretation, is withdrawn from them. Finally, their very life is taken away, which yet is the victory of the saints over the beast.

units.la: XLVII. Judicium porro de colenda cum errantibus vel inordinatis communione, ex Ecclesiae erroribus & ἀπαξία petendum est.
units.tr: XLVII. Furthermore, the judgment on whether to maintain communion with erring or disorderly churches must be drawn from the errors of the Church and from its disorder [ἀπαξία].

units.la: Errores non unius generis, vel ponderis sunt, alii in fundamento, alii circa fundamentum, alii praeter illud consistentes. In fundamento dicuntur, qui illud directè & manifestè destruunt; sive qui doctrinam de Christo Salvatore, & salutari ejus officio tollunt. Circa fundamentum, qui illud quidem relinquunt, sed ejusmodi tamen dogmata adstruunt, ex quibus per necessariam consequentiam utcunque illud quaü quati & labefactari potest. Præter fundamen-tum, qui in curiosis quæstionibus & inanibus rixis positi sunt, nec ad cognitionem veritatis, quæ secundum pietatem est, faciunt, quíque adeò non trabis, sed festucæ, nec non stipulæ & fœni, 1. Cor. III. 12.13. rationem habent. Ecclesia ἀπακτ seu inordinata est, quæ in fundamento religionis consentiens, vel ritus non satis decoros & convenientes habet, vel morum defectus non ea disciplinæ ecclesiasticæ severitate, qua par erat, corrigit, sed matris indulgentis atque blandæ instar, tolerat. Cum Ecclesia in fundamento sic errante, ut errorem suum definiat, & pertinaciter tueatur, dissentiendi & erroris sanandi libertatem tollat, & verba & sensum genuinum fundamentalis veritatis aboleat, atque omnino insanabilis fit, communio coli nulla potest. Cavete à Pseudoprophetis, qui ad vos veniunt in vestibus ovium, intus autem lupi rapaces sunt, Matth. VII. 15. Mittite eos: Duces cæci cæcorum sunt. Cæcus autem, si cæcum duxerit, ambo in foveam cadunt, ibid. XV. 14. Quæ consensio est Christi & Belialis? Aut quæ portio fidelis cum infideli? 2. Cor. VI. 15. Hæreticum hominem post unam & alteram admonitionem vita, Tit. III. 10. Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam (quæ Jesum Christum in carne venientem negat) non affert, ne recipite eum domi vestræ, & ave ei ne dicite. Nam qui ei ave dicit, cum operibus ejus malis communicat, 2. Joh. v. 10. 11. Communio enim corporis mystici, seu Ecclesiæ, nititur μία πίστις unitate fidei, fundamentalis puta, Ephes. IV. 4. 5. At illic unitas fidei fundamentalis non est, ubi à fundamento fidei sic discedit, ut per communionem τῶν δοκίμων sanandi erroris nulla spes superfit. Sed quæ Ecclesia circa vel præter fundamentum errat, cum ea communio temerè abrumpi non debet; dummodo sic errans nec pertinax fit, & indies proficere, & errores, quorum ex verbo Dei convicta est, exuere parata sit, adeóque zelo carnis affecta hostile adversus dissentientes odium, cum persecutione conjunctum non concipiat & gerat. Nam etiam stipulas atque fœnum fundamento superstruentes, quasi per ignem salvari possunt, 1. Cor. III. 12. 15. & ad quod usque pervenimus, eodem canone ambulare, idem sentire jubemur, Phil. III. 16. Ideo nec S. Paulus ab Ecclesiis Corinthiaca, Galatica, Colossensi, erroribus non paucis laborantibus, sibi discedendum putavit. Neque etiam ab Ecclesia inordinata, quæ ritus non aperte impios & idololatricos, sed vel minus decoros, & simplicitati Ecclesiæ parum convenientes, vel priscæ superstitionis aliquid redolentes, habet. Non enim ratio veræ unitatis, vel Regnum Dei in rituum, sed in fidei consonantia consistit; &, salva fidei compage, rituum diversitas in Ecclesiis ex Judæis & Gentibus, Græcis & Latinis, variorumque Regnorum & provinciarum, semper obtinuit. Par disciplinæ ratio est, quæ sic ad rectum sanumque Ecclesiæ statum requiritur, ut tamen Ecclesiæ non sic essentialis vel necessaria sit, ut neglecta ea, quando neglectus non manat ex regula & dictamine doctrinæ, Ecclesia esse desinat, quod exemplis Ecclesiarum Corinthiacæ & Asiaticarum constat. Fides enim per puram verbi prædicationem & legitimam Sacramentorum administrationem,
units.tr: Errors are not all of one kind or weight. Some concern the foundation, some lie near the foundation, and some lie beside it. Those are said to concern the foundation which directly and plainly overthrow it, that is, which deny the doctrine of Christ as Saviour and of his saving office. Those are said to concern what is near the foundation which leave the foundation itself standing but assert such doctrines that, by necessary consequence, it can in some way be shaken and weakened. Those lie beside the foundation which rest on curious questions and empty quarrels, and do not promote the knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness; they are of the kind that are not beams but splinters, and have the character of "stubble and hay" (1 Cor. 3:12–13). A church is disorderly [ἄτακτος] if, while agreeing on the foundation of religion, it has rites that are not sufficiently seemly and fitting, or if it does not correct moral failings with the strictness of church discipline that is required, but tolerates them like an indulgent and soft mother. When a church errs in the foundation in such a way that it defines its error and stubbornly defends it, removes the freedom of dissent and of correcting error, and abolishes both the words and the genuine sense of the fundamental truth, and so becomes wholly incurable, communion with it cannot be maintained. "Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves" (Matt. 7:15). "Let them alone: they are blind guides of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch" (Matt. 15:14). "What agreement has Christ with Belial? Or what part has the believer with the unbeliever?" (2 Cor. 6:15). "A heretical man, after one or two warnings, reject" (Titus 3:10). "If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine (which denies that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh), do not receive him into your house, and do not say 'Hail' to him. For he who says 'Hail' to him shares in his evil works" (2 John 10–11). For communion of the mystical body, that is, of the Church, rests on the "one faith" [μία πίστις], the unity of the fundamental faith (Eph. 4:4–5). But there is no unity of fundamental faith where a church so departs from the foundation of faith that no hope remains of curing its error through the fellowship of the approved [τῶν δοκίμων]. However, a church that errs beside or near the foundation must not be lightly cut off from communion, provided that it is not obstinate, that it is making progress from day to day, and that it is ready to lay aside the errors of which it has been convicted by the word of God; so long as it does not conceive and carry on a hostile hatred against dissenters, joined with persecution, stirred by fleshly zeal. For even those who build "stubble and hay" on the foundation may be saved, as through fire (1 Cor. 3:12, 15), and we are commanded to walk by the same rule to which we have attained, and to think the same (Phil. 3:16). Therefore neither did St. Paul think that he should separate himself from the churches of Corinth, Galatia and Colossae, which laboured under not a few errors. Nor should one separate from a disorderly church which has rites that are not openly impious and idolatrous, but only less seemly and little suited to the simplicity of the Church, or which smack of some ancient superstition. For the reason of true unity, or the kingdom of God, consists not in the uniformity of rites but in agreement of faith; and, with the bond of faith preserved, a diversity of rites has always prevailed among churches, among Jews and Gentiles, Greeks and Latins, and among different kingdoms and provinces. The same holds for discipline: it is required for the right and sound state of the Church, yet it is not so essential or necessary to the Church that a church ceases to be a church when it is neglected, provided that the neglect does not arise from the rule and dictate of doctrine. The examples of the churches of Corinth and of Asia show this. For faith is begotten and nourished through the pure preaching of the word and the lawful administration of the sacraments,

units.la: tanquam ordinaria ejus media, gignitur & alitur. Ubi autem fides est, ibi etiam Ecclesia est. Sed disciplina tamen non sic negligi, & neglecta jacere debet, ut vitia & scelera etiam excusentur, pallientur, defendantur, nedum ex Ecclesiæ dictamine fluere debent; sed improbanda potius & interdicenda semper sunt, etiam ubi minus severè vindicantur. Alias in perniciem & ruinam Ecclesiæ redundant. Et si aliter communio externa retineri non posset, nisi cum aliis male faciamus, & bona omittamus: aut mala vocemus bona, & bona mala, & veritati ac bonis moribus, hoc est, legi Divinæ anathema dicamus, communio sarta & tecta periri non potest.
units.tr: as its ordinary means. And where there is faith, there also is the Church. Yet discipline must not be so neglected, nor lie so neglected, that vices and crimes are excused, glossed over or defended, much less that they flow from the dictate of the Church. Rather they must always be condemned and forbidden, even where they are punished less severely. Otherwise they bring ruin and destruction upon the Church. And if external communion could not be kept otherwise than by our doing wrong with others and omitting good things, or by calling evil good and good evil, and by pronouncing anathema on truth and good morals, that is, on the divine law, then communion, though preserved outwardly, cannot be kept whole and intact.

units.la: XLVIII. Abrupta Ecclesiæ communio schisma seu separationem efficit. Est autem schisma res per se media, nec bona nec mala; sed bonam vel malam causa separationis facit. Nam causa justa & necessaria pium & laudabile: non justa, & non necessaria impium & detestabile schisma facit. Esse autem quandoque pium & laudabile, Scriptura & tota Ecclesia Christiana testantur. Scriptura, jubens recedere ab iis, qui dissensiones & scandala præter doctrinam, quam pii didicerunt, facinnt, Rom. XVI. 17. non misceri cum quibusdam, non una comedere, 1. Cor. V. 11. anathema facere eum, qui non amat Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, ibid. XVI. 22. non conjugari jugo cum infidelibus, 2. Corinth. VI. 14. eos ὑποτάσσεσθαι aversari, 2. Tim. III. 5. hæreticum hominem ... vitare, Tit. III. 10. venientem ad nos, & doctrinam Christi non afferentem non recipere domi nostræ, neque ei ave dicere, 2. Joh. v. 10. non sinere mulierem Jezabel docere, & errare facere servos Dei, Apoc. II. 20. exire ex Babylone, ibid. XVIII. 4. non tantum exitu animi dissentientis, sed etiam corporis, consortium & communionem vitantis, quia Babyloni permixti prius haud dubiè eam agnitam animo & corpore deserere tenentur. Tota Ecclesia Christiana id ipsum comprobat. Omnes enim Israelitæ, quotquot in Christum crediderunt, & omnes, qui ex gentibus ad Christum conversi sunt, se à Judæis & gentibus separarunt, & abdicata eorum congregatione, in unum corpus coaluerunt. Cujus rei culpa non in Christianis, sed in Gentibus & Judæis fuit. De Judæis enim Esajas dicit: Fratres vestri sunt, qui separant vos, Esaj. LXVI. 5. Et factum illud est partim mandato Dei jubentis recedere, hinc exire, & impurum non contingere, Esaj. LII. 11. partim judicio Divino, quod sic Moses pronuntiavit: Non volet Dominus condonare ipsi. Nam tum fumabit ira Dei, & zelus ejus in virum hunc, & separabit eum ab omnibus tribubus Israel, ibidem LXV. 5.
units.tr: XLVIII. A broken communion of the Church produces a schism, or separation. A schism is in itself an indifferent thing, neither good nor evil; but the cause of the separation makes it good or evil. For a just and necessary cause makes the schism pious and praiseworthy; a cause that is neither just nor necessary makes it impious and detestable. That a schism is sometimes pious and praiseworthy is attested by Scripture and by the whole Christian Church. Scripture bids us withdraw from those who cause dissensions and offences contrary to the doctrine that the godly have learned (Rom. 16:17); not to mix with certain persons, nor to eat with them (1 Cor. 5:11); to make anathema him who does not love our Lord Jesus Christ (ibid. 16:22); not to be yoked with unbelievers (2 Cor. 6:14); to avoid those who are "turned away" [ὑποτάσσεσθαι] (2 Tim. 3:5); to shun a heretical man (Titus 3:10); not to receive into our house, nor to say "Hail" to, one who comes to us and does not bring the doctrine of Christ (2 John 10); not to allow the woman Jezebel to teach and to lead the servants of God astray (Rev. 2:20); to come out of Babylon (ibid. 18:4), not only by the departure of the dissenting mind, but also of the body, avoiding its fellowship and communion, because those who have been mixed with Babylon are no doubt bound to forsake it in both mind and body once they have recognised it. The whole Christian Church approves this same thing. For all the Israelites who believed in Christ, and all who were converted to Christ from the Gentiles, separated themselves from the Jews and the Gentiles, and, renouncing their assembly, grew together into one body. The fault for this lay not with the Christians but with the Gentiles and the Jews. For Isaiah says of the Jews: "Your brethren who hate you, who cast you out" (Isa. 66:5). And this happened partly by the command of God, who bids them depart, go out from there, and touch no unclean thing (Isa. 52:11), and partly by the divine judgment, which Moses pronounced thus: "The Lord will not be willing to forgive him. For then the wrath of God and his zeal shall smoke against that man, and he shall separate him from all the tribes of Israel" (Deut. 29:20; cf. Isa. 65:5).

units.la: XLIX. Cùm igitur separatio quædam justa, quædam injusta esse possit, non separatio ipsa, sed separationis causa ad dijudicandum schisma spectari debet. Et vera quidem Ecclesia existit in communione externa, vel undique pura, saltem fundamenti fidei & salutis tenaci, & errores suos non violenter obtruden-te: vel in Ecclesia non undique pura, sed quorundam saltem, vel plurium etiam in communione ea dominantium respectu, erroribus lethalibus corrupta, & errores suos legibus stabiliente, biliente, atque in idola erigente. Existente Ecclesia priore sensu, separatio ab ea injusta & schisma detestabile est. Non enim sine sontica causa τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν congregationem deserere licet, Hebr. X. 25. Et τὸν ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει in-firmum fide suscipere, & non ab eo nos segregare, Rom. XIV. 1. & ἀσθενήματα τῶν ἀδυνάτων infirmitates imbecillium ferre. & non nobis placere, ibid. XV. 1. alii alios suscipere, sicut & Christus nos suscepit ad gloriam Dei, ibid. v.7. jubemur. Dei igitur & Christi abnegatores esse, qui schisma sine sontica causa suscitant, Calvinus, & gravius esse Ecclesiam scindere, quàm idolis immolare, veteres pié reéteque dixerunt. Criminis hujus rei olim Novatiani, Cathari, Donatistæ fuerunt; hodie sunt Anabaptistæ, ac præ cæteris omnibus schismaticis veteribus & novis Pontificii, qui incendiarii maximi aliis suum crimen impingentes, existente, saltem quoad fundamentum fidei, vera in Oriente & Occidente Ecclesia, Romæ segregem cœtum Papæ & Principum dominantium instituerunt,& in ea Cathedram ac Regnum, spiritualium prætextu, merè terrenum & mundanum erexerunt,atque in illud tyrannidem, errores pestiferos,Christo & justitiæ ejus contrarios induxerunt, totúmque in mundum illud vi & dolo proferre hactenus contenderunt; denique impietati huic, ob solum solius Dei timorem, non consentientes Ecclesias Orientales & Occidentales non paucas ἐπισυναγωγὰς fecerunt, à corpore suo singulari, igne & aqua interdictas,resecuerunt,& schisma ejusmodi introduxerunt,cui par ab omni ævo in mundo nullum fuit. Non enim is schisma facit, qui communionem impiam ob timorem Dei deserere cogitur; sed qui sua impietate, φιλαρχίᾳ dominandi libidine, crudelitate & indomita pervicacia deserere cogit.
units.tr: XLIX. Since, then, some separation may be just and some unjust, it is not the separation itself but the cause of the separation that must be considered in judging whether there is schism. A true Church exists in external communion either entirely pure, at least holding firmly to the foundation of faith and salvation and not forcibly imposing its errors; or in a Church that is not entirely pure, but corrupted in its deadly errors with respect to some or even many who dominate in that communion, and that enforces its errors by laws and raises them up into idols. When the Church exists in the former sense, separation from it is unjust and a detestable schism. For it is not permitted to abandon the assembly [τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν] without a guilty cause (Heb. 10:25); and we are commanded to receive the one who is weak in faith [τὸν ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει], and not to separate ourselves from him (Rom. 14:1), and to bear the infirmities of the weak [ἀσθενήματα τῶν ἀδυνάτων], and not to please ourselves (ibid. 15:1), and "to receive one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God" (ibid. 15:7). Therefore those who stir up a schism without a guilty cause are deniers of God and of Christ, as Calvin says; and the ancients rightly and piously said that it is more grievous to rend the Church than to sacrifice to idols. Of this crime the Novatians, the Cathari and the Donatists were once guilty; today the Anabaptists are, and above all other schismatics, old and new, the Papists. Setting their own crime upon others, these greatest of incendiaries, while the true Church existed in East and West, at least as regards the foundation of faith, established in Rome a separate assembly of the Pope and of the dominant princes, and in it raised a throne and kingdom, under the pretext of spiritual things, that is purely earthly and worldly; and they introduced into it a tyranny and pestilent errors contrary to Christ and to his righteousness, and have hitherto striven to carry that whole thing into the world by force and by fraud. Finally, against those who did not consent to this impiety, and who did so only for the sake of the fear of God, they made many assemblies of Eastern and Western churches, cut them off from their own single body, interdicted them with fire and water, and introduced such a schism as has had no equal in the world at any time. For it is not he who is compelled to abandon an impious communion for fear of God who makes a schism; but he who, by his impiety, by a love of rule [φιλαρχίᾳ], by lust for domination, by cruelty and by unbending obstinacy, compels others to depart.

units.la: L. Sed separatio justa, schisma laudabile est, cùm existente Ecclesia posteriore sensu, pii ex communione ejus, propter insanabilem ejus impietatem,& præsentissimum salutis periculum sponte exeunt, vel corruptorum crudelitate ejecti & proturbati segreges cœtus instituunt; vel ex eadem communione scandala & zizania eradicant, cultum publicum ad amussim verbi Divini componunt, & externam communionem sic purificant, ut omnes שׁרץ ἐυσεβεῖς, pié in mundo vivere volentes, illam colere magno cum pietatis quæstu, seductionis verò periculo nullo pollint. Tantum enim enim abest, ut, qui id faciunt, veri schismatici,Dei Christique abnegatores sint,ut potiùs ejus adversus abnegatores nominis ejus impios, sancti, constantes omníque laude dignissimi confessores sint,& dici haberique debeant; similes illis,qui olim à Gentilibus & Judæis ad Christianos transierunt; vel Ecclesiam hæresibus & scandalis obrutam non semel liberarunt & purgarunt. Tales Ecclesiæ Reformatores, Lutherus,Zwinglius aliique ἰσότιμον πίστιν λαχόντες æquè pretiosam fidem sortiti, fuerunt, qui Romanam communionem, in qua contagiosa illa elephantiasis ad ἀκμὴν suam jam pervenit, & errores lethales, idololatria, tyrannis ambigua palma jam certarunt, atque in leges publicas transierunt,corripientes,& ex verbo Dei convincentes ab Italica factione Ec-
units.tr: L. But a separation is just, and the schism praiseworthy, when, while the Church exists in the latter sense, the godly leave its communion of their own accord because of its incurable impiety and the most immediate danger to their salvation; or when they are driven out and expelled by the cruelty of the corrupt and form separate assemblies; or when they root out scandals and tares from that same communion, arrange public worship strictly according to the rule of the divine Word, and so purify the external communion that all who are godly [ὅσοι εὐσεβεῖς], wishing to live piously in the world, can cultivate it with great gain to their piety and with no danger of seduction. For those who do this are so far from being true schismatics and deniers of God and Christ that they are rather holy, steadfast confessors, worthy of all praise, of his name against the impious deniers of that name, and ought to be called and regarded as such. They are like those who once passed from the Gentiles and Jews to the Christians, or who more than once freed and cleansed a Church overwhelmed by heresies and scandals. Such were the Reformers of the Church, Luther, Zwingli and others, who "having obtained a faith equally precious" [ἰσότιμον πίστιν λαχόντες] were the ones who challenged the Roman communion, in which that contagious elephantiasis has now reached its height [ἀκμὴν], with its deadly errors, idolatry and tyranny, contending for the ambiguous palm, and who passed over into public laws, rebuking and convincing from the Word of God those condemned by the Italian faction, which has been mixed everywhere into the Church of God,

units.la: clesiæ Dei passim admixta damnati,vel impietatem manifestam & insanabilem approbare, vel nullam religionem colere, quod illis amor Dei,vis conscientiæ,& omnis pudor prohibuit, vel sublata impietate & corruptione incurabili, se & Ecclesias suas à Romana Hierarchica communione,quà tali,Deo volente,jubente& favente, debuerunt.
units.tr: or who were to approve manifest and incurable impiety, or to worship no religion at all, which the love of God, the force of conscience and every sense of shame forbade them to do; or who, once impiety and incurable corruption were removed, were bound, by God's will, command and favour, to separate themselves and their Churches from the Roman hierarchical communion as such.

units.la: LI. Non desunt tamen hodie,qui omnem ab Ecclesia etiam corruptissima digressionem impiam esse clamitent. Nam eò impudentiæ & impietatis promotum est, ut palam Hierarchicorum parasitæ & emissarii asserant, nemini mortalium fas esse ab Ecclesia Romana secedere, si vel maximè idololatrica & hæretica tota esset. Sed aliud Christi discipulus ἐγνώλ-πιῶ Johannes docet, jubéique præcipiens. Filioli, cavete ab idolis, 1. Joh. V. 21. & quidnî etiam ab idololatris, 1. Cor. V. 10.? Neque illorum argumenta quicquam roboris habent. Nam quòd in V. T. Mosen & Prophetas idololatricis temporibus non erexisse nova altaria, neque fideles secessisse ab Ecclesia quamvis idololatrica, vel segreges cœtus & novum Ministerium instituisse,clamitant,nihil clamore eo proficiunt. Alia enim temporum illorum ratio fuit,quibus Deus cultum suum ita uni loco addixit,& in eo memoriam nomini suo posuit, ut alibi convenire,vel sacra facere, nefas fuerit. At in N. T. ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ in omni loco sanctas manus elevare licet, 1. Tim. II. 8. & veri adoratores Patrem in spiritu & veritate adorant, Joh. IV. 23. Neque etiam ita idololatria unquam invaluit,ut in legem abierit,vel ad eam exercendam vi adacti fuerint, quibus vero Deo adhærere propositum fuit. Atque id etiam locum habuit respectu Ecclesiæ Judaicæ tempore Christi,quæ utut varios abusus & corruptelas haberet,sola tamen adhuc erat Ecclesia & Templum Dei, in quo rite Deo litari poterat, & fidelibus sine crimine vivere licuit. Sic enim iis à fermento Pharisæorum cavendum fuit ut tamen cultum Mosaicum observare,& Pharisæos docentes, atque in Cathedra Mosis sedentes audire fideles, usque ad tempus mortis Christi,debuerint. Neque separationem, vel correctionem quamvis Ecclesiæ prohibuit ille Paterfamilias,qui vetuit zizania colligere, ne una cum iis triticum evellerent, Matth. XIII. 28. 29. Nam per zizania non intelliguntur omnis generis vel verba scandalosa & falsa loquentes, vel peccata facientes. Nam in his,qui peccata cum scandalo faciunt, & verba inutilia cum scandalo loquuntur, zizania sunt. Quis enim dubitet, factis & verbis malis zizania cognosci? Certè occultos hypocritas,& tamen viventes Christianorum more, & Christianorum verba loquentes servi Patrisfamilias non judicant zizania, sed sperant esse frumenta. Porrò neque vetantur à Patrefamilias spinas,carduos & venenatas herbas de medio tollere, sed zizania, quæ possunt videri triticum, ne, dum zizania tollere conantur, triticum tollant. Hoc ergo sibi parabola vult,non omnes,qui prima fronte videntur ἀκαρπι, hoc est,ignorantia fundamenti laborantes, & Deum non glorificantes, extra Ecclesiam ejiciendos, vel ab iis recedendum esse,ne forte & triticum evellatur,hoc est, ne
units.tr: LI. Yet there are not lacking today those who loudly declare that every impious departure from the Church, even from the most corrupt, is wrong. For impudence and impiety have advanced so far that the parasites and emissaries of the Hierarchy openly assert that no mortal may secede from the Roman Church, even if it were wholly idolatrous and heretical. But the beloved [ἀγαπητὸς] disciple of Christ, John, teaches otherwise, and commands, saying: "Little children, keep yourselves from idols" (1 John 5:21), and why not also from idolaters (1 Cor. 5:10)? Nor do their arguments have any force. For when they cry out that in the Old Testament Moses and the Prophets did not set up new altars in idolatrous times, nor did the faithful secede from a Church, however idolatrous, nor form separate assemblies and a new ministry, they gain nothing by their clamour. For the circumstances of those times were different, when God so confined his worship to one place, and placed his name there in memory, that to assemble or sacrifice elsewhere was unlawful. But in the New Testament "in every place" it is lawful "to lift up holy hands" (1 Tim. 2:8), and "true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and in truth" (John 4:23). Nor has idolatry ever so prevailed that it became law, or that those who wished to cleave to the true God were forced by violence to practise it. This also held good with respect to the Jewish Church in the time of Christ, which, however much it had various abuses and corruptions, was still the only Church and the Temple of God, in which God could rightly be worshipped, and in which the faithful could live without sin. For thus they were to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and yet they were bound to observe the Mosaic worship and, until the time of Christ's death, to hear the Pharisees teaching and sitting in the chair of Moses. Nor did that householder, who forbade the tares to be gathered "lest in gathering the tares you root up the wheat also" (Matt. 13:28-29), forbid separation from or correction of a Church. For by the tares are not meant all who speak scandalous and false words, or who commit sins. For those who sin scandalously and speak useless words scandalously are indeed tares. For who would doubt that tares are known by evil deeds and words? Certainly the servants of the householder do not judge the secret hypocrites, who nevertheless live in the manner of Christians and speak the words of Christians, to be tares, but hope that they are wheat. Moreover, the householder does not forbid the removal of thorns, thistles and poisonous herbs from the field, but only the tares, which may appear to be wheat, lest in trying to pull up the tares they pull up the wheat also. Therefore the parable means this: not all who at first sight seem unfruitful, that is, who labour under ignorance of the foundation and do not glorify God, are to be cast out of the Church, or are to be shunned, "lest perhaps" the wheat be uprooted, that is, lest

units.la: {a} Aliquando justa & necessaria est. ne propter errores quosdam, quos hypocritæ pro veritatibus fundamentalibus habent, etiam illi priventur communione fidelium, qui eosdem errores fidei fundamenti & principii admiscuerunt, & propterea Deum non glorificarunt, sicut oportet. Diversi enim eadem vel à Deo, vel ab hominibus dicta loqui possunt, non una mente. Qui enim à Deo dicta habent pro solido principio, & ex illis intelligunt, quod in fide primum est, parati sunt credere omnia, quæ Deus ipsis revelat, & cum principio fidei congruunt, dummodo ipsis demonstrentur. Hi verum aliquid ignorantes, & à Deo non dictum pro vero amplectentes, non pro zizaniis, sed pro tritico habendi sunt, propter fidem principii, obedientiam Dei, amorem veritatis & Christi, atque famem justitiæ ejus. Contra, qui dicta Dei loquuntur, & aliud fidei principium habent, & dicta hominum sibi fidei principium statuunt, zizania sunt. Licet tamen zizania, seu errores tales tolerari à fidelibus debeant, ut ii, qui eos fovent, non ilico ex Ecclesia expellantur, vel fideles ab iis recedant: tamen non ita tolerandi sunt, ut eis permittatur etiam docere, quod Angelo Ecclesiæ Thyatirensis, Jezabelem docere permittenti exprobratur. Quin potius & reprehendi, & per doctrinam veritatis corrigi debent, donec malum ἀνίατον & impietas ad ἀχμλω, & manifestam defensionem & executionem violentam legis Antichristi perveniat. Tum enim quid peccant pii, si inter se privatim congrediantur in nomine Christi, & inter se colloquantur? Tum collocuti sunt timentes Dominum quisque cum proximo suo, & attendit Dominus, & audivit, & scriptus est liber commentarius coram ipso pro timentibus Dominum, & æstimantibus nomen Domini,Malach. III.16. Ubi duo vel tres coacti fuerint in nomen meum, ibi sum in medio ipsorum, Matth. XVIII.20. Non enim hoc illos extra Ecclesiam collocat, quòd non in eodem secum loco omnes vel plures oves Christi vident, illas inprimis, quæ salva charitate & obedientia erga Christum, & fide fundamenti, aliquid inutile docent vel discunt, sed adhuc cum errantibus sunt, nescientes profunditates Sathanæ, Apoc. II.24. Num quid hoc illos ab eis separat, quòd cum iis, cum quibus esse desiderant, & pro quibus etiam sanguinem fundere parati sunt, esse non possunt? Annon potius eos cum illis conjungit, quòd Christus idem omnium Dominus, in medio ipsorum est? Si enim Christus non est, nisi ubi etiam zizania congregantur, quomodo de N. T. temporibus dici potest: In die illo, dicit Dominus, Deus exercituum, vocabitis quisque alterum sub vitem & sub ficum, Zach. III.10. Non enim id proprium temporis Regni Christi est, ut homines vel epulantes, vel fabulantes quidvis, sub vite & ficu confideant, sed quod non habent opus convenire ad certum Templum & montem, sed sedentibus coram Domino sub vite & ficu, ut in nomine ejus colloquantur; Dominus præsto est, & cum illis mansionem facit. Neque denique illud obstat, quod parabola dicit; in messe, hoc est, ἐν Συντελεία τῆς αἰῶνος in consummatione seculi demum per Angelos zizania à tritico separatum iri, Matth. XIII.30.39.40.41. Nam Συντέλεια τῆς αἰῶνος non necessariò
units.tr: {a} Sometimes it is just and necessary, lest, on account of certain errors, which hypocrites hold to be fundamental truths, those also be deprived of the fellowship of the faithful who have mixed the same errors with the foundation and principle of faith, and for that reason have not glorified God as they ought. For different people may speak the same words, whether they are said by God or by men, but not with the same mind. For those who hold what is said by God as a solid principle, and from it understand what is first in faith, are ready to believe all that God reveals to them, and agree with the principle of faith, provided it is shown to them. Such people, though ignorant of some truth and embracing as true what God has not said, are to be regarded not as tares but as wheat, on account of their faith in the principle, their obedience to God, their love of truth and of Christ, and their hunger for his righteousness. On the other hand, those who speak the words of God, but have another principle of faith, and set the words of men up as their principle of faith, are tares. Yet although such tares, or errors of this kind, ought to be tolerated by the faithful, so that those who foster them are not at once expelled from the Church, nor the faithful withdraw from them, they are not to be tolerated to the extent of being permitted even to teach, which is rebuked in the angel of the Church of Thyatira for allowing Jezebel to teach. Rather they ought both to be reproved and to be corrected by the teaching of truth, until the evil becomes incurable [ἀνίατον] and the impiety reaches its height [ἀκμή], and open defence and violent enforcement of the law of Antichrist. For then what sin do the godly commit if they meet together privately in the name of Christ and talk with one another? "Then they that feared the Lord spoke often one to another; and the Lord hearkened, and heard it; and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord, and that thought upon his name" (Mal. 3:16). "Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them" (Matt. 18:20). For it does not place them outside the Church that they do not see all or many of Christ's sheep in the same place with them, especially those who, saving love and obedience towards Christ and faith in the foundation, teach or learn something useless, but are still among the erring, "not knowing the depths of Satan" (Rev. 2:24). Does it then separate them from those with whom they desire to be, and for whom they are ready to shed their blood, that they cannot be with them? Does it not rather join them to them, in that Christ, the one Lord of all, is in the midst of them? For if Christ is only where tares are also gathered, how can it be said of New Testament times: "In that day, says the Lord of hosts, you shall call every one to his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree" (Zech. 3:10)? For it is not a peculiar feature of the time of Christ's Kingdom that men, whether feasting or chatting about anything, trust under the vine and fig tree, but that they need not assemble at a certain Temple and mountain, but, sitting before the Lord under the vine and fig tree, may talk in his name; the Lord is present and makes his abode with them. Finally, that which the parable says does not stand in the way: that at the harvest, that is, "in the consummation of the age" [ἐν συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος], the tares will be separated from the wheat by the angels (Matt. 13:30, 39-41). For "the consummation of the age" [συντέλεια τοῦ αἰῶνος] does not necessarily

units.la: ultimum judicium significat. Potest enim etiam ultimos dies seculi notare. Quomodo etiam Johannes ultimam horam, hoc est, ultimam partem seculi, quod usque ad manifestationem Christi fluit, esse, 1. Joh. II.18. & Paulus πλὴν τῶν αἰώνων fines seculorum dies prædicationis Evangelii, 1. Cor. X.11. dicunt. Sed esto etiam, ante ultimum diem non colligantur omnia scandala ex Regno Christi, non tamen nulla ex eo, seu Ecclesia, quæ solum Christum Regem agnoscit, eliminabuntur. Quomodo alias Judæi infideles à fidelibus; tot hæreticorum syrmata ab Ecclesia separata sunt? Quomodo juxta adversarios, tota Ecclesia Græca, & nos facti sumus schismatici, si nulla secessio ante finem mundi locum habere potuit? Non ergo hoc sibi Christus vult, quòd ante ultimum judicium nulla secessio & divisio futura sit; quia certè facta est; at Christi prædictio fallere non potuit; sed piis ministrantibus Angelis, quando impietas ad maturitatem pervenit, operam navaturi sint, ut zizania colligantur, & labor ille non ante finem mundi consummetur. Denique nec separationem quamvis illegitimam esse, prædictiones, quibus prænuntiatum est, fore, ut Ecclesia per totum terrarum orbem diffundatur, Christo gentes in hæreditatem, & fines terræ in possessionem dentur, Psal. II.8. & ut plures sunt filiæ sterilis & derelictæ, quàm ejus, quæ habet maritum, Esaj. LIV.1. &c. evincunt. Quas prædictiones illi negant impleri, cùm pauci à pluribus separantur, quia sic eveniret, ut Ecclesia non esset diffusa per totum terrarum orbem, & ut cedat Israelitarum numero. Quo argumento Augustinus Donatistas obruit, sed non separationem quamvis configere voluit. Putarunt enim Donatistæ, se solos in Africæ angulo relictos esse immunes à culpa traditionis, atque adeò solos Ecclesiam esse. Sed argumentum isthoc neminem pium commovet, ut se multitudini malum & facienti, & imperanti subjiciat, quod Bestiam adorare est. Nam & Abrahamo promissum est, fore ut Semen ipsius sit instar pulveris terræ & stellarum cæli, Genes. XIII.16. XV.5. Et tamen non metuit Elias dicere: Ego solus relictus sum, 1. Reg. XIX.10. Non enim prius aliquis se in Regno vel loco aliquo solum videns non consentientem erroribus vulgi, & super eo ingemiscens, & se excludi, vel cum reliquis sine approbatione erroris, aut patratione peccati eorum communicare non posse videns, propterea promissionem Dei de multiplicando semine Christi intercidisse, vel se solum filium Dei esse, credere cogitur. Nam promissioni Dei innixus securus esse potest, vel in aliis partibus terrarum esse, qui veritatem noverint & diligant; vel sperare, singulos eorum, à quibus secluditur, nescire, quid faciant, & fratres suos esse, dummodo fundamentum & principium retineant. Potest enim etiam, qui Deum amat, fundamento stipulos superstruere, & salvari quasi per ignem. Sed pius, qui sic solus esse cogitur, & sic animatus est, à fratribus corpore & sententia, sed non amore separatur; per quem & videre illos cupit, & illis correptionem preces & passiones suas impendit, nullus dubitans, quin Deus promissiones suas impleturus sit, licet forte non intelligat, quid Deus de hoc vel illo tempore promiserit. Non enim omnium temporum similis facies est. Neque proin rite concluditur: Multi credent Christo: Ergo haec multitudo, quae nunc est, nullum habet vulgarem errorem, qui vel ab omnibus teneatur, vel a multis dissimuletur: vel: Hic solus est; Ergo non habet communionem cum illis, qui Deum amant. Quae illa exsibilatio est, de qua pii conqueruntur: Quomodo dicitis animae meae: Fugite in monte vestro, velut avicula. Atqui, inquit, Ego ad Dominum confugio, Psal. XI. 1. 2. Fac enim, multos esse, qui dicant, quod mature in Ecclesia Christiana multi dixerunt, & serius etiam multi dicere potuerunt: Ego sum Pauli: Ego sum Cephae; & unus sit, qui dicat: Ego sum Christi, 1. Cor. III. 4. an propter multitudinem, quae dicit: Ego sum illius, ille non est Christi, qui non dicit: Ego sum illius hominis; vel non habet communionem cum pueris in Christo, qui dicunt; Ego sum illius, & nesciunt, quid faciant; si non possit cum illis esse in uno loco, nisi cum illis dicat; Ego sum illius? Denique nec simul semelque, sed sero, & demum sub septima tuba audiuntur voces illae gratulabundae: Facta sunt Regna mundi Domini nostri & Christi ejus, & regnabit in secula seculorum. Gratias agimus Domine, Deus omnipotens, qui es, qui eras, & qui venturus eras, quod acceperis potentiam tuam magnam, & regnaveris, Apoc. XI. 15. 17. Prius enim Bestia & Pseudo-propheta in stagnum ignis conjici debet, ibid. XIX. 20.
units.tr: It does not necessarily mean the last judgment; it can also denote the final days of the age. Thus John says that the last hour, that is, the last part of the age, which runs on until the manifestation of Christ, is here (1 John 2:18), and Paul says that the days of the preaching of the Gospel are the ends of the ages [τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώνων] (1 Cor. 10:11). But even if we grant that before the last day not all offences will be gathered out of the kingdom of Christ, it does not follow that none will be removed from it, that is, from the Church, which acknowledges Christ alone as King. Otherwise, how did the unbelieving Jews get separated from the faithful, and how were so many trains of heretics cut off from the Church? If no secession could take place before the end of the world, how, according to our opponents, did the whole Greek Church and we ourselves become schismatics? Therefore Christ does not mean that there will be no secession and division before the final judgment, since it has certainly already happened, and Christ's prediction could not deceive. Rather, when wickedness has reached its height, the pious, with the help of the angels, will set about gathering the tares, and that labour will not be finished before the end of the world. Finally, the prophecies which foretell that the Church will spread through the whole world, that the nations will be given to Christ as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth as a possession (Ps. 2:8), and that the children of the desolate are more than of her who has a husband (Isa. 54:1), etc., prove that even a separation, though illegitimate, is not excluded. Our opponents deny that these prophecies are fulfilled when few are separated from many, because on that view the Church would not be spread through the whole world, and would not equal the number of the Israelites. Augustine used this argument to overthrow the Donatists, but he did not wish to deny separation altogether. For the Donatists thought that they alone, left in a corner of Africa, were free from the guilt of handing over the Scriptures, and so that they alone were the Church. But no pious person is moved by this argument to submit himself to the multitude which does evil and commands evil, since that is to worship the beast. For Abraham was also promised that his seed would be like the dust of the earth and the stars of heaven (Gen. 13:16; 15:5), and yet Elijah was not afraid to say, I alone am left (1 Kings 19:10). For no one is forced to believe, when he sees himself alone in a kingdom or some place, not agreeing with the errors of the crowd and groaning over it, and seeing that he is shut out, or that he cannot share with the rest without approving their error or committing their sin, that God's promise to multiply the seed of Christ has failed, or that he alone is the son of God. Relying on God's promise he may be secure, believing that there are others in other parts of the earth who know and love the truth; or he may hope that those from whom he is excluded do not know what they are doing, and that they are his brothers, provided that they keep the foundation and principle. For one who loves God can also build stubble upon the foundation and be saved as through fire. But the pious man who is forced to be alone in this way, and is separated from his brothers in body and opinion, though not in love, is still one through whom they wish to be seen, and for whom he pours out correction, prayers and sufferings, with no doubt that God will fulfil his promises, even if he perhaps does not understand what God has promised at this or that time. For the face of all times is not alike. Nor is it rightly concluded: Many believe in Christ; therefore this multitude which now exists has no common error, which either is held by all or is tolerated by many; or: This man is alone; therefore he has no communion with those who love God. What is that hissing of which the pious complain? How do you say to my soul, "Flee to your mountain like a little bird"? But, he says, I take refuge in the Lord (Ps. 11:1-2). For suppose there are many who say what many said early in the Christian Church, and many could later say as well, I am of Paul; I am of Cephas, and there is one who says, I am of Christ (1 Cor. 3:4). Is he not of Christ, because of the multitude which says I am of that man, and does he not have communion with those children in Christ who say I am of him and do not know what they are doing? If he cannot be in one place with them unless he says with them I am of him? Finally, those joyful voices are heard not all at once but late, and only under the seventh trumpet: The kingdoms of the world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign for ever and ever. We give thanks to you, Lord God Almighty, who are and who were, and who are to come, because you have taken your great power and begun to reign (Rev. 11:15, 17). For first the Beast and the False Prophet must be cast into the lake of fire (Rev. 19:20).

units.la: LII. Ecclesia externa & visibilis quatenus deficere, vel non deficere possit, paucis nunc declaramus. Ante omnia dispar Ecclesiae Catholicae, quae universitas credentium, toto orbe dispersorum, nullique loco terrestri alligatorum est: & Ecclesiae visibilis atque externae, in qua sunt pastores & oves, ratio est. Illam nunquam deficere, sed perennare in mundo militantem, & consummari in Coelo triumphantem, supra astruximus. Haec vel in particulari coetu quovis, vel in omnibus Ecclesiis particularibus toto orbe dispersis consideratur. Et defectionis modus duplex est, vel a veritate & vita, vel a flore & vigore. Ille cum Ecclesia sic deficit, ut esse desinat, & penitus intercidat; hic, dum ita obscuratur, imminuitur & corrumpitur, ut exstiens & vivens licet, nulla tamen poene appareat. Praeterea defectio vel tritici, piorum & credentium; vel palae, seu factionis hypocritarum, coetui fidelium permixtorum est. Quibus sic distinctis, asserimus, quamvis Ecclesiam particularem visibilem, nulla excepta, posse deficere & interire totaliter, ut nec pastores, nec oves supersint. Quoad omnes vero Ecclesias particulares, toto orbe dispersas, licet non ita simul illae excidere & penitus interire possint, ut verbum Dei, ceu sceptrum roboris Regis Christi, Psal. CX. 2. nusquam in mundo existat & praedicetur, sic tamen corrumpi, obscurari & imminui illae possunt, vix ut ullae residuae, purae inprimis & ab errore omni defaecatae, in mundo appareant, sed defecisse universae videantur. Quoad particulares singulas res ἀντιξαγωνιζόμενος est; quia omnes Ecclesiae particulares in V. & N. T. obscurari & deficere potuerunt, uti & Ecclesiae veteris notabilia intervalla, ab Adamo ad Noë quo defectio Cainitarum & filiorum Dei; à Noe ad Mosen, quo apostasia Chami, filiorum Japheti, & Semi ipsius, in cujus posteritate fuit successio sancti Seminis, & instauratio Ecclesiae idololatricae per Abrahamum facta, Josh. XXIV. 1. 2. & post etiam Ismael & Esavus declinarunt, reliqui vero a Jacobo oriundi superstitionem gentilium in Aegypto admiserunt, Ezech. XX. 7. à Mose ad Christum, quo sub Mose ipso, Judicibus, Regibus, captivitate Babylonica, & post eam, inprimis sub Antiocho Epiphane & successoribus tot defectionum & corruptelarum exempla occurrunt, vix ut numerari possint: Et nova etiam, tum ante publicum Christi ministerium, quando Ecclesia in paucis & obscuris hominibus substitit; tum in ipso durante ipsius ministerio, quando Christus exiguum & contemptum gregem virorum & mulierum secum duxit; tum post ascensionem ejus in Coelum, ubi cujusmodi Ecclesia ab Apostolis ex gentibus collecta fuerit, ipsa Apostolorum acta & epistolae testantur; tum denique ab excessu Apostolorum ad consummationem usque seculi, intra quod tempus, non obortae duntaxat haereses innumerae, sed magna etiam apostasia & Antichristi Regnum grassatae sunt; fidem amplissimam faciunt. Nulla enim perpetuitatis constantiae in fide cujusquam Ecclesiae particularis in mundo causa vel in Deo, vel in Ecclesia, vel in hostibus extra Ecclesiam, reddi potest. Non in Deo, quia nusquam is perennitatem ullius Ecclesiae particularis, vel Spiritus S. ὑπεμονίαν ulli hominum ordini Deus alligavit. Non in Ecclesia, quia errores exitiales in doctrina, & scandala in moribus, quae causae internae, proximae, corrumpentes & destruentes Ecclesiam sunt, in quamlibet Ecclesiam particularem ab admixtis hypocritis & occultis Christi hostibus induci, & in eadem praevalere posse supra ostendimus. Non in iis, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, quia Sathanas, ἀντικείμενος hostis, nunquam eam oppugnare desinit. Ac licet ille nunquam Ecclesiae electorum, vocatorum praevaleat, eam tamen, quae vocatorum, at non electorum est, tandem vincit & opprimit. Cui etiam suppetias fert mundus, qui vel vi Ecclesiam persequitur, vel ex insidiis eam adoritur, & per illecebras capit & evertit. Ideo Scriptura gloriationem de inconcussa & perpetua duratione atque vigore Ecclesiae particularis Meretrici Babylonicae eximiam facit, pleno gutture jactanti: Sedeo Regina, & vidua non ero, & luctum non videbo, Apoc. XVIII. 7.
units.tr: LII. We now briefly explain how far the external and visible Church can fail, or not fail. First of all, the Catholic Church, which is the whole body of believers scattered throughout the world and bound to no earthly place, is different from the visible and external Church, in which there are ministers and sheep. We have already shown that the former never fails, but endures in the militant world and is brought to completion in the triumphant heaven. The latter is considered either in any particular assembly or in all the particular Churches scattered throughout the world. The manner of failing is twofold: either from truth and life, or from bloom and vigour. The first is when the Church so fails that it ceases to be and is utterly destroyed; the second is when it is so obscured, diminished and corrupted that, though it still exists and lives, it scarcely appears at all. Moreover, the failing is either of the wheat, that is, of the pious and believers, or of the chaff, that is, of the faction of hypocrites mixed with the company of the faithful. Having distinguished these, we assert that any visible particular Church, none excepted, can fail and perish altogether, so that neither ministers nor sheep remain. As for all the particular Churches scattered throughout the world, although they cannot all fall and perish utterly at the same time, so that the word of God, which is the sceptre of the strength of King Christ (Ps. 110:2), should nowhere exist and be preached in the world, nevertheless they can be so corrupted, obscured and diminished that scarcely any remnant, pure above all and cleansed from all error, appears in the world, but all seem to have failed. As for each particular matter, the claim is contrary to the argument [ἀντιξαγωνιζόμενος], because all particular Churches in the Old and New Testament could be obscured and fail, as could the notable intervals of the ancient Church: from Adam to Noah, when the Cainites and the sons of God fell away; from Noah to Moses, when the apostasy of Ham, of the sons of Japheth and of Shem himself took place, in whose posterity there was a succession of the holy seed and a restoration of the Church, made through Abraham, from idolatry (Josh. 24:1-2); and afterwards Ishmael and Esau also declined, and the rest, descended from Jacob, admitted the superstition of the Gentiles in Egypt (Ezek. 20:7). From Moses to Christ, under Moses himself, under the Judges and Kings, during the Babylonian captivity and after it, and above all under Antiochus Epiphanes and his successors, examples of so many defections and corruptions occur that they can scarcely be counted. There were also new ones: before Christ's public ministry, when the Church subsisted in a few obscure people; during his ministry itself, when Christ led with him a small and despised flock of men and women; after his ascension into heaven, when the kind of Church gathered from the Gentiles by the Apostles is attested by the Acts and Epistles of the Apostles themselves; and finally from the death of the Apostles to the end of the age, during which time not only countless heresies arose but also a great apostasy and the kingdom of Antichrist raged. These facts give ample proof. For no cause of constancy and perpetuity in the faith of any particular Church in the world can be assigned either in God, or in the Church, or in enemies outside the Church. Not in God, because God has nowhere bound the perpetuity of any particular Church, or the perseverance [ὑπεμονίαν] of the Holy Spirit, to any order of men. Not in the Church, because we have shown above that deadly errors in doctrine and offences in morals, which are the internal, proximate causes that corrupt and destroy the Church, can be introduced into any particular Church by mingled hypocrites and hidden enemies of Christ, and can prevail in it. Not in those outside the Church, because Satan, the adversary [ἀντικείμενος], never ceases to assail it. And although he never prevails against the Church of the elect and called, he finally conquers and oppresses that which is of the called but not of the elect. To him the world also gives help, which either persecutes the Church with force or attacks it by stealth, and takes and overturns it by allurements. Therefore Scripture makes a remarkable boast of the unshaken and perpetual duration and vigour of a particular Church, in the words of the Babylonian Harlot, who boasts with full throat: I sit a queen, and I shall be no widow, and I shall not see mourning (Rev. 18:7).

units.la: LIII. Est sane Regnum Christi aeternum, Luc. I. 33, & Ecclesia Regnum Christi est, sed catholica illa absolute, vel secundum quid specialiter in coetu visibili & particulari, in quo sunt vocati, electi & credentes, non in coetu vocatorum duntaxat, at non electorum. Ab Ecclesia enim particulari vocatorum tolli Regnum Dei, & genti, quae fructus ejus ferat, dari potest, Matth. XXI. 43. Id vero ubi contingit, Regnum Dei esse desinit, nec aeternum dici potest. Neque tamen, qui in tali coetu particulari deficiente credentes & sancti sunt, ipsi quoque deficiunt, vel ante totalem ejus interitum vel evocantur ad Dominum, Esaj. LVII. 1. vel alio transferuntur & migrant, ut Lothi familia Tzoarem,& Ecclesia Hierosolymitana Pellam. Reliqui, quotquot in Ecclesiis corruptis & obscuratis permanent, Divinitus ab earum corruptelis, saltem quoad fundamenta salutaris doctrinæ, præservantur; & vel latent, fugientes tyrannidem & impietatem atque superstitionem publicè grassantem abominantes,exemplo Eliæ,1. Reg. XVIII.4. 13. vel,Divina vocatione exciti,intrepidè se persecutoribus objiciunt; & quidem, ut vel martyrio veritatem obsignent,vel secessu cogant novos cœtus,Ecclesiam instaurent, & puritatem doctrinæ redintegrent. Ita deficientibus cœtibus particularibus electi vocati non deficiunt; nec Christus Ecclesiam suam deserit,vel ei omnino finem imponit. Præterea nec deficientibus vel obscuratis Ecclesiis particularibus simul Ecclesiæ ministerium deficit. Est enim medium ordinarium colligendi Ecclesiam in terris,duraturum usque ad consummationem seculi, Ephes. IV. 11. &c. sed non eo sensu, quasi continua successionis serie in una aliqua sede,nec non eodem semper splendore tam incorruptæ doctrinæ, quàm inviolati ordinis, atque etiam spectatæ dignitatis perpetuandum sit. Nam varia ejus in mundo conditio & vicissitudo est, uti ex Actor. XX.29. 2.Thessal.II.3.4. 7.8. 1.Tim.IV.1.2.3. & 2.Tim.III.1.&c. colligere est. At nec conclamata erit salus hominum,si non semper visibilis & illustris aliqua in mundo Ecclesia extet, ad quam se recipere salutis suæ appetentes valeant. Licèt enim particulares Ecclesiæ deficiant,non tamen Catholica deficit. Ac licèt etiam Ecclesia Catholica in Ecclesiis particularibus sic obscurari possit, ut vix appareat; tamen conspicua illa est membris suis, pluribus aut paucioribus, 1. Reg. XVIII.13. Luc.II.38. & conspicua etiam exteris, non quidem omnibus,quia Deus non omnes etiam sub N. T. ad cognitionem veritatis perducere decrevit, sed iis tamen, quos visum est Deo Ecclesiæ adjungere, ut salvi fiant, Actor. II.47. quacunque occasione, providente Deo,redditur. Ingressus verò in Ecclesiam per fidem verbi Dei etiam tum fieri potest, cùm Ecclesia nulla apparet, per professionem verò fieri potest,etiam cùm minùs illustris est,& mundi oculos fugit,Deo aperiente oculos illorum , quos salvos esse vult jubétque. Denique nec subtilis illa ratiocinatio , quòd Ecclesiæ corruptæ & obscuratæ membra, si palàm fidem profitentur, & ab idololatria abstinent, Ecclesiam visibilem & conspicuam reddant; sin fidem non profitentur, & idololatriam ipsi quoque exercent, ne vera quidem Ecclesia censeri possint, pondus ullum habet. Datur enim tertium,in eo consistens,quòd occultæ Ecclesiæ membra occultè quoque Deo fidem servare, & ab idololatria abstinere possunt,uti centum illi Prophetæ in speluncis latitantes 1.Reg.XVIII.13. XIX.18. fecerunt. Dispar autem fidei & confessionis adultorum necessitas est, quia fides semper requiritur, at confessio non semper, sed tum demum, cùm vel à nobis petitur, 1.Petr.III.15. vel gloria Dei asserenda,Actor.XVII.16. vel salus proximi per eam promovenda est, Matth. V.16. Alias illud Salvatoris: Ne date sanctum canibus, ibid,VII.6, valet. Accedit, quòd nec simpliciter unquam Ecclesia invisibilis est,sed,uti supra etiam dicere occupavimus,modo duntaxat quodam,quatenus non semper hostibus patet, neque uni loco affixa,in eadem sede perpetuo cum puritatis doctrinæ & status externi splendore continuatur.
units.tr: LIII. It is certainly true that the Kingdom of Christ is eternal, Luke 1:33, and the Church is the Kingdom of Christ. But this holds of the catholic Church absolutely, or of the visible and particular assembly in a special sense, in which there are called, chosen and believing people, and not merely of the assembly of the called who are not chosen. For the Kingdom of God can be taken away from the particular Church of the called and given to a nation that bears its fruits, Matt. 21:43. When that happens, the Kingdom of God ceases to exist there and cannot be called eternal. Yet those who are believers and saints in such a particular assembly do not themselves perish when it fails, either before its complete destruction, or when they are called to the Lord, Isa. 57:1, or when they are carried off and migrate elsewhere, as Lot's family went to Zoar and the Jerusalem Church went to Pella. The rest, however many remain in Churches that are corrupted and obscured, are preserved by God from their corruptions, at least as regards the foundations of saving doctrine. Either they lie hidden, fleeing the tyranny, impiety and superstition that openly rage there and abhorring them, following the example of Elijah, 1 Kings 18:4, 13; or, roused by a divine calling, they fearlessly expose themselves to the persecutors, either to seal the truth with martyrdom or to withdraw and form new assemblies, restoring the Church and renewing the purity of doctrine. Thus when particular assemblies fail, the called and chosen do not fail, and Christ does not desert his Church or bring it to an end altogether. Moreover, even when particular Churches fail or are obscured, the ministry of the Church does not fail at the same time. For it is the ordinary means of gathering the Church on earth, to last until the end of the age, Eph. 4:11 etc. But this does not mean that it must be perpetuated in an unbroken line of succession in one particular see, or always with the same splendour of incorrupt doctrine, inviolate order and respected dignity. For its condition and changes in the world are varied, as can be gathered from Acts 20:29; 2 Thess. 2:3, 4, 7, 8; 1 Tim. 4:1, 2, 3; 2 Tim. 3:1 etc. Nor would the salvation of men be hopeless if some visible and illustrious Church did not always stand in the world, to which those seeking their salvation can betake themselves. For although particular Churches fail, the Catholic Church does not fail. And although the Catholic Church may be so obscured within particular Churches that it hardly appears, it is nonetheless conspicuous to its own members, more or fewer, 1 Kings 18:13; Luke 2:38, and also conspicuous to outsiders, though not to all, since God has not decreed to lead all people, even under the New Testament, to knowledge of the truth, but only to those whom it has pleased God to join to the Church so that they may be saved, Acts 2:47, by whatever occasion God provides. Entry into the Church through faith in the word of God can happen even when no Church appears; entry by profession can happen even when the Church is less conspicuous and escapes the eyes of the world, God opening the eyes of those whom he wills to be saved and commands it. Finally, that subtle argument carries no weight: that the members of a corrupted and obscured Church, if they openly profess the faith and abstain from idolatry, make the Church visible and conspicuous; but if they do not profess the faith and practise idolatry themselves, they cannot even be considered a true Church. For there is a third possibility: the members of a hidden Church can keep the faith and abstain from idolatry secretly before God, as those hundred prophets hiding in caves did, 1 Kings 18:13; 19:18. The necessity of faith and of confession in adults is different, because faith is always required but confession is not always required; it is required only when it is asked of us, 1 Pet. 3:15, or when the glory of God must be asserted, Acts 17:16, or when the salvation of a neighbour is to be advanced by it, Matt. 5:16. Otherwise that saying of the Saviour applies: Do not give what is holy to dogs, ibid. 7:6. Add that the Church is never simply invisible; as we have already said above, it is invisible only in a certain respect, in so far as it is not always open to enemies, nor fixed to one place, but continues in the same see for ever, with the splendour of pure doctrine and of its external state.

units.la: LIV. Cùm Ecclesiam externam erroribus ratione fidelium, qui in ea degunt, non exitialibus, at ratione hypocritarum exitialibus infici, & scandalis etiam non parùm turbari,imò & deficere posse,ex iis,quæ hactenus diximus, constet, subinde etiam eandem aberroribus gravioribus,& γάγγραιναν gangrænam facientibus , nec non à scandalis purgari , atque ita reformari debere,consequitur. Sed duplex Ecclesiæ Reformatio est, ordinaria & extraordinaria. Ordinaria continua esse debet,quia nunquam non ignorantiæ erroribus & scandalis, quibus Ecclesia à carne, mundo & Sathana infestatur, resistendum,& in veritate atque pietate proficiendum semper est. Quod superest, fratres,lætamini, καταρτίζεσθε reconcinnamini,consolamini vos mutuo.2.Cor.XIII.11. Ubi καταρτίζεσθε est studere reconcinnationi, ferre reconcinnantes, corrigentes, docentes, corripientes, castigantes. Nam correptio & reconcinnatio hæc fratrum in nomine Domini est visitatio Dei ipsius, hoc agentis, ut nos purget ab omni malo. Habet enim etiam fides in hac vita τὰ ὑστερήματα defectus suos,quales in Thessalonicensibus καταρτίζειν farcire & concinnare Apostolus 1.Thess.III.10. gestivit. Nam fides in eo,qui convertitur, primò est ut in puero carnali, & paulatim proficit, ut fit tanquam ἐν πλείῳ in perfecto, ut verbum auditum in eo sapientia fiat, 1.Cor.III.1. H.6. Licèt enim qui fidei legem in Christum audit,& eam recipit,omnia noverit, 1.Joh.II.20. quia novit, Deum sanctum & misericordem esse, & quicquid disci potest,continetur in eo,quod novit ut in fundamento; non tamen statim cuncta ad πλεῖγμὸν firmitudinem & confirmationem pertinentia cognoscuntur; neque statim vel omnia mysteria,quæ Deus revelavit omnes fidei consequentiæ & artes Sathanæ, quibus Ecclesiam oppugnat,patent; vel omnes errores & opiniones,quæ sunt velut paleæ & stipulæ, quas sæpe homines non satis vigilantes fundamento adjungunt,simul semélque exuuntur: deniqUe non statim patet,nec semper in promptu est,quid fides omni in loco & tempore suadeat. Ideò Christus in Cœlum sublatus implevit omnia donis, & dedit alios Apostolos,&c. alios Pastores & doctores ad καταρτισμὸν concinnationem Sanctorum & ædificationem corporis Christi,donec perveniamus omnes ad unum fidei & cognitionis Filii Dei, ad virum perfectum ad mensuram staturæ ejus,quod completur à Christo,ut non amplius simus infantes, &c. Ephes.IV.10-14. Ecclesia enim corpus Christi, domus Dei est. Corpus Christi crescit,ædificatur,concinnatur in dies, donec ad virum perfectum & mensuram staturæ ejus, quod completur à Christo, perveniat. Etiam domus Dei non simul semélque perfecta & consummata omnibus numeris surgit; sed in ea primò fundamenta jaciuntur, quibus deinceps alii aurum,argentum & pretiosos lapides; alii etiam fœnum & stipulas superstruunt, 1.Cor.III.10-13.
units.tr: LIV. Since it is clear from what we have said so far that the external Church can be infected with errors, not deadly to the faithful who dwell in it, but deadly on account of the hypocrites, and can be considerably disturbed by scandals and even fail, it follows that it must sometimes be reformed, both from more serious errors that produce gangrene [γάγγραιναν] and from scandals. There are two kinds of reformation of the Church, ordinary and extraordinary. The ordinary reformation must be continual, because we must always resist the errors of ignorance and the scandals with which the Church is assailed by flesh, world and Satan, and always make progress in truth and piety. Finally, brothers, rejoice, be made complete [καταρτίζεσθε], be comforted, be of one mind with one another, 2 Cor. 13:11. Here "be made complete" [καταρτίζεσθε] means to strive for restoration, to bear with those being restored, and to correct, teach, reprove and chastise them. For this correction and restoration of brothers in the name of the Lord is the very visitation of God himself, doing this to cleanse us from all evil. Even faith in this life has its deficiencies [τὰ ὑστερήματα], which the Apostle eagerly wished to supply and make complete in the Thessalonians, 1 Thess. 3:10. For faith in one who is converted is at first like that of a carnal child, and it gradually advances until it becomes, as it were, [ἐν πλείῳ] in the perfect, so that the word heard becomes wisdom in him, 1 Cor. 3:1; Heb. 6. For although one who hears the law of faith in Christ and receives it knows all things, 1 John 2:20, because he knows that God is holy and merciful, and whatever can be learned is contained in what he knows as in a foundation, not all the matters pertaining to the completeness [πλεῖγμὸν] of firmness and confirmation are known at once. Nor are at once all the mysteries God has revealed, all the consequences of faith and all the arts of Satan by which he assails the Church, laid open. Nor are all errors and opinions, which are like chaff and stubble that careless men often attach to the foundation, stripped away at once. Finally, it is not immediately obvious, nor always at hand, what faith requires in every place and time. Therefore Christ, taken up into heaven, filled all things with gifts, and gave some apostles, etc., some pastors and teachers for the completion [καταρτισμὸν] of the saints and the building up of the body of Christ, until we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ, so that we are no longer infants, etc., Eph. 4:10-14. For the Church is the body of Christ and the house of God.
