The body of Christ grows, is built up and is fitted together day by day, until it reaches a perfect man and the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. Likewise the house of God does not rise all at once perfect and complete in every respect; first its foundations are laid, on which afterwards some build gold, silver and precious stones, and others also build hay and stubble, 1 Cor. 3:10-13.

units.la: L V. Reformatio extraordinaria est, qua errores, abusus & scandala securitate, infirmitate, conniventia nimia in Ecclesiam subrepentia, diuque tolerata, & jam inveterata, atque fastigium illud pertingentia, ut sine praesentissimo fidei & salutis dispendio amplius ferri & tolerari nequeant, verbo & Spiritu Dei ex Ecclesiae externae gremio eliminantur, ut Ecclesia sic purgata & reformata piis & fidelibus per verbi & Sacramentorum ministerium restitutum utilis & salutaris esse possit. Ita non semel Ecclesia Judaica, vera Dei Ecclesia, sed identidem maleferiatorum, qui in externa ejus communione haerebant, respectu, in idololatriam collapsa a Mose, Prophetis extra ordinem excitis, piis Regibus, Asa inprimis, Josia & Ezechia, nec non ab Esdra & Nehemia reformata est. Et Johannes Baptista, viam Christo praeparaturus, Ϲκολιὰ εἰς εὐθείαν, καὶ τρογεῖας εἰς ὁδὸς λείας obliqua in rectum, & obliquas vias in planum, corda Patrum ad filios, & filiorum ad Patres convertit, Luc. I. 17. III. 5. Christus quoque ventilabrum in manu sua habens, aream Ecclesiae purgare, Matth. III. 12. & Pharisaeorum atque Scribarum falsam doctrinam & fermentum in Ecclesiae intima penetralia invectum expurgare, atque sic ut ignis aurificis, & smegma fullonum sedere, conflare, purificare filios Levi & fundere illos ut aurum & argentum, Mal. III. 2. 3. Matth. V. 17. &c. debuit. Sed & Apostoli Ecclesias, Corinthiacam & Galatensem maxime, quas propter fideles & Sanctos in externa eadem communione domicilium metantes, Sanctificatorum in Christo Jesu, vocatorum sanctorum & Ecclesiae augusto nomine insignit, reformare, & falsae ac lethalis de justificatione, Evangelio, lege, resurrectione mortuorum, doctrinae fermentum & venenum ex iisdem extirpare, ipsasque Ecclesias in meliorem formam restituere necesse habuerunt. Cumque post eorum ἀφίξιν discessum, juxta praedictiones varias, graves lupi, viri perversa loquentes incessere, haereses in Ecclesiam invehi, zizania cum tritico miscere & crescere, apostasia magna intrare, & homo peccati in ipso Templo Dei, ut Deus, sedere debuerint, malis hisce nimium praevalentibus, Ecclesiae quandoque insigni modo reformari, zizania eradicari, homo peccati spiritu oris Christi aboleri, terra a gloria Angeli Babylonem eversuri, illustrari, Apoc. XVIII.1. & aeternum Evangelium iterum praedicari, ibid. XIV. 6. &c. debuit. Neque ante Concilium Tridentinum dubitationem in Ecclesia Papali ipsa habuit, quin Ecclesia reformari possit & debeat. Nam ab optimis quibusque Reformatio flagitata, & in Conciliis integris, Constantiensi, Basileensi & Tridentino Reformatio quaedam, sed ludicra illa, suscepta est; & in Tridentino ipso non tam de Reformationis necessitate, quam de ordine & modo reformandi disputatum est. Sed post illud in deterius versa omnia sunt. Ejus enim decretis dementati Papae gnathones, querelas in Ecclesiae Romanae laudes converterunt, & perpetuam Papae impeccantiam (detur venia Tertulliani verbo) tribuere coeperunt. Nunc ergo Jesuitae & Emissarii perfricta fronte negant, Papam in fide, imo etiam in facto errasse unquam, vel errare, adeoque reformari potuisse vel posse, quod paradoxum, novissimorum temporum pudendus abortus, & indurationis in errore, veluti mortis secundae, certissimum argumentum est.
units.tr: L V. Extraordinary reformation is that by which errors, abuses and scandals that have crept into the external Church through carelessness, weakness and excessive connivance, and have been tolerated for a long time until they are now inveterate and have reached such a height that they can no longer be borne without the most serious loss to faith and salvation, are removed from the bosom of the external Church by the word and Spirit of God. Thus the Church, purged and reformed, through the restored ministry of word and sacraments, may be useful and salutary to the pious and faithful. So the Jewish Church, the true Church of God, but on account of the wicked who clung to its external communion, fell into idolatry not once but repeatedly, and was reformed by Moses, by prophets raised up outside the ordinary way, by pious kings, especially Asa, Josiah and Hezekiah, and also by Ezra and Nehemiah. And John the Baptist, to prepare the way for Christ, turned the crooked into straight and the rough ways into plain, the hearts of the fathers to the children and of the children to the fathers [Ϲκολιὰ εἰς εὐθείαν, καὶ τρογεῖας εἰς ὁδὸς λείας], Luke 1:17; 3:5. Christ too, having his fan in his hand, to purge his threshing floor, the Church, Matt. 3:12, had to expel the false doctrine of the Pharisees and Scribes and the leaven introduced into the innermost parts of the Church, and so to sit as the refiner's fire and the fullers' soap, to refine and purify the sons of Levi and pour them out like gold and silver, Mal. 3:2, 3; Matt. 5:17 etc. The Apostles also, especially to the Corinthian and Galatian Churches, which were giving a home to faithful and saints in the same external communion, though they were marked with the august name of those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, and of the Church, found it necessary to reform them, to root out the leaven and poison of false doctrine concerning justification, the gospel, the law and the resurrection of the dead, and to restore the Churches themselves to a better form. And when after their departure, according to various predictions, grievous wolves, men speaking perverse things, were bound to attack, heresies to be brought into the Church, tares to be mixed with the wheat and to grow, the great apostasy to come, and the man of sin to sit in the very Temple of God as God, with these evils prevailing too much, the Church had at some time to be reformed in a remarkable way: the tares to be uprooted, the man of sin to be destroyed by the spirit of the mouth of Christ, the earth to be illuminated by the glory of the Angel who was to overthrow Babylon, Rev. 18:1, and the eternal Gospel to be preached again, ibid. 14:6 etc. Nor before the Council of Trent did the Papal Church itself doubt that the Church can and must be reformed. For reformation was demanded by all the best men, and at the councils of Constance, Basel and Trent a certain reformation, but a trifling one, was undertaken; and at Trent itself the dispute was less about the necessity of reformation than about the order and manner of reforming. But after that everything was turned for the worse. For by its decrees the demented Popes' flatterers turned complaints into praises of the Roman Church, and began to attribute to the Pope a perpetual impeccability (let the expression of Tertullian be pardoned). Now therefore the Jesuits and emissaries deny with brazen face that the Pope has ever erred, or errs, in faith or even in fact, and so that he could have been, or could be, reformed. This paradox, a shameful abortion of recent times, is a most certain sign of hardening in error, like a second death.

units.la: L VI. Non tam rationes, quam ludibria sunt, quae moderni Emissarii Reformationis possibilitati objiciunt. Fere enim Ecclesiae Papalis infallibilitate & indefectibilitate, nec non confusione Ecclesiae verae proprie & improprie atque latius dictae & falsae Papalis, nituntur, qua cadente ipsorum sophismata etiam cadunt. Ajunt, Ecclesiam optimam suam formam semper retinere, adeoque reformari nunquam posse. Quae ipsissima Catharorum, Novatianorum, fanaticorum haeresis, terram cum Coelo, luctam cum triumpho, cursum cum brabeo turpiter, simul & superciliose confundit. At nos supra probavimus Ecclesiam etiam proprie & angulte, nedum improprie & late dictam, quandiu hic militat, imperfectam esse, multa ignorare, errare, labi & peccare posse. Eadem enim Ecclesiae, quae singulorum vocatorum & fidelium ratio est. At singuli fideles fidei & charitatis suae formam optimam demum in Coelo obtinebunt, I. Cor. XIII. 9. 10. Phil. III. 12. Quomodo alias μεταμορφούμεθα transformamur ex gloria in gloriam, 2. Cor. III. 18. ἀνακαινούμεθα renovamur de die in diem, ibid. IV. 16. si optimam semper formam retinemus? Eadem vero totius Ecclesiae, cujus forma ex collectione formarum, quas singuli fideles habent, constat, ratio est, quam Christus sibi gloriosam, non habentem maculam, rugam, vel simile quid, in Coelo demum fiffit, Ephes. V. 27. Et quanto minus Ecclesia impropre & late dicta, quae mixturam hypocritarum, & occultorum Atheorum etiam patitur, imo quandoque etiam ἀνομίαν illegalitatem in contubernium suum recipere, Exlegem & Adversarium Christi, sedentem in Templo Dei pati debuit, formam Ecclesiae optimam retinet? Contingere enim juxta parabolas & praedictiones horrenda metamorphosi debuit, ut Ecclesia in Babylonem, civitas fidelis in meretricem, arca Noe in haram porcorum Epicuri, sponsa Christi in gregem lupanum, libertas filiorum Dei in tyrannidem dominantium, denique cultus unius soliusque Dei in cultum creaturae praeter Creatorem commutaretur. Et eo usque impietas progredi debuit, ut nihil piis reliqui esset praeter querelam & suspiria: Salva, Domine, quia defecit pius; ad pugilli parvitatem reducti sunt fideles ex filiis hominum. Temerarium loquuntur quisque cum proximo suo; labium blandum loquuntur corde duplici, Psal. XII. 2. 3. Nam quod Ecclesiae formam optimam, nativam esse veram Dei cognitionem, retinemque ejus cultum, sine quo ne Ecclesia quidem esse posset, asserunt, ambiguum nimis & confusum est. Esto Ecclesiae propriae dictae haec forma; & esto optima nativa Ecclesiae, qualis in hac terra militat. At non est forma simpliciter optima, & talis, in qua nihil unquam mutari, nihil in melius reformari possit; quia optima nativa illa forma suae bonitatis, quatenus in Ecclesia recipitur, gradus, incrementa & decrementa habet. At Ecclesiae improprie dictae, Papalis inprimis, alia forma est; illius, verbi praeconium & Sacramentorum usus, utrumque non semper optimum, sed modo modò purum, modò impurum ; hujus obsequium Papæ, quod non idem semper in Ecclesia Papali est. Similis fraus est alterius argumenti, quòd Ecclesiæ forma nunquam perdi vel corrumpi possit, quia ex hypothesi etiam nostra semper fuerit, sit, & finem usque mundi futura sit Ecclesia, seu cœtus fidelium, Deum verè cognoscentium, & rite colentium; adeòque nec restitui & reformari possit, quia restitutio, seu reformatio, & amissio seu corruptio correlativa sint. Nam Ecclesia quidem proprie dicta, hoc est, vocati, electi & fideles, formam equidem suam nunquam sic perdunt, & penitus corrumpunt, ut prorsus eam amittant. Nihilominus nativæ suæ corruptionis, seu veteris hominis reliquias circumferunt, paulatim spiritu regenerationis atterendas, donec morte penitus exuantur. Est etiam, cùm formam illam suæ sanctificationis & renovationis erroribus, peccatis, securitate carnali, inadvertentia sic polluunt, ut necesse habeant καταρτίζεσθαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως resarciri defectus fidei, 1. Thess. III. 10. Si de Ecclesia sermo sit, & Apostolica erravit circa Regnum Christi: & consequens primitiva certi temporis universa fere erroneas de chiliasmo, animabus ante finem mundi ad visionem Dei non admittendis, omnibus hominibus etiam sanctissimis per ignem conflagrationis mundi lustrandis, juramento nunquam adhibendo, belli jure nullo, Eucharistia infantibus etiam administranda, &c. sententias amplexa est. Sed magis etiam Ecclesia externa latiùs dicta corruptioni & destructioni obnoxia est, quia admixti ei hypocritæ inprimis apti nati sunt. Unde etiam διαφθεῖραι τὴν γῆν corrumpere terram Apoc. XI. 18. dicuntur. Etiam Hierosolymitana Ecclesia, Dei licèt Ecclesia, formam suam mirè olim corrupit. Quomodo meretrix facta est urbs fidelis? æquitatis plena, in qua justitia versabatur, nunc autem parricidæ? Argentum tuum in scoriam factum est, & merum tuum aqua vitiatum, &c. Propterea dicit Dominus: Et admoliar manum meam tibi, & excoquam ad purum putum scoriam tuam, & auferam omne stannum tuum: deinde restituam judices tuos, quemadmodum olim fuerunt, & Senatores tuos, sicut antiquitus, Esaj. I. 21. &c. Fuit hæc nativæ formæ corruptio, fuit corruptæ, perditæ redhibitio. Quæ verò perpetua est Ecclesia, Catholica, non externa particularis hæc vel illa est; quæque etiam sic in mundo comparata est, ut non raro de forma sua aliquid delibet. Ejusdem commatis & illa ratio est, quòd semper in mundo formata Ecclesia extiterit, adeòque alia quæcunque, Reformationis titulo, subinducenda Ecclesia locum habere nunquam habuerit; & sicut unus Deus alia Numina, unus in Cœlo formatus Sol alium quemcunque reformatum excludat: ita in terris una formata Ecclesia omnes reformatas alias excludat. Quod inane μορφολυκῶν est. Nam quæ Ecclesia in terris militat, sic formata est, ut imperfectioni, corruptioni, mutationi obnoxia, adeòque identidem reformanda sit. Neque formata reformatam, sed reformata corruptam & adulteratam excludit. Et non æquè Ecclesia reformata à formata quoad essentiam differt, vel formata immutabilis & incorruptibilis est, atque Deus verus à falso Numine, Sol verus ab
units.tr: LVI. The arguments that the modern emissaries of the Reformation raise against the possibility of reformation are less arguments than mockeries. They rest almost entirely on the infallibility and indefectibility of the Papal Church, and on confusing the true Church, taken properly, improperly and more broadly, with the false Papal Church. When that foundation falls, their sophisms fall with it. They say the Church always keeps its best form and so can never be reformed. This is exactly the heresy of the Cathari, the Novatians and the fanatics, which shamefully and haughtily confuses earth with heaven, the struggle with the triumph, and the race with the prize. But we have shown above that the Church, even taken properly and narrowly, let alone improperly and broadly, is imperfect for as long as it fights here. It can be ignorant of many things, err, slip and sin. The same account holds for the Church as for the individual called and faithful. But individual believers obtain the best form of their faith and love only in heaven, 1 Cor. XIII. 9. 10; Phil. III. 12. Otherwise, how are we transformed from glory to glory [μεταμορφούμεθα] (2 Cor. III. 18) and renewed day by day [ἀνακαινούμεθα] (ibid. IV. 16), if we always keep the best form? The same holds for the whole Church, whose form consists in the collection of the forms that the individual faithful have. Christ at last presents it to himself in heaven as glorious, not having spot, wrinkle or any such thing (Eph. V. 27). And how much less does the Church taken improperly and broadly keep the best form, when it suffers a mixture of hypocrites and hidden atheists, and at times even had to admit lawlessness [ἀνομίαν] into its fellowship, to endure the lawless one and adversary of Christ, sitting in the temple of God? According to the parables and predictions, it had to undergo a horrible metamorphosis: the Church became Babylon, the faithful city a harlot, the ark of Noah a sty of Epicurus's swine, the bride of Christ a flock of brothel-dwellers, the liberty of the sons of God a tyranny of lords, and finally the worship of the one and only God was changed into worship of a creature in place of the Creator. And impiety had to advance so far that nothing was left to the pious but complaint and sighs: Save, Lord, for the godly man ceaseth; the faithful fail from among the children of men... they speak vanity every one with his neighbour; with flattering lips and a double heart do they speak (Psal. XII. 2. 3). For their claim that the best native form of the Church is the true knowledge of God, and that it keeps its worship, without which the Church could not even exist, is too ambiguous and confused. Grant that this is the form of the Church properly so called, and grant that it is the best native form of the Church as it fights on this earth. Still, it is not simply the best form, such that nothing in it could ever change or be reformed for the better, because that best native form, insofar as it is received in the Church, has degrees, increases and decreases. The Church improperly so called, the Papal Church above all, has another form: the proclamation of the word and the use of the sacraments are not always the best, but now pure and now impure; and the obedience owed to the Pope is not always the same within the Papal Church. A similar fallacy lies in the other argument, that the form of the Church can never be lost or corrupted, since on our hypothesis too it has always been, is, and will be, until the end of the world, the Church, that is, the assembly of those who truly know God and worship him rightly. From this they conclude that it cannot be restored or reformed, since restoration or reformation and loss or corruption are correlatives. For the Church properly so called, that is, the called, the elect and the faithful, indeed never lose their form in such a way, nor so utterly corrupt it, as to lose it altogether. Nevertheless, they carry about remnants of their native corruption, or of the old man, which by degrees must be worn down by the Spirit of regeneration until they are wholly stripped off in death. There is also the case where they so pollute that form of their sanctification and renewal by errors, sins, carnal security and carelessness that they need the defects of their faith to be made good [καταρτίζεσθαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως] (1 Thess. III. 10). If the question concerns the Church, the apostolic Church too erred about the kingdom of Christ. Consequently, for a certain time the primitive Church almost universally embraced the erroneous opinions about chiliasm, that souls are not to be admitted to the vision of God before the end of the world, that all men, even the most holy, must be purified by the fire of the world's conflagration, that oaths are never to be used, that there is no right of war, that the Eucharist is to be given even to infants, and so on. But the external Church, taken more broadly, is even more liable to corruption and destruction, because hypocrites are especially apt to be mixed in with it. Hence they are said to corrupt the earth [διαφθεῖραι τὴν γῆν] (Apoc. XI. 18). Even the Jerusalem Church, though it was God's Church, once wonderfully corrupted its form: How is the faithful city become a harlot! She was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in her; but now murderers. Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water... Therefore saith the Lord... I will turn my hand upon thee, and purge away thy dross as with lye, and take away all thy tin; and I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning (Esai. I. 21 etc.). This was a corruption of the native form, and a restoration of what had been corrupted and lost. But the perpetual Church is the catholic Church, not this or that particular external Church, and it is so constituted in the world that it not infrequently alters something of its form. The same reasoning applies to the claim that a Church formed in the world has always existed, so that any other Church introduced under the title of reformation could never have a place. Just as one God excludes other deities, and the one sun formed in heaven excludes any other sun reformed, so, they say, one formed Church on earth excludes all other reformed Churches. This is an empty bugbear [μορφολυκῶν]. For the Church that fights on earth is so formed that it is liable to imperfection, corruption and change, and so must be reformed again and again. Nor does the formed Church exclude the reformed one; rather, the reformed Church excludes the corrupted and adulterated. Nor does the reformed Church differ from the formed Church in essence in the way that the formed Church is immutable and incorruptible, as the true God differs from a false deity, or the true sun from

units.la: adulterino quoad essentiam differt, & uterque immutabilis & incorruptibilis est. Planè igitur similia ἀπαραλλάκτως sunt. Sicut tamen verus ille formatus Cœli Sol talis esse, & unus esse non definit, licèt subinde nubilis & tenebris noctis aspectui nostro subducatur, &, mox splendorem recuperaturus, obscuretur: ita nec Ecclesia vera formata una esse desinit, vel Sol justitiæ occidit, quando fumus ex puteo, ut fumus fornacis magnæ ascendens, Solem & aera obtenebrans, Apoc. IX. 2. imò nigrum, ut saccum ex pilis, efficiens, ibid. VI. 12. Reformatione discutitur. Sicut etiam verus Deus unus est, & erit in æternum, licèt quæ ei falsa & sterco-rea Numina obducuntur, Deo volente & valente paulò post in orcum relegentur: ita nec una & formata in mundo Ecclesia esse desinit, licèt illi, qui tabernaculum Molochi, & idolum Dei Remphan in ipsa Ecclesiæ externa communione portarunt, Actor. VII. 43. pariterque Pseudo-christiani omnes alios Deos, Divos, cudentes & religiosè colentes, quin & Antichristus in Templo Dei sedens, & se, ut Deum, ostentans, Reformationis beneficio ab Ecclesia summoti æternis tenebris damnentur. Sed frustra Emissariis Ecclesiæ, Scripturæ sensu acceptæ notionem & ideam aptamus vel opponimus, cùm animo illorum nil nisi idea Ecclesiæ, Pontificio sensu acceptæ, hoc est, Monarchiæ Papalis, quæ Romæ Mystarcham suum, Regem regum, & Dominum dominantium, metropolin, visibilem cathedram, Hierarchas, principes fidei cæcæ populi dominantes, habet, obversetur. Sed non hanc veram Ecclesiam, sed falsam, seu civitatem illam, quæ Babylonis nomine seu stigmate compungitur, esse, mox probatum dabimus. Denique nec schismatis rei sunt, qui Ecclesiam reformant, eò quòd, uti illi argutantur, exi-stente vera Ecclesia alios segreges cœtus instituunt, vel sequuntur. Nam vera Ecclesia existit in communione externa vel undique pura, saltem fundamenti fidei & salutis tenace: vel à fundamento fidei & salutis defi-cIscente. Exi-stens Ecclesia vera in communione externa priore sensu sine schismatis reatu illam deserere non potest; at corrigere tamen & reformare, non deserendo eam, sed rectius informando, potest. At exi-stens in communione externa posteriore sensu, eámque ob concussa fidei & salutis fundamenta deserens, schismatis reatum non contrahit; uti fusiùs supra demonstravimus.
units.tr: a counterfeit one in essence, and each is immutable and incorruptible. They are therefore plainly alike [ἀπαραλλάκτως]. Yet just as that true sun, formed in heaven, does not cease to be such and to be one, although it is sometimes veiled from our sight by clouds and the darkness of night, and is darkened so that it will soon recover its brightness, so the true formed Church does not cease to be one, nor does the Sun of righteousness set, when smoke rises from the pit, like the smoke of a great furnace, darkening the sun and the air (Apoc. IX. 2), or indeed makes the sun black as sackcloth of hair (ibid. VI. 12); it is dispelled by reformation. Likewise the true God is one and will be for ever, although the false and filthy deities that are cast over him will, by God's will and power, soon be consigned to hell. So too the one formed Church in the world does not cease to be, although those who carried the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Remphan within the external communion of the Church itself (Acts VII. 43), and all the pseudo-Christians who mint and devoutly worship other gods, and even Antichrist, sitting in the temple of God and displaying himself as God, will, removed from the Church by the benefit of reformation, be condemned to eternal darkness. But it is in vain that we fit or oppose to the emissaries of the Church a notion and idea of the Church as received in the sense of Scripture, since in their minds there is nothing but the idea of the Church as received in the Papal sense, that is, the Papal monarchy, which at Rome has its Mystarch, its King of kings and Lord of lords, its metropolis, its visible chair, its hierarchs, and princes ruling over the blind faith of the people. But we will soon show that this is not the true Church but the false one, or that city which is marked with the name or brand of Babylon. Finally, those who reform the Church are not guilty of schism, on the ground, as these men wrangle, that while the true Church exists they set up or follow separate assemblies. For the true Church exists either within external communion, wholly pure or at least holding firmly to the foundation of faith and salvation, or in a communion that has fallen away from the foundation of faith and salvation. A true Church existing in external communion in the former sense cannot be deserted without the guilt of schism; yet it can be corrected and reformed, not by deserting it but by informing it more rightly. But one existing in external communion in the latter sense, and deserting it because the foundations of faith and salvation have been shaken, does not incur the guilt of schism, as we demonstrated more fully above.

units.la: LVII. Fuit idea veræ Ecclesiæ, quam ex verbo Dei repræsentavimus. Deinceps idea falsæ Ecclesiæ investiganda nobis venit. Eam tum Fanatici, tum Pontificii exhibent; quorum illi Ecclesiam improprie dictam, externam & visibilem; hi proprie dictam & invisibilem tolunt, aliámque substituunt. Fanatici quibus & Sociniani astipulantur, Ecclesiam angusto fine circumscribentes, publicam esse non sinunt, cunctósque cœtus, qui à scandalis non satis expurgati sunt, Ecclesiæ nomine dedignantur: pios autem, alibi oberrantes, quos inter etiam religiosos ex gentibus, nullo externo verbo vocatos, numerant, in Ecclesia invisibili collocant; atque ita vel nullam, vel non aspectabilem Ecclesiam in mundo faciunt. Negat enim Weigelius asta voce, quòd Ecclesia cœtus visibilis bilis sit, asseritque illam in omnibus mundi sectis, infideli um etiam paganorum, Judæorum & Muhammedanorum, abscondiam latere; nisi quòd certa nota sodalibus ὁμοπνεύστοις innotescat, quam alii charitatem ἀνυπόκριτον ex intimo corde; alii obedientiam verbi Dei, seu vitam Christianam, quæ ex Deo est, nominant. Quorum assertionum error ex iis, quæ de congregationis & communionis externæ atque visibilis necessitate, & ejusdem notis γνώσεως supra diximus, nullo negotio cognosci potest. Apostolicæ autem Ecclesiæ, Hierosolymitana, Antiochena, Romana, Corinthiaca, Philippensis, &c. visibiles fuerunt, & in iis Catholica Ecclesia extitit. Et Ecclesiam adire & audire Christus, Matth. XVIII. 17. atque ex eadem incestuosum tolli Apostolus, 1. Cor. V. 2. jusserunt. Idem etiam Christus ministerium verbi & Sacramentorum perpetuo, seu usque ad consummatam corporis Ecclesiæ ædificationem, in mundo duraturum instituit, Matth. XXVIII. 19. 20. Eph. IV. 11. &c. Ministerio verò verbi & Sacramentorum auditus verbi & usus Sacramentorum respondet. His velut vinculis Dominus fideles in Ecclesiasticam communionem consociari vult. Imò ad fidem ordinariè generandam auditus verbi & usus Sacramentorum necessarius est, Rom. VI. 3. X. 17. Gal. III. 27. 1. Cor. X. 16. Neque etiam charitatem ad notandam Ecclesiam sufficere, sine præcedente judicio fidei, quod ex verbo Dei depromendum est, supra ostendimus. Ideo S. Paulus fidem & charitatem conjungit, Eph. I. 15. Philem. v. 5. & quod in omnibus, infidelibus etiam, sectis Ecclesiam illi collocant, proprio & perverso, non Dei judicio faciunt. Infideles enim extranei, 1. Cor. V. 12. 13. per infidelitatem defracti, Rom. XI. 20. alieni à pactis promissionis, absque Christo & Deo in mundo, Ephes. II. 12. sunt. Neque ulla extra Christum spes salutis est, Actor. IV. 12. Qui non credit Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super ipsum, Joh. III. 36.
units.tr: LVII. We have set out the idea of the true Church from the Word of God. Next we must examine the idea of the false Church. The Fanatics and the Papists both present it, though they treat the Church differently. The Fanatics take away the Church as it is improperly called, external and visible, while the Papists take away the Church as it is properly called, invisible, and put another in its place. The Fanatics, whom the Socinians support, limit the Church to a narrow scope. They do not allow it to be public, and they refuse the name of Church to every assembly not sufficiently purged of scandals. They place the godly, who wander elsewhere (among whom they also count religious people from the Gentiles, called by no external word), in the invisible Church. In this way they make the Church either nonexistent or not discernible in the world. Indeed Weigelius openly denies that the Church is a visible assembly, and he asserts that it lies hidden in all the sects of the world, including the unbelieving pagans, Jews, and Muslims, except that it is made known by a certain mark to its like-spirited members [ὁμοπνεύστοις]. Some call this mark unfeigned love [ἀνυπόκριτον] from the inmost heart; others call it obedience to the Word of God, or the Christian life, which is from God. The error of these assertions can easily be recognised from what we said above about the necessity of an external and visible congregation and communion, and about its marks of knowledge [γνώσεως]. But the apostolic churches, at Jerusalem, Antioch, Rome, Corinth, Philippi, and so on, were visible, and the Catholic Church existed in them. Christ commanded that the Church be told (to approach and hear the Church), Matth. 18:17, and the Apostle ordered that the incestuous person be taken away from it, 1 Cor. 5:2. Christ also instituted the ministry of the Word and the Sacraments to last in the world perpetually, that is, until the building of the body of the Church is complete, Matth. 28:19, 20; Eph. 4:11, etc. Hearing the Word and using the Sacraments correspond to the ministry of the Word and the Sacraments. The Lord wills that the faithful be joined in ecclesiastical communion by these bonds as if by chains. Indeed, hearing the Word and using the Sacraments are necessary for ordinarily generating faith, Rom. 6:3; 10:17; Gal. 3:27; 1 Cor. 10:16. Nor does love alone suffice to mark the Church, without a prior judgment of faith, which must be drawn from the Word of God, as we have shown above. Therefore St. Paul joins faith and love, Eph. 1:15; Philem. 5. And those who place the Church in all sects, even unbelieving ones, do so by their own perverse judgment, not God's. For unbelievers are outsiders, 1 Cor. 5:12, 13, broken off through unbelief, Rom. 11:20, aliens from the covenants of promise, without Christ and without God in the world, Eph. 2:12. Nor is there any hope of salvation outside Christ, Acts 4:12. He who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him, John 3:36.

units.la: LVIII. Inanis fanaticorum metus est, ne, si Ecclesia visibilis statuatur, iterum loco affigatur, uti in V. T. factum, & in N. T. Pontificii id æmulati sunt.
units.tr: 58. It is an empty fear of the fanatics that, if a visible Church is established, it will be fastened again to a place, as happened under the Old Testament, and as the Papists have imitated under the New.

units.la: Non enim loco affigitur, quod certo & determinato loco, extra quem salvari nemini contingat, non affigitur. Christus in mundo conspicuus versabatur, neque tamen certo loco se alligavit, vel alligari passus est. Neque Apostolorum Ecclesia, post festum Pentecostes, certo loco alligata, sed per totum terrarum orbem propagata est, visibilis licet. Neque Christus veros Dei adoratores alicubi, seu in loco aliquo, sed tantùm in certo loco, Hierosolymæ, vel in Templo Samaritanorum, Deum in Spiritu & veritate adoratu·ros negavit. Ac licet etiam Deus, extra visibilem cœtum coli possit, tamen temerè congregationem deserere non licet, Heb. X. 25. Deus enim sicut civilem, ita etiam religiosam societatem instituit. Præterea neque solo spiritu, sed etiam corpore coli vult. Empti estis pretio. Glorificate igitur Deum in corpore vestro, & in spiritu vestro, quæ Dei sunt, 1. Corinth. VI. 20. Nam corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem fit confessio ad salutem, Rom. X. 10. Neque ideo charitas sola Ecclesiæ nota est, quia Christus dixit: Ex hoc omnes cognoscent, vos esse discipulos meos, si charitatem habueritis invicem, Joh. XIII.
units.tr: For it is not fastened to a place merely because it is not fixed to a certain and definite place, outside which no one can be saved. Christ moved about visibly in the world, yet he did not bind himself to a certain place, nor did he allow himself to be bound. Nor was the Church of the Apostles, after the feast of Pentecost, tied to a certain place, but was spread throughout the whole orb of the earth, and yet remained visible. Nor did Christ deny that true worshippers would worship God in spirit and truth in some place or other, but only that they would do so in a certain place, Jerusalem or the Temple of the Samaritans. And although God can be worshipped even outside the visible assembly, it is nevertheless not lawful to desert the congregation rashly, Heb. X. 25. For God has instituted religious society just as he has instituted civil society. Moreover, he wishes to be worshipped not by the spirit alone but also by the body: You were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's, 1 Cor. VI. 20. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation, Rom. X. 10. Nor for this reason is love alone the mark of the Church, because Christ said: By this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another, John XIII. 35.

units.la: 35. Nam de ea charitate loquitur, quam discipuli Christi ex verbo & exemplo Christi didicerunt. Inde enim discipuli Christi dignoscuntur. Præcedit ergo doctrina Christi, & ex charitate discipulorum illa dignoscitur, Doctrina enim Christi est, ut diligant invicem, quemadmodum Christus dilexit nos, ibid. v. 34. Ipsa verò charitas fratrum ad communionem invicem colendam impellit, de quo supra diximus. Neque Christus ex solo eo, quòd invicem diligimus, cognoscimus, quòd simus discipuli Christi, asserit. Nam charitas fidei doctrinam supponit; sine qua vera charitas non est. Fides per professionem, charitas per opera in verbo Dei præscripta se exerit. Ac licèt Ecclesia sit in omnibus populis, nationibus & linguis, quoad communionem civilem, tamen non sic est in omnibus sectis, ut in quavis secta, quà tali, verae Ecclesiæ membra delitescant. Ut verò Ecclesia Catholica sit, non necesse est, ut in omnibus populis, nationibúsque simul sit, sed ut successive in iis sit. Neque etiam ideo, quia in omnibus cœtibus sunt, qui per fraternam dilectionem se conjungunt, sequitur, in omnibus cœtibus & sectis vera Ecclesiæ membra reperiri. Alia enim ratio est dilectionis, quam natura dirigit; alia ejus, quam fides ἀνυπόκριτος, Christo capiti inserens, nec non cor purum & bona conscientia, 1. Tim. I. 5. dirigit. Illa communis esse potest; hæc solorum Christianorum, qui veri Christi discipuli sunt, est. Diligant ergo se Pagani, Judæi, Muhammedani. Non ideo, qua tales, vera Ecclesiæ membra sunt. Denique nec in omnibus sectis sunt, qui credunt, quòd Deus sit, & remunerator sit credentium, Hebr. XI. 6. sicut id credere oportet eos, qui ad Deum accedunt, & eum quærunt, & ei ἐκζητοῦσιν placere contendunt. Fides verò illa non communis, sed electorum propria illa est, qua credunt promissioni justitiæ & salutis in Christo Jesu, adeòque persuasi sunt, se per fidem meriti Christi ad Deum accessuros, eum propitium inventuros, & vitam atque justitiam consecuturos esse. Neque credere quòd Deus sit, est credere tantùm, quòd Deus existit, quia id non tantum creditur, sed etiam scitur, & fides existentiæ Dei non efficit προσέρχεσθαι accessum ad Deum, sed, sine alia fide, Dei, ceu justi judicis odium & fugam efficit; sed quòd sit in Deum, sicuti Enocho credenti & cum Deo ambulanti fuit; & talis sit, qualis ad justitiam & salutem peccatoris credi debet; & sufficiens ad eum salvandum, & voluntatem salvandi per Christum habens, gratiosus, misericors, dignus, qui ametur, & omni studio à peccatore, cujus Deus fieri vult, quæratur, ut ad eum accedere, & eum invenire liceat. Non potest autem Deus sic peccatori in Deum fieri, quæri & adiri, nisi in Filio, qui via, veritas & vita est, Joh. XIV. 6. Deus enim verus non est, qui talis non est, & qui Triunus non est, quia nonnisi talem se in verbo revelavit. In fide ergo illa cognitio peccati nostri, sanctitatis & justitiæ & meriti Christi nobis donati, & Spiritus S. nobis dati; atque propter hæc omnia Dei amor & glorificatio continetur. Cujusmodi fides nec omnium sectarum, nec omnium, qui Christum nominant, sed solorum electorum, vocatorum & fidelium est.
units.tr: 35. For he speaks of that love which the disciples of Christ learned from Christ's word and example. It is by this that the disciples of Christ are recognised. So the doctrine of Christ comes first, and by the love of the disciples it is recognised, for the doctrine of Christ is that they love one another, as Christ has loved us, ibid. v. 34. Brotherly love itself impels us to cultivate communion with one another, as we said above. Nor does Christ assert that we know we are his disciples from our mutual love alone. For love presupposes the doctrine of faith, without which there is no true love. Faith shows itself through profession, and love through works prescribed in the Word of God. And although the Church is among all peoples, nations and tongues as regards civil communion, it is not so in all sects, that in any sect, as such, the true members of the Church lie hidden. For the Catholic Church to exist, it is not necessary that it be among all peoples and nations at the same time, but that it be among them successively. Nor, because there are people in all assemblies who join themselves together by brotherly love, does it follow that true members of the Church are to be found in all assemblies and sects. For the love which nature directs is one thing; the love which faith unfeigned [ἀνυπόκριτος], joining us to Christ the head, and a pure heart and a good conscience, 1 Tim. I. 5, direct is another. The former can be common; the latter belongs only to Christians who are true disciples of Christ. Let Pagans, Jews and Muhammadans love one another; they are not true members of the Church on that account, as such. Finally, not all sects include those who believe that God is, and is a rewarder of those who believe, Heb. XI. 6, just as it is necessary that those believe who draw near to God, and seek him, and strive to please him [ἐκζητοῦσιν]. But that faith is not common; it is the peculiar possession of the elect, by which they believe the promise of righteousness and salvation in Christ Jesus, and so are persuaded that through faith in Christ's merit they will come to God, find him propitious, and obtain life and righteousness. To believe that God is, is not merely to believe that God exists, for that is not only believed but also known, and faith in the existence of God does not produce approach [προσέρχεσθαι] to God; without other faith it produces only hatred and flight from God as a just judge. Rather, it is faith in God as Enoch had, who believed and walked with God, and such as must be believed for the righteousness and salvation of a sinner: sufficient to save him, having the will to save through Christ, gracious, merciful, worthy to be loved, and to be sought by the sinner with all zeal, so that it may be permitted to approach him and find him as his God. But God cannot become such to a sinner, nor be sought and approached, except in the Son, who is the way, the truth and the life, John XIV. 6. For he is not the true God who is not such, and who is not Triune, since he has revealed himself in the Word only as such. In that faith, therefore, is contained the knowledge of our sin, of holiness and righteousness, of the merit of Christ given to us and of the Holy Spirit given to us; and from all these the love and glorification of God. Such faith belongs not to all sects, nor to all who name Christ, but only to the elect, the called and the faithful.

units.la: LIX.
units.tr: LIX.

units.la: Sicut Fanatici Ecclesiam externam & visibilem: ita Pontificii Ecclesiam proprie dictam & invisibilem tollunt, & visibilem externam in civitatem mundanam convertunt. Quorum perversissima, quam cuderunt, Ecclesiae idea paucis nunc excutienda nobis venit. Et Ecclesiae quidem vocem, Papali dialecto, non coetum vel electorum vocatorum, vel vocatorum tantum, sed Papatum, seu Monarchiam Ecclesiasticam, & Papae dominatum atque principatum supremum in temporalibus & spiritualibus, adeoque in utrisque suprematum significare, supra animadvertimus. Sic quum quondam in armis esset Julius II. belligerare-turque cum nationibus, vel ut reciperet amissas ditiones, vel ut imperii sui fines proferret, Ecclesiae negotiis distineri dicebatur. Et Papae ditiones status Ecclesiae nomine veniunt. Constat id inprimis ex historia Italica a Guiciardino de negotiis illis conscripta; ubi (lib. VI.) Fuenza & urbes illae, quas a Venetis sibi reddi postulabat, Urbes Ecclesiae appellantur: &(lib. VI. VII.) cum illas armis aut compositione recuperavit, illae in ditionem & obedientiam Ecclesiae redire dicuntur; & sicubi militaria ejus stratagemata infeliciter successerunt, (lib. VI. & IX.) quamvis res haereant (inquit Julius) Deus tamen Ecclesiae suae veniet auxilio: & omnia, quibus utebatur, omnesque praeliandi fines, quos sibi proposuit, Ecclesiae titulo veltiuntur, & (lib. VIII. & IX.) duces Ecclesiae, exercitus Ecclesiae, hostes, perduelles, equites, pedites, memorantur; & cuncta, quae Papatus possidet Status Ecclesiae passim dicuntur. Si igitur nominis Ecclesiae definitio ab iis exigatur; non aliud iis Ecclesia, quam Papa, seu Papae status & Regnum est. Sed particularis status aliquis solus, Ecclesiae nomine tectus, & a reliquis omnibus segregatus, non magis Ecclesia Catholica esse potest, quam Cajaphas Pontifex maximus cum sua factione Ecclesia Catholica fuit. Et tam significatus hic Ecclesiae, ignotus Scripturis sacris est, quam Papa & Papatus ipse, nisi quatenus in Scripturis coelestibus divis, nomine Adversarii, Antichristi, Exlegis, Bestiae, Babylonis, &c. passim configitur.
units.tr: Just as the Fanatics abolish the external and visible Church, so the Papists abolish the Church properly so called and invisible, and turn the visible external Church into a worldly city. Their most perverse idea of the Church, which they have devised, now comes before us to be briefly examined. We have noted above that in the Papal dialect the word Church signifies not an assembly of the elect, or of the called, or of the called only, but the Papacy, or ecclesiastical monarchy, and the Pope's dominion and supreme sovereignty in temporal and spiritual matters, and so supremacy in both. So when Julius II was once in arms and waging war with nations, either to recover lost dominions or to extend the boundaries of his empire, he was said to be occupied with the affairs of the Church. And the Pope's dominions go under the name state of the Church. This is evident above all from the Italian history of Guicciardini written about those affairs, where (book VI) Faenza and those cities which he demanded be returned to him by the Venetians are called Cities of the Church; and (books VI and VII) when he recovered them by arms or agreement, they are said to return into the dominion and obedience of the Church; and wherever his military stratagems met with misfortune (books VI and IX), although the matter hangs in the balance (says Julius), yet God will come to the aid of his Church; and all the means he used, and all the ends of fighting he set for himself, are called by the title Church; and (books VIII and IX) leaders of the Church, armies of the Church, enemies, traitors, horsemen, foot soldiers are mentioned; and everything the Papacy possesses is everywhere called the state of the Church. If therefore a definition of the name Church is demanded of them, the Church for them is nothing other than the Pope, or the Papal state and kingdom. But some particular state alone, hidden under the name of Church and separated from all the rest, cannot be more the Catholic Church than Caiaphas the high priest with his faction was the Catholic Church. And this meaning of Church is as unknown to the holy Scriptures as the Pope and the Papacy itself, except insofar as they are constantly invented under the names Adversary, Antichrist, Lawless One, Beast, Babylon, and so on in the divine heavenly Scriptures.

units.la: LX.
units.tr: LX.

units.la: Definitionis nominis rei ipsius definitio respondet. Eam a conditione principali sic passim definiunt, quod sit universitas obtemperantium Papae Romano; juxta statutum Johannis XXII. in Jure Canonico de Majorit. cap. Una, S. sic declarantis: Omnino est de necessitate salutis omnem humanam creaturam subesse Papae Romano. Et certe a subjectione erga Papam Pontificii praecipue Ecclesiam & ejus membra aestimant. Plenius vero Bellarminus de Eccles. milit. lib. III. 2. Ecclesiam sic definit: Nos dicimus Ecclesiam illam unam & veram esse coetum hominum ejusdem fidei Christianae professione, & eorundem Sacramentorum communione colligatum sub regimine legitimorum Ecclesiae Pastorum, ac praecipue unius Christi in terris Vicarii, Romani Pontificis: Differentiam porro suam inter & nostram sententiam sic ibidem explicat: Hoc interest inter sententiam nostram & omnes alias, quod omnes aliae requirunt internas virtutes ad constituendum aliquem in Ecclesia & propterea Ecclesiam veram invisibilem faciunt. Nos autem credimus, in Ecclesia inveniri omnes virtutes, fidem, spem & charitatem, & cetera.
units.tr: The definition of the thing answers to the definition of the name. They generally define it from its principal condition, that it is the whole body of those obeying the Roman Pope; following the statute of John XXII in the Canon Law, de Majorit. cap. Una, S., which declares: It is wholly necessary for salvation that every human creature be subject to the Roman Pope. And certainly the Papists chiefly reckon the Church and its members by their subjection to the Pope. More fully, Bellarmine, de Eccles. milit. lib. III. 2., defines the Church thus: We say that the one and true Church is an assembly of men bound together by profession of the same Christian faith and communion in the same sacraments, under the rule of the legitimate pastors of the Church, and especially of the one Vicar of Christ on earth, the Roman Pontiff. He explains his difference from our opinion there thus: This is the difference between our view and all others: all the others require internal virtues to constitute someone in the Church, and so make the true Church invisible. But we believe that all virtues, faith, hope and charity, and the rest, are found in the Church.

units.la: Tamen, ut quis aliquo modo dici possit pars verae Ecclesiae, de qua Scripturae loquuntur, non putamus requiri ullam internam virtutem, sed tantum externam professionem fidei, & Sacramentorum communionem, quae ipso sensu percipitur. Ecclesia enim est coetus hominum ita visibilis & palpabilis, ut est coetus populi Romani, vel Regnum Galliae, vel Respublica Venetorum. Illos porro, qui nullas virtutes internas habent, & tamen spe aut timore aliquo temporali fidem profitentur, & in Sacramentis communicant sub regimine Papae, subjicit idem, esse de corpore, at non de anima Ecclesiae, & tales, quales sunt capilli, aut ungues, aut mali humores in corpore humano. Haec Pontificiae Ecclesiae idea est. Et talem Ecclesiam esse, quae in symbolo Sancta & Catholica dicitur; hanc unam, solam fidei magistram, perpetim, Regni temporalis praepotentis adinstar, illustrem, invisibilem, infallibilem, irreformabilem & aeternam esse, sine fine & modo jactant, & quotquot ab illa discessionem faciunt, aeternum damnari definiunt.
units.tr: Yet, for someone to be in any way called a part of the true Church of which the Scriptures speak, we do not think any internal virtue is required, but only external profession of faith and communion in the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses themselves. For the Church is an assembly of men as visible and tangible as the assembly of the Roman people, or the kingdom of France, or the Venetian republic. Moreover, those who have no internal virtues, and yet profess the faith and communicate in the sacraments under the rule of the Pope out of some temporal hope or fear, the same writer says belong to the body but not the soul of the Church, and are like hairs, or nails, or bad humours in the human body. This is the Papist idea of the Church. And they boast without end that the Church which is called holy and catholic in the creed, this one sole teacher of faith, like a most powerful temporal kingdom, is illustrious, invisible, infallible, unreformable and eternal; and they define that whoever departs from it is damned forever.

units.la: LXI. Caeterum Pontificia Ecclesiae definitio & obscura est, & explicatior genuinam Ecclesiae verae ideam prorsus corrumpit, & pro Ecclesia Dei Ecclesiam malignantium substituit. Etenim primo Ecclesiam coetum hominum definiens, non quemvis coetum vel congregationem, sed Cathedralem, hoc est, talem, quae ad visibilem quampiam in mundo cathedram alligata sit, intelligit. Sicut enim in V.T. populi Israelitici coetus ad certam cathedram, quae Hierosolymis sedem fixit, adstrictus fuit: ita in N.T. non ex Christi institutione, sed suo arbitrio, & quia ita Monarchiae Papae expedire visum est, cathedram certam, visibilem & conspicuam, cui se Christiani omnes ad salutem subjicere teneantur, & quae sine Scripturae luce evidens, quin & Scriptura ipsa prior & notior sit, illi finxerunt, & Romae affixerunt. Quo sensu Catholica illa esse non potest. Nam certo loco, certae in mundo cathedrae, extra quam spes salutis nulla sit, alligari, & Catholicum universale esse, dis dia pantōn differunt. Sed Ecclesia proprie coetus & congregatio est non propter respectum ad certum locum, sed propter vinculum & communionem, quam credentes cum Deo in Christo, & inter se habent. Neque desinunt eo modo esse congregatio, licet in mundo dissipentur, & mundus illos, ut passeres palantes in monte suo Psal. XI.1. rideat. Nam & Ecclesia est, si duo vel tres in distinctis locis in nomine Christi conveniant, Matth. XVIII. 20. & ad Ecclesiam & sortem Sanctorum in luce pertinent, qui in carceribus detinentur, vel in sylvis & cavernis terrae propter metum hostium latere coguntur. Secundo definitio illa de veris fidelibus, & virtutibus altum silet. Et tamen magnificae promissiones illae, quae Ecclesiae factae sunt, proprie ad fideles & Sanctos, non ad alios pertinent. Nam boni quid promissum esse iis, qui audiunt, & ad Ecclesiam labia sua, at non cor afferunt, adeoque necessario falsas opiniones sub verbis sive veris, sive falsis habent: & iisdem privilegium non erranti datum esse, saltem eos in petra sic aedificatos esse, ut iis portae inferorum non praevaleant, quis, ut credat, induci potest? Sicut congregatio capillorum, unguium, malorum humorum corpus humanum ipsum non est, sed excrementorum corporis foeda colluvies; ita nec coetus hominum non fidelium, non sanctorum, adeoque virtutibus non praeditorum Christi corpus esse non potest. Nec sine Numine factum est, quod sic Ecclesiam suam, quam ceu infallibilem tantopere praedicant, & adorant, & qua nihil in mundo augustius habent, definire debuerunt. Ecquis enim amplius dubitaverit, talem Ecclesiam ex hypocritis & occultis infidelibus conflatam, errare & deficere, imo nil nisi errare & deficere posse? Cum miraculo potius simile sit, ejusmodi porcorum gregem in voluptatum & flagitiorum suorum coeno aliquid de fide & de Coelo grunnire.
units.tr: LXI. Moreover, the Papist definition of the Church is both obscure, and its fuller explanation utterly corrupts the genuine idea of the true Church, and substitutes for the Church of God the church of evildoers. For, first, in defining the Church as an assembly of men, they understand not any assembly or gathering, but a cathedral one, that is, one bound to some visible chair in the world. For just as in the Old Testament the assembly of the Israelite people was bound to a certain chair, which fixed its seat at Jerusalem, so in the New Testament, not by Christ's institution but by their own choice, and because it seemed expedient to the Papal monarchy, they invented a certain chair, visible and conspicuous, to which all Christians are bound to submit for salvation, and which, without the light of Scripture, indeed when Scripture itself is earlier and better known, they fixed and attached to Rome. In that sense it cannot be Catholic. For to be bound to a certain place, a certain chair in the world, outside which there is no hope of salvation, and to be universal Catholic, differ, as the Greeks say, dis dia pantōn [δὶς διὰ πάντων]. But the Church is properly an assembly and congregation, not on account of regard for a certain place, but on account of the bond and communion which believers have with God in Christ and with one another. Nor do they cease in that way to be a congregation, even if they are scattered in the world, and the world laughs at them, like sparrows wandering on their mountain, Ps. XI. 1. For there is a Church even if two or three meet in different places in the name of Christ, Matth. XVIII. 20; and those who are held in prisons, or forced to hide in the woods and caves of the earth for fear of enemies, belong to the Church and to the lot of the saints in light. Second, that definition is silent about true believers and virtues. And yet those magnificent promises which were made to the Church pertain properly to believers and saints, not to others. For who can be induced to believe that anything good was promised to those who hear and bring their lips to the Church but not their heart, and so necessarily hold false opinions, whether under true or false words; and that the privilege of not erring was given to them, or that at least they are so built upon the rock that the gates of hell do not prevail against them? Just as a gathering of hairs, nails and bad humours is not the human body itself, but a foul sewage of the body's excrements, so an assembly of men who are not faithful, not holy, and so not endowed with virtues, cannot be the body of Christ. Nor was it without divine will that they were compelled to define their Church in this way, which they so greatly proclaim as infallible, and adore, and which they hold more august than anything in the world. For who would further doubt that such a Church, made up of hypocrites and hidden unbelievers, errs and falls away, indeed can do nothing but err and fall away? It is more like a miracle that a herd of such swine should grunt something about faith and heaven from the mire of their pleasures and crimes.

units.la: Tertio Christianae fidei professionem & Sacramentorum usum recte equidem definitio ad Ecclesiam exigit, quia illi, qui haeresles profitentur, Ecclesia non sunt. Unde consequens est, congregationem illam, quae Ecclesiae nomine venit, ex Christianae fidei professione, adeoque ex veritate doctrinae, quae creditur, aestimandam esse. Atqui illa nonnisi in Scripturis reperiri potest. Ergo Scripturae authoritas quoad nos non pendet ab Ecclesia, sed Ecclesia se Dei vivi Ecclesiam esse probat, quando Scripturam & sanam ex eadem doctrinam profitetur. Quarto ambiguum est, quod definitio congregationem & professionem illam fieri sub regimine legitimorum Pastorum, docet. Nam legitimos Pastores vel eos intelligit, qui a Christo ordinati, & legitime vocati officium Ecclesiam recte docendi & gubernandi accipiunt: vel qui officio sic suscepto rite, sine ullo errore & defectu defunguntur. Si prius, constat sane, tum Ecclesiam pastoribus talibus subinde viduatam, Ecclesiam Christi esse non desinere: quomodo nec Israelitae Ecclesia vera esse desierunt, quando quaesti sunt: Signa nostra non videmus, non est ultra Propheta, nec est qui cognoscat, Psal. LXXIV. 10. & eo ipso quod fideles vocationi Dei per Evangelium undecunque cognitum parent, participes Christi, & interioris communionis cum ipso & fidelibus universis esse incipiunt, & simul jus se aggregandi fratrum per externam professionem adipiscuntur: tum fideles aggregatos coetui cuipiam Pastorum Ecclesiae institutionem, curam, vigilias, solicitudinem sibi jure vendicare, & viciissim illis in nomine Christi loquentibus obedientiam debere; sic tamen, ut ad eorum dicta attendere, & ad lapidem lydium verbi Divini ea exigere fas illis piumque sit, neque illis dicta sua non demonstrantibus, vel fidem simpliciter dictantibus obedire ullatenus teneantur; Regimen proin Pastorum legitimorum nec ad τὸ εἶναι Ecclesiae pertinet, nec ubi obtinere potest, δικαιοκρατικὸν vel ἱεραρχικὸν (quale Hierarchae in animo habent) sed οἰκονομικὸν & ἱεροδιδασκαλικὸν est, juxta illa Apostoli: ἐλευθερῷ ὢν ἐκ πάντων, πάσιν ἑμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα: Liber ab omnibus, omnibus me servum addixi, 1. Cor. IX 19. ac praeterea non ἀνυπεύθυνον, sed examini ac judicio fidelium, qui & Ecclesiae totius, juxta regulam verbi Divini obnoxium. Sed a tali Pastorum regimine Papatus abhorret. Si posterius, nuspiam Ecclesiae promissum est, fore, ut in perpetuum non aliis Pastoribus, quam piis, officium facientibus, nihil ultra commissum a Deo facientibus, nunquam errantibus,
units.tr: Third, the definition rightly requires of the Church a profession of the Christian faith and the use of the sacraments, because those who profess heresies are not the Church. Whence it follows that that assembly which goes by the name of Church is to be judged by the profession of the Christian faith, and so by the truth of the doctrine which is believed. But that truth can be found only in the Scriptures. Therefore the authority of Scripture, as far as we are concerned, does not depend on the Church, but the Church proves itself to be the Church of the living God when it professes Scripture and sound doctrine drawn from it. Fourth, it is ambiguous when the definition teaches that the assembly and that profession are made under the rule of legitimate pastors. For by legitimate pastors it means either those who have been ordained by Christ and lawfully called, and receive the office of rightly teaching and governing the Church; or those who discharge the office so undertaken properly, without any error or defect. If the former, it is certainly clear that the Church does not cease to be the Church of Christ when at times it is deprived of such pastors; just as the Israelites did not cease to be a true Church when they complained, We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet, nor is there anyone who knows, Ps. LXXIV. 10. And by the very fact that the faithful, wherever they are, obey the call of God through the Gospel once known, they begin to be partakers of Christ and of inward communion with him and all the faithful, and at the same time obtain the right to join themselves to their brethren by external profession. Then the faithful, once gathered into some assembly of pastors, may rightly claim for themselves the instruction, care, watchfulness and solicitude of the Church, and in turn owe obedience to those speaking in the name of Christ; yet in such a way that it is lawful and pious for them to attend to their words and to test them by the touchstone of the divine Word, and they are in no way bound to obey those who do not demonstrate their words, or who simply dictate faith. So the rule of legitimate pastors belongs neither to the being [τὸ εἶναι] of the Church, nor, where it can prevail, is it a rule of right [δικαιοκρατικὸν] or hierarchical [ἱεραρχικὸν] (such as the hierarchs have in mind), but it is economic [οἰκονομικὸν] and of sacred teaching [ἱεροδιδασκαλικὸν], according to that saying of the Apostle, Free from all, I have made myself a servant to all, 1 Cor. IX. 19 [ἐλευθερῷ ὢν ἐκ πάντων, πάσιν ἑμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα]; and moreover it is not unaccountable [ἀνυπεύθυνον], but is subject to the examination and judgment of the faithful, who are also answerable to the whole Church according to the rule of the divine Word. But the Papacy shrinks from such a rule of pastors. If the latter, nowhere has it been promised to the Church that it will forever have to do with no pastors but pious ones, performing their office, doing nothing beyond what God has committed, never erring,

units.la: necessaria ignorantibus, vel deficientibus, & quidem omnibus in locis utatur. Haec vero illa Platonica Respublica est, quam nobis Ecclesiam invisibilem asserentibus, illi objectare solent. Quinto professio fidei qualiscunque, communio Sanctorum, & regimen legitimorum pastorum non facit Ecclesiam, si sic profitentes, communicantes, & Pastoribus utentes errores fundamentum evertentes committant, tyrannidem exerceant, & cultum falsum miseant. Nam etiam Judaei Apostolorum tempore Mosen & Prophetas profitebantur, Sacramenta a Deo instituta, & legitimos Pastores ordine successionis Divinitus constituto in cathedra Mosis sedentes habebant, neque tamen eo tempore vera Ecclesia fuerunt. De haereticis pluribus idem dici potest. Sexto, Ecclesiae Papalis Alpha & Omega, regimen unius Christi in terris Vicarii Romani Pontificis, hoc est, Monarchia Papae externa, suprema in totum terrarum orbem, in quo cuncta in spiritualibus & temporalibus ex plenitudine potestatis ei facere licet, nulla ratione demonstrari, ut necessaria ad Ecclesiae essentiam, potest, ac ne quidem necessaria iis, quos Bellarminus capillis, unguibus & humoribus malis comparavit, quamvis regimen Papae ad talem Ecclesiam referri haud aegre ferimus. Romani enim Pontificis nomen ne quidem in Scripturis occurrit, & remotae illae consequentiae, quibus architecti Papatus vicariatum eum demonstrare satagunt, ad principium aliquod fidei, & Ecclesiae fundamentum constituendum, utpote quod verbis simplicissimis & clarissimis fieri debuisset, neutiquam sufficiunt; atque insuper illae incertae, lubricae, fallaces, imo fallacissimae sunt: denique gravissimum, intolerandum, plenumque horrendi schismatis facinus est, omnes illos, qui in orbe Christiano, ob mandati Divini defectum, Papae se subjici nunquam passi sunt, neque patientur unquam, aeternae damnationi, ceu victimas nil miserantis orci, devovere, & cum eodem Bellarmino hunc fidei articulum obtrudere, quod nemo, etiamsi velit, possit communicare cum Ecclesia Christi, qui non subest Pontifici.
units.tr: ...and makes use of them in all places, for those who are ignorant of necessary things or lack them. This is indeed the Platonic Republic, which our opponents are accustomed to throw at us when we assert an invisible Church. Fifth, a profession of faith of whatever kind, the communion of the saints, and government by lawful pastors do not make a Church if those who profess, communicate and use such pastors commit errors that overturn the foundation, exercise tyranny and spread false worship. For in the time of the Apostles the Jews also professed Moses and the Prophets, had sacraments instituted by God, and had lawful pastors, divinely established by the order of succession, sitting in the chair of Moses; yet at that time they were not the true Church. The same can be said of many heretics. Sixth, the Alpha and Omega of the Papal Church, the rule of the one Christ on earth through the Vicar of the Roman Pontiff, that is, the external monarchy of the Pope, supreme over the whole world, in which he may do everything in spiritual and temporal matters from the fullness of power, cannot be shown by any argument to be necessary to the essence of the Church, nor even necessary for those whom Bellarmine compared to hair, nails and bad humours, although we do not object to referring the government of the Pope to such a Church. For the name of Roman Pontiff does not occur even in the Scriptures, and those remote consequences by which the architects of the papacy labour to prove that vicariate are by no means sufficient to establish any article of faith or foundation of the Church, since it should have been done in the simplest and clearest words. Moreover, those consequences are uncertain, slippery, deceptive, indeed most deceptive. Finally, it is a most grave, intolerable and thoroughly horrible crime of schism to devote to eternal damnation, as victims of a pitiless hell, all those in the Christian world who, lacking any divine command, have never allowed themselves to be subjected to the Pope and never will, and with Bellarmine to impose this article of faith: that no one, even if he wished, could communicate with the Church of Christ who is not subject to the Pontiff.

units.la: LXII. Quid ergo de Ecclesiae idea illa, qua praeter & contra Scripturam Ecclesia vera in Monarchiam visibilem & mundanam, quae professionis doctrinae Christi, communionis Sacramentorum, & infallibilitatis jactatae praetextu quaesita, a Papa Romano, ceu supremo in terris Numine, omni Divino & humano jure calcato, impotentissime administratur, judicandum sit, abunde jam liquet.
units.tr: LXII. What, then, is to be judged of that idea of the Church, by which the true Church, sought beside and against Scripture in a visible and worldly monarchy, under the pretext of the profession of Christian doctrine, communion of the sacraments and a boasted infallibility, is most impotently administered by the Roman Pope as a supreme deity on earth, trampling underfoot all divine and human law, is already abundantly clear.

units.la: Non enim Ecclesia talis Sponsa Christi est; sed meretrix, Deo & Christo fidem fallens, & quaestum in mundo faciens, est. Nihil certe de Ecclesia tali dicitur, quod de infami illa meretrice, quae Babylonis Magnae nomine & emblemate in Scripturis figuratur, dici non possit. Nam & Babylon illa, seu mulier, magna civitas habens Regnum supra Reges terrae, Apocal. XVII. 18: adeoque coetus illustris & visibilis hominum, qualis est populus Romanus, Regnum Galliae, Respublica Venetorum, uti Bellarminus loquitur, est. Et sedet illa mulier super aquis multis, & supra Bestiam coccineam, ibid. v. 1.3. adeoque habet eos, qui magnae multitudini populorum, qui aquarum & Bestiae nomine veniunt, praesunt, sunt, quos inter unus inprimis Monarcha cum absoluta potestate, multitudinem illam hominum prodigiosam regit & subigit; cum quo Reges terræ scortantur, & à cujus fcortationis vino habitatores terræ inebriantur, ibid. v. 2. Sed quid multis? Ipsi adversarii fere ὁμοψήφως fatentur, Babylonem illam Romam esse. At non fuit Roma illa Ethnica vetus: nec erit Roma Antichristiano Ethnica sub finem Mundi. Non fuit Roma Ethnica vetus, uti Alcasar, aliique pertendunt, tum quia illa mysterii prætextu ad incestum sui amorem & scortationem neminem invitavit, sed potius militaris potentiæ præsidio homines libidini suæ subjecit; tum quia non fuit meretrix inebrians Reges & gentes terræ, ut secum scortarentur, hoc est, cultum religiosum & Divinum sibi impenderent: tum quia Bestia, super qua Babylon equitavit, ibid. vers. 7. 8. &c. non fuit populus Romanus gentilis vetus, utpote quæ Draconi seu Diabolo, gentes ad idololatriam crassam seducenti, successit: tum quia Roma vetus Ethnica non suevit ψυχὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων animas hominum nundinari, quod Babyloni ibid. XVIII.11.12.13. tribuitur: tum quia judicium Babyloni intentatum nunquam, illa subivit: Neque etiam erit Roma Antichristiano-Ethnica sub finem mundi, uti Viegas, Ribera, à Lapide aliique pertendunt, tum propter rationes similes jam allatas: tum quia opinio nova, incerta & improbabilis, neque ulla ratione nixa, ænigmati huic extricando idonea non est, quo argumento Alcasar Riberæ & Viegæ expositionem jugulat. Accedit, quòd Antichristum non Romæ, sed Hierosolymæ illi ostendant. Cùm igitur Babylon Roma sit, & Roma Ethnica non sit, Christiana certi temporis sit oportet; quia medium nullum datur. Id si verum est, uti verissimum esse, alibi demonstravimus, Babylon illa Romana Christiana vel Pseudochristiana esse nisi per fidei Christianæ professionem, & Sacramentorum usum, non potest. Sed fidei Christi professio & Sacramentorum usus purus & integer, vel impurus & adulterinus esse potest. Purus & integer Romæ adhuc puræ & integræ fuit: impurus & adulterinus ejusdem Christum ore profitentis, at fidem ejus multis modis adulterantis, & Sacramenta ejusdem utcunque usurpantis, adeóque Romæ Christianæ non integræ, sed corruptæ & Babylonicæ est. Cùmque juxta Bellarmini effatum; ut quis aliquo modo dici possit pars veræ Ecclesiæ, de qua Scriptura loquuntur, non requiratur ulla interna virtus, sed tantùm externa professio fidei, & Sacramentorum communio, quæ ipso sensu percipitur; nullo negotio assequimur, quomodo cum fucata externa professione fidei, & Sacramentorum communione qualicunque omnia illa, quæ Prophetia Babyloni vendicat, cohærere, adeóque Ecclesia Papalis sic, uti diximus, definita, Babylonis Magnæ numeros impleat.
units.tr: For such a Church is not the Spouse of Christ, but a harlot, who deceives the faith of God and Christ and makes gain in the world. Certainly nothing can be said of such a Church that cannot also be said of that infamous harlot who is figured in Scripture under the name and emblem of Babylon the Great. For that Babylon, or woman, is a great city having a kingdom over the kings of the earth, Apocal. XVII. 18; and so she is an illustrious and visible assembly of men, such as the Roman people, the Kingdom of France, the Republic of Venice, as Bellarmine puts it. And the woman sits upon many waters, and upon a scarlet beast, ibid. vv. 1, 3; and so she has rulers over the great multitude of peoples, who are named by the terms waters and beast, and among them above all one Monarch with absolute power rules and subdues that prodigious multitude of men. With her the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication, ibid. v. 2. But why say more? The adversaries themselves almost unanimously [ὁμοψήφως] confess that Babylon is Rome. But old pagan Rome was not Babylon, nor will Antichristian-pagan Rome at the end of the world be Babylon. Old pagan Rome was not Babylon, as Alcasar and others maintain, first because she did not invite anyone to incest and fornication under the pretext of a mystery, but rather subjected men to her lust by the protection of military power; second, because she was not a harlot making the kings and nations of the earth drunk so that they would fornicate with her, that is, so that they would offer her religious and divine worship; third, because she was not the old pagan Roman people, the beast on which Babylon rode, ibid. vv. 7, 8, etc., since that beast succeeded the Dragon or Devil, who led the nations into gross idolatry; fourth, because old pagan Rome was not accustomed to traffic in the souls of men [ψυχὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων], which is attributed to Babylon, ibid. XVIII. 11, 12, 13; fifth, because old Rome never underwent the judgment threatened against Babylon. Nor will Antichristian-pagan Rome at the end of the world be Babylon, as Viegas, Ribera, a Lapide and others maintain, for reasons similar to those already given; and also because this new opinion, uncertain, improbable and supported by no reasoning, is not suited to unravelling this riddle, by which argument Alcasar cuts the throat of the interpretation of Ribera and Viegas. Moreover, they point to Jerusalem, not Rome, as the place of the Antichrist. Since, then, Babylon is Rome, and Rome is not pagan, she must be Christian for some period of time, since no middle course is given. If this is true, as we have shown elsewhere that it is most true, Roman Babylon can be Christian or pseudo-Christian only through the profession of the Christian faith and the use of the sacraments. But the profession of Christ's faith and the use of the sacraments can be either pure and whole or impure and adulterated. Rome was once pure and whole; she is now impure and adulterated, professing Christ with her mouth but in many ways corrupting his faith and using his sacraments in whatever way she pleases; and so she is not an entire Christian Rome but a corrupt and Babylonian one. And since, according to Bellarmine's dictum, in order that someone may in some way be called part of the true Church of which Scripture speaks, no inner virtue is required, but only the external profession of faith and communion in the sacraments, which is perceived by the senses itself, we easily see how all those things which the prophecy ascribes to Babylon cohere with an outward, feigned profession of faith and a communion in the sacraments of whatever kind, and so the Papal Church, defined as we have said, fulfils the numbers of Great Babylon.

units.la: LXIII. Sed rectè & ordine se Ecclesiam definivisse, argumentis nonnullis probare satagunt.
units.tr: LXIII. But they try to prove by some arguments that they have defined the Church rightly and in proper order.

units.la: Nam & genus à se ei assignatum esse, quòd sit cœtus hominum, & differentiam specificam in actibus tribus propriis, professione fidei Christianæ, communione Sacramentorum, & sub Pontificis Romani imperium subjectione, positam, crepant, nulla specie, nedum veritatis. Ejusmodi enim cœtum hominum, intelligunt, qualis Ecclesiæ N.T. nullatenus competit.
units.tr: For they cry out that the genus assigned to it by them, namely that it is an assembly of men, and the specific difference, placed in three proper acts, profession of the Christian faith, communion in the sacraments, and subjection to the rule of the Roman Pontiff, are correct, though they have no basis in any kind of truth. For they understand by this assembly of men the kind that by no means belongs to the Church of the New Testament.

units.la: {elector} electorum, vocatorum & fidelium, oppugnatio, adjuncta. Ecclesiæ existens proprië Ecclesiæ est, & cui soli omnes promissiones factæ sunt, membra sunt. Vos non estis ex ovibus meis, Joh. X. 26. Non omnes qui ex Israele, sunt Israel, Rom. IX. 6. Ac licèt etiam reprobi quidam baptizentur, non tamen æquè ac electi, in unum corpus baptizantur, neque revera Christum induunt, sed fallaci duntaxat judicio hominum, qui baptizatos verè Christum induentes à non verè induentibus discernere non possunt. Est enim illis Baptismus depositio sordium carnis, sed non stipulatio bonæ conscientiæ ad Deum, 1. Petr. III. 21. Ac licèt etiam electio sola Ecclesiæ membra non faciat, nulli tamen nisi electi Ecclesiæ membra esse possunt, quia vocatio efficax, per quam formaliter actu ipso membra constituuntur, ex electione est, & nonnisi electorum est, Rom. VIII. 28. 1. Cor. I. 26. 27. Neque tamen sic omnia incerta sunt, non Pastor oves, non oves Pastorem, non fratrem frater novit; licèt verò hi se invicem non noverint à priori, uti Deus novit; at nôrunt tamen, quantum iis sufficit, à posteriori ex fructibus fidei & charitatis. Aliud enim est agnoscere aliquem Pastorem, aliud prædestinatum: aliud, agnoscere ovem communiter, aliud prædestinatum singulariter.
units.tr: The Church, understood as the assembly of the elect, the called and the faithful, is the Church properly so called, and those who belong to it are its members, to whom alone all the promises have been made. You are not of my sheep, John 10:26. Not all who are of Israel are Israel, Rom. 9:6. Although some reprobate are also baptized, they are not baptized into one body in the same way as the elect, nor do they truly put on Christ. They are baptized only in the deceptive judgment of men, who cannot distinguish those who truly put on Christ from those who do not. For Baptism is for them the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but not the appeal of a good conscience toward God, 1 Pet. 3:21. And although election alone does not make someone a member of the Church, no one can be a member of the Church except the elect, because the effectual calling, through which people are formally constituted members by the act itself, comes from election and belongs only to the elect, Rom. 8:28; 1 Cor. 1:26–27. Yet not everything is thereby uncertain: the shepherd does not know the sheep, nor the sheep the shepherd, nor a brother a brother, in the same way that God knows them. Although they do not know one another a priori, as God knows, they do know, as far as is sufficient for them, a posteriori, from the fruits of faith and love. For it is one thing to recognize someone as a shepherd, and another to recognize him as predestined; one thing to recognize a sheep in common, and another to recognize one as predestined individually.

units.la: LXIV. Ad falsæ ideæ Ecclesiæ rationem
units.tr: LXIV. The rationale of the false idea of the Church

units.la: id inprimis pertinet, quòd eam, Regni instar mundani, velut populi Romani, Regni Galliæ & Reipublicæ Venetæ, perpetuò, ad finem usque mundi, sic gloriosè visibilem esse asserunt, ut nunquam non regimen Pastorum, unius inprimis Pastoris summi, Papæ thronum & cathedram suam Romæ figentis, & sibi totum mundum obnoxium reddentis, in mundo splendeat, numquámquè adeò multitudo ejusmodi spiritualium salsissimo prætextu imperantis πατριαρχικῶς, & parentium ὑπερδυλικῶς, obscuretur & imminuatur, vel obscurari & imminui possit. Quæ non vera Ecclesiæ idea sed fallax & impia Ecclesiæ φαντασία est. Regnum enim Christi non est de hoc mundo, Joh. XVIII. 36. quia non est simile Regnis hujus mundi, in quibus visibile caput, cum pompa externa eminens, dominatur. Principes gentium dominantur iis, & Magnates in potestatem eos redigunt. Vos autem non sic. Sed qui inter vos magnus esse voluerit, esto minister vester, Matth. XX. 26. Quæ verba cùm non intelligerent Papæ, & conjicerent, Apostolis non aliud quàm ethnicam quandam tyrannidem interdici, & ipsi tamen Monarchiam externam & pomposam amplecterentur, visibilem à se excitatam Monarchiam pro Christi Monarchia excitarunt, & Regnum ejus, quod ex hoc mundo non est, in mundanum Regnum, seu Regnum Romanorum, uti Turrianus de Eccl. & ordin. Min. Eccl. lib. I. 2. appellat, transmutarunt. Neque continent se ejusmodi Regni finibus, cujusmodi Principes gentium possederunt, sed se ipsos Principes super omnes gentes & Regna, uti Johannes XXII. Extrav. com. loquitur, constituunt. Sic ergo illis Ecclesia visibilis est, uti Regna mundana, quæ Regem certo loco residentem, atque prædominantem, non sine splendore eximio, & eidem subjectos plurimos, Majestatem non comiter colentes, sed humiliter & devoto cum obsequio veneran-
units.tr: This pertains above all to the following: they assert that the Church, like a worldly kingdom, such as the Roman people, the kingdom of France or the Venetian republic, is so gloriously visible, perpetually and to the end of the world, that the government of pastors, above all of the one supreme Pastor, the Pope, who fixes his throne and chair at Rome and makes the whole world subject to himself, always shines forth in the world. They also hold that the multitude of such spiritual persons, who rule patriarchically [πατριαρχικῶς] under the most salty pretext and serve hyperdulically [ὑπερδυλικῶς], is never obscured or diminished, nor can it be. This is not the true idea of the Church but a false and impious fantasy [φαντασία] of the Church. For the kingdom of Christ is not of this world, John 18:36, because it is not like the kingdoms of this world, in which a visible head, prominent with external pomp, rules. The rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great exercise authority over them. But it shall not be so among you. Whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be your minister, Matt. 20:26.
