Since the Popes did not understand these words, and supposed that the Apostles forbade only a certain heathen tyranny, while they themselves embraced an external and pompous monarchy, they set up a visible monarchy of their own in place of Christ's monarchy, and changed his kingdom, which is not of this world, into a worldly kingdom, or kingdom of the Romans, as Turrianus calls it in De Ecclesia et ordinatione ministrorum Ecclesiae, book I, chapter 2. Nor do they keep within the limits of such a kingdom as the rulers of the Gentiles possessed. Instead they make themselves rulers over all peoples and kingdoms, as John XXII speaks in the Extravagantes communes. So for them the Church is visible in the way that worldly kingdoms are: they have a king residing and presiding in a fixed place, with outstanding splendor, and many subjects who honor his majesty not in a courteous manner but humbly, with devoted obedience and reverence.

units.la: tes, habent: imò tantò etiam visibilior & splendidior, quantò Papa Romæ dominans, quovis Rege splendidior, potentior & pomposior est, imò impotentius omnes Reges terræ eorúmque Regna libidini suæ subjicit. Sed nos Regnum Christi merè spirituale & cœleste esse, supra Loc. XIX. 104-107. adversus Judæos & Pontificios evicimus. Quin & Ecclesiæ proprië dictæ eam indolem nativam esse, ut planè invisibilis sit; atque Ecclesiam etiam externam sic visibilem esse, ut tamen visibilitas ea nec cathedræ dominantis, & uni loco affixæ sit, & gradus splendoris & visibilitatis ejusmodi habeat, ut quandoque etiam obscuretur, ac tantùm non luce externa omni destituatur, supra § XIV. XXXV. XXXVI. XLVI. XLVII. probare occupavimus, & deinceps etiam pluribus confirmavimus. Ecclesia certè ejusmodi, quæ cathedræ Romanæ dominanti affixa sensum fidei & obsequium omne eidem subjecit, nec semper fuit, quia suo demum tempore homo peccati revelandus fuit, 2. Thess. II. 2. 6. nec semper erit, quia homo ille peccati Spiritu oris Christi jam consumi coepit, & consumetur magis, ibid. v. 8. & quando fuit, atque est, & erit, semper etiam fuerunt, sunt, & erunt, qui repudiata illa pompa & φαντασία Regni fuco spiritualium obducti; soli Christo & verbo ejus crediderunt, credunt, & creditur, atque falsæ illius Ecclesiæ contradixerunt, contradicunt, & contradicturi sunt; qui etiamsi in rebus quibusdam decepti & hallucinati, soli vera illa Ecclesia sunt, cui portæ inferorum non prævalebunt, & quæ visibilis atque illustris fieri debebat in mundo, sive patiendo pro nomine Christi, sive ut adularentur ei inimici ejus, & gentes illam nutrirent, sive ut abominationibus glíscentibus contradicerent, sive ut ab errantibus separarentur, & ab illis violentiam & tyrannidem omnem experirentur, sive ut ex illorum manibus vindicarentur, sive ut viderent hostium suorum ruinam, & in toto mundo per verbum Christi liberè prædas agerent, quod & Scripturis, earúmque promissionibus, & historicis, aliisque temporum præcedentium monimentis testatum est. Quæ vera illa Ecclesiæ veræ visibilitas multis parasangis fucatæ terrestri splendore & fumo Ecclesiæ visibilitatem antecellit, & non parum hanc obscurat, atque tenebris suis involvit. Tantam enim inter visibilitatem Ecclesiæ & Regni Christi, ac visibilitatem cathedræ talis dominantis interest, quantum inter visibilitatem Pilati & cathedræ ejus, atque inter visibilitatem Filii Dei, & Regni ejus, quod per Spiritum S. gerit, intercedit. Nam quando Antichristus in Ecclesia sedet, & cathedram obtinet, quomodo deficit? Numquid à cathedra visibili, quam ipse obtinet, an à cathedra invisibili, in qua Christus sedet, quod caput non tenet, qui ipse caput esse vult? Et quomodo Ecclesia non potest participare cum Antichristi cathedra? An tenendo cathedram terrestrem, & cum ea communicando; an eam fugiendo, & soli cathedræ cœlesti adhærendo? Sed Christus non dedit ulli cathedram in terra, quam non dederit omnibus fidelibus, quorum est sedere coram Domino, & ipsum solum doctorem audire. Unus enim est καθηγητὴς ductor, Chri-
units.tr: Indeed, the Church is all the more visible and splendid, in proportion as the Pope ruling at Rome is more splendid, more powerful and more pompous than any king, and subjects all the kings of the earth and their kingdoms to his lust more shamelessly. But we have shown above, at Loc. XIX, §§ 104–107, against the Jews and the Papists, that the kingdom of Christ is purely spiritual and heavenly. Moreover, we have undertaken to prove above, at §§ XIV, XXXV, XXXVI, XLVI and XLVII, and have further confirmed later, that the Church properly so called has the innate character of being entirely invisible, and that the external Church is visible in such a way that this visibility is neither that of a dominating chair nor fixed in one place, and has degrees of splendor and visibility such that at times it is obscured and is almost wholly deprived of external light. Certainly a Church of that kind, attached to the ruling Roman chair and subjecting all sense of faith and all obedience to it, neither always existed, since the man of sin had to be revealed in his own time, 2 Thess. 2:2, 6, nor will it always exist, since that man of sin has already begun to be consumed by the Spirit of the mouth of Christ, and will be consumed more, ibid. v. 8. And whenever it existed, and exists, and will exist, there have always been, are, and will be those who, rejecting that pomp and fantasy of kingdom, obscured by the paint of spiritual men, have trusted, trust, and will be trusted only in Christ and his word, and have opposed, oppose, and will oppose that false Church. Although they are deceived and mistaken in certain matters, they alone are that true Church, against which the gates of hell will not prevail, and which had to become visible and illustrious in the world, whether by suffering for the name of Christ, or when his enemies flattered it and the nations nourished it, or when it resisted the spreading abominations, or when it was separated from those who erred and experienced from them all violence and tyranny, or when it was vindicated from their hands, or when it saw the ruin of its enemies and freely carried off spoils throughout the whole world by the word of Christ. This is attested both by the Scriptures and their promises, and by histories and other monuments of earlier times. This true visibility of the true Church surpasses by many parasangs the visibility of the Church that is cloaked in earthly splendor and smoke, and it does not little to obscure that visibility and to wrap it in its own darkness. For there is as great a difference between the visibility of the Church and of the kingdom of Christ and the visibility of such a ruling chair as there is between the visibility of Pilate and his chair, and between the visibility of the Son of God and of his kingdom, which he rules through the Holy Spirit. For when Antichrist sits in the Church and holds the chair, how does he fail? Does he fail from the visible chair which he holds, or from the invisible chair in which Christ sits, since he does not hold the head, though he wishes to be the head himself? And how can the Church not share in the chair of Antichrist? By holding the earthly chair and communicating with it, or by fleeing from it and clinging only to the heavenly chair? But Christ has not given any one a chair on earth which he has not given to all the faithful, whose part it is to sit before the Lord and to hear him alone as teacher. For one is your teacher [καθηγητὴς], Christ.

units.la: Ecclesia etiam externa & visibilis non gloriosè visibilis, Regni mundani instar; nec uni loco & cathedræ alligata est. Christus. Vos autem omnes fratres estis ; Matth. XXIII. 8.
units.tr: The external and visible Church is not gloriously visible in the manner of a worldly kingdom, nor is it bound to one place and chair. But you are all brethren, Matt. 23:8.

units.la: LXV. Quæ pro Cathedræ & Regni sui specie externa spiritualis, revera autem temporalis perpetua & illustri visibilitate Hierarchici afferunt, mera & futilis verborum Scripturæ, quin & sententiæ de visibilitate Ecclesiæ orthodoxæ detorsio sunt. Nam quæcunque Scripturæ Ecclesiæ veræ, sive proprie, sive improprie & latius dictæ tribuunt, illi ad Hierarchiam Romanam, & propter Hierarchiam Romanam ad eos, qui se totos huic mancipant, ejusque signaturam recipiunt, improbè transferunt. Quæ enim Scripturæ de Apostolis in totum terrarum orbem missis, nec non de eorum & pastorum Ecclesiæ omnium officio, ut sint instar lucis mundi, civitatis in monte positæ, quæ occultari non potest, Matth. V. 14. enuntiant, illi ad impletionem actualem perpetuam officii, & lucis atque civitatis illius non in Scripturis, sed in pompatico & mundano superstitiosorum apparatu quæsitionem sic detorquent, ut inde colligant, nunquam in Ecclesiæ externa communione, ceu magno & visibili quodam Imperio defuturos Pastores, Principes, Doctores infallibiles & irreformabiles, qui infallibili, incorrupta doctrina & ministerio actu perpetim sic in mundo luceant, splendeant, ut nullis unquam tenebris implicari & obscurari valeant. Cùm tamen contrarium Christus ipse de Pharisæis & Scribis Judæorum, quibus æquè ac Christianis Pontificii infallibilem cathedram deputant, v. 17. &c. docuerit, quando eorum fœdas Divinæ legis παρεμ-βάσεις perstringit. Taceo tot vaticinia Christi & Apostolorum, quæ alia omnia loquuntur. Quæ de portis Sionis seu Ecclesiæ jugiter aperiendis ad introducendas videlicet gentes, & illustriori modo sub initium vel finem prædicationis Evangelii, promittuntur, Esaj. LX. 11. illi ad perpetuum Ecclesiæ Monarchicæ splendorem externum, & infallibilitatis in doctrina privilegium nequiter detorquent. Quæ de Verbo & Spiritu Dei ab Ecclesia non recessuro in seculum, Esaj. LIX. 21. prædicuntur, illi ad infallibilitatem perpetuam eorum, qui Evangelium prædicare debuerant, rapiunt, perinde ac si absque talibus in visibili cathedra sedentibus, & nunquam, sive dicta sua ex verbo Dei demonstrent, sive non, errantibus, nec verbum Dei in ore Ecclesiæ unquam esse, nec Spiritus Dei super ea volutari posset. Quæ de vigilibus super muros Hierosolymæ certa temporis periodo constituendis, qui tota die & nocte non sileant, adeóque erroribus & scandalis invalescentibus se opponant, apud eundem Prophetam cap. LXII. 6. promittuntur, illi ad vigiles omnes omnium temporum N. T. eósque infallibiles & irreformabiles in externa Ecclesiæ communione constituendos & constitutos inflectunt; immemores, tot Ecclesiæ rabiosos, tot mutos canes, & rapaces gravésque lupos obrepsisse. Quos Christus Ecclesiæ Pastores & doctores dedisse, Ephes. IV. 11. &c. dicitur, hos illi continua successionis serie in una aliqua illustri sede, puta Romana; nec non eodem semper tum incorruptæ & infallibilis doctrinæ, tum inviolati ordinis, atque etiam spectatæ dignitatis splendore locum perpetim habituros fingunt; cùm tamen Apostolus non aliud innuerit, quàm quòd ministerium Ecclesiæ futurum sit medium ordinarium colligendæ ejusdem ad consummationem usque seculi; reliqua verò de varia conditione & vicissitudine Ministerii in hoc mundo, alibi, Actor. XX. 29. 2. Thess. II. 3. 4. 7. 8. 1. Timoth. IV. 1. 2. &c. expositoris. Quam Ecclesiam Deum in justitia, judicio, gratia & misericordia sibi desponsaturum, oraculum Hos. II. 19. prædicat, hanc non alibi, quàm in externæ communionis Ecclesiæ Antistitibus, vel uno potiùs individuo, Papa infallibili & irreformabili illi ostendunt, cùm de Ecclesia Catholica & electorum ibi sermonem esse, ipsæ expressæ spiritualis matrimonii dotes dubitare neminem sinant. Quæ de Episcopis sibi & universo gregi attendere, & Ecclesiam pascere à S. Paulo Actor. XX. 28. jussis dicuntur, sine subordinatione & subjectione sub uno visibili Monarcha, & non quoad internam cum Christo unionem, sed quoad externam professionem & disciplinam, ubi rectores & subditi possunt esse seductores & seducti, ut videatur ibi esse Ecclesia, ubi non est; illi ad Episcopos Hierarchas, & unumquemp piam supremum Monarcham, sine demonstratione veritatis dictatorem fidei, & Cathedram in mundo perpetim illustrem & infallibilem obtorto collo rapiunt. Quæ S. Paulus de Evangelio dicit, quòd, si opertum illud est, pereuntibus opertum sit, 2. Cor. IV. 3. illi ad Ecclesiam, nec quamvis illam, sed factionem facturientem & gloriosam, quæ sibi nomen Ecclesiæ Catholicæ arrogat, dum Evangelium è manibus illud expetentium subducit, vel commentis suis sub modio abscondit, transferunt. Neque profectò ibi semper vera Ecclesia esse deprehenditur, ubi coetus quispiam Evangelium clamosius crepat, quia videmus coetum hominum, qui Ecclesia est, sed quòd coetus ille Ecclesia fit, non videmus, sed credimus. Homines enim objectum visus, at Ecclesia fidei est. Quæ Christus de mansione sui apud Ecclesiam ad consummationem usque seculi, & de eadem per Apostolos aliósque Evangelium prædicantes & baptizantes Matth. XXVIII. 19. 20. promisit, illi tum ad congregationem πανεκλησίαν ejusmodi, quæ sensus suos subjiciat sensui unius hominis, nominatim Papæ, cui subesse sit de necessitate salutis, & illius illustrem conspicabilitatem, & ab omni errore immunitatem, nec non ad necessitatem Pastorum cum auctoritate Apostolica docentium, à quibus salus sic pendeat, ut sine eorum præconio salvari nemini contingat, violenter trahunt. Etenim promissio illa Christi dicentis: Sum vobiscum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem seculi, Matth. XXVIII. 20. primò & proprie, si emphasin intueamur, pertinet ad τῶν ἵνδεκα undecim v. 16. & S. Matthiam, Paulum, Evangelistas, quatenus iidem, ex parte, cum Apostolis adhuc ministerio suo fungentibus, officium sortiti sunt, ut partim Christi resurrectionem testarentur, partim scriberent Evangelicam historiam Christi præcepto. Quibus promittit, quòd verbum & testimonium eorum efficax futurum sit omnibus diebus, ad consummationem seculi. Ex eo autem sequebatur, ut in posterum etiam essent, qui per verbum eorum credant, Joh. XVII. 20. & qui verba ba eorum narrent, catechesin fidei & morum propagent, etiamsi plurimi id faciant non εἰλι- κρινῶς sincerè, sed ἐν προφάσει prætex.tu, & ut verbum Apostolorum à mendacio secerni possit, atque de eo triumphet: ut ita verè & unicè Apostolorum tum, cùm Christus in Cœlum ascendit, loquentium verbum ac testimonium, sine ulla authoritate alia, locuples instrumentum servandi Ecclesiam sit. Unde necesse prædicari & audiri Evangelium, Christum & ejus justitiam sed non ita, ut omnes præcones Evangelii ab errore immunes sint, à Papa mittantur, & ab ejus nutu pendeant, & ut sit congregatio talibus sensus suos subjiciens & unus talibus Pastoribus notabilibus semper notabilis. Si enim id necesse foret, nec verbum Apostolorum manifestam & eminentissimam authoritatem haberet, neque ei, quatenus ab initio in fidem venit, Christus adesset; sed, ea authoritate & credibilitate illius verbi deserta, singulis seculis alios daret, quo verbo ad horam Ecclesiam instrueret. Denique dixit Apostolus: Quotiescunque manducaveritis, &c. mortem Domini annuntiate usque dum venerit, 1. Cor. XI. 26. Atque inde omnino sequitur, Cœnam manSuram in terra, usque dum Christus venerit, & cum Cœna etiam Evangelium, quod in Cœna obsignatur, & annuntiatione mortis Christi. Sed simul prædictum est, fore ut Antichristus sedeat in Templo Dei, 2. Thess. II. 4. adeóque in medio profitentium nomen Christi sedens ut doctor & judex, verbum Dei, & potiíssimas ejus particulas, inprimis annuntiationem mortis Dominicæ, ab ore cœtus illius, cui præest, non tollat, quod impletum etiam est, sed non sequitur, congregationem quandam suos sensus subjicientium capiti alicui aspectabili, & præpositis, tanquam ab illo missis, esse Ecclesiam, & eam nunquam errare posse; cùm & ipse Apostolus declaraverit, jam illo tempore multos indignè comedisse, & convenientibus ipsis schismata (ut dicerent nonnulli, se Cephæ, &c. esse) inter eos esse, ibid. v. 18. Summa est, Ecclesiam veram externam non ex aspectabili, & externa pompa & gloria, sed ex verbo Dei, ejúsque pura prædicatione, & sincera Sacramentorum administratione, juxta indubitatam Scripturæ normam, æstimari debere.
units.tr: LXV. The Hierarchists bring forward, as the outward form of their chair and kingdom, a spiritual yet in fact temporal, perpetual and conspicuous visibility. This is a mere and frivolous twisting of the words of Scripture, and indeed of the meaning of the orthodox doctrine of the visibility of the Church. For whatever Scripture ascribes to the true Church, whether properly or improperly and in a wider sense, they wrongly transfer to the Roman Hierarchy, and, because of the Roman Hierarchy, to those who give themselves wholly to it and receive its mark. Take what Scripture says of the Apostles sent into the whole world, and of the office of them and of the ministers of every Church, that they should be like the light of the world, a city set on a hill, which cannot be hidden (Matt. 5:14). They twist this to refer to the actual and perpetual fulfilment of that office, and they seek the light and the city not in Scripture but in the pompous and worldly display of superstitious men. From this they conclude that there will never be lacking, in the outward communion of the Church, like some great and visible empire, pastors, princes and teachers who are infallible and unreformable, and who by an infallible and uncorrupted doctrine and ministry shine and gleam in the world without ever being able to be entangled or obscured by any darkness. Yet Christ himself taught the opposite about the Pharisees and scribes of the Jews, to whom the Papists, no less than to Christians, assign an infallible chair (v. 17 and following), when he exposed their foul transgressions [παρεμβάσεις] of the divine law. I pass over the many prophecies of Christ and the Apostles, which all speak otherwise. The promise that the gates of Zion or of the Church are to be kept continually open, namely to admit the nations, and in a more illustrious way at the beginning or the end of the preaching of the Gospel (Isa. 60:11), they wickedly twist to the perpetual outward splendour of a monarchical Church and to the privilege of infallibility in doctrine. What is foretold of the Word and Spirit of God which will not depart from the Church for ever (Isa. 59:21) they snatch to the perpetual infallibility of those who ought to preach the Gospel, as if the Word of God could not be in the mouth of the Church and the Spirit of God could not hover over it without such men sitting in the visible chair, and never erring, whether or not they demonstrate their words from the Word of God. What is promised by the same Prophet (62:6) about watchmen to be set on the walls of Jerusalem at fixed times, who shall not keep silent day or night, and so will oppose the growing errors and scandals, they bend to mean that watchmen of every time of the New Testament are to be appointed and have been appointed, infallible and unreformable, in the outward communion of the Church, forgetting how many raging Churches, how many dumb dogs, and how many rapacious and grievous wolves have crept in. Those whom Christ is said to have given to the Church as pastors and teachers (Eph. 4:11 and following), they imagine will always have their place in one continuous line of succession in some single illustrious see, namely the Roman, and with the same splendour of uncorrupted and infallible doctrine, of an inviolate order, and of a respected dignity. Yet the Apostle indicated nothing other than that the ministry of the Church would be the ordinary means of gathering the Church until the end of the age, while the rest about the varied condition and vicissitudes of the ministry in this world he explained elsewhere (Acts 20:29; 2 Thess. 2:3, 4, 7, 8; 1 Tim. 4:1, 2 and following). They point to the oracle in Hosea 2:19, which declares that God will betroth to himself the Church in righteousness, judgement, grace and mercy, and they show that this Church is nowhere else than among the leaders of the outward communion of the Church, or rather in one individual, the infallible and unreformable Pope, although the very dowry of the spiritual marriage named there allows no one to doubt that the discourse concerns the Catholic Church and the elect. What is commanded by St Paul (Acts 20:28), that the bishops should attend to themselves and to the whole flock and feed the Church, they say is without subordination and subjection under one visible monarch, and not with respect to the inward union with Christ but with respect to outward profession and discipline, where rulers and subjects can be seducers and seduced, so that it would seem that there is a Church where there is not. They drag this, against its grain, to bishops as hierarchs, to each pious supreme monarch as dictator of faith without any demonstration of the truth, and to a chair in the world that is perpetually illustrious and infallible. What St Paul says of the Gospel, that if it is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing (2 Cor. 4:3), they transfer to the Church, and not to just any Church but to a faction that is swollen with itself and glorious, which claims for itself the name of the Catholic Church, while it withdraws the Gospel from the hands of those who seek it, or hides it under a bushel by its own inventions. Certainly it is not always found that the true Church is where some gathering loudly proclaims the Gospel, for we see the gathering of men which is the Church, but that this gathering becomes the Church we do not see, but believe. For men are the object of sight, but the Church is the object of faith. What Christ promised of his abiding with the Church until the end of the age, and of the same Church through the Apostles and others preaching the Gospel and baptizing (Matt. 28:19, 20), they forcibly drag to a congregation of such a kind as subjects its own judgement to the judgement of one man, namely the Pope, to whom subjection is necessary for salvation, and to his illustrious conspicuousness and immunity from every error; and also to the necessity of pastors teaching with apostolic authority, on whom salvation so depends that no one can be saved without their proclamation. For that promise of Christ saying, I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matt. 28:20), pertains first and properly, if we look at the emphasis, to the eleven [τῶν ἕνδεκα] (v. 16), and to Matthias, Paul and the Evangelists, inasmuch as these, along with the Apostles who were still performing their ministry, received the office partly to bear witness to the resurrection of Christ and partly to write the Evangelical history by Christ's command. To them he promises that their word and testimony will be effective all the days, to the end of the age. From this it follows that there would also afterwards be those who believe through their word (John 17:20), and who relate their words, and who propagate the catechesis of faith and morals, even though many do so not sincerely [εἰλικρινῶς] but under pretext [ἐν προφάσει], and so that the word of the Apostles can be separated from falsehood and triumph over it. Thus the word and testimony of the Apostles, speaking truly and uniquely when Christ ascended into heaven, without any other authority, is a sufficient instrument for preserving the Church. Hence it is not necessary that the Gospel, Christ and his righteousness be preached and heard only because all the heralds of the Gospel are free from error, are sent by the Pope, and depend on his nod, and because the congregation subjects its judgement to such men and one notable man is always notable among such pastors. For if this were necessary, the word of the Apostles would not have manifest and most eminent authority, and Christ would not be present with it, inasmuch as it first came to faith; but with that authority and credibility of the word abandoned, he would give other men in each age by whose word he would instruct the Church for the time being. Lastly, the Apostle said: As often as you eat, etc., you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes (1 Cor. 11:26). From this it altogether follows that the Supper is to remain on earth until Christ comes, and with the Supper also the Gospel, which is sealed in the Supper, and the proclamation of the death of Christ. But at the same time it was foretold that Antichrist would sit in the temple of God (2 Thess. 2:4), and so, sitting in the midst of those who profess the name of Christ as teacher and judge, he would not remove the Word of God and its most powerful parts, above all the proclamation of the Lord's death, from the mouth of that gathering over which he presides. This too has been fulfilled, but it does not follow that a certain congregation subjecting its judgement to some visible head, and to those placed over it as sent by him, is the Church, and that it can never err. For the Apostle himself declared that already at that time many were eating unworthily, and that when they came together there were schisms among them (so that some said they were of Cephas, etc.) (ibid., v. 18). In sum, the true outward Church must be judged not by its visible outward pomp and glory, but by the Word of God, by its pure preaching, and by the sincere administration of the sacraments, according to the indubitable rule of Scripture.

units.la: LXVI.
units.tr: LXVI.

units.la: Sed nihil magis Ecclesiæ illius, quæ perpetuum splendorem & visibilitatem, ceu mundani Regni alicujus, sibi arrogat, vanitatem & falsitatem arguit, quàm quòd & prædictiones & eventus, seu historia, prædictionibus respondens, vicissitudines in Ecclesia lucis & umbræ, Solis majoris & minoris lucis jubare in eo radiantis, valetudinis & languoris manifestè ponunt. Si enim veritati dederimus, cum Regno Christi, seu Ecclesia etiam Regnum Sathanæ & Antichristi commiscerí; Regnum Antichristi per gradus invalescere, Ecclesiam Dei inde gravem jacturam pati, Sanctos, probos minui, humiliari, quandoque tacere, latere, vinci debuisse, neque tamen sic Ecclesiam interiisse unquam, de Ecclesiæ perpetuo splendore, simili illi, quo florentia mundi Regno potiuntur; adeóque simul de veritate illius Ecclesiæ, quæ ejusmodi splendorem & visibilitatem perpetuam sibi arrogat, concla-mabitur. Atqui ex prædictionibus constat, ibi esse debuisse triticum, ubi zizania, Matth. XIII. 30. Ibi triticum, ubi palea, ibid. III. 12. ibi ναὸν Templum Dei, ubi Antichristus in Templo Dei sessurus, 2. Thess. II. 4. Ibi Angelum Ecclesiæ, quæ Thyatiris est, cum fidelibus pluribus, cujus opera, charitatem, ministerium, fidem, patientiam, & τὰ ἔσχατα πλείονα πρώτων novissima opera prioribus præstantiora Filius Dei laudavit, ubi etiam Jezabel (Meretrix illa, significans falsum Prophetam, falsorum Prophetarum systema, & omnium illum choragum & caput Antichristum) quæ vindicando sibi infallibilitatis & judicii, quod omnes sequi teneantur, privilegium, dicit se ipsam Prophetissam, & errare facit servos Dei, scortari & idolothyta comedere, hoc est, alium Deum, alium Christum, aliud verbum, aliud fundamentum habere, & accedere ad mensam cum idololatris, cum iis, eorumque factis communicare docet, Apoc. II. 18. 19. 20. Ibi illos, quibus datum est Civitatem sanctam calcare menses quadraginta duos. Ubi ἡ πόλις ἡ ἁγία Civitas illa sancta calcanda, nec non duo illi testes, qui prophetare dies mille ducentos sexaginta propheticos, debuerunt, duæ olea, duo candelabra, &c. cum quibus Bestia sic belligerata erat, ut eos vincere, occideret, ibid. XI. 1-8. Ibi gentes Ecclesiæ nutritias, ubi Mulierilla, quæ filium peperit, & in desertum fugiens, in eo per dies, seu annos 1260. à gentibus nutriri debuit, ibid. XII. 6. &c. Ibi Bestiam priorem ex mari ascendentem, hoc est, ingentem multitudinem hominum, Ecclesiæ se adjungentium, & nomen Christi ore, non corde profitentium, ubi etiam sancti, & scripti in libro vitæ Agni, ibid. XIII. 1-11. Ibi Bestiam posteriorem ex terra ascendentem, habentem cornua duo similia Agno, & loquentem ut Draco, hoc est, corpus humanum ad nominatam Ecclesiam pertinentium, paulatim sese in capite suo, Pseudo-propheta ferentem supra fideles; ubi etiam μὴ προσκυνοῦντες τῷ εἰκόνι τῆς θηρίου non adorantes imaginem Bestiæ, & non habentes signaturam in manu dextra & in frontibus suis, ibid. XIII. 11. 15. nec non Agnus stans in monte Sion, & cum eo centum quadraginta quatuor millia, habentia nomen Patris scriptum in frontibus suis; citharœdi canentes Canticum novum; Virgines, cum mulieribus non inquinati, empti ab hominibus primitiæ Deo & Agno; Angelus per medium Cœlum volans, & æternum Evangelium prædicans, ibid. XIV. 1. 4. 6. Ibi Babylonem Magnam sedentem super aquis multis, super Bestia coccinea, habentem in manu sua poculum aureum, plenum abominationibus & impuritate scortationis, in fronte vero scriptum nomen Μυστήριον Mysterium, hoc est, Hierarchiam aliquam mysterii prætextu, dominantem ingenti multitudini hominum & ad idololatriam eam seducentem; ubi etiam sunt Sancti, testes Jesu, quorum sanguine Babylon inebriari debuit; nec non ii, quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ à fundatione mundi, esse debuerunt, ibid. XVII. 1-8. Quæ clarissima vaticinia detorqueri possunt, eludi non possunt. Nunquam enim inficetis & infrunitis suis interpretationibus Hierarchici efficient, ut Papa Numinis instar se proferens, Scripturas libidini suæ subjiciens, idololatriam imperans, aperta vi in mundo grassans, Sanctus, fidelis Dei Servus, ipsum Dei Templum, & unâ cum
units.tr: But nothing more clearly exposes the vanity and falsehood of that Church which claims for itself a perpetual splendour and visibility, like some worldly kingdom, than the fact that both the predictions and the events, that is the history answering to the predictions, plainly set out changes of light and shadow in the Church, of health and sickness, with the greater and lesser radiance of the sun shining in it. For if we concede to the truth that the kingdom of Antichrist and of Satan was mingled with the kingdom of Christ, or the Church, that the kingdom of Antichrist grew strong by degrees, that the Church of God thereby suffered serious loss, that the saints and the upright were diminished, humbled, sometimes silent, hidden and overcome, and yet that the Church never perished in this way, then we shall have to cry out against a perpetual splendour of the Church like that by which the flourishing kingdoms of the world hold power, and at the same time against the truth of that Church which claims such a splendour and perpetual visibility for itself. But it is clear from the predictions that there ought to have been wheat where there were tares, Matth. XIII. 30; wheat where there was chaff, ibid. III. 12; the temple [ναὸν] of God where Antichrist was to sit in the temple of God, 2 Thess. II. 4; the angel of the Church which is at Thyatira, with many faithful, whose works, love, ministry, faith and patience, and whose last works, more numerous than the first, the Son of God praised as better than the former; where also Jezebel (that harlot signifying the false prophet, the system of false prophets, and Antichrist the leader and head of them all), who, claiming for herself the privilege of infallibility and of judgment which all are bound to follow, says that she is a prophetess, and makes the servants of God err, teaching them to commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols, that is, to have another God, another Christ, another word, another foundation, and to come to the table with idolaters and share in their deeds, Apoc. II. 18, 19, 20; those to whom it was given to tread the holy city underfoot for forty-two months; where that holy city is to be trodden underfoot, and likewise the two witnesses who were to prophesy one thousand two hundred and sixty days, the two olive trees, the two candlesticks, etc., against whom the beast made war so as to conquer and kill them, ibid. XI. 1-8; the Gentiles nursing the Church, where that woman who bore a son and fled into the wilderness was to be nourished there by the Gentiles for days, that is years, 1260, ibid. XII. 6, etc.; the first beast rising out of the sea, that is, a vast multitude of men joining themselves to the Church and professing the name of Christ with the mouth, not the heart; where there are also saints, and those written in the book of life of the Lamb, ibid. XIII. 1-11; the second beast rising out of the earth, having two horns like a lamb and speaking like a dragon, that is, the human body belonging to the named Church, gradually bearing itself in its head as a false prophet over the faithful; where also those not worshipping the image of the beast, and not having its mark on their right hand or on their foreheads, ibid. XIII. 11, 15; and the Lamb standing on Mount Sion, with him one hundred and forty-four thousand having the name of the Father written on their foreheads; harpists singing a new song; virgins undefiled with women, bought from men as firstfruits to God and the Lamb; an angel flying through the midst of heaven and preaching the eternal Gospel, ibid. XIV. 1, 4, 6; Babylon the Great sitting upon many waters, upon a scarlet beast, holding in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the filth of fornication, and written on her forehead the name Mystery, that is, some hierarchy under the pretext of a mystery, ruling over a vast multitude of men and seducing them to idolatry; where there are also saints, witnesses of Jesus, with whose blood Babylon was to be made drunk; and also those whose names were written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, ibid. XVII. 1-8. These most clear prophecies can be twisted but cannot be eluded. For the hierarchs will never, by their coarse and foolish interpretations, bring it about that the Pope, presenting himself as a divinity, subjecting the Scriptures to his own lust, commanding idolatry, raging in the world with open force, is a holy servant of God, the very temple of God, and together with

units.la: Ecclesiam in mundo vicissitudines lucis & umbræ habere, & ex commixto Antichristi Regno & Xristianis gravem subinde jacturam pati, nec tamen interire debuisse, ex prædictionibus Divinis confirmatur. cum dominationis suæ instrumentis Civitas illa sancta, patientiæ, martyrii, charitatis exemplar, Agni in monte Sionis stantis, sequax: contra reprehensores Papæ & discipuli Scripturæ, oves mactationi perpetuæ propter nomen Christi & testimonium ejus destinatæ & subjectæ, zizania, Antichristus efferens se supra omne id, quod Deus dicitur, in Templo Dei sedens, Jezabel, Bestia habens thronum, Regnum & Imperium, Pseudo-Propheta, denique Babylon illa magna, qua cum Reges terræ scortati sunt, sedens super Bestia coccinea, decem cornua, id est, totidem Reges habens, ⲉπλαλόφῳ, civitas magna habens Regnum super Reges terræ, &c. fuerint, & à Spiritu S. sub talibus symbolis indigetati sint. Prius enim locusta bovem pariet, quàm Hierarchici tale quid comprobaverint.
units.tr: the Church has in the world changes of light and shadow, and from the mingling of Antichrist's kingdom with Christians suffers grave loss from time to time, yet ought not to perish, is confirmed by the divine predictions. Together with the instruments of his domination, that holy city, a pattern of patience, martyrdom and charity, following the Lamb standing on Mount Sion; against the reprovers of the Pope and the disciples of Scripture, sheep destined and subjected to perpetual slaughter for the name of Christ and his testimony; the tares; Antichrist exalting himself above everything that is called God, sitting in the temple of God; Jezebel; the beast having a throne, kingdom and dominion; the false prophet; and finally that great Babylon, with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication, sitting upon the scarlet beast, having ten horns, that is, as many kings, the great city having a kingdom over the kings of the earth, etc., were and were designated by the Holy Spirit under such symbols. For the locust will sooner bear an ox than the hierarchs will prove any such thing.

units.la: LXVII. Eadem verò prædictiones etiam modum, quo Ecclesia ab agnatis hostibus suis, & circumsidente Antichristo modò pressa, modò palmitis instar sub pondere surgens, sub Papali Regno conservari debuit, insinuant. Nam Antichristus sedere in Templo Dei, adeóque non inter Diabolos, merè infideles, sed in Ecclesia Dei debuit. Sunt autem Ecclesiæ bona eximia, verbum & Testamentum Dei, Decalogus, Symbolum Apostolicum, Oratio Dominica, invocatio Christi in Baptismo. Illa ergo sub Antichristo manere, & semen regenerationis salvandis omnibus præstare debuerunt. Neque unquam ab agnato Ecclesiæ hoste Antichristo aboleri debuerunt vel potuerunt, utcunque ille externa bonorum illorum Ecclesiæ specie abominationes suas tegere, & auri aliquid ab ærario Domini mutuatus; vini aliquid de prelis Apostolorum delibans, & ex lapidibus nonnullis Sionis Babylonem ædificans, fidem sibi in mundo astruere debuerit. Tum Bestia, bello duobus testibus indicto, eosdem sic victura & occisura erat, ut tamen cadavera eorum sepelire non potuerit, Apoc. XI. 7. 8. Sive duo illi testes intelligantur, qualis erat Antipas ille μάρτυς testis Dei, ibid. II. 13. sive duo testantium principia, seu, uti vocantur, duæ oleæ, duo candelabra, Vetus & Novum Testamentum, verbum Dei, in quo est μαρτυρία Ἰησοῦ testimonium Jesu, ibid. XX. 4. parum refert. Testes enim Jesu non aliter testes esse possunt, quàm proferendo ex Scripturis testimonium de Jesu. Cùm ergo hi, seu testes, seu testantium principia, Scripturæ V. & N. T. vinci, occidi, hoc est, hebetata earum per falsas, ineptas & frivolas interpretationes. (cujusmodi sunt illa verborum Christi; Tu es Petrus; pasce oves, &c.) acie, iis, qui seductioni parebant, inutiles, odor mortis ad mortem evadere debuerint; at sepeliri, ab hominum conspectu amoveri non potuerint, sed potiùs prophetare apud eos, qui retinent sermonem Dei & testimonium Jesu, in saccis, hoc est, mœsti licèt, opprobrio & sordibus obruti, debuerint; clarissimè liquet, toto eo tempore dominantis Bestiæ, verbum Dei, Scripturam V. & N. T. conservari, & publicè extare debuisse, Ecclesiæ conservandæ remedium inprimis efficax. Accedit, quòd Bestia posterior, ex terra, seu Ecclesia exteriore ascendens, ceu habens κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ cornua duo similia Agno & loquens ut Draco, ibid. XIII. 11. inducitur. Est enim monstrum simile Catilinæ, quem Cicero monstrum ex contrariis diversisque inter se pugnantibus naturæ studiis cupiditatibusque conflatum dixit. Habuit autem cornua Agni, Christi, ut agni specie simulata Draconis operationem exerceret felicius. Non potuit ergo falsus Propheta Ecclesiæ dominari sine cornibus Agni, hoc est, specie veritatis, verbo Dei, & ex eodem fundamento fidei, & articulorum positivorum, qui in Symbolo Apostolico comprehenduntur, professione, Sacramentorum usu. Atque hæc ipsa publici ejus Ministri, Pastores in ore habere, neque sine ea professione ad populum Christianum commeatum sibi facere debuerunt. Denique eodem facit Babylonis Magnæ habitus externus, purpura, coccus, pretiosus lapis, margarita, aureum poculum, &c. quæ cuncta mystico sensu externam professionem, & obtentum verbi Dei, Spiritus S. & charismatum ejus, pretiosi sanguinis Christi, Apostolorum, S. Petri inprimis (cujus opera & suprematu fictitio sic iis uti placuit, uti opera Imperatorum illorum, qui dextrum ephippii cremastera manu tenebant, dum Papa equum conscendisset) S. Patrum, Martyrum, &c. insinuarunt.
units.tr: LXVII. The same predictions also indicate the manner in which the Church, now pressed by her own kindred enemies and beset by Antichrist, now rising under the weight like a vine branch, ought to be preserved under the papal kingdom. For Antichrist was to sit in the temple of God, and so not among devils or mere unbelievers, but in the Church of God. Now the outstanding goods of the Church are the word and covenant of God, the Decalogue, the Apostles' Creed, the Lord's Prayer, and the invocation of Christ in baptism. Those were therefore to remain under Antichrist and to supply the seed of regeneration for all who are to be saved. Nor could or should they ever be abolished by Antichrist, the Church's own kindred enemy, however he might hide his abominations behind an external appearance of those goods of the Church, borrowing some gold from the Lord's treasury, tasting some wine from the presses of the Apostles, building Babylon out of some stones of Sion, and establish his faith in the world. Then the beast, having declared war on the two witnesses, was to conquer and kill them in such a way that it could not bury their corpses, Apoc. XI. 7, 8. Whether those two witnesses are understood as Antipas, that witness of God, ibid. II. 13, or as the two principles of testimony, or, as they are called, the two olive trees and two candlesticks, the Old and New Testament, the word of God, in which is the testimony of Jesus [μαρτυρία Ἰησοῦ], ibid. XX. 4, matters little. For those witnesses of Jesus can be witnesses only by bringing forward testimony about Jesus from the Scriptures. Since, therefore, these witnesses, or the two principles of testimony, the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament, were to be conquered and killed, that is, had their edge blunted by false, inept and frivolous interpretations (of which kind are those of the words of Christ, "You are Peter", "feed my sheep", etc.), and useless to those who obeyed the seduction, the odour of death was to turn into death for them; but they could not be buried or removed from the sight of men, but were rather to prophesy among those who keep the word of God and the testimony of Jesus, clothed in sackcloth, that is, though mourning, overwhelmed with reproach and filth. It is quite clear that throughout the whole time of the dominant beast the word of God, the Scripture of the Old and New Testament, was to be preserved and to remain publicly, the most effective remedy for preserving the Church above all. Add that the second beast, rising out of the earth, or the external Church, is introduced as having two horns like a lamb and speaking like a dragon, ibid. XIII. 11. For it is a monster like Catiline, whom Cicero called a monster compounded of contrary and mutually conflicting natural tendencies and desires. But it had the horns of the Lamb, Christ, so that by a simulated appearance of a lamb it might more successfully carry out the work of the dragon. The false prophet therefore could not rule the Church without the horns of the Lamb, that is, the appearance of truth: the word of God, the profession of the same foundation of faith and of the positive articles comprehended in the Apostles' Creed, and the use of the sacraments. And these very public ministers, the pastors, were to have these things in their mouths, nor could they make their way to the Christian people without that profession. Finally, the external dress of Babylon the Great, purple, scarlet, precious stone, pearl, golden cup, etc., all of which in a mystical sense hint at an external profession and a pretence of the word of God, the Holy Spirit and his gifts, the precious blood of Christ, the Apostles, St Peter especially (whose work and fictitious supremacy they were pleased to use, just as those emperors who held the right strap of the saddle with their hand while the Pope was mounting the horse), the holy Fathers, the Martyrs, and so on, were insinuated.

units.la: LXVIII. Neque intra prædictiones has restitit. Nam illæ, fatis viam invenientibus, in nervum eruperunt; quia & conservata est, dominante ipso Antichristo, Ecclesia, & iisdem, quibus diximus, mediis conservata est. Conservatam esse Catalogi Testium veritatis, quorum numerus tantùm non Libycam arenam superravit, comprobant. Etenim veræ Ecclesiæ, & cœlestis Hierosolymæ (συμπολῖται cives), sub ipso Papatu dominante (ne quid de Ecclesiis in Oriente & Occidente separatis dicam) fuerunt, quotquot Scripturam S. fidei regulam & principium esse crediderunt, & tum in cognitione veritatis, tum in mortificatione operum carnis proficere studuerunt, quotquot se Papæ tyrannidi & erroribus in fide & charitate opposuerunt, parati Deo obedire, & petentes oculos sibi ab eo revelari: quotquot Antichristi adventum metuerunt, ejus doctrinam ad S. Scripturam examinandam, & vitandam docuerunt: quotquot reformationem in capite & membris flagranter desiderarunt, & Concilium supra Papam, Scripturam supra Concilium esse, tenuerunt: quotquot propter abominationes in Ecclesia grassantes, ambitionem, avaritiam, Simoniam, impuritatem cleri, & reliquam corruptionem ingemuerunt: quotquot reprehensionem errorum Papatus exilio, carceribus, morte ipsa expiarunt: quotquot profunditates Sathanæ ignorarunt, infirmitate sua, & temporum injuria impediti non animadverterunt: quotquot in ipso agone emortuali, juxta ritualia publica, jussi, ejuratis meritis suis, soli gratiæ Dei & merito Christi confidere, ei soli confisi sunt, & Christo ac fideli Creatori suo animas suas humiliter commendarunt, licèt vel omnes hi, vel plurimi de cætero in multis cespitaverint, neque per omnia κατὰ τὴν κανόνα secundum regulam incesserint, & subinde etiam fundamento stipulas suas inædificaverint, & multi eorum non fortiter satis & cordatè se gesserint, & Jezabelem docere siverint. Nam qui & μάλις difficulter, & combustis operibus, ὡς διὰ πυρὸς tanquam per ignem, salvantur, salvantur tur tamen illi, 1. Cor. III. 15. 1. Petr. IV. 18. Novit autem Deus Agni sui & signatorum asseclas, centum quadraginta quatuor chiliadas; licet eorum pars magna oculos hominum fugerit. Quomodo Christiani tempore persecutionis Sauli in genere non ignorabantur, in individuo latebant, ideóque etiam inquirebantur.
units.tr: LXVIII. Nor did it stop within these predictions. For those, finding a path through the fates, broke out into the sinews. The Church was also preserved, even while Antichrist himself was dominant, and it was preserved by the same means we have mentioned. That the Catalogue of the Witnesses of the Truth, whose number has nearly surpassed the sands of Libya, confirms its preservation. For the true Church and the heavenly Jerusalem (fellow citizens [συμπολῖται]) existed under the Papacy in its dominance (not to mention the Churches separated in East and West). They were all who believed Holy Scripture to be the rule and principle of faith, and who strove to make progress both in the knowledge of the truth and in the mortifying of the works of the flesh. They were all who opposed themselves to the tyranny and errors of the Pope in faith and charity, ready to obey God and asking that their eyes be opened by him. They were all who feared the coming of Antichrist, and taught that his doctrine should be examined by Holy Scripture and avoided. They were all who ardently desired reformation in head and members, and held that the Council is above the Pope and Scripture above the Council. They were all who groaned over the abominations spreading in the Church: ambition, avarice, simony, the impurity of the clergy, and the rest of the corruption. They were all who atoned for their rebuke of the errors of the Papacy by exile, prisons, and death itself. They were all who did not know the depths of Satan, hindered by their own weakness and the injury of the times, and so did not notice them. And they were all who, in the very agony of death, were ordered by the public rituals to renounce their own merits, to trust in the grace of God alone and the merit of Christ, trusted in him alone, and humbly commended their souls to Christ and their faithful Creator. Although all of these, or most of them, afterwards stumbled in many things, and did not walk in every respect according to the rule [κατὰ τὴν κανόνα], and at times even built their straw upon the foundation, and many of them did not conduct themselves boldly and wisely enough, and allowed Jezebel to teach, nevertheless, those who are saved, though with difficulty [μάλις] and with their works burnt, as through fire [ὡς διὰ πυρὸς], are still saved: 1 Cor. 3:15; 1 Pet. 4:18. God knows the followers of his Lamb and of the sealed, the hundred and forty-four thousand, although a great part of them has escaped the eyes of men. Just as Christians at the time of Saul's persecution were not unknown in general, but were hidden as individuals, and therefore were also sought out.

units.la: LXIX. Sicut porro de conservatione Ecclesiæ, Papatu prædominante, constat, ita etiam media, per quæ conservata illa est, haud in obscuro sunt. Non enim Spiritus S. suos reliquit orphanos, sed in verè fidelibus ad fidei & pietatis conservationem mediante verbo Dei scripto efficax fuit. Licèt enim illud Latina lingua velatum quodammodo & obseratum fuerit, lectum tamen à pluribus & intellectum etiam est. Non enim versiones variæ aberant, ac ne Teutonica quidem, authoritate Ludovici Pii rhythmis illigata, à non paucis, idiotis etiam, licèt non promiscuè ab omnibus lecta. Nondum enim feralia illa edicta emanaverant, ne Scripturas, sine speciali dispensatione Papali, legere fas piúmque esset. Et præcipua religionis capita, Decalogo, Symbolo Apostolico, Oratione Dominica, & Sacramentorum Liturgia comprehensa, licèt diversimodè interpolata, apud totam Ecclesiam singulari Dei gratia conservata sunt. Unde quid credendum ad salutem, quid faciendum sit, constare, Spiritu Dei rectore, & verbo ejus opitulatore, poterat. Ac ne quidem, quod in corruptione externæ communionis viguit, ministerium, fructum omnino nullum ad salutem multorum obtinuit. Licèt enim illud, grassantibus passivè erroribus, summopere corruptum jam fuerit, præcipua tamen illa Christianismi capita, & articulos, quos positivos vocant, retinuit, publicèque docuit. Potuit tamen Deus, neque desiit etiam per vitiosa ejusmodi organa opus suum perficere, procurando Spiritus sui gratia, ut fideles, ceu oves Christi rationales, spiritu discretionis veritatem à mendacio, verbum Dei à verbo & traditionibus hominum, pretiosum à vili, cibum salutarem à veneno admixto, hoc est, Caput Ecclesiæ verum ab ejusdem capite spurio, invocationem Dei ab invocatione defunctorum, satisfactionem Christi ab humanis, sacrificium crucis à Missatico, &c. prudenter felicitérque secernerent. Atque id eò factu proclivius fuit, quòd corruptelæ illæ, quæ externam communionem infecerunt, non per viam oppositionis apertæ, & rejectionis fidei à Christo & Apostolis traditæ, sed per viam conjunctionis & commixtionis mendacii cum veritate, superstitionis cum vero Dei cultu introductæ sunt. Potuerunt ergo assectæ castrorum Agni, qui iis cum Spiritu suo præerat, omnia probare, & bonum retinere. Imò quia doctrina Papalis ex articulis re ipsa contradictoriis, partim à Deo in verbo ejus traditis, partim ab hominibus confictis, v. gr. sacrificio crucis & Missatico, cultu Dei & Sanctorum, merito Christi & hominum, verbo Dei & traditionibus &c. conflata erat, jam sola veritatis retentio, erroris rejectio erat. Ministerii publici institutioni subordinata fuit privata in Scholis, Monasteriis & familiis, in quibus domestica ruminatio errores publicos corrigere, & pii
units.tr: LXIX. Moreover, just as the preservation of the Church while the Papacy prevailed is established, so the means by which it was preserved are not obscure. For the Holy Spirit did not leave his orphans, but among those truly faithful the written Word of God, mediated by it, was effective for the preservation of faith and piety. For although that Word was in some measure veiled and locked up in the Latin tongue, it was nonetheless read and understood by many. There were not lacking various versions, nor even the German one, bound in rhymes by the authority of Louis the Pious, which was read by not a few, even laymen, though not indiscriminately by all. For those deadly edicts had not yet been issued, forbidding it to read the Scriptures, unless by special papal dispensation, as unlawful and impious. And the principal heads of religion, contained in the Decalogue, the Apostles' Creed, the Lord's Prayer, and the liturgy of the sacraments, although variously interpolated, were preserved throughout the whole Church by the singular grace of God. Hence, with the Spirit of God as guide and his Word as helper, it was possible to establish what must be believed for salvation and what must be done. Nor did the ministry, which flourished in the corruption of external communion, obtain no fruit at all for the salvation of many. For although that ministry, with errors passively spreading, had been greatly corrupted, it nevertheless retained and publicly taught those principal heads of Christianity and the articles which they call positive. God was able, and did not cease, even through such faulty instruments, to accomplish his work, by providing through the grace of his Spirit that the faithful, as Christ's rational sheep, might by the spirit of discernment prudently and happily separate truth from lie, the Word of God from the word and traditions of men, the precious from the vile, and wholesome food from admixed poison. That is, they could separate the true Head of the Church from its spurious head, the invocation of God from the invocation of the dead, the satisfaction of Christ from human satisfactions, the sacrifice of the cross from the Mass, and so on. And this was the more easily done because those corruptions which infected external communion were introduced not by way of open opposition and rejection of the faith delivered by Christ and the Apostles, but by way of conjunction and mixing of lie with truth, and of superstition with the true worship of God. Therefore the adherents of the camp of the Lamb, whom his Spirit led, were able to prove all things and hold fast what is good. Indeed, since the Papal doctrine had been compounded of articles that are in reality contradictory, partly delivered by God in his Word and partly invented by men (for example the sacrifice of the cross and the Mass, the worship of God and of the saints, the merit of Christ and of men, the Word of God and traditions, and so on), the mere retention of truth and rejection of error was now enough. Private instruction in schools, monasteries and families was subordinate to the institution of the public ministry, and in these settings domestic meditation could correct public errors, and the pious

units.la: lectione, meditatione, precibus veritatis cognitionem impetrare, ejúsque femina liberis ingenerare, Deo juvante, potuerunt. Neque parum innumeri illi testes veritatis, martyriis & patientia sua veritatis conservationem adjuverunt. Hoc enim Ecclesiæ privilegium est, ut morte vincat. Præterea admirabilis ea Divinæ providentiæ administratio erat, quòd errores non statim ad ἀκμήν suam pervenire, neque mox ex serpigine gangrænam, ex errore hæresin, ex hæresi apostasiam catholicam inundare, vel errores tam latè grassari passus Deus est, ut illorum recipiendorum necessitas omnibus imponeretur, atque illi in leges publicas abeuntes malum insanabile redderent, quod per Concilium Tridentinum demum contigit. Denique in agone, seu certaminibus emortualibus non defuisse fidelibus consolationem in sola Dei gratia & passione Christi fundatam, ex libris illis, quibus ægrotorum visitatio dirigebatur, nominatim eo, qui Ordo baptizandi cum modo visitandi, nec non altero, qui Hortulus animæ inscribitur, & ante Reformationem receptus utrumque fuit, clarissimè liquet. In iis enim moribundi ad solam Dei misericordiam, & meritum atque sacrificium Christi, abdicatis propriis meritis, & alio quovis modo, revocantur. Hæc media Manna illa cœlestis, qua cœlitus depluta Ecclesia Christi in mundi hujus immundi deserto conservari debuit, fuerunt. scripsit; Bertrami & Rabani Mauri errorem de corporali Christi in Eucharistia præsentia à Paschasio Ratberto recens invectum refutavit; Godeschalci saniorem Scripturæ,& S. Augustini de Prædestinatione, gratia & Libero arbitrio sententiam restituit; Caroli Calvi & Hincmari Papæ dominationem oppugnavit: Ludovici Pii Scripturam vernaculum in idioma transferri curavit: tum יפה כלבנה pulchra ut luna, quando ad dimidium usque seculi duodecimi, in distinctis phasibus suis, tempore Imperatorum Othonum, Henricorum aliorumque Papali dominationi, Hildebrandinis moliminibus,& legibus iniquis, quibus investituras cleri summo Magistratui & matrimonium clero violenter eripere Pontifices ausi sunt, strenuè se oppositi, imò Cleri Leodiensis exemplo, Papatum cum Babylone comparare, & Ecclesiæ Reformationem flagitare non reformidavit: mox ברה כחמה clara ut Sol; quando inde à medio seculo duodecimo, ad decimi quarti declinationem usque tum Waldenses aliique segreges à Romana Ecclesia cœtus instituerunt, atque sic Solis adinstar à tenebris jam deficientis, oculos carnales καυματίζειν urere, caloremque verum & Divinum, hoc est, fidem & charitatem passim in mundo exerere reveriti non sunt; tum plurimi in Papatu adhuc hærentes veritatis testes aperte inveteratam corruptionem damnarunt: denique אימה כנדגלות terribilis instar vexillifera; inde à declinatione seculi undecimi ad Reformationem usque, quando novi exercitus signifer Wiclevus, assentientibus Angliæ Rege Eduardo, Regni Proceribus,& Clero potiore, Scripturam Anglicè convertit, & eo nomine à Johanne XXIV. hæreseos damnatus, Papam esse (audi terribilitatem) Hæresiarcham, Antichristum, abominationem desolationis in abstracto, astu Sathanæ introductum, apostema Ecclesiæ, pronuntiavit, quin & cubilia doctrinæ ipsius ingressus, Papalem idololatriam, Missam, dispensationes, peregrinationes, indulgentias, merita operum &c. ex verbo Dei profligavit, effecitque, ut in Angliæ Parlamento decerneretur, ne Episcopi Romam amplius adirent; & mox doctrina eadem ex Anglia in Bohemiam propagata, & à discipulis authoritate, numero, scriptis, martyriis nobilissimis Johanne Purvejo, qui A. 1382. scribere ausus est, ante septem annos primò GENERALITER vulgatum esse à præconibus & Evangelicis, quòd Papa Romanus Antichristus magnus sit; inprimis Johanne Husso & Hieronymo Pragensi scriptis & præconio in totum fere orbem Christianum dispersa; in Bohemia Reginam Sophiam & Regem Poggiebratium consentientem, quin & Hussiticæ militiæ ducem fortissimum Zizcam, vim Ecclesiæ illatam vi armata plusquàm quadraginta millium virorum, unum in locum convenientium, pellentem, defensorem nacta est: denique ubique liberæ voces Imperatorum, Principum, totius orbis Christiani melioris, de Reformatione Ecclesiæ in libero & Christiano Concilio instituenda, percrebuerunt: quibus cùm nec Constantiense, nec Basileense, nec Pisanum, nedum Lateranense sub Leone X. institutum; satisfacerent, demum successit Dei gratia Angelus ille ex Cœlo, potestatem magnam habens, & terram totam gloria sua collustrans, Apoc. VIII. 1. & aperta jam per Evangelii æterni præconium & anathematismos hostium, clamans: Exite Babylone populi, ne communicetis cum peccatis ejus, & ex plagis ejus accipiatis, ibid. v. 4.
units.tr: by reading, meditation and prayer could obtain the knowledge of the truth and, with God helping, instil it into their children. Nor were those countless witnesses of the truth of little help in preserving the truth by their martyrdoms and patience. For this is the privilege of the Church, that it conquers by death. Moreover, this was the admirable administration of divine providence: God did not allow errors to reach their full vigour at once, nor to spread from a creeping sore into gangrene, from error into heresy, or from heresy into catholic apostasy. Nor did he allow errors to spread so widely that the necessity of accepting them was imposed on everyone, and that they, passing into public laws, made the incurable evil, which at last came about through the Council of Trent. Finally, that in the agony, or struggles, of death the faithful were not without consolation founded solely in the grace of God and the passion of Christ, is clearly evident from those books by which the visitation of the sick was guided: especially the one entitled The Order of Baptizing with the Manner of Visiting, and the other, entitled The Little Garden of the Soul, both of which were received before the Reformation. For in them the dying are called back to the sole mercy of God and the merit and sacrifice of Christ, with their own merits and every other means set aside. These means were that heavenly manna, which the Church of Christ, rained down from heaven, had to be preserved by in the desert of this unclean world. He wrote; he refuted the error of Bertram and Rabanus Maurus concerning the bodily presence of Christ in the Eucharist, a error lately brought in by Paschasius Radbertus; he restored the sounder opinion of Gottschalk on Scripture and of St Augustine on predestination, grace and free will; he opposed the domination of Charles the Bald and of Pope Hincmar; he took care that Scripture was translated into the vernacular under Louis the Pious. Then the Church was beautiful as the moon [יפה כלבנה], in its distinct phases, from the time of the Emperors Otto and Henry and the other rulers, down to the middle of the twelfth century, when it strenuously opposed the Papal domination, the Hildebrandine endeavours, and the unjust laws by which the Popes dared to wrest from the supreme magistrate the investiture of the clergy and to take marriage violently from the clergy; indeed, following the example of the clergy of Liège, it did not shrink from comparing the Papacy with Babylon and demanding the reformation of the Church. Soon after, it was clear as the sun [ברה כחמה]: from the middle of the twelfth century down to the decline of the fourteenth, the Waldenses and other separatists from the Roman Church formed assemblies, and so, like the sun already failing from the shadows, they did not shrink from scorching carnal eyes and from spreading the true and divine heat, that is faith and charity, throughout the world; then many who still clung to the Papacy openly condemned its long-standing corruption as witnesses of the truth. Finally it was terrible as an army with banners [אימה כנדגלות]: from the decline of the eleventh century down to the Reformation. When Wycliffe, the standard-bearer of a new army, with the assent of King Edward of England, the nobles of the realm and the better part of the clergy, translated the Scripture into English, he was condemned as a heretic on that account by John XXII. Yet he declared the Pope to be (hear the terror) the chief of heretics, Antichrist, the abomination of desolation in the abstract, introduced by the cunning of Satan, the abscess of the Church. Indeed, entering the lairs of his doctrine, he drove out Papal idolatry, the Mass, dispensations, pilgrimages, indulgences, the merits of works and so on, from the Word of God, and he brought it about that in the English Parliament it was decreed that the bishops should no longer go to Rome. Soon that same doctrine was spread from England into Bohemia, and it was dispersed through its disciples, by their authority, numbers, writings and most noble martyrdoms. Among them was John Purvey, who in 1382 dared to write that seven years earlier it had first been made generally known by the heralds and evangelicals that the Roman Pope is the great Antichrist; above all, it was spread across almost the whole Christian world by the writings and proclamation of John Hus and Jerome of Prague. In Bohemia the Queen Sophia and King Podiebrad agreed with it, and indeed the most valiant leader of the Hussite army, Zizka, found it a defender, repelling with armed force the violence done to the Church by more than forty thousand men gathered in one place. Finally, everywhere the free voices of emperors, princes and the better part of the whole Christian world were loudly raised for the reformation of the Church to be instituted in a free and Christian council. As neither the Council of Constance, nor Basel, nor Pisa, much less the Lateran Council under Leo X, satisfied these demands, at last by the grace of God there came that angel coming down from heaven, having great power, and lighting the whole earth with his glory, Rev. 8:1, and, with the Gospel of eternal truth now openly proclaimed and the enemies' anathemas, cried out: Come out of her, my people, that you may not share in her sins, and that you may not receive of her plagues, ibid. v. 4.

units.la: LXXI. Hæ ergo vicissitudines, multúmque variantia Ecclesiæ fata jubare meridiano clarius ostendunt, nec veram illam & Catholicam Christi Ecclesiam semper in mundo, mundani imperii instar, coruscare & gloriosè, hostibus æquè atque fidelibus ipsis, videri & splendere debuisse: & veram potiùs atque Catholicam Christi Ecclesiam illam esse, quæ non sic gloriosè visibilis in mundo est, sed visibilis tamen eo modo, iisque gradibus visibilitatis, quales Sol & Luna, modò nocte & nubilis serenam faciem abscondens, modò potentius & hilarius emicans, habet: denique non propterea Ecclesiam veram, etiam ante Reformationem, periisse & extinctam esse, quia cum Regno Antichristi in Ecclesiæ externo cœtu prædominantis conflictari, atque in eo conflictu modò à prævalida Papatus factione premi, obscurari, & tantùm non vinci; modò resurgens gloriosius emicare, vincere, conspici, debuit. Planè enim sic constat Ecclesiam nostram, quæ Reformationis tempore à Papatu separata est, non demum à Reformationis tempore cœpisse. Si enim doctrinam Christi & Apostolorum integram in ea retineri constiterit (& constat ex omnibus articulis fidei) jam dubitari non potest, quin ea ipsa Ecclesia sit, quæ cum Christo, Apostolis, & Sanctis omnibus convenit, & quæ eo etiam tempore, quo Antichristus, ceu carcinoma quoddam, Ecclesiæ corpus invasit, & apostasia prædicta eam infestam habuit, juxta prædictiones Divinas existere, & per media à nobis explicata conservari, subinde premi & obscurari, at mox iterum emergere, & emicare debuit, ac demum ab agnato illo carcinomate, & mundano atque carnali Regno, spiritualium fuco tecto, separari, & in pristinam libertatem vindicari debuit. Sic aliter res habet, aliam ergo illi Ecclesiam dominantem, & Sanctos vexantem, atque ad tantas subinde angustias redigentem, quàm Hierarchicam Papalem; aliam captivam velut, & libertate sua spoliatam, & subinde tantùm non oppressam, quàm eam ipsam, quæ à factione Papali ad summam jam impietatem provecta, & insanabili juxta atque intolerabili, discessionem fecit, segregésque cœtus instituit, ostendant.
units.tr: LXXI. These changes and the many varying fates of the Church show more plainly than the noonday sun that the true and Catholic Church of Christ has never been meant to shine forth gloriously in the world like a worldly empire, visible equally to enemies and to the faithful themselves. The true and Catholic Church of Christ is rather the one that is not so gloriously visible in the world, yet is visible in that manner and with those degrees of visibility that the sun and moon have: now hiding its serene face by night or clouds, now shining out more brightly and cheerfully. In short, the true Church did not perish and become extinct even before the Reformation simply because it struggled against the kingdom of Antichrist, which prevailed in the external assembly of the Church, and in that conflict was at one time pressed down by the very powerful faction of the Papacy, obscured, and almost conquered, while at another time, rising again, it ought to have shone out more gloriously, prevailed, and been seen. For it is plain that our Church, which separated from the Papacy at the time of the Reformation, did not begin only at the time of the Reformation. If it is established that the doctrine of Christ and the Apostles is retained whole in it (and it is established from all the articles of faith), then there can be no doubt that this is the very Church which agrees with Christ, the Apostles and all the saints. Even at the time when Antichrist invaded the body of the Church like a certain cancer, and the predicted apostasy held it in its grip, this Church was bound, according to the divine predictions, to exist and to be preserved by the means we have explained, to be pressed down and obscured from time to time, but soon to emerge and shine again, and finally to be separated from that cancer which had grown into it, and from the worldly and carnal kingdom covered with the paint of spiritual things, and to be restored to its former liberty. Things stand otherwise, so the Church that dominated, oppressed the saints and from time to time reduced them to such straits is one thing, namely the hierarchical Papal Church. The Church that was, as it were, held captive and stripped of its liberty, and from time to time all but crushed, is another; this is the very Church which, when the Papal faction had advanced to the height of impiety, made an incurable and intolerable secession and set up separate assemblies. Let them show otherwise.

units.la: LXXII. Frustra verò iidem Hierarchici hanc nobis legem dicunt, ut Ecclesiam visibilem demonstremus, cum qua Ecclesia ante Reformationem sub Papatu gemens, & per Reformationem à Papatu separata se conformaverit & univerit, cùm communionem Sanctorum & Ecclesiæ Catholicæ ipsi quoque profiteamur. Fuerunt, inquiunt, iis temporibus Ecclesiæ Christiani nominis complures, Romana, Græcæ, Ruthenicæ, Æthiopicæ, Ægyptiacæ, Habessina, aliæ atque aliæ, quarum aliqua vera Christi Ecclesia fuerit, necesse est. Cui, inquiunt, illarum Ecclesia sic sub Papatu gemens, & post ab eodem separata se conformavit, univit? Et si cum nulla se conformavit & univit, quomodo ipsa, & non potiùs Romana Catholica fuit? Sed cogimur queri de stupore
units.tr: LXXII. But in vain do the same hierarchists tell us this rule, that we must show the visible Church with which the Church, groaning under the Papacy before the Reformation and separated from it through the Reformation, conformed and united itself, since we ourselves also profess the communion of saints and the Catholic Church. There were, they say, at those times many churches bearing the Christian name: Roman, Greek, Ruthenian, Ethiopian, Egyptian, Abyssinian, and others, some of which must necessarily have been the true Church of Christ. With which of them, they ask, did that Church, groaning so under the Papacy and afterwards separated from it, conform and unite itself? And if it conformed and united itself with none, how was it the true Church, and not rather the Roman Catholic Church? But we are compelled to complain of the stupidity

units.la: fallacia eorum, qui in tenebris & confusione sua saltantes, non distinguunt Ecclesiam ratione status sui interni, quatenus est corpus Christi mysticum, vocatorum, electorum & fidelium coetus; & externi, quatenus externus, verbi & Sacramentorum usus communione sociatus, isque vel universalis, in toto mundo existens, vel particularis, in certa ac singulari natione, populo & loco collectus, est. Perperam enim sic privationem communionis externae, qualis in summa Ecclesiae corruptione contingere inprimis potest, communionis omnis, adeoque etiam internae, privationem interpretantur. Tum Ecclesiae externae unius cum alia in mundo existente conformitas intelligitur, vel ut Ecclesiae ejusdem pretiosae fidei sociae, pari potestate praeditae, jure Divino liberae, non obnoxiae ulli, cum alia pariter pretiosae ejusdem fidei socia, potestate pari praedita, jure Divino libera, nec ulli alii obnoxia: vel ut Ecclesiae servientis & obnoxiae cum alia, ut infallibili magistra & archetypa veritatis, a qua proponente verbum Dei, ejus rectam intelligentiam, fidem universam, ceu infallibili oraculo, emendicare ita necesse habeat, ut absque ea se Christi & Apostolorum doctrinae conformare nequeat. Priori conformitas Ecclesiae sub Papatu gementis, & ab eadem separatae cum aliis Orientalibus & Occidentalibus Ecclesiis tum existentibus, saltem quoad fundamentum fidei, nullo negotio probari potest, & probata etiam est; licet illa ad salutem necessario non requiratur. Justus enim sua fide, vel fide ejus, Testis vel praeconis Christi, fide recepti, vivit, Habac. II. 4. neque ideo damnatur, quod cum aliis communicare ei non licet. Sed adversarii communionem & conformitatem cum alia Ecclesia in mundo existente praescribentes, non aliam, quam communionem & conformitatem subditorum cum dominis, cum Cathedra visibili dominante, cui parere de necessitate salutis sit; verbo dicam, cum Pythagorico illo Papae, somniant. Tollant modo Cathedrae Monarchicae velamen illud, quod simile ei, quod Judaeorum Mosen legentium corda hodieque occupat, illorum pariter cordibus incubans, eorum indurat; inveteratas, inquam, & veternosas, illas de Monarchia Papali, ejusque in universum orbem imperio, cui se per subjectionem omnis anima conformare teneatur, hypotheses, & salva res erit. Ejusmodi enim cum Cathedra in mundo visibili & Monarchica consociatio, vel potius servilis subjectio ad salutem si requiritur, ostendant illi, cui visibili in mundo Cathedrae prima, post promissionem in Paradiso factam Ecclesia, Enoschi tempore in coetum publicum coalescens: cui prima post diluvium in Semi familia plantata Ecclesia; cui prima post Christum in Coelum evectum Ecclesia particularis Christiana se conformaverit? Vel enim omnibus, quae in mundo sunt, Ecclesiis externis quaevis Ecclesia particularis, vel uni seorsim se conformare debet. Si omnibus, quo pacto id fieri potest, cum nec omnes dominari possint & huic vel illi particulari Ecclesiae omnes, quae in mundo sunt, vix innotescere possint; nedum, ut cum illis in doctrina & sua con-
units.tr: and deceit of those who, leaping about in their darkness and confusion, fail to distinguish the Church according to its internal state, insofar as it is the mystical body of Christ, the assembly of the called, the elect and the faithful, from its external state, insofar as it is external, joined in communion through the use of the Word and the sacraments; and this external Church is either universal, existing throughout the whole world, or particular, gathered in a certain single nation, people and place. For they wrongly interpret the loss of external communion, which in the great corruption of the Church can happen above all, as the loss of all communion, and therefore also of internal communion. Then the conformity of one external Church with another existing in the world is understood either as the conformity of Churches that are sisters of the same precious faith, endowed with equal power, free by divine right, subject to no one, with another likewise sister of the same precious faith, endowed with equal power, free by divine right and subject to no other; or as the conformity of a Church that serves and is subject to another, as to an infallible teacher and archetype of truth, from which, as it proposes the Word of God, its correct understanding and the whole faith, it must beg as from an infallible oracle, so that without it it cannot conform itself to the doctrine of Christ and the Apostles. The first kind of conformity, of the Church that groaned under the Papacy and was separated from it, with the other Eastern and Western Churches that then existed, at least as regards the foundation of faith, can be proved without any difficulty, and indeed has been proved, although it is not necessarily required for salvation. For "the just shall live by his faith" (Hab. 2.4), faith received as the witness or herald of Christ, and he is not condemned because he is not permitted to communicate with others. But the adversaries, who prescribe communion and conformity with another Church existing in the world, mean nothing other than the communion and conformity of subjects with lords, with a visible dominant Chair to which obedience is necessary for salvation; in a word, they dream with that Pythagorean Papal ideal. Let them only remove that veil of the monarchic Chair, which lies upon their hearts as it does upon the hearts of the Jews who read Moses to this day, and hardens them; I mean those old and decrepit hypotheses about the Papal monarchy and its dominion over the whole world, to which every soul is bound to conform by submission, and all will be well. For let them show, if such a consortium with a Chair that is visible in the world and monarchic, or rather servile subjection, is required for salvation, with which visible Chair in the world the first Church, promised in Paradise and gathered into a public assembly in the time of Enoch, conformed itself; with which the first Church planted in the family of Shem after the flood; with which the first Christian particular Church after Christ was taken up into heaven did conform itself? For either any particular Church must conform itself to all the external Churches in the world, or to one of them alone. If to all, how can this be done, since not all can be under the rule of this or that particular Church, and all the Churches in the world can scarcely be made known to any one Church, let alone agreed with it in doctrine and its

units.la: tesserari possint, quin & contingere possit, ut singulae fere singulare & privum quid habeant? Sin uni seorsim, cui huic magis quam illi? Quae unius cujuspiam solida, clara ratio est? Nobis vero ratum est, tum clavim cognitionis filios Dei in N. T. a nullo homine, aut cathedra ulla infallibili repetere, cum lex Dei jam publicata, & in omnium ore & cogitatione collocata sit, Jerem. XXXI. 33. & omnes Dei discipuli a Deo edocti sint, Esaj. LIV. 13. tum Deum non dedisse ulli Ecclesiae Cathedram, nisi quam dedit Ecclesiis & fidelibus omnibus, qui sedere non coram humano quopiam doctore, Propheta infallibili & fidei magistro, sed coram solo Deo, Christo, illo doctore ad justitiam, Joel. II. 23. Apostolo & Pontifice confessionis nostrae, Hebr. III 1. Filio Dei dilecto, quem vox coelestis, Hunc audite, nobis commendavit, Matth. III. 17. XVII. 5. qui Cathedram unicam in Coelo habens, per verbum suum in terra nobiscum loquitur, debent. Aliam vero in terris cathedram infallibilem figere, eidemque per subjectionem & caecam obedientiam se conformare est post Deum, post Christum scortari.
units.tr: could be agreed upon? Indeed, it may even happen that almost each one has something singular and private of its own. But if to one alone, which one rather than another? What solid and clear reason is there for choosing one? For we hold it certain that the sons of God in the New Testament do not derive the key of knowledge from any man or any infallible chair, since the law of God has now been published and placed on everyone's lips and in their thoughts (Jer. 31.33), and "all God's disciples are taught by God" (Isa. 54.13). We hold too that God has given no Church a Chair except the one he gave to all the Churches and all the faithful, who sit not before any human teacher, infallible prophet and master of faith, but before God alone, Christ, that teacher to righteousness (Joel 2.23), "the Apostle and High Priest of our confession" (Heb. 3.1), "the beloved Son of God", whom the heavenly voice commended to us: "Hear him" (Matt. 3.17; 17.5), who, having the one Chair in heaven, speaks with us on earth through his Word. To fix another infallible chair on earth, and to conform oneself to it by submission and blind obedience, is to play the harlot after God and after Christ.

units.la: LXXIII. Neque tamen Ecclesia Evangelica, quando Ecclesiae Romanae contra diserte mandatum Christi dominantis terribili jugo collum subduxit, & a factione illa Italica, corpori Ecclesiae insidente, & pro cibo salutari venenum, pro pane lapidem, pro pisce serpentem, pro ovo scorpium ostentante, se separavit, propterea a vera Christi Ecclesia in mundo existente se separavit. Mansit enim & permanens in benignitate Dei, Rom.
