Nor can a confirmation, which is later than and accessory to the council, make it infallible; for it would be just as if someone said that a dead man cannot lie. Nor can a bulled edict, such as those of the later pontiffs, be drawn from the whole of antiquity. Rather, confirmation by edict belonged to the emperors. Thus Constantine the Great confirmed the Council of Nicaea by law, as Theodoret reports (Book II, ch. 4). The Council of Constantinople I asked Theodosius to fortify the end of its decrees with his seal. The Pontiffs of later times have seized this role also, and what once the princes, for the sake of keeping external peace and public tranquillity, did in the external forum, these men have unjustly dragged to the tribunal of conscience, just as if the consciences of men were bound by the decrees of the synod as infallible now because of the Pope's confirmation, just as everyone is bound to stand by the supreme judicial sentence of the praetor in the external forum. But we have sufficiently shown, in the place where we discussed the judge of faith, that no man, but God alone in his Word, can impose on the conscience a judicial, praetorial and principal sentence, and can bind it to obedience. Moreover, a conciliar sentence, whether confirmed by human judgment or not, either agrees with the Word of God or does not. If the former, those who pronounced it are not praetorial judges, because the sentence proceeds not from them but from the Word of God; they are faithful interpreters of the divine judgment, not making the law itself, which is the proper work of a judge, but declaring what has been made elsewhere. If the latter, they do not deserve to be heard. Therefore history teaches that even the most approved councils have erred in some matters that do not concern the chief points of faith. For the First Council of Nicaea, in its excellent canon 19, ordered that heretics such as the Paulianists and Arians, who, as some interpret, were not born but made, be rebaptized altogether; but the First Council of Constantinople, canon 7, ordered that Arians, not rebaptized, be received in the Greek manner. One of these councils must have erred. The same First Council of Nicaea forbade those who had once cast off the belt to return to military service. I shall say nothing of the Second Council of Nicaea, of Florence, of Trent, which are conventicles rather than lawful councils, and bands of an Italian faction. Scripture certainly foretold that all the inhabitants of the earth would worship the Beast (Rev. 13.8), a time when no council would be infallible. Indeed, the reasoning for all councils is the same as for the particular churches from which they are gathered. But we have established in the proper place that any particular churches whatever can err. Moreover, no mortal can judicially try his own causes, just as no one can bear witness concerning himself (John 5.31). But the causes of faith and morals are the proper concern of all men, since it concerns all men to believe the truth and to do what is right. Finally, no one denies that a general council can err in questions of fact. Therefore, to that extent, they may lack the assistance of the Holy Spirit, and so they may dominate in those matters, and may obstruct the formation of instruction and the inquiries into truth, even in the knowing of faith, so that they do not assemble in the name and fear of Christ.

units.la: LXIV. Fuit & Caput & Corpus Regiminis Ecclesiæ, quod Antichristianum diximus, sed de Antichristo ipso, qualis & quis sit dicenda nonnulla restant. Et notat illa vox eum, qui partim Christo ἀντικείμενον adversatur ceu ἀντίχρηστος hostis crucis Christi, Phil.III.18. quomodo adversarii Christi sunt, qui sanam doctrinam non tolerant, 2.Tim.IV.3. & τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀντιστατοῦσι veritati resistunt, ib.cap.III.8. quos inter unus singulariter & cum denotatione. O' Ἀντίχριστος ille Antichristus, 1.Joh.II.18. 2.Joh. vers.7. dicitur: partim est ἀντὶ Χριστοῦ pro, seu vice Christi, Prochristus vicarius Christi, quemadmodum ἀντιπάτωρ, ἀντιπροσώπος, Proconsul, Propraetor, ducis militiæ vicarius. Vocatur etiam ψευδόχριστος falsus Christus, Matth.XXIV.24. quia se Ecclesiæ pro Christo, vel loco ejus obtrudit. Quia autem nullus potest Christus alius esse, & opus ipsius facere, aut ipsius vicem implere; qui hæc sibi arrogat, ἀντικείμενος adversarius, 2.Thess.II.3. dicitur, quod convenire videtur cum appellatione מלך ירב Regis adversarii, seu contentiosi, Hos. V.13. sunt & alia ejusdem epitheta, velut סדם נבן vitis Sodomæ, Deut. XXXII.32. utpote à quo dependent alii, cum Sodoma convenientes, tanquam palmites à vite, membra à capite, ראש Caput, Psal.CX.6. ראש קדקד שער caput & vertex capillosus, ib.LXVIII.22. quia multi populi, capillorum instar, ei adhærent: רעה אורל Pastor/stultus, Zach.XI.15. Rex se efferens, & consociatus cum Deo suo peregrino, מעוז munitionum, Dan.XI.39. Ἀνομος Exlex, 2.Thess.II.8. Ἀποστάτης defector, ib. v.3. 1.Tim.IV.1. ψευδοπροφήτης Pseudopropheta, Apocal.XVI.13. XIX.20. Facit huc emblema Bestiæ, inprimis secundæ, ex quibus nata est εἰκὼν θηρίου imago Bestiæ, quæ imaginem Christi refert, ibid.XIII.11. &c. Civitas verò illa, & corpus, in quo, & cui dominatur Antichristus nomine Tyri, Esaj. XXIII.1. &c. Sodomæ & Ægypti, Apoc.XI.8. Babylonis, & Babylonis magnæ, ib.XVII. XVIII. nominibus venit.
units.tr: LXIV. There was both a head and a body of the ecclesiastical government that we have called Antichristian. But some things still need saying about Antichrist himself: what sort of person he is and who he is. The name denotes one who partly opposes [ἀντικείμενον] Christ, as an enemy [ἀντίχρηστος] of the cross of Christ (Phil. 3:18), as those are adversaries of Christ who will not endure sound doctrine (2 Tim. 4:3), and who resist the truth [τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀντιστατοῦσι] (ibid. 3:8). Among these one is singled out with a special designation: that Antichrist [Ἀντίχριστος] (1 John 2:18; 2 John v. 7). He is partly in the place of [ἀντὶ Χριστοῦ] Christ, that is, in the stead or on behalf of Christ, a vicar of Christ, just as ἀντιπάτωρ [antipatōr] and ἀντιπροσώπος [antiprosōpos] mean a proconsul, a propraetor, a deputy of a military leader. He is also called a false Christ [ψευδόχριστος] (Matt. 24:24), because he thrusts himself upon the Church in place of Christ or instead of him. But since no one can be another Christ, or do his work, or fill his place, the one who claims these things for himself is called an adversary [ἀντικείμενος] (2 Thess. 2:3). This seems to agree with the title King Jareb [מלך ירב], that is, the king who is an adversary or a contender (Hos. 5:13). There are also other epithets of the same kind, such as the vine of Sodom [גפן סדם] (Deut. 32:32), since others depend on him and agree with Sodom, as branches on a vine and members on a head. He is the head [ראש] (Ps. 110:6), the crown and hairy scalp [קדקד שער] (Ps. 68:22), because many peoples cling to him like hair. He is the foolish shepherd [רעה אויל] (Zech. 11:15), a king who exalts himself and is allied with his foreign god, a fortress of fortresses [מעוז] (Dan. 11:39). He is lawless [Ἄνομος] (2 Thess. 2:8), a defector [Ἀποστάτης] (ibid. v. 3; 1 Tim. 4:1), a false prophet [ψευδοπροφήτης] (Rev. 16:13; 19:20). To this belongs the emblem of the beast, chiefly the second beast, from which the image of the beast [εἰκὼν θηρίου] arose, which imitates the image of Christ (Rev. 13:11, etc.). The city and body in which and over which Antichrist rules come under names such as Tyre (Isa. 23:1, etc.), Sodom and Egypt (Rev. 11:8), and Babylon, and Great Babylon (Rev. 17–18).

units.la: LXV. Sicut Messiæ seu Christi notitiam duo absolvunt, idea Messiæ, & ejusdem ad subjectum suum Jesum Nazarenum, relatio: ita duo de Antichristo, idea & characteres genuini ejus, & ejusdem ad subjectum suum applicatio, adeóque qualis sit Antichristus, & quis sit, penitius cognoscenda sunt. Sicut verò in quæstione de Messia, Christo, Judæi à Christianis tam in thesi, quàm in hypothesi dissident: ita Pontificii in quæstione de Antichristo utrobique ab orthodoxis discrepant. Convenit Judæis cum Pontificiis, quòd hi in pietatis, illi in impietatis mysterio nihil fere mysticum, sed omnia pinguia, crassa & carnalia somniant. Oportuit enim Judæos, qui Christum abnegant, & Antichristi sectatores simili cæcitate percuti, atque ea ipsa cæcitas veritatem Prophetiæ probat. Rursus ut ante Christi in carnem adventum pii Israelitæ ejus officia & beneficia subobscurius noverunt, pleniore & clariore singularium circumstantiarum notitia in Christianæ Ecclesiæ ævum dilata: sic ante revela-
units.tr: LXV. Just as two things make up our knowledge of the Messiah or Christ: the idea of the Messiah, and the relation of that idea to its subject, Jesus of Nazareth, so two things must be known more deeply about Antichrist: his genuine idea and characteristics, and the application of these to his subject, and so what sort of Antichrist he is and who he is. But just as the Jews and Christians disagree about the Messiah, Christ, both in theory and in application, so the Papists differ from the orthodox on the question of Antichrist in both respects. The Jews agree with the Papists in this, that the Papists in the mystery of godliness and the Jews in the mystery of impiety dream up almost nothing mystical, but everything gross, crude and carnal. For it was fitting that the Jews, who deny Christ, and the followers of Antichrist should be struck with a similar blindness, and that very blindness proves the truth of prophecy. Again, just as before the coming of Christ in the flesh the pious Israelites knew his offices and benefits somewhat obscurely, and a fuller and clearer knowledge of the particular circumstances was revealed in the age of the Christian Church, so before Antichrist was revealed,

units.la: tum Antichristum prisci Ecclesiæ doctores multa conjectarunt potius, quasi in tenebris palpantes, quàm perspicuè viderunt, quæ posteris ex eventu, qui vaticiniorum certissimus interpres est, evidentissima sunt. Ac proin Patrum in hoc argumento sublaestam fidem & authoritatem esse, ipsimet adversarii nulli diffitentur.
units.tr: the early teachers of the Church conjectured many things, groping as it were in the dark, rather than seeing them clearly. Those things are most evident to posterity from the event, which is the most certain interpreter of prophecies. Accordingly, the adversaries themselves do not deny that the Fathers' faith and authority on this subject are slight.

units.la: LXVI. Genuini Antichristi veram ideam ejusdem definitio pandit. Est autem Antichristus, qualem Apostoli nobis describunt, vi nominis & attributorum ejus. Vicarius simul & Adversarius Christi, qui speciem ferens amici Christi, & vicarii ejusdem, lege ejusdem excussa, ab eodem deficit, & se eidem opponit, efferens se super omne, quod Deus vel Augustum dicitur, ipsùmque adeò Christum, tum quoad ejus officia, tum quoad ejus regimen, sedens quippe vice Christi in Templo Dei, & demonstrans se ipsum, quòd Deus sit; homo peccati, meretrix, mater fornicationum cum Regibus & incolis terræ, filius perditionis & Apollyon, sibi commeatum ad Ecclesiam faciens juxta operationem Sathanæ in omni potentia, & signis & prodigiis mendacii, & in omni deceptione iniquitatis, in iis, qui pereunt, revelatus, amoto eo, qui diu detinebat eum, ne plenius agnosceretur, & consumptus atque consumendus Spiritu oris Christi, & abolendus in adfulgentia praesentiæ ejus. Quæ totidem fere verba Spiritus S. 2.Thessal.II.3–11. 1.Joh.II.18.22. Apoc.XVII.1.&c. sunt.
units.tr: LXVI. The definition of Antichrist sets forth the true idea of the genuine Antichrist. He is what the Apostles describe to us, according to the force of his name and attributes: at once the vicar and the adversary of Christ. Bearing the appearance of a friend of Christ and his vicar, he, having shaken off the law of Christ, falls away from him and sets himself against him, exalting himself above everything that is called God or Augustus, and above Christ himself, both as to his offices and as to his rule. For he sits in the Temple of God in the place of Christ, showing himself that he is God; the man of sin, the harlot, the mother of fornications with the kings and inhabitants of the earth, the son of perdition and Apollyon, making for himself a way into the Church according to the working of Satan, in all power, and with signs and wonders of lies, and in all the deception of iniquity, revealed among those who perish; with him who long restrained him removed, so that he would not be more fully recognised, and consumed and to be consumed by the Spirit of the mouth of Christ, and to be abolished by the brightness of his presence. These are almost the same words as the Holy Spirit uses in 2 Thess. 2:3–11, 1 John 2:18, 22, Rev. 17:1, etc.

units.la: LXVII. Characteres igitur & γνωσιτικά Antichristi sunt, quòd vice Christi fungi se profitetur, quippe Ἀντίχριστος Vicarius Christi λεγόμενος: quòd sub hoc schemate Christo adversatur, quippe Ἀντικείμενος Adversarius Christi, 2.Thess.II.4. Quòd Christo adversatur negando, quòd Jesus sit Christus, & venerit in carnem, 1.Joh.IV.3. intervertendo & rapiendo id quod Christi est, negans quòd Jesus sit Christus, ibid.II.22. adeóque id omne, quod Christi nomen involvit, & propter quod ea Deo Patre unctus est; involando ejus tum Prophetiam, quia est ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης ille Pseudo-Propheta, Apoc.XVI.13. Ἀποστάτης defector, 2.Thess.II.3. 1.Tim.IV.1. à doctrina Christi; & author novæ doctrinæ, quam velut Dei verbum obtrudit; & Ἀνομος Exlex, 2.Thess.II.8. quia calcata lege Christi novam legem molitus est: tum Sacerdotium, quia negat Christum venisse in carnem, ut videlicet salvaret oblato unico & cruento sacrificio, peccatores, 1.Joh.IV.3. 1.Tim.I.15. tum Regnum, quia se effert, ceu Rex & dominus ipse, supra omne quod Deus & Augustum dicitur, & sedet in Templo Dei, tanquam Deus, demonstrans se ipsum, quòd Deus sit, ceu Deus, Rex & dominus Ecclesiæ, 2.Thess. II.4. quatenus corpus, cui incubat, communium signorum & quasi Sacramentorum cogulo cum eo coagmentatum est, & ab infirmioribus membris pro capite habetur; & caput est membrorum suorum pereuntium. Quòd est ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας homo peccati, ib. v.3. quatenus non tantum ipse nil nisi ἁμαρτωλὸς peccator, perinde ut gentiles, qui nil nisi peccant, & ideò κατ' ἐξοχὴν ἁμαρτωλοί peccatores, Matth.XXVI.45. Rom.III.7. Gal.II.15. dicuntur; sed etiam author peccandi aliis est, peccata quædam crassiora laudando, legibus latis illis occasionem præbendo; permittendo
units.tr: LXVII. The characters and marks of knowledge [γνωσιτικά] of Antichrist are therefore these: that he professes to act in the place of Christ, being called [λεγόμενος] Antichrist, the vicar of Christ. Under this guise he opposes Christ, being the opponent [ἀντικείμενος] of Christ (2 Thess. 2:4). He opposes Christ by denying that Jesus is the Christ and that he came in the flesh (1 John 4:3). He subverts and seizes what belongs to Christ, denying that Jesus is the Christ (ibid. 2:22), and so everything that the name of Christ includes, and on account of which he was anointed by God the Father. He does this by assailing his prophetic office, since he is that false prophet [ψευδοπροφήτης] (Rev. 16:13), a defector [ἀποστάτης] (2 Thess. 2:3; 1 Tim. 4:1) from the doctrine of Christ, and the author of a new doctrine, which he thrusts forward as if it were the Word of God. He is lawless [ἄνομος] (2 Thess. 2:8), because having trampled upon the law of Christ he has devised a new law. He assails his priestly office, since he denies that Christ came in the flesh to save sinners by offering a single bloody sacrifice (1 John 4:3; 1 Tim. 1:15). He assails his kingly office, since he exalts himself as king and lord above everything that is called God or Augustus, and sits in the Temple of God as if he were God, showing himself that he is God, as God, king and lord of the Church (2 Thess. 2:4). Inasmuch as the body upon which he sits is joined with him in a clot of common signs and, as it were, of sacraments, and is regarded by the weaker members as the head, he is the head of his own perishing members. He is the man of sin [ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας] (ibid. v. 3), in that he is not merely himself nothing but a sinner [ἁμαρτωλός], like the Gentiles who do nothing but sin, and so are called sinners par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν ἁμαρτωλοί] (Matt. 26:45; Rom. 3:7; Gal. 2:15); but he is also the author of sin to others, commending certain grosser sins, giving occasion for them by the laws he has enacted, and permitting

units.la: Regiminis Antichristiani author Antichristus est Vox Antichristi, & synonymæ explicantur.
units.tr: The author of the Antichristian government is Antichrist. The name Antichrist and its synonyms are explained.

units.la: Gemina de Antichristo quaestio est, qualis sit, & quis sit? tendo atrocissima quæque: & υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας filius perditionis, ibid. vocatur; ut & ᾿Απολλυων Apollyon perdens, Apoc. IX. 11. non passivè duntaxat, quo sensu etiam filius ille prodigus ἀπο-λωλώς, perditus, Luc. XV. 32. & Judas filius perditionis dicitur, Joh. XVII. 12. sed ἐνεργητικῶς activè, quia se ipsum & alios perdit: quòd sedes ejus est in Templo, Ecclesia Christi, cui, Dei & Christi instar, dominatur, 2. Thess. II. 4. & quidem in septem montibus, Apoc. XVII. 9. qui non alibi quàm in civitate ἐπτὰ λόφῳ septicolli Romana ostendi possunt; & in civitate magna, quæ Regnum habet super Reges terræ, quæque nisi Roma intelligi non potest, ib. v. 18. quòd mater est fornicationum & abominationum terræ, idololatriæ & impuritatis omnis, ib. v. 5. quòd plena est blasphemiis, ib. v. 3. quòd crudelis est, inebrians se sanguine testium Jesu, ib. v. 6. quòd φαρμακείᾳ incantatione, magia multiplice seduxit gentes, ib. XVIII. 23. Circæo abominationum poculo inebrians, dementans, ib. XVII. 2. 4. quòd non statim agnosci, sed operante diu mysterio iniquitatis demum renato, qui tyrannidem ejus hactenus impediebat, κατέχων detinente revelari debuit, 2. Thess. II. 7. quòd progressus Regni ejus secundum operationem Sathanæ in omni potentia, signis & prodigiis mendacii fieri debuit, ib. v. 9. quòd spiritu oris Christi consumi, & in affulgentia ejus præsentiæ aboleri debuit & debet, ib. v. 8. quòd denique eidem tribuitur certum corpus, ἀπολυμένοι pereuntes, quia amorem veritatis non receperunt, ut salvarentur, quibus Deus erroris efficaciam misit, ut credant mendaciis, 2. Thess. II. 10. 11. quique etiam Bestiæ meretricem Babylonicam portantis, eique subjectæ nomine venit, Apoc. XVII. 3. 7. 8. Hi Antichristi characteres & gnorismata, verbis Spiritus S. expressa, omni exceptione majora sunt, neque ampliorem explicationem merentur.
units.tr: There is a twofold question about Antichrist: what sort of man he is, and who he is. Aiming at the most atrocious things, he is called the son of perdition [υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας] (ibid.), and also Apollyon, the destroyer [Ἀπολλύων] (Rev. 9:11). This is not merely in the passive sense, in which the prodigal son is lost [ἀπολωλώς] (Luke 15:32), and Judas is called the son of perdition (John 17:12), but in the active sense [ἐνεργητικῶς], because he destroys himself and others. His seat is in the Temple, the Church of Christ, over which he rules in the manner of God and Christ (2 Thess. 2:4). He is indeed on seven mountains (Rev. 17:9), which can be shown nowhere but in the seven-hilled [ἐπτὰ λόφῳ] city of Rome; and he is in the great city which has dominion over the kings of the earth (ibid. v. 18), which cannot be understood as anything but Rome. He is the mother of fornications and abominations of the earth, of idolatry and of all impurity (ibid. v. 5). He is full of blasphemies (ibid. v. 3). He is cruel, drunk with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus (ibid. v. 6). By sorcery [φαρμακεία], by enchantment and manifold magic, he has seduced the nations (Rev. 18:23). He makes people drunk, and drives them mad, with the Circean cup of abominations (Rev. 17:2, 4). He was not to be recognised at once, but was to be revealed only when the mystery of iniquity had long been at work, and when he who had until then been restraining his tyranny was taken out of the way [κατέχων] (2 Thess. 2:7). The progress of his kingdom was to occur according to the working of Satan in all power, signs and lying wonders (ibid. v. 9). He was to be, and is to be, consumed by the Spirit of the mouth of Christ and abolished by the brightness of his presence (ibid. v. 8). Finally, a definite body is assigned to him: those who are perishing [ἀπολλύμενοι], because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved; for this reason God sends them a working of error, that they should believe lies (2 Thess. 2:10–11). He is also named in connection with the beast that carries the Babylonian harlot and is subject to her (Rev. 17:3, 7, 8). These characters and marks of Antichrist, expressed in the words of the Holy Spirit, are beyond all exception, and do not deserve any fuller explanation.

units.la: LXVIII. Sed adversarii Antichristum occultari, & in impietate Antichristiana se indurantes, Antichristi falsam ideam, ne agnosci ab iis, quibus ille dominatur, posset, commenti sunt.
units.tr: LXVIII. But the opponents, to keep Antichrist hidden and to harden themselves in Antichristian impiety, have devised a false idea of him, so that he could not be recognised by those over whom he rules. a false idea

units.la: Nam gente Judæorum ex Tribu Dan oriundum; singularem & unam numero personam; pro Messia se venditaturum, spatio trium & dimidii annorum Templum Hierosolymitanum instauraturum, orbemque reliquum subacturum, usque dum à Christo in monte oliveti vincatur & conficiatur, fingunt. Quæ nullo Scripturarum præsidio suffulta, Patrum quorundam, experientiæ & eventus luce adhuc carentium incertis ariolationibus innituntur. Egredi enim debuit ἐξ ἡμῶν ex nobis, ex Ecclesia Christiana, 1. Joh. II. 19. Cumque Antichristus describatur ut ἀποστάτης defector, cujus ἀποστασία defectio erit à fide, 2. Thess. II. 3. 1. Tim. IV. 1. multum certè abest, ut gente & religione Judæus agnoscatur. Nam qui inter Judæos, ex Judæis, è tribu Dan, in civitate Babyloniæ Nearda, uti illi asserunt, nasciturus est; qui circumcisus, qui Judæis, ipsum excipere paratis, & religioni Judaicæ totus erit addictus, quinam ille à fide, quam nunquam susceperit, deficere, & apostasiæ accusari poterit? Omnino igitur Antichristus Christi nomen & doctrinam, saltem in speciem, profiteatur, Agnique cornua gerat, & sermonem ementiatur, necesse est, ut, Judæ instar, amicitiæ obtentu facilius eum prodat.
units.tr: For they imagine him to be a Jew by nation, of the tribe of Dan; a single person, one in number; that he will pass himself off as the Messiah, will rebuild the Temple at Jerusalem within three and a half years, and will subdue the rest of the world until Christ overcomes and destroys him on the Mount of Olives. These claims have no support in Scripture. They rest on the uncertain guesses of certain Fathers, who lacked the light of experience and of the outcome. For he was to go out [ἐξ ἡμῶν] from us, from the Christian Church, 1 John 2:19. And since Antichrist is described as a [ἀποστάτης] defector, whose [ἀποστασία] defection will be from the faith, 2 Thess. 2:3; 1 Tim. 4:1, it is certainly far from the case that he should be recognised as a Jew by nation and religion. For how could one who is to be born among the Jews, of the Jews, of the tribe of Dan, in the city of Nearda in Babylonia, as they claim, who will be circumcised and wholly devoted to the Jewish religion, which is ready to receive him, be accused of falling away from a faith he never embraced? Antichrist must, therefore, at least in appearance, profess the name and doctrine of Christ, and wear the lamb's horns and feign his speech, so that, like Judas, he may betray more easily under the pretext of friendship.

units.la: Neque etiam una numero, seu singularis, verùm una statu, in quo, perinde ut in Imperio mundano, successores sunt, persona est. Neque enim uni & singulari personæ conveniunt, quæ Scriptura Antichristo tribuit. S. Johannes certè quamvis τὸν Ἀντίχριστον eximiè consideret, intelligit tamen πολλοὺς Ἀντιχρίστους ad idem genus pertinere, dicens: Sicut audivistis, quòd ὁ Ἀντίχριστος Ille Antichristus eximius venit, & nunc multi Antichristi facti sunt, 1. Joh. II. 18. Non ergo in uno homine prædictio illa de Antichristo absolvitur. Satis clarè enim S. Johannes indicat, se Antichristum & collectivè intelligere, quia dicit, multos Antichristos factos esse; & eximit, quia dicit; jam in mundo esse, ib. cap. IV. 3. sic tamen ut venturus sit, scilicet ἐν ἀνομίᾳ lua. Sed & Antichristo distinctæ periodi tribuuntur, nempe ἐν μυστηρίῳ in mysterio, ἐν ἀποκαλύψει in revelatione, in eo quòd ἀναλίσκεται consumitur, & in eo quòd καταργεῖται aboletur in affulgentia adventus Christi, 2. Thess. II. 7. 8. quæ tam diversa uno homini non competunt. Natus Apostolorum tempore, demum etiam amoto eo, qui detinebat, revelari debuit, & in affulgentia præsentiæ seu adventus Christus aboleri, ib. v. 7. 8. debet. Facit huc gloriatio illa meretricis: Sedeo regina, & vidua non sum, & luctum non videbo, Apoc. XVIII. 7. quæ verba non recens arreptæ, sed diuturna possessione stabilitæ & communitæ tyrannidi conveniunt.
units.tr: Nor is he a single person, one in number, but one in office, in which, as in a worldly empire, there are successors. The things Scripture attributes to Antichrist do not fit one individual. St John, though he considers the Antichrist in an eminent sense, nevertheless understands that many Antichrists belong to the same kind, saying: "As you have heard that [ὁ Ἀντίχριστος] the Antichrist is coming, and now many Antichrists have arisen," 1 John 2:18. The prophecy about Antichrist is therefore not fulfilled in one man. For St John indicates quite clearly that he understands Antichrist collectively, since he says that many Antichrists have come, and individually, since he says already in the world, ib. 4:3, yet in such a way that he is still to come, namely [ἐν ἀνομίᾳ] in lawlessness. But distinct periods are also assigned to Antichrist: [ἐν μυστηρίῳ] in mystery, [ἐν ἀποκαλύψει] in revelation, in that he is [ἀναλίσκεται] consumed, and in that he is [καταργεῖται] abolished at the brightness of Christ's coming, 2 Thess. 2:7, 8. Such different things do not belong to one man. Born in the time of the apostles, he was at last to be revealed once the one who restrained had been removed, and Christ was to abolish him in the brightness of his presence or coming, ib. vv. 7, 8. To this belongs the boast of the harlot: "I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no mourning," Rev. 18:7. These words suit not a tyranny newly seized, but one established and fortified by long possession.

units.la: Planè sicut prior Bestia æternæ urbis & imperii supercilio tumebat, non certè in ipso utriusque conditu, sed post aliquot demum annorum centurias. Et Antichristi fore statum, personis pluribus sibi succedentibus constantem, abundè etiam illud comprobat, quòd non solùm princeps est ejus Regni, quod Apocalypsis Bestiam primam vocat, & primatum obtinet inter Pseudoprophetas Bestiæ secundæ, Apoc. XIII. quod Regnum utriusque Bestiæ diutiùs quàm unus singularis homo, stabit; & Regnum ejus per Regnum æternum, à cujus mixtura Regnum divisum dicitur, in statua Danielis significatur; sed etiam civitas magna habens Regnum in Reges terræ, ib. XVII. 18. XVIII. 18. vocatur. Breviuscula proin etiam nimis est Antichristi duratio, quam spatio trium & dimidii annorum definiunt.
units.tr: Just as the former Beast swelled with the pride of the eternal city and empire, certainly not at the founding of either, but only after some centuries, so too the state of Antichrist, persisting through several successive persons, is amply confirmed by the fact that he is not only the prince of that kingdom which the Apocalypse calls the first Beast, and holds the primacy among the false prophets of the second Beast, Rev. 13, a kingdom which will endure longer than any single man; his kingdom is also signified in the statue of Daniel by the eternal kingdom, from whose mixture the divided kingdom is said to come. He is also called the great city having a kingdom over the kings of the earth, ib. 17:18; 18:18. The duration of Antichrist which they fix at three and a half years is therefore far too short.

units.la: Sicut enim Christus ab initio mundi & Ecclesiæ primordio mysterium pietatis tam per se, licèt nondum in carne patefactus, quàm per servos suos promovit: ita & Antichristus mox ab initio Ecclesiæ Christianæ mysterium impietatis aggressus est per administros suos; quamvis personam illam, sive primarium myst am in statu suo adhuc latentem, primis illis temporibus demonstrare non valeamus. Nam ut Johanni, Antichristum jam tum venisse, affirmanti: sic Paulo, tum revelatum fuisse neganti, 1. Joh. II. 18. IV. 3. 2. Thess. II. 6. ex æquo credimus. Aliud nativitatis, aliud adolescentiæ, aliud virtus roboris & revelationis Antichristi tempus est. Sicut non simul conceptum, fotum, formatum & natum est monstrum hoc horrendum, informe ingenii, sic nec mysterii sui omnes statim ab ipso ortu, numeros implevit, ungues que & cornua priùs accepit & aptavit, quàm ad pugnam ostendit & ex-
units.tr: For just as Christ, from the beginning of the world and the dawn of the Church, advanced the mystery of godliness, both in himself, though not yet revealed in the flesh, and through his servants, so Antichrist, straight from the beginning of the Christian Church, has attacked the mystery of iniquity through his agents, although we cannot point out that person, or the chief mystery, still hidden in its state, in those first times. For as John affirmed that Antichrist had already come, so Paul denied that he had then been revealed, 1 John 2:18; 4:3; 2 Thess. 2:6. We believe both with equal reason. The time of birth is one thing, the time of youth another, and the time of the strength and revelation of Antichrist yet another. As this horrible monster of unformed nature was not conceived, nourished, formed and born all at once, so too it did not fill out all its numbers from the very origin; it first received and fitted its claws and horns, before it displayed itself for battle and

units.la: Idea falsa Antichristi refellitur. & exeruit. Si veniet ad Judæos magnus ille Antichristus, & ipse Judæus, & spatio trium & dimidii anni Hierosolymæ Templum instaurabit, atque inde orbem totum subiget, vel id faciet ante conversionem Judæorum, vel post eam. Si post eam, tum Judæi Circumcisionem non reciperent. Et prædixit Christus, prædicationem universalem Evangelii esse signum τέλος finis mundi, Matth. XXIV. 14. Paulus quoque ἀποστασίαν assumptionem Judæorum fore ζωὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν vitam ex mortuis, adeóque prodromum resurrectionis mortuorum, Rom. XI.15. Sic ergo foret πρώτως induratio post ἀποστασίαν assumptionem, cùm tamen induratio cessatura post intrantem multitudinem gentium, ib.XI.25. dicatur. Si ante eam, non constabit, quod dicunt Pontificii, Antichristum 45. diebus ante finem mundi moriturum. Quomodo enim Judæi paucis adeò diebus converterentur? quo cum Ecclesiæ, & aliarum gentium fructu? Etsi Antichristus unà cum Judæis seducet etiam gentes, plenitudo igitur gentium non intrabit, ut etiam Judæi intrent; neque sic gentes Judæos ad æmulationem provocare deberent, quod tamen futurum, Deut. XXXII.21. prædictum est. Accedit, quòd Hierosolyma à gentibus calcari usque dum gentium tempora impleantur, debuit, Luc. XXI. 24. Non igitur habebunt Judæi Regem Hierosolymæ regnaturum, & in omnes gentes dominaturum. Nam post impletionem temporum gentium induratio cessabit. Sed Regnum Antichristi Judaicum cum Prophetiis de statu Judæorum usque ad finem mundi, Levit. XXVI. Deut. XXVIII. XXXII. & alibi prædicto aperte pugnat. Quid verò multis? Babylonem magnam, qua cum Antichristus in re ipsa convenit, septimontiam urbem, Apoc. XVII. 9. & civitatem magnam, habentem Regnum in Reges terræ, ib.v.18. qualis nunquam Hierosolyma fuit, vel erit, sed Roma est, Prophetia definit. Non igitur Templum in quo Antichristus sessurus erat, noviter erectum Hierosolymæ Templum, quale nunquam erectum iri ipse etiam Baronius ad A.C.72. probat. Sed Ecclesia Romana Christiana, hoc est, ore fatem Christum confessa, est. Romæ enim, digresso inde Constantino M. & divisio in Orientale & Occidentale Imperium orbe, paulatim Templum Antichristi dominantis erigi debuit, & erectum est; & in eo Antichristus sedere debuit. Licet enim qui ἀντικείμενος adversari Christi est, in numerum, fœdus & corpus Sanctorum intrare non posset, at potest tamen intrare, quemadmodum gentes possunt intrare in civitatem Sanctam, Apoc.XI.2. Cúmque in eam sic intraverit, potest in ea, ceu Templo, considere, non simpliciter, ut pædagogus, sed ut Rex, dominus & Princeps.
units.tr: The false idea of Antichrist is refuted. and stretched them out. If that great Antichrist is to come to the Jews, himself a Jew, and in three and a half years will rebuild the Temple at Jerusalem and from there subdue the whole world, then he will do this either before the conversion of the Jews or after it. If after it, the Jews would not receive circumcision. Christ foretold that the universal preaching of the Gospel is the sign of the end of the world, Matt. 24:14. Paul also says that the reception of the Jews will be [ζωὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν] life from the dead, and so a forerunner of the resurrection of the dead, Rom. 11:15. Thus the hardening would come first, after the reception, although the hardening is said to cease after the entry of the multitude of the Gentiles, ib. 11:25. If before it, it will not stand that the Papists say Antichrist will die forty-five days before the end of the world. For how could the Jews be converted in so few days, and with what fruit for the Church and the other nations? Even if Antichrist, together with the Jews, should also seduce the nations, the fullness of the Gentiles would not enter, so that the Jews might enter as well; nor would the Gentiles then provoke the Jews to emulation, which nevertheless is predicted to happen, Deut. 32:21. Add that Jerusalem was to be trodden down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, Luke 21:24. The Jews therefore will not have a king reigning at Jerusalem and ruling over all nations, for after the fulfilment of the times of the Gentiles the hardening will cease. The Jewish kingdom of Antichrist plainly conflicts with the prophecies about the state of the Jews until the end of the world, Lev. 26, Deut. 28, 32, and elsewhere. What more need be said? Prophecy defines the great Babylon, with which Antichrist in fact agrees, as the city of seven hills, Rev. 17:9, and the great city having a kingdom over the kings of the earth, ib. v. 18. Jerusalem never was, and never will be, such a city; Rome is. Therefore the Temple in which Antichrist was to sit is not a newly erected Temple at Jerusalem, such as Baronius himself, at ad A.C. 72, proves will never be erected. It is the Christian Church of Rome, that is, the one which with its mouth confesses Christ. For at Rome, after Constantine the Great had departed and the world was divided into the Eastern and Western Empires, the Temple of the dominant Antichrist was to be erected gradually, and it was erected; and in it Antichrist was to sit. For although he who is [ἀντικείμενος] the adversary of Christ cannot enter into the number, covenant and body of the saints, he can nevertheless enter, just as the Gentiles can enter the holy city, Rev. 11:2. Having thus entered it, he can sit in it as in a Temple, not simply as a tutor but as king, lord and prince.

units.la: LXIX. Falsam Antichristi ideam ratiunculis quibusdam frivolis nequicquam Adversarii sustentare conantur. Fere enim nænias & fabulas veterum de Antichristo tum adhuc latente, recoquunt. Qualis illa est, qua verba Jacobi emortualia de Dane: Erit Dan ut serpens juxta viam, ut cerastes juxta semitam, &c. Genes.XLIX.17. fictitio Antichristo applicantes, eundem Judæum & Danitam fore somniant. Nimis enim id allegoricum est, neque fidem facere sententiæ nisi aliis argumentis pro-
units.tr: LXIX. Our opponents try in vain to uphold the false idea of Antichrist with certain flimsy little arguments. They revive almost the trifles and fables of the ancients about an Antichrist who was then still hidden. Such is the one that applies Jacob's dying words about Dan, Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path, etc. (Gen. 49.17), to a fictitious Antichrist, and dreams that he will be a Jew and a Danite. That is far too allegorical, and it can lend no credibility to the opinion unless it is supported by other arguments.

units.la: batæ, facere potest. Danis tribum universam ibi cum serpente & cerastes ob situm & ingenium tribus, non seram nativitatem Antichristi ex Dane comparari, alibi ostendimus. Ille porrò ἀλλος alius, in nomine proprio venturus, & à Judæis recipiendus, Joh. V. 43. similis est Antichristo, qui in nomine proprio venit, & credi sibi intestato postulat, imò Judaismum introducturus fuit; sed proprie tamen non Antichristus, sed Pseudo-Messiarum aliquis, quos inter Barchocoba, aut quivis forte alii bellatores ex domo Davidis corporalem libertatem promittentes, & novissimè Sabbathai Levi sunt, intelligitur. Neque etiam in loco eo ἀλλος alius singularem personam significat magis, quàm ibid.I V.37. Alius est qui seminat, alius qui metit; & alibi etiam velut, 1.Cor. VI. 1. X. 24. 29. XII. 9. 10. XIV. 17. Gal.I. 19. Jac.IV. 12. quibus locis ἀλλος alius non proprie & singulariter, sed indeterminatè & particulariter accipitur. Opponitur autem Christo-personæ certæ, alius indefinitè, sicut Paulo-personæ certæ opponitur εἶ τις si quis, vel alius quis, 2.Cor. XI.20.21. & εἰ ἄλλος si alius, Phil.III.4. Articulus porrò ὁ in vocibus Ἀντίχριστος, Ἀνθρωπος, Υιὸς, Ἀνομος, 2.Thess.II.3.4.8. 1.Joh.II.18. IV.3. personam quidem & individuum notat, sed ἀδηλον & commune potiùs, quàm τὸ δεῖ τι singulare, tametsi quod affirmatur de illo, verè etiam affirmatur de isto, non contra. Sic qui Imperatoris potentiam prædicat, non solùm Augustum vel Trajanum singulariter, sed communiter omnes intelligit, quamvis nec Augustum nec Trajanum excludat. Eadémque ratione ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος, ὁ ἀντίχριστος, ille homo peccati, ille filius perditionis, ille adversarius, ille Antichristus, &c. communiter unumquemque in Bestiæ throno sedentem denotant, licèt quandoque etiam intelligantur singulariter, putade Gregorio VII. Bonfacio VIII. Articulus ille remissivus est, ut & ἡ ἀποστασία illa defectio, de qua toties Prophetæ loquuntur; adeóque impietatis excellentiam potiùs, quàm personæ singularitatem declarat, quod ex adjunctis, sedere in Templo Dei, efferre se supra Deum, &c. perspicuè colligitur. Et sic ὁ Ἀντίχριστος Antichristus dicitur, ut etiam ἀντίχριστοι πολλοὶ Antichristi multi dicantur, 1.Joh.II.18. Nomen porrò Bestiæ, certum numerum 666. habens, Apocal. XIII.17.18. non necessariò unius individui, sed commune omnibus successoribus est, ut Pharao, Abimelech, &c. Neque nomen Antichristi est 666. sed ille numerus nominis Bestiæ numerus est; ad quem inveniendum νοῦς ἐν σοφία intelligentia & sapientia requiritur. Auctoritas verò Patrum Antichristum singulare aliquam personam facientium nihil probat, quia eorum hac in re errores sunt mendacia Sathanæ, hunc in finem ab eo sparsa, ne Antichristus agnosceretur, & à Patribus incautè arrepta. Deinde in individuo non consentiunt. Neque etiam pugnat, esse Antichristum ordinem hominum, & tamen quædam evidentia prædicata in uno ilJius ordinis suo modo notabiliter impleri. Ineptissimè verò etiam singularitatem Antichristi ex singularitate personæ Christi, cui opponitur, probare conantur. Christus enim nonnisi unus numero esse potest, test, propter dignitatem tum personæ ; quæ Ἀνθρώπῳ est, tum officii, quod nullum socium vel successorem patitur. Antichristus vero cùm sit homo mortalis, quemadmodum impii mysterii sui telam non solus ordiri, ita nec sine successoribus pertexere potest. Et par ratio est argumentorum ex typo Antichristi, qui persona singularis, Antiochus Epiphanes fuit, petitorum. Spectari enim hic debet ratio typi, quæ tota posita est in odio verbi Dei, & crudelissima tyrannide & persecutione, qua uterque populum Dei infestat, quorum scelerum hæreditatem ut Antichristus ad successores, sic etiam Antiochus ad successorem, filium suum, Eupatorem transmisit, 1.Macchab. VI.17. 2.Macchab.XIII.9. Tempus porrò quadraginta duorum mensium, Apoc.XI.2. XIII.5. & mille ducentorum sexaginta duorum dierum, ibid. XI.3. XII.6. Temporis temporum & dimidii temporis, ibid. XII.14. non completuntur tempus universum Antichristi, sed tantùm tempus ϑηρίω πολέμου πάντης Bestiæ bellum faciențis, seu prosperantis, vincentis, ibid.XIII.5. & secundum votum suum facientis, Dan.XI.2.6. ubi vocem πολεμον plerique codices non habent. Ipse Bellarminus dies 30. iis assuit. Fieri potest, ut singulariter tot dies proprii intelligantur, quot diebus Antichristus in summo gradu suo victor erit. Sed tamen dies non proprios, sed Propheticos, & per tempus, tempora & dimidium temporis, non annos tres & dimidium intelligi, constat satis, tum quia iis mille anni illi, Apoc.XX.4. includuntur: tum quia cuncta, quæ de Bestia Capp.XI.XII.XIII. prædicantur 1260. diebus propriis, & ab una singulari persona perfici non possunt, & nominatim plagæ ibid.XVI. multò longius tempus requirunt: tum quia similiter Scriptura Prophetica, Ezech.IV. 5. Dan.IX.26. Apoc.II.10. per dies annos significat: tum quia probari non potest, tempus idem significare annum proprie dictum: & tempora præcisè annos duos proprie dictos. Ac si maximè obscurum dubiúmque esset, per dies anni, an dies proprios intelligere conveniat, interpretatio ex implemento sumenda esset. Denique sedes Bestiæ & Antichristi ibi est, ubi Dominus noster crucifixus est, ibid. XI.8. Verùm sicut ibidem locus ille spiritualiter dicitur Sodoma & Ægyptus: ita spiritualiter quoque Hierosolyma persecutrix dicitur. Et quamvis Christus Hierosolymæ crucifixus sit, non tamen iccirco πόλις μεγάλη civitas illa magna, in qua Dominus noster crucifixus est, non est Imperium Romanum, utpote quod civitatis magnæ nomine venit, ibid.XVII.18. & Judæam provinciam sibi subjectam & obnoxiam habuit. Templum verò metaphoricè de Ecclesia dicitur, ut & alibi, 1.Cor.III.16. VI.19. 2.Corinth.VI.15.16. Et Roma quidem combueretur igne, Apoc.XVII.16. sed non veniente, verùm patefacto demum Antichristo, & termino scortationis quorundam Regum impleto, ib. v.17. Neque etiam urbs sedens super septem montibus, ibid.v.11. præcisè urbem Romam, mœnibus suis inclusam, sed Regnum semipoliticum & semiecclesiasticum in septem magnis mundi partibus notat.
units.tr: For that the whole tribe of Dan is there compared with the serpent and the adder because of the tribe's location and character, not as a late birth of Antichrist from Dan, as we have shown elsewhere. Moreover, that other [ἄλλος], another, who will come in his own name, and who is to be received by the Jews (John 5.43), is like Antichrist, who comes in his own name and demands to be believed without any witness. Indeed he was to introduce Judaism. Strictly speaking, however, he is not Antichrist but one of the false Messiahs, among whom are to be understood Bar Kokhba, or some other warrior of the house of David promising bodily liberty, and most recently Sabbatai Levi. Nor does another [ἄλλος] in that passage signify a single particular person any more than in John 4.37, one sows and another reaps, and elsewhere too, as in 1 Cor. 6.1; 10.24, 29; 12.9, 10; 14.17; Gal. 1.19; Jas. 4.12, where another [ἄλλος] is taken not strictly and singularly but indefinitely and particularly. Moreover, another in the indefinite sense is opposed to a definite person, Christ, just as if anyone [εἴ τις] or some other [ἄλλος τις] is opposed to the definite person of Paul (2 Cor. 11.20, 21), and if another [εἰ ἄλλος] (Phil. 3.4). Again, the article ὁ in the words Antichrist [ἀντίχριστος], man [ἄνθρωπος], son [υἱός], lawless one [ἄνομος] (2 Thess. 2.3, 4, 8; 1 John 2.18; 4.3) indicates indeed a person and an individual, but one that is indefinite and general rather than a single definite individual, although whatever is affirmed of the one is truly affirmed of the other, not conversely. Thus he who proclaims the power of the Emperor means not only Augustus or Trajan singularly but all of them in common, although he does not exclude Augustus or Trajan. And by the same reasoning, the man of sin [ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας], the son of perdition [ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας], the adversary [ὁ ἀντικείμενος], the Antichrist [ὁ ἀντίχριστος], that man of sin, that son of perdition, that adversary, that Antichrist, etc., denote in common each one who sits on the throne of the Beast, although at times they may also be understood singularly, for example of Gregory VII or Boniface VIII. That article is relative, as is also that apostasy [ἡ ἀποστασία], the defection of which the prophets so often speak. It therefore declares the eminence of impiety rather than the singularity of a person, as is plainly gathered from the accompanying words, sitting in the temple of God, lifting himself above God, etc. And so ὁ Ἀντίχριστος, the Antichrist, is so called, just as many Antichrists [ἀντίχριστοι πολλοί] are called so (1 John 2.18). Furthermore, the name of the Beast, having the certain number 666 (Rev. 13.17, 18), belongs not necessarily to one individual but in common to all his successors, like Pharaoh, Abimelech, etc. Nor is the name of Antichrist 666; rather that number is the number of the name of the Beast, and finding it requires mind in wisdom [νοῦς ἐν σοφία], understanding and wisdom. The authority of the Fathers, who made Antichrist some singular person, proves nothing, because their errors in this matter are lies of Satan, scattered by him to this end, that Antichrist should not be recognised, and were carelessly taken up by the Fathers. Moreover, they do not agree about the individual. Nor is it inconsistent that Antichrist is an order of men, and yet that certain evident things predicated of him are in some way remarkably fulfilled in one member of that order. Most absurdly, they also try to prove the singularity of Antichrist from the singularity of the person of Christ, to whom he is opposed. For Christ can be only one in number, on account of the dignity both of his person, which is God-man, and of his office, which admits no colleague or successor. But Antichrist, since he is a mortal man, cannot weave the web of his impious mystery alone, and so he cannot weave it without successors. The same holds for the arguments drawn from the type of Antichrist, who was a single person, Antiochus Epiphanes. For the nature of the type must be considered here, which consists wholly in hatred of the Word of God and in the most cruel tyranny and persecution by which both attack the people of God. Just as Antichrist transmitted the inheritance of these crimes to successors, so Antiochus transmitted it to his successor, his son Eupator (1 Macc. 6.17; 2 Macc. 13.9). Moreover, the period of forty-two months (Rev. 11.2; 13.5), and of one thousand two hundred and sixty days (ibid. 11.3; 12.6), and of a time, times and half a time (ibid. 12.14), do not make up the whole time of Antichrist, but only the time of the Beast making war, that is, prospering and conquering (ibid. 13.5), and doing according to his will (Dan. 11.2, 6), where most manuscripts lack the word war [πόλεμον]. Bellarmine himself adds thirty days to these. It may be that the days are understood singularly as proper days, equal in number to the days on which Antichrist will be victorious at the height of his power. But that the days are not proper days but prophetic ones, and that a time, times and half a time means not three and a half years, is sufficiently clear: first, because those thousand years (Rev. 20.4) are included in them; second, because everything that is predicated of the Beast in chapters 11, 12 and 13 cannot be accomplished in 1260 proper days by one single person, and the plagues in chapter 16 in particular require a much longer time; third, because likewise prophetic Scripture signifies days as years (Ezek. 4.5; Dan. 9.26; Rev. 2.10); fourth, because it cannot be proved that time means properly a year, and times precisely two proper years. And even if it were most obscure and doubtful whether it is fitting to understand days of a year or proper days, the interpretation must be taken from the fulfilment. Finally, the seat of the Beast and of Antichrist is there where our Lord was crucified (Rev. 11.8). But just as that place is called spiritually Sodom and Egypt there, so Jerusalem is also called spiritually the persecutor. And although Christ was crucified at Jerusalem, that great city in which our Lord was crucified is not on that account the Roman Empire, since the Roman Empire comes under the name of the great city (Rev. 17.18), and held Judaea, a province subject and obedient to it. The temple, moreover, is spoken of metaphorically as the Church, as also elsewhere (1 Cor. 3.16; 6.19; 2 Cor. 6.15, 16). And Rome indeed will be burned with fire (Rev. 17.16), but not on its arrival; rather, when Antichrist has finally been revealed and the time of the fornication of certain kings is fulfilled (ibid. v. 17). Nor does the city sitting on seven mountains (ibid. v. 11) signify precisely the city of Rome enclosed within its walls, but a kingdom half political and half ecclesiastical, spread over the seven great parts of the world.

units.la: LXX. Qualis sit & non sit Antichristus, explicata vera & falsa ejus idea, profligatóque Antichristo chimærico, vidimus. Quis sit, cui idea vera Antichristi conveniat, parùm dispiciendum. Levato velo, quod res est, & sine ambagibus dicamus, Papam Romanum, quà Papa & in statu Papatus est, Antichristum esse. Persona qualis sit, quæ Papatum gerit, non moramur admodum; cùm ipsi Pontificii negent esse de fide, hanc vel illam personam esse Papam, eò quòd rei illius dijudicatio ex circumstantiis multis, iisque incertis, dependeat. Non igitur de persona sed de munere: non de persona, quà hæc vel illa persona est, sed quà Papa est, & munus Papæ gerit atque tuetur, σωληρὸν λόγον, durum, sed verissimum tamen sermonem pronuntiamus, quòd Antichristus ille magnus, in verbo Dei vivis coloribus suis descriptus, sit.
units.tr: LXX. We have seen what Antichrist is and is not, the true and false idea of him having been explained, and the chimerical Antichrist overthrown. It is necessary to examine briefly who it is to whom the true idea of Antichrist applies. Lifting the veil and speaking without circumlocution, we say that the Roman Pope, as Pope and in the state of the papacy, is Antichrist. We do not dwell at length on what sort of person holds the papacy, since the Papists themselves deny that it is a matter of faith whether this or that person is Pope, because the judgment of that matter depends on many circumstances, and uncertain ones. So we speak not of the person but of the office: not of the person as this or that individual, but as Pope, when he bears and maintains the office and function of Pope. We pronounce a hard [σκληρὸν λόγον] but most true saying, that this great Antichrist, described in God's Word in its living colours, is he.

units.la: LXXI. Papam igitur, quà talis est, & munus atque statum Papæ gerit atque tuetur, Antichristum γνήσιον & κατ' ἐξοχὴν talem esse, characteres & γνωρίσματα Antichristi, superius ex Scripturis eruta extra aleam dubitationis omnis ponunt. Nam ipse se 'Αντιχριστον Vice-Christum, & vicarium Christi, eidem in terra ἀντὶ Χριστοῦ vice Christi substitutum, palam profitetur, & in hac professione sua Papatus sui vim, dignitatem & fastigium omne collocat. Et, quod majus est, se ipsum etiam, specie obducta vicariatus hujus, 'Αντιχριστον, hoc est, ἐναντίον Χριστῷ contrarium Christo & ἀντικείμενον adversarium Christi, non nomine, sed re tamen & opere demonstrat. Nam ante omnia negat Jesum esse Christum & in carne venisse, qui præcipuus Antichristi character, 1.Joh.IV.3. ponitur. Nam qui confitetur, Jesum esse Christum, is confitetur, non potuisse nos servari per obedientiam & opera propria, sed Jesum invenire verum δικαίωμα & λυτρον; & sic perfecte justum esse, qui in ipso est, & hoc ipso justum esse, quòd in ipso est, neque aliam justitiam esse: nullum alium, ceu Sacerdotem, potuisse accedere ad Deum, & nos ad eum adducere: ipsum pro₍ Romum factum esse in Cœlum, ut semper cum ipso sint, qui credunt in ipsum: omnem accusationem & servitutem legis ablatam esse: nullum esse in Regno ipsius discrimen gentium & hominum, quoad sedem religionis & subjectionem: Regnum ejus non esse de hoc mundo, neque cum observatione, vel humana auctoritate conjunctum: eum solum esse Mediatorem, Caput, Salvatorem populi sui, quem, ceu corpus suum Spiritu suo impleat: eum solum esse Prophetam & doctorem perfectum per verbum & Spiritum suum, ita ut nullo alio doctore infallibili indigeamus: solum objectum fidei: melius esse Ecclesiæ Christum abire ad Patrem suum, & Spiritu atque verbo suo per ministros prædicato eam regere, quàm ipsum in carne præsentem esse, vel semper visibili, externo & humano imperio eam regere: confugientes ad ipsum solum fieri filios, & habere gloriationem in spe gloriæ Dei, & non venire in judicium: Christum habere semen, quod redemerit, sibi, & quod per spiritum fidei sibi inserat certóque servet: præceptis ejus nos alligari, & ea in toto mundo prædicata esse omni creaturæ & etiamnum per Evangelium scriptum prædicari & si quid simile aliud. Hæc omnia in valore & potestate verborum, quòd Jesus sit Christus, & in carne venisse, con-
units.tr: LXXI. The Pope, therefore, insofar as he is such, and bears and maintains the office and status of the Pope, beyond all doubt fits the marks and characteristics of Antichrist that were drawn above from the Scriptures: he is the genuine Antichrist [γνήσιον] and Antichrist par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχήν]. For he openly professes himself to be Vice-Christ and vicar of Christ, set up on earth in the place of Christ [ἀντὶ Χριστοῦ], and in this profession he places all the power, dignity and pinnacle of his papacy. What is more, under the appearance of this vicariate, he shows himself to be Antichrist, that is, contrary to Christ [ἐναντίον Χριστῷ] and opposed to Christ [ἀντικείμενον], not in name but in fact and in deed. For above all he denies that Jesus is the Christ and has come in the flesh, which is set down as the chief character of Antichrist, 1 John 4:3. For whoever confesses that Jesus is the Christ confesses that we could not be saved by obedience and our own works, but that in Jesus we find the true righteousness [δικαίωμα] and ransom [λύτρον]; and so he who is in Jesus is perfectly righteous, and is righteous by the very fact that he is in him, and there is no other righteousness; no other could approach God as priest and bring us to him; he has been taken up into heaven so that those who believe in him may always be with him; all accusation and the bondage of the law have been removed; in his kingdom there is no distinction between nations and men as regards the seat of religion and subjection; his kingdom is not of this world, nor joined with observance or human authority; he alone is Mediator, Head and Saviour of his people, whom he fills as his body with his Spirit; he alone is Prophet and perfect teacher through his word and Spirit, so that we need no other infallible teacher; he alone is the object of faith; it is better for the Church that Christ go away to his Father and rule her by his Spirit and by his word preached through ministers, than that he be present in the flesh or rule her always with visible, external and human dominion; those who flee to him alone become sons and have boasting in the hope of the glory of God, and do not come into judgment; Christ has a seed which he has redeemed for himself, and which he inserts into himself through the Spirit of faith and keeps safe; we are bound by his precepts, and these have been preached to every creature in the whole world and are still preached through the written Gospel; and whatever else is similar. All these things are contained in the force and meaning of the words that Jesus is the Christ and has come in the flesh, con-

units.la: Papa Romanus, quà Papa, & munus Papæ gerens, Antichristus est.
units.tr: The Roman Pope, as Pope, and bearing the office of the Pope, is Antichrist.

units.la: Quod probatur tum ex nomine Antichristi, tum ex eo, quòd negat Jesum esse Christum, & non confitetur Christum venisse in carne, & Je supra id, quod Deus & Angelum dicitur, effert. contineri, extra dubitationem omnem positum est, quia absque illis omnibus esset, Iesus non esset Christus, & in carne frustra venisset, imò non venisset. Sed Papam cuncta hæc rotundo ore negare, antithesis doctrinæ ejus, quam procedente etiam hoc opere nostro discussimus, ostendit. Per eum non licet Christo soli esse Prophetæ, Sacerdoti, vel Regi. Non esse Propheta, quia ille, ceu ἄνομος Exlex, verbum & legem Christi à Deo Patre ipsius acceptam & in Scriptura revelatam, propositione sua, velut sola authentica, infallibili & ad fidem obligante, in peregrinum & novum sensum detorquet, & in verbo à se propositio, ceu nova quadam lege, Conciliorum & Patrum fuco inducta, qua & verba Christi retinentur, & vis eorum atque potentia omnis abnegatur, sine ulla ejus ad conscientiam manifestatione, ceu unica fidei regula, omnes stupere & acquiescere jubet. Scripturam ipsam, quatenus sensu Ecclesiæ Romanæ proponentis non exponitur, immanissimis convitiis proscindens, verè ut Pseudo-propheta ille, qualis & Antichristus describitur, dicatur. Non Sacerdoti, quia & sacerdotio Christi cruento, non applicato per incruentum, quod nullum est, & quæstus tantùm, & carnis gratia confictum est, quenquam ad fidem & salutem consummari pertendit; & alios apud Deum mediatores & intercessores, & quidem à se, non à Deo Patre, per auream canonizationem unctos fingendo, Christi solius intercessionem, ceu minimè ratam & efficacem, nefariè infringit; & satisfactionibus, justitia inhærente & meritis operum propriis hominem peccatorem coram Deo justificari pertendit, ut innumera mittam. Denique non Regi, quia ipse se effert supra omne, quod Deus & Σεβαστα Augustum dicitur, adeò ut in Templo Dei sedeat, ut Deus, demonstrans se ipsum, quòd Deus fit, 2.Thess.I 1.4. qui ἀντικείμενος adversarii, seu Antichristi conspicuus maximè character est. Nam Papa se ipsum ὑπεραιρόμενος effert, superextollit, quod negari non potest. Vicarium enim Christi, & œcumenicum Ecclesiæ Pastorem se facit. In ipso autem τῷ ὑπερ-αιρεσθαι fui elatione vitium Antichristianum est, quia in Regno Christi omnes fratres sunt, Psal. CXXXIII.1. habentes unum Patrem, Matth. XXIII.9. O Cœli! cœlum est Domini nostri. Terram verò dedit filiis hominum, Psal. CXV.16. Sed Papa se effert supra omne, quod Deus & Σεβαστα Augustum dicitur; supra Magistratus & Monarchas Σεβαστὸς Augustos, & Θεὸς Divos olim dictos, quos diabolico fastu ad oscula pedum suorum adigit, & quorum, ceu sibi in spiritualibus & spiritualium titulo etiam in temporalibus subjectorum, potestatem omnem sui arbitrii & beneficii esse contendit, & movere thronos, transferre regna, regna dare & auferre, & ipsos Reges anathemate, vim sententiæ principalis habente, ferire audet, quod Petrus & Judas τὰς δόξας βλασφημῶν Gloriae blasphemare, 2.Pet.II.10. Jud.v.8. dicunt. Supra Angelos, quorum se judicem constitutum jactat, & quibus in mandatis dat, ut cunctos cruce lignatos in Cœlum asportent: supra ipsum verum atque æternum Deum, cujus placita, edicta, interdicta mutat, & cum suis commutat*: Sacramenta nihil obstante institutione Christi, mutat, mutilat, vi nativa omni spoliat, & fictitiis nonnullis, ad potestatem suam amplificandam, auget. Idem verò etiam sedet in Templo Dei, Ecclesia Christi, ceu ejus Rex, Dominus, caput, Petra, Fundamentum, Pontifex & Sponsus, eandem, ceu suum corpus & peculium omni libertate, quam Christus ei acquisivit, spoliatam libidini suæ subjiciens & gloriæ suæ mactans. Facit huc monarchia ejus, specie spiritualis, reapse verò temporalis, eaque absoluta & πιμξαυιλικὴ de qua pluribus jam egimus. Denique etiam demonstrat se ipsum, quod Deus sit. Equidem non is duntaxat se Deum, Numen Divinitatis participes facit, qui præsumit esse & haberi æternus Deus; causa prima rerum, author & largitor vitæ æternæ per efficaciam; sed etiam qui quicquam eorum, quæ ad Dei honorem, cultum, fœdus, justitiam & vitam spectant, attrectat; qui, ut Optati Milevitani verbis lib.III. ubi Donati Chartaginensis temeritatem exagitat, utar, quamvis non sit usus hac voce, tamen aut fecit, aut pajjus est, quod defectum hujus vocis impleret. Quanquam li de syllabis quæstio est, Concilia, Bullæ Papales, inscriptiones publicæ, jus Canonicum, libri ceremoniarum, aliaque similia tentantur, Papam non semel Dei nomen à gnathonibus sibi impositum admisisse. Sed de hoc quicquid sit, facit ille & patitur, quod defectum hujus vocis implet, adeoque demonstrat, quod Deus sit, quatenus id fieri potest ab homine peccati, qui in Ecclesia, ceu Ἀρχιποίμην princeps pastor, & Deum repræsentans, sedet. Probant id tum attributa Dei, quæ Papa sibi vindicat: tum cultus religiosus, quem sibi impendi patitur. Attributa, cujusmodi sunt, quòd se regulam & objectum fidei, quale solus Deus, & verbum ejus est, facit, & legibus judiciisque suis conscientias adstringit: quòd media justificationis proprio motu, & aliunde non accepta, velut opus operatum Sacramentorum, satisfactiones, absolutionem Sacerdotis, indulgentias, merita operum, Missam, &c. tradit: quòd potestatem herilem clavium, & in peccatis remittendis judicialem sibi asserit; se Caput, Fundamentum, Petram Ecclesiæ mentitur; potestatem transferendi Regna, & imperitandi omnibus Regibus Divinam sibi vendicat; potestatem dispensandi contra Legem Divinam, juramenta & vota sibi tribuit: in apotheosi Sanctos & Divos pro lubitu creat. Quæ cuncta cùmsolius Dei attributa sint, ipse sibi vendicans declarat, quòd Deus sit. Cultum quoque religiosum sibi impendi patitur. Nam Papam à suis adorari, & praxis, & Scriptores de adoratione Papæ, velut Mazaronius, Diana & Stevanus, probant. Recens electus à Cardinalibus in sacrario Conclavis, & Basilica Petri, altari impositus, dein etiam in coronatione solenniissimè, in Missa, Jubilæo, processionibus solennibus; Conciliabulis, coronatione Imperatoris, canonizatione, &c. minùs solenniter adoratur. Maximos etiam Imperatores & Reges, nedum medioxumos, vel imos lata lege, ad pudenda pedum oscula adegit. Qui honos Papæ delatus nec civilis tantum, sed Divinus & religiosus est, qui ei, ceu vicario Christi & Ecclesiæ capiti atque Monarchæ, Divinitatem affectanti & usurpanti, defertur; & adorationis nomine venit:
units.tr: This is proved both from the name of Antichrist and from the fact that he denies that Jesus is the Christ, does not confess that Christ has come in the flesh, and exalts himself above everything that is called God. It has been placed beyond all doubt that these things are contained in the matter, since without all of them Jesus would not be Christ, and would have come in the flesh in vain, indeed would not have come at all. But that the Pope denies all these things with a bold mouth is shown by the contrast with his doctrine, which we have discussed as this work has proceeded. Through him it is not allowed that Christ alone be Prophet, Priest or King. He is not Prophet, because he, like the lawless one [ἄνομος], twists the word and law of Christ, received from God the Father and revealed in Scripture, into a strange and new sense by his proposition, which he presents as the only authentic, infallible and binding interpretation for faith, and by which, under the cover of the Councils and the Fathers, he introduces into the word a new kind of law. While the words of Christ are retained, their force and power are all denied, and without any manifestation of this to the conscience he orders everyone to be astonished and acquiesce, as the only rule of faith. Insofar as Scripture is not expounded in the sense of the Roman Church, he tears it apart with the most savage insults, so that he may truly be called that false prophet, which is how Antichrist is described. Not Priest, because he maintains that the bloody priesthood of Christ, which is not applied through an unbloody one (for there is none), and which is a fiction devised for gain and the favour of the flesh, brings anyone to faith and salvation; and by feigning that other mediators and intercessors are anointed before God, and indeed by himself and not by God the Father, through golden canonization, he wickedly overthrows the intercession of Christ alone, as if it were not sufficiently valid and effective; and he maintains that a sinner is justified before God by satisfactions, inherent righteousness and the merits of his own works, to say nothing of countless others. Finally, not King, because he exalts himself above everything that is called God and Augustus [Σεβαστός], so that he sits in the temple of God as God, showing himself that he is God, 2 Thess. II.4; this is the most conspicuous character of the adversary, or Antichrist. For the Pope exalts himself [ὑπεραιρόμενος], and raises himself above all, which cannot be denied. For he makes himself the vicar of Christ and the universal Pastor of the Church. In his very self-exaltation there is an Antichristian vice, because in the kingdom of Christ all are brethren, Psalm 133:1, having one Father, Matthew 23:9. The heavens are the heavens of the Lord, but the earth he has given to the sons of men, Psalm 115:16. But the Pope exalts himself above everything that is called God and Augustus; above magistrates and monarchs, who were once called Augusti [Σεβαστοί] and gods [θεοί], whom with diabolical arrogance he compels to kiss his feet, and over whom, as over his subjects in spiritual things and, under the title of spiritual things, also in temporal ones, he claims all power at his own will and pleasure; he dares to move thrones, transfer kingdoms, give and take away kingdoms, and to strike kings themselves with anathema, which has the force of a princely sentence, which Peter and Jude call blaspheming glories [τὰς δόξας βλασφημῶν], 2 Pet. II.10, Jude v.8. Above the angels, whose judge he boasts himself to be, and to whom he gives orders to carry all who are marked with the cross into heaven; above the true and eternal God himself, whose decrees, edicts and prohibitions he changes, and exchanges them for his own. He changes, mutilates and strips the sacraments of their native force, despite the institution of Christ, and augments them with certain fictitious additions to enlarge his power. Moreover, he also sits in the temple of God, the Church of Christ, as its king, lord, head, rock, foundation, high priest and bridegroom, subjecting the Church, which Christ has acquired for himself with all freedom as his own body and possession, stripped of it, to his lust and slaughtering it for his own glory. To this belongs his monarchy, which is spiritual in appearance but in fact temporal, and absolute and imperial [πιμξαυιλικὴ], about which we have already spoken at length. Finally, he also shows himself that he is God. Indeed, he makes himself a partaker of the divine majesty not only when he presumes to be and be held the eternal God, the first cause of things, the author and giver of eternal life through his efficacy, but also when he handles anything that pertains to the honour of God, his worship, covenant, righteousness and life. He, to use the words of Optatus of Milevis in book III, where he rebukes the temerity of Donatus of Carthage, though he did not use this word, nevertheless either did or suffered that which fills the lack of this word. Although there is a question about syllables, Councils, papal bulls, public inscriptions, canon law, books of ceremonies and similar things are brought forward to show that the Pope has more than once admitted the name of God given him by flatterers. But whatever be the case here, he does and suffers that which fills the lack of this word, and so he shows that he is God, insofar as this can be done by a man of sin, who sits in the Church as the chief shepherd [Ἀρχιποίμην] and represents God. The attributes of God which the Pope claims for himself prove this, and so does the religious worship which he allows to be paid to himself. The attributes are such as this: he makes himself the rule and object of faith, which God alone and his word are, and binds consciences by his laws and judgments; he delivers the means of justification from his own motion and not received from elsewhere, as the work done in the sacraments, satisfactions, the absolution of the priest, indulgences, the merits of works, the Mass, etc.; he asserts for himself the lordly power of the keys, and a judicial power in remitting sins; he falsely claims to be the Head, Foundation and Rock of the Church; he claims for himself the divine power of transferring kingdoms and of commanding all kings; he grants to himself the power of dispensing against the Divine Law, and of dispensing oaths and vows; he creates saints and gods at will in apotheosis. When he claims all these things, which are attributes of God alone, he declares that he is God. He also allows religious worship to be paid to himself. For that the Pope is adored by his people, both the practice and the writers on the adoration of the Pope, such as Mazaronius, Diana and Stevanus, prove. Recently elected by the Cardinals in the sacristy of the Conclave and the Basilica of Peter, placed on the altar, then also most solemnly at his coronation, in the Mass, at the Jubilee, in solemn processions, at councils, at the coronation of the Emperor, at canonization, etc., he is adored less solemnly. He has also compelled the greatest emperors and kings, not to mention middling or lowly ones, by a law he laid down, to kiss his shameful feet. This honour paid to the Pope is not merely civil but divine and religious; it is paid to him as the vicar of Christ and head and monarch of the Church, who lays claim to and usurps divinity, and it comes under the name of adoration.

units.la: * Sacramenta nihil obstante institutione venit: & Papicolæ pedes hos osculantes maxima quæque & Divina beneficia à Papa expectant; & ceremoniæ ejus, velut tunsio cordis, incensatio, & Papæ in altari sedentis adoratio, religiosæ omnes sunt; & ex hypothesi Papolatrarum cultus ille duliæ, hyperduliæ & latriæ, adeóque Divinus est: & si civilis etiam foret, pridem in idololatriam, qualis politica est, degenerasset.
units.tr: Nothing stands in the way of this institution: the Papalists who kiss these feet expect from the Pope the greatest of all divine benefits. His ceremonies, such as the beating of the breast, the incense, and the adoration of the Pope seated at the altar, are all religious. On the hypothesis of the Papal worshippers, that cult of dulia, hyperdulia and latria is therefore divine. And if it were merely civil, it would long since have degenerated into idolatry, as political idolatry is.

units.la: LXXII. Sufficere hæc demonstrando Papatui Antichristiano poterant. Sed reliqui etiam Antichristi characteres examussim ei conveniunt. Ille enim est ἀνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας Homo peccati, quia non tantùm Pontifices plerique inde à pluribus seculis peccatis maximis, uti historiæ eorum domesticæ etiam produnt, polluti, apud omnem posteritatem infames sunt, adeò ut integro seculo, vix unus & alter non aperte sceleratam vitam traduxerit; sed inprimis author peccandi iis est, qui ejus χαρακτηρα signaturam acceperunt. Nam ex peccatis non peccata, & vicissim se facere posse non errore aliquo, sed expressa lege, stultè gloriatur: & præcipit atque laudat cultum creaturarum multiplicem, qui merè idololatricus est: & gravissima scelera, à quibus omnis natura nondum penitus corrupta, vehementer abhorret; velut conjugia incestus in verbo Dei damnata, perjuria, fœderum sacrosanctorum violationem, æquivocationes, aliáque ejusmodi, quæ profani etiam homines, solo naturæ lumine præditi execrantur, ceu legitima permittit, & eorum gratiam libens volensque facit. Neque tantùm homo peccati, sed etiam υιος της απωλειας Filius perditionis est, non passivè tantùm, quia quà Papa & ἀμελωνιστης, perditus est: sed etiam activè Ἀπολλύων & Ἀβαδδῶν Perdens, quia & se & alios perdit. Fatentur enim testes ex sinu, seu domestici, non paucos Pontifices, ante Papatum haud malos, postquam Cathedram Papalem semel insidere cœperunt, in execrabiles & crudelissimas bestias degenerasse; perinde ac si Cathedræ Papali venenata lues inhæreret, cujus afflatu illicò, qui eam occupant, corripiantur, & veneno eo contracto se aliósque perditum eant. Sed & Locus Antichristi quadrat, quem Romam esse, supra ostendimus. Ille enim, ceu Capitolii Romani Jupiter, in Templo suo Romano, Numinis instar, sedet, atque inde circumfusum orbem terrarum ferrea sua virga regit. Quadrant inprimis teterrima omnium flagitia, quæ Antichristo tribui supra ostendimus. Impuritas seu scortationum abominatio, blasphemandi cacoëthes, plusquam cyclopica tyrannis & crudelitas: Impietas magica, & spiritualis nundinatio atque avaritia. Scortationum abominatio, quia & spirituali & carnali scortatione & impuritate fœdissima totus scatet. Spirituali, quia populum sibi obnoxium à vero Dei cultu ad cultum creaturarum falsámque religionem seducit. Quod ex erroribus ejus idololatricis, puta papolatria, artolatria, hagiolatria, iconolatria, lipsanolatria & hierolatria alibi ad liquidum perduximus. Carnali, cui ansam non unam præbet, velut cùm δυναμιν σαρκος potentiam luxuriæ, Apoc. XVIII. 3. II. 12. seu instrumenta luxuriæ potentia & prævalida, immensas opes comparat, & iisdem ad luxum & potentiæ exaltationem abutitur:
units.tr: LXXII. These points could suffice to demonstrate the Antichristian Papacy. But the remaining marks of Antichrist also fit him exactly. He is the [anthrōpos tēs hamartias] man of sin, for not only have most Popes, for many centuries, been stained with the greatest sins, as their own domestic histories also reveal, and they are infamous to all posterity, so that in a whole century hardly one or two have not lived an openly wicked life. Above all, he is the author of sin to those who have received his [charaktēra] mark. For he foolishly boasts that from sins he can make not-sins, and, conversely, that he can do so not by some error but by express law. He commands and praises the manifold worship of creatures, which is purely idolatrous. He freely and willingly grants favour to the gravest crimes, which all nature not yet wholly corrupted shrinks from with horror: incestuous marriages condemned in the word of God, perjuries, the violation of sacred covenants, equivocations, and other such things, which even profane men, endowed with the light of nature alone, detest, he permits as lawful. He is not only the man of sin but also the [huios tēs apōleias] Son of perdition, not merely passively, since as Pope he is also [amelōnistēs] lost, but actively too, as [Apollyōn] and [Abaddōn] Destroyer, since he destroys both himself and others. Witnesses from his own household confess that not a few Popes, who were not bad before the Papacy, degenerated into execrable and most cruel beasts once they began to occupy the Papal chair, as if a poisonous plague clung to that chair, and whoever occupies it is at once seized by its breath, and having contracted the poison, goes to ruin himself and takes others with him. The place of Antichrist also fits Rome, which we have shown above. For he sits in his Roman temple like the Jupiter of the Roman Capitol, as if a divine power, and from there rules the whole circle of the earth with his iron rod. The most foul of all crimes, which we have shown above are attributed to Antichrist, fit him especially: the abomination of fornication, the itch for blasphemy, a more than Cyclopean tyranny and cruelty, magical impiety, and spiritual trafficking and greed. He is the abomination of fornication because he is wholly soaked in both spiritual and carnal fornication and the most foul impurity. He is spiritually so because he leads the people subject to him away from the true worship of God to the worship of creatures and to false religion. We have clearly demonstrated elsewhere that this follows from his idolatrous errors, namely papolatry, artolatry, hagiolatry, iconolatry, lipsanolatry and hierolatry. He is carnally so, for he provides more than one occasion for it, as when he procures, from his powerful and very strong resources, [dynamin sarkos] the power of lust (Rev. 18.3; 2.12), or the instruments of lust, and abuses them for luxury and the exaltation of his power. He indulges in religious leisure, which inclines to similar luxury. He strongly commends the law of celibacy for priests and the monastic vow of continence, from which, among those who lack the gift of continence, the most foul fruits spring up: every kind of lust and impurity grows from the vice of those who forbid and commend it. He has instituted auricular confession of such a kind that priest-confessors, by shameless questions, shamefully corrupt both themselves and those who confess. He admits voluptuous music into the very worship of God. He thinks lightly of fornication, adultery and the sin of sodomy, dictates light penalties for them, and releases people from them for a price in money. He dispenses from degrees of kinship divinely forbidden. He permits brothels and so favours pimping, not to speak of the utterly unrestrained impurity of the hierarchy, the Popes and the whole clergy, which is clearly proved by the light and testimony of experience and history itself.

units.la: religiosum otium, ad similem luxuriam inclinans; indulget: Legem cœlibatus Sacerdotibus, & votum continentiæ monasticum enixè commendat, ex quibus apud eos, qui continentiæ dono destituuntur, fructus fœdissimi, omne genus libidinum & impuritatis eorum, qui prohibent, & commendant, vitio pullulat: Confessionem auricularem instituit talem, in qua Sacerdotes confessarii quæstionibus impudicis & se & confitentes nefariè corrumpunt: Musicam voluptariam in ipso cultu Dei adhibet: de fornicatione, adulterio, peccato Sodomiæ tenuiter sentit, & pœnas iisdem leves dictat, atque ab iis pecuniæ pretio relaxat: In gradibus Divinitus prohibitis dispensat: Lupanaria permittit, adeóque lenoniæ favet, ne quid de Hierarchiæ, Paparum & cleri omnimoda impuritate, experientiæ & historiæ ipsius luce & testimoniis liquidò probata, dicam. Blasphemandi cacoëthes manifestum est, quia nomen Dei tum in Papolatria, tum in idololatria & superstitione reliqua omni blasphematur; & Papa Scripturam, Christum ipsum, veram Ecclesiam, ejus doctrinam & pios antistites, dominationes, Sanctos in Cœlo, honorem debitum iis detrahendo, Apostolos, Petro eos subjiciendo, Deiparam Virginem, de qua in legendis suis contumeliosa multa infarciunt. S. Patres, & corpora Sanctorum, falsis honoribus ea mactando, immanibus convitiis, & veritimis blasphemiis proscindit. Tyrannis & crudelitas summa, quia eos, qui verbi Divini scripti authoritate, aliisque legitimis rationibus freti, ei se subjicere detrectant, probroso hæreticorum titulo traductos, & lege lata cogendos, puniendos, excindendos immaniter decernit; & instituto tribunali horribili inquisitionis, injustis modis torquet, punit, occidit: per Emissarios Regum Principúmque indignationi & furoribus exponit, & sanguinariorum decretorum suorum executione pro viribus suis & extremis modis, quoad conscientias, corpora, honores & fortunas omnes infestat.
