Magica impietas, quia idololatriam, in qua magia est, propalam exercet: impietatem magicam extenuat: religionem universam ejusdem impietatis labe fœdat: cum dæmonibus & mortuis hominibus, ad veritatem ex iis expiscandam, familiare commercium colit. Verbum Dei in exorcismis & benedictionibus profanat: Baptismum exorcismis contaminat: in Eucharistia certorum verborum murmure corpus Christi excantat: Unctionibus certis, chrismati inprimis, in Sacramentis spuriis effectus tribuit, quos nec à natura, nec à Deo supra naturam operante habent: amuletis benedictis, verbis, figuris & numeris efficaciam tribuit: fortuitis significationem affingit: Magiam per remedia magica depellere conatur: Magos professos, & scripta consuetudinésque notorie magicas in sinu suo fovet: Magos levibus poenis subjicit: denique nullam criminis hujus emendationem patitur. Avaritia denique & spiritualis nundinatio, quia merces illæ, quas Scriptura, Apoc. XVIII. 11. 17. 23. Antichristo & Babyloni tribuit, in Papæ coetum ad literam, in cultu externo, & Missa inprimis, tum secundum allegoriam varii reperiuntur; quatenus & in Missa Deum remissionem sionem peccatorum : & in cultu reliquo externo Sanctorum, imaginum, & reliquiarum invocatarum opem & intercessionem apud Deum; nec non viventium,Monachorum inprimis, pro viventibus & defunctis in fictitio Purgatorio laborantibus, vicarias orationes, oblationes,suffragia & supererogationis merita in Sacramento Poenitentiae & extra illud in applicatione thesauri meritorum Christi & Sanctorum abundantium, per indulgentiarum dispensationes, inprimis claves Regni Coelorum: in Sacramento Ordinis collationem tum ordinum, adeoque ipsum Spiritum S. tum beneficiorum: in regimine Ecclesiae tum leges & Divinas & humanas, tum judicia & censuras Ecclesiasticas: in communione externa Ecclesiae opera pietatis & charitatis: in sanctificatione externa benedictiones & consecrationes rerum: denique in jurisdictione universa, animas hominum,venalia cuncta illa & in commercio habet, suamque illam nundinationem legibus censurisque firmat, & in publicis officinis, Poenitentiaria, Dataria, impune exercet; neque, reclamantibus licet optimis quibusque ea in re emendationem patitur. Quae singula,scortationum & impuritatis,blasphemiarum,crudelitatis,magiae & avaritiae atque nundinationis spiritualis Papae externam & vere Antichristianam impietatem convincentia, obiter,& generalibus titulis suis indicata & delibata pridem integro volumine Mysterii Babylonis Magnae diffusissime & ἀναλλαγήτως probata manifestae luci & veritati dedimus.
units.tr: The itch for blasphemy is plain, because the name of God is blasphemed both in Papal worship and in idolatry and every other superstition. The Pope, by detracting from Scripture, from Christ himself, from the true Church, its doctrine, its godly bishops and dominions, and the saints in heaven, by denying them the honour due to them, by subjecting the Apostles to Peter, and by stuffing many insulting things about the Virgin Mother of God into his legends, blasphemes them all. He tears apart the Holy Fathers and the bodies of the saints, mangling them with false honours and with monstrous abuse and lying blasphemies. Tyranny and cruelty are supreme, because he decrees that those who refuse to submit to him, relying on the authority of the written Word of God and other legitimate reasons, be disgracefully branded with the title of heretics, and, by law enacted, be compelled, punished and cut off most savagely. By establishing the dreadful tribunal of the Inquisition, he tortures, punishes and kills by unjust means. Through the emissaries of kings and princes he exposes them to indignation and fury, and by carrying out his bloodthirsty decrees, with all his strength and by extreme measures, he harasses consciences, bodies, honours and all fortunes. Magical impiety, because he openly practises idolatry, in which magic is present; he extenuates magical impiety; he defiles all religion with the stain of the same impiety; he cultivates familiar dealings with demons and dead men, to fish out the truth from them. He profanes the word of God in exorcisms and blessings; he contaminates baptism with exorcisms; in the Eucharist he enchants the body of Christ by murmuring certain words. By certain anointings, chiefly with chrism, he attributes to spurious sacraments effects which they have neither from nature nor from God working above nature. He ascribes efficacy to blessed amulets, words, figures and numbers, attaches significance to chance events, and tries to drive off magic by magical remedies. He cherishes in his bosom professed magicians and writings and customs notoriously magical; he subjects magicians to light penalties; and finally he permits no amendment of this crime. Lastly, avarice and spiritual trafficking, because the wares which Scripture (Rev. 18.11, 17, 23) assigns to Antichrist and Babylon are found in the Papal assembly, literally in external worship and especially in the Mass, and in various ways allegorically: in the Mass he sells God's remission of sins; in the rest of external worship he sells the aid and intercession with God of invoked saints, images and relics, as well as the vicarious prayers, oblations, suffrages and works of supererogation of living monks above all, for the living and the dead who suffer in the imaginary Purgatory. He sells the abundant treasury of the merits of Christ and the saints, applied through the dispensing of indulgences, and above all the keys of the kingdom of heaven, both within and outside the Sacrament of Penance. In the Sacrament of Orders he sells the conferral of orders, and so the Holy Spirit himself, and of benefices. In the governance of the Church he sells both divine and human laws, judgments and ecclesiastical censures; in the external communion of the Church, works of piety and charity; in external sanctification, blessings and consecrations of things. Finally, in universal jurisdiction he has all those saleable things in trade, and the souls of men, and he confirms this traffic by laws and censures and carries it on with impunity in public offices, the Penitentiary, Datary. He suffers no amendment in this matter, though the best men protest. We have already published these individual things, which convict the Pope of fornication and impurity, blasphemy, cruelty, magic, avarice and spiritual trafficking as an external and truly Antichristian impiety, in a whole volume, The Mystery of Babylon the Great, where we proved them, indicated and touched on in passing under general headings, most fully and irrefutably to the clear light and truth.

units.la: LXXIII. Praeterea etiam distinctae periodi Antichristi, puta operationis mysterii,revelationis, consumptionis ejus per Spiritum oris Christi & plenariae abolitionis, Papae Romano exacte congruunt. Operationis mysterii iniquitatis, utpote quod jam Apostolorum aetate operari coepit, 2. Thess. II. 7. & ad revelationem usque ejusdem operari perrexit; quia jam Apostolorum aetate falsi fratres, non casti & sincere Christum praedicantes intrarunt, Phil. I. 15. &c. & schismata invaluerunt, 1.Cor. I. 12. IV.6. & φιλοπρωτεύοντες primatus amantes incesserunt,3. Joh. vers. 9. & quidam ut hostes Christi ambulaarunt,Phil.III. 18. & multi haereses pestiferas, de persona inprimis & excellentia Christi, invexerunt; quarum occasione οἱ φιλοπρωτεύοντες occasionem damnandi haereses dictatoria potestate arripuerunt. Persuasum deinceps multum est, controversias per praescriptionis & traditionis auctoritatem rectius, quam per demonstrationem ex Scripturis definiri. Traditionis,velut apud se potius quam apud alios depositae, praetextu locus datus est sedi Romanae sese efferendi supra alias. Doctrinae de libero arbitrio, justitia fidei,& unico sacrificio Christi minus accurate, solide, perspicue, nec sine phrasium novarum ambiguitate a Philosophis; Rhetoribus, Causidicis ad Christum conversis, adeoque neophytis, adhibita, traditae errandi occasionem praebuerunt. Unus multis Episcopis praelatus, & potestate eximia χειροθεσίας donatus,controversias & lites fidelium ad se delatas definiendas suscepit, qua occasione Episcoporum eorum inprimis, qui magnis urbibus praesidebant,cupiditas, ut in mundo potentes esse,& jurisdictionem habere cuperent,incrementum cepit; & Imperatores Christiani desideriis Episcoporum factuti satis, iisdem jurisdictionem concesserunt, prohibentes Officialibus suis, ne quenquam a judicio Episcopi abstraherent. Deinceps Synodica & Caesarea authoritate cathedrae Patriarchales erectae, atque eas inter τὰ πτωλεια Romanae sedi tributa,multúque dementati sunt, ut crederent,eam sedem a Deo prae caeteris electam esse, ut ejus beneficio Ecclesia a corruptione & haeresibus, quas maiculè illa oppugnavit,custodiretur; id etiam Sathana machinante, ut Episcopus unus in reliquos omnes dominium,titulum &potestatem Episcopi universalis oecumenici affectaret,&Romanus tandem, indulgente Phoca, impetraret: quin & paulatim ab obedientia Imperatoris deficiens, se supra omne,quod Deus & Σεβαστὸς dicitur, efferret,supremamque in spiritualibus & temporalibus potestatem non pretio auferret, sed vi raperet. Quae omnia qua ratione,& quibus gradibus successerint, in Historia Papatus narravimus. Saltem liquidò inde constat,Mysterium iniquitatis illud, seu defectionis a lege Dei ἐν μυστηρίῳ in mysterio, hoc est, in multis artibus & per latentia incrementa operans, in Romana denique Ecclesia ita consummatum esse, ut non frustra Spiritus S. Babyloni mysticae, quae Roma est,titulum Μυστήριον Mysterium, ceu perenne quoddam ejus,unde dignosceretur,monumentum, in fronte ejus a quovis sanae mentis noscendum legendumque, exsculpserit,Apoc.XVII.5. Eidem Papae ἀποκάλυψις revelatio Antichristi ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ καιρῷ in tempore suo, amoto τὸ κατέχον eo, qui hactenus, quo minus revelaretur, detinebat, 2. Thess. II. 6. 7. convenit. Ille κατέχων detinens erat Imperator Romae, obtinens imperium in eo loco,in quo futurum erat,ut homo peccati, subjugato Imperatore hactenus monarchiae Papalis plenitudinem detinente & impediente,in Templo Dei consideret, & se Deum declararet. Multi Imperatores diu satis cum Papa conflictati sunt,eúmque,ne cupitis potiretur, detinuerunt, quorum ultimus Ludovicus Bavarus, post cujus tempora Antichristus plenè revelatus est, quando Papa Eugenius IV. per Concilium Florentinum A.MCDXXXIX. in literis Unionis, ultimae Sessioni Concilii illius insertis,verbo ὁρίζομεν definimus usus,Pontificem Romanum in orbem universum habere primatum, & esse successorem B. Petri, & Vicarium Christi, totius Ecclesiae caput, & omnium Christianorum patrem & doctorem, & ipsi in B.Petro pascendi,regendi& gubernandi totam Ecclesiam universalem a Domino nostro Jesu Christo (κατὰ ἐξουσίαν) plenam potestatem traditam esse; definivit. Atque idem ille Antichristi per revelationem ejus adventus factus secundum operationem Sathanae in omni potentia, signis & prodigiis mendacibus,& in omni deceptione iniquitatis,2.Thess. II.9.10. Haec Antichristi,non clam operantis adhuc in mysterio , sed detecti & revelati operatio, Sathanam authorem habens,cui magis,quàm Papae convenit? Ille enim miraculorum gloriam inter Ecclesiae suae notas retulit. Et cum Evangelii doctrina semel miraculis Christi , Apostolorum & primorum fidelium
units.tr: LXXIII. Moreover, the distinct periods of Antichrist, namely the working of the mystery, its revelation, its consumption by the Spirit of the mouth of Christ, and its complete abolition, correspond exactly to the Roman Pope. The working of the mystery of iniquity began already in the age of the Apostles (2 Thess. 2:7) and has continued to work until its revelation. Already in the Apostles' age false brethren, not chaste and sincere preachers of Christ, crept in (Phil. 1:15, etc.); schisms gained strength (1 Cor. 1:12; 4:6); those who love primacy [φιλοπρωτεύοντες] made their way in (3 John, v. 9); and some walked as enemies of Christ (Phil. 3:18). Many brought in pestilent heresies, chiefly concerning the person and excellence of Christ, and on the occasion of these those who love primacy seized the opportunity of condemning heresies by dictatorial power. It was afterwards widely held that controversies are settled more rightly by the authority of prescription and tradition than by demonstration from the Scriptures. Under the pretext of tradition, as if it had been deposited with the Roman see rather than with others, room was given to that see to raise itself above the rest. The doctrines of free will, justification by faith, and the unique sacrifice of Christ were handled less accurately, solidly and clearly, and not without the ambiguity of new phrases, by philosophers, rhetoricians and lawyers who had been converted to Christ and were therefore neophytes; and these gave occasion for error to be handed down. One man was set above many bishops and endowed with the outstanding power of laying on of hands [χειροθεσίας]; he undertook to define the controversies and disputes of the faithful that were brought to him. On this occasion there grew especially the desire of those bishops who presided over great cities to be powerful in the world and to have jurisdiction. Christian emperors, satisfying the wishes of the bishops, granted them jurisdiction and forbade their officials to drag anyone away from the bishop's judgment. Afterwards, by synodal and imperial authority, patriarchal sees were erected, and among them the first place [τὰ πρωτεῖα] was given to the Roman see. Men became so deluded as to believe that this see had been chosen by God above all others, so that by its benefit the Church would be guarded from corruption and heresies, which that see chiefly attacked. This too was done with Satan at work, so that one bishop should aspire over all the rest to the lordship, title and power of universal ecumenical bishop, and the Roman at last obtained it, Phocas indulging him. Indeed, gradually falling away from obedience to the emperor, he raised himself above everything that is called God or Augustus [Σεβαστὸς], and he seized supreme power in spiritual and temporal affairs, not by price but by force. We have narrated in the History of the Papacy by what reasoning and through what steps all these things came about. At least it is clear from this that that mystery of iniquity, or defection from the law of God, working in a mystery [ἐν μυστηρίῳ], that is, through many arts and by hidden increments, has in the Roman Church finally been so consummated that the Holy Spirit did not in vain carve on the forehead of mystical Babylon, which is Rome, the title Mystery [Μυστήριον], as a lasting monument by which she might be recognized, to be known and read by anyone of sound mind (Rev. 17:5). To the same Pope there agrees the revelation [ἀποκάλυψις] of Antichrist in its own time [ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ καιρῷ], with that which restrains [τὸ κατέχον] removed, namely the one who until then was holding back, so that he might not be revealed (2 Thess. 2:6, 7). He who restrains [κατέχων] was the emperor at Rome, who held the empire in the place where it was to happen that the man of sin should sit in the temple of God and declare himself God. While the emperor was subjugated, he, who until then had held back and hindered the fullness of papal monarchy, could no longer do so. Many emperors contended with the Pope for a long time and held him back from getting what he wanted; the last of them was Louis the Bavarian, after whose time Antichrist was fully revealed. When Pope Eugenius IV, through the Council of Florence in 1439, in the letters of union inserted into the final session of that council, used the word we define [ὁρίζομεν], he defined that the Roman Pontiff has primacy over the whole world, is the successor of blessed Peter and Vicar of Christ, head of the whole Church, and father and teacher of all Christians, and that full power to feed, rule and govern the whole universal Church has been handed down to him in blessed Peter by our Lord Jesus Christ (by authority [κατὰ ἐξουσίαν]). The same revelation of Antichrist brings with it his coming, which is according to the working of Satan, in all power, with lying signs and wonders, and in all deception of iniquity (2 Thess. 2:9, 10). Who does this operation of Antichrist belong to more than to the Pope, the operation not still secretly at work in the mystery but detected and revealed, which has Satan as its author? For he has counted the glory of miracles among the marks of his Church. And since the doctrine of the Gospel was once confirmed and sealed by the miracles of Christ, of the Apostles and of the first believers,

units.la: LXXIII. Praeterea etiam distinctae periodi Antichristi lium confirmata & obsignata, novis miraculis apud Christianos, & inter eos edendis, non indigeat, vel miracula sero adeo in Ecclesia Papæ affectata, illa signa & prodigia mendacia secundum operationem Sathanæ, & in omni potentia ejus sunt: vel nulla sunt, vel erunt unquam. Quid enim signa & prodigia mendacia sunt, si non sunt illa, quibus mendacium & ἀπώλεια defectio universa Papæ tegitur, imo quibus falsa illa pro doctrina Christi ipsius obtruditur: & quæ pleraque etiam mendacia & fallacia sunt. Cujusmodi imprimis sudor, lachrymæ, risus, incessus statuarum, sanationes ægrorum ad Sanctorum defunctorum reliquias ac monumenta: Virtutes Jesuitarum apud Garamantas & Indos patratæ; panis & vini in corpus & sanguinem Christi transubstantiatio, & si quæ alia ejusdem furfuris sunt, quæ alii operose integris voluminibus persecuti sunt. Accedit ἀπάτη τῆς ἀδικίας deceptio injustitiæ Papæ, quæ est omne sophisma & διαλογισμός, quo fit, ut homines nec Christum, nec ejus justitiam ad salutem agnoscant, & pro causa justitiæ habeant, quod tale non est. Quæ revelationi Antichristi successit ejusdem ἀνάλωσις consumptio per Spiritum oris Christi, 2. Thess. II. 8. in Regno Papæ clarissime successit, quando per verba Christi & eorum in Reformatione Ecclesiæ ab hominibus imbellibus prædicatorum efficaciam, & per Spiritum ab ipso exeuntem, corpus Papæ, sive multitudo eorum, qui cum ipso erant, mirum in modum diminui & consumi coepit; integris Regnis & Provinciis pluribus gloria Angeli Evangelistæ, Apoc. XVIII. 1. illustratis, ut agnoscerent, τὸν ἄνομον esse doctorem mendacii, impietatis, injustitiæ & idololatriæ. Quam etiam in rem plura in loco, cum primis in Diatriba de Æterno Evangelio, diximus. Supererit καταργήσις abolitio Antichristi, futura ὁν ἐπιφάνεια τῆς παρουσίας in affulgentia præsentiæ vel adventus Christi, 2. Thess. II. 8. hoc est, vel in jubare quodam Regni Christi, præcessuro adventum ejus ad judicandum vivos & mortuos, quomodo aurora solis antecambula ἐπιφάνεια παρουσίας affulgentia præsentiæ vel adventus solis dici potest, licet nondum sol horizontem illum ingressus sit: vel in die ultimi judicii. Licet enim vix dubitari possit, quin Antichristi politia, Regnum & status Hierarchicus abolendus sit ante finem mundi, atque ei rei Scriptura, Apoc. XVIII. 9. &c. ubi Spiritus S. Reges terræ, mercatores terræ & nautæ, deploraturos excidium Babylonis, inducit, fidem facit: tamen fieri potest, ut ad finem usque mundi, & illustrem adventum Domini, apostatæ seu defectores improbi, Christo occasionem finiendæ patientiæ ejus præbituri, demum a Christo ad judicium vivorum & mortuorum adventante abolendi, superstant. Ita populus Judaicus tum abolitus est, cum politia ejus abolita est; licet Judæi hincinde palantes, & æternum Regem Christum hodieque blasphemantes, non desint. Sed de hoc quicquid sit, abolitio illa Antichristi erit abolitio Regni Papalis, quia abolebitur ille ipse, qui in Apocalypsi Babylonis nomine venit, & de qua dicitur: Uno die venient ejus plagæ, &c. & igni comburetur, Apoc. XVIII. 8. Atqui Babylon illa Roma est, & Roma Christiana est, uti inte-
units.tr: LXXIII. Moreover, the distinct periods of Antichrist ... does not need new miracles to be wrought among Christians and by them. Either miracles have been sought so late in the Church of the Pope that those lying signs and wonders according to the working of Satan, and in all his power, are either nothing or will never be. For what are lying signs and wonders, if they are not those by which the lie and the total defection of the Pope are covered over, and by which those falsehoods are foisted upon us as the doctrine of Christ himself? Many of these are also lying and deceptive. Chief among them are sweating, weeping, laughing and walking statues, the healing of the sick at the relics and tombs of dead saints, the virtues wrought by the Jesuits among the Garamantes and the Indians, and the transubstantiation of bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ, and whatever else is of the same chaff, which others have pursued with laborious whole volumes. To these is added the deception of injustice [ἀπάτη τῆς ἀδικίας] of the Pope, which is every sophism and reasoning by which men come to acknowledge neither Christ nor his righteousness for salvation, and to hold as the cause of righteousness what is not such. The consumption [ἀνάλωσις] which followed the revelation of Antichrist, by the Spirit of the mouth of Christ (2 Thess. 2:8), has most clearly followed in the Kingdom of the Pope. When, through the words of Christ and the efficacy of those preached in the Reformation of the Church by men not unwarlike, and through the Spirit proceeding from him, the body of the Pope, or the multitude of those who were with him, began to be diminished and consumed in a wonderful manner, whole kingdoms and many provinces were illuminated by the glory of the Angel the Evangelist (Rev. 18:1), so that they recognized that the lawless one [τὸν ἄνομον] is the teacher of lies, impiety, injustice and idolatry. On this point we have said more in place, especially in the Diatribe on the Eternal Gospel. There remains the abolition [καταργήσις] of Antichrist, which is to come at the appearing of his presence [ἐπιφάνεια τῆς παρουσίας], in the brightness of the presence or coming of Christ (2 Thess. 2:8). That is, it will be either in a certain radiance of the Kingdom of Christ, which will precede his coming to judge the living and the dead, just as the dawn that goes before the sun can be called the appearing of the sun's presence or coming, although the sun has not yet entered the horizon; or it will be on the day of the last judgment. For although it can hardly be doubted that the polity, kingdom and hierarchical state of Antichrist must be abolished before the end of the world, and Scripture bears witness to this (Rev. 18:9, etc.), where the Holy Spirit introduces the kings of the earth, the merchants of the earth and the sailors lamenting the destruction of Babylon, nevertheless it may happen that wicked apostates or defectors remain until the end of the world and the glorious coming of the Lord, giving Christ occasion to finish his patience, and are finally to be abolished when Christ comes to judge the living and the dead. Thus the Jewish people were abolished when their polity was abolished, although Jews wandering here and there, and even today blaspheming the eternal King Christ, are not lacking. But whatever be the case with this, that abolition of Antichrist will be the abolition of the Papal Kingdom, because he himself will be abolished who came in the name of Babylon in the Apocalypse, and of whom it is said: Her plagues will come in one day, etc., and she will be burned with fire (Rev. 18:8). But Babylon is Rome, and Rome is Christian, as we have proved by irrefutable arguments in the whole volume, as

units.la: gro Volumine argumentis irrefragabilibus probatum dedimus.
units.tr: as we have proved by irrefutable arguments throughout the whole of the preceding volume.

units.la: LXXIV. Denique & Corpus Antichristi cum corpore Papæ consonat.
units.tr: LXXIV. Finally, the body of Antichrist also agrees with the body of the Pope.

units.la: Illud enim sunt οἱ ἀπολλύμενοι pereuntes, qui non acceperunt amorem veritatis, ut salvi fierent, & quibus Deus immittit efficaciam erroris, ut credant mendacio; ut judicentur omnes, qui non crediderint veritati, sed delectati fuerint injustitia, 2. Thess. II. 10-13. qui etiam nomine Bestiæ, Meretricem Babylonicam portantis, Apoc. XVII. 3. 7. 8. veniunt. Si Papa filius perditionis Ἀπολλύων perdens est, ejusdem corpus supra fusius a nobis explicatum ἀπολλύμενον periens est. Licet enim multo minus de perionis hujus corporis mystici, quam de persona ipsa capitis mystici judicemus, memores Apostoli vetantis alienum servum judicare, Rom. XIV. 4. nullique etiam dubitantes, quin commixti externæ communioni Papæ nonnulli per verba fundamenti, quæ non plane in ea obliterantur, & neglectum veneni, quod cum iisdem superstitio miscuit, ὡς διὰ πυρὸς velut per ignem, 1. Cor. III. 15. & μόλις difficulter, 1. Petr. IV. 18. ob tyrannidem & insidias Sathanæ, quæsitiores longe, quando Ecclesia communionem Papæ reliquit, salventur, at salventur tamen; omnes tamen illos, qui Papæ, ut Papæ capitis membra sunt, & signaturam ejus in manu sua dextra, vel faciebus suis recipiunt, Apoc. XIII. 16. & à cædibus, veneficiis, scortatione & furtis suis non resipiscunt, cap. IX. 21. in numero pereuntium esse nulli ambigimus, quia capitis & corporis idem fatum sit oportet. Cumque amor veritatis sit ille, quo veritas propter se, non propter manem delectationem carnis & commoda mundi diligitur; & veritas in Scripturis patefacta sola cognoscitur & sic diligitur, ut secundum eam vita omnis institutur, fides & conscientia bona retineatur, 1. Tim. I. 19. illi, qui Scripturam non legunt, ac ne quidem legere sinuntur, & de veritate in Scripturis patefacta, oppositoque ei mendacio liberum judicium nullum habent, amorem veritatis nullum habere possunt. Cumque amorem hunc veritatis ejurent, mirum non est, efficaciam erroris iis a Deo immitti, ut mendacio credant. Quod in iis, qui Papæ per cæcam obedientiam subjiciuntur, eique jurant, nimis manifestum est. Justa enim Dei sententia est, à S. Johanne, tanquam amanuensi Dei publicata: Qui injustè agit, adhuc amplius injustè agat; qui sordidus est, adhuc sordescat, Apoc. XXII. 11. Nam peccator ita peccati servus est, ut & lex ipsa sit lex peccati, peccato, dominium in peccatorem potens, patrocinans. Quomodo igitur non justa hæc in peccatorem, qui non credit veritati, nec eam diligit, ut per eam salvetur, sententia esset? Ideo etiam judicari, hoc est, puniri eos, quibus Deus erroris efficaciam immittit, & judicari propterea, quia non crediderunt veritati, & delectantur injustitia, Apostolus dixit. Nam tradi in errorem, & fidem mendacii, poena gravissima est, quam hodie experiri Papæ populum, apud quem omne veritatis lumen extinctum est, res ipsa clamat. Et eò gravius isthoc judicium est, quia est poena ingratitudinis post veritatem publicè manifestatam, & per eam posteriora fiunt deteriora prioribus; neque per verbum veritatis conconverti possunt, quod ipsimet sibi interfecerunt,& non habent victimam pro peccato,quia Christi justitiam rejecerunt, eúmque denuo crucifigunt,quæ secunda mors est. Qui etiam ἀναπολόγητοι sunt,quia mendacio credunt,cùm veritati non credant, cùm tamen mendacium sint tenebræ,& veritas sit lux,hoc est,se lucem esse,omni conscientiæ probet; mendacium autem apud conscientiam hominis testimonium & suffragium non reperiat. Jam & Papæ corpus esse Bestiam illam, quæ Babylonicam meretricem, Papam ipsum portat, alibi Myst. Babyl. M. Dissert. VIII. § 2. eo argumento demonstravimus,quia ejus corpus est Imperium Romanum Pseudo-Christianum , à Romano Ethnico ortum, Israeli carnali haud absimile, per sanguinis Christi professionem coloratum, & sanguinis sanctorum , blasphemiarúmque reum; sub Imperatore Constantino M. septem dynastiis, totidémque directoribus distinctum, quarum quinque post Phocam ceciderunt una, Imperium Græcum stetit,supervenientibus in Occidente Regno Italico & Germanico, quod decem Regibus sociatis pro Papa,adversus Christum, unicum Ecclesiæ caput decertavit,& ab eodem denique victum est.
units.tr: For these are "those who are perishing" [οἱ ἀπολλύμενοι], who did not receive the love of the truth that they might be saved, and to whom God sends a working of error, so that they should believe the lie, that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness (2 Thess. 2:10–13). They also come under the name of the Beast carrying the Babylonian harlot (Rev. 17:3, 7, 8). If the Pope is the son of perdition [ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας], destroying [ἀπολλύων], then his body, which we have explained more fully above, is perishing [ἀπολλύμενον]. For although we judge far less about the persons of this mystical body than about the person of the mystical head itself, mindful of the Apostle who forbids us to judge another's servant (Rom. 14:4), and though we do not doubt that some who are joined to the external communion of the Pope will be saved, through the words of the foundation which are not entirely effaced in them, and through the neglect of the poison which superstition has mixed with them, as through fire [ὡς διὰ πυρός] (1 Cor. 3:15), and with difficulty [μόλις] (1 Pet. 4:18), because of the tyranny and snares of Satan, far more searchingly, when the Church has left the communion of the Pope, yet they will be saved, nonetheless. Still, we have no doubt that all those who receive the Pope, as members of the Pope's head, and his mark in their right hand or on their foreheads (Rev. 13:16), and who do not repent of their murders, sorceries, fornication and thefts (Rev. 9:21), are among the number of those who perish, since the fate of the head and the body must be the same. And since the love of truth is that by which truth is loved for its own sake, and not for the sake of the fleeting pleasures of the flesh and the advantages of the world; and since truth revealed in the Scriptures is alone known and so loved that the whole of life is ordered according to it, and faith and a good conscience are retained (1 Tim. 1:19), those who do not read the Scriptures, and are not even allowed to read them, and who have no free judgement about the truth revealed in the Scriptures and the lie opposed to it, cannot have the love of the truth. Since they renounce this love of the truth, it is no wonder that a working of error is sent to them by God, so that they believe the lie. That this is so in those who submit to the Pope by blind obedience and swear allegiance to him is all too plain. For it is a just sentence of God, proclaimed by St John as God's amanuensis: He who does wrong, let him do wrong still; he who is filthy, let him be filthy still (Rev. 22:11). For the sinner is so much the slave of sin that even the law itself becomes the law of sin, exercising dominion over the sinner, a patron of sin. How then would this sentence not be just against the sinner who does not believe the truth, nor love it, so as to be saved by it? Hence the Apostle said that they are also judged, that is, punished, to whom God sends a working of error, and judged for this reason, because they did not believe the truth and took pleasure in unrighteousness. For to be handed over to error and to faith in a lie is the most grievous punishment, as the very fact now cries out, which the Pope's people, among whom every light of truth has been put out, experience. And this judgement is all the heavier because it is a punishment for ingratitude after the truth has been publicly made manifest, and through it the latter things become worse than the former; nor can they be converted by the word of truth, since they have themselves put Him to death, and they do not have a sacrifice for sin, because they have rejected the righteousness of Christ and crucify Him again, which is the second death. They are also without excuse [ἀναπολόγητοι], because they believe the lie while not believing the truth, although the lie is darkness and the truth is light, that is, the truth proves itself to be light to every conscience; but the lie finds no witness or support in the conscience of man. Moreover, that the body of the Pope is that Beast which carries the Babylonian harlot, the Pope himself, we have demonstrated elsewhere, Myst. Babyl. M. Dissert. VIII. § 2., by this argument: that his body is the pseudo-Christian Roman Empire, arising from the pagan Roman, not unlike the carnal Israel, coloured by a profession of the blood of Christ, and guilty of the blood of the saints and of blasphemies; divided under the Emperor Constantine the Great into seven dynasties, and as many directors, of which five fell after Phocas, one, the Greek Empire, stood, while the kingdoms of Italy and Germany arose in the West, which, joined with ten kings for the Pope, fought against Christ, the sole head of the Church, and was at last defeated by Him.

units.la: LXXV. Corpori caput dominatur. Sic & corpori suo Papa.
units.tr: LXXV. The head rules the body. So too the Pope rules his own body.

units.la: Nam ille corpus ex iis, qui Christi solius corpus & peculium esse debuerant, sibi aptans,& illud libertate à Christo parta nefariè spolians, sibi & libidini suæ subjecit. Nihil enim hic Christus fecit, sed Antichristus omnia. Et qua ratione id perfecerit, operæ pretium est cognoscere. Postquam enim Bonifacius III. Imperatoris Phocæ indultu,titulum Universalis Episcopi, reclamante Oriente, & in Occidente refragantibus non paucis, obtinuit,corpus sibi ex populoChristiano,ejúsque clericis & laicis, uti vocant, formandum, & tyrannidi suæ subjiciendum putavit. Nam & Imperatores atque Reges, & populum, & populi doctores atque pastores, & universam Ecclesiam miris artibus, & non sine mysterio iniquitatis efficaciter operante , sibi subjecit. Imperatoris enim jugum excussit , eo modo, quem supra ex Guicciardino,& in Historia Papatus fusius expositimus. Populum barbararum gentium invasionibus & inundationibus rudem atque ignarum factum, in ignorantia fovit,& sciendi desiderium per fidem implicitam, aliásque rationes extinxit,ut opportuniore eo ad ferendum jugum uteretur. Porrò Scripturæ verba non abjecit equidem, sed eorum sensum, ceu animam, sui arbitrii fecit, & paulatim etiam ejusdem versiones & lectionem prohibuit,ejus loco traditiones ἀδήλως & imagines mutas , ceu laicorum doctores, invexit, cultum omnem peregrina lingua celebrari jussit, poculum Eucharisticum laicis surripuit, jus eligendi pastores eidem ereptum in alios transtulit, jugum ciborum & dierum, aliarúmque ceremoniarum oculos ignari vulgi fascinantium introduxit,innumeris expilationibus,variis satisfactionum,dispensationum,Missarum, indulgentiarum,Jubilæorum. Purgatorii ignis &c. prætextibus effictis,populum emunxit,& resistentibus apertam vim & sævissimas persecutiones opposuit, denique eò promovit, ut populo eidem persuasum esset, non licere sibi absque sacerdotibus pararis & proxenetis ad Deum accedere. Doctores in sua verba jurare subegit,& studiis vel promoventibus Monarchiam suam,vel saltem ei non obstantibus distraxit; Academias eorum Episcoporum potestate solutos sibi mancipavit. Monachos & monasteria similiter ab Episcoporum jurisdictione exemptos,& sibi subjectos,arctissimè devinxit, & pro viribus suis eorum ordines auxit,ut fides suæ Monarchiæ hyperaspistes, ærarium etiam publicum locupletantes,experiretur. Sacerdotes & Pastores Missæ quæstui habitæ unicè adstrinxit,impositio cœlibatu impuro & corrupit, & sibi uni solíque devinxit ; atque per casus sibi reservatos, & dispensationes à se solo concedendas jura eorum audacter infregit. Episcoporum dignitatem & jurisdictionem,Monachos & Academias iis subtrahendo, & Ecclesias commendatoriis atque curtisanis,qui ab omni potestate eorum liberi uni Papæ obnoxii fuerunt, committendo ; causas & judicia eorum per reservationes & appellationes ad se devolvendo , multisque aliis modis iis dominando,mirè accidit. Metropolitanorum confirmationem, redemptione Pallii carissimo pretio constantis impetrandam,sibi vindicavit,& mensibus Papalibus atque Annatis introductis, Synodis Provincialibus ad se pertractis,suffraganeis eorum jurisdictione solutis, eorum jura non parum delibavit , omnes quoque Ecclesiarum summas prærogativas in ministros suos Datarios, Cancellarios, Aulicos, aliáque dominationis suæ instrumenta transtulit. Episcopos omnes immediatè non à Christo, sed à Ie pendere pertendens,iis,velut clitellariis mancipiis ad inserviendum monarchiæ suæ adegit. Denique totam Ecclesiam per Concilia generalia repræsentatam, suæ libidini subjecit, jus Concilia convocandi, moderandi,suffragatores in iis, quos vellet constituendi, confirmandi,ceu Divino etiam jure sibi collatum & eximium, rapuit, & eò rem perduxit,ut suppressa Conciliorum potestate fidei decreta etiam absque Concilio & extra illud, conderet,& pro infallibilibus obtruderet, quod nil aliud est, quàm Concilia abolere, & cuncta sibi, ceu novo oraculo ; quale olim Urim & Tummim fuerunt, subjicere. Graves enim conjecturæ suppetunt, nunquam deinceps fore,ut ullum Concilium generale,ex Papali etiam orbe suo convocet, ut sine arbitris solus regnet. Nam & ipsa Papæ jactata infallibilitas in jure, imò quod novissimè etiam Jesuitæ in Collegio Lutetiæ Claremontano ceu Catholicæ fidei articulum, propugnarunt, etiam in facto, etiam extra Concilium, jugulum Conciliis omnibus incidit.
units.tr: For he fits to himself a body taken from those who ought to have been the body and property of Christ alone, and he wickedly strips it of the liberty won by Christ and subjects it to himself and his lust. Christ did nothing here; Antichrist did everything. It is worth knowing how he accomplished this. After Boniface III obtained, by the indulgence of the Emperor Phocas, the title Universal Bishop, while the East protested and not a few in the West objected, he thought that he should form for himself a body out of the Christian people, its clergy and laity, as they are called, and subject it to his tyranny. He subjected to himself, by wonderful arts and by a mystery of iniquity working effectively, both the emperors and kings, the people, the teachers and ministers of the people, and the whole Church. He threw off the yoke of the Emperor, in the manner which we have set out above from Guicciardini and more fully in the Historia Papatus. The People, made rude and ignorant by the invasions and inundations of the barbarous nations, he kept in ignorance, and by implicit faith and other devices he extinguished the desire to know, so that he might use them more conveniently for bearing the yoke. Indeed, he did not discard the words of Scripture, but he made their sense, as if it were the soul, his own to decide; and gradually he also forbade their translations and reading, and in their place he introduced traditions [ἀδήλως, obscurely] and dumb images as teachers for the laity. He ordered all worship to be conducted in a foreign tongue; he snatched the Eucharistic cup from the laity; he transferred to others the right of choosing ministers, which had been taken from the people. He introduced the yoke of foods and days and other ceremonies, which dazzle the eyes of the ignorant crowd. By countless extortions under the pretexts he invented, such as satisfactions, dispensations, Masses, indulgences, Jubilees, and the fire of Purgatory, he drained the people; and he opposed open force and the most savage persecutions to those who resisted. At last he advanced to the point that the people were persuaded that they could not approach God without priests as their agents and go-betweens. He compelled teachers to swear to his words, and he drew them away into studies that either advanced his monarchy or at least did not hinder it. He made the universities his own, freed from the power of the bishops. Monks and monasteries, likewise exempted from the jurisdiction of the bishops and made subject to himself, he bound most tightly, and according to his strength he increased their orders, so that they might serve as the champions of his monarchy and, at the same time, enrich the public treasury. He bound priests and ministers of the Mass, which was made a source of profit, exclusively to himself, and by imposing an impure celibacy he corrupted them, binding them to himself alone; and by cases reserved to himself and dispensations to be granted by himself alone, he boldly infringed their rights. He stripped the bishops of their dignity and jurisdiction, taking away monks and universities from them, and entrusting churches to commendatory and courtier clergy, who, free from all their power, were answerable to the Pope alone; by transferring their causes and judgments to himself through reservations and appeals, and by lording it over them in many other ways, he wonderfully prevailed. He claimed for himself the confirmation of metropolitans, which was to be obtained at the very dear price of the redemption of the pallium; and by introducing papal months and annates, by drawing provincial synods to himself, and by freeing their suffragans from the jurisdiction of their metropolitans, he not a little diminished their rights. He also transferred all the chief prerogatives of the churches to his ministers, the datary, the chancellors, the courtiers, and other instruments of his dominion. Insisting that all bishops depend immediately not on Christ but on himself, he forced them, like pack-animals, to serve his monarchy. Finally, he subjected the whole Church, represented through general Councils, to his lust. He seized for himself, as a right given even by divine law and as his own special prerogative, the right to convene councils, to direct them, and to appoint and confirm those who vote in them as he pleases. He brought the matter to the point that, with the power of the councils suppressed, he made decrees of faith even without a council and apart from one, and forced them upon the people as infallible; this is nothing other than abolishing councils and subjecting everything to himself as to a new oracle, like the Urim and Thummim of old. For there are strong grounds for conjecture that henceforth he will never convene any general council, even from his own papal world, so that he may reign alone without arbiters. For the Pope's boasted infallibility, both in law and, what the Jesuits in the Clermont College at Paris most recently defended as an article of the Catholic faith, in fact, even outside a Council, strikes at the throat of all councils.

units.la: LXXVI. Rationes porro,quibus Antichristianismi probrum à Papa gnathones ejus amoliri contendunt,ficulneæ sunt. Ante omnia enim sicuti Judæi Messiam venisse, ita illi Antichristum venisse, adeóque Papam Antichristum esse posse negant.
units.tr: LXXVI. Next, the arguments by which the Pope's flatterers try to remove the disgrace of Antichristianism from him are flimsy. First of all, they deny that the Pope can be Antichrist, just as the Jews deny that the Messiah has come.

units.la: Nam Evangelium in universo orbe ante ejus adventum prædicandum,Matth. XXIV. 14. nondum prædicatum esse,objiciunt. Verùm ibi nihil de Antichristi adventu dicitur. Et sive per πλήρη finem excidium Hierosolymæ intelligatur, pridem illud peractum est , & ante illud ἐν ἀλη τῇ οἰκουμένῃ in
units.tr: For they object that the Gospel has not yet been preached in the whole world before his coming, Matt. 24:14. But nothing about the coming of Antichrist is said there. And whether by the complete [πλήρη] end the destruction of Jerusalem is understood, that was accomplished long ago, and before it the Gospel was preached [ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, in the whole inhabited world]

units.la: Pontificiorum argumenta contraria ad partes respiciunt, Antichristum illam, quibus praedicare conantur, Antichristum nondum venisse; in tota habitabili, non propriè, sed synecdochicè, hoc est, in plurimis gentibus Evangelium prædicatum est: sive finis mundi, scire convenit, post revelatum Antichristum & casum ejus maximam multitudinem gentium, & ipsos quoque Judæos convertendos esse, Apoc. XI. 15. XV. 1. 2. 3. Non ergo adventus Antichristi signum proximè adventum Christi ultimum præcedens esse potest. Cum ipsa autem prima Evangelii prædicatione jam tum mysterium iniquitatis operabatur, & Antichristus in mundo fuit, 2. Thess. II. 7. 1. Joh. II. 18. IV. 3. Non debuit igitur universalis prædicatio Evangelii adventum Antichristi præcedere. Sed manifestationem Antichristi in plenario dominationis suæ usu publicatio Evangelii, & prædicatio vincens, Apoc. VI. 2. consummatio testificationis duorum testium plenam fidem doctrinæ de Christo facientium, arcem idolatriæ evertentium, idola subigentium, Sathanam de throno dejicientium, ibid. XI. 7. præcedere debuit, & processit. S. Paulus vero revelationem Antichristi amoto τῷ κατέχοντι eo, qui detinebat subjiciens, 2. Thess. II. 6. 7. non simpliciter Imperatorem, seu Imperium Romanum de medio sublatum, hoc est, desolatum iri ante revelationem Antichristi, sed sublatum iri tum Romæ & in Italia, ex qua Imperium ad Germanos solo nomine tenus Romanos (cum tamen nomen Romani solum sine Imperio, non potuerit esse illud κατέχον detinens) pervenire debuit, & pervenit: tum quoad supremam potestatem, quam paulatim Papa sibi rapuit, & hactenus retinet, prædixit. Igitur ὁ ἐκ μέσου ἀρθεὶς ex medio tolli, non notat simpliciter desolari, aboleri; sed cedere & non amplius Ex legem revelandum detinere, impedire. Quandiu enim Imperator Romæ imperium cum vi imperii retinuit, tandiu Papa se declarare ut Deum, & supra Deum & σέβασμα dictum se extollere non potuit, quia ut homo peccati revelaretur in sua ὑπερφανὴ elatione in omnem dictum Deum, necesse erat ei dari potestatem definiendi, decidendi, præcipiendi, & eum ad hoc a Principibus, potestatem suam ipsi dantibus, Apoc. XVII. 13. ipsique adeò servientibus juvari; & ut se efferret in omne dictum Augustum, necesse pariter fuit, Principem Romanum locum facere homini peccati, ei relinquere terram magnam; ipsum autem debilitari, & cogi tandem ipsi concedere, & se subjicere. Quod factum esse ab Imperatoribus Ludovicum Bavarum sequentibus, sive Romani, sive Germani dicantur & sint, historiarum monumenta probant. Neque de nihilo est, quod Dan. VII. 8. &c. dicitur de Cornu parvo, seu Antichristo, fore ut crescat, antequam destruatur corpus quartæ Bestiæ, quod Imperium Germanicum est; quódque ibid. II. 40. &c. pedes statuæ unum Regnum faciunt, quartum scilicet Romanum, in quo distinguuntur crura ferrea, Imperium Romanum simplex sine mistura, sub Imperatoribus gentilibus: deinde tibiæ, itémque pedes, sive plantæ testaceæ & ferreæ, hoc est, Imperium Romanum divisum & mixtum ex hierarchia & imperio, ubi decem digiti notare divisionem regnorum, potestatem suam Bestiæ dantium possunt. Sed Imperium Romanum pridem è medio sublatum esse tam manifestum est, ut & Archiepiscopus quidam Aventino Annal. lib. VII. teste dixerit: Imperatorem esse vanam appellationem, & solam umbram: & Bellarminus ipse de Antichr. cap. 5. fassus sit, Romam imperium amisisse: & Thomas Aquinas in 2. Thess. II. lect. 2. propter hoc ipsum non potuerit alia ratione negare, quòd Antichristus venerit, quàm Papam Imperatoris in locum surrogando. Quomodo, inquit, est hoc, quia jam diu gentes à Romano Imperio recesserunt, & tamen necdum venit Antichristus? Dicendum est, quod nondum cessavit, sed est commutatum de temporali in spirituale. Addit, Papam esse ultimum caput Imperii, sed sine nomine Imperatoris Romani. Si igitur, uti Bellarminus cap. 15. dicit, Antichristus est ultimus Rex, qui tenebit Romanum Imperium, tamen sine nomine Romani Imperatoris; & quod Thomas assumit; Papa est ultimus Rex tenens Romanum Imperium sine nomine Imperatoris: invicta conclusio erit, quòd Papa sit Antichristus. Futilis porro est illa ratio, quòd Elias & Enochus ceu duo testes, adventum Antichristi præcessuri, Apoc. XI. 3. &c. nondum venerint. Nam Eliæ adventus, Mal. IV. 5. signum adventus Christi, non Antichristi ponitur; & illum venisse, Christus ipse testis est, Matth. XVII. 12. Duo testes illi, Vetus & Novum Testamentum in Scriptura loquentia, & pauci nonnulli Antichristo se opponentes, & ex iisdem loquentes sunt. Henoch autem translatus est, ne videret mortem, Hebr. XI. 5. non igitur, perinde ut testes illi, mori debet. Quòd Antichristus juge sacrificium, hoc est, Missam abrogaturus sit, & nondum ea abrogata, nondum venerit Antichristus, nequicquam illi ex Dan. VIII. 12. probare conantur. Antichristus enim nec verbum Dei, nec Sacramenta tollere debuit, quia alias ne speciem quidem Ecclesiæ retineret: nec Missam, quæ non juge sacrificium, sed ejus unici abnegatio est, aboliturus erat, qui inter præcipua mysteria Missam habet. Si juge sacrificium illud typicum intelligitur, Antiochus illud abrogavit; sin verum, hoc est, Christus verum sacrificium nostrum, intercedens pro nobis, & sedens in dextra Dei εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς in perpetuum, Hebr. X. 12. 14. & oratio in fide atque confessio Christi Regis & justitiæ ejus intelligitur, certè illud Antichristus abrogare debuit, & Papa, Missa & ejus idololatria multiplice introducta, abrogavit. Quod de nomine Bestiæ, seu potius numeri Bestiæ 666. & charactere Bestiæ, Apoc. XIII. 17. 18. certi quid constiturum sit, si Antichristus advenisset, iidem objiciunt, dilutum certè nimis est. Nam nec nomen proprium Antichristi, sed nomen numeri Bestiæ, hoc est, Ecclesiæ Antichristianæ, ibi ponitur: & illud non à quovis cognitum iri, eo innuitur, quòd ad cognoscendum illud Σοφία καὶ νοῦς sapientia & intelligentia, vers. 18. requiritur, adeóque nomen illud mysticè intelligi innuitur. Sufficit autem, quòd nomen omnium Pontificum sit Ἀλλη- ν⊗, & nomen Ecclesiæ Romanæ sit רומית & Ἐκκλησία Ἰταλικὴ, Ecclesia Italica, & in iis nominibus numerus 666. reperitur; quódque Papæ lex sit παράδοσις traditio superveniens verbo Christi, qualis est, quæ libris sex decretalium comprehenditur, quibus sex demptis 660. remanent; verbum Christi & Apostolorum rum significantes, quia numerus 12. seu duodecim Apostolorum, ceu cubica radix numeri 660. adhibitus numerum illum exacte exhaurit. Constat autem satis, traditionem humanam Papalis Ecclesiae fundamentum unicum esse. Quid vero sit χαράγμα character Bestiae suscipere, Apoc. XIII. 16. satis jam constat. Sicut Dei legem habere pro frontali nomen Agni & Patris ejus habere scriptum in frontibus, ibid. XIV. 1. est illud manu suscipere, opere exequi, & in omni actu ante oculos habere: ita Bestiae characterem in manu & fronte habere, est ejus legem profiteri & servare. Et sine hoc charactere non posse emere vel vendere, ibid. XIII. 17. est pertinere ad civitatem illam magnam, quae emporium est, & cum Tyro comparatur. Ita enim Simonia Bestiae per μυστήριον perstringitur; quia ibi remissio peccatorum, officia venduntur a praepositis, & emuntur a plebejis.
units.tr: The Papists' arguments run against their own position. They try to maintain that Antichrist has not yet come, and that the Gospel has been preached "in the whole inhabited world" (in tota habitabili) not strictly but by synecdoche, that is, among very many nations. Yet we should recognise that before the end of the world, after Antichrist is revealed and has fallen, a very great multitude of the nations, and the Jews themselves, are to be converted (Rev. 11:15; 15:1–3). The coming of Antichrist therefore cannot be the sign immediately preceding the final coming of Christ. Moreover, the mystery of iniquity was already at work from the very first preaching of the Gospel, and Antichrist was already in the world (2 Thess. 2:7; 1 John 2:18; 4:3). The universal preaching of the Gospel therefore need not have preceded the coming of Antichrist. Rather, the publication of the Gospel and its victorious preaching (Rev. 6:2), together with the completion of the testimony of the two witnesses, who make the doctrine of Christ fully believed, overthrow the citadel of idolatry, subdue idols and cast Satan from his throne (ibid. 11:7), ought to and did precede the manifestation of Antichrist in the full exercise of his dominion. St Paul, for his part, foretold that the revelation of Antichrist would follow the removal of "the one who restrains" (τῷ κατέχοντι), that is, of him who held back (2 Thess. 2:6–7). He did not mean simply that the Emperor, or the Roman Empire, would be taken out of the way, that is, left desolate, before the revelation of Antichrist. He meant that it would be removed at Rome and in Italy, from which the empire would pass to the Germans, who bore only the name of Romans (though the name of Roman without the empire could not be that which restrains), and that it did so pass. He also foretold that the power would be removed in respect of supreme authority, which the Pope gradually seized for himself and has kept until now. So the phrase "taken out of the way" (ὁ ἐκ μέσου ἀρθεὶς) does not simply mean "laid waste" or "abolished", but "to give way and no longer to hold back the revelation of the law", that is, to hinder it. For as long as the Emperor kept the imperial power at Rome with its force, the Pope could not declare himself to be God, or exalt himself above God and above everything called sebasma (2 Thess. 2:4). For the man of sin to be revealed in his arrogant exaltation over every so-called God, it was necessary that he be given the power to define, to decide and to command, and that he be aided in this by the princes who gave him their power and served him (Rev. 17:13). And for him to raise himself above every so-called Augustus, it was equally necessary that the Roman prince make room for the man of sin, leave him "the great land", and himself be weakened and at last forced to yield and submit. That this was done by the emperors who followed Louis of Bavaria, whether they are called and are Romans or Germans, the records of history prove. Nor is it without reason that Daniel 7:8 and following says of the little horn, that is, Antichrist, that it will grow before the body of the fourth beast is destroyed, which is the German Empire. Nor is it without reason that Daniel 2:40 and following says that the feet of the statue make one kingdom, namely the fourth, the Roman, in which the iron legs stand for the simple Roman Empire without admixture under the pagan emperors; and then the shins and likewise the feet or soles, partly of clay and partly of iron, that is, the Roman Empire divided and mixed of hierarchy and empire, in which the ten toes, which signify the division of kingdoms, can give their power to the beast. But that the Roman Empire was removed from the midst long ago is so plain that a certain archbishop, according to the witness of Aventinus (Annales, bk 7), said that the emperor was an empty title and only a shadow; and Bellarmine himself, in De Antichristo, ch. 5, confesses that Rome lost the empire; and Thomas Aquinas, on 2 Thess. 2, lect. 2, could give no other reason for denying that Antichrist had come, precisely because of this, than that the Pope had been substituted in the place of the Emperor. "How is this," he says, "since the nations have long since departed from the Roman Empire, and yet Antichrist has not come? It must be said that it has not ceased, but has been changed from the temporal to the spiritual." He adds that the Pope is the last head of the empire, but without the name of Roman Emperor. If therefore, as Bellarmine says in ch. 15, Antichrist is the last king who will hold the Roman Empire, yet without the name of Roman Emperor, and if what Thomas assumes is true, that the Pope is the last king holding the Roman Empire without the name of Emperor, the conclusion will be unanswerable: the Pope is Antichrist. Further, the argument that Elijah and Enoch, as the two witnesses who are to precede the coming of Antichrist (Rev. 11:3 and following), have not yet come, is feeble. For the coming of Elijah is set down as the sign of the coming of Christ, not of Antichrist (Mal. 4:5), and Christ himself testifies that he has come (Matt. 17:12). Those two witnesses are the Old and New Testaments speaking in Scripture, together with a few men who oppose Antichrist and speak from the same Scriptures. Enoch, however, "was translated that he should not see death" (Heb. 11:5), and so, unlike those witnesses, he is not bound to die. Their attempt to prove from Daniel 8:12 that Antichrist is to abolish the continual sacrifice, that is, the Mass, and that since it has not yet been abolished Antichrist has not yet come, is in vain. For Antichrist was to remove neither the word of God nor the sacraments, since otherwise he would not even keep the appearance of the Church; nor was he to abolish the Mass, which is not a continual sacrifice but the denial of its one sacrifice, since he who holds the Mass among the chief mysteries would hardly abolish it. If the continual sacrifice is understood as the typical one, Antiochus abolished it. If it is understood as the true sacrifice, that is, Christ our true sacrifice, interceding for us and sitting at the right hand of God eis to diēnekes, for ever (Heb. 10:12–14), and the prayer and confession of Christ the King and of his righteousness in faith, then certainly Antichrist ought to abolish that, and the Pope, with the Mass and its manifold idolatry introduced, has abolished it. As to the name of the beast, or rather the number of the beast, 666, and the mark of the beast (Rev. 13:17–18), the same people object that something certain would be settled if Antichrist had come. This is certainly too easily refuted. For the name given there is not the proper name of Antichrist, but the name of the number of the beast, that is, of the Antichristian Church; and that it would not be known by everyone is hinted by the fact that to know it "wisdom and understanding" (Sophia kai nous, v. 18) are required, so that the name is hinted to be understood mystically. It is enough, however, that the name of all the Popes is Lateinos (the Latin), and the name of the Roman Church is rwmyt (Romit) and Ekklēsia Italikē, the Italian Church, and in these names the number 666 is found. The Pope's law is paradosis, a tradition added to the word of Christ, such as is contained in the six books of the Decretals; with six removed, 660 remains, which signifies the word of Christ and the Apostles, because the number twelve, or the twelve Apostles, as the cube root of 660, when applied, exactly exhausts that number. It is indeed sufficiently clear that human tradition is the sole foundation of the Papal Church. What it is to receive the charagma, the mark of the beast (Rev. 13:16), is now sufficiently clear. Just as to have the law of God as a frontlet, and to have the name of the Lamb and of his Father written on the foreheads (ibid. 14:1), means to take it in hand, to carry it out in deed and to keep it before one's eyes in every action, so to have the mark of the beast in the hand and forehead is to profess and keep its law. And "not to be able to buy or sell" without this mark (ibid. 13:17) means to belong to that great city which is a marketplace and is compared with Tyre. For in this way the simony of the beast is struck through by the mysterion, because there the forgiveness of sins and offices are sold by the prelates and bought by the common people.

units.la: LXXVII. Papam porro Antichristum non esse, ex Antichristi, qualem illi describunt, characteribus aliisque argumentis probare conantur.
units.tr: LXXVII. That the Pope is not Antichrist: they try to prove it from the marks of Antichrist as they describe him, and from other arguments.

units.la: Sed characteres illos & ideam Antichristi ab illis perhibitam falsam esse, supra convicimus. Cadentibus ergo illis, argumenta ex illis arcessita simul concidunt. At nec reliqua argumenta, quibus labem Antichristianismi a Papa abstergere conantur, ullius momenti sunt. Licet enim Papa se servum Christi, imo & Servum servorum nuncupet, non ideo Antichristus esse definit. Nam & Sathanae ministri, Pseudapostoli, dolosi operarii, transformant se in Apostolos Christi, 2. Cor. XI. 13. qui non ideo Christi aemuli & hostes non sunt. Antichristus enim hostis & aemulus Christi non professus, sed dissimulatus, & in mysterio latens esse debuit, 2. Thess. II. 7. Apoc. XVII. 5. Agni cornua gestare, sed ut Draco loqui, ibid. XIII. 11. dicitur. Monstrum igitur est, cujus capita veriora religionis cornuum Agni instar, quibus Christiano orbi illudit: at doctrinae impiae & blasphemae de Missa meritis, satisfactionibus, Purgatorio, invocatione Sanctorum, &c. Os Draconis, blasphema loquentis, sunt. Quid igitur inanes tituli sine re juvant? Qualiscunque Papa videri vult, aemulus Christi est, etiam nomina ejus, qualia sunt Caput, Petra, Fundamentum, Sponsus Ecclesiae: & hostis Christi est, quia in doctrina, cultu & regimine Ecclesiae ei se opponit. Servum servorum se appellat degeneris instar & maledicti Noae nepotis, & non ex officio & re, uti Canonistae loquuntur, sed ex humilitate, tanto deterior, quod simul hypocritam se prodit, simul depositia servi humilitate, pueros & puellas heri sui cadit, comedit, bibit & inebriatur, Luc. XII. 45. Quo sensu Antichristus neget quod Jesus sit Christus, & neget Patrem & Filium, & neget, quod Jesus Christus venerit in carne, 1. Joh. II. 22. 23. IV. 3. & quomodo id in Papa impletum sit, supra fusius expositum. Non enim Antichristus palam ipsis syllabis dicet, Jesum non esse Christum, vel negabit Patrem & Filium, & quod Jesus Christus in carne venerit. Satis est, quod ejus doctrina talis est, ut qui eam tenent, censendi sint non confiteri JesumChristum in carne venientem, 2. Joh. v. 7. 1. Joh. II. 22. Quo pertinent regulae illae Scripturae: Omnis transgrediens,
units.tr: But I have already shown above that those marks, and the idea of Antichrist put forward by them, are false. So when those fall, the arguments drawn from them fall with them. Nor do the remaining arguments, by which they try to wipe the stain of Antichristianity from the Pope, carry any weight. For although the Pope calls himself "servant of Christ," and even "Servant of servants," he does not for that reason cease to be Antichrist. For the ministers of Satan too, "false apostles, deceitful workers, transform themselves into apostles of Christ" (2 Cor. 11:13), and yet they are not therefore no rivals and enemies of Christ. Antichrist was to be an enemy and rival of Christ not openly professed but disguised, and hidden in mystery (2 Thess. 2:7; Rev. 17:5). He is said to have "horns like a lamb, but to speak like a dragon" (Rev. 13:11). So he is a monster whose heads, like "the horns of the Lamb," are the more genuine parts of religion, by which he mocks the Christian world; but his impious and blasphemous doctrines about the merits of the Mass, satisfactions, Purgatory, the invocation of saints, and so on, are "the mouth of the Dragon," speaking blasphemy. Why then do empty titles help without the reality? Whatever kind of Pope he wishes to appear, he is a rival of Christ, and even his titles, such as Head, Rock, Foundation, and Bridegroom of the Church, are rivals of Christ's own. He is an enemy of Christ because in doctrine, worship and the government of the Church he sets himself against Christ. He calls himself "servant of servants" like the degenerate grandson of cursed Noah, and not "by office and reality," as the canonists put it, "but by humility." He is so much the worse for it, because at the same time he betrays himself as a hypocrite: having laid aside the humility of a servant, he beats his fellow-servants, "the boys and girls," eats, drinks and gets drunk (Luke 12:45). In this sense Antichrist denies "that Jesus is the Christ, and denies the Father and the Son, and denies that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh" (1 John 2:22, 23; 4:3), and how this has been fulfilled in the Pope has been set out more fully above. For Antichrist will not openly say in so many words that Jesus is not the Christ, or deny the Father and the Son, or that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. It is enough that his doctrine is such that those who hold it are to be judged "not to confess Jesus Christ coming in the flesh" (2 John 7; 1 John 2:22). To this belong those rules of Scripture: "Everyone who transgresses,"

units.la: & non manens in doctrina Christi, Deum non habet, 2. Joh. v. 9. Si maneat in vobis, quod ab initio audivistis, & vos in Filio & Patre manebitis, 1. Joh. II. 24. Omne mendacium ex veritate non est, ibid. v. 21. Non tantum ergo syllabis expungendis abnegatur Jesus Christus, qui in carne venit, sed etiam negando eo, quod in pondere, vigore & consequentia illius veritatis est, & affirmando id, quod consequentia illius articuli destruit. Si enim mendacium ex veritate non est, tum quod ex veritate est, veritas est. Non igitur verba ἀρνέομαι negare, ibid. v. 22. & ὁμολογεῖν confiteri, ibid. IV. 3. obstant. Nam ex Scripturae usu negare Deum non eorum duntaxat est, qui primam illam veritatem Deus est, verbo negant, sed eorum etiam, qui Deum se cognoscere confessi, eundem factis abnegant, Tit. I. 16. & abnegare fidem dicuntur non solum infideles, sed illi etiam, qui suis, maxime domesticis, non providen t, 1. Tim. V. 8 Et sicut affirmativa illa: Qui confitetur Jesum Christum in carnem venisse, ex Deo est, 1. Joh. IV. 2. confessionem cordis pariter & oris exigit, nec omnes tamen illi, qui ore confitentur ex Deo sunt: ita negativa sequentia: Qui non confitetur, Jesum Christum venisse in carne, ex Deo non est, arguunt, non confiteri aliquem, quod Jesus Christus venerit in carne, qui ore id confessus opere & doctrina reliqua id abnegaverit. Falsum & illud est, quod Antichristus rotundis verbis & palam se proclamaturus sit Deum, & alium praeter se Deum passurus sit. Nam in Templo Dei, Ecclesia Christianorum sedere, non Deus, sed ὡς Θεὸς sicut Deus, 2. Thess. II. 4. Deum Maozim in loco suo venerari, Dan. XI. 38. & ἀπατᾶν decipere per mysterium iniquitatis, 2. Thess. II. 7. 10. imo etiam perinde ut alii Pseudo-Christi & Pseudo-Prophetae, dicere: Hic est Christus, in eremo est, Matth. XXIV. 23. &c. & μορφωσιν deformationem pietatis, Scripturam retinere, & δύναμιν potentiam tamen ejus abnegare, 2. Tim. III. 5. Pseudo-Propheta esse, & cornua etiam Agni habere debuit. Neque etiam illud obstat, quod Papa se non Deum vel Christum, sed vicarium Christi appellat. Inter Regem enim & vicarium Regis hoc interest, quod ille potestatem a Deo, vel populo, hic a Rege commissam habet. Interim utrumque idem facit. Sic igitur Vicarius Christi habet eandem potestatem, & facit idem quod Christus. Tum Vicarius & Rex uterque homo est. Si igitur Papa est Vicarius Dei, proprie Deus est. Demonstrat vero Papa se esse Deum, 2. Thess. II. 4. licet nomen Dei sibi non praescribat, quia ea sibi tribuit quae Dei sunt: & in altari sedet atque adoratur eo modo, quo Deus ab ipsis adoratur. Denique & quae Bestiae tribuuntur, quod signa magna patratura atque effectura sit, ut ignis ex Coelo in terram decidat, imagini Bestiae spiritum datura, ut loquatur imago Bestiae, & effectura sit, ut occidantur quotquot imaginem illam non adorant, Apoc. XIII. 13. 14. 15. Ecclesiae Papali & Papae apprime conveniunt. Nam Papa sententias velut nomine Dei omnipotentis in Principes & haereticos cum eventu interitus illorum tanquam θυλαττ, adhibita etiam solenni quadam excommunicationis ceremonia, ardentes faces e sublimi jaculandi, pronuntians, imo fulminans, ignem
units.tr: "and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ, has not God" (2 John 9). "If what you have heard from the beginning abides in you, you also will abide in the Son and in the Father" (1 John 2:24). "No lie is of the truth" (ibid. v. 21). Jesus Christ, who came in the flesh, is therefore denied not only by the erasing of syllables, but also by denying what lies in the weight, force and consequence of that truth, and by affirming what the consequence of that article destroys. For if no lie is of the truth, then what is of the truth is truth. So the words "deny" [ἀρνέομαι] (ibid. v. 22) and "confess" [ὁμολογεῖν] (ibid. 4:3) are no obstacle. For in the usage of Scripture, "to deny God" belongs not only to those who deny the first truth, "God is," in words, but also to those who, having confessed that they know God, deny him by their deeds (Titus 1:16); and not only unbelievers but also those who fail to provide for their own, especially their households, are said to "deny the faith" (1 Tim. 5:8). And just as that affirmative statement, "Whoever confesses Jesus Christ to have come in the flesh is of God" (1 John 4:2), demands confession of the heart as well as of the mouth, yet not all who confess with the mouth are of God, so the negative sequel, "Whoever does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God," shows that someone does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, even if he has confessed it with his mouth, when by his works and his other teaching he denies it. It is also false that Antichrist will proclaim himself God in round words and openly, and will allow another God besides himself. For he "sits in the temple of God," the Church of the Christians, not as God but "as God" [ὡς Θεὸς] (2 Thess. 2:4); he worships "the God Maozim in his place" (Dan. 11:38); and he deceives [ἀπατᾶν] through "the mystery of iniquity" (2 Thess. 2:7, 10). Indeed, he will also say, just as other false Christs and false prophets do: "Here is Christ, he is in the wilderness" (Matt. 24:23), and so on; and he will keep the "form" [μορφωσιν] of godliness, that is, retain Scripture, but deny its "power" [δύναμιν] (2 Tim. 3:5). He had to be a false prophet, and he had to have the horns of a lamb as well. Nor does it stand in the way that the Pope calls himself not God or Christ but the vicar of Christ. For between a king and the vicar of a king this difference holds: the one has power from God or the people, the other has it committed by the king. Yet both do the same thing. So the vicar of Christ has the same power, and does the same thing, as Christ. Moreover, the vicar and the king are both men. If therefore the Pope is the vicar of God, he is properly God. Indeed the Pope "shows himself to be God" (2 Thess. 2:4), although he does not claim the name of God for himself, because he attributes to himself the things that belong to God; and he sits upon the altar and is adored in the manner in which God is adored by them. Finally, what is attributed to the Beast also fits the Papal Church and the Pope especially well: that he will work great signs, such as "fire coming down from heaven upon the earth," that he will give "breath to the image of the Beast so that the image of the Beast speaks," and that he will bring it about that "as many as do not worship that image are killed" (Rev. 13:13–15). For the Pope, in the name of almighty God, hurls sentences against princes and heretics with the result of their destruction, as if they were thunderbolts, and with a solemn ceremony of excommunication also, throwing down burning torches from on high, pronouncing and even thundering, fire

units.la: Partim illa, quibus contendunt, Papam non esse Antichristum, petita ex professione Papae, quod se famulum Christi, & servum servorum profitetur, Jesum Christum non abnegat, confitetur, quod Jesus venerit in carne, & se Deum manifeste non facit, sed vicarium Dei; alium praeter se Deum patitur, & signa, qualia Apocalypsis Bestiae tribuit, nunquam patravit. ex Cœlo frequenter elicuit. Et Bestia secunda, Ecclesia Papalis, imagini à se factæ, Antichristo, repræsentanti Deum, Christum & Ecclesiam dedit spiritum, ut loquatur, decernendo, quòd Papa habeat Spiritum infallibilitatis, & solus in Ecclesia doceat & judicet, tali cum effectu, ut, qui ad Bestiam pertinent, id crederent, & imaginem illam, Papam, adorarent; & non adorantes occiderentur, quod factum experientia, locuples testis, confirmat.
units.tr: Some of the arguments by which they contend that the Pope is not Antichrist are drawn from the Pope's profession that he is a servant of Christ and servant of servants: that he does not deny Jesus Christ, confesses that Jesus came in the flesh, and does not openly make himself God but the vicar of God; that he suffers no other God besides himself; and that he has never worked the signs which the Apocalypse attributes to the Beast, or frequently drawn fire from heaven. And the second Beast, the Papal Church, gave breath to the image made by itself, the Antichrist who represents God, Christ and the Church, so that it speaks, by decreeing that the Pope has the Spirit of infallibility and alone teaches and judges in the Church. The effect was that those who belong to the Beast believe this and adore that image, the Pope; and those who do not adore it are killed, a fact which experience, a rich witness, confirms.

units.la: LOCUS VICESIMUS OCTAVUS. De GLORIFICATIONE. BREVIARIUM.
units.tr: TWENTY-EIGHTH LOCUS. On GLORIFICATION. A SUMMARY.

units.la: Beneficiorum Christi coronis Glorificatio fidelium est. 1. Quæ vel animæ, vel totius hominis est. Illa definitur. 2. & ex 2.Cor.V.2. illustratur. 3. Animæ fidelium à corpore separatio in morte est, quæ variè describitur. 4. Mortis fidelium à morte profanorum differentia. 5. Quatenus illa timenda sit, exponitur. 6. Procurandæ ἀφθαρσίας mortis remedia. 7. Mortis processus ex Solomone describitur. 8. Post mortem alius corporis, alius animæ status est. Corpus redit ad terram. 9. Honestè deduci & sepeliri debet. 10. Reliquiæ & ossa corporis humi defodienda, non ad religiosum cultum & idololatriam prostituenda sunt. 11. Sepulturæ locus & circa eundem superstitio Papalis. 12. Sepeliendi omnes homines videntur. 13. Ritus funebres Hebræorum, Pontificiorum, Evangelicorum. 14. Anima post mortem redit ad Deum. 15. Animæ à corpore separatæ διαμονή in statu separato, quem in Cœlo obtinet; opposita migrationi in corpora hominum vel belluarum. 16. Nec non migrationi in Purgatorium. 17. Quod pluribus argumentis ponderosis refellitur. 18. Argumentis, quibus Purgatorium incrustari solet, occurritur. 19. Locus inprimis 1.Cor.III.3. pro Purgatorio obductus, vindicatur. 20. Nec Baptismus pro mortuis, ibid. XV. 29. nec veterum preces pro mortuis Purgatorio favent. 21. Purgatorii vera origo panditur. 22. Anima à corpore separata ilico plenè sanctificatur, & ab omni peccato liberatur. 23. & statim in Cœlum locum beatitudinis & gloriæ transfertur. 24. Veterum, sinus quosdam extra Cœlum, in quos animæ post mortem relegentur, fingentium, error eliditur. 25. Status animæ à corpore separatæ gloriosus est. 26. Neque dormire eas, adversus Anabaptistas, neque nihil omnino agere, adversus Socinianos, aštruitur. 27. Psychopannychitarum argumenta contraria refelluntur. 28. Animæ separatæ ignorant, quid in terris sigillatim à quovis agatur; nec in speculo essentiæ Divinæ cuncta cognoscunt. 29. Pontificiorum argumenta contraria diluuntur. 30. Canonizatio Sanctorum Papalis refellitur. 31. Religiosus Divorum cultus, juramento etiam impositò à Papa mandatus, in praxi quotidiana obtinet. 32. Argumenta prægnantia eidem opponuntur. 33. Hagiolatrarum argumenta discutiuntur. 34. Animæ cum corpore conjunctæ quædam in terram redierunt; quibus quid factum postea sit, incertum est. 35. Animæ à corpore separatæ nullæ in terram revertuntur, & hominibus apparent. 36. Neque Samuelis anima Sauli apparuit. 37. Continuatio status animarum separatarum ad Christi adventum usque. 38. Glorificatio totius hominis describitur. 39. Ejusdem gradus, ad quos exequendos Christus ex Cœlo redibit. 40. Vaticinia de adventu Domini ad Judicium. 41. Illusorum contrariis argumentis S. Petrus respondit. 42. Tempus adventus Domini in verbo Dei definitum non est. 43. Signa tamen quædam eundem adventum pronuntiantia in verbo Dei descripta sunt. 44. Qualia cumprimis illa sunt, quæ Christus ipse Matth.XXIV. indicavit. 45. Et Johanni dilecto suo, atque per eum Ecclesiæ emblemate sigillorum septem, & totidem tubarum revelavit. 46. Regni Christi, & cum eodem regnaturæ Ecclesiæ profectus explicatur. 47. De Ecclesiæ statu novissimo adventum Christi ad Judicium præcessuro sententiæ doctorum discordant. 48. Probabilior sententia est, quòd abolita Antichristi Politia Evangelium in toto mundo prædicandum, atque tum finis mundi futurus sit, Antichristi abolitio qualis futura sit, ostenditur. 49. Eo abolito, gentium plenitudo intrabit. 50. Ac demum Judæi convertentur. 51. Hic status Ecclesiæ adventum Christi ad judicium præcedens quædam resurrectio & vivificatio erit. 52. Cujus spem Christus quærens: Filius hominis cum venerit, an fidem reperiet? Luc. XVIII. 8. non præcidit. 53. Status ille Ecclesiæ florentior comitem pacem & securitatem habebit. 54. Adventurus ex Cælo Dominus non eriget in mundo Regnum particulare constans ex sanctis omnibus, vel Martyribus resuscitatis, mille annos in mundo regnaturus. 55. Chiliasmus hæreticus Cerinthianorum refellitur. 56. Chiliasmus dogmaticus veterum & recentiorum Theologorum, nævus condonandus potius, quam odiose exagitandus est. 57. Refellitur tamen, ceu verbo Dei repugnans. 58. Perperam ad tuendum eum locus Apoc. XX. 1–8. detorquetur. 59. Vera Christi ex Cælo in terram adventantis opera sunt resuscitatio mortuorum, judicium universale & glorificatio electorum. Resuscitatio mortuorum definitur. 60. Fundamentum fidei Christianæ est. 61. Probatur illa expressis Scripturæ testimoniis, exemplis, typis; 62. Nec non rationibus ex Scriptura. 63. & lumine naturæ, saltem quoad possibilitatem ejus, petitis. 64. Historia Sadducæorum, Philosophorum, & Pseudo-Christianorum resurrectionem negantium. 65. Argumentis eorundem occurritur. 66. Solus Deus mortuos resuscitat. 67. Singulariter Christus causa resurrectionis piorum & impiorum est; sed non sine discrimine. 68. Elenchus eorum, qui mortuos naturaliter resurgere statuunt. 69. Proprie non totus homo, sed corpus ejus organicum resurgit, & resurgit idem numero, quod cecidit. 70. Resuscitatis ex morte corpus & anima; membra organica, spiritus atque humores necessarii; & pertinentia ad ornatum omnia constabunt. 71. Neque omnis moles carnis, neque nulla resuscitabitur. 72. Historia resurrectionem carnis ejusdem numero negantium. 73. Eorundem argumenta ad partes vocata. 74. Non obstat resurrectioni carnis ejusdem pulveris corporei dissipatio, & carnium humanarum ab anthropophagis hominibus, vel bestiis consumptio. 75. Resurrectio erit universalis, etiam injustorum. 76. Judæorum & Socinianorum argumenta contraria dissolvuntur. 77. Modus, quo in resuscitandis mortuis Christus utetur. 78. Locus resurgentium. 79. resurrectioni mortuorum mutatio superstitum in adventu Domini analoga erit. 80. Modus mutationis superstitum. 81. Finis resurrectionis. 82. Alterum reducis adventantis Christi opus Judicium universale vivorum & mortuorum erit. 83. Cujus futuri veritas demonstratur. 84. Et adversus infideles veteres & novos, Socinianos imprimis, vindicatur. 85. Judex Deus triunus erit. 86. Nec Angeli, nec Sancti proprie judices erunt. 87. Judicabuntur vivi & mortui, adeoque homines in universum omnes. 88. Etiam Angeli mali à Christo, & in ac cum ipso ab Angelis bonis & sanctis judicabuntur. 89. Præparatio ad judicium. 90. Judicii administratio cognitione causæ, sententiæ dictione, & executione ejusdem consistit. 91. Judicii tempus & locus. 92. Judicium ultimum finis mundi & consummatio seculi excipiet. 93. Etiam recta ratio finem mundi arguit. 94. Judæorum, Philosophorum & Æternalium elenchus. 95. Mundo finem non natura, sed Deus imponet. 96. Quod testimoniis V. & N. T. demonstratur. 97. Causæ & modus conflagrationis mundi à Rumetio assertus expenditur. 98. Effectus conflagrationis mundi non ejus annihilatio, sed renovatio erit. 99. Veterum & recentiorum dissensus, & dissentientium argumenta excutiuntur. 100. Creatura per conflagrationem renovandæ explicantur. 101. Burneti homines sanctos novi mundi incolas statuentis & ortum novi mundi, nec non dotes & conditiones ejusdem curiosius definientis elenchus. 102.
