Et cessabit illa induratio per pœnitentiam & conversionem illorum, quando Deus corde lapideo ablato carneum,oculos ad videndum,& aures ad audiendum dabit,quod ultimo tempore,& paulò ante resurrectionem, futurum Apostolus v. 15. innuit his verbis: Si rejectio (Judæorum) reconciliatio est mundi, quæ erit assumptio, nisi vita ex mortuis,quid iis aliumptis expectandum ultra nisi resurrectio mortuorum ? Quæ etiam causa est,quòd tum Moses in conversione Judæorum finit,dicens: Canite gentes, populus ejus, quia sanguinem servorum suorum vindicat, & ultionem retribuit hostibus ejus, expiabit terram suam, populum suum, Deut. XXXII. 43. tum Ezechiel conversionem Judæorum, ceu typum resurrectionis mortuorum, cap. XXXVII. 6. seqq. proponit: tum omnes fere Prophetæ in eadem desinunt. Rationes porrò, quibus non offendisse ut corruant, v. 11. adeóque quandoque conversum iri, & indurationem eorundem cessaturam, Apostolus demonstrat,ab eodem petuntur tum à fine vocationis gentium, ut Judæos ad æmulationem provocaret, v. 11-16. tum à sanctitate Patrum,ceu primitiarum & radicis,quia primitiæ, seu delibatio sanctæ sunt, etiam massa sancta est; & si radix sancta, etiam rami, v. 16. adeóque non si Judæi, qui nunc sunt,incredduli sunt,sequitur, etiam filios ipsorum mansuros esse in incredulitate,quia non magis sunt filii parentum rejectorum, quàm pars massæ sanctæ, & rami arboris sanctæ; adeóque sub verbo promissionis indefinito continentur,utpote quod verum non esset, si non esset prænotio reliquiarum: tum à facilitate insitionis ramorum effractorum, qui si gentes ex naturali oleastro excisæ præter naturam in bonam oleam inferi potuerunt: multò magis Judæi,qui secundum naturam sunt, si non permanserint in incredulitate,ea non delectentur,& de traditionibus doctorum suorum dubitare incipiant; oleæ suæ inseri poterunt, atque potens est Deus, ut & infidelitatem illam tollat, (quod facere velle spondet, quia rami & massa talis sunt) & iterum eos inserat,v. 23.24. tum denique ex testimonio Esajæ: Veniet לציון הגאל Sioni redemptor, & revertentibus à defectione in Jacob. Et hoc est Testamentum meum,&c.Esaj.LIX.20.21. Quæ verba conjuncta cum verbis,ibid.XXVII. 9. יכפר עון יעקוב expiabit iniquitatem Jacobi; sic Paulus reddit. Ἥξει ἐκ Σιὼν ὁ ῥυόμενος, καὶ ἀποστρέψει ἀσεβείας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβ. Veniet ex Sion, qui eripiet,& avertet impietates à Jacob. Et hoc est Testamentum meum illis à me factum, cùm sustulero peccata eorum,Rom.XI.26.27. Quæ cum prioribus sensu convenire,planum est;& eum sensum habent, quòd ὁ ῥυόμενος Redemptor, cujus est dicere: Hi mei sunt,Esaj. XLIII. 1. Jacobum, seu ejus posteros circa finem mundi (nam ordo Prophetiarum Esajæ,cujus una comprehensio est omnium temporum ab initio N. T. id docet) à pravitatibus & peccatis suis expiaturus adeóque reducturus sit. Generalia enim verba illa ostendunt, quòd quandiu Jacob induratus est, expectanda sit gratia,idque juxta Testamentum illud,cujus objectum sunt Sion & Jacob; & quo promissum
units.tr: LI. When the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, the hardening [πώρωσις] of Israel will cease. If you were cut from the wild olive which is by nature yours, and grafted contrary to nature into the good olive, how much more shall these, who are natural branches, be grafted into their own olive? For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, of this mystery, lest you be wise in your own eyes, that a hardening has come upon part of Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. And so all Israel shall be saved, as it is written, Isa. LIX. 20, There shall come out of Zion one who shall deliver, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob, Rom. XI. 24–27. The hardening therefore will one day cease, which has fallen upon Israel in part [ἐκ μέρους], upon those who have rejected Christ and the Gospel preached by the Apostles; or, in exchange for that hardening, which befell the Gentiles in the Old Testament. And that hardening will cease through their repentance and conversion, when God takes away the stony heart and gives a fleshly one, eyes to see and ears to hear. This the Apostle hints at in v. 15, in these words, that will come to pass at the last time and shortly before the resurrection: If the rejection (of the Jews) is the reconciliation of the world, what will the acceptance be, but life from the dead? What else is to be expected after their acceptance but the resurrection of the dead? This is also why Moses, speaking of the conversion of the Jews, ends with the words: Sing, O nations, his people, for he avenges the blood of his servants, and returns vengeance upon his enemies, and makes atonement for his land and his people, Deut. XXXII. 43. Then Ezekiel presents the conversion of the Jews as a type of the resurrection of the dead, Ezek. XXXVII. 6 ff. And almost all the prophets end with the same theme. Moreover, the reasons by which the Apostle shows that Israel did not stumble so as to fall, v. 11, and therefore that they will at some time be converted and their hardening will cease, are drawn from the same source: first from the purpose of the calling of the Gentiles, that he might provoke the Jews to emulation, vv. 11–16; then from the holiness of the Fathers, as the firstfruits and the root, since if the firstfruit is holy, the lump is holy; and if the root is holy, so are the branches, v. 16. Hence, it does not follow, because the Jews who are now alive are unbelievers, that their sons will also remain in unbelief; for they are no more the sons of rejected parents than the part is of the holy lump or the branches of the holy tree; and so they are included under the indefinite word of promise, which would not be true if there were no foreknowledge of a remnant. Then from the ease with which the broken branches can be grafted in again, for if the Gentiles, cut from the wild olive which was theirs by nature, could be grafted contrary to nature into the good olive, much more may the Jews, who are natural branches, if they do not remain in unbelief, and begin to be dissatisfied with the traditions of their teachers, be grafted into their own olive; and God is able to remove that unbelief (which he promises to do, since the branches and the lump are of such a kind), and to graft them in again, v. 23, 24. Finally, from the testimony of Isaiah: There shall come to Zion the redeemer [לציון הגאל], and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob. And this is my covenant, etc., Isa. LIX. 20, 21. These words, joined with those in Isa. XXVII. 9, he shall atone for the iniquity of Jacob [יכפר עון יעקוב], are rendered thus by Paul: There shall come out of Zion the deliverer, and he shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob. And this is my covenant with them, when I shall take away their sins, Rom. XI. 26, 27. That these agree in sense with the earlier passages is plain; and they carry the meaning that the deliverer [ὁ ῥυόμενος], whose it is to say these are mine, Isa. XLIII. 1, will at the end of the world, concerning Jacob or his posterity (for the order of Isaiah's prophecies, which is a single whole embracing all times from the beginning of the New Testament, teaches this), make atonement for them and so bring them back from their perversities and sins. For those general words show that as long as Jacob is hardened, grace is to be awaited, and that according to that covenant, whose object are Zion and Jacob, and in which it is promised that the Spirit shall be upon him, and the words I have put in his mouth shall not depart out of his mouth, nor out of the mouth of his seed, nor out of the mouth of his seed's seed, from that time and forever, Isa. LIX. 21.

units.la: est, fore ut Spiritus super ipsum, & verba in ore ejus posita non recedant de ore ejus, & ore Seminis ejus, & de ore Seminis Seminis ejus ex eo tempore, & usque in seculum, ibid. LIX.21. Id cùm factum fuerit, totum Israelem salvatum iri, Apostolus colligit; Israelem intelligens non omnes, qui sunt ex carne & sanguine Jacobi, sed qui ejus filii secundum promissionem sunt: in quo Israele Judæi, de quibus S. Paulus præcipuè sermonem instituit, excludi non possunt, quia aliás aliter argumentaretur. Addit S. Paulus, Judæos secundum Evangelium hostes, secundum electionem dilectos esse propter patres: & Dei charismata & vocationem esse sine pœnitudine,vers. 28.29. Negari certè non potest,quin promissio Gentibus facta fit in Semine Abrahami, hoc est, tum in Christo,ut auctore, Gal.III.16. tum in Israele,ut exemplo benedictionis, juxta illa Petri: Vos estis filii Prophetarum, & testamenti, quod disposuit Deus Patribus vestris, dicens Abrahamo: In Semine tuo benedicentur omnes familiæ terræ, Actor. III.25. Atqui hactenus, si populum integrum, vel majorem ejus partem spectes, exemplum iræ, non benedictionis factus est. Non igitur sine Israelis assumptione gentium plenissimæ divitiæ, & resurrectio ex mortuis fient. Illustre eandem in rem vaticinium & promissio Dei,Levit.XXVI. est, qua, indicatis prioribus fatis, exhibitione Seminis Abrahamo & Jacobo promissi, v.42.. & desertione populi infidelis, v. 43. subjicit v. 44. 45. Atque etiam nihilominus, ipsis agentibus in terra inimicorum ipsorum, non rejeci eos, ut irritum facerem fœdus meum, quod cum ipsis pepigi, quòd ego Jehova Deus ipsorum sim. Et recordabor ipsis fœdus priorum,quos eduxi ex Ægypto in oculis gentium,ut fierem ipsis Deus. Ego Jehova. Qui tantus est, quem Apostolus Rom. XI.25. 26. & seqq. explicavit. Neque minùs illustre apud Hoseam vaticinium est: Diebus multis sedebunt filii Israel sine Rege & sine Principe, & sine sacrificio, & sine unctio lapide, & sine Ephod & imaginibus, (non habentes politiam & sacerdotium, neque tamen idololatriæ dediti, ut gentes antea & Pontificii deinceps,qui lapides ungunt,altaria & imagines erigunt) Postea convertentur filii Israel, & quærent Jehovam, Deum suum,& Davidem Regem suum, & trepidabunt ad Jehovam, & ad bonum ejus, באחרית הימים in novissimo dierum,Hos.III.4. 5. Denique iterum S. Paulus: Indurata sunt cogitationes, vel mentes eorum,&c. usque in hodiernum diem,quando legitur Moses,velamen incumbit cordi ipsorum. Quando verò convertentur ad Deum, auferetur velum, 2. Cor. III. 14--17.
units.tr: When this has come to pass, the Apostle concludes that all Israel shall be saved, understanding by Israel not all who are of the flesh and blood of Jacob, but those who are his sons according to the promise. Nor can the Jews, of whom St. Paul mainly speaks, be excluded from this Israel, for otherwise his argument would be different. St. Paul adds that the Jews are enemies according to the Gospel, but beloved according to election for the sake of the fathers; and that the gifts and calling of God are without repentance, vv. 28, 29. It certainly cannot be denied that the promise was made to the Gentiles in the seed of Abraham, that is, both in Christ as its author, Gal. III. 16, and in Israel as an example of blessing, according to Peter's words: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham: In your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed, Acts III. 25. But hitherto, if you look at the whole people, or at the greater part of it, it has become an example of wrath, not of blessing. Therefore the most abundant riches of the Gentiles, and the resurrection from the dead, will not come about without the acceptance of Israel. A striking prophecy and promise of God to the same effect is in Lev. XXVI., where, after the earlier punishments have been announced, the fulfilment of the seed promised to Abraham and Jacob (v. 42) and the desertion of the unfaithful people (v. 43) are set forth, and then in v. 44, 45 it is added: And even then, while they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, nor break my covenant which I made with them, that I am Jehovah their God. And I will remember for them the covenant with their forefathers, whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am Jehovah. This is so great a thing that the Apostle explained it at Rom. XI. 25, 26 and following. No less striking is the prophecy in Hosea: For many days the children of Israel shall sit without king and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without a sacred stone, and without ephod or images (having neither polity nor priesthood, yet not given to idolatry, as the Gentiles were before, and as the Papists afterwards were, who anoint stones and erect altars and images). Afterwards the children of Israel shall return and seek Jehovah their God and David their king, and shall tremble before Jehovah and his goodness in the latter days [באחרית הימים], Hos. III. 4, 5. Finally, St. Paul again: Their minds were hardened, etc., until this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies upon their heart. But when they shall turn to God, the veil shall be taken away, 2 Cor. III. 14–17.

units.la: LII. Hic Ecclesiæ consummationis status, adventum Domini præcedaneus, propter analogiam cum resurrectione carnis,etiam resurrectio & vivificatio quædam est. Nam populi Judaici assumptio typus resurrectionis carnis, Ezech. XXXVII. 11. 12. 13. statuitur. Et Deus ipse hostes Ecclesiæ, ejúsque persecutores,Antichristum inprimis,coërcens Ecclesiæ acclamat: Videte nunc, quòd ego sim, & non est Deus mecum: quòd ego mortifico & vivifico: Ego vulneravi, & sano, Deut. XXXII. 39. Assumptio Israelis quid est nisi ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν vita ex mortuis, resurrectio spiritualis, corporalis præ- Hic status Ecclesiæ adventum Christi ad judicium præcedens quædam resurrectio & vivificatio erit. via? Rom. XI. 15. Datur enim quædam resurrectio universalem resurrectionem corporum antecedens, spiritualis videlicet ex ignorantia Dei & peccatis, eáque gemina: prior per vocationem Apostolorum, de qua Christus: Amen, Amen dico vobis, quòd veniat hora, & nunc fit, qua mortui audient vocem Filii Dei, & audientes vivent, Joh. V. 25. Beatus & sanctus est, qui habet partem in resurrectione prima. Super tales secunda mors (induratio) non habet potestatem, Apoc. XX. 6. posterior, sequens secundæ mortis regnum in Gentibus per indurationem eorum, qui ad agnitionem veritatis aliquam pervenerant, sed seducti ad errores & obfirmationem in iisdem, denuo velut mortui sunt: & ex hac morte per conversionem universalem vivificati postliminio resurgent. Venite & revertamur ad Jehovam, quia ipse rapuit, & sanabit nos; percussit & obligabit nos. Vivificabit nos post biduum; die tertia suscitabit nos, & vivemus in conspectu ejus, Hos. VI. 1. 2.
units.tr: LII. This state of the Church's consummation, which goes before the Lord's coming, is also a kind of resurrection and quickening, because of its analogy with the resurrection of the flesh. The assumption of the Jewish people is set down as a type of the resurrection of the flesh, Ezek. 37:11-13. God himself, restraining the enemies of the Church and its persecutors, above all Antichrist, cries out to the Church: See now that I am, and there is no God with me; I kill and I make alive; I have wounded and I heal, Deut. 32:39. What is the assumption of Israel but life from the dead [ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν], a spiritual resurrection that goes before the bodily one, Rom. 11:15. For there is a certain resurrection that precedes the universal resurrection of bodies, namely a spiritual one, from ignorance of God and from sins, and it is twofold. The first comes through the calling of the Apostles, of which Christ says: Amen, amen, I say to you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live, John 5:25. Blessed and holy is he who has a part in the first resurrection; over such the second death (hardening) has no power, Rev. 20:6. The later one follows the reign of the second death among the Gentiles, through the hardening of those who had attained some knowledge of the truth but were seduced into errors and obstinacy in them, and so are again as if dead. From this death they will rise again, restored and quickened, through universal conversion. Come, and let us return to Jehovah, for he has torn us, and he will heal us; he has struck us, and he will bind us up. He will revive us after two days; on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight, Hos. 6:1-2.

units.la: LIII. Regni hujus Christi amplioris, & propter cognitionem Evangelii, qualis N. T. promissa est, plurimis jam communem, florentioris spem non præcidit Christus, interrogans: Veruntamen Filius hominis cùm venerit, anne fidem reperiet in terra? Luc. XVIII. 8.
units.tr: LIII. Christ does not cut off the hope of a larger and more flourishing kingdom of this Christ, such as the New Testament promises, which is now common to very many because of the knowledge of the Gospel, when he asks: However, when the Son of man comes, will he find faith on the earth? Luke 18:8.

units.la: Nam dum sic interrogat Christus, non simpliciter negat id quod interrogat, tum quia nec interrogans, ibid. v. 7. Deus annon faciet vindictam electorum suorum: id non negavit: tum quia cùm Filius hominis venerit, vindicabit electos, adeóque non deerit simpliciter fides: tum quia Christus caput nunquam est sine corpore; sed id solùm innuit, superaturum omnem fidem quòd Christum venientem ad vindicandos electos, die & nocte ad ipsum clamantes vindictam adversus hostes pro electis ἐν τάχει cito adeò sumere videbunt. Sed cùm id videbunt & experientur, inducentur plane, ut credant id, quod hactenus propter μακροθυμίαν, qua Deus erga hostes usus est, vix sperare ausi sunt. Qui sensus cum scopo parabolæ convenit, neque absurdi quicquam habet.
units.tr: For while Christ asks this, he does not simply deny what he asks about. He does not deny it, because the asker himself says in v. 7: Will not God avenge his elect? Nor is faith simply lacking, since when the Son of man has come he will avenge the elect. Nor is Christ ever without his body. He only hints that faith will be overcome, since they will see Christ coming to avenge the elect, who cry to him day and night, and will see him take vengeance on their enemies for the elect, speedily [ἐν τάχει]. But when they see and experience this, they will be plainly led to believe what, on account of the long-suffering [μακροθυμία] God has shown toward the enemies, they have hardly dared to hope. This sense agrees with the aim of the parable and has nothing absurd in it.

units.la: Nam etiam Christus prædixit, venturum Dominum in die, ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη, qua non expectat ipsum, & in hora qua non cognoscit, Matth. XXIV. 50. Et Ecclesia ab hostium suorum furoribus liberata dicit: Quando redire fecit Jehova captivitatem שיבת ציון fuimus sicut somniantes, Psal. CXXVI. 1. Quales somniantes ubivis turbantur phantasmatis, & inter ὄναρ & ὕπαρ non possunt distinguere, & sæpenumero dubitant, an id quod viderunt & audiverunt, vere viderint & audiverint, & quid ex iis, quæ viderunt, secuturum sit, providere non possunt, novis semper spectris se ingerentibus. Vident enim & audiunt, quæ incredibilia videbantur; atque ita hæsitant & stupent, quasi ea non viderent & audirent. Sed non quia hominibus mirabilia multa sunt, etiam Deo mirabilia sunt, vel plane non sunt. Quia mirabile est in oculis residui populi hujus, his diebus, etiam in meis oculis mirabile foret, inquit Dominus Zebaoth? Zach. VIII. 4. Non igitur fides illa cognitionem mysteriorum fidei, sed cognitionem judicii Dei particularis adversus hostes & liberationis Ecclesiæ subitaneæ ab iisdem notare videtur; sive id futurum erat in adventu Filii hominis ad erigendum Regnum Dei, & posterius sive novum seculum introducendum & compescendam persecutionem gentilium, quia dicit Christus, venturum se ἐν τάχει ocyùs ibid. & de initio judicii in Judæos Christus dicit, esse hic stantes, qui non gustabunt mortem, donec viderint Filium hominis venientem in Regno suo, Matth. XVI. 28. sive in adventu ejusdem ad judicium particulare Babylonis & Antichristi, sive in adventu ad judicium novissimum.
units.tr: For Christ also foretold that the Lord would come on the day [ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη], when they do not expect him, and in an hour when they do not know, Matt. 24:50. And the Church, freed from the rage of its enemies, says: When Jehovah brought back the captivity of Zion [שיבת ציון], we were like dreamers, Ps. 126:1. Dreamers are everywhere troubled by phantasms; they cannot distinguish between a dream [ὄναρ] and waking [ὕπαρ], and they often doubt whether what they saw and heard they really saw and heard, and they cannot foresee what will follow from what they saw, since new apparitions keep thrusting themselves in. They see and hear things that seemed incredible, and so they hesitate and stand dumbfounded, as if they did not see and hear them. But it is not because many things are wonderful to men that they are wonderful to God, or wonderful at all. For is it wonderful in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days; shall it also be wonderful in my eyes, says the Lord of hosts? Zech. 8:4. So faith here seems to signify not knowledge of the mysteries of faith but knowledge of God's particular judgement against the enemies and of the Church's sudden deliverance from them. Whether this was to happen at the coming of the Son of man to set up the Kingdom of God, and afterwards, or to introduce a new age and restrain the persecution of the Gentiles, is not clear; for Christ says that he will come speedily [ἐν τάχει], ibid. And concerning the beginning of judgement on the Jews, Christ says: There are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom, Matt. 16:28. Or it refers to his coming to the particular judgement of Babylon and Antichrist, or to his coming to the final judgement.

units.la: Si enim mysteriorum fidei cognitionem, qualis erit, cùm Christus ad judicium veniet, notaret, vix occurreret ratio, qua Scripturam cum Scriptura, Judæorum conversionem & prædicationem Evangelii in toto mundo, proximè finem mundi antecessurum, Rom. XI. 14. conciliare, sine violentia & ψευδολογία liceret. Tentavit quidem conciliationem Hieronym. Zanchius in Thesibus, de quibus cum Marbachio funem contentionis duxit, asserens, Antichristo ultimo grassante, exiguam in mundo fidem fore; eodem per Christum abolito, & conversione Judæorum facta, magnam fore; quam Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ Pastores & Professores communi & publico scripto, ceu Scripturis non repugnantem, laudarunt. Tentavit etiam Gualtherus Conc. 66. in Ep. ad Rom. scribens: fieri posse, ut universalem veluti conversionem totius mundi nova securitas excipiat, & plerique ad novam audaciam prolabantur, atque ita Deus dies mundi propter electos decurtet. Sed abundet quisque suo judicio; dummodo ne obelo configatur expositio omnium verissimilima, quam perhibuimus. Neque etiam obstat, quòd Esajas cap. X. 21. 22. 23. & Daniel, cap. IX. 27. declaraverunt, Judæorum excidium fore כלה ונחרצה universale & peremptorium; quia tale erit, quoad Politiam & Sacerdotium, cùm diebus Christi & Regno Dei non conveniat is status, qui sub V. T. fuit, non quoad fidem quorundam, vel totius populi in Christum. Multi enim in Christum crediderunt, & plures deinceps credent. Eodem sensu Christus dixit ad Judæos: Ecce relinquitur vobis domus vestra desolata, Matth. XXIII. 38. Domus enim illa est templum, quod Deo inde recedente, non poterat vocari, nisi domus Judæorum, Zach. V. 4. sub appellatione domus furis & perjuri continetur. Sequentia verò verba Christi: Dico enim vobis: Non videbitis me ἀπάρτι à nunc, donec dixeritis: Benedictus est, qui venit in nomine Domini, ibid. v. 39. pertinent ad desertionem templi, qua Christus innuit, ultimam hanc esse visitationem templi, qua Christus illud, tanquam domum Patris sui visitavit. Non enim fore prædicit, ut amplius ipsum videant, quia secundum corporalem præsentiam mox ab illis auferendus sit, & Judæi in dispersione sua per totum mundum Christum quæsituri, sed non inventuri sint. En dies venient, dicit Dominus, & mittam famem in terram, non famem panis, neque sitim aquæ, sed audiendi verba Jehovæ. Et discurrent a mari usque ad mare, ab Aquilone usque ad Orientem, circuibunt quærendo verbum Jehovæ, & non invenient, Amos. VIII. 11. 12. Quòd verò Christus addit, ἕως ἂν εἴπωλε, donec dicatis: Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, non obscurè significat, suo tempore futurum esse, ut Judæi à sua infidelitate resipiscant, & Jesum Christum ac Filium Dei agnoscant. Magna, fateor, & tremenda Antichristi pertinacia & potentia: ingens & stupenda Judæorum hodiernorum induratio, crassa & obstinata gentium infidelitas est; quæ abolitionis illius, & conversionis horum spem & fiduciam magnopere tentant. Sed præmonuit S. Paulus, cum cessationem indurationis inter mysteria, quoad modum saltem conversionis, ne ad rationis humanæ, prudentiæ carnalis, & præjudiciorum modulum illam exigamus, refert, & vetat nos apud nosmet ipsos prudentes esse, judicio nostro nimium confidere, & carnem atque sanguinem, in externa hominum potentia stupentem, in consilium adhibere, Rom. XI. 25. Atque, ut sapientiam carnalem retundamus, Scriptura hoc in negotio potentiam Dei opponit. Ἰσχυρὸς Κύριος Fortis Dominus Deus est, qui Babylonem judicat, Apoc. XVIII. 8. Δυνατὸς ὁ Θεὸς Potens est Deus ad illos (Judæos) iterum oleæ inserendos, Rom. XI. 23. Neque profectò minor Gentium incredulitas fuit, quando jam olim per præconium Apostolorum ex naturali excisæ oleastro præter naturam in bonam oleam insertæ sunt, ibid. v. 24. quàm hodierna Judæorum induratio, & Gentium infidelitas est. Denique nec sic carnalis securitas alitur, & metus instantis judicii minuitur magis, quàm cùm Apostolus negavit instare diem Christi priusquàm ἀποστασία venerit, & homo peccati revelatus fuerit, 2. Thess. II. 2. 3. Satis incentivi ad pietatem habent, qui de Judicio extremo persuasi sunt, sive illud proximè instet, sive remotum sit. Omnes nos oportet manifestari coram tribunali Christi, ut reportet quisque in corpore secundum id quod fecit bonum vel malum. Scientes igitur τὸν φόβον τοῦ Κυρίου timorem Domini, hominibus suademus, Deo verò manifesti sumus, 2. Cor. V. 10. 11. Etiam judicium particulare in conscientia subeundum in ipso mortis articulo stimulum ad pietatem acrem satis infigere potest & debet.
units.tr: For if it meant the knowledge of the mysteries of faith, such as it will be when Christ comes to judgement, scarcely any reason would present itself by which one could reconcile Scripture with Scripture without violence and false reasoning [ψευδολογία]: the conversion of the Jews and the preaching of the Gospel throughout the whole world, which will come just before the end of the world, Rom. 11:14. Hieronymus Zanchius did try a reconciliation in his Theses, over which he drew a rope of contention with Marbach. He asserted that when Antichrist rages at the end there will be little faith in the world, but when he has been abolished by Christ and the conversion of the Jews has taken place, there will be great faith. The Pastors and Professors of the Church of Zurich praised this in a common public writing as not contrary to Scripture. Gualtherus also tried it, in Homily 66 on the Epistle to the Romans, writing that a new security may follow the universal, as it were, conversion of the whole world, and that most people will slip into a new boldness, so that God shortens the days of the world for the sake of the elect. But let each abound in his own judgement, provided only that the exposition which we have put forward, which is the most probable of all, is not struck through with an obelus. Nor does it stand in the way that Isaiah 10:21-23 and Daniel 9:27 declared that the destruction of the Jews would be universal and final [כלה ונחרצה]. For it will be so as regards the polity and the priesthood, since the state which existed under the Old Testament does not fit the days of Christ and the Kingdom of God; but it is not so as regards the faith of some or of the whole people in Christ. For many believed in Christ, and more will believe afterwards. In the same sense Christ said to the Jews: Behold, your house is left to you desolate, Matt. 23:38. For that house is the temple, which, with God departing from it, could be called nothing but the house of the Jews, and it is contained under the name house of the thief and perjurer, Zech. 5:4. But the following words of Christ: For I tell you, you will not see me henceforth [ἀπάρτι] until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, ibid. v. 39, pertain to the desertion of the temple. By them Christ hints that this is the last visitation of the temple, in which he visited it as the house of his Father. For he does not predict that they will see him again, since he is soon to be taken from them as to bodily presence, and the Jews, in their dispersion throughout the whole world, will seek Christ but will not find him. Behold, days will come, says the Lord, and I will send a famine into the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Jehovah. And they will wander from sea to sea, from north to east; they will go round seeking the word of Jehovah, and will not find it, Amos 8:11-12. But that Christ adds until [ἕως ἂν] you say [εἴπητε], Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, does not obscurely signify that in its own time the Jews will repent of their unbelief and acknowledge Jesus Christ as the Son of God. I admit that the obstinacy and power of Antichrist are great and terrible; the huge and stupefying hardening of the Jews today and the gross and stubborn unbelief of the Gentiles greatly test the hope and confidence in that abolition and in this conversion. But St Paul forewarned us. When he reports the cessation of the hardening among the mysteries, at least as to the manner of conversion, he tells us not to measure it by the standard of human reason, carnal prudence and prejudices. He forbids us to be wise in our own eyes, to trust too much in our own judgement, or to take counsel from flesh and blood, which is stunned by the external power of men, Rom. 11:25. And so that we may blunt carnal wisdom, Scripture sets the power of God against it in this matter. Strong is the Lord God who judges Babylon [Ἰσχυρὸς Κύριος], Rev. 18:8. God is able [Δυνατὸς ὁ Θεὸς] to graft them (the Jews) back into the olive, Rom. 11:23. Nor was Gentile unbelief any less when long ago, through the proclamation of the Apostles, they were grafted contrary to nature from the wild olive, which was cut off by nature, into the good olive, ibid. v. 24, than the present hardening of the Jews and unbelief of the Gentiles are. Finally, carnal security is not nourished, and the fear of the approaching judgement is not lessened more, than when the Apostle denied that the day of Christ was at hand before the apostasy comes and the man of sin is revealed, 2 Thess. 2:2-3. Those who are persuaded of the final judgement have enough incentive to piety, whether it is near at hand or far off. For we must all be made manifest before the judgement seat of Christ, so that each may receive in the body according to what he has done, good or evil. Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord [τὸν φόβον τοῦ Κυρίου], we persuade men, but we are manifest to God, 2 Cor. 5:10-11. Even the particular judgement, to be undergone in conscience at the very point of death, can and ought to fix a sharp goad to piety.

units.la: LIV. Cùm in mundo nihil ex omni parte beatum sit, etiam status ille Ecclesiæ adventui Domini prævius, habebit, quod felicitatem minuat. Nam pax Ecclesiæ reddita uti semper securitatem post se traxit, ita trahet in fine mundi. Sicut enim erant in diebus ante diluvium, edentes, bibentes, nubentes & nuptum dantes, ad eum usque diem, quo Noe arcam ingressus est, & non cognoverunt, quòd diluvium venerit, quod omnes sustulit; ita erit adventus Filii hominis, Matth. XXIV. 38. 39. Conveniet enim dies adventus Domini cum die, quo Noe arcam ingressus est, tum in pace, tum in securitate. Ipsi nostis exactè, quòd dies Domini veniet, sicut fur in nocte. Cùm enim dixerint: Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια Pax & tutum, tum verò subitus ipsis adest interitus, quemadmodum dolor ei, quæ uterum fert, & non effugient. 1. Thess. V. 2. 3. Pacem igitur securitas, carnalis plurium, inprimis carnalium comitabitur. Antediluviani homines Noam per CXX annos interitum prædicantem irriserunt, nil metuentes, & tuta omnia rati, quia pacata. Pari ratione circa ultimum dierum erunt irrisores secundum concupiscentias suas ambulantes, qui dicturi sunt. Ubi est promissio adventus ejus? Ex quo enim Patres obdormiverunt, omnia ita manent ab initio creationis, 2. Pet. III. 4. Quæ verba arguunt, homines ultimi temporis negleckturos signa temporis instantis judicii, quasi nihil viderent mutatum in mundo, & nulla ultimi temporis signa extarent. Erit igitur ante adventum Domini ἀμέτως pax, & in pace opinio ἀσφαλεία rerum tutarum, sive securitas, in filiis inprimis tenebrarum, ut non acturi sint poenitentiam à viis suis malis; ex eo oriunda, quòd nolint animadvertere, illa facta esse, quæ fieri debebant, & in Prophetiis præscripta sunt. Si enim illa observarent, cognoscerent etiam, postquam omnia facta fuerint, jam diem Domini ἐπιφανείας allutescere, & tubas antecedentes Christi audirent. In tali ergo statu, & talem ob causam, quia dicturi profani sunt; Pax & tutum, seu securitas; veniet Dominus sicut fur in nocte, subitò & ἀπροσδοκήτως præter expectationem. Sicut enim Christus cùm venit in carnem, venit פתאום subitò, Malach. III. 1. quia postquam venisset, Angelus, qui viam coram ipso paraverat, templum suum inexpectatus adiit; in medio Israelitarum fuit, non agnitus ab illis: Johannis indicio & testimonio proditus, denique ad templum suum præter omnium opinionem venit, non observantibus hominibus signa temporum, & quod Deus circa nativitatem ejus fecerat, dicentibusque adeò: ubi manet Deus judicii? ibid. II. 17. Licet interim Maria, Elisabetha, Joseph, Zacharias & alii sancti, haud ignari, quid ipso nascente factum sit, in dies salutem ab ipso expectaverint: ita Christus hominibus stupidis, & opera Dei negligentibus, veniet tanquam fur. Nam & dies & hora adventus ejus non est revelata, Matth. XXIV. 36. Marc. XIII. 32. & opus Dei illi non animadvertunt. Iccirco veniet ut fur, & impiis ἀφνίδιος λεθος subitus interitus accidet, quemadmodum dolor ei, quæ uterum fert: Et non effugient, 1. Thess. V. 3. Nam ut fur veniat, necesse non est; at ut gravidæ dolor veniat, necesse est, licet quando is accessurus sit, exactè nesciat. Talis adventus subitaneus celerem chiasmo interitum afferet, quem impii evitare nullo modo poterunt. Dei enim mos est, celeriter punire. Ita nec homines diem diluvii præsciverunt: & Sodoma lasciviebat eversioni proxima: & Pharao in aquis, quas audacter ingressus est, periit. Judicium enim Dei est collisio, seu subitus ictus, sonus ab ictu, & desitio ejus, Knall und fall / in loco spectantium seu theatro, cum pudore & ignominia eorum, qui judicantur, & in exemplum aliorum, atque consolationem eorum, qui oppressi sunt, Job. XXXIV. 26.
units.tr: LIV. Since nothing in the world is wholly blessed, the state of the Church that precedes the coming of the Lord will also have something that diminishes its happiness. For just as the peace given to the Church has always brought security in its wake, so it will bring it at the end of the world. For as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away, so will be the coming of the Son of man, Matt. 24:38, 39. For the day of the Lord's coming will coincide with the day Noah entered the ark, both in peace and in security. For you yourselves know well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. For when they say, "Peace and security" [εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια], then sudden destruction comes upon them, like labour pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape, 1 Thess. 5:2, 3. Peace, then, will bring security, and most of all carnal security, in carnal men. The antediluvians mocked Noah for one hundred and twenty years as he preached destruction, fearing nothing and judging everything safe because it was peaceful. In the same way, at the end of days there will be mockers walking according to their own lusts, who will say, "Where is the promise of his coming? For since the Fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation," 2 Pet. 3:4. These words show that men of the last time will neglect the signs of the approaching time of judgement, as if they saw nothing changed in the world and no signs of the last time existed. Before the Lord's coming there will therefore be peace without ceasing [ἀμέτως], and in peace the opinion of safety [ἀσφάλεια] regarding safe things, or security, especially among the sons of darkness, so that they will not repent of their evil ways. This arises from their refusing to notice that those things have happened which had to happen and which were foretold in the prophecies. For if they observed these things, they would also recognise that, once all things have been fulfilled, the day of the Lord's appearing [ἐπιφάνεια] is already dawning, and they would hear the trumpets announcing Christ. In such a state, and for this reason, because the profane will say, "Peace and security," the Lord will come like a thief in the night, suddenly and unexpectedly [ἀπροσδοκήτως], beyond expectation. For just as Christ, when he came in the flesh, came suddenly [פתאום], Mal. 3:1, because after the angel who had prepared the way before him had come, he entered his temple unexpectedly; he was in the midst of the Israelites without being recognised by them, and was made known by John's indication and testimony. Finally he came to his temple beyond everyone's expectation, because men did not observe the signs of the times, nor what God had done at his birth, and they said, "Where is the God of judgement?" Mal. 2:17. Meanwhile Mary, Elisabeth, Joseph, Zechariah and the other saints, who were not ignorant of what had happened at his birth, kept daily expecting salvation from him. So Christ will come like a thief upon stupid men who neglect the works of God. For neither the day nor the hour of his coming has been revealed, Matt. 24:36; Mark 13:32, and they do not notice the work of God. Therefore he will come like a thief, and sudden destruction [ἀφνίδιος ὄλεθρος] will befall the impious, like the pain of a woman in labour, and they will not escape, 1 Thess. 5:3. For it is not necessary that a thief should come, but it is necessary that the pain of a pregnant woman should come, even though she does not know exactly when it will arrive. Such a sudden coming will bring swift destruction, which the impious will in no way be able to avoid. For it is God's way to punish quickly. Thus men did not foreknow the day of the flood; Sodom was indulging in lust on the very eve of its overthrow; and Pharaoh perished in the waters into which he had rashly entered. For God's judgement is a collision, that is, a sudden blow, the sound of the blow, and its cessation, a crack and a fall in the place of spectators or theatre, with the shame and disgrace of those who are judged, and as an example to others and a consolation to those who have been oppressed, Job 34:26.

units.la: LV. Adventans sic Dominus non Regnum aliquod in terra nova eriget, constans ex Sanctis ex mortuis resuscitatis, mille annos in terra duraturum, & resurrectioni universali præiturum. Quale Regnum, & aureum quodam seculum in mundo transigendum Judæi & Christiani nonnulli, Chiliastæ dicti, quorum omni tempore in Ecclesia numerus & locus fuit, somniant. Judæis nempe promissus fuit Messias, futurus Rex Israelis, illustri inprimis loco Zach. IX. 9. Ecce Rex tuus veniet tibi justus & Salvator, alibique passim. Ac licet Christus ipse Regni sui conditionem explicaverit, adseverans, Regnum suum non esse de hoc mundo, Joh.
units.tr: LV. The Lord, coming in this way, will not set up some kingdom on a new earth, consisting of saints raised from the dead, which will last a thousand years on earth and will precede the universal resurrection. Certain Jews and Christians, called Chiliasts, who have always had a place and a number in the Church, dream of such a kingdom and of a golden age to be spent in the world. For the Jews were promised a Messiah, who would be the king of Israel, especially in the famous passage Zech. 9:9: Behold, your king comes to you, just and a saviour, and elsewhere in many places. And although Christ himself explained the nature of his kingdom, asserting that my kingdom is not of this world, John

units.la: XVIII. 36. tamen Pharisæi Regnum hoc fore πομπεύσαν pomposum, & Regem ipsum venturum μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας, cum Regio splendore & apparatu, Luc. XVII. 20. somniarunt. Eodem errore discipuli Christi dementari se passi sunt, ægrè ferentes prædictiones Christi de morte sua, Matth. XVI. 21. Marc. IX. 31. 32. Luc. XVIII. 31–34. Post Apostolorum tempora ejusmodi Regnum Messiæ, aureo seculo similimum Judæi sibi finxerunt, discorde licèt de bonis & duratione illius Regni sententia. Celebris inprimis est R. Ketinæ in Gemarah Sanhedrin, Perek Chelek traditio: Sex annorum millibus stat mundus, & uno vastabitur, de quo dicitur: Et exaltabitur Dominus solus die illo. Unde viri docti colligunt, priscos Judæos tempus illud Millenario definivisse. A Judæis in Ecclesiam Christianam contagio erroris manavit. Licet enim dubium illis non fuerit, quin jam Christus Regnum Ecclesiæ occupaverit, & ceu Rex in Cœlo, apud dextram Patris sedeat, ne tamen pulcherrima & amabilis hæc persuasio periret, finxerunt illi, Christum è Cœlo quandoque rediturum, & Regnum cum fidelibus suis in externa & adspectabili forma administraturum. Et tempus quidem unanimiter annis mille finiverant, sive quòd Apoc. XX. 4. Sancti annos mille cum Christo regnasse dicantur; sive quòd Judæi veteres diem judicii integro millenario, eóque ultimo Sabbathico, antecedente definiverint. Quæ Josephi Mede conjectura est. Verùm quod formam & Bona aurei hujus seculi attinet, sententiis etiam variatum est. Sicut enim Judæos inter veteres quosdam, quos Majmonides מבלובלי pervertentes, seu infatuantes intellectam appellat, regnum Messiæ in cibo & potu collocarunt; alii, quibus etiam Majmonides accedit, in justitia & pace, hoc est, abundantia scientiæ & bonorum societate stabili & jucunda: ita inter Christianos, qui hic Judæorum simias se gesserunt, duplex aureum seculum, duplex Chiliasmus prognatus est; Crassior alter & hæreticus, eorum, qui Regnum Christi è Cœlo in terram reducis terrenum, in quo Judæis in terram suam postliminio introductis, & cultu Levitico restituto, omnes per universum mundum fideles omni genere deliciarum corporearum fruituri, multitudine uxorum, ludis carnalibus, festis & conviviis genialibus & perpetuis beandi & exhilarandi sint: alter subtilior & dogmaticus eorum, qui docuerunt, ultimo mundi millenario, utpote Sabbathico, Christum in terram ex Cœlo rediturum, & debellatis impiis solos inter fideles regnaturum, restituta Ecclesiæ pace altissima, omniúmque spiritualium & corporalium bonorum & beneficiorum Divinorum cum affluentia. Prioris Chiliasmi author Cerinthus hæresiarcha, dogma hoc per revelationem velut à magno Apostolo scriptam se accepisse, mentitus; cujus etiam assecla in Synodo Antiochena damnati, superiore seculo in Anabaptistis Monasterienses, & nostro in Johanne Archer, ejúsque in Scotia & Anglia assecli, ejusmodi in mundo Regnum fidelium, in quo omnibus Regibus & Magistratibus abolitis soli Sancti in terris rerum potituri sint, fingentibus; de quibus plura Honorius Reggius Comment. de statu Eccles. Britan. scripsit; revixerunt, & lacertos moverunt: Posterior author Papias, Episcopus Hierosolymitanus, Johannis non Apostoli, sed Presbyteri cujusdam, qui circa finem Imperii Trajani vixit, auditor, est, homo σμικρὸς τὸν νῦν exigui judicii Eusebio dictus, qui velut acceptum ex traditione Johannis docuit, millenarium annorum post resurrectionem mortuorum, futurum, quo Regnum in terris corporaliter consistere debeat. Eum secutus est Justinus M. cujus contra Tryphonem verba sunt, p. 309. Εγὼ ἢ καὶ εἰσὶν οἱ ἐρθογωνιμένες ... Ego, & si qui per omnia recta sententia Christiani sunt, & carnis resurrectionem futuram novimus, & mille annos in Hierusalem restaurata & exornata, & dilatata. Plerorumque igitur Christianorum ætate Justini is error fuit. Irenæus certè, Tertullianus, Sulpitius Severus, Lactantius, Nepos Ægyptius, alii abripi se errore eo passi sunt; & nonnulli eorum de Regno hoc periculosè satis locuti sunt, quasi nonnihil ex Cerinthi lacunis haurientes. Neque superiore & nostro seculo defuerunt, qui Regnum millenarium ab omnibus Sanctis, vel saltem à Martyribus, vel in Cœlo, uti Piscator, vel in terra, uti Alstedius pertendit, transfigendum putarunt. Demum author Clavis Apocalypticæ Josephus Mede, fretus verbis Petri: Unum hoc non lateat vos, charissimi, unum diem apud Dominum esse, sicut mille anni, & mille annos, sicut unus dies, 2. Pet. III. 8. tubam septimam cum tota χλιασμὸς, cæterisque eodem spectantibus oraculis ... magnum illum priscæ Ecclesiæ Judaicæ, Christo & Apostolis celebratum judicii diem, Sabbathicum & Jubilæum, qui à particulari primùm, & quasi matutino Antichristi cæterorúmque vivorum Ecclesiæ hostium, judicio per gloriosam Domini nostri ἐν πνεύματι φλογὸς ἐπιφάνειαν inchoandum, tandémque post mille annorum Regnum novæ Hierosolymæ, sponsæ suæ sanctissimæ, indultum novorúmque adhuc suboriturorum die magno adveniente, Sathanáque iterum soluto, hostium πανολεθρίαν universali demum omnium mortuorum tum resurrectione, tum judicio absolvendum, notare contendit. Taceo ὁμοψήφως plures alios.
units.tr: 18:36, nevertheless the Pharisees dreamed that this kingdom would be a showy [πομπεύσαν] one, and that the King himself would come with much display [μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας], with royal splendour and pomp, Luke 17:20. The disciples of Christ likewise allowed themselves to be deluded by the same error, being reluctant to accept Christ's predictions of his death, Matt. 16:21; Mark 9:31, 32; Luke 18:31–34. After the time of the Apostles the Jews imagined for themselves a kingdom of the Messiah of this kind, much like a golden age, although their opinions about its goods and its duration disagreed. Especially well known is the tradition of R. Ketina in the Gemara, Sanhedrin, Perek Chelek: the world stands for six thousand years and will be laid waste during one, of which it is said: And the Lord alone will be exalted on that day. Hence learned men gather that the ancient Jews defined that period as a millennium. From the Jews the contagion of error flowed into the Christian Church. For although it was not doubtful to them that Christ had already taken possession of the kingdom of the Church, and sits as King in heaven at the right hand of the Father, nevertheless, so that this most beautiful and lovely persuasion might not perish, they imagined that Christ would one day return from heaven and rule with his faithful in an external and visible form. Indeed they had unanimously set the time at a thousand years, either because the saints are said in Rev. 20:4 to have reigned with Christ for a thousand years, or because the ancient Jews defined the day of judgement as preceded by a whole millennium, and that last one a sabbatical one. This is the conjecture of Joseph Mede. But regarding the form and the goods of this golden age, opinions also varied. For just as among the ancient Jews certain men, whom Maimonides calls מבלובלי [mevalvelei], that is, those who pervert or infatuate the understanding, placed the kingdom of the Messiah in food and drink, while others, to whom Maimonides also belongs, placed it in righteousness and peace, that is, in an abundance of knowledge and a stable and pleasant fellowship of goods, so among Christians, who here played the apes of the Jews, a twofold golden age and a twofold Chiliasm arose. The one was cruder and heretical, of those who brought the kingdom of Christ down from heaven to an earthly one, in which the Jews, restored to their land by right of return and with the Levitical worship re-established, would enjoy every kind of bodily delight throughout the whole world, with the faithful delighting in and rejoicing at a multitude of wives, carnal games, feasts and perpetual convivial banquets. The other was more subtle and dogmatic, of those who taught that at the last millennium of the world, as a sabbath, Christ would return from heaven to earth, and after defeating the impious would reign alone among the faithful, with the peace of the Church restored to the highest degree and with an abundance of all spiritual and bodily goods and divine benefits. The author of the former Chiliasm was Cerinthus, a heresiarch, who falsely claimed that he had received this dogma through a revelation, as if written by a great Apostle. His followers, condemned at the Synod of Antioch, revived in the last century among the Anabaptists of Münster, and in our own among John Archer and his followers in Scotland and England, who imagine such a kingdom of the faithful in the world, in which, with all kings and magistrates abolished, only the saints would hold power over things on earth. Honorius Reggius wrote more about these men in his Commentary on the State of the Church of Britain. They have revived and stirred their limbs again. The author of the latter Chiliasm was Papias, bishop of Hierapolis, a hearer not of the Apostle John but of a certain presbyter, who lived near the end of the reign of Trajan. Eusebius called him a man of small judgement [σμικρὸς τὸν νοῦν]. He taught, as if received from the tradition of John, that a millennium of years after the resurrection of the dead is to come, in which the kingdom must exist bodily on earth. Justin Martyr followed him, whose words against Tryphon are at p. 309: "I, and as many as are orthodox Christians in every respect, know that there will be a resurrection of the flesh, and then a thousand years in Jerusalem rebuilt, adorned and enlarged." Therefore in the age of most Christians this was Justin's error. Irenaeus certainly, Tertullian, Sulpicius Severus, Lactantius, Nepos of Egypt and others were carried away by this error, and some of them spoke about this kingdom quite dangerously, as if drawing something from the cesspools of Cerinthus. Nor in the last century or in our own have there been lacking those who thought that the millennial kingdom would be spent by all the saints, or at least by the martyrs, either in heaven, as Piscator maintained, or on earth, as Alsted contended. Finally, the author of the Clavis Apocalyptica, Joseph Mede, relying on the words of Peter, Let this one thing not escape you, beloved, that one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day, 2 Pet. 3:8, strives to show that the seventh trumpet, together with the whole chiliasmus and the other oracles bearing on the same point, notes the great day of judgement celebrated by the ancient Jewish Church, by Christ and by the Apostles, as a sabbath and jubilee, which is to begin with the particular judgement, first and as it were morning, of the Antichrist and of the other enemies of the living Church, through the glorious appearing of our Lord in a spirit of flame [ἐν πνεύματι φλογὸς], and which is finally to be concluded, after the reign of a thousand years granted to the new Jerusalem, the most holy bride of Christ, and with the coming of the great day of the new generations that are still to arise, and with Satan loosed again, by the total destruction [πανολεθρία] of the enemies, through the universal resurrection of all the dead and their judgement. I pass over several others who agree in this view.

units.la: LVI. Cerinthianorum Chiliasmum hæreticum, Judaismum deteriorem, imò & Epicuraismum incrustantem, merito Ecclesia damnavit, & damnabit semper. Regni enim Christi status & conditio spiritualis, non corporalis, nedum corporalis ejusmodi est, in quo τρυφᾶν, vivere lautè & genialiter, comessari, pergræcari liceat. Neque cultus Levittheir in urbe Hierosolyma unquam restituetur. Et debuit Christus esse שלום pacificator, Gen. XLIX. 10. שר שלום princeps pacis, Esaj. IX. 6. sed non pacis temporalis, nec pacis impiis etiam omnibus conferendae, quia non est pax impiis, ibid. XLVIII. 22. LVII. 21. & super eos manet ira, Joh. IIL 36. Pacem verò universalem, numeris omnibus absolutam Scriptura non cunctis hominibus in terra, sed solis electis & fidelibus in Cœlo promittit. Deliciae inprimis corporales, quales Judæi & Cerinthiano aureo illi seculo eximias faciunt, plane ... verbi Dei sunt. Spirituales enim Regno Messiæ non deerunt, sed non eo gradu, quo illas Maimonides aliúque ei deputant. Hoc enim consilium Dei sanctissimum est, ut virtutibus obsequium & humilitatem nostram probantibus & testificantibus in lucta hujus vitæ integer dari possit. Voluptates porrò liberales nunquam in hac vita ea cum copia & mensura indulgentur, quin adversa & tristia multa apud optimos, lætiora apud pessimos sint. Illiberales verò & inhonestatum Christo Rege, tum Sanctis, Regni ejus civibus indignissimæ sunt. Foris canes & adulteri, Apoc.XXII.15. Neque ulla capitalior pestis generi humano à natura mala & corrupta, quàm voluptas corporis, data est. Grandis quinetiam Sanctis Patribus, quos ad Regnum tale resurrecturos fingunt, injuria infertur. Sive enim in Cœlo sunt, melius illis ibi est, quàm in tali porcorum hara, & vanitatum Regno. Sive extra Cœlum, ubicunque degunt, meliore conditione sunt, quàm illa Palæstinica edendi, bibendi, & pecora ad sacrificia mactandi, licentia, quam superstites adhuc abominati sunt, est. Sumentne liceat cum Ludov. Vive quærere, pharmacum aliquod, quo illis jam sapiant, quæ prius illis fatua & insipidissima esse solebant? At nec Josephi Medi opinio illa, quòd ultimus millenarius consummationem sæculi præcessurus Sabbathicus & Jubilæus futurus sit, placere potest, quia non ex limpidis Israelis fontibus, sed ex Judaicis δἀ πρώσει deprompta est. Quomodo etiam Judicii dies dici potest, qui Sabbathicus & Jubilæus erit? Petrus verò asseverans ex Davide, unum diem apud Dominum esse instar mille annorum, hoc unum sibi voluit, quòd tempus illud, quo Christus adventum suum comperendinat, respectu Dei minimè longum sit, neque adeò illa mora trahi in argumentum sententiæ profanæ debeat, quia apud Deum unus dies mille annorum instar sit.
units.tr: LVI. The Church has rightly condemned the heretical millenarianism of the Cerinthians, a Judaism worse than the original and even tainted with Epicureanism, and it will always condemn it. For the state and condition of Christ's kingdom is spiritual, not corporal, and far from being corporal of that kind, in which one may live in luxury [τρυφᾶν], feast well and sumptuously, and indulge in revelry. Nor will the worship of the Levitical law ever be restored in the city of Jerusalem. Christ ought to be the peacemaker [שלום], Gen. 49:10, and the Prince of Peace [שר שלום], Isa. 9:6, but not of temporal peace, nor of a peace to be bestowed on all the wicked, because "there is no peace for the wicked," Isa. 48:22; 57:21, and "the wrath of God abides on them," John 3:36. Scripture promises a universal peace, complete in every respect, not to all men on earth, but to the elect and faithful alone in heaven. Bodily delights above all, such as the Jews and the golden age of the Cerinthians make outstanding, are plainly contrary to the Word of God. Spiritual blessings will certainly not be lacking in the kingdom of the Messiah, but not to the degree that Maimonides and others assign to them. For it is the most holy counsel of God that obedience and humility, which test and attest our virtues, should be given entire scope in the struggle of this life. Moreover, honourable pleasures are never indulged in this life in such abundance and measure that there are not many adversities and sorrows among the best men, and more cheerful things among the worst. Base pleasures, however, are most unworthy of Christ the King and of the saints, his citizens: "Outside are the dogs and the adulterers," Rev. 22:15. Nor has any more deadly plague been given to the human race by nature, which is evil and corrupt, than bodily pleasure. Moreover, a great wrong is done to the holy Fathers, whom they imagine will rise again to such a kingdom. For if they are in heaven, they are better off there than in such a sty of swine and kingdom of vanities. And if they are outside heaven, wherever they dwell, they are in a better condition than that licence of eating, drinking, and slaughtering cattle for sacrifices in Palestine, which they abhorred even while still living. Whether one may ask, with Ludovicus Vives, "Is there some drug by which those things may now taste good to them, which used to seem foolish and utterly insipid?" is another question. Nor can the opinion of Joseph the Mede be approved, that the last millennium, which is to precede the end of the age, will be a Sabbath and a Jubilee, because it is drawn not from the clear fountains of Israel but from Jewish sources. And how can the day of judgement be called a Sabbath and Jubilee? As for Peter, who asserts from David that "one day with the Lord is as a thousand years," he meant only this: that the time during which Christ postpones his coming is by no means long in relation to God, and that this delay ought not to be drawn into an argument for a profane opinion, since with God one day is as a thousand years.

units.la: LVII. Tolerabilior longè Chiliasmus dogmaticus Veterum & recentiorum est, si à quibusdam veterum dictis periculosioribus, alibi à nobis notatis, discesseris.
units.tr: LVII. A dogmatic millenarianism is far more tolerable, provided one departs from certain more dangerous sayings of some of the Fathers, which we have noted elsewhere.

units.la: Non enim malè Augustinus de Civ. D. lib. XX.7. dixit: Hæc opinio (de Regno millenario) esset utcunque tolerabilis, si aliquæ delicæ spirituales in illo Sabbatho, scilicet mille annorum affuturæ Sanctis per Domini præsentiam crederentur. Nam etiam nos hoc opinati fuimus aliquando. Etiam Hieronymus lib.IV. in Jerem. nec non lib.XVIII. in Esaj. opinionem de aurea & gemmata Hierosolyma restituenda, nec non victimis, sacrificiis (eucharisticis) conjugiis Sanctorum in ea frequentandis, crudam satis & enormem, quàmque minimè se sequi, &, utpote à Dionysio Alexandrino peculiari libro mille annorum fabulam & aureaam atque gemmatam Hierusalem irridente, refutatam, profitetur; damnare non sustinuit, quia, inquit, multi Ecclesiasticorum virorum & martyres ista dixerunt; & unusquisque in suo sensu abundat, & Domini cuncta judicio reservantur. Sed & ἐπείκειαν suam Celeb. Altingius Theolog. Problem. Loc.XX11. testatur his verbis: Posteriorum Patrum dicimus esse peculiare dogma quorundam doctorum; non hærefin, sed nevum condonandum potius, quam insectandum, aut odiosè exagitandum.
units.tr: Augustine said, not badly, in De Civitate Dei, book 20, chapter 7: "This opinion (about a millennial kingdom) would be tolerable in some measure, if certain spiritual delights were believed to be going to come to the saints in that Sabbath of a thousand years through the presence of the Lord. For we too once held this opinion." Jerome too, in book 4 on Jeremiah and book 18 on Isaiah, while professing that the opinion about the restoration of a golden and jewelled Jerusalem, and about sacrifices (eucharistic ones) and marriages of the saints being carried on in it, is quite crude and monstrous, and that he does not follow it at all, and since it was refuted by Dionysius of Alexandria in a special book, which ridiculed "the fable of a thousand years and a golden and jewelled Jerusalem," he did not venture to condemn it, "because," he says, "many men of the Church and martyrs have said these things; and each man abounds in his own sense, and all things are reserved for the judgement of the Lord." Moreover, the famous Altingius, in Theological Problems, locus 22, bears witness to his own leniency in these words: "We say that it is a peculiar dogma of certain later Fathers and teachers; not a heresy, but a blemish to be pardoned rather than pursued or harshly attacked."

units.la: Chiliasmus dogmaticus veterum & recentiorum Theologorum, nævus condonandus potius, quàm odiosè exagitandus est.
units.tr: The dogmatic millenarianism of the ancient and recent theologians is a blemish to be pardoned rather than harshly attacked.

units.la: LVIII. Nihilominus Chiliasmus etiam dogmaticus ille, licèt non exagitandus, at refutandus tamen est.
units.tr: LVIII. Nevertheless, even this dogmatic millenarianism, though it is not to be harshly attacked, must still be refuted.

units.la: Non tantum enim ἀχρα- φφ, sed etiam ἀντιχαφφ est. Scriptura enim nuspiam adventum Christi nisi illustrem & conspicabilem illum prædicat, quo Dominus cum celeusmate, cum voce Archangeli, & cum tuba descendet ex Cœlo, resurgentibus mortuis primùm, dein superstitibus immutatis, & juxta cum mortuis in occursum ejus in aera raptis, secuturo non regno millenario terrestri, sed vita æterna beatis donanda, & supplicio æterno impiis irrogando, Act.I.11. III.21. 1.Cor.XV.25.26.52. 1.Thess.IV.16.17. Heb.IX.26. Oportet inprimis Christum Cœli contineant ἀχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων usque ad tempora restitutionis omnium, quæ locutus est Deus per os omnium Prophetarum ipsius inde à sæculo, Act.III.21. Si igitur Prophetæ de Regno ejusmodi millenario locuti sunt, Christum Cœli ad consummationem usque ejus continere debuerunt. Quomodo igitur in terram venire ad instituendum ejusmodi Regnum poterit? Ea quoque conditio piorum in terra degentium est, ut nonnisi adversa, quamvis pro diversitate temporum magis vel minùs aspera iis prædicantur & obnuntiantur. In mundo θλίψιν affliction habebitis, Joh.XVI.33. Omnes qui pie vivere volent in Christo Jesu, persecutionem patientur, 2.Tim.III.12. Neque ullum tempus in mundo adeò felix & aureum unquam fuit, vel erit, quin generalia de cruce Ecclesiæ, & perpetuis fidelium persecutionibus ei competere possint. Præpostérum igitur est medio in certamine triumphum cogitare, debitam Cœlo lauream intempestivè in terris præcerpere, & in exilio ipso patriæ bona & commoda prægustare velle. Ὢδε ἴ ἡ σύδιον, ἐκεῖ δὲ ὁ στέφανος Hic stadium, ibi corona est. Scriptura quoque tempora novissima adventum Christi ad judicium præcedentia ejusmodi describit, qualia fuerunt tempora Noæ, quæ Deo finiendæ patientiæ causam præbuerunt, Matth. XXIV.37. quibus etiam securitas ingens, 1. Thess.V.3. regnabit, & ἐμπαίζω irriores, 2. Pet.III.3. Virgines fatuæ, Matth.XXV.2. &c. Ἀνομία Exlegis, seu Antichristi reliquiæ, 2. Thess.II.8. obtinebunt; & quæ erunt χαλεπὰ difficilia, in quibus erunt homines ambitiosi, avari, superbi, &c. qui habebunt speciem pietatis, verum vim ejus abnegabunt, 2. Tim.III.1.2.&c. Quomodo etiam signa adventum Christi ad judicium, passim descripta, quorum pleraque vel jam impleta sunt, vel in ipsius complementi ἀχμὴ versantur, statui possunt signa præcedentia finem mundi, & adventum Christi ad judicium, si iis impletis succedet non finis mundi, sed novum Christi & Sanctorum in mundo Regnum? Denique & Christus ipse universale præconium Evangelii in mundo, plandúmque, seu poenitentiam omnium tribuum terræ, Judæorum & Gentium, Matth.XXIV.14.30. finem mundi proximè præcessurum, clarissimè prædixit.
units.tr: For it is not only unfounded, but even opposed to Scripture. Scripture nowhere announces the coming of Christ except as that illustrious and visible coming, in which the Lord will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet: first the dead will rise, then those still living will be changed, and together with the dead they will be caught up in the air to meet him. What follows is not a terrestrial millennial kingdom but eternal life, to be given to the blessed, and eternal punishment, to be inflicted on the wicked: Acts 1:11; 3:21; 1 Cor. 15:25, 26, 52; 1 Thess. 4:16, 17; Heb. 9:26. "Christ must indeed be received by heaven until the times of the restoration of all things" [ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων], "until the times of the restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all his prophets since the world began," Acts 3:21. If therefore the prophets spoke of such a millennial kingdom, they must have kept Christ in heaven until its consummation. How then can he come to earth to establish such a kingdom? The condition of the pious who live on earth is also such that only adversities are announced and threatened to them, though with greater or lesser severity according to the diversity of times: "In the world you shall have tribulation" [θλῖψιν], John 16:33; "All who want to live piously in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution," 2 Tim. 3:12. Nor has there ever been, or will there ever be, any time in the world so happy and golden that what is general about the cross of the Church and the perpetual persecutions of the faithful cannot apply to it. It is therefore absurd to think of triumph in the midst of the contest, to snatch prematurely on earth the laurel due in heaven, and to wish to taste in exile the goods and comforts of the homeland. "Here the race, there the crown" [Ὧδε ὁ στάδιον, ἐκεῖ δὲ ὁ στέφανος]. Scripture also describes the last times preceding Christ's coming to judgement as like the times of Noah, which gave God cause to end his patience, Matt. 24:37; in which also great security will reign, 1 Thess. 5:3, and scoffers will mock, 2 Pet. 3:3; foolish virgins, Matt. 25:2, etc. The lawlessness of the lawless one, or the remnants of Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2:8, will prevail; and there will be difficult times [χαλεπά], in which men will be ambitious, avaricious, proud, etc., having a form of godliness but denying its power, 2 Tim. 3:1, 2, etc. Moreover, how can the signs of Christ's coming to judgement, described everywhere, most of which have already been fulfilled or are at the very height [ἀκμή] of their fulfilment, be considered signs preceding the end of the world and the coming of Christ to judgement, if, when they are fulfilled, there will follow not the end of the world but a new kingdom of Christ and the saints in the world? Finally, Christ himself most clearly foretold that the universal proclamation of the gospel in the world, and the mourning, or repentance, of all the tribes of the earth, both Jews and Gentiles, Matt. 24:14, 30, would immediately precede the end of the world.

units.la: LIX. Sed Chiliastarum ὁ Ἀχμέους ἀπ- γρόμφων est locus sic satis difficilis, Apoc.XX. 1--8. qui non parum emunctarum etiam narium subactique judicii interpretes veteres & recentiores torsit. Ibi enim Sathanas ligandus di- citur Perperam ad tuendum enim locus Apoc. XX. 1-8 detorquetur. citur mille annos, conjiciendúsque in abyssum obsignandam, ne amplius gentes seduceret, donec illi anni mille consummentur, postea solvendum μικρὸν χρόνον ad exiguum tempus. Addit S. Johannes: Et vidi thronos, & sederunt super illis, & judicium iis datum est, & animas eorum, qui occisi sunt propter testimonium Jesu, & propter sermonem Dei, & qui non adorarunt Bestiam, nec imaginem ejus; & non receperunt characterem super faciem suam, & super manum suam. Et vixerunt, & regnarunt cum Christo mille annos. Reliqui autem ex mortuis non revixerunt, usque dum consummarentur mille anni. Et hæc prima resurrectio est. Sed Prophetia illa, nondum impleta, tot manifestis Scripturæ dictis opponi non potest. Ipse quoque textus argumenta Chiliastis opponenda suppeditat, cujusmodi sunt, quòd anni illi mille, quibus regnasse Sancti illi dicuntur, in mille illos annos, quibus Sathanas ligatus dicitur, ne gentes seduceret, incidunt; cùm tamen in statu illo aurei seculi Gentes seducendæ nullæ supersint, & pridem anni mille ligati Sathanæ, ne Gentes seducat, impleti sint; quia à longo jam tempore Gentes ad persequendam Ecclesiam à Sathana seductæ non sunt: quòd Sancti regnasse cum Christo per mille annos dicuntur, at regnasse cum eodem visibiliter ex cœlo descendente, & in terris visibiliter regnasse non dicuntur: quòd regnandi dignitas non martyribus, sed eorum animabus tribuitur, adeóque verba illa ad personas ipsas, & corporum etiam resuscitationem extendere non licet: quòd v. 6. beatitudo & sanctitas illis tribuitur, qui partem in prima resurrectione habent; quæ si resurrectio carnis est, plures utique beati & sancti sunt, quàm qui primi in carne resurrecturi dicuntur, quod absurdum satis est, qui pro Evangelio mortui sunt; Patriarchas verò & Prophetas, qui disertam promissionem κληρονομίας τῆς γῆς hæreditatis terræ habuerunt, quibus præ cæteris ejusmodi resurgendi jus competiisset, non resurrecturos, ut cum Christo regnent: quòd denique post mille annos solvendus Sathanas dicitur, ut prodeat iterum ad seducendas gentes, & congregandum Gogum & Magogum ad prælium, & educendos eos super latitudinem terræ, ut circumeant castra Sanctorum & contra urbem dilectam, quod quomodo futurum sit tum, cùm Gentes seducendæ nullæ supersunt, dici non potest. Sed textus difficilis licèt, commodè tamen sic explicari potest, ut Chiliasmo incrustando locus nullus supersit. Apocalypsis enim post judicium Babylonis cap XVIII. & XIX. explicatum, cap.XX. judicium etiam Draconis, de quo cap. XI. egerat, explicat, & gemina captivitate, temporaria una, mille annos duratura, v.2–9. altera æterna & perpetua v. 9. 10. absolvit. De priori sic loquitur. Et vidi Angelum descendentem de Cœlo habentem clavim abyssi, & catenam magnam in manu sua. Et apprehendit Draconem, serpentem antiquum, qui est Diabolus & Sathanas, & ligavit eum mille annos. Et misit eum in abyssum, & clausit, & obsignavit super illum, ut non seducat amplius gentes, donec consummarentur mille anni. Et posthac oportet illum solvi modico tempore. v. 1. 2. 3. Cùm Draco Sathanas, Imperio gentili vestitus, fit, ligatus ille est, quando Imperium Romanum Christum palam & liberè, extirpata idololatria, profiteri coepit. Tum e-nim desiit gentes ad idololatriam, & persecutionem Ecclesiæ Christianæ, quæ hactenus grassabatur, seducere. Ligatus verò est non absolutè, ut nihil ageret, sed ut non posset talis apparere, qualis antehac apparuit, neque seducere eodem modo, quo hactenus, & nonnisi transfigurans se in Angelum lucis, posset. Degeneravit enim paulatim in Antichristi spiritum. Vidit dein Johannes thronos & sedentes super eos, quibus datum judicium est, quales throni vel illorum sunt, qui statim tanquam regnaturi intra annos mille inducuntur: vel throni, quos mox Episcopi insederunt, qui paulatim uni Papæ cesserunt. Tum vidit duo genera hominum, unum, animas secuti percussorum propter testimonium Jesu, puta Martyres in Cœlum translatos; alterum eorum, qui non adorarunt Bestiam & imaginem ejus, & non acceperunt signaturam ejus in frontem suam & manum suam, qui in nomine Christi liberè convenientes Christo nomen dederunt, vel ore & corde simul, vel saltem ore; neque adeò Bestiæ, Antichristo adhæserunt. Utrisque commune quid tribuitur, quòd ἔζησαν vixerunt & cum Christo mille annos regnarunt. Sed quíque suo modo; Martyres in Cœlo, non adorantes Bestiam in terra, quando ligato Sathana, liberè Christum profesi sunt, & factum est, ut verbo & Spiritu Dei, ad vitam Dei in Christo regenerarentur, à Sathanæ, peccati & mortis servitute liberarentur, & vindicati in libertatem filiorum Dei, Reges & Sacerdotes Deo in Christo fierent. Qui statuus finitur mille annis, hoc est, non minus quàm mille annis, inde à pace, quam Constantinus M. Ecclesiæ dedit, ad seculum usque decimum quartum, in cujus initium Bonifacii VIII. Papatus incidit, quo tempore, remoto eo, qui detinebat, Antichristus revelatus; & Sathanas denuo plenè solutus, nam & antea tempora solvi coeperat, solutione per gradus suos procedente, operam navavit, ut Reges potestatem suam Bestiæ traderent, & imaginem Bestiæ pro capite agnoscerent. Tum enim Sathanas Pseudo-Prophetam ad apertè graßandum, & Draconis instar loquendum, maximáque vi omnes ad defectionem impellendum, concitavit. Unde factum, ut Antichristus revelatus à multis agnosceretur, & palam perstringeretur, donec æternum Evangelium iterum prædicari coepit. Si regnum illud ad animas Martyrum cœlesti gloria perfruentes referatur (quod nulla tamen necessitas postulat) determinatio temporis millenarii ad illas non aliter pertinebit, quàm ut dicatur, illas mille annos regnasse, non ultrò regnasse, imò in æternum regnare. Neque enim definitio temporis millenarii absolutè intelligi, sed cum ligatione Sathanæ comparari debet. Reliqui autem mortuorum non ἐζησαν vixerunt, vel, ut alii codices legunt, ἀνέζησαν resurrexerunt donec finirentur mille anni, quia spiritualiter, in peccato & præputio carnis mortui, & Bestiam adorantes, atque in errore indurati, ex morte peccati virtute verbi & Spiritus S. opera regeniti non sunt, sed in morte sua spirituali manserunt, ἕως donec finirentur mille anni. Ubi particula ἕως donec continuationem actus sine termino, uti sæpe alibi, notat. Nam illi veritatem constanter repudiarunt, longámque adeò noctem sterterunt; Status porrò regnantium cum Christo ἀνάστασις πρώτη resurrectio prima appellatur, hoc est, vivificatio è morte peccati, Joh. V.25. Ephes.II.5. V.14. Col.III.1. Quæ resurrectio illos custodivit, ne mors secunda, ἀπώλεια defectio, induratio potestatem in eos haberet.
units.tr: LIX. But the passage of the Chiliasts' Ἀχμέους ἀπ- γρόμφων [ἀχμέους ἀπογρόμφων] is difficult enough. Apoc.XX. 1–8 has tormented not a few keen-sighted and sharp-witted interpreters, both older and more recent. The passage Apoc.XX. 1–8 is wrongly twisted to support their cause. There it is said that Satan is to be bound, and cast into a sealed abyss, so that he should no longer deceive the nations, until those thousand years are fulfilled; afterwards he is to be loosed for a little time [μικρὸν χρόνον]. St John adds: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. But that prophecy, not yet fulfilled, cannot be set against so many plain sayings of Scripture. The text itself supplies arguments to be set against the Chiliasts, such as these: that the thousand years in which those saints are said to have reigned coincide with the thousand years in which Satan is said to be bound so that he should not deceive the nations. Yet in that state of the golden age there will be no nations left to deceive, and the thousand years of Satan's binding, so that he should not deceive the nations, have long since been fulfilled, since for a long time now Satan has not seduced the nations to persecute the Church. It is said that the saints reigned with Christ for a thousand years, but it is not said that they reigned with him visibly as he descends from heaven and visibly reigns on earth. The dignity of reigning is attributed not to the martyrs but to their souls, and so it is not permitted to extend those words to the persons themselves, or even to the resurrection of their bodies. In v. 6 blessedness and holiness are ascribed to those who have a share in the first resurrection; but if that resurrection is of the flesh, then surely there are more who are blessed and holy than those who are said to rise first in the flesh, which is absurd enough, since they died for the Gospel. Moreover, the patriarchs and prophets, who had the express promise of the inheritance of the land [κληρονομίας τῆς γῆς], and to whom such a right of rising, above all others, would have belonged, are not to rise so that they may reign with Christ. Finally, after a thousand years Satan is said to be loosed, so that he may come forth again to deceive the nations and gather Gog and Magog to battle, and lead them out over the breadth of the earth, to surround the camp of the saints and the beloved city. How this is to happen when no nations are left to deceive cannot be said. But however difficult the text, it can be explained so conveniently that no place is left for propping up Chiliasm. For the Apocalypse, after the judgment of Babylon has been set out in chapters XVIII and XIX, in chapter XX explains also the judgment of the Dragon, of which it had treated in chapter XI, and it finishes off a twofold captivity: the one temporary, to last a thousand years (vv. 2–9), the other eternal and perpetual (vv. 9, 10). It speaks thus of the former: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil and Satan, and bound him a thousand years. And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season. (vv. 1, 2, 3). When the Dragon, Satan, clothed in the gentile empire, is bound, that happens when the Roman Empire began openly and freely to profess Christ, idolatry having been uprooted. For then it ceased to seduce the nations to idolatry and to the persecution of the Christian Church, which had hitherto raged. He was bound, however, not absolutely, so that he could do nothing, but so that he could not appear in the form he had before, nor seduce in the same way as hitherto, and could only deceive by transforming himself into an angel of light. For he gradually degenerated into the spirit of Antichrist. Then John saw thrones, and those sitting on them, to whom judgment was given: such thrones as either belong to those who are immediately brought in as about to reign for a thousand years, or thrones which soon were occupied by bishops, who gradually yielded to the one Pope. Then he saw two kinds of men: one, the souls of those who had been slain for the witness of Jesus, that is, martyrs translated into heaven; the other, those who had not worshipped the beast or his image, and had not received his mark on their foreheads or in their hands, who, gathering freely in the name of Christ, gave their name to Christ, either with mouth and heart together or at least with the mouth, and did not cleave to the beast, that is, to Antichrist. A common attribute is given to both, that they lived [ἔζησαν] and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But each in his own way: the martyrs in heaven, the others not worshipping the beast on earth, when Satan was bound and they professed Christ freely. And it came about that by the word and Spirit of God they were regenerated to the life of God in Christ, were freed from the slavery of Satan, sin and death, and, being vindicated into the liberty of the children of God, became kings and priests to God in Christ. This state is defined by a thousand years, that is, not less than a thousand years, from the peace that Constantine the Great gave to the Church, down to the fourteenth century, at whose beginning fell the papacy of Boniface VIII. At that time, the one who was restraining having been removed, Antichrist was revealed; and Satan, now fully loosed (for he had already begun to be loosed in times past, his release proceeding by stages), set to work to make kings hand over their power to the beast and acknowledge the image of the beast as their head. For then Satan stirred up the false prophet to rage openly and to speak like a dragon, and with the greatest force to drive everyone into defection.
