units.tr: Highest good: what is it? II.771. God alone is it. 773.b. seq. See Vision.

units.la: Bonifacius III. primus Universalis Episcopi titulo gavitas visus est. I I. 688.
units.tr: Boniface III seems to have been the first to hold the title of Universal Bishop. II.688.

units.la: Bossuetus peritringitur de Coena Domini. I I. 469. a. 471. a.
units.tr: Bossuet is criticised on the Lord's Supper. II.469.a. 471.a.

units.la: Bos cornupeta, ejusque dominus, qua poena assi- ciendi? I. 717. a. Bos & asinus animalia ⲏπεόξυα. 733. b.
units.tr: The goring ox, and its owner: by what penalty is he to be punished? I. 717. a. The ox and the ass, animals [ἠπεόξυα]. 733. b.

units.la: Boves cur in sacrificiis mactari solitifuerint? 675. b.
units.tr: Why were oxen customarily slaughtered in sacrifices? I.675.b.

units.la: Bullingerus laudatur. I I. 605. b.
units.tr: Bullinger is praised. II.605.b.

units.la: Bullus Theol. Anglus, subordinationem Personarum S. S. Trinit. statuens perstringitur. I, 122. 125.
units.tr: Bull, the English theologian who maintains the subordination of the Persons of the Holy Trinity, is criticised. I.122, 125.

units.la: Burnetus in opinione de mundi conflagratione notatur. I I. 753. b. item de renovatae terrae incolis. 756. a.
units.tr: Burnet is noted for his opinion on the conflagration of the world. II.753.b. Likewise on the inhabitants of the renewed earth. 756.a. ## C.

units.la: C.
CAbbala Judaeorum quid? & unde orta? I. 41. b. Caini ultio cur prohibita à Deo fuerit? I. 583. b.
units.tr: Cabbala of the Jews: what is it, and whence did it arise? I.41.b. Why did God forbid the vengeance on Cain? I.583.b.

units.la: Calix in S. Coena plebi sacrilegè negatur. I I. 468. b. ostenditur. 469. contrarium asseritur, 470. b. objectiones diluuntur, 471. b.
units.tr: The cup in the Holy Supper is wickedly denied to the laity. II.468.b. It is shown, 469. The opposite is asserted, 470.b. Objections are dissolved, 471.b.

units.la: Campanarum Baptismus improbatur. I I. 453. a.
units.tr: Baptism of bells is disapproved. II.453.a.

units.la: Canaan Populi Israel. Typica tantùm haereditas fuit. I. 472. b.
units.tr: Canaan of the people of Israel: it was only a typical inheritance. I.472.b.

units.la: Candelabrum aureum Templi Hierosol. Ecclesiae emblema fuit. I. 680. a.
units.tr: The golden candlestick of the Temple at Jerusalem was an emblem of the Church. I.680.a.

units.la: Canon Scripturae, non Ecclesiae authoritate, sed Dei solius testimonio nititur. I. 31. b. Librorum Vet. Test. ab Esdra non constitutus nec restitutus est, 35. a. eum Malachias clausit, ibid.
units.tr: The canon of Scripture rests not on the authority of the Church but on the testimony of God alone. I.31.b. The books of the Old Testament were neither constituted nor restored by Ezra, 35.a. Malachi closed the canon, ibid.

units.la: Canonem Prophetiarum & Doctrinae Moses tradidit. I. 480. b.
units.tr: Moses handed down the canon of prophecy and doctrine. I.480.b.

units.la: Canon Missae refutatur. I I. 491. b.
units.tr: The canon of the Mass is refuted. II.491.b.

units.la: Canonici Vet. Test. Libri qui? I. 35. a. nulli perierunt. 36. b. 37. a. Apocryphi ad canonem non pertinent. ibid.
units.tr: Which are the canonical books of the Old Testament? I.35.a. None have perished. 36.b. 37.a. The Apocrypha do not belong to the canon, ibid.

units.la: Canonizatio Papalis Sanctorum refellitur. I I. 711. a.
units.tr: Papal canonization of saints is refuted. II.711.a.

units.la: Cantus quis sit usus? I. 348. b. abusus cantus papalis. 349. b.
units.tr: What is the use of song? I.348.b. The abuse of papal chant. 349.b.

units.la: Capellus, Cod. Hebr. Vet. Test. corruptum dicens, arguitur. I. 36. a.
units.tr: Capellus, who says the Hebrew text of the Old Testament is corrupt, is challenged. I.36.a.

units.la: Capitalia supplicia cur Magistratus irroget, I I. 614. b.
units.tr: Why does the magistrate inflict capital punishments? II.614.b.

units.la: Καπηλεῦν τὸν λόγον quid? I I. 583. a.
units.tr: To peddle the word [καπηλεῦν τὸν λόγον]: what is it? II.583.a.

units.la: Caprae & hirci cur in sacrificiis adhiberi sueverint? I. 675. b.
units.tr: Why were goats and he-goats customarily used in sacrifices? I.675.b.

units.la: Captiva qua cum conditione in matrimonium duci potuerit? I. 723. a.
units.tr: On what condition could a female captive be taken in marriage? I.723.a.

units.la: Captivi finito bello quomodo ex lege Dei sint tractandi? 736. b.
units.tr: How are captives to be treated after a war ends, according to the law of God? 736.b.

units.la: Captivitas, quam Christus ascendens captivam duxit, non sunt Patres ex limbo liberati. I I. 66. b.
units.tr: The captivity which Christ led captive when he ascended: the Fathers were not freed from limbo. II.66.b.

units.la: Caput Ecclesiae Christus fidelium salutem in tuto collocat. I. 390. b. Illud est Christus. I I. 507. b. Varia capitis notio observanda. 555. a. quinque modis Christus caput est, ibid. 556. a. dignitate, ibid. vid. Brev.
units.tr: Christ as head of the Church places the salvation of believers in safety. I.390.b. That head is Christ. II.507.b. The various senses of "head" are to be observed, 555.a. In five ways Christ is head, ibid. 556.a. By dignity, ibid. See Brev.

units.la: Caput Ecclesiae non Papa, sed solus Christus est. I I. 639. b.
units.tr: The head of the Church is not the Pope but Christ alone. II.639.b.

units.la: Cardinales quinam, & unde dicti sint? I I. 671. b.
units.tr: Who are the cardinals, and whence are they so called? II.671.b.

units.la: Caro, Propinqua carnis quae sit. I. 590. b. caro & carnis quid. 591. a. carnis tentationes. 373. b. carnis instituta, quae in Populo Israelitico fuerint? 647. a.
units.tr: Flesh: what is kindred of the flesh? I.590.b. Flesh and body: what are they? 591.a. Temptations of the flesh, 373.b. Fleshly ordinances: what were they among the Israelite people? 647.a.

units.la: Caro seu corpus organicum resurget, atque idem numero quod cecidit. I. 736. a.
units.tr: The flesh, or organic body, will rise, and be the same in number as that which fell. I.736.a.

units.la: Caro Filii Dei quid? I I. 4. a. b. non ejus infirmitatem notat. 4. b. 5. a. eam non ex coelo Christus accepit. 14. b. τῷ λόγῳ intimè, i.e. hypostatice unita est. 19. b.
units.tr: The flesh of the Son of God: what is it? II.4.a.b. It does not denote his infirmity, 4.b. 5.a. Christ did not receive it from heaven, 14.b. It is intimately united to the Word, that is, hypostatically, 19.b.

units.la: Carnalia peccata quae? I. 357. a.
units.tr: Carnal sins: which are they? I.357.a.

units.la: Carpocratianorum haeresis, se esse filios Dei natura jactitantium. I. 350. a.
units.tr: The heresy of the Carpocratians, who boast that by nature they are sons of God. I.350.a.

units.la: Cartesius laudatur. I. 49. a.
units.tr: Descartes is praised. I.49.a.

units.la: Castigatio fidelium non est poena peccati propriè dicta. I. 369.
units.tr: The chastisement of believers is not properly a punishment for sin. I.369.

units.la: Castitas quid? ejusdem necessitas & praestantia. I. 589. a. Virginalis & conjugalis comparantur, ibid. b.
units.tr: Chastity: what is it? Its necessity and excellence. I.589.a. Virginal and conjugal chastity are compared, ibid. b.

units.la: Casus, à Fortuna quid differat? I. 249. quid in Scriptura notent? 250. a.
units.tr: Chance: how does it differ from fortune? I.249. What do the words signify in Scripture? 250.a.

units.la: Casuales & fortuiti rerum eventus Providentiae Dei subsunt. I. 263. a.
units.tr: Chance and accidental events are subject to the providence of God. I.263.a.

units.la: Casuistarum Pontif. protervia. I, 321. b.
units.tr: The impudence of the Papist casuists. I.321.b.

units.la: Κατάνυξις compunctio qualis requiratur? I. 313. a.
units.tr: Compunction [κατάνυξις]: what kind is required? I.313.a.

units.la: Κατάρα maledictio, quomodo Christus pro nobis sit factus? I I. 112. a.
units.tr: Curse [κατάρα], malediction: how was Christ made a curse for us? II.112.a.

units.la: Catechesis semper in mundo est & erit. I. 48. a.
units.tr: Catechesis always is and always will be in the world. I.48.a.

units.la: Catechismus in veteri Ecclesia qualis fuerit? I I. 439. b. Veterum Ecclesiae Patrum Catechismi recensentur. 598.
units.tr: What was catechism like in the ancient Church? II.439.b. The catechisms of the ancient Fathers of the Church are listed, 598.

units.la: Catechisatio quid sit? I I. 597. b. ejusdem summa necessitas panditur. 598. a. ordo & methodus, ib. b.
units.tr: What is catechizing? II.597.b. Its supreme necessity is set out, 598.a. Order and method, ib. b.

units.la: Catechistae qui? I I. 676. a. antiquitus fuerunt Ecclesiae ministri. 597. b.
units.tr: Who are catechists? II.676.a. In antiquity they were ministers of the Church, 597.b.

units.la: Catechumeni quinam fuerint? I I. 397. b. S. Coenae participes fieri non possunt. 462. a.
units.tr: Who were the catechumens? II.397.b. They cannot be made partakers of the Holy Supper, 462.a.

units.la: Κατέχων detinens Antichristum, 2. Thess. I I. 6. 7. quid sit explicatur. I I. 689. a.
units.tr: Restraining [κατέχων] the Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2.6, 7: what it means is explained. II.689.a.

units.la: Catena salutis recensetur. I I. 224. 225.
units.tr: The chain of salvation is listed. II.224, 225.

units.la: Cathari quinam fuerint? I. 316. a. eorum origo, errores. I I. 237.
units.tr: The Cathari: who were they? I.316.a. Their origin and errors. II.237.

units.la: Cathedra Antichristi qualis? I I. 537. a. ejus pro perpetua & illustri visibilitate argumenta confutantur. 538. a.
units.tr: The seat of Antichrist: what sort is it? II.537.a. The arguments for its perpetual and illustrious visibility are refuted, 538.a.

units.la: Catholica cur & quomodo Ecclesia dicatur? I I. 513. b. 514. a. 544. a. 545. a. Romana non est. 514. b. etiam quaevis Ecclesia particularis vocari potest catholica, 546. b.
units.tr: Why and in what sense is the Church called catholic? II. 513. b. 514. a. 544. a. 545. a. The Roman Church is not catholic. 514. b. Any particular church may also be called catholic. 546. b.

units.la: Causa rerum universalis Deus est; sed non uti Sol causa universalis habetur. I. 267. a. Causa prima cum secundis in operando non coordinatur, sed secundae subordinantur. 267. b. quomodo causa prima cum subordinatis secundis concurrat & operetur, ibid. 268. b. Causarum omnium nexus & ordo fatum. 246. b. Spinozae incrustatum fatum Stoicum est. 247. Deo, Enti liberrimè agenti repugnat. 247. a. causarum nexus & natura explicatur, ibid. b.
units.tr: God is the universal cause of things, but he is not regarded as a universal cause in the way the sun is. I. 267. a. The first cause is not coordinated with secondary causes in operating; rather, the secondary causes are subordinated to it. 267. b. How the first cause concurs with and works through subordinate secondary causes. Ibid. 268. b. The nexus and order of all causes is fate. 246. b. Spinoza's fate is the Stoic fate dressed up anew. 247. It is repugnant to God, the most freely acting Being. 247. a. The nexus and nature of causes is explained. Ibid. b.

units.la: Centrum terrae an Infernus sit? I I. 767. a.
units.tr: Is the centre of the earth Hell? II. 767. a.

units.la: Ceremoniae Legales. Spenceri de earum institutione error. I. 649. b. singulae Mysterium aliquod involvunt. 649. a. earum institutio Divina asseritur, & origines ostenduntur. 650. seq. earum γυμνασία σωματικὴ & ψήλωσις πνευματικὴ ostenditur. 651. b. earum spiritualis significatio. 673. a. erant umbra futurorum bonorum, ibid. b. earum Mystica significatio contra Judaeos asseritur. 692. a.
units.tr: Legal ceremonies. Spencer's error about their institution. I. 649. b. Each of them involves some mystery. 649. a. Their divine institution is asserted and their origins are shown. 650 ff. Their bodily exercise [γυμνασία σωματικὴ, gymnasia sōmatikē] and their spiritual training [ψήλωσις πνευματικὴ, psilōsis pneumatikē] are shown. 651. b. Their spiritual meaning. 673. a. They were a shadow of good things to come. Ibid. b. Their mystical meaning is asserted against the Jews. 692. a.

units.la: Ceremoniale Sabbathi in quo consistat? I. 556.
units.tr: In what does the ceremonial of the Sabbath consist? I. 556.

units.la: Ceremoniae Ecclesiasticae quid? I I. 599. a. non sunt pars necessaria Divini cultus, ibid. conscientiam non obligant, ibid. Regulae circa earum observantiam tenendae. 600. a.
units.tr: What are ecclesiastical ceremonies? II. 599. a. They are not a necessary part of divine worship. Ibid. They do not bind the conscience. Ibid. Rules to be observed concerning their observance. 600. a.

units.la: Ceremoniae superstitiosae in Baptismo Ecclesiae Rom. I I. 460. b.
units.tr: The superstitious ceremonies in Baptism in the Roman Church. II. 460. b.

units.la: Cerinthus primus Chiliasta fuit. I I. 726. a. refellitur, 726. 727. a. finem mundi negavit. 751. a.
units.tr: Cerinthus was the first Chiliast. II. 726. a. He is refuted, 726–727. a. He denied the end of the world. 751. a.

units.la: Certitudo & Certum definiuntur. I I. 409. b.
units.tr: Certainty and the certain are defined. II. 409. b.

units.la: Certitudinis fidei & Theologiae, conclusionis & Theol. distinctio refellitur. I. 15. a.
units.tr: The distinction between certainty of faith and certainty of theology, and between conclusion and theological conclusion, is refuted. I. 15. a.

units.la: Certitudo Salutis resp. Dei eligentis summa est. I. 170. a. etiam resp. hominis electi. 171. a. adversantium argumenta diluuntur, 171. b. eam sponsio Christi confirmat, 389. a. eam tanquam Ecclesiae suae Dominus, Rex, caput stabilit, 390. b. ceu Redemtor & Salvator idem praestat, 391. b. ejus intercessio item, 392. b. ut triumphator Sathanae, 393. a.
units.tr: The certainty of salvation with respect to God electing is supreme. I. 170. a. It is also so with respect to the elect man. 171. a. The arguments of the opponents are dissolved. 171. b. The promise of Christ confirms it. 389. a. The Lord, as King and Head of his Church, establishes it. 390. b. As Redeemer and Saviour he likewise provides it. 391. b. So too does his intercession. 392. b. As triumphant over Satan. 393. a.

units.la: Certitudo Salutis perseverantiae comes est. I I. 409. a. definitur, 410. a. ejus promissiones Dei, 413. a. eam fidei natura confirmat, ibid. eam fidei causa, objectum & fructus ostendunt, 414. b. Spei natura eam confirmat, 415. a. charitatis item indoles, 416. a. communio cum Deo, 416. a. electionis firmandae studium, precum efficacia, ibid. Sacramentorum obsignatio, 417. a. quomodo à quovis explorari queat? 418. a. ex eo quòd Spiritus S. fidem habeat, 419. a. Imperfecta in hac vita est, ibid. b. labefactatur tentationibus, non tamen evertitur, 420. a. de ea Ecclesiae Veteris sensus, ibid. b. Objectiones diluuntur, 421. non est mater securitatis carnalis, 424. b.
units.tr: The certainty of salvation is the companion of perseverance. II. 409. a. It is defined. 410. a. God's promises concerning it. 413. a. The nature of faith confirms it. Ibid. The cause, object and fruit of faith show it. 414. b. The nature of hope confirms it. 415. a. So too does the character of love. 416. a. Communion with God. 416. a. The zeal to confirm election; the efficacy of prayer. Ibid. The sealing of the sacraments. 417. a. How can anyone test it? 418. a. From the fact that the Holy Spirit holds faith in us. 419. a. It is imperfect in this life. Ibid. b. It is weakened by temptations but not overthrown. 420. a. The sense of the Ancient Church concerning it. Ibid. b. Objections are answered. 421. It is not the mother of carnal security. 424. b.

units.la: Cessatio ab operibus, an moralis sit? 554. b. cessatio Judaeorum stricta narratur, 557. hodie non sanctificatio Dei, 558. b.
units.tr: Is cessation from works moral? II. 554. b. The strict cessation of the Jews is described. 557. Today it is not a sanctification of God. 558. b.

units.la: Ceti quando creati sint? 213. a.
units.tr: When were the whales created? II. 213. a.

units.la: Chaos Veterum an fuerit Mosis תהו. I. 199. a. 201. b.
units.tr: Was the chaos of the Ancients the Mosaic tohu [תהו]? I. 199. a. 201. b.

units.la: Character indelebilis in Baptismo nullus imprimitur. I I. 458. seq.
units.tr: No indelible character is imprinted in Baptism. II. 458 ff.

units.la: Characterem Bestiae suscipere Apoc. XIII. 16. quid sit? I I. 690. a.
units.tr: What does it mean to receive the mark of the Beast? Apoc. XIII. 16. II. 690. a.

units.la: Characteres Personales Trinitatis, I. 123. Patris. ibid. b. Filii, 124. a. Spiritus S. 138. a.
units.tr: The personal characteristics of the Trinity: of the Father, I. 123, ibid. b.; of the Son, 124. a.; of the Holy Spirit, 138. a.

units.la: Charismata Spititus S, diversa diversis collata. I. 20. b. Varia sunt. I I. 558. a. 559.
units.tr: The gifts of the Holy Spirit, bestowed diversely on diverse people. I. 20. b. They are various. II. 558. a. 559.

units.la: Χαρὶτων, gratiæ donatio in Christo.II.204.a; Χαριζόμεναι in remissione peccatorum quid? II.118.a.
units.tr: Charitōn [Χαρίτων], the bestowal of grace in Christ. II. 204. a. Charizomenai [Χαριζόμεναι], forgiving in the remission of sins: what is it? II. 118. a.

units.la: Charitas non est verè fidei forma.I.237. b. ejus ordo explicatur.708. a. b. in corda nostra diffusa non est habitus infusus & inhærens.II.273. a. fidelium perpetuò durat.400. a, charitatis officium, 516.b. Sola non est verè Ecclesiæ nota.533.a. est vita piæ animæ.708.
units.tr: Charity is not truly the form of faith. I. 237. b. Its order is explained. 708. a. b. The love shed abroad in our hearts is not an infused and inherent habit. II. 273. a. It lasts perpetually in believers. 400. a. The duty of charity. 516. b. Charity alone is not a true mark of the Church. 533. a. It is the life of a pious soul. 708.

units.la: Χειροδήκαι Hesiodi quinam fuerint? I.609. b.
units.tr: Who were the Cheirodaikai [Χειροδήκαι] of Hesiod? I. 609. b.

units.la: Χειροτονία, an ordinatio ad Ecclesiæ Ministerium fuerit? II.670.b.
units.tr: Was cheirotonia [Χειροτονία] an ordination to the ministry of the Church? II. 670. b.

units.la: Χειροτονία qualis eligendi mos? II.567.a. à Χειροθεσία distinguitur, ibid. & 571. a. 572.a.
units.tr: What manner of choosing was cheirotonia [Χειροτονία]? II. 567. a. It is distinguished from cheirothesia [Χειροθεσία]. Ibid., and 571. a. 572. a.

units.la: Cherubim Angeli sunt, I.280. non fuerunt idola ad cultum, 534. b. in Arca fœderis quid significârint? 681. a.
units.tr: Cherubim are angels. I. 280. They were not idols for worship. 534. b. What did they signify in the Ark of the covenant? 681. a.

units.la: Chiliasmus veterum & recentiorum qualis & quotuplex, II.716. a. Proponitur, ibid. refellitur, 717. a. Dogmaticus Veterum & recentiorum Theologorum non odiosè nimis exagitandus, ibid. refellitur, ceu Verbo Dei repugnans, ibid. b. ad tuendum eum perperam locus Apoc.X X.1--8. detorquetur, ibid.718.a. sed commodè explicari potest,728. a.
units.tr: Chiliasm of the Ancients and of recent writers: what sort, and how many kinds? II. 716. a. It is set forth. Ibid. It is refuted. 717. a. The dogmatic view of the ancient and recent theologians is not to be attacked too harshly. Ibid. It is refuted as repugnant to the Word of God. Ibid. b. The passage Apoc. XX. 1–8 is wrongly twisted to defend it. Ibid. 718. a. But it can be suitably explained. 728. a.

units.la: Choreæ & Saltationes vetitæ, I.596. b.
units.tr: Dances and saltations are forbidden. I. 596. b.

units.la: Χρηματιστὴς Patriarcharum, I.444.
units.tr: The Chrēmatistēs [Χρηματιστὴς] of the Patriarchs. I. 444.

units.la: Χρηστὸς Benignitas Dei, I. 96. a.
units.tr: Chrēstos [Χρηστὸς], the benignity of God. I. 96. a.

units.la: Chrismatis Pontificii ritus ridiculi,I.499,500.
units.tr: Chrism: the ridiculous rites of the Papists. I. 499, 500.

units.la: CHRISTUS Fundamentum fidei & salutis solum & unicum est, I. 16. a. quâ Mediator, electionis nec causa, nec fundamentum est, 159.b. Ecclesiæ sponsor factus, 376.a. vide Sponsio. Sacerdos, Mediator, 379. Pontifex, 379.380. non electis tantùm morte sua vitam æternam, sed etiam sibi summam gloriam ceu caput, Rex, Dominus, Ecclesiæ meruit, 383. a. comparatur cum Abel, Enoch, Noah, Melchisedeco, 452.453.a. patiens comparatur cum Aguo Paschali, 490. a. b. Templum flagello purgans non patrocinatur hæreticidis, 588. b. est primogenitus, 679. a. Pontifex noster, 686. a. Ejus cum Melchisedeco & Aharone convenientia, ibid. b. Ipsius Sacerdotis nostri sanctitas, integritas cum Leviticis Sacerdotibus collata, 688. a. major est Mose, 695. a. Sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedec, ibid. sponsor melioris Testamenti, ibid. Rex populi sui, 703. a. non temporalis sed spiritualis, II.610. a.
units.tr: CHRIST is the sole and only foundation of faith and salvation. I. 16. a. As Mediator he is neither the cause nor the foundation of election. 159. b. He was made surety of the Church. 376. a. See Suretyship. Priest, Mediator. 379. High Priest. 379–380. By his death he merited eternal life not only for the elect but also for himself, as head, King and Lord of the Church, the highest glory. 383. a. He is compared with Abel, Enoch, Noah and Melchizedek. 452–453. a. As sufferer he is compared with the Passover Lamb. 490. a. b. Cleansing the Temple with a scourge, he does not defend the killers of heretics. 588. b. He is the firstborn. 679. a. Our High Priest. 686. a. His agreement with Melchizedek and Aaron. Ibid. b. The holiness and integrity of our High Priest, compared with the Levitical priests. 688. a. He is greater than Moses. 695. a. Priest after the order of Melchizedek. Ibid. Surety of the better covenant. Ibid. King of his people. 703. a. Not temporal but spiritual. II. 610. a.

units.la: CHRISTUS heri & hodie & in secula idem est, II. 1-4. Ejus Persona definitur, 3. a. vid. Brev. quomodo ascenderit priùs quàm descendit? 3. b. 4. a. ceu λόγος caro factus est, 4. a. Deus in carne manifestatus est, 4. b. quomodo corpus sibi fecerit, 5. a. secundum carnem ex semine Davidis, secundum spiritum sanctitatis definitus est Filius Dei in potentia, 5. a. spiritus Jehovæ super eo Evangelium prædicante fuit, 5. b. formam servi assumsit, 6. a. plenitudo Deitatis in eo corporaliter habitat, 6. a. semen Abrahæ assumsit, 7. a. Goël & ἱπλήπτως noster factus est, 7. b. ἀγχιστὴς, 7. b. Moses & Prophetæ ejus incarnationem prædixerunt, 7. b. in ejus Persona, humana cum Divina natura unita est, 8. a. Verus Deus & verus homo est, 8. b. Ipsius anima non notat Divinitatem, 8. b. Ceu Deus, Patri, ceu homo nobis consubstantialis est, 9. a. Ejus natura hum. propriâ licèt personalitate destituta, verus tamen & perfectus homo fuit, 17. a. De Ejus Statu, II. 34. seqq. vid. Brev. ejus vita privata; ubi Infantiæ memorabilia, 38. a. b. cur circumcisus & Nazaræus dictus? ibid. 39. a. Pueritia ejus, ibid. faber fuit, ibid. ejus Minis-
units.tr: CHRIST is the same yesterday, today and for ever. II. 1–4. His person is defined. 3. a. See Brev. How did he ascend before he descended? 3. b. 4. a. As the Word he was made flesh. 4. a. God was manifested in the flesh. 4. b. How he made a body for himself. 5. a. According to the flesh he was of the seed of David; according to the Spirit of holiness he was defined as the Son of God in power. 5. a. The Spirit of Jehovah was upon him while he preached the Gospel. 5. b. He took the form of a servant. 6. a. The fullness of the Godhead dwells in him bodily. 6. a. He took the seed of Abraham. 7. a. He became our Goel [ἀγχιστὴς] and [ἱπλήπτως]. 7. b. Moses and his Prophets foretold his incarnation. 7. b. In his person the human nature is united with the divine nature. 8. a. He is true God and true man. 8. b. His soul does not signify the Divinity. 8. b. As God he is consubstantial with the Father; as man, with us. 9. a. His generation differs from the generation of other men. 9. a. He had to arise from Judah. 9. b. He is the son of David; Tsemach [צמח] and Yerach [ירח]. 9. b. He is Immanuel. 11. a. His birth from a virgin is vindicated against the blasphemies of the Jews. 11. b. He was born of a virgin by conception from the Holy Spirit, without excluding the operation of the Father and the Son. 12. b. The formation of his human nature in the Virgin's womb is explained and vindicated against the Socinians. 13. b. He is without father. Ibid. He took flesh from the substance of the Virgin. 14. b. His double genealogy is shown and vindicated. 15. b. In his mother's womb he was sanctified by the Holy Spirit so that he might be born free from stain. 17. a. He received a rational soul created by God. 17. b. He assumed human nature into the unity of his person. 18. a. He grew in wisdom; some things he did not know as man. 21. a. He had a body capable of suffering, tangible and visible. 21. b. The time of his birth is unknown. 15. a. His human nature, though lacking its own personality, was nonetheless a true and perfect man. 17. a. On his state, II. 34 ff.; see Brev. His private life; memorable events of his infancy. 38. a. b. Why was he circumcised and called a Nazarene? Ibid. 39. a. His boyhood. Ibid. He was a carpenter. Ibid. His Minis-

Ascensio ejus in cœlos, ibid. ἀνάληψις ejus fuit in cœlum ascensio, 65. b. argumentum ejus justificationis est, ibid. ejus Sessio ad dextram Patris, 67. a. De Officio Mediatorio, vid. Breviar. Miraculorum ejus vetitas contra Judæos asseritur, 97. b. eorum Divinitas, 98. a. ejus Martyrium, 101. b. Vitam habet ἀχαπάλυτον, 103. a. fuit victima piacularis, 104. 105. a. 122. a. oblatio ejus ad mortem voluntaria, 105. b. & necessaria, 106. a. æternum pœnam quomodo sustinuit, 116. a. factus pro nobis אשם, 122. b. ejus oratio pro crucifigentibus ipsum indefinita est, 123. b. ex humano affectu profecta, 128. a. ejus interpellatio proclectis in cœlo, 127. seq. ejus munus Regium, 129. b. potestas ejus in populum peculiarem, 130. a. b. Regnum ejus Mediatorium ab essentiali distinctum est, ibid. b. non re; sed solâ ratione, quia etiam Mediatorium, nisi Deus, exercere potuisset, 131. a. id secundum Patris voluntatem administrat. ibid. b. tanquam Θεάνθρωπος, ibid. 132. a. Spirituale & cœleste totum est, ibid. b. 133. seq. in populi sui gubernatione & defensione consistit, ibid. 35. a. æternum est; quod aliter in Vet. aliter in N. Test. administravit, ibid. b.
units.tr: was three and a half years in length, 40. b. His temptation, 41. b. He prepares the supper and washes the disciples' feet, 44. b. His passion unto death; see Brev. His struggle; prayer; bloody sweat in the garden; betrayal, etc. II.44.45. seqq. His soul, after death, received into heaven, 58. b. How he exhibited the kingdom to Israel, 64. a. His ascension into the heavens, ibid. His ascension [anālēpsis] was an ascent into heaven, 65. b. The argument of his justification is, ibid. His session at the right hand of the Father, 67. a. On the Mediatorial Office, see Brev. Christ's name derives from anointing, II. 76. b. 77. a. His anointing, 77. In what it consists, 78. It is threefold, ibid. For this reason he is more excellent than all the anointed prophets, 79. a. The threefold office, 87. a. He is Mediator according to both natures, 79. 80. He is called [mlmwny] and [plmwny], 87. b. His rapture into heaven after baptism is a fiction of Socinus, 88. 89. What are his commandments, and how are they to be observed? 91. a. He is King, 93. b. What is the nature of his power to teach? 95. a. The reality of his miracles is asserted against the Jews, 97. b. Their divinity, 98. a. His martyrdom, 101. b. He has indissoluble life [akatalytos], 103. a. He was a propitiatory victim, 104. 105. a. 122. a. His offering unto death was voluntary, 105. b. and necessary, 106. a. How he endured eternal punishment, 116. a. Made for us an offering for guilt ['asham], 122. b. His prayer for those who crucified him is indefinite, 123. b. It proceeded from human feeling, 128. a. His intercession for the elect in heaven, 127. seq. His kingly office, 129. b. His power over a peculiar people, 130. a. b. His mediatorial kingdom is distinguished from the essential one, ibid. b. Not in reality, but only in reason, since God alone could have exercised even the mediatorial kingdom, 131. a. He administers this according to the Father's will, ibid. b. As God-man [Theanthrōpos], ibid. 132. a. The whole is spiritual and heavenly, ibid. b. 133. seq. It consists in the governing and defending of his people, ibid. 35. a. It is eternal, though he administered it differently in the Old Testament and in the New, ibid. b.

units.la: Christum Messiam esse quibus argumentis demonstretur, I I.146. vide Brev. argumenta Judæorum, quibus Jesum non esse Messiam probare conantur, diluuntur, 148. a. Vitæ ejus innocentia contra Judæos defenditur, 149. b. ejus Lex in N. Test. 161. a. ejus Redemtio est causa meritoria Justificationis, 267. ejus Justitia tam activa quam passiva nobis imputatur. 283. b. seq. ejus obedientia non in passionibus solis consistit, 284. a. 285. Ille tanquam Ecclesiæ caput fidelium salutem in tuto collocat, 390. b. ceu Redemtor & Salvator idemque præstat, 391. b. ut triumphator Sathanæ, 393. a. ejus victoria de Sathana perfectissima est, ibid. Unio ejus cum fidelibus variis similitudinibus adumbratur, 396. a. efficit ne unquam dissolvatur, ibid. b. instituit S. Cœnam, 461. b. Caput est Ecclesiæ, 507. b. 555. Rex Ecclesiæ est, 515. a. Vocat Ecclesiæ Ministros, 565. b. Vetans resistere malo, &c. & jubens inimicos diligere, judicia criminalia non sustulit, 614. a. solus est unus ille Ecclesiæ Pastor, 639. 640. unicum Ecclesiæ caput, ibid. b. redibit ad Judicium, 716. b. vide Adventus item Judicium ult. singulariter resurrectionis tam piorum quàm impiorum causa est, sed non sine discrimine, 734. b. quomodo dicatur factus in spiritum vivificantem, 739. a. Voce sua omnipotente excitabit mortuos, 741. a. singulariter causa est resurrectionis mortuorum, 735. ut & vitæ æternæ, 769. b.
units.tr: That Christ is the Messiah, and by what arguments this is demonstrated, I I.146. See Brev. The arguments of the Jews by which they try to prove that Jesus is not the Messiah are refuted, 148. a. The innocence of his life is defended against the Jews, 149. b. His law in the New Testament, 161. a. His redemption is the meritorious cause of justification, 267. His righteousness, both active and passive, is imputed to us, 283. b. seq. His obedience does not consist in his sufferings alone, 284. a. 285. As head of the Church he places the salvation of the faithful in safety, 390. b. As Redeemer and Saviour, and he is the same, he bestows it, 391. b. As triumphant over Satan, 393. a. His victory over Satan is most complete, ibid. His union with the faithful is shadowed forth by various similitudes, 396. a. He brings it about that it is never dissolved, ibid. b. He instituted the Lord's Supper, 461. b. He is the head of the Church, 507. b. 555. He is King of the Church, 515. a. He calls the ministers of the Church, 565. b. In forbidding resistance to evil, etc., and in commanding us to love our enemies, he did not abolish criminal courts, 614. a. He alone is that one Shepherd of the Church, 639. 640. The sole head of the Church, ibid. b. He will return to judgement, 716. b. See Advent, also the Last Judgement. He alone is the cause of the resurrection of the pious and the impious alike, but not without distinction, 734. b. In what sense he is said to have been made a life-giving spirit, 739. a. By his almighty voice he will raise the dead, 741. a. He alone is the cause of the resurrection of the dead, 735. and of eternal life, 769. b.

units.la: Christianorum ψευδώνυμον impietas Religionis veritati nihil derogat, 1.6. b.
units.tr: The false name Christians: the impiety of professors does not detract from the truth of the religion, 1.6. b.

units.la: Christomachorum historia, I I. 25. b. &c. quatuor classes, I. eorum, qui carnem Christi phantasticam docuerunt, ibid. 26. a. II. eorum, qui circa originem naturæ ejus humanæ erraverunt, III. eorum, qui de persona Christi erraverunt, ibid. IV. eorum, qui de unione naturarum in una persona hallucinati sunt, ibid. 26. b. eorundem argumenta confutantur, ibid. 27. a.
units.tr: The history of the Christomachi, I I. 25. b. etc. Four classes: I. of those who taught that the flesh of Christ was phantasmal; ibid. 26. a. II. of those who erred concerning the origin of his human nature; III. of those who erred concerning the person of Christ, ibid. IV. of those who went astray concerning the union of the natures in one person, ibid. 26. b. Their arguments are refuted, ibid. 27. a.

units.la: Chrysippi enunciatum, quo de quacunque re dici ab æterno potuerit, aut erit, aut non erit; explicatur & refutatur, 248.
units.tr: The saying of Chrysippus, by which it could be said of any thing from eternity that it either is or will be, or is not or will not be; it is explained and refuted, 248.

units.la: Cibus. Veterum non herbæ & arborum fructus, sed etiam animalia fuerunt, I. 235. eorum delectus non est jejunium, 362. a. Sacramentalis V. Test. 491. 492. N. Test. 492. b. vide Manna.
units.tr: Food. Among the ancients the food was not only herbs and the fruits of trees, but also animals, I. 235. Their choice is not fasting, 362. a. Sacramental food of the Old Testament, 491. 492. of the New Testament, 492. b. See Manna.

units.tr: Food–

units.tr: Food laws of the Hebrews: what were they? I. 671. b. 689. b. These, and in them the distinction between clean and unclean animals, were not without mystery, 689. b.

units.la: Cicero conflagrationem mundi statuit. II.752. a.
units.tr: Cicero held that the world would be consumed by fire, II.752. a.

units.la: Circumcisio quale fuerit Sacramentum? I.449. a. tempus circumcidendi, ibid. personae circumcidendae, ibid. b. ritus, ibid.450. a. instrumentum, ibid. b. Mysterium, 451. a. cordis circumcisio quae? 451. a. ejusdem duratio, 452. abrogata in Nov. Test. ibid. b.
units.tr: Circumcision: what kind of sacrament was it? I.449. a. The time for circumcising, ibid. The persons to be circumcised, ibid. b. The rite, ibid. 450. a. The instrument, ibid. b. The mystery, 451. a. What is circumcision of the heart? 451. a. Its duration, 452. Abrogated in the New Testament, ibid. b.

units.la: Circumcisus est Christus, ut nostro loco ceu sponsor Legem impleret, II.358. b.
units.tr: Circumcised: Christ was circumcised, so that in our place, as surety, he might fulfil the law, II.358. b.

units.la: Civitas. Earum origo, I I.617.
units.tr: Cities. Their origin, II.617.

units.la: Civitas magna illa, in qua Dominus noster crucifixus est, est Imperium Romanum, II.683. a.
units.tr: That great city in which our Lord was crucified is the Roman Empire, II.683. a.

units.la: Clamantia peccata quaenam? 357. a.
units.tr: Crying sins: which are they? 357. a.

units.tr: Keys. What is the power of the keys? II.653. b. It was given not to Peter alone, whether as a promise or as a gift, ibid. In what manner was it given to the ministers of the Church? I.321. a. To the apostles? II.292. b. What did the insignia of the keys delivered to teachers signify? II, 584. a. In what does their power consist? 587. b. The twofold power of the keys of the kingdom of heaven, 588. What was given to Peter? 589. a. The power of the keys granted to the apostles does not prove the temporal power of the Pope, 648. b.

units.la: Clerus, ejus appellatio Papae ministris non convenit, II.662. b. Cleri exemtio a potestate seculari, vi tonsurae, Antichristiana est, 667 b. argumenta contraria afferuntur & refelluntur, 668. a.
units.tr: Clergy: the designation does not apply to the ministers of the Pope, II.662. b. The exemption of the clergy from secular power, by virtue of the tonsure, is antichristian, 667. b. Arguments to the contrary are adduced and refuted, 668. a.

units.la: Clerici in primitiva Ecclesia quinam fuerint? II. 570. b. quinam olim appellati sint? 612 a. Clerici gubernantes primi Episcopi sunt, 668 b. supererogantes sunt Monachi, 672. a.
units.tr: Clerics: who were they in the primitive Church? II. 570. b. By what names were they formerly called? 612. a. Clerics who govern were the first bishops, 668. b. The supererogating clerics are the monks, 672. a.

units.la: Clypeus Dei Abrahamo promissus, I.428. b.
units.tr: Shield of God, promised to Abraham, I.428. b.

units.tr: Celibacy of the Papists and the monastics does not surpass marriage, I. 589. b. Its disadvantages are weighed, 590. a. The vow of celibacy is rejected, 595. b. Its law, annexed to the greater orders, is wholly antichristian, II.664. b. Its disadvantages and harms, 666. The reasons in its favour are answered, ibid. b. The vow of celibacy is assailed, 169. b.

Is it in a place, and how? ibid. 196. a. It is not immutable and incorruptible, ibid. b. The highest heaven was created first, 199. a. It is a place, 200. a. The nature of the third heaven is not perceived in this life, 200. b. Its orbs are not solid, 203. b. God governs heaven and the heavenly bodies, 259. b. The heavens are not moved by angels, 283. a.

units.la: Caelum in quod Christus ascendit, supremum, idemque locus proprie dictus ab aliis distinctus est, II, 66. a. beatorum quale sit, declaratur, 694. a.
units.tr: Heaven into which Christ ascended: the highest, and the place properly so called, distinguished from others, II, 66. a. What the heaven of the blessed is, is declared, 694. a.

units.la: Coena Domini definitur, II 460. b. varia ejus nomina, 461. a. quando a Christo instituta, ibid. b. partes ejus Ministerium & Mysterium, ibid. Symbola ejus externa, 461. b. locus & tempus, 473. b. 474. a. Mysterium, 474. b. finis, 478. a.
units.tr: Coena Domini (the Lord's Supper) is defined, II 460. b. Its various names, 461. a. When it was instituted by Christ, ibid. b. Its parts, the ministry and the mystery, ibid. Its outward signs, 461. b. Place and time, 473. b. 474. a. The mystery, 474. b. Its end, 478. a.

units.la: Coenobitarum & Coenobiorum origo, I I.675. a. b.
units.tr: The origin of Coenobitae and Coenobia (monks living in community), I 675. a. b.

units.la: Coetus sacri fidelium vocatorum Ecclesia est, II. 506. b.
units.tr: The Coetus of the holy called faithful is the Church, II 506. b.

units.la: Coetuum publicorum ad cultus Divini exercitium antiquitas, I.437. a.
units.tr: The antiquity of public assemblies for the exercise of divine worship, I 437. a.

units.la: Coge intrare non favet haereticidio, I.588. b.
units.tr: Coge intrare (compel them to come in) does not favour the killing of heretics, I 588. b.

units.la: Cagitatio & locutio honorifica de Deo, I. 542. b.
units.tr: Cogitatio and honourable speech about God, I 542. b.

units.la: Cogitare recte de Deo homo naturalis non potest, I. 10. a.
units.tr: Natural man cannot think rightly about God, I 10. a.

units.la: Cognatio spiritualis suscepto rum nulla est, II.460. a.
units.tr: Spiritual kinship between those who have been received (into the Church) does not exist, II 460. a.

units.la: Cognitio Dei, ejus partes, I. 62. a a cognitione creaturarum quomodo differat, I. 81. 82. extendit se ad singula hominum dicta & facta, 83. a. causa ejus in Scriptura expressa non traditur, ib. b.
units.tr: The knowledge of God, its parts, I 62. a. How it differs from knowledge of creatures, I 81, 82. It extends to each word and deed of men, 83. a. The cause of it is not expressly handed down in Scripture, ibid. b.

units.la: Cognitio Dei, qua cognoscitur: ad amorem Dei requiritur, I. 520. b. cognoscitur Deus a creaturis non quoad Essentiam, 273. b.
units.tr: The knowledge of God, by which God is known: it is required for the love of God, I 520. b. God is known by creatures not as to His essence, 273. b.

units.la: Cognitio Angelorum qualis sit, I.273. seq. vide Brev. hominis in vita aeterna perfecta erit, I I.780. b.
units.tr: The knowledge of angels, what it is like, I 273 ff.; see Brev. Man's knowledge in eternal life will be perfect, II 780. b.

units.la: Cognoscere virum vel uxorem quid in Scriptura significent? I.119. b.
units.tr: What do "to know" a man or a wife (Gen. 4 etc.) mean in Scripture? I 119. b.

units.la: Colemanniani Ecclesiae potestatem in Magistratum transferunt, II,616. a.
units.tr: The Erastians transfer the power of the Church to the magistrate, II 616. a.

units.la: Collybista qui? I.615. b.
units.tr: Who were the Collybistae? I 615. b.

units.la: Columna & stabilimentum veritatis an, & quomodo Ecclesia fit? II.513. a.
units.tr: Is the Church the "pillar and ground of the truth", and if so, how? II 513. a.

units.la: Combustione quaenam criminia plectebantur? I.711. b.
units.tr: What crimes were punished by burning? I 711. b.

units.la: Comitas (seu affabilitas quid? I.630. b.
units.tr: What is courtesy (or affability)? I 630. b.

units.la: Comminationes Dei implexam conditionem habent, I.80. b.
units.tr: God's threatenings have an implied condition, I 80. b.

units.la: Commodatum & mutuum affinia sunt, I.615. a.
units.tr: Loan for use (commodatum) and loan for consumption (mutuum) are related, I 615. a.

units.la: Communio bonorum quousque obtinuerit? I. 235. a. communio rerum ab initio negativa obtinuit, 602. a. possessionum nulla locum habet, 602. b.
units.tr: Communion of goods: how far did it prevail? I 235. a. Community of goods was negative from the beginning, 602. a. Ownership of possessions has no place, 602. b.

units.la: Communio fidelium N. Test. cum spiritibus coelestibus, II.181. a. cum Christo, quibus verbis Scriptura exprimat? 253. a. qualis sit? 475. b. communio sanctorum est Ecclesia, 510. a. fidelium cum Ecclesia errante & inordinata quatenus licita sit? 525. a.
units.tr: Communion of the faithful of the New Testament with heavenly spirits, II 181. a. With Christ: what words does Scripture use to express it? 253. a. What kind is it? 475. b. The communion of saints is the Church, 510. a. How far is it lawful for the faithful to have communion with the erring and disorderly Church? 525. a.

units.la: Communio sub una specie in Veteri Ecclesia non obtinuit, II. 472. b.
units.tr: Communion under one kind did not prevail in the Old Church, II 472. b.

units.la: Communicatio Idiomatum, unionem naturarum in una Christi Persona consequens non-mutua & mutua explicatur, II.20. a. &c. vide Idioma, Apotelesmata, Christus. Mutua triplex, tum Idiomatum, tum officii, tum operationum, 21. a. Idiomatum, 22.23.a. officii & honoris, ib.d. operationum seu Apotelesmatum, 23. b. errantium circa hoc dogma perplexitas attingitur, 27. b.
units.tr: Communication of idioms, which follows from the union of the natures in the one Person of Christ, is explained as non-mutual and mutual, II 20. a. etc.; see Idioma, Apotelesmata, Christus. There is a threefold mutual communication: of idioms, of office, and of operations, 21. a. Of idioms, 22, 23. a. Of office and honour, ibid. d. Of operations or apotelesmata, 23. b. The perplexity of those who err about this doctrine is touched upon, 27. b.

units.la: Communicatio cum peccato alieno, quot modis fiat? I.561. b. 561.
units.tr: Communication with another's sin: in how many ways does it happen? I 561. b. 561.

units.la: Communicantes in S. Coena vel digni, II.481. a. vel indigni sunt, ibid.
units.tr: Those who communicate at the Lord's Supper are either worthy or unworthy, II 481. a., ibid.

units.la: Compositio nulla in Deum cadit, I.72. b. 73. a.
units.tr: Composition does not fall upon God, I 72. b. 73. a.

units.la: Conceptio Christi est è Spiritu S. II, 12. b. cujus initia super B. Virg. explicatur, ibid. non ideo ejus Pater est, 13. b. conceptionis Christi, III. actus explicantur, 13. a. b. quomodo immaculata in utero B. Virg. exit, 17. b Pontificiorum error, ib. a.
units.tr: The conception of Christ is by the Holy Spirit, II 12. b. Its beginnings with regard to the Blessed Virgin are explained, ibid. He is not therefore His Father, 13. b. The acts of Christ's conception are explained, III 13. a. b. How was He born immaculate in the womb of the Blessed Virgin? 17. b. The error of the Papists, ibid. a.

units.la: Concilia. ea Judex controversiarum supremus & infallibilis non sunt, I. 56. a. concilii Chalcedonensis de unione naturarum in Christo sententia, II. 19. a. Tridentinum Pelagianismum tuetur, 116. b. praeceptorum Dei perfectam observantiam possibilem esse docet, 237. a. fidem omnem amissibilem esse, 242. a. charitatem fidei formam constituit, 255. b. propositionem illam: Gratia, quae justificamur, est tantum favor Dei, anathemate notat, 266. b. ejus error de Justificatione causa formali, 270. eandem in remissionem peccatorum & renovationem mentis partitur, 271. b. hominem imputatione sola Justitiae Christi justificari negat, 278. Fidem a poenitentia salutari removet, 323. b. bona opera propter Christum mereri, affirmat, 333. b. ejusdem de coelibatu sententia, 666. a. Episcopos Presbyteris superiores esse definivit, 668. b. Nicenum non prohibet clericis matrimonium, 667. a. Neocaesariense clericis post ordinationem matrimonium vetat, ibid. b. Carthaginense non vetat clericis conjugium, ibid. Toletanum resurrectionem ejusdem numero carnis statuit, 738.
units.tr: Councils: they are not the supreme and infallible judges of controversies, I 56. a. The view of the Council of Chalcedon on the union of the natures in Christ, II 19. a. The Council of Trent defends Pelagianism, 116. b. It teaches that perfect observance of God's commandments is possible, 237. a. It holds that all faith can be lost, 242. a. It makes charity the form of faith, 255. b. It anathematizes the proposition: "The grace by which we are justified is only the favour of God", 266. b. Its error on formal cause in justification, 270. It divides the same into remission of sins and renewal of mind, 271. b. It denies that man is justified by the imputation of Christ's righteousness alone, 278. It removes faith from saving repentance, 323. b. It affirms that good works merit through Christ, 333. b. Its view on celibacy, 666. a. It defined that bishops are superior to presbyters, 668. b. The Council of Nicaea does not forbid marriage to clergy, 667. a. The Council of Neocaesarea forbids marriage to clergy after ordination, ibid. b. The Council of Carthage does not forbid marriage to clergy, ibid. The Council of Toledo held that the resurrection is of the same numerical flesh, 738.

units.la: Conciliorum & Synodorum Ecclesiasticarum institutum utile, II.613. b. controversiae quomodo in iis definiendae? 614. b. eorundem distributio, 615. eorundem membra quinam esse possint? ib. b. quis in iis ordo servandus? 616. a. Conciliis Papa subest, 676. seq. nec convocandi, nec moderandi, nec confirmandi concilia jus habet, ib. 677. b. Veteras Imperatores convocarunt, 678. a. & quoad ordinem praesederunt, ibid. argumenta pro jure suprematus Papae refelluntur, ib. b. conciliorum a Papa confirmatorum sententia, nec judicialis, nec absolute infallibilis est, 679. a. Veteras ab Imperatoribus confirmata sunt, ibid. b. concilia errare possunt, ibid.
units.tr: Councils and ecclesiastical synods: a useful institution, II 613. b. How are controversies to be settled in them? 614. b. Their distribution, 615. Who may be their members? ibid. b. What order is to be observed in them? 616. a. Councils are subject to the Pope, 676 ff. He has no right to convene, to direct, or to confirm councils, ibid.; 677. b. The ancient emperors convened them, 678. a. And presided over them as to order, ibid. The arguments for the right of papal supremacy are refuted, ibid. b. The judgment of councils confirmed by the Pope is neither judicial nor absolutely infallible, 679. a. The ancient councils were confirmed by the emperors, ibid. b. Councils can err, ibid.

units.la: Concio Conciones ex Thoma & Scoto Tiguri aliquando habitae, II.595. a. Doctrina qualis esse debeat? 593. b. 594. ejus norma Verbum Dei est, ibid. b. exhortatio Sacra qualis esse debeat? 594. a. conciones quales haberi conveniat? 596. Catechetica laudantur, 598. b. Textus Sacri in concionibus ad populum quales esse, quomodo declarari ac tractari debeant, 596. Doctrina in Concione quid sit? ejusdem applicatio quomodo instituenda, 596. Usus in concione quid sit, ibid.
units.tr: Sermons: sermons delivered at Zurich sometimes from Thomas and Scotus, II 595. a. What should the doctrine be like? 593. b. 594. Its norm is the Word of God, ibid. b. What should a sacred exhortation be like? 594. a. What kind of sermons ought to be preached? 596. Catechetical sermons are commended, 598. b. How the holy texts are to be explained and handled in sermons to the people, 596. What is doctrine in a sermon, and how is its application to be made? 596. What is use in a sermon? ibid.

units.la: Concionator V. Dei qualis esse debeat? II.594. b. ejus proprium munus oste nditur, 595. b. aedificatio Ecclesiae praecipuus ejus scopus esse debet, 596. a. non breves tantum pericopas, sed liberaliores Scriptu-
units.tr: The preacher: what kind of person should he be? II 594. b. His proper office is shown, 595. b. The building up of the Church should be his chief aim, 596. a. He must expound not only short passages but the fuller portions of Scripture,

units.la: iæ explicare debet, ibid. privatim auditores instituere tenetur, 596. 597.
units.tr: ibid. He is bound to instruct his hearers privately, 596, 597.

units.la: Concomitantia figmentum in S. Cœna exploditur, II. 472. a.
units.tr: The fiction of concomitance in the Lord's Supper is exploded, II 472. a.

units.la: Concordia gratiam Dei inter & voluntatem humanam qualis vigere debeat? II.219. b.
units.tr: What harmony should prevail between the grace of God and the human will? II 219. b.

units.la: Concupiscentia non exhaurit naturam peccati originalis, I.349.a. Veri nominis peccatum est, 351. a. ejus gradus Jac.I.14. 355. b. alia recta, alia corrupta, 638. b. de ea Pauli mens qualis fuerit, Rom. VII.7. 639. a. quotuplex sit? ibid. b. 640. a. habitualis perversitas, vanitas perstringitur, ibid. a; primæ ejus in homine motiones à peccato immunes non sunt, ib. b. ejus objecta innumera sunt, 641. b.
units.tr: Concupiscence does not exhaust the nature of original sin, I 349. a. It is sin in the true sense, 351. a. Its degrees, James 1:14, 355. b. Some are right, others corrupt, 638. b. What was Paul's mind about it, Rom. 7:7, 639. a. How many kinds are there? ibid. b. 640. a. Habitual perversity and vanity are censured, ibid. a. The first motions of it in man are not free from sin, ibid. b. Its objects are innumerable, 641. b.

units.la: Concursus causæ primæ cum secundis, I. 253. b. concursus Dei cum causis liberis non est indifferens, 266. a. 267. a. nec tamen Eum peccati authorem facit, ibid.
units.tr: The concurrence of the first cause with secondary causes, I 253. b. The concurrence of God with free causes is not indifferent, 266. a. 267. a. Yet it does not make Him the author of sin, ibid.

units.la: Condescensus in sermone non est adulationis species, I. 631. b.
units.tr: Condescension in speech is not a form of flattery, I 631. b.

units.la: Condonanda peccata proximo, II.603. b.
units.tr: Sins are to be forgiven to one's neighbour, II 603. b.

units.la: Confessio Christi in cruce, I, 542. b. Veritatis necessaria est. 619. a. Adversariorum, an sit nota veræ Ecclesiæ, II.551. b.
units.tr: Confession of Christ on the cross, I 542. b. Confession of the truth is necessary, 619. a. Whether the confession of adversaries is a mark of the true Church, II 551. b.

units.la: Confessio Helvetica laudatur, II. 596. b. circa disciplinam Ecclesiasticam, 609. a, de bonis Ecclesiæ, 612. a.
units.tr: The Helvetic Confession is commended, II 596. b. On ecclesiastical discipline, 609. a. On the goods of the Church, 612. a.

units.la: Confessio peccatorum soli Deo facienda, II. 319. b. quando & quomodo hominibus? 320. auricularis refellitur, ibid.
units.tr: Confession of sins is to be made to God alone, II 319. b. When and how is it to be made to men? 320. Auricular confession is refuted, ibid.

units.la: Confirmatio Angelorum in bono immutabilis est, I.278. b. nec tamen ex merito ullo, 279. a.
units.tr: The confirmation of angels in good is immutable, I 278. b. Yet not from any merit, 279. a.

units.la: Confirmationis Sacramentum refutatur, II.499.
units.tr: The sacrament of confirmation is refuted, II 499.

units.la: Conflagratio Mundi in consummatione seculorum fiet, quæ tum ex Scripturæ testimoniis disertis, II.751. tum gentilium etiam consensu, 752. demonstratur. Causa & modus ejus à Burneto assertus expenditur, 753. a. interim ea non annihilabitur, sed renovabitur Mundus, ib. b. Veterum & recentiorum hac in re dissensus, & dissentientium argumenta excutiuntur, 754. b. creaturæ per conflagrationem renovandæ explicantur, 755. b. vide Mundi finis.
units.tr: The conflagration of the world will take place at the consummation of the ages; this is demonstrated both from plain testimonies of Scripture, II 751, and from the agreement of the Gentiles also, 752. Its cause and manner as asserted by Burnet are examined, 753. a. Meanwhile it will not be annihilated, but the world will be renewed, ibid. b. The disagreement of the ancients and moderns on this matter, and the arguments of the dissenters, are examined, 754. b. The creatures to be renewed through the conflagration are explained, 755. b. See End of the World.

units.la: Congregationes fidelium sunt frequentandæ, II.516. earundem necessitas, ibid. b.
units.tr: Congregations of the faithful are to be attended; II.516. Their necessity, ibid. b.

units.la: Conjugium, ejus primæva institutio, I.230. b. ei polygamia repugnat, 231. a. ejus fides cum fœdere Gratiæ comparatur, 384. Conjugium legitimum cœlibatu per se non inferius est, 589. b. seq. ejus utilitas, 590. a. definitur, ib. b. ejus pactum indivulsum, 592. b. ejus plures utilitates recensentur, 594. b. ejus interdictum ad doctrinas Dæmoniorum pertinet. II.665. b.
units.tr: Marriage: its original institution, I.230. b. Polygamy is contrary to it, 231. a. Its faithfulness is compared with the covenant of grace, 384. Lawful marriage is not in itself inferior to celibacy, 589. b. seq. Its usefulness, 590. a. Its definition, ib. b. Its indissoluble bond, 592. b. Its several benefits are listed, 594. b. Its prohibition pertains to the doctrines of demons, II.665. b.

units.la: Conjugum officia mutua quæ? I. 570. a. 594. b. 595. a. 728. b.
units.tr: What are the mutual duties of spouses? I.570. a. 594. b. 595. a. 728. b.

units.la: Conjunctio Christi cum Ecclesia, eum caput Ecclesiæ declarat, II.556. a.
units.tr: The conjunction of Christ with the Church declares him to be the head of the Church, II.556. a.

units.la: Consanguineitatis gradus qui statuendi, I. 590. b. graduum Divina lege prohibitorum rationes investigantur, 591. b.
units.tr: Which degrees of consanguinity are to be fixed? I.590. b. The reasons for the degrees of kinship forbidden by divine law are examined, 591. b.

units.la: Conscientia Dei quid? I.8. a.
units.tr: What is the conscience of God? I.8. a.

units.la: Conscientia cujusvis hominis Dei existentiam arguit, I.63. b. ejus tribunal quale sit? 304. b. errans quid? 357. b. ejus circa Deum officia, 522. a. conscientiam bonam expellere quid sit? II. 407. b. ejus testimonium magnam vim habet, 745. a.
units.tr: The conscience of every person argues for the existence of God, I.63. b. What sort of tribunal is the conscience? 304. b. What is an erring conscience? 357. b. Its duties towards God, 522. a. What is it to put away a good conscience? II.407. b. The testimony of conscience has great force, 745. a.

units.la: Consensus quatenus conjugium faciat? I.592. a.
units.tr: To what extent does consent make a marriage? I.592. a.

units.la: Consensus Evangelicorum circa S. Cœnam in quibus, vicissim dissensus in quibus confisitat, II. 496. a. consensus in Doctrina cum Ecclesia antiqua & Patribus, an nota verae Ecclesiæ sit? I I.548. a.
units.tr: The consensus of the Evangelicals concerning the Holy Supper: in what points they agree, and conversely in what points they disagree, II.496. a. Whether agreement in doctrine with the ancient Church and the Fathers is a mark of the true Church, II.548. a.

units.la: Consecratio Symbolorum in Eucharistia quomodo facta sit à Christo, & quomodo fiat à Sacrificulis Romanis? I I.464. a. à quo vim suam accipiat? ibid. b.
units.tr: How was the consecration of the elements in the Eucharist performed by Christ, and how is it performed by the Roman sacrificing priests? II.464. a. From whom does it receive its power? ibid. b.

units.la: Consequentiæ quæ & quando in rebus fidei locum habeant? I.12. b. an ad fidem obligent? ibid. 13. a. earum usus docetur, 13. b.
units.tr: What are consequences, and when do they have a place in matters of faith? I.12. b. Are they binding on faith? ibid. 13. a. Their use is taught, 13. b.

units.la: Conservatio rerum Dei cooperationem requirit, I. 65. a. est continuata creatio, 241. b, actus prior Providentiæ est, 250. b. 251. b.
units.tr: The conservation of things requires the cooperation of God, I.65. a. It is a continued creation, 241. b. It is a prior act of Providence, 250. b. 251. b.

units.la: Consilium Dei quid? I. 148.149. vide Decretum in Breviario L.V.
units.tr: What is the counsel of God? I.148, 149. See Decree in the Breviary, L.V.

units.la: Consilium Pacis quid? I.157. b. inter Deum Patrem & Filium, 376. a, 377. a. in tempore per gradus processit, 382. a.
units.tr: What is the counsel of peace? I.157. b. Between God the Father and the Son, 376. a, 377. a. In time it proceeded by stages, 382. a.

units.la: Consilia Evangelica confutantur, II. 164. 165. eorum origo & occasio ostenditur, 167. b.
units.tr: The evangelical counsels are refuted; II.164, 165. Their origin and occasion are shown, 167. b.

units.la: Consolatio afflictorum ex sanctificatione, I.315. b. præsentissima ex morte Christi, II.127. b.
units.tr: Consolation of the afflicted from sanctification, I.315. b. Most immediate from the death of Christ, II.127. b.

units.la: Constantini M. in Ecclesiam liberalitas, II.611. a.
units.tr: The liberality of Constantine the Great towards the Church, II.611. a.

units.la: Consubstantiatio refellitur, II, 493. argumenta contraria diluuntur, 494. b.
units.tr: Consubstantiation is refuted; II.493. The arguments to the contrary are dissolved, 494. b.

units.la: Consummatio promissionum in N. Test. II.170. b. fidelium N.Test. in his terris, 181. b.
units.tr: The fulfilment of the promises in the New Testament, II.170. b. The New Testament believers in this earthly life, 181. b.

units.la: Consummatio seculi quid notet? II.528. a.
units.tr: What does the consummation of the age signify? II.528. a.

units.la: Contentio pia, I I.251. b.
units.tr: Godly contention, II.251. b.

units.la: Continentia donum non omnibus concessum est, II. 667, a.
units.tr: Continence is not granted as a gift to all; II.667. a.

units.la: Contingens & necessarium quomodo aliquid dici possit respectu Dei? I.87. a. contingens quid? & contingentia in rebus quotuplex? 262. b.
units.tr: How can something be called contingent or necessary with respect to God? I.87. a. What is the contingent, and how many kinds of contingency are there in things? 262. b.

units.la: Contractus quid? I.610. b. contractuum differentia multiplex, 611.
units.tr: What is a contract? I.610. b. The kinds of contracts are many, 611.

units.la: Contritio ad resipiscentiam qualis requiratur, I,323. b.
units.tr: What sort of contrition is required for repentance? I.323. b.

units.la: Controversiæ Religionis quomodo in Conciliis vel Synodis definiendæ sint? II.614. b.
units.tr: How are controversies of religion to be settled in councils or synods? II.614. b.

units.la: Conversatio bona, I.542. a.
units.tr: Good conduct, I.542. a.

units.la: Conversio hominis in Scripturis gratiæ soli accepta refertur, I, 220. b. 221. est omnipotentiæ Dei opus, 221. a. prædicatio Verbi externa absque interna Spiritus S. operatione, inutilis est in convertendo homine, II.210. a.
units.tr: The conversion of a human being is ascribed in Scripture to grace alone; I.220. b. 221. It is a work of the omnipotence of God, 221. a. The external preaching of the Word, without the internal operation of the Holy Spirit, is useless in converting a human being, II.210. a.

units.la: Convivium spirituale & Mysticum est S.Cœna, II.475. a. duplex ejus cibus & potus, ibid.
units.tr: The Holy Supper is a spiritual and mystical banquet, II.475. a. Its food and drink are twofold, ibid.

units.la: Copernici Solem stantem & terram mobilem statuentis quæ fuerit mens? I.211. b.
units.tr: What was the mind of Copernicus, who held that the sun stands still and the earth moves? I.211. b.

units.la: Cor à Diabolo impleri quid sit? I.292. a. ejus immunditia peccatum est, 345. a. cor novum à solo Deo datur, 475. a. cor seu animus ad cultum Dei requiritur, 525. a. 527. b.
units.tr: What does it mean for the heart to be filled by the Devil? I.292. a. Its uncleanness is sin, 345. a. A new heart is given by God alone, 475. a. The heart or mind is required for the worship of God, 525. a. 527. b.

units.la: Corpus quid sit, II. 6. b. ejus proprietates panduntur, 30. b. Deum accipere sibi visibile corpus magnum miraculum est, 18. b.
units.tr: What a body is, II.6. b. Its properties are set out, 30. b. That God should take to himself a visible body is a great miracle, 18. b.

units.la: Corpus hominis, corporis humani creatio & admiranda structura circularis & quadrata, I.216. a. b. non moriturum nisi peccasset homo, 224, a. ejus organa peccato corrupta sunt, 348. b. corporum glorificatorum subtilitas, spiritualitas qualis futura sit? 200. a. quid de eo post mortem fiat? II.697. a. honeste deduci & sepeliri debet, ibid. Corpus organicum idem numero, quod cecidit per mortem, resurget, 736. membra organica spiritusatque humores, & quæ ad ornatum pertinent, 737. a. corpus humanum in perpetuo fluxu est, ibid. b. mutabitur ejus status, 738. a. Negantium, idem numero corpus resuscitatum iri, historia, ibid. b. eorum argumenta ad partes vocata, ibid. 739. a. non obstat pulveris corporei dissipatio, & carnium humanarum ab Anthropophagis, hominibus vel bestiis, consumtio, 740. a. corpus etiam hominis glorificati, gloria implebitur, II. 781. b. ejus essentia non mutabitur, 782. a. a. ejus dotes explicantur, ibid.
units.tr: The human body: the creation and admirable structure of the human body, round and square, I.216. a. b. Man would not have died had he not sinned, 224. a. Its organs were corrupted by sin, 348. b. The subtlety of glorified bodies; what the spirituality of the future body will be like, 200. a. What happens to the body after death? II.697. a. It ought to be decently laid out and buried, ibid. The organic body, numerically the same as that which fell in death, will rise, 736. The organic members, spirits and humours, and those things that pertain to adornment, 737. a. The human body is in perpetual flux, ibid. b. Its state will be changed, 738. a. The history of those who deny that the same body numerically will be raised again, ibid. b. Their arguments are summoned to the field, ibid. 739. a. The dispersal of bodily dust, and the consumption of human flesh by cannibals, men or beasts, is no obstacle, 740. a. The body of glorified man too will be filled with glory, II.781. b. Its essence will not be changed, 782. a. Its endowments are explained, ibid.

units.la: Corpus Christi ante Resurrectionem passibile, quantum, visibile fuit, I I.21. b. quomodo aquis sustentatum fuerit? ibid. post Resurrectionem verum corpus, at spirituale & gloriosum fuit, 58. b. ejus tamen gloria in terra nondum consummata fuit, 59. a, non est ubique, sed in cœlum ascendit, 66. b, sedet ad dextram Patris, 69. b. summè gloriosum, ibid. non tamen novum est, sed quod crucifixum, suscitatum, 70. b.
units.tr: The body of Christ before the Resurrection was passible, and as far as it was visible, II.21. b. How it was sustained by the waters, ibid. After the Resurrection it was a true body, but spiritual and glorious, 58. b. Yet its glory was not yet complete on earth, 59. a. It is not everywhere, but ascended into heaven, 66. b. It sits at the right hand of the Father, 69. b. Most gloriously, ibid. Yet it is not new, but the very body that was crucified and raised, 70. b.

units.la: Corpus Christi, quale in Missa fingatur, II. 483. non est præsens in Eucharistia, modo invisibili, 485. a, non potest simul esse in cœlo & in hostia, 486. a. est in loco tantùm circumscriptive, ibid. b. corpus & sanguis Christi spiritualis in Cœna cibus & potus est, 493. b. quomodo quis reus corporis & sanguinis Christi fiat? 495. a.
units.tr: The body of Christ, as it is imagined in the Mass; II.483. It is not present in the Eucharist in an invisible manner, 485. a. It cannot be at once in heaven and in the host, 486. a. It is in a place only circumscriptively, ibid. b. The spiritual body and blood of Christ are food and drink in the Supper, 493. b. How does someone become guilty of the body and blood of Christ? 495. a.

units.la: Correptio seu redargutio proximi peccantis qualis esse debeat? II.603.604. seq.
units.tr: How ought the correction or rebuke of a sinning neighbour to be conducted? II.603, 604. seq.

units.la: Corruptio hominis quoad potentias naturales & qualitates ex peccato summa est, I.347. seq. etiam organa corporis invasit, 348. b. corruptio naturalis hominis, quoad intellectum, voluntatem & affectus, 364.
units.tr: The corruption of man in his natural powers and qualities, from sin, is complete; I.347. seq. It has also invaded the organs of the body, 348. b. The natural corruption of man in respect of the intellect, will and affections, 364.

units.la: Creare, Creatio quid? I. 184. a. vide Breviar. an momentanea fuerit? 197. 198. rerum omnium creatio etiam Christo tribuitur, 132. a. at non ut instrumento vel causæ secundæ, sed principali, ibid, 133. a.
units.tr: To create; creation: what is it? I.184. a. See the Breviary. Was it instantaneous? 197, 198. The creation of all things is also ascribed to Christ, 132. a. But not as an instrument or secondary cause, but as the principal cause, ibid. 133. a.

units.la: Creaturæ, per eas jurare non licet, I.544. a.
units.tr: It is not lawful to swear by creatures; I.544. a.

units.la: Credere in Christum an, & quomodo omnes teneantur. II.126. b. explicatur, ibid. 127. a. credendi facultatem infideles nunquam acceperunt, 215. a. nec omnibus ea communis est, ibid. credere quòd Deus sit, & quòd remunerator sit, quid significet? 533. b.
units.tr: Whether and how all are bound to believe in Christ; II.126. b. It is explained, ibid. 127. a. Unbelievers have never received the ability to believe; 215. a. Nor is this ability common to all, ibid. What does it mean to believe that God exists and that he is a rewarder? 533. b.

units.la: Credentes soli Sacramenta participant, I.400. a.
units.tr: Only believers partake of the sacraments; I.400. a.

units.la: Credita probè custodienda sunt, I.616. a.
units.tr: Things entrusted are to be carefully kept; I.616. a.

units.la: Crescite & Multiplicamini &c. quale fuerit præceptum? I.232.
units.tr: "Increase and multiply," etc.: what sort of precept was it? I.232.

units.la: Critici. Eorum falsa censura de libris V. Test. itémque de Scriptis Mosis, I.34. b. Morinus & Capellus, codicem V.Test. corrupt m asserentes, arguuntur, 36. a. error illorum de Evang. Matthæi Heb. 39. a. 11, qui Mosis authoritatem vellicant, arguuntur, 481. a.
units.tr: Critics. Their false judgement concerning the books of the Old Testament, and likewise concerning the writings of Moses; I.34. b. Morinus and Capellus, who assert that the text of the Old Testament is corrupt, are refuted, 36. a. The error of those concerning the Hebrew Gospel of Matthew, 39. a. Those who carp at the authority of Moses are refuted, 481. a.

units.la: Cruciatus Inferni Dæmonum in quo consistat? I. 228. a.
units.tr: In what does the torment of the Devils in hell consist? I.228. a.

units.la: Crucifixio Christi nos liberavit à chirographo legis, I.697. a. crucifixionem Hebræis non fuisse in usu, ostenditur, 712. a. Crucifixio Christi, II.46. b. necessaria fuit, ib. ejus historia, ib 47. a.
units.tr: The crucifixion of Christ freed us from the handwriting of the law; I.697. a. It is shown that crucifixion was not in use among the Hebrews, 712. a. The crucifixion of Christ, II.46. b. It was necessary, ibid. Its history, ibid. 47. a.

units.la: Crux. Dolor ex cruciis sensu æquus est, I.341. a. Stoica ἀνεξιθρησία camnatur, ib. b. ejus tolerantia, ib. a. necessitas & utilitas, ib. Crucis certum cuique demensum Deus destinavit, II.294. a.
units.tr: Cross. Pain from crosses is fitting in the sense of feeling, I.341. a. The Stoic apathy [ἀνεξιθρησία] is condemned, ib. b. Its endurance, ib. a. Its necessity and usefulness, ib. God has appointed to each person a fixed measure of the cross, II.294. a.

units.la: Crux quomodo à patibulo differat? II.476.
units.tr: How does the cross differ from the gallows? II.476.

units.la: Cultus Deo habendus ore, opere & corde, I.525. a. ἀγιάσεως sanctis debitus nullus est, 526. a. religiosus à civili in quibus differat? 527. a. Cultus Dei partes, 527. b. Modus, 529. a. vel qu ad cultus substantiam, vel circumstantias, ib. b. cultus Divini publici, tempus, locus, modus, &c. 554 555. cultus sacri V.Test. tempora distinguuntur & excitantur, 665. a. Test. prædictus, Mal. I.10. ib. etiam externus spiritualis est, ib. b.
units.tr: Worship is to be rendered to God with the mouth, work and heart, I.525. a. Honour [ἀγιάσεως] due to the saints is nothing, 526. a. In what respects is religious worship different from civil? 527. a. The parts of divine worship, 527. b. The manner, 529. a. Whether it concerns the substance of worship or its circumstances, ib. b. Public divine worship: time, place, manner, &c., 554, 555. The times of worship in the Old Testament are distinguished and stirred up, 665. a. In the Church of the New Testament it is not carnal but spiritual, II.183 b. The sacraments of the New Testament belong to spiritual worship, 184. The difference between natural and instituted worship of God, 428. a. The instituted worship of the New Testament is foretold in Malachi, I.10. ib. Even external worship is spiritual, ib. b.

units.la: Cukus Angelis boni quinam debeatur? I.283. a.
units.tr: What worship is due to good angels? I.283. a.

units.la: Cultus relativus, seu transitivus imaginum refellitur, I.535. seq.
units.tr: Relative or transitive worship of images is refuted, I.535 ff.

units.la: Curiositas vitanda est, I.343. a.
units.tr: Curiosity is to be avoided, I.343. a.

units.la: Custodia seu φυλακὴ pop. Israel. q uæ fuerit? I.648. a.
units.tr: What was the custody or guard [φυλακὴ] of the people of Israel? I.648. a.

units.la: Kyrie nomen Christo tributum Divinitatis argumentum est, I.127. b.
units.tr: The name Kyrie given to Christ is an argument for his divinity, I.127. b.
