units.la: DÆmones non à Deo tales creati, sed sua culpa facti sunt, I.286. b. Habent aliquod caput ceu Regem, 287. a. eorum cognitio limitata, 288. b. hominum cogitationes per se non cognoscunt, 274. vid. Angeli & Sathanas.
units.tr: Demons were not created such by God; they became so through their own fault, I.286. b. They have some head, as a king, 287. a. Their knowledge is limited, 288. b. They do not know men's thoughts of themselves, 274. See Angels and Satan.

units.la: Damnatio, ejus causa peccatum est, I.175. a. de sua vel aliorum nemo certus esse potest, 179. b.
units.tr: Condemnation: its cause is sin, I.175. a. No one can be certain of his own or another's, 179. b.

units.la: Δανάξιος quid significat? I.614. a.
units.tr: What does δανάξιος [danaxios] mean? I.614. a.

units.la: Dare quàm accipere beatius esse, quomodo fit intelligendum, I.618. a.
units.tr: How is it to be understood that it is more blessed to give than to receive? I.618. a.

units.la: David gravissimè licet peccârit, non tamen amisit Spiritum S. I.406. a. Christus cur ejus filius esse debuit? 9. b.
units.tr: Although David sinned most grievously, he did not lose the Holy Spirit, I.406. a. Why did Christ have to be David's son? 9. b.

units.la: Debitum. Quomodo Deus hominem perfectam legi obedientiam præstanti vitam æternam secundum debitum addixerit? I.324. b. hominis justificandi, 265.
units.tr: Debt. How did God, by a perfect obedience to the law, adjudge eternal life to a man according to debt? I.324. b. Of the man to be justified, 265.

units.la: Debita in oratione Dominica cur pro peccatis sumantur, I.357. a. an citra satisfactionem remitti possint, II.116. a.
units.tr: Why are debts in the Lord's Prayer taken to mean sins? I.357. a. Can they be forgiven without satisfaction? II.116. a.

units.la: Decalogus. Ejus definitio, I.500. b. est legis moralis & juris naturalis compendium, ibid. & 313. a. vid. Brev. ejus explicandi regulæ, 313. b. 501. b. Divisio in 2 tabulas, 511. a. variæ variorum divisiones, ibid. 512. Augustini non placet, 513. a 514. a. Petri Martyris, 513 a. ejus præcipua capita, 513. b. ejus usus respectu hominis integri, peccatoris & inprimis regeniti explicatur, 642. b. quos gratiæ strictura s continet, 464. a. norma est resipiscentiæ & novæ vitæ, ibid. ejus præcepta à Christo aucta non sunt, II. 168. a. 169. a. Prooemium exponitur, I.517. a. ejus truncus est, quòd damnet nativam hominis corruptionem, 518 a. rami sunt tres, habere Deum. 518. a. habere unum Deum, 522. b, habere Deum verum, 523. b. vide Præceptum.
units.tr: The Decalogue. Its definition, I.500. b. It is a summary of the moral law and of natural law, ibid. and 313. a. See the Summary. Rules for explaining it, 313. b, 501. b. Division into two tables, 511. a. Various divisions by various writers, ibid., 512. Augustine's division does not please, 513. a, 514. a. Peter Martyr's, 513. a. Its main chapters, 513. b. Its use with respect to the whole man, the sinner, and above all the regenerate, is explained, 642. b. What restraint of grace it contains, 464. a. It is the norm of repentance and of new life, ibid. Its precepts were not increased by Christ, II.168. a, 169. a. Its preface is explained, I.517. a. Its trunk is that it condemns man's native corruption, 518. a. It has three branches: to have God, 518. a; to have one God, 522. b; to have the true God, 523. b. See Precept.

units.la: Decernens voluntas Dei est altissima causa rerum, I.90. a. semper efficax, ib. 91. a. 92. b.
units.tr: The decreeing will of God is the highest cause of things, I.90. a. It is always effective, ib.; 91. a; 92. b.

units.la: Decimæ, an jure Divino Ecclesiæ ministris solvendæ? II.577. a. an solis Ecclesiasticis debeantur? I.722. a. earum genera distinguenda, I.662. a. quid in V. T. significaverint, 679. b.
units.tr: Tithes: are they to be paid to the ministers of the Church by divine right? II.577. a. Are they due to ecclesiastics alone? I.722. a. Their kinds are to be distinguished, I.662. a. What did they signify in the Old Testament? 679. b.

units.la: Decimum Decalogi præceptum malè in duo dispescitur, I.514. b.
units.tr: The tenth precept of the Decalogue is wrongly divided into two, I.514. b.

units.la: Decretum Dei definitur, I.148. a. vid. Brev. Nullum generale est, 152. a. quo sensu generale dici possit, 154. a. Decreta Dei quomodo absoluta autconditionata sint, 151. b. eorum ordo tenendus, 152. b.
units.tr: The decree of God is defined, I.148. a. See Summary. There is no general decree, 152. a. In what sense it can be called general, 154. a. How God's decrees are absolute or conditional, 151. b. Their order must be kept, 152. b.

units.la: Decretum electionis absolutum esse ostenditur, 162. a. vindicatur ab objectionibus, 165. seqq. vid. Electio.
units.tr: The decree of election is shown to be absolute, 162. a. It is defended against objections, 165 ff. See Election.

units.la: Defensio sui quatenus licita sit? I.583. b. aliena, 586. b.
units.tr: In what cases is self-defence lawful? I.583. b. Defence of others, 586. b.

units.la: Defunctis Missæ nihil prosunt, II.491. b.
units.tr: Masses for the dead profit nothing, II.491. b.

units.la: Deperatio quid? I.547. a.
units.tr: What is despair? I.547. a.

units.la: Deitas & Deus quomodo differant? I.111. a. Patris, I.123. b. Filii, 124. 125. seqq. Filii firmissimè demonstrata, 134. b. ejus hostium historia, 135. a. Vindicatur ab adversariorum objectionibus, 136, a. Spiritus S. 141. b. 143.
units.tr: How do the Deity and God differ? I.111. a. The Deity of the Father, I.123. b. Of the Son, 124, 125 ff. The deity of the Son is most firmly demonstrated, 134. b. History of its enemies, 135. a. It is defended against the objections of opponents, 136. a. The Holy Spirit, 141. b, 143.

units.la: Dinos qualis precum species? I.346. b. 347. a.
units.tr: What kind of prayer is a dinos? I.346. b, 347. a.

units.la: Denarius numerus an sit mysticus? I.512. a.
units.tr: Is the number denarius mystical? I.512. a.

units.la: Deorum gentilium distributio, I.106. a.
units.tr: Distribution of the pagan gods, I.106. a.

units.la: Dependentia creaturæ à creatore non impedit, quò minus eæ sint veræ suarum actionum causæ, I.253. b. Non obest voluntatis libertati, 254. b. 267. a.
units.tr: The dependence of a creature on its creator does not prevent it from being a true cause of its own actions, I.253. b. It does not hinder the freedom of the will, 254. b, 267. a.

units.la: Dependentia Ecclesiæ à Christo eum declarat Caput Ecclesiæ, I.556. b.
units.tr: The dependence of the Church on Christ shows him to be the Head of the Church, I.556. b.

units.la: Descensus Christi ad inferos explicatur, II.51. b.
units.tr: The descent of Christ into hell is explained, II.51. b.

units.la: Desertio Christi in cruce non fuit ejus desperatio, II.48. b.
units.tr: Christ's desertion on the cross was not his despair, II.48. b.

units.la: Desiderium Christi & justitiæ ejus salutare est, I.252. a.
units.tr: The desire of Christ and of his righteousness is wholesome, I.252. a.

units.la: Desperatio quid? I.519. b.
units.tr: What is desperation? I.519. b.

units.la: Determinatio Dei non obest voluntatis libertati, I.254. b.
units.tr: The determination of God does not hinder the freedom of the will, I.254. b.

units.la: Deus Θεὸς quale sit nomen infiniti entis, I.70. a. nulla imagine effingi potest, 553. a. 536. b. vid. Brev. diligendus est propter se, non propter aliud, I.503. a. quomodo Rex & Pater hominum.301. 302. eum accipere sibi visibile corpus magnum miraculum est, II.18. b. Dei cognitio occupat omnes hominis facultates, I.518. b.
units.tr: God [Θεὸς]: what kind of name is it for an infinite being? I.70. a. He cannot be represented by any image, 553. a, 536. b. See Summary. He is to be loved for his own sake, not for anything else, I.503. a. How he is King and Father of men, 301, 302. That he took a visible great body is a great miracle, II.18. b. The knowledge of God occupies all the faculties of man, I.518. b.

units.la: Dextra an sinistra dignior habenda? II.67. b. Dei symbolum potentiæ & honoris est, 67. b. 70. b. Nihil ubiquitati corporis chiliti patrocinatur, 67, b, 70. a.
units.tr: Is the right hand or the left to be regarded as more worthy? II.67. b. The right hand of God is a symbol of power and honour, 67. b, 70. b. Nothing in it supports the ubiquity of Christ's circumscribed body, 67. b, 70. a.

units.la: Diabolus. Ejus μεταβολή, I.289. b. potentia, ibid. Regnum variè circumscriptum, 390. a. in aëra magna pollet potestate, ibid. b. animalia vera generare non potest, ibid. potestas ejus in exteriorem hominem explicatur, 291. a. æmulum se operum Dei in magia præbet, 293. a. ejus apparitiones per spectra, 297 Hominum cœtibus etiam interest, 298. a. ejus regnum describitur, 299. ligatio ejusdem, ibid. Divinum cultum affectat, 537. b. veri nominis mi acula patrare non potest, II.98. a. 99. a. Ejus in Baptismo exorcismo ridicula est, 460. b.
units.tr: The devil. His change [μεταβολή], I.289. b. His power, ibid. His kingdom variously described, 290. a. In the air he has great power, ibid. b. He cannot beget true animals, ibid. His power over the outward man is explained, 291. a. In magic he sets himself up as a rival to the works of God, 293. a. His appearances through apparitions, 297. He also takes part in gatherings of men, 298. a. His kingdom is described, 299. His binding, ibid. He aims at divine worship, 537. b. He cannot work true miracles, II.98. a, 99. a. His exorcism in baptism is ridiculous, 460. b.

units.tr: Deacons of the Church: who they were and what sort of men they were at first, II.586. a. Their duty, ibid. Calling to the office, 587. a.

units.la: Diaconissæ, quales olim fuerint, II. 586. b.
units.tr: Deaconesses: what they were like in former times, II.586. b.

units.la: Dies. Dierum observantia ad cultum Divinum in N.T. nulla est, I.364. a. 366. b. Dominica à Christo resurrectione cœpit, II.57. b. ejus institutio nihil favet festis Papalibus, I.367. Natalis Christi certò definiri nequit, II 25. a.
units.tr: Days. The observance of days is no part of divine worship in the New Testament, I.364. a, 366. b. The Lord's Day began with Christ's resurrection, II.57. b. Its institution gives no support to the papal feasts, I.367. The birthday of Christ cannot be fixed with certainty, II.25. a.

units.la: Διδραχμον didrachmum quid fuerit? I.663. b.
units.tr: What was the didrachm [Διδραχμον]? I.663. b.

units.tr: Who are the strange gods? I.57. a. Who are the good or merely named gods [ἀγαθοί]? I.113. Of the greater and lesser pagan nations, I.537. a.

units.tr: The perfect love of God commanded in the law: what must it be like? I.317. a. That most highly appreciative love of God of the Schoolmen: what is it? ibid. b. It is the sum of the Decalogue, I.502. a, to which love of neighbour is most closely joined, ibid. b. What it must be like, I.503. a, 508. b. VI.

units.la: b. vide Proximus. item Amor.

units.la: Diluvium Noachicum etiam Gentilibus innotuit, II. 717. b. Ejus aquæ typus fuerunt Baptismi per aquam, 444. b.
units.tr: The Noachic flood was known also to the Gentiles, II.717. b. Its water was a type of baptism by water, 444. b.

units.la: Dionysius Areopagita Theologiæ mysticæ primus author, I.19. b. Angelorum hierarchiam fingens confutatur, 280. b.
units.tr: Dionysius the Areopagite, the first author of mystical theology: I.19. b. Refuted for inventing the hierarchy of angels: 280. b.

units.la: Disciplina Ecclesiastica quid? II.600. b. ejus necessitas, ibid. b. Divina institutio, 601. a. Rationes eam confirmantes, ibid. b. peccata, quæ ei subsunt, definiuntur, 602. a. units.tr: What is ecclesiastical discipline? II.600. b. Its necessity: ibid. b. Its divine institution: 601. a. Reasons confirming it: ibid. b. The sins that fall under it are defined: 602. a. Its manner of exercise is spiritual, not corporal: ib. b. Its opponents are refuted: 606. a. The practice in the Church of the fatherland is defended: 609. a. See Brev.

units.la: Discipulus Christi quomodo quis fiat? 451. b.
units.tr: How does one become a disciple of Christ? 451. b.

units.la: Dispositio prævia ad regenerationem in homine nulla est, I.233. b. 234. a.
units.tr: There is no preparatory disposition in man for regeneration: I.233. b. 234. a.

units.la: Disputationum utilitas monstratur, II,583. b.
units.tr: The usefulness of disputations is shown: II.583. b.

units.tr: The disagreement of the Protestants concerning the communication of idioms is weighed: II.33. b.

units.la: Distantia inter ens & nihil infinita est, I.189. b.
units.tr: The distance between being and nothing is infinite: I.189. b.

units.tr: The chimerical gods of the Papists: I.539. a. Their worship is enjoined by the Pope, even by oath: 711. b.

units.la: Divinationes Diaboli vanæ sunt, I.188. b. contrà Divinæ Prophetarum infallibiles, 289. a. vide Prophetia.
units.tr: The divinations of the Devil are vain: I.188. b. In contrast, the divine prophecies of the prophets are infallible: 289. a. See Prophecy.

units.tr: Divinatory lots are unlawful: I.548. b. Their various kinds: ibid.

units.tr: The divinity of God cannot be defined: I.66. b. Yet it can be described in some way: ibid. 67. a. The ψυχή of Christ does not denote his divinity: II.8. b. See CHRIST. Scripture's assertion of it: I.25. a. See Scripture.

units.la: Divitiarum amor noxius, I. 604. a. moderatum earum studium laudabile, 605. contemptus vitiosus, ib.
units.tr: The love of riches is harmful: I.604. a. A moderate pursuit of them is commendable: 605. Contempt for them is sinful: ib.

units.la: Divortia Hebræorum, I. 714. a. eorum causæ & formulæ, ibid. b. injustæ causæ refelluntur, 593. b. justæ causæ quænam? 592. b. Pontificiorum, 594. a.
units.tr: Divorces among the Hebrews: I.714. a. Their causes and formulas: ibid. b. Unjust causes are refuted: 593. b. What are the just causes? 592. b. Of the Papists: 594. a.

units.tr: What kind of power of teaching did Christ have? II.95. a. How the office of teaching is to be carried out in the Church: 593. b.

units.tr: What kinds of offerings or gifts were the sacrifices of the Old Testament: I.674. a. How they were a type and shadow of Christ: ibid. b.

units.la: Dormire in sacris pro statu mortuorum sumitur, I I.708. b. animas defunctorum post mortem dormire usque ad resurrectionem, Anabaptistæ cum Socin. docent. 708. b.
units.tr: To sleep in the sacred writings is taken to mean the state of the dead: II.708. b. That the souls of the departed sleep after death until the resurrection: the Anabaptists, with the Socinians, teach this: 708. b.

units.la: Doxologia Orationis Domin. explicatur, I.359. b.
units.tr: The doxology of the Lord's Prayer is explained: I.359. b.

units.la: Dubitandi formulæ in Scripturis sacris quid notent? II. 422.423. a.
units.tr: What do the forms of doubting in Holy Scripture signify? II.422, 423. a.

units.la: Duella improbantur, I.581. b.
units.tr: Duels are disapproved: I.581. b.

units.la: Dulia cultus sanctis nullus debetur, I.526. a.
units.tr: Dulia: no such worship is owed to the saints: I.526. a.

units.la: Αυλέα & Αυτζέα an differant, I. 283. b.
units.tr: Whether Aulea [Αὐλέα] and Autzea [Αὐτζέα] differ: I.283. b.

units.la: Duratio Angelorum aliquando ævi nomine venit, I. 278. a. perpetua an veræ Ecclesiæ nota sit, 546. a.
units.tr: The duration of angels is sometimes called by the name of aeon: I.278. a. Whether perpetuity is a mark of the true Church: 546. a. ## E.

units.la: E.
Ebionitæ Dicei Dominico etiam Sabbathum Judaicum junxerunt, I.552. b.
units.tr: The Ebionites joined the Jewish Sabbath to the Lord's Day as well: I.552. b.

units.la: Ecclesia. Ejus nomina, II.505. proprie dicta definitur, II.507. a. ejus elogia in Scriptuis, 508. a. est ipsa communio sanctorum, 510. invisibilis, 510. b. vide Brev. Una, sancta, Catholica, 511. a. errare & pror-sus deficere non potest, 512. b. seqq. Catholica, 513. b. perpetuò exstitit, 514. b. Latius dicta definitur, 517 a. Externæ notæ, 518. genuinæ a notis quomodo dignoscendæ, 519 a. veræ & genuinæ notæ criteria, ibid. b. Visibilis est, 522, b. non est erroris & vitii expers. 523. b. & particularis quævis deficere potest, 529. a. reformari aliquando debet. 530. b. Sancta quomodo sit, 511. b. seqq. 544. b. In externa cur sint hypocritæ, 517. a. 523. b. mixtura zizaniorum cum tritico in ei semper est & erit, 524. b. Ecclesiæ falsæ idea, 532. b. Pontificii ex visibili Monarchiam Papalem faciunt, 534. a. Ecclesiæ definitio ex mente Bellarmini, 534. a. illa definitio ideam Ecclesiæ falsæ exhibet, 534. b. est Babylon illa magna, ib.d. refutatur Bellarm. 536. a. Ecclesia visibilis non splendida, nec unicum Cathedræ affixa est, 537. a. vicissitudines lucis & umbræ habet, 539. a. premitur, sed non opprimitur, ibid. b. ejus rei historia, 540. b. media, quibus sub Antichristo conservata est, 541. a. ante Reformationem extitit, 542. b. per Reformationem à vera non recessit, 543.a.b. Quod una, Sancta, Catholica dicitur, non sunt bonæ notæ, 544. b. Catholica cur & quomodo dicatur. 544. seq. etiam quævis particularis suo sensu Catholica est, 546.a. Una quomodo sit & dicatur, 544. a. Apostolica cur dicatur, 544. b. Ejus notæ Bellarminianæ ad incudem revocantur, 545. a. seqq. Lumen propheticum an vera nota? 551. a. an multitudo credentium? 546. an miraculorum gloria? 550. an confessio adversariorum? 551. b. an consensus in doctrina cum Ecclesia antiqua & Patribus? 548. a. an antiquitas? 545 b. Ecclesia à solo Christo capite ejus dependet, 507. b. 556. b. ejus regimen Christianum quale esse debeat 597.b. vide Gubernatio. Item Breviar. Ecclesia Papalis Antichristiana, 507. ejus regimen, 601. vide Brev.
units.tr: Church. Its names, II.505. Its proper definition, II.507. a. Its praises in Scripture, 508. a. It is the communion of the saints itself, 510. Invisible, 510. b. See Brev. One, holy, Catholic, 511. a. It cannot err or wholly fail, 512. b. seqq. Catholic, 513. b. It has existed perpetually, 514. b. Its broader definition, 517. a. External marks, 518. How the genuine are to be distinguished from the marks, 519. a. Criteria of the true and genuine marks, ibid. b. It is visible, 522. b. It is not free of error and vice, 523. b. Any particular church can fail, 529. a. It must sometimes be reformed, 530. b. How it is holy, 511. b. seqq. 544. b. Why there are hypocrites in the external church, 517. a. 523. b. The mixture of tares with the wheat is and always will be in it, 524. b. The idea of a false church, 532. b. The Papists make the Papal monarchy out of the visible church, 534. a. The definition of the Church according to Bellarmine's mind, 534. a. That definition presents the idea of a false church, 534. b. It is that great Babylon, ib. d. Refuted, Bellarm. 536. a. The visible church is neither splendid nor attached to a single chair, 537. a. It has the vicissitudes of light and shadow, 539. a. It is pressed but not crushed, ibid. b. History of this matter, 540. b. The means by which it was preserved under Antichrist, 541. a. It existed before the Reformation, 542. b. Through the Reformation it did not depart from the true faith, 543. a. b. That it is called one, holy, Catholic, are not good marks, 544. b. Why and how it is called Catholic, 544. seq. Even any particular church is Catholic in its own sense, 546. a. How it is one and is called one, 544. a. Why it is called apostolic, 544. b. Its Bellarminian marks are brought back to the anvil, 545. a. seqq. Is the prophetic light a true mark? 551. a. Is it the multitude of believers? 546. Is it the glory of miracles? 550. Is it the confession of adversaries? 551. b. Is it agreement in doctrine with the ancient Church and the Fathers? 548. a. Is it antiquity? 545. b. The Church depends on Christ alone as its head, 507. b. 556. b. What its Christian government ought to be, 597. b. See Government. Also Brev. The Papal, Antichristian Church, 507; its government, 601. See Brev.

units.la: Ecclesia V.T. varias temporum periodos continet, I. 419.b.quibus in rebus ab Ecclesia N.T discrepet, aut cum ea conveniat, 420. a. utriusque typus sub Hagaris & Saræ ac genitorum ex iis allegoria explicatur, 420. b. Ejus regimen spirituale quale fuerit, II.136. a. ejus œconomia diversa pro ejus diversa ætate fuit, I. 7. a. Testimonium Ecclesiæ ad probandam S. Scripturæ divinitatem quid conferat, I. 28.29.non principale & authenticum, sed fallibile, errori obnoxium est, 30. a. quomodo columna & fundamentum veritatis sit, 30. b. sua authoritate Canonem Scripturæ non fixit,31. b. Ecclesiæ dicere quid sit? II.604. a. Quot modis id fiat, ibid. b. Ejus judicium adversus refractarios, 605. b. an ab ea ad Magistratum provocare liceat? 606. b. Status ejus novissimus ante Christi adventum qualis sit futurus, doctorum sententiæ discordant, 721. est resurrectio & vivificatio quædam, 723. a. Ejus authoritas & potestas in dandis præceptis & legibus, 644. b. 645. b. quatenus obligent ejus mandata? 599. b.
units.tr: The Church of the Old Testament contains various periods of time. In what respects it differs from the Church of the New Testament, or agrees with it, I.419. b. Its type under Hagar and Sarah, and the allegory of their offspring, is explained, I.420. a. b. What its spiritual government was like, II.136. a. Its economy was different according to the different ages of it, I.7. a. What the testimony of the Church contributes to proving the divinity of Holy Scripture, I.28, 29; it is not the principal and authentic witness but a fallible one, open to error, I.30. a. How it is the pillar and foundation of the truth, I.30. b. By its own authority it did not fix the canon of Scripture, I.31. b. What it is for the Church to pronounce, II.604. a. In how many ways this is done, ibid. b. Its judgment against the refractory, II.605. b. Whether it is lawful to appeal from it to the magistrate, II.606. b. What its final state before Christ's coming will be is disputed among the teachers, I.721. It is a certain resurrection and quickening, I.723. a. Its authority and power in giving precepts and laws, I.644. b. 645. b. Insofar as its commands bind, I.599. b.

units.la: Ecclesiæ Reform. apologia adversus improperium gentii dominantibus intensi, I 1.622. a.
units.tr: The Reformed Church's apology against the taunts of the Gentiles, directed at those in power, I 1.622. a.

units.la: Ecclesiastici à jure jurando immunes non sunt, II.545.a. etiam magistratui subsunt, 592. b.
units.tr: Ecclesiastics are not exempt from the oath, II.545.a.; they are also subject to the magistrate, 592. b.

units.la: Eclipsis solis in Christi crucifixione plane miraculosa fuit, I I.49. a.
units.tr: The eclipse of the sun at Christ's crucifixion was plainly miraculous, I I.49. a.

units.la: Εἴδωλον, idolum quid, I.530. b. 532. a.
units.tr: Εἴδωλον [eidōlon]: what an idol is, I.530. b. 532. a.

units.la: Ex, ex vocula non semper causam materialem notat, II. 14. a.
units.tr: The preposition "ex" does not always denote the material cause, II. 14. a.

units.la: Electio quid? I.156. b. definitur, 157. a. vide Breviar. Ejus causa & simul medium est Christus diverso respectu, 159. a. ejus objectum sunt homines miseri à Christo salvandi, ibid. b. 167. b. facta est non solum ad salutem, sed etiam ad media, 169. b. Non est universalis, ibid. 168. a. Electio temporalis est vocatio interna per Spiritum S, I.211. b.
units.tr: Election: what is it? I.156. b.; it is defined at 157. a.; see Breviarium. Its cause and at the same time its means is Christ, viewed in different respects, 159. a. Its object is miserable men to be saved by Christ, ibid. b.; 167. b. It was made not only for salvation but also for the means, 169. b. It is not universal, ibid. 168. a. Temporal election is the internal calling by the Holy Spirit, I.211. b.

units.la: est fundamentum perseverantiæ Sanctorum, 379. ejusdem efficacia & cum cæteris gratiæ beneficiis nexus, ibid. ejus firmandæ studium certitudinem salutis ostendit, II.416. b.
units.tr: Election is the foundation of the perseverance of the saints, 379.; its efficacy and its connection with the other benefits of grace, ibid.; the zeal to confirm it shows the certainty of salvation, II.416. b.

units.la: Electi, eorum est certus & definitus numerus, I. 167. b. 170. a. ergo electio non est universalis, 168. a. contraria argumenta diluuntur, ibid. & 169. a. soli participes fiunt fœderis gratiæ & bonorum promissorum, 389. b. 390. a. certò perseverant. 380. II. 400. b. seduci non possunt, ibid. ante conversionem à non conversis reliquis nihil differunt, 212. b.
units.tr: The elect: their number is certain and fixed, I.167. b. 170. a. Therefore election is not universal, 168. a.; the contrary arguments are answered, ibid. and 169. a. They alone become partakers of the covenant of grace and of the promised goods, 389. b. 390. a. They persevere with certainty, 380.; II.400. b. They cannot be seduced, ibid. Before conversion they do not differ from the other unconverted, 212. b.

units.la: Eleemosyna quid? I.617. b. cur Hebræis צדקה justitia dicatur, ibid. ejus officium, 618. a. eam erogandi regulæ, 618. b. ejus curatores primitus Diaconi fuerunt, II.586. a.
units.tr: Alms: what are they? I.617. b. Why is צדקה [tsedaqah] called righteousness by the Hebrews? ibid. Their office, 618. a. Rules for distributing them, 618. b. Its stewards were originally the deacons, II.586. a.

units.la: Elias & Elisæus cum Filiis Prophetarum non monachi, fuerunt, II.674. b.
units.tr: Elijah and Elisha with the sons of the prophets were not monks, II.674. b.

units.la: Emendandæ vitæ studium resipiscentiam absolvit, I. 324. a.
units.tr: The eagerness to amend one's life completes repentance, I.324. a.

units.la: Emissariorum Pontificiorum impietas separationem quamvis ab Ecclesia Romana damnantium, II. 527. b. Reformationem Ecclesiæ impossibilem clamantium, II. 531. b.
units.tr: The impiety of the Papist emissaries who condemn separation from the Church of Rome, II.527. b.; who cry out that reformation of the Church is impossible, II.531. b.

units.la: Εμπικὸς ultimorum tempor um athei sunt, I I.717. b. 751. b.
units.tr: Ἔμπικος [empikos]: the atheists of the last times, II.717. b. 751. b.

units.la: Εμπιεχώμενος in Divinis quid sit? I.111. b.
units.tr: Ἐμπεχώμενος [empechomenos] in divine matters: what does it mean? I.111. b.

units.la: Ενεργεια, ενεργητικὸν & ενεργημα quomodo differant, ex Damasceno docetur I I.23. b.
units.tr: How ἐνέργεια [energeia], ἐνεργητικόν [energētikon] and ἐνέργημα [energēma] differ, is taught from Damascene, II.23. b.

units.la: Energumenorum operationes diabolicæ, I.291. b.
units.tr: The diabolical operations of the demon-possessed, I.291. b.

units.la: Enjedinus notatur, I I.5.6. b. ad locum Rom.I.3. Christi Deitatem vellicans, ibid.
units.tr: Enjedinus is noted, II.5.6. b., on the passage Rom. 1.3., where he undermines the deity of Christ, ibid.

units.la: Εγκρατης, continens quis sit? I I.667. a.
units.tr: Ἐγκρατής [enkratēs]: who is the continent man? II.667. a.

units.la: Enochus non fuit Monachus,I I.674.a. ejus pietas laudatur, I. 425. a. Ejus μετάθεσις typus fuit Christi in Cœlum ascendentis,452. a. Prophetia qualis, 482. a. non est εγγραφος, II.716. b.
units.tr: Enoch was not a monk, II.674. a. His piety is praised, I.425. a. His translation (μετάθεσις [metathesis]) was a type of Christ ascending into heaven, 452. a. What kind of prophecy, 482. a. He is not ἔγγραφος [engraphos], II.716. b.

units.la: Ἐντευξις seu Intercessio qualis precum species? I. 347. b.
units.tr: Ἔντευξις [enteuxis], or intercession: what kind of prayer? I.347. b.

units.la: Enthusiastarum verbum internum & spiritus privatus rejicitur, I. 44. a. vide Fanatici, eorum dogma falsum, insulsum & impium est, ibid. b.
units.tr: The internal word and private spirit of the Enthusiasts are rejected, I.44. a.; see Fanatics; their doctrine is false, insipid and impious, ibid. b.

units.la: Ἐντυγχανειν κατα τὸν θεὸν accusare aliquem, contrà ὑπὲρ τὸν θεὸν pro aliquo interpellare significat, I I.129. a.
units.tr: Ἐντυγχάνειν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ [entygchanein kata tou theou] means to accuse someone; ὑπὲρ τοῦ θεοῦ [hyper tou theou] means to intercede on someone's behalf, II.129. a.

units.la: Ἐπικλησις Spiritus S. super B. Virginem explicatur, II. 12. b.
units.tr: The epiclesis of the Holy Spirit upon the Blessed Virgin is explained, II.12. b.

units.la: Epicuri & sequacium de Providentia Dei error, I. 244. a.
units.tr: The error of Epicurus and his followers concerning God's providence, I.244. a.

units.la: Ἐπιείκεια Dei & gratia justificans non idem sunt, I. 182. a. Legis ceremonialis, rituum, judicialis, I. 676. a. seq.
units.tr: God's ἐπιείκεια [epieikeia] and justifying grace are not the same, I.182. a. Of the ceremonial, ritual and judicial law, I.676. a. and following.

units.la: Ἐπιλυσις ἰδία S.Scripturæ quid? I. 59. a.
units.tr: What is a private interpretation (ἐπίλυσις ἰδία [epilysis idia]) of Holy Scripture? I.59. a.

units.la: Ἐπιφάνεια Christi, II.4. a. τ' πυρσοῦ, affulgentia adventus Christi qualis sit, 722. a.
units.tr: The epiphany of Christ, II.4. a.; τὸ πυρσοῦ [to pyrsou], the brightness of Christ's coming: what is it? 722. a.

units.la: Ἐπομιάζειν quid proprie significet? II. 13. a.
units.tr: What does ἐπομνιάζειν [epomniazein] properly signify? II.13. a.

units.la: Episcopatus. In eo tria probe discernenda sunt.I I. 592. b. an, & qua lege appetendus sit? 566. a.
units.tr: Episcopacy: three things in it must be carefully distinguished, II.592. b.; whether it is to be sought, and by what law? 566. a.

units.la: Episcopi. Titulares unde orti, I I.571. a. quando Ecclesiæ ministros ordinare coeperint, 572. a. Apostolorum ævo à Presbyteris non differebant, 590. b. 592. b. hodierni Pontificii à primis plurimum differunt, 593. a. inter Clericos gubernantes primi sunt,668. b. eorum prærogativæ,669. a. supra Presbyteros jure Divino nullam habent eminentiam, 670. a. hodierni cum veteribus nihil commune habent,671. a. non prædicant Evangelium,671. b.
units.tr: Bishops, titular: whence they arose, II.571. a.; when they began to ordain ministers of the Church, 572. a.; in the age of the apostles they did not differ from the elders, 590. b. 592. b.; today's Papist bishops differ greatly from the first ones, 593. a.; they were the first among the clergy who governed, 668. b.; their prerogatives, 669. a.; they have no eminence over the elders by divine right, 670. a.; the modern bishops have nothing in common with the ancient ones, 671. a.; they do not preach the Gospel, 671. b.

units.la: Episcopius subordinationem Personarum Trinitatis statuens perstringitur, I.112. b. de imputatione justitiæ notatur, 280. b. 281. a. infantes & usu rationis carentes à peccato originali eximit,353. b. peccandi non unum aut alterum actum, sed habitum pœnam mortis mereri docet,363. a. ejus error circa vocationis gratiam, II. 205. b. de vocatione ad crucem,124. b. redarguitur, ibid. ejus impia de S. Cœna sententia,461. b. de sacrificiorum origine, I.444. b. Socinianizat,423. promissionem primam de semine mulieris pervertit, 424. a.
units.tr: Episcopius, who posits a subordination among the Persons of the Trinity, is censured, I.112. b.; he is noted on the imputation of righteousness, 280. b. 281. a.; he exempts infants and those lacking the use of reason from original sin, 353. b.; he teaches that not one or another act of sin but the habit deserves the penalty of death, 363. a.; his error concerning the grace of calling, II.205. b.; on the vocation to the cross, 124. b., refuted, ibid.; his impious opinion on the Lord's Supper, 461. b.; on the origin of sacrifices, I.444. b.; he Socinianizes, 423.; he perverts the first promise concerning the seed of the woman, 424. a.

units.la: Erasmus pelagianizans notatur,I.366. a. de S. Scripturæ lectione in lingua vernacula laudatur, II. 434. a.
units.tr: Erasmus is noted as Pelagianizing, I.366. a.; he is praised for reading Holy Scripture in the vernacular, II.434. a.

units.la: Erastus disciplinam ecclesiasticam impugnans arguitur, I I.606. a. Ecclesiæ potestatem in Magistratus transfert,626. a.
units.tr: Erastus, who attacks church discipline, is charged, II.606. a.; he transfers the power of the Church to the magistrates, 626. a.

units.la: Eremitæ aliorum Christianorum membra esse non possunt, II. 673. a. primus Paulus Thebæus fuit, 675. a.
units.tr: Hermits cannot be members of other Christians, II.673. a.; the first was Paul the Theban, 675. a.

units.la: Erigena Scotus primus Theologiam mysticam in Ecclesiam Latinam invexit,I.19. b.
units.tr: Erigena the Scot first introduced mystical theology into the Latin Church, I.19. b.

units.la: Errantes in Religione quomodo distinguendi & curandi sint,II.634. b. 635. a.
units.tr: How erring persons in religion are to be distinguished and cared for, II.634. b. 635. a.

units.la: Errare Ecclesia visibilis & particularis quævis potest,II.511. b. 512.a, 513. b. 523. b. vid.Ecclesia.
units.tr: The visible and particular Church may err in any way, II.511. b. 512. a., 513. b., 523. b.; see Church.

units.la: Errores vel in fundamento, vel circa fundamentum, vel præter fundamentum fidei explicantur,I I.525.526. a. fundamentales quinam sint, I.16. b. II. 526. a. circa cultum Dei quomodo oriantur,II.521. a.
units.tr: Errors are explained as either in the foundation, or concerning the foundation, or beyond the foundation of faith, II.525. 526. a. Which are the fundamental errors? I.16. b.; II.526. a. How they arise concerning the worship of God, II.521. a.

units.la: Esdras Canonem librorum V.T. nec constituit, nec restituit, I.35. a.
units.tr: Ezra neither established nor restored the canon of the books of the Old Testament, I.35. a.

units.la: Esseni quinam fuerint,II.674. b. jurandum esse negarunt,I.544. a.
units.tr: Who the Essenes were, II.674. b.; they denied that one should swear, I.544. a.

units.la: Ἐξηλοτυπικα quid? I.529.b.
units.tr: Ἐξηλοτυπικά [exēlotypika]: what are they? I.529. b.

units.la: Ethica Aristotelis aliquando publicè populo, loco S. Scripturæ prælegebatur,I I. 595. a.
units.tr: Aristotle's Ethics was sometimes publicly read to the people in place of Holy Scripture, II.595. a.

units.la: Eva prior peccavit, I.332. b. cur illam potius quàm Adamum Sathanas aggressus sit, 333. a. ejus peccatum explicatur,334. a. ejus, ap mariti peccatum graviusfuerit,335. b. ratio ὀνομασίας ejus, 339. b. ejus fides in Messiam,424.b.
units.tr: Eve sinned first, I.332. b.; why Satan attacked her rather than Adam, 333. a.; her sin is explained, 334. a.; whether her husband's sin was graver than hers, 335. b.; the reason for her name, 339. b.; her faith in the Messiah, 424. b.

units.la: Evangelium. Ejus origo & homonymia, II.154. vide Breviar. Convenientia cum Scripturis prophetiis, 162. a. non est doctrina operum,163. b. Qualis Lex sit, ibid. Lux est,185.a. spiritus justitiæ, ibid. vid. Breviar. quomodo Lex Christi vocetur, 402. Præcipua Christi doctrina fuit,II.93.a. ejus summa,94. a. prædicationis ejus modus & efficacia,94.b. 95. a. miraculis firmara,96. a.
units.tr: The Gospel: its origin and its ambiguity, II.154.; see Breviarium. Its agreement with the Scriptures and the prophecies, 162. a.; it is not a doctrine of works, 163. b.; what kind of law it is, ibid.; it is light, 185. a.; it is the spirit of righteousness, ibid.; see Breviarium; how the law of Christ is so called, 402. The chief doctrine of Christ was, II.93. a.; its summary, 94. a.; the manner and efficacy of its preaching, 94. b. 95. a.; confirmed by miracles, 96. a.

units.la: Evangelistæ quinam sint,I I.100. b. quales ministri Ecclesiæ fuerint,559. a.
units.tr: Who the evangelists were, II.100. b.; what kind of ministers of the Church they were, II.559. a.

units.la: Ἐυδοξια Dei quid? I.89.b. est causa prædestinationis, 175. a.
units.tr: The good pleasure (εὐδοκία [eudokia]) of God: what is it? I.89. b.; it is the cause of predestination, 175. a.

units.la: Eucharistica sacrificia qualia & quando offerri debuerint,I.655. b, 676. a.
units.tr: What kinds of eucharistic sacrifices should be offered, and when, I.655. b., 676. a.

units.la: Eugenius Papa suam ipsius,ceu Papæ, potestatem mirificè depræ(dicat,II. 639. a. idem amplius in Concilio Florentino,686. b.
units.tr: Pope Eugenius wonderfully exalts his own power as Pope, II.639. a.; the same further at the Council of Florence, II.686. b.

units.la: Εὐαγγελιζομένα Christi. I. 631. a.
units.tr: The Gospel-preachings (εὐαγγελιζόμενα [euangelizomena]) of Christ, I.631. a.

units.la: Εὐτραπελία an virtus sit? I.632. a. à S. Paulo damnatur, 633. a.
units.tr: Is εὐτραπελία [eutrapelia] a virtue? I.632. a.; it is condemned by St. Paul, 633. a.

units.la: Eutychii error de resurrectione,I I.738. b.
units.tr: The error of Eutyches concerning the resurrection, II.738. b.

units.la: Exaltationis Christi status explicatur, II. 54. b. 55. a. tres ejus gradus, ib, 57. a.
units.tr: The state of the exaltation of Christ is explained, II.54. b. 55. a.; its three degrees, ibid., 57. a.

units.la: Excæcatio & induratio reproborum in quo consistat,I. 179. a. quomodo Deo tribuatur,272. b.
units.tr: In what the blinding and hardening of the reprobate consists, I.179. a.; how it is attributed to God, 272. b.

units.la: Excidii pœna apud Hebræos qualis pœna fuerit, I. 713. b.

units.tr: Faith. Its general definition, II.240. a. It does not destroy reason, ibid. b. It is directed toward God alone, ibid. See Breviary. Its proper definition, 242. a. The difference between common and proper faith, ibid. b. Its object, 245. a. What is believed is prescribed in the Word of God; that by which it is believed exists in the heart of believers, 246. a. Carbonarian faith, the implicit faith of the Papists, 249. b. Its formal act, 252. Its consequent acts, 254. It occupies the whole soul, 257. a. The excellence and usefulness of saving faith, 254. b. It is an infused habit, not an acquired one, 244. a. Its great necessity is explained, 384. a. Its nature confirms the certainty of salvation, 297. a, 413. b. How one can know whether he is in faith, 414. a. It includes trust in itself, ibid. Its cause, object and fruit, ibid. Faith justifies, 296. b, but not as a work, 282. b, 283. a, 297. a, 301. b. It alone justifies, 297. b. How it is opposed to works, 298. a, 300. a. It justifies as an instrument, 299. b. It alone justifies, 300. a, but it is not solitary, 301, which is explained more fully from James, II.12, 305. b. Justifying faith and obedience to the Law are set against each other, 258. b. Faith in Christ is the form of the Church, 509. a. Through it the Church is united to Christ, ibid. b. It is a mark of the visible Church, 510. a. Its earnest [ἀρραβών] is shown, 399. b. It is not part of repentance strictly taken, I.323. a. Although it rests on revelation, it does not abolish sobriety of mind or the truths known by nature, I.10. b, which is explained from Hebrews XI.1, 14. a. How temporary faith differs from justifying faith, II.404. a. How many kinds there are, 409. Implicit faith is not faith, 431. b. Foreseen faith is refuted, I.163. b. What was the faith of the sacrificers in the Old Testament, 446. a. The faith of Abraham, 432. a.

units.tr: Filius. The person of the Son of God and his eternal generation are explained, I.124. a. See Breviary. He is called Only-begotten, Firstborn, Proper Son, etc., 125. a. His deity is proved by a general argument, ibid. b, 126. a, and by a special one, ibid. See Breviary. His divine attributes, simplicity, eternity, immensity, omniscience, veracity, holiness, omnipotence and omnipresence, are demonstrated, 130, 131. His divine works, 131, 132. Creation, 132. b. Redemption, 133. a. Miracles, 133. b. Divine worship, 134. The history of the enemies of the deity of Christ, 135, 136. See CHRIST.

units.tr: The covenant of God with men is the centre and marrow of all Scripture, I. 302. a. See Brev. Defined, 305. b. Whether it is a covenant of works or of grace, 305. b. Its definition, 306. a. Grace is defined, I. 374. a. Its names are set out, ibid. b. It is proved from Scripture, ibid. See Breviar. With respect to God it is πρωτοῦ ἔχον, 375. The covenant of God the Father with the Son, 376. a. See Brev. The difference between the covenant of works and the covenant of grace, 377. a. Its cause is the goodness of God, 383. b. Its threefold sanction, 39. b. The constancy of the covenant of grace, II. 377. a. See Breviar. Its economy under the New Testament had distinct periods, 188. a. Its sealing was the same in the Old and New Testaments, I. 415. a. Its promulgation through the word, both of command, 401, and of promise, 402. b. It is one and the same in the Old and New Testaments, 403. b. See Breviar. Its agreement under the Law of Moses and under the Gospel, 495, 496, notwithstanding the severity of the Mosaic legislation, 496. a. What was the state of those in covenant under the Law? 498. a. The arguments of those who deny the unity of the covenant of grace under the Old and New Testaments are answered, 410, 411. Of works, 305. b. Its promise was emptied by sin, I. 372. b. The covenant is not an eternal and unchangeable covenant of nature, 373. a. Its abolition proceeded by degrees, 422. b. The history of the Noachic covenant, 426. a. Of the Abrahamic, 428. a. The twofold stipulation of the Sinaitic covenant is explained, 470. The promise of righteousness and life in Christ, ibid. b. The possession of the land of Canaan, which was a type of heaven, 471. The stipulation of the people, 474. b. The restipulation, 477. a. Sanction through the blood of the testament, 480. a. Promulgation, ibid. Its contents, parts, 456. b. History, 461. a. Stipulation, ibid. b. The preamble of the legal covenant was promised and given to believers not by any merit of obedience but from grace alone, 477. b. That which God made with Abraham is the same as the covenant of grace, I. 409. a. What is the relation and agreement of the covenant of works to the covenant of grace? I. 416. b.

units.tr: Frugality: what kind of virtue is it? I. 620. b.

units.la: Fructus terrae Providentiae Dei subsunt,260.a.
units.tr: The fruits of the earth are subject to the providence of God, 260. a.

units.la: Fundamentum Ecclesiae non Petrus aut Papa, sed Petra Christus soluseft, II.651.b.
units.tr: The foundation of the Church is not Peter or the Pope, but Christ alone, the Rock, II. 651. b.

units.la: Fundamentum fidei definitur & distinguitur, I. 15.b. solus Christus est,16.a.
units.tr: The foundation of faith is defined and distinguished, I. 15. b. Christ alone is it, 16. a.

units.la: Fundamentalis veritas quid? I. 16.a. diversimode in Scripturis exprimitur,ibid. b. articuli quinam, ib. Errores fundamentales, ibid. II.526. circa eosdem triplex cautio,ibid.I.17.a.
units.tr: Fundamental truth: what is it? I. 16. a. It is expressed in various ways in the Scriptures, ibid. b. Which are the articles? ibid. Fundamental errors, ibid.; II. 526. A threefold caution concerning them, ibid.; I. 17. a.

units.la: Funebres ritus variarum Gentium,I I,699. b. sermones rectius intermittuntur,quam habentur,699.b.
units.tr: Funeral rites of various nations, II. 699. b. Funeral sermons are rightly omitted rather than delivered, 699. b.

units.la: Fungibilis res quaenam sit & dicatur,I,612. b.
units.tr: A fungible thing: what it is and how it is called, I. 612. b.

units.la: Fures effractores noctu occidere licet,I.584. b.
units.tr: Thieves breaking in at night may lawfully be killed, I. 584. b.

units.la: Furtum proprie dictum quid? I.607. b. ejus variae species recensentur,608. b. improprie dictum rapina est, ibid. b. naturali justitiae repugnat,610.a. ejus poena juxta Legem, 718. furtum proprie dictum an Israelitae ex Aegypto egressi commiserint? I. 610.a.
units.tr: Theft properly so called: what is it? I. 607. b. Its various species are listed, 608. b. What is improperly called theft is robbery, ibid. b. It is repugnant to natural justice, 610. a. Its punishment under the Law, 718. Did the Israelites who came out of Egypt commit theft properly so called? I. 610. a.

units.la: Futura contingentia praescire & praedicere Dei donum est, I.440.b. dogma hoc contra Socinum & Philosophos defenditur,I.87.b.
units.tr: To foreknow and foretell future contingent things is a gift of God, I. 440. b. This dogma is defended against Socinus and the philosophers, I. 87. b.

units.tr: G.

units.la: Galatinus de Tikkun Sopherim arguitur,I.36.b. item.I I. 27. a. 60. a.
units.tr: Galatinus is refuted on the Tikkun Sopherim, I. 36. b; likewise II. 27. a, 60. a.

units.la: Ganeo maximus Papa Rom. est, I. 598. a.
units.tr: Ganeo is the greatest Roman Pope, I. 598. a.

units.la: Garrulitas seu ἀδολεσχία quale vitium? I. 635. a.
units.tr: Garrulity, or idle talk [ἀδολεσχία]: what kind of vice is it? I. 635. a.

units.la: Gehenna, Teneri ad gehennam, Matth.5:22. quid sit, I.708. ejus metus per se non est respiscentiae pars, I.322.a.
units.tr: Gehenna; to be liable to hell, Matt. 5:22: what it is, I. 708. Its fear in itself is not a part of repentance, I. 322. a.

units.la: Genealogia Christi humana duplex panditur, II.15.a. vindicatur contra Fanaticos, 15.b.& conciliatur, ibid.
units.tr: The human genealogy of Christ is set out in two forms, II. 15. a; it is vindicated against the Fanatics, 15. b, and reconciled, ibid.

units.la: Genebrardus tres Hebraeorum Canones constituens, notatur,I.37.b.
units.tr: Genebrardus, in establishing three canons of the Hebrews, is censured, I. 37. b.

units.la: Generatio Filii Dei est aeterna,I.120.a. incomprehensibilis,124.b. 125.a. nihil habet cum naturali commune,121.b. a Processione Spiritus S. differt. ibid. Christi hominis a reliquorum hominum generatione multum differt,I I. 9. a.
units.tr: The generation of the Son of God is eternal, I. 120. a; incomprehensible, 124. b, 125. a; it has nothing in common with natural generation, 121. b; it differs from the procession of the Holy Spirit, ibid. The generation of Christ as man differs greatly from the generation of other men, II. 9. a.

units.la: Generationis naturalis & supernaturalis differentia,I I. 232.b. 233.b. Ejus impuritas quid notet, 690. a. Generatio rerum Dei cooperationem requirit, I. 65.a.
units.tr: Of generation, the difference between natural and supernatural, II. 232. b, 233. b. What its impurity signifies, 690. a. The generation of things requires the cooperation of God, I. 65. a.

units.la: Genesis. Prima Geneseos verba: In principio Deus creavit Coelum & terram, non sunt epitome totius Creationis,I. 198. b.
units.tr: Genesis. The first words of Genesis, In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, are not an epitome of the whole of creation, I. 198. b.

units.la: Genethliacorum vanitas ex stellis vaticinantium, I. 210.seq.
units.tr: The vanity of the genethliacs, who prophesy from the stars, I. 210 seq.

units.la: Gentiles creaturae praeter creatorem serviunt,I.105.a. Unum Principem Deorum agnoverunt, 105.b. eorum religio mera superstitio est, 6.b. a foedere Gratiae sub Lege exclusae fuerunt, I.457. a. quod pluribus asseritur,458.a. eorum bona opera peccaminosa fuerunt,330.a. peccatum originale quodammodo agnoverunt, 346.b. sua etiam Sabbatha habuerunt, 553.b. eorum in Coelum ascendentium exempla fabulosa sunt, I I.65. a. eorum nonnulli resurrectionem mortuorum crediderunt,732. b. item sensum aliquem futuri ultimi judicii habuerunt, 745.b.
units.tr: Gentiles serve creatures besides the Creator, I. 105. a. They acknowledged one Prince of the gods, 105. b. Their religion is mere superstition, 6. b. They were excluded from the covenant of grace under the Law, I. 457. a, which is asserted in many places, 458. a. Their good works were sinful, 330. a. They recognised original sin in some way, 346. b. They also had their own sabbaths, 553. b. Their fabulous examples of those ascending into heaven, II. 65. a. Some of them believed in the resurrection of the dead, 732. b; likewise they had some sense of a future last judgment, 745. b.

units.la: Gentium conversio varie praedicta est,II.722.b. earum plenitudo nondum intravit, ibid.
units.tr: The conversion of the Gentiles has been variously predicted, II. 722. b. Their fullness has not yet come in, ibid.

units.la: Gerhardus in dogmate de communicatione idiomatum notatur,I I. 27. b.
units.tr: Gerhard is censured on the doctrine of the communication of idioms, II. 27. b.

units.la: Gestatio Christi in utero B. Virginis novimestris adeoque ordinaria fuit, II. 16. a.
units.tr: Christ's gestation in the womb of the Blessed Virgin lasted nine months and was therefore ordinary, II. 16. a.

units.la: Gibeonitarum dolus an probandus ? I.735. b.
units.tr: The deceit of the Gibeonites: is it to be approved? I. 735. b.

units.la: Γινώσκειν quid notat ? I. 166. idem καταγνωσιν notat, ibid.
units.tr: Γινώσκειν [ginōskein]: what does it mean? I. 166. The same as καταγνῶσιν [katagnōsin] means, ibid.

units.la: Gladii poena apud Hebraeos gravissima habebatur, I. 711. b.
units.tr: The punishment of the sword was regarded among the Hebrews as the most severe, I. 711. b.

units.la: Gloria Dei ex ejus perfectionibus resultat, I. 103.b. eam quomodo Deus manifestare decreverit, 153. b. est omnium rerum creatarum finis, 191. a. ea, quam sibi Christus meruit, tum in ejus Deitate, tum in Humanitate relucet,383. b.
units.tr: The glory of God results from his perfections, I. 103. b. How God has decreed to manifest it, 153. b. It is the end of all created things, 191. a. That glory which Christ merited for himself shines forth both in his Deity and in his Humanity, 383. b.

units.la: Gloriae in vita aeterna an gradus sint futuri? I I.784. b. quod Scripturae testimoniis, parabolis, exemplis & rationibus probatur, 785.a. contraria argumenta examinantur,786. a. Augustini de gloria beatorum sententia,787.b.
units.tr: Degrees of glory in eternal life: are there to be any in the future? II. 784. b. This is proved from the testimonies of Scripture, parables, examples and reasons, 785. a. Contrary arguments are examined, 786. a. Augustine's opinion on the glory of the blessed, 787. b.

units.la: Glorificatio coronis est beneficiorum Christi, I I. 698. a. vid. Breviar. totius hominis describitur, I I. 716. a. ejusdem gradus, ibid.784.b. vide Breviar.
units.tr: Glorification is the crown of the benefits of Christ, II. 698. a. See Breviar. It is described for the whole man, II. 716. a; its degrees, ibid., 784. b. See Breviar.

units.la: Gnosticorum origo & dogmata,I.19.b.
units.tr: The origin and doctrines of the Gnostics, I. 19. b.

units.la: Godeschalcus quis fuerit, II.124.b. Pelagianis acriter se opposuit,ibid.
units.tr: Godeschalcus: who was he? II. 124. b. He opposed the Pelagians vigorously, ibid.

units.la: Goel, ἐπιλύτρωσις noster Christus est,II.7.b.80.a.
units.tr: Goel, redemption [ἐπιλύτρωσις]: our Christ is this, II. 7. b, 80. a.

units.la: Gog & Magog quinam? I I. 134. b. an & quomodo bellum gesturi, ibid. cum Messia juxta Judaeorum placita,146.a.
units.tr: Gog and Magog: who are they? II. 134. b. Whether and how they will wage war, ibid. With the Messiah according to the opinions of the Jews, 146. a.

units.la: Gonorrhaei impuritas & purificatio legalis,ejusque mystica significatio,I.672. a.
units.tr: The uncleanness of gonorrhoea and its legal purification, and its mystical significance, I. 672. a.

units.la: Graecae Linguae antiquitas,dignitas,I,39.a.
units.tr: The antiquity and dignity of the Greek language, I. 39. a.

units.la: Graecae Versionis antiquitas, I. 50. Recentiores versiones sunt Aquilae Pontici, Symmachi, Theodotionis, Hierichuntina, Nicopolitana, ibid. b.
units.tr: The antiquity of the Greek version, I. 50. The more recent versions are those of Aquila of Pontus, Symmachus, Theodotion, the Hierichuntine, and the Nicopolitan, ibid. b.

units.la: Graeci, eorum error circa processionem Spiritus S. I, 139.a. Christum in Paschate emortuali pane fermentatou sum esse docent,I I.44. a. Legem coelibatus a Papis Rom. latam nunquam receperunt, 666. a.
units.tr: Greeks: their error about the procession of the Holy Spirit, I, 139a. They teach that Christ used leavened bread at the Passover, I, 44a. They never received the law of celibacy enacted by the Roman Popes, 666a.

units.la: Gratia. Dei χάρις abundantia quid sit, I I.273. ea, qua justificamur non est ἐπίκτητος, 282.a. liberum arbitrium non tollit, 219.b. suaviter trahit, non torquet, 230.a. omnibus sufficiens data nulla est, 219.a. congruae figmentum evertitur,220.a. Gratia justificamur, 298. Gratiae assertorum historia, 402. a.
units.tr: Grace. What the abundance of God's grace [χάρις] is, II, 273. The grace by which we are justified is not acquired [ἐπίκτητος], 282a. It does not abolish free will, 219b. It draws sweetly and does not force, 230a. No grace is given that is sufficient for all, 219a. The fiction of congruous grace is overthrown, 220a. We are justified by grace, 298. History of the defenders of grace, 402a.

units.la: Gratiae humanae naturae Christi communicatae sunt tum Eminentiae.I I.20. a. tum habituales, ib. b.
units.tr: The graces of Christ's human nature were communicated to it, both eminent, II, 20a, and habitual, ibid. b.

units.la: Gratiarum actio qualis precum species est.346. a.
units.tr: Thanksgiving: what kind of prayer it is, 346a.

units.la: Gratiositas Dei, I.97.a.
units.tr: Graciousness of God, I, 97a.

units.la: Gratitudo quid, 567. b.
units.tr: Gratitude: what it is, 567b.

units.la: Gratuitum quo sensu quid dicatur,I I.117. b.118. a.
units.tr: The gratuitous: in what sense it is said of a thing, II, 117b–118a.

units.la: Grotius materiae mundi aeternitatem asserens notatur, I.187. a. de Chao primo quid sentiat,201.b. de juramento non benefensit, 546.b. de causa mendacii notatur,622.b. de descensu & ascensu Christi ad locum,Ephes.4:9.10. perverse agit,I I.3. b.4. b. ejus error usum Eucharistiae necessarium esse negantis perstringitur,499.
units.tr: Grotius is noted for asserting the eternity of matter, I, 187a. What he thinks of the primal Chaos, 201b. He did not speak well about oaths, 546b. He is noted for his account of the cause of lying, 622b. He acts perversely concerning Christ's descent to and ascent into a place, Eph. 4:9–10, II, 3b–4b. His error, which denies that the use of the Eucharist is necessary, is censured, 499.

units.la: Gubernatio Dei rerum creatarum, I.252. a. ejus varii modi,I.252, b. vide Breviar.
units.tr: The government of God over created things, I, 252a. Its various modes, I, 252b. See Breviary.

units.la: Gubernatio Ecclesiae nec Monarchica, nec Aristocratica, nec Democratica, sed oeconomica dici debet, 591.b. per ministeria in quo consistat, 587. a. civilis definitur,616. a. b. populi Christi vel interna vel externa est,135.b.
units.tr: The government of the Church should be called neither monarchical, nor aristocratic, nor democratic, but economic, 591b. In what it consists through the ministries, 587a. Civil government is defined, 616a–b. The government of the people of Christ is either internal or external, 135b.

units.la: Guicciardini testimonium de origine Primatus Papae Romani laudatur,I I.659.a.
units.tr: Guicciardini's testimony on the origin of the primacy of the Roman Pope is praised, II, 659a.

units.la: Γυμναστικα spiritualis quid.I I.318. b.
units.tr: Spiritual gymnastics: what it is, II, 318b.

units.la: Γυναικοβαπτισμος refellitur,I I.439.b. 440.a.
units.tr: Women's baptism is refuted, II, 439b–440a.

units.la: Gustare bonum Dei verbum, Heb.6:5. quid sit? II. 405. a.
units.tr: To taste the good word of God, Heb. 6:5. What does it mean? II, 405a.

units.tr: H.

units.la: Habel fides,I.425.a.; ejus Sacrificium,443.b. cur Deo magis quam Caini placuerit? ib. b. quomodo occisus Christi typus fuerit? 452.b.
units.tr: Abel's faith, I, 425a. His sacrifice, 443b. Why it pleased God more than Cain's, ibid. b. In what way was his murder a type of Christ? 452b.

units.la: Habitus infusus fides est,II.243. a. non acquisitus, 144.
units.tr: Infused habit is faith, II, 243a. Not acquired, II, 144.

units.la: Haereditas excludit meritum,I.336. a. 337.b. illa terrae Canaan non vera sed typica fuit,472.b. 474.non tamen ex merito data,477. b.

units.la: Haereditas seu successio in bona defuncti apud Hebraeos quintuplex distinguitur, I. 729. a. non debebat de tribu in tribum migrare,730.a.
units.tr: Inheritance, or succession to the goods of a deceased person among the Hebrews, is distinguished in five ways, I, 729a. It was not to pass from tribe to tribe, 730a.

units.tr: Inheri-

units.la: Hared'tas Filii Dei, sunt quidam homines ei à Deo da-ti, I.559. a. Ei à Patre promissa qualis sit? 378.a.
units.tr: Inheritance of the Son of God: certain men given to him by God, I, 559a. What kind of inheritance is the one promised to him by the Father? 378a.

units.la: Hareditas gentium fidelibus N. Test. data est, II,181. a. 186. a.
units.tr: The inheritance of the Gentiles was given to the faithful of the New Testament, II, 181a, 186a.

units.la: Haereses unde exortae? I.7. a.

units.la: Haeretici, Eis fides jurata servanda est, I.546. a. simpliciter tales poenis externis non sunt puniendi, 587. a. 588. Christi templum flagello purgantis exemplum non patrocinatur Haereticidis, 588. b. eorum baptismus quatenus probari possit? II.440. a. quomodo à Magistratu tractandi sint? 634, b. 635. an, & quousque illis fides servanda sit? ibid. b. eis sepultura non est neganda, 698. b.
units.tr: Heretics: faith sworn to them must be kept, I, 546a. Such persons are not to be punished simply by external penalties, I, 587a, 588. The example of Christ cleansing the temple with a whip does not support the killing of heretics, 588b. How far can their baptism be proved valid? II, 440a. How are they to be treated by the magistrate? 634b, 635. Whether and how far faith is to be kept with them, ibid. b. Burial is not to be denied them, 698b.

units.la: Hagiolatria fundamenta, II. 709. seqq. hagiolatrarum argumenta discutiuntur, 713. vide Sancti.
units.tr: Hagiolatry: its foundations, II, 709 ff. The arguments of the hagiolaters are discussed, 713. See Saints.

units.la: Harmonia partium Scripturae ejus Divinitatem evincit, I. 17. a.
units.tr: The harmony of the parts of Scripture proves its divinity, I, 17a.

units.la: Harmonia & ordo rerum creatarum Providentiam Dei arguit, I. 142. b.
units.tr: The harmony and order of created things argues the providence of God, I, 142b.

units.la: Harmonia rituum Ecclesiasticorum exacta obtineri nequit, II.592. a. ordinum Ecclesiastici & civilis in gubernanda Ecclesia, eam beatam reddit, 636.
units.tr: An exact harmony of ecclesiastical rites cannot be obtained, II, 592a. The order of ecclesiastical and civil government in governing the Church makes it blessed, 636.

units.la: Hasidaeorum mos oferendi, I.671. a.
units.tr: The custom of the Hasideans of offering, I, 671a.

units.tr: Heinsius is censured, I, 62a.

units.tr: The Helvetic Confession on the Sabbath, I, 554a; praised, II, 596b. On church discipline, 609a. On the goods of the Church, 611a.

units.la: Herbae, earum creatio & distinctio, 207. b. iis vesci cur homo lapsus jussus fuerit? 236. a. herbae amarae cum Paschali agno edi solitae, quales fuerint? 488. b.
units.tr: Herbs: their creation and distinction, 207b. Why was fallen man ordered to eat them? 236a. What were the bitter herbs customarily eaten with the Passover lamb? 488b.

units.la: Herbertus Religionem naturalem quinque Veritatibus comprehensam, salutarem statuens arguitur, I.4. b. ejusdem de Prophetis impietas arguitur, 441. a. idem, remissionem peccatorum Religionem mollire causatus arguitur, II.195. a.
units.tr: Herbert, who holds that natural religion, comprehended in five truths, is salutary, is accused, I, 4b. His impiety concerning the prophets is accused, 441a. The same man, who alleges that the remission of sins softens religion, is accused, II, 195a.

units.la: Heri & Hodie quomodo de Christo dicantur. II.2. 3. a.
units.tr: How "yesterday" and "today" are said of Christ, II, 2–3a.

units.la: Herorum & servorum officia, I.571. b.
units.tr: The duties of heroes and servants, I, 571b.

units.la: Hierarchia Angelorum fictitia est, I. 280. a. à Platone & Judaeis Cabbalistis excogitata, & à Pseudo-Dionysio Areopagita propugnata, ibid. b.
units.tr: The hierarchy of angels is fictitious, I, 280a. It was devised by Plato and the Jewish Cabbalists, and defended by Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, ibid. b.

units.la: Hierarchia Papalis depingitur. II. 539. b. est Regnum mundanum & carnale Antichristi, 638. a. 641. a. quam non Christi, sed Romuli spiritus peperit, ibid.
units.tr: The Papal hierarchy is depicted, II, 539b. It is the worldly and carnal kingdom of Antichrist, II, 638a–641a. It was born not of the spirit of Christ but of the spirit of Romulus, ibid.

units.la: Hierosolyma nova de coelo descendens, qualis sit futura, II.755. a.
units.tr: The New Jerusalem descending from heaven: what it will be like, II, 755a.

units.la: Hillerus de Keri & Ketibh laudatur, I.36. a.
units.tr: Hillerus is praised on Keri and Ketib, I, 36a.

units.la: Hircus Hazazel quid significaverit? I.683. seq. piacularis quando immolari consueverit? 658.b. Hircus in desertum abactus, 657. b. 661. a.
units.tr: What did the goat Azazel signify? I, 683 ff. When was the sin-offering goat customarily sacrificed? 658b. The goat driven into the wilderness, 657b, 661a.

units.la: Hobbesius notatur, I 45. a. ejus, Scripturae authoritatem a civili potestate suspendentis, impietas perstringitur, 31. b. ejusdem impietas, cognitionem Dei homini impossibilem, asserentis, 62. b. idem negans Deum magnum vel maximum, nisi corpus habeat, arguitur, 71. b. ejusdem Decalogi praecepta in mere civilia commutantis, elenchus, 101. a. idem de animae immortalitate notatur, 218. b. 220. b. ejusdem error Providentiae Dei res inanimatas & Atheos subducentis, 260. b. Deum peccati Authorem statuentis, 170. a. Angelos substantias spirituales esse negantis, 171. b. Daemones negat, 286 a. 297. a. Jus naturale negat, 311. a. vel saltem ex sola propriae salutis cura, ab hominibus latum esse, ibid. ejus rationes discutiuntur, 311, b. 312. a. Legem naturalem non obligare in foro externo asserit, quando secreto praestari non possit, 314. b. ejusdem error de statu hominis naturali, 506. b. item, de honore Deo exhibendo sine externis corporis signis, qui refellitur, 527. a. idem de superiorum & inferiorum officiis notatur, 567. b. coecam obedientiam inferiorum statuit, 569. b. ejusdem impia dogmata; Jus esse homini occidendi alterum, etiam innocentem, &c. perstringuntur, 581. a. 582. b. idem ἀνσεκλω (seu jus omnium in omnes asserens, etiam in statu naturali hominis, notatur, 609. b. 610. b. idem mendacio patiocinatur, 625. b. fidelitatem arrodit, 630. a. ejusdem impiae de Magistratu assertiones refelluntur, II. 610. b. 611. idem aeternitatem poenarum infernalium negans vapulat, 763. b. 764. b.
units.tr: Hobbes is noted, I, 45a. His impiety, which makes the authority of Scripture subject to the civil power, is censured, 31b. His impiety, which asserts that the knowledge of God is impossible for man, 62b. He is accused for denying that God is great or greatest unless he has a body, 71b. His elenchus of the precepts of the Decalogue, which he turns into purely civil ones, 101a. He is noted on the immortality of the soul, 218b–220b. His error, which withdraws the providence of God from inanimate things and atheists, 260b. His claim that God is the author of sin, 170a. His denial that angels are spiritual substances, 171b. He denies demons, 286a, 297a. He denies natural law, 311a, or at least holds that it was introduced by men only from concern for their own salvation, ibid. His arguments are examined, 311b–312a. He asserts that the natural law does not bind in the external court when it cannot be observed in secret, 314b. His error concerning the natural state of man, 506b. Likewise his view that honour is to be paid to God without outward bodily signs, which is refuted, 527a. He is noted on the duties of superiors and inferiors, 567b. He lays down a blind obedience of inferiors, 569b. His impious dogmas are censured: that it is a man's right to kill another, even an innocent person, etc., 581a–582b. He is noted for his ἀνσεκλω (that is, the right of all against all, which he asserts even in the natural state of man), 609b–610b. He also defends lying, 625b. He undermines fidelity, 630a. His impious assertions about the magistrate are refuted, II, 610b, 611. He denies the eternity of infernal punishments and is scourged for it, II, 763b–764b.

units.la: Hoc enim est corpus meum symbola non transsubstantiant, II. 464. a.
units.tr: "For this is my body": the symbols do not transubstantiate, II, 464a.

units.la: Hoc in loquutionibus quid significet, II. 477. seq. 498, a,
units.tr: What "this" signifies in locutions, II, 477 ff., 498a.

units.la: Hodie Psal. II.7. aeternam generationem Filii notat, I, 120. quomodo de Christo dicatur? II. 3. a.
units.tr: "Today" in Ps. 2:7 denotes the eternal generation of the Son, I, 120. In what way is it said of Christ? II, 3a.

units.la: Holocaustia quales victimae fuerint? I.654. b. fusius explicatur, 655. a. eorum mystica significatio, 675. b.
units.tr: Burnt offerings: what kinds of victims they were, I, 654b. Explained more fully, 655a. Their mystical significance, 675b.

units.la: Homicidium quot modis committatur? I.580. a. casuale quale? ibid. b. voluntarium, ibid. ejus indicia, ibid. atrocitas, 581. a. limitatio. 583. a.
units.tr: In how many ways is homicide committed? I, 580a. What kind is accidental? ibid. b. Voluntary, ibid. Its signs, ibid. Its atrocity, 581a. Its limitation, 583a.

units.la: Homicidarum poena in Lege qualis sit? I.716. involuntariis lex consulens explicatur, 719. a.
units.tr: What is the penalty for homicide in the Law? I, 716. The law's provision for involuntary homicide is explained, 719a.

units.la: Homiliae Patrum cur & quando scriptae? II. 595. a.
units.tr: Why and when were the homilies of the Fathers written? II, 595a.

units.la: Homo, Historia corporis humani expulveie creati, & ratio nominis אדם eidem impositi, I.215. b. 216. a. non indifferens sive ad bonum sive ad malum creatus est, 228. a. hominis primi Itatus in puris naturalibus confutatur, 225. a. homines eorumque actiones omnes, quomodo subsint Providentiae Dei? 257. b. hominis Itatus duplex, corruptae naturae & peccati, vel conversionis & gratiae, II. 118. a. homo vetus quomodo deponatur? 230. b. 231. homo vetus & novus, ibid.
units.tr: Man: the history of the human body, formed from dust, and the reason for the name אדם [adam] given to him, I, 215b–216a. He was not created indifferent to good or evil, 228a. The state of the first man in pure nature is refuted, 225a. How all men and all their actions are subject to the providence of God, 257b. The state of man is twofold: of corrupted nature and sin, or of conversion and grace, II, 118a. How the old man is put off, 230b–231. Old man and new man, ibid.

units.la: Honor Dei ex persuasione de Ejus excellentia oritur, I.524. a. honoris & cultus objectum est excellentia vel divina vel humana, 526. a.
units.tr: The honour of God arises from the conviction of His excellence; the object of honour and worship is excellence, either divine or human, I.524a, 526a.

units.la: Honor Parentibus habendus qualis esse debeat? I. 564. b.
units.tr: What kind of honour is to be shown to parents? I.564b.

units.la: Horae canonicae Pontificiorum perstringuntur, I.350. b.
units.tr: The canonical hours of the Papists are criticised, I.350b.

units.la: Hornius laudatur, II. 733. a.
units.tr: Hornius is praised, II.733a.

units.la: Hostiae numulariae in Missa exploduntur, I I.463 b. ejus asservatio in pixide improbatur, 467. a, ejus adoratio idololatrica est, 492. b. confutatur, 493.
units.tr: Coin-shaped hosts in the Mass are rejected, I.463b; their reservation in the pyx is disapproved, 467a; their adoration is idolatrous, 492b; refuted, 493.

units.la: Hostis. Hostibus & Haereticis juramenta servanda sunt, I.546. a. hostes Ecclesiae variisunt generis. II, 135. a. infelix eorum exitus, an sit verae Ecclesiae nota? 511. b.
units.tr: Enemy. Oaths are to be kept with enemies and heretics, I.546a. The enemies of the Church are of various kinds, II.135a. Their unhappy end: is it a mark of the true Church? 511b.

units.la: Hottingerus laudatur, II. 733. a.
units.tr: Hottinger is praised, II.733a.

units.la: Huetius laudatur, I.21. b. 28. b.
units.tr: Huet is praised, I.21b, 28b.

units.la: Humani corporis creatio & admiranda structura, I.116, a. b. humanum genus universum in Adamorepraesentabatur. 307. b.
units.tr: The creation and admirable structure of the human body, I.116a, b. The whole human race was represented in Adam, 307b.

units.la: Humana Christi natura probatur, II.8. b. ejus in utero B. Virginis formatio explicatur & adversus Socinianos vindicatur, 13. b. ex substantia Virginis formata, 14. b. successu temporis facta est, 16. a. ea in utero matris a Spiritu S. ita sanctificata est, ut labis expers nasceretur, 17. a. quomodo in unitatem personae & λόγος assumta, 18. a.
units.tr: The human nature of Christ is proved, II.8b. Its formation in the womb of the blessed Virgin is explained and defended against the Socinians, 13b. Formed from the substance of the Virgin, 14b. Brought about in the course of time, 16a. Sanctified in the womb of the mother by the Holy Spirit, so that He was born free from stain, 17a. How it was assumed into the unity of the person and the Word, 18a.

units.la: Humanitas quid? I.575. a. an, & quatenus etiam erga bruta se extendat? ibid. ejus erga se ipsum officia spiritualia & corporalia extenduntur, 575. b. externa, 579. a.
units.tr: What is humanity? I.575a. Whether and how far it extends even to the brute beasts, ibid. Its spiritual and bodily duties toward oneself extend, 575b; external duties, 579a.

units.la: Humiliatio coram Deo, I.161. b. sui ipsius necessaria, II, 251, a. humiliandi nos argumenta, I, 10. a.
units.tr: Humiliation before God, I.161b; necessary humiliation of oneself, II.251a; arguments for humbling ourselves, I.10a.

units.la: Humiliatio Christi usque admorem crucis, II,43. a.b.
units.tr: The humiliation of Christ even to the death of the cross, II.43a, b.

units.la: Humilitas quid? I. 521. b. 565. b. 566. a 578. a.
units.tr: What is humility? I.521b, 565b, 566a, 578a.

units.la: Hymenaeus & Philetus an à fide justificante defecerint? II. 407. a.
units.tr: Hymenaeus and Philetus: did they fall away from justifying faith? II.407a.

units.la: Hypocritae cur in Ecclesia externa sint? II,517. a.
units.tr: Why are hypocrites in the external Church? II.517a.

units.la: Hypostasis quid in Divinis? I. 111. a.
units.tr: What is hypostasis in the Divine persons? I.111a.

units.tr: J.

units.la: Jacobus & Esavus Decreti Divini objecta fuerunt, I. 162. a. 175. a.
units.tr: Jacob and Esau were the objects of the divine decree, I.162a, 175a.

units.la: Jacobus foedus Dei cum Abrahamo XII. filiis suis applicavit, 433. b. ejus item emortuale de Schilo vaticinium, ib. b, ejus genuina interpretatio. 434. b. 435. a. an è nepotibus suis post obitum religiose invocari petierit? II.713. b.
units.tr: Jacob applied the covenant of God with Abraham to his twelve sons, II.433b. Likewise his dying prophecy concerning Shiloh, ibid. b; its genuine interpretation, 434b, 435a. Did he ask to be religiously invoked by his grandsons after his death? II.713b.

units.la: Jacobi cum Paulo in Justificatione conciliatio, I.304, 305.
units.tr: The reconciliation of James with Paul on justification, I.304, 305.

units.la: Jactantia quid? I.565. b.
units.tr: What is boasting? I.565b.

units.la: Jansenius, Augustini, de gratia Dei salvifica, assertor laudatur, II 124. b.
units.tr: Jansenius, the champion of Augustine's doctrine of saving grace, is praised, II.124b.

units.la: Ideae rerum in Deo quid? I.152. a.
units.tr: What are the ideas of things in God? I.152a.

units.la: Idea Ecclesiae falsa, I I. 532. b.
units.tr: A false idea of the Church, II.532b.

units.la: Idiomatum naturae Div. communicatio facta est non naturae humanae, sed Personae Christi, II.21. a.b. realis & verbalis diverso sensu est, ibid. 23. a. Idiomata Divina naturae humanae Christi non communicata esse ostenditur, 29. a. b. dissensus Protestantium circa hoc Dogma Ecclesiam scindere non debet, 33. b.
units.tr: The communication of the divine attributes was made not to the human nature but to the Person of Christ, II.21a, b. It is real and verbal in different senses, ibid. 23a. It is shown that the divine attributes were not communicated to the human nature of Christ, 29a, b. The dissension of the Protestants over this doctrine ought not to split the Church, 33b.

units.la: Idiotae quomodo certi sint, se habere vel audire Verbum Dei, I. 51. a.
units.tr: How can the unlearned be certain that they have or hear the Word of God? I.51a.

units.la: Idolum quid? I.530. b. ab imagine non differt. 531. b. quoquomodo nihil sit in mundo? 533. a.
units.tr: What is an idol? I.530b. It does not differ from an image, 531b. In what way is it nothing in the world? 533a.

units.la: Idololatria interna quid? I. 523. a. Idololatria quid? 530. a. male à Bellarmino & de Valentia definitur, ib. b. refellitur, 531. Papalis pigmenta, 538. b. Indirectæ & analogicæ species, 539. a. participata explicatur, 540. a. Idololatriæ instrumenta quomodo retecranda fuerint, 720. b. abolenda, 721. a.
units.tr: Idolatry inward: what is it? I.523a. Idolatry: what is it? 530a. It is wrongly defined by Bellarmine and de Valentia, ibid. b; it is refuted, 531. The Papal pretexts, 538b. Indirect and analogical forms, 539a. Participation explained, 540a. How the instruments of idolatry ought to be unmasked, 720b; to be abolished, 721a.

units.la: Idololatyis quando abstinendum sit? I.563. a.
units.tr: Idolatries: when must one abstain from them? I.563a.

units.la: JEHOVA est etiam Nomen Christi, I.126. a. ei respondet in N. Test. Κύριος, 127. b.
units.tr: JEHOVAH is also the name of Christ, I.126a. In the New Testament the corresponding word is Kyrios [Κύριος], 127b.

units.la: R. Jehuda Haccados de Resurrectione Christi loquitur, II. 60. a.
units.tr: R. Jehuda Haccados speaks of the resurrection of Christ, II.60a.

units.la: Jejunium definitur, I.360. b. ejus utilitas, 361. b. vide Breviar.
units.tr: Fasting is defined, I.360b; its usefulness, 361b. See Breviary.

units.la: Jephta an filiam, & quomodo occiderit? I. 582. a. ejus devotamentum quale fuerit? 714. b. ex extranea muliere natus est, 719. a.
units.tr: Jephthah: did he kill his daughter, and how? I.582a. What kind of devoting was his vow? 714b. Was he born of a foreign woman? 719a.

units.la: JESUS CHRISTUS. Ejus traditio in manus gentilium necessaria fuit, II. 45. b. crucis supplicium subire debuit, ibid.46. b. crucifixionis historia, ib. 47. a. b. septem ejus in cruce verba, 48. a. desertus à Deo quomodo fuerit? 48. b. renebrae, ibid.49. a. prodigia mortem consecuta, 49. b. Sepultura, ibid. 50. b. Mysteria ejus varia panduntur, 51. b. descensus ejus ad inferos, ibid. animae Christi passiones, ibid. 53. a. Exaltationis status, ibid. 54. b, 55. a. Nomen super omne Nomen sibi meruit, ibid. 55. a. Resurrectio, 57. a. &c. secundum carnem resurrexit, ibid. 58. b. iterum orbem habitabilem intravit, ibid.61. a. Apparitiones ejus post resurrectionem IX. ibid. 61. b. quatuor singulis vel paucis factae, 61. b. duae in Judaea, 62. a. duae in Galilaea, 63. a. novissima in monte oliveti, 63. b. 64. a. Ascensio, 64. a. ejus veritas asserentur, 64. b. 65. a. suo jure & merito ascendit, 65. b. Sessio ad dextram Patris. 67. a. ibi triplex munus Mediatorium exercet, 68. a. ejus officium. vide Breviar. 72. seq. Mediatorium definitur. 74. Nomina JESU, ibid. Salvator populi sui, ib.75. CHRISTI, 77. a. soli Christo Jesu competit, ibid. de Unctione Personae Christi, 77. b, unctio ejus spiritualis, ib. 78. Mediator est, 79. Sacerdos, ibid. quà Mediator adorari debet, 82. b. Mediator Deum inter & homines non Angelos, 83. a. b. Mediator est merito & efficacia, 85. b. Ejus officium triplex, 87. a. Prophetia, ib. b. 88. vide Breviar. vel legalis vel Evangelica fuit, 90. a. Rex est, 93. b. Doctrinae summa, 94. efficacia, 94. b. μίσυαγκτ, ib.95. a. Miracula, 95 96. Pseudo-Propheta non fuit, ibid. 99. a. vitae exemplo doctrinam confirmavit, 100. b. & morte sua, 101. a. Sacerdotium definitur & explicatur, 102. a. ipse Sacerdos & victima est, 104. b. Mors vim expiandi habuit, ibid. 106. a. vicaria fuit, ib. b. satisfactio ejus vindicatur, 116. seqq. vide satisfactio. Meritum infinitum intensive, 118. b. pro solis electis mortuus est, 122. a. quibus etiam Spiritum S. & fidem meruit, ibid. Victimae in coelo repraesentatio, 117. b. Advocatus & Patronus noster apud Patrem. ib. 128. a. ejus Regium munus, 129. vide CHRISTUS.
units.tr: JESUS CHRIST. His delivery into the hands of the Gentiles was necessary, II.45b. He had to undergo the punishment of the cross, ibid. 46b. The history of the crucifixion, ibid. 47a, b. His seven words on the cross, 48a. How was he forsaken by God? 48b. Darkness, ibid. 49a. Prodigies that followed his death, 49b. His burial, ibid. 50b. His various mysteries are unfolded, 51b. His descent into hell, ibid. The sufferings of Christ's soul, ibid. 53a. The state of exaltation, ibid. 54b, 55a. He merited the name above every name, ibid. 55a. The resurrection, 57a, etc. He rose according to the flesh, ibid. 58b. He entered the inhabited world again, ibid. 61a. His nine appearances after the resurrection, ibid. 61b: four made to single persons or to a few, 61b; two in Judaea, 62a; two in Galilee, 63a; the last on the Mount of Olives, 63b, 64a. The ascension, 64a; its truth is asserted, 64b, 65a; he ascended by his own right and merit, 65b. Sitting at the right hand of the Father, 67a; there he exercises the threefold mediatorial office, 68a; his office: see Breviary, 72ff. Mediatorship defined, 74. The names of Jesus, ibid.; Saviour of his people, ibid. 75. CHRIST, 77a; it belongs to Jesus Christ alone, ibid. On the anointing of the Person of Christ, 77b; his spiritual anointing, ibid. 78. He is Mediator, 79; Priest, ibid.; as Mediator he ought to be worshipped, 82b. The Mediator between God and men, not angels, 83a, b. He is Mediator by merit and efficacy, 85b. His threefold office, 87a. Prophecy, ibid. b, 88; see Breviary. Whether it was legal or evangelical, 90a. He is King, 93b. The sum of his doctrine, 94; its efficacy, 94b; the Greek term [μίσυαγκτ], ibid. 95a. Miracles, 95, 96. He was not a false prophet, ibid. 99a. He confirmed his doctrine by the example of his life, 100b, and by his death, 101a. The priesthood is defined and explained, 102a. He is himself both priest and victim, 104b. His death had power to expiate, ibid. 106a; it was vicarious, ibid. b. His satisfaction is vindicated, 116ff; see satisfaction. His merit is infinite in intensity, 118b. He died only for the elect, 122a, for whom he also merited the Holy Spirit and faith, ibid. The representation of the victim in heaven, 117b. Advocate and Patron with the Father, ibid. 128a. His kingly office, 129; see CHRIST.

units.la: Jesuitae. Eorum de scientia Dei media commentum refellitur, I. 85.86. eorum error de Praedestinatione, 149. b. de peccato Philosophico. 330. b. Diligendi Dei obligationem homines non habere asserunt, 503. b. eorum aequivocatio in juramentis, 544. b. aequivocationes eorum depinguntur, 625.626.627. a. nullum in Scriptura praesidium habent, 618. b. eorum cacozelia, qui se JESU sodales, socios jactitant, II 75. b. Pelagianizant, 219. b. 265. b.
