units.tr: Jesuits. Their figment of the middle knowledge of God is refuted, I.85, 86. Their error on predestination, 149b. On philosophical sin, 330b. They assert that men are not bound to love God, 503b. Their equivocation in oaths, 544b. Their equivocations are depicted, 625, 626, 627a. They have no support in Scripture, 618b. The cacozeal of those who boast of being companions and associates of Jesus, II.75b. They Pelagianize, 219b, 265b.

units.la: Jethro, Socer Moisis, quis? I.435. b.
units.tr: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law: who was he? I.435b.

units.la: Ignis sacer, primigenius qui sacrificia consumebat, explicatur, I. 660. b. quid in V. Test. praefiguraverit? 678. b.
units.tr: The sacred primeval fire that consumed the sacrifices is explained, I.660b. What did it prefigure in the Old Testament? 678b.

units.la: Ignis consumet Mundum in die judicii, I I.751. b. nihil tamen piis, aut ruineptis, nocebit, 753. a.
units.tr: Fire will consume the world on the day of judgement, II.751b; yet it will do no harm to the godly or to the ruinous, 753a.

units.la: Ignis de quo, 1.Cor.III.12. agitur, non est purgatorius Pontificiorum, I I.703. a.
units.tr: The fire of which 1 Cor. 3.12 speaks is not the purgatorial fire of the Papists, II.703a.

units.la: Ignis Infernalis qualis sit? I I.760. b. 761. a.
units.tr: What kind of fire is the infernal fire? II.760b, 761a.

units.la: Ignorantia quotuplex? 357 b.
units.tr: Ignorance: how many kinds are there? 357 b.

units.la: Illuminationis Spiritus S. in cognoscenda veritate Divina necessitas & efficacia, I.8. b. 9. a.
units.tr: Illumination by the Holy Spirit in knowing divine truth: its necessity and efficacy, I.8. b.–9. a.

units.la: Illuminari quousque Apostatae possint? I I.404. b. Φοenicionum Deus fuit, I.450. a.
units.tr: Illuminated: how far can apostates be illumined? I I.404. b. The god of the Phoenicians, I.450. a.

units.la: Imago. Imaginis Divina rudera in cujusvis hominis conscientia exstitunt, I.63. a. Imago Dei ad quam primus homo conditus est, in quo consistat? 136. a, 237. a. contra Socin. vindicatur, 237. ad imaginem Dei etiam Angeli facti sunt, 273. a. 275. b. in homine per lapsum quomodo amissa sit? 338. a. Imaginis Divinae perfecta communio ex beatifica Dei visione sequetur, I I.779. a.
units.tr: Image. Remnants of the divine image exist in the conscience of every person, I.63. a. In what does the image of God, in which the first man was created, consist? 136. a., 237. a. It is defended against Socinus, 237. Angels also were made in the image of God, 273. a., 275. b. How was it lost in man through the fall? 338. a. Perfect fellowship with the divine image will follow from the beatific vision of God, I I.779. a.

units.la: Imagine Deum colere est idololatria symbolica, I.513. b. Deus nulla imagine effingi potest, 533. a. 536,b.
units.tr: To worship God by an image is symbolic idolatry, I.513. b. God cannot be represented by any image, 533. a., 536. b.

units.la: Imago, simulachrum, an sint idolum falsi Numinis? I. 530. Imagines quatenus facere licet? 531. b. quales prohibeantur? 534. 535. earum ad cultum usus in Ecclesia tero obtinuit, 535. earum cultus à Pontificiis male distinguitur, ib. b. earum cultus relativus seu transitivus refellitur, ib. etiam earum factura ad cultum illicita est, 536. b.
units.tr: Image, statue: are they the idol of a false deity? I.530. To what extent is it lawful to make images? 531. b. Which kinds are forbidden? 534., 535. The use of images in worship has long prevailed in the Church, 535. Their worship is wrongly distinguished by the Papists, ib. b. Their relative or transitive worship is refuted, ib. Even making them for worship is unlawful, 536. b.

units.la: Imitatio Christi in totam legem fertur, ceu exemplar vitae & actionum, I I.9. b. 100. in quibus consistat? 100. 101. a. 339. b.
units.tr: Imitation of Christ extends to the whole law, as the pattern of life and action, I I.9. b., 100. In what does it consist? 100., 101. a., 339. b.

units.la: Immensitas Dei explicatur, I.77. a. nulli creaturae competit, 79. a.
units.tr: Immensity of God is explained, I.77. a. It belongs to no creature, 79. a.

units.la: Immersio apud orientales, asperso vero aquae apud occidentales in Baptismo cur adhibeatur? I I.442. b. hujus ritus cum re significata analogia, 444. a.
units.tr: Immersion among the Easterners, but sprinkling with water among the Westerners, in Baptism: why is each used? I I.442. b. The analogy of this rite with the thing signified, 444. a.

units.la: Immortalitas animae rationalis altruitur, I.218. b. exratione probatur, 219.
units.tr: Immortality of the rational soul is asserted, I.218. b. It is proved by reason, 219.

units.la: Immundities cordis peccatum est, I.145, a.
units.tr: Uncleanness of heart is sin, I.145. a.

units.la: Immutabilitas Dei varie asserit, I.79. a.
units.tr: Immutability of God is asserted in various ways, I.79. a.

units.la: Immutabilitas Legis naturalis unde? 314. a.
units.tr: Immutability of the natural law: whence does it come? 314. a.

units.la: Imperatores multi Antichristi revelationem continuerunt, I I.686. b.
units.tr: Emperors: many have held back the revelation of Antichrist, I I.686. b.

units.la: Imperfectio regenerationis in hac vita, I.234.235.236.
units.tr: Imperfection of regeneration in this life, I.234., 235., 236.

units.la: Implacabiles quinam fuerunt? I I.326. a.
units.tr: The implacable: who were they? I I.326. a.

units.la: Imputabile resp. Dei quid fit? I.101. an Deus homini impossibilia praecipiat? 367. b.
units.tr: Imputation: what is it on God's part? I.101. Does God command man impossible things? 367. b.

units.la: Imprecari aliis non licet, I.348. a.
units.tr: Imprecation is not lawful against others, I.348. a.

units.la: Impuritas Legalis, I. 672. a. circa quae observabatur? ib. non cativit multica significatione, 690. a. spiritualis impuritas, ib.
units.tr: Legal impurity, I.672. a. With what things was it concerned? ib. It does not bind in every sense, 690. a. Spiritual impurity, ib.

units.la: Imputatio quid? I. 275. b. duplex, rei alienae vel propriae, 276. vide Breviar. Imputatio peccati Adami posteris ejus fuse probatur, I.340. 341. seq. ejus mediatae & immediatae distinctio rejicitur, 342. b. eam imputationem negantium Historia, 343. a.
units.tr: Imputation: what is it? I.275. b. It is twofold, of another's or one's own deed, 276. See the Breviarium. The imputation of Adam's sin to his posterity is fully proved, I.340., 341. and following. The distinction between mediate and immediate imputation is rejected, 342. b. The history of those who deny this imputation, 343. a.

units.la: Inauguratio Ministrorum ubi & quando necessaria, I I. 571. b.
units.tr: Inauguration of ministers: where and when is it necessary? I I.571. b.

units.la: Incarnationis Christi Typi in V. Test, I I,7. b.
units.tr: Incarnation of Christ: its types in the Old Testament, I I.7. b.

units.la: Incestus poena juxta Legem capitalis est, I.718. a.
units.tr: Incest: according to the Law, the penalty is capital, I.718. a.

units.la: Independentia est attributum Dei incommunicabile, I.71. b.
units.tr: Independence is an attribute of God that cannot be communicated, I.71. b.

units.la: Independentium Synodos oppugnantium elenchus, I I. 614. a.
units.tr: Refutation of the Independents who attack synods, I I.614. a.

units.la: Indifferentia Dei naturae repugnat, I.93. b.
units.tr: Indifference is repugnant to the nature of God, I.93. b.

units.la: Indifferens ad bonum & malum homo conditus non est, I. 228. a.
units.tr: Indifference to good and evil: man was not created so, I.228. a.

units.la: Indulgentiarum Papalium vanitas, I I.292. b. 293. confutantur 294. a. seio in Ecclesia cognitae, 294. b.
units.tr: Papal indulgences: their vanity, I I.292. b., 293. They are refuted, 294. a. Their knowledge in the Church, 294. b.

units.la: Induratio malorum quomodo Deo tributur, I.262. a. 272. Indurare, excaecare, impinguare cor hominis quomodo Deus dicatur? I.273. b.
units.tr: Hardening of evil men: how is it ascribed to God? I.262. a., 272. How can God be said to harden, blind, or fatten the heart of man? I.273. b.

units.la: Infantes à peccato originali non immunes sunt, I.353. b. nec à poena, 361. a. quomodo illis prosit Baptismus, 397. b. baptizatis in infantia morientibus baptismus regenerationis & insitionis in Christum gratiam certo obsignat, I I.449. a. ejus rei ratio explicatur, ib. b. infantes spurii, expositi, haeretico rum, infide ium an baptizandi? 452. a. ante baptismum morientibus salus non abjudicanda est, 455. 456. iis sacra Coena non est administranda, 462. a.
units.tr: Infants are not free from original sin, I.353. b., nor from its punishment, 361. a. How does baptism profit them? 397. b. For infants baptized and dying in infancy, baptism, as the regeneration and engrafting into Christ, certainly seals grace, I I.449. a. The reason for this is explained, ib. b. Are bastard infants, foundlings, the children of heretics or of unbelievers to be baptized? 452. a. Salvation is not to be denied to those dying before baptism, 455., 456. The Lord's Supper is not to be administered to them, 462. a.

units.la: Infantia & pueritia hominis subest Providentiae Dei, I. 257.
units.tr: Infancy and childhood of man are subject to the providence of God, I.257.

units.la: Infantia Christi memorabilia sigillatim recensentur, I I. 38. a.
units.tr: Infancy of Christ: its memorable events, one by one, I I.38. a.

units.la: Infernus in quem descendit Christus qualis sit? I,221.a. Inferi seu Infernus & ᾅδης idem sunt, I I.52. a.
units.tr: Hell, into which Christ descended: what sort of place is it? I.221. a. Hades and Hell [ᾅδης] are the same, I I.52. a.

units.la: Infernus quid? ejus nomina, II.757. b. ejus existentia probatur tum disertis Scripturae testimoniis, 758. a. tum rationibus à justitia, veracitate & natura Dei, testimonio conscientiae, & consensu gentium petitis, 758. b infernalium poenarum atrocitas, 759. vide Poena. locus, 767. a.
units.tr: Hell: what is it? Its names, I I.757. b. Its existence is proved both by explicit testimonies of Scripture, 758. a., and by arguments drawn from the justice, truthfulness, and nature of God, the testimony of conscience, and the consent of the nations, 758. b. The atrocity of infernal punishments, 759. See Punishment. Its place, 767. a.

units.la: Infidelis. Credendi facultatem infideles nunquam acceperunt, I I.215. a.
units.tr: Unbeliever. Unbelievers never received the faculty of believing, I I.215. a.

units.la: Infidelitatis causa quae? II.215. a.
units.tr: Unbelief: what is its cause? I I.215. a.

units.la: Infinitas Dei explicatur, I. 74. b. vide Brev. & contra Socinum & Spinozam vindicatur, ib. 75. a.
units.tr: Infinity of God is explained, I.74. b. See the Breviarium. It is defended against Socinus and Spinoza, ib., 75. a.

units.la: Infusa justitia hominis lapsi nulla est. I. 269. 271. 273.
units.tr: Infused righteousness of fallen man is nothing, I.269., 271., 273.

units.la: Inhærens justitia & charitas non est causa Justificationis, I. 268. 269. refellitur, 271. a.
units.tr: Inherent righteousness and charity is not the cause of justification, I.268., 269. It is refuted, 271. a.

units.la: Inimicus etiam diligendus, I. 504. b.
units.tr: Enemy is also to be loved, I.504. b.

units.la: Inquinamenta mundi, 2. Pet. II. 18. effugere quid sit? II. 405. a.
units.tr: Pollutions of the world, 2 Pet. 2:18. What is it to escape them? II.405. a.

units.la: Instar Dei quomodo Christus fuerit? II. 9. a.
units.tr: In the likeness of God: in what way was Christ so? II.9. a.

units.la: Instinctus naturalis Creaturarum qualis? 252. b.
units.tr: Natural instinct of creatures: what sort is it? 252. b.

units.la: Institutio populi non tam publica, quàm privata, cum primis Juventutis V.D. Ministris incumbit. I. 597. a. b. quæ vel domestica vel Ecclesiastica est, 598. b.
units.tr: Instruction of the people, not so much public as private, lies chiefly upon the ministers, especially for the youth. I.597. a., b. Whether it is domestic or ecclesiastical, 598. b.

units.la: Instrumentalis causa in creatione nullum habet locum. I. 189. a.
units.tr: Instrumental cause has no place in creation. I.189. a.

units.la: Intellectus quomodo Deo tribuatur & quid sit? I. 81. a. vid. Brev.
units.tr: Understanding: how is it ascribed to God, and what is it? I.81. a. See the Breviarium.

units.la: Intellectus Angelorum, I. 273. seq.
units.tr: Understanding of angels, I.273. and following.

units.la: Intentio Ministri ad Sacramenti validitatem non requiritur, I. 394. b. Antithesis Pontificiorum, 395. confutatur, ib. b. Intentio bona, I. 329. b.
units.tr: Intention of the minister is not required for the validity of the sacrament, I.394. b. The antithesis of the Papists, 395. is refuted, ib. b. A good intention, I.329. b.

units.la: Intercessionis Christi efficacia certitudinem salutis confirmat. I. 392. efficacia ostenditur, II. 148. b.
units.tr: Intercession of Christ: its efficacy confirms the certainty of salvation, I.392. Its efficacy is shown, II.148. b.

units.la: Interpellatio Christi pro electis & redemtis in cœlo, II. 127. seq.
units.tr: Intercession of Christ for the elect and redeemed in heaven, II.127. and following.

units.la: Interpres Scripturæ non est Philosophia, sed Deus in Scriptura loquens, I. 49. a. b.
units.tr: Interpreter of Scripture is not philosophy, but God speaking in Scripture, I.49. a., b.

units.la: Invidia Sathanam ad seducendum hominem impulit, I. 333. a. ejus μεγαλεῖα explicatur, ibid.
units.tr: Envy drove Satan to seduce man, I.333. a. Its greatness [μεγαλεῖα] is explained, ibid.

units.la: Invidia quid? I. 565. b. 578. b.
units.tr: Envy: what is it? I.565. b., 578. b.

units.la: Invisibilitas Dei attributum est, I. 73. b.
units.tr: Invisibility of God is an attribute, I.73. b.

units.la: Invisibilem Ecclesiam esse astruitur, II. 510. b.
units.tr: The invisible Church is shown to exist, II.510. b.

units.la: Inumbratio Virtutis Altissimi in B. Virgine quid effecerit? II. 13. a.
units.tr: Overshadowing of the power of the Most High upon the Blessed Virgin: what did it effect? II.13. a.

units.la: Invocatio Religiosa Christo competit, contra Socinum, &c. I. 134.
units.tr: Religious invocation belongs to Christ, against Socinus, etc. I.134.

units.la: Invocationis Sanctorum fundamenta, II. 709. seq. vid. Sancti, confutatur fusè, 712.
units.tr: Invocation of the saints: its foundations, II.709. and following. See Saints. It is refuted at length, 712.

units.la: Job quis fuerit? I. 435. carnis resurrectionem verè credidit, II. 733. b.
units.tr: Job: who was he? I.435. He truly believed in the resurrection of the flesh, II.733. b.

units.la: Joci qui & quatenus liciti sint? I. 632. b. liberalis & ingenui joci genera definiuntur, 634. a.
units.tr: Jests: which are lawful, and how far? I.632. b. The kinds of free and gentlemanly jests are defined, 634. a.

units.la: Johannes Bapt. primus Evangelii præco fuit, I. 188. 189. 192. a. vid. Brev. ejus præconium, 190. a. testimonium de Christo, ibid. Baptismus, 191. ejus ministerium merè Evangelicum fuit, ibid. ejus cibus in deserto, 363. b. ejus Baptismus in quibus à Christi differat? II. 437. b. objectiones Pontificiorum diluuntur, 438. a. non fuit Monachus, 674. b.
units.tr: John the Baptist was the first herald of the Gospel, I.188., 189., 192. a. See the Breviarium. His proclamation, 190. a. His testimony concerning Christ, ibid. Baptism, 191. His ministry was purely evangelical, ibid. His food in the desert, 363. b. In what respects his baptism differed from Christ's, II.437. b. The objections of the Papists are answered, 438. a. He was not a monk, 674. b.

units.la: Johannes Evangelista Canonem N. Test. clausit, II. 39. b.
units.tr: John the Evangelist closed the canon of the New Testament, II.39. b.

units.la: Johannes VIII. Papa, divitiarum cupidissimus Christum divitem in cruce repræsentari voluit, I. 606. b.
units.tr: Pope John VIII, most eager for riches, wished Christ to be represented as rich on the cross, I.606. b.

units.la: Josaphati vallis, an sit futura locus ultimi Judicii, I I. 750. a.
units.tr: Valley of Jehoshaphat: will it be the place of the last judgment? II.750. a.

units.la: Josephi venditio, quid in ea homines, quid Deus præstiterit? I. 272. a.
units.tr: Sale of Joseph: what did men do in it, and what did God accomplish? I.272. a.

units.la: Josephus Judæus resurrectionis Christi testis est, II. 60. a. ejus testimonium, ibid. b. ejusdem de Miraculis Christi testimonii contra nonnullos γνη- ϛ ϲἀσπις defenditur, II. 97. a.
units.tr: Josephus the Jew is a witness to the resurrection of Christ, II.60. a. His testimony, ibid. b. His testimony concerning the miracles of Christ is defended against some who reject it as the genuine shield [γνησία ἀσπίς], II.97. a.

units.la: Iracundia quid? I. 578. b.
units.tr: Anger: what is it? I.578. b.

units.la: Iris, quale signum fœderis gratiæ fuerit? I. 448. a. ejus mystica ratio oltenditur, ibid. b.
units.tr: Iris: what sort of sign of the covenant of grace was it? I. 448. a. Its mystical meaning is set out, ibid. b.

units.la: Ironia. Ironica Dei locutio de homine lapso, I. 337. b. 338. b.
units.tr: Irony: God's ironic speech about fallen man, I. 337. b. 338. b.

units.la: Irrisores ἰμπαικταὶ Athei sunt, II. 751. b. 717. b.
units.tr: Mockers [ἐμπαικταί] are atheists, II. 751. b. 717. b.

units.la: Isaci immolatio fidei Abrahamicæ tentatio fuit, I. 432. a. Isacus, Ismael & Josephus typi erant Ecclesiæ in diverso statu, I. 453. b.
units.tr: Isaac: the offering of Isaac was a trial of Abrahamic faith, I. 432. a. Isaac, Ishmael and Joseph were types of the Church in different states, I. 453. b.

units.la: Israelis Deus, verus Deus est, I. 109. b. Israelitici populi præ aliis προλογείσει ,470. b. 473. b. Israelitæ Moscholatræ an Deum corporeum coluerint? 534. b. Israelitici populi pueritia qualis? 647. b.
units.tr: The God of Israel is the true God, I. 109. b. The precedence of the Israelite people over others, 470. b. 473. b. Did the Israelites worship a corporeal God? 534. b. What was the childhood of the Israelite people like? 647. b.

units.la: Ita, ita, & non non in sermone quid notet? I. 542. b. 543. b.
units.tr: What does "Ita, ita, and non non" mean in speech? I. 542. b. 543. b.

units.la: Jubilæus annus Judæorum, I. 666. a. Papalis origo, progressus, II. 292. b.
units.tr: The Jubilee, the year of the Jews, I. 666. a. Its papal origin and progress, II. 292. b.

units.la: Juda. Ex tribu Juda Christus oriri debuit. II. 9. b.
units.tr: Judah: Christ had to arise from the tribe of Judah, II. 9. b.

units.la: Judæi, eorum Religio hodierna falsa est, I. 6. b. S. Scripturam integram conservârunt. 27. b. eorum distributio Vet. Test. in תורה נביאים וכתובים non probatur, 34. a. Error de lege oiali unde ortus? 41. a. Kabbala & Thalmude, ib. b. de Traditionibus, 43. error de Arbore vitæ. 326. a. qui Politiam aliquando restituendam esse obtendunt, refutantur, 738. b. Angelos in creando homine Deum juvisse, asserunt, 189. b. eorum de sex mille mundi annis opinio, 197. stellis animam vel spiritum motorem tribuunt, 209. Imaginem Dei in homine male definiunt, 236. a. cuivis homini Angelum bonum & malum tribuunt, 281. b. Spectra esse credidérunt, 297. a. Promissionum illam de Semine contriturò caput serpentis, pervertunt, 433. a. Vaticinium Jacobi de Schilo pervertunt, 433. b. Patriarchas non nisi religionem naturalem habuisse, fuisse sub חודי 437. Sacrificia justitiam contulisse, 446. b. Angelum illum in monte Sinai cum Mose loquentem ministrum Dei fuisse, 456. b. Promissiones legis ad sola terrena restringunt, 473. b. per proximum tantùm amicos intelligunt, 504. a. eorum de Tabulis Decalogi fabulæ, 512. b. contradictorias Rabbinorum sententias utrasque veras esse asserunt, 615. b. in legis ritualis observantia justitiam quærunt, 648. b. ceremonias legales nullam habere significationem mysticam; item, Legem ceremonialem non esse abrogatam, 692. b. ubi fusè refutantur, ib. Eorum blasphemiæ adversus Nativit. Jesu ex B. Virgine; Mariam adulteram dicunt, II. 1 i. b. Christum Pantherîs filium appellant, ibid 12. a. עלמה conjugem esse pertendunt, 12. a. b. Stadæ & Pandiræ filium esse blasphemant, ibid. Verba Prophetiæ de Christo enervare aut eradere, quàm credere malunt, 18. b. annum Nativitatis Christi octoginta novem annis serius constituunt, quàm Christiani, 24. b. stygius liber Toldus Jeschu arguitur, 25. a. quem VVagenseilius confutavit, ibid. Judæorum veterum de miraculis Christi testimonia, 97. a. regnum Messiæ temporale & terrenum statuunt, 133. a. eorum argumenta diluuntur, 134. a. 138. a. Messiam geminum obtrudunt, ibid. commenti hujus absurditas, ibid. b. Eorum exceptio, quòd populi peccata Messiæ adventum retardent, eliditur, 143. quale fingant Regnum Messiæ, 144. 145. eorum argumenta Messiæ adventui oppositi diluuntur, 148. probrosa vocis Evangelii detorsio, 155. a. Nov. Testamentum promissum esse negant, 158. b. ipsum fœdus Mosaicum esse pertendunt, 159. confutantur, ibid. 160. propriam justitiam jactant, 268. b. 269. eorum error circa respiscentiam, 325. b. eorum jejunia in Vet. Test. 364. b. Regnum Messiæ pomposum sibi finxerunt, 716. a. eorum nugæ, de resurrectione carnis futura, 735. b. eorundem argumenta refutantur, 741. resurrectionem in terra Canaan futuram esse nugantur, 741. b. pœnarum infernalium æternitatem negant, 763. b. eorum argumenta refelluntur, 764.
units.tr: Jews: their present religion is false, I. 6. b. They have preserved Scripture entire, 27. b. Their division of the Old Testament into Torah, Prophets and Writings is not approved, 34. a. From where did the error about the oral law arise? 41. a. The Kabbalah and the Talmud, ib. b. On the Traditions, 43. Their error about the tree of life, 326. a. Those who claim that the polity is to be restored at some time are refuted, 738. b. They assert that angels helped God in creating man, 189. b. Their opinion about six thousand years of the world, 197. They attribute a soul or moving spirit to the stars, 209. They define the image of God in man wrongly, 236. a. They attribute a good and an evil angel to every man, 281. b. They believed that there are ghosts, 297. a. They pervert the promise that the Seed would crush the serpent's head, 433. a. They pervert Jacob's prophecy about Shiloh, 433. b. They hold that the patriarchs had only natural religion, under the [חודי], 437. They claim that sacrifices conferred righteousness, 446. b. They claim that the angel who spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai was a minister of God, 456. b. They restrict the promises of the law to earthly things alone, 473. b. They understand "neighbour" only as friends, 504. a. Their fables about the tables of the Decalogue, 512. b. They assert that the contradictory opinions of the rabbis are all true, 615. b. They seek justification in observance of the ritual law, 648. b. They hold that the legal ceremonies have no mystical significance, and that the ceremonial law has not been abrogated, 692. b., where these are fully refuted, ib. Their blasphemies against the nativity of Jesus from the Blessed Virgin: they call Mary an adulteress, II. 11. b. They call Christ the son of Pantheras, ibid. 12. a. They contend that [עלמה] means a wife, 12. a. b. They blaspheme that he is the son of Stada and Pandira, ibid. They prefer to weaken or erase the prophetic words about Christ rather than believe them, 18. b. They date the year of Christ's birth eighty-nine years later than the Christians do, 24. b. The infamous book Toldoth Jeschu is refuted, 25. a., which Wagenseil refuted, ibid. The testimonies of the ancient Jews concerning Christ's miracles, 97. a. They hold the kingdom of the Messiah to be temporal and earthly, 133. a. Their arguments are answered, 134. a. 138. a. They foist a twofold Messiah upon us, ibid.; the absurdity of this invention, ibid. b. Their objection, that the sins of the people delay the Messiah's coming, is refuted, 143. What kind of kingdom of the Messiah they imagine, 144. 145. Their arguments against the Messiah's coming are answered, 148. Their shameful twisting of the word "gospel", 155. a. They deny that the New Testament was promised, 158. b. They maintain that the Mosaic covenant itself is the new one, 159; refuted, ibid. 160. They boast of their own righteousness, 268. b. 269. Their error concerning repentance, 325. b. Their fasts in the Old Testament, 364. b. They invented for themselves a pompous kingdom of the Messiah, 716. a. Their trifles about the future resurrection of the flesh, 735. b. Their arguments on the same point are refuted, 741. They babble that the resurrection will take place in the land of Canaan, 741. b. They deny the eternity of infernal punishments, 763. b. Their arguments are refuted, 764.

units.la: Judæorum conversio confessionibus publicis non definitur, II. 721. problema est, ibid. eorum ταμεῖον quando cessatura? 722. b.
units.tr: The conversion of the Jews is not defined in public confessions, II. 721; it is a problem, ibid. When will their veil [ταμεῖον] cease? 722. b.

units.la: Judaicæ Ecclesiæ קנאים Seniores, quales olim fuerint? II. 580. b.
units.tr: The elders [קנאים] of the Jewish Church: what were they like formerly? II. 580. b.

units.la: Judaizantes, qui Politiæ Judaicæ restitutionem somniant, refelluntur, 738. b. 739.
units.tr: Judaizers, who dream of the restoration of the Jewish polity, are refuted, 738. b. 739.

units.la: Judex controversiarum ipsa Scriptura, non Papa aut Ecclesia est, I. 54. 55.
units.tr: The judge of controversies is Scripture itself, not the Pope or the Church, I. 54. 55.

units.la: Judicium Scripturæ infallibile est, I. 54. a. Judicium discretionis singulis fidelibus competit, 57. a. ejus norma sola Scriptura est, ibid. 58. a. non est ιδία ι. πλάνης, 59. a.
units.tr: The judgment of Scripture is infallible, I. 54. a. The judgment of discernment belongs to individual believers, 57. a. Its sole norm is Scripture, ibid. 58. a. It is not a private error [ἰδία πλάνη], 59. a.

units.la: Judicium temerarium quid? I. 566. a.
units.tr: What is rash judgment? I. 566. a.

units.la: Judiciorum etiam capitalium administratio necessaria est, II. 613. b. penes Magistratum est, ibid. 614. contra Anabaptistas vindicatur, ibid. b. in judiciis quibus personis veritatis studium incumbat, I. 636. b. Judicia publica Hebræorum trium generum fuerunt, 710. b. quo ordine fuerint administrata, 711. a. Christus in Judicio damnari debuit, II. 46. a.
units.tr: The administration of judgments, even capital ones, is necessary, II. 613. b. It rests with the magistrate, ibid. 614. It is vindicated against the Anabaptists, ibid. b. In judgments, to which persons does the study of truth belong? I. 636. b. Public judgments among the Hebrews were of three kinds, 710. b. In what order they were administered, 711. a. Christ had to be condemned in judgment, II. 46. a.

units.la: Judiciis Dei boni juxtà atque mali involvuntur, I. 100. b.
units.tr: The judgments of God, good as well as evil, are involved, I. 100. b.

units.la: Judicialem Potestatem Papa falsò sibi arrogat, II. 647. a. ejusdem iniquitas ostenditur, 648. a. argumenta pro eodem ad partes vocantur, 648. b.
units.tr: The Pope falsely arrogates judicial power to himself, II. 647. a. Its iniquity is shown, 648. a. Arguments in its favour are brought forward, 648. b.

units.la: Judicialis Lex definitur, I. 700. a. Deo Authori acceptä refertur, ibid. b. triplex ejus usus explicatur, 737. b. quo respectu & quatenus in Nov. Test. abrogata sit? 738. a. rationes pro immutabilitate ejus diluuntur, 739. a.
units.tr: Judicial law is defined, I. 700. a. It is referred to God as its author, ibid. b. Its threefold use is explained, 737. b. In what respect, and how far, it was abrogated in the New Testament, 738. a. The arguments for its immutability are answered, 739. a.

units.la: Judicium ultimum in adventu Domini probatur; de eodem vaticinia Veterum, II. 716. tempus ejus in Scriptura definitum non est, 718. a. signa id prænuntiantia in Scriptura quædam describuntur, ibid. b, generalia, 719. specialia, 720. 721. de eo Gentilium um sententia, 745. b. Universale erit vivorum & mortuorum, 744. a. 747. a. cujus futuri veritas demonstratur, ibid. b. 745. & contra infideles Veteres & novos, Socinianos imprimis vindicatur, ib. b. à Deo Triuno habebitur, 746. præparatio ad Judicium in quo consistat, 747. seq. judicii administratio in quo consistat, 748. a. ejus tempus & locus, 749. b.
units.tr: The final judgment at the Lord's coming is proved; the prophecies of the ancients concerning it, II. 716. Its time is not defined in Scripture, 718. a. Certain signs foretelling it are described in Scripture, ibid. b; general signs, 719; special signs, 720. 721. The opinion of the Gentiles about it, 745. b. It will be universal, of the living and the dead, 744. a. 747. a. The truth of its future coming is demonstrated, ibid. b. 745, and it is vindicated against unbelievers, ancient and modern, and above all the Socinians, ib. b. It will be held by the triune God, 746. What preparation for judgment consists in, 747 f. What the administration of judgment consists in, 748. a. Its time and place, 749. b.

units.la: Juramenta, quibus Deus promissiones suas confirmat, I, 385. b. Juramentum Dei, quo fœdus seu Testamentum gratiæ firmavit. 391. b. Juramentum Dei quid sit? II.80. a.
units.tr: The oaths by which God confirms his promises, I. 385. b. God's oath by which he confirmed the covenant or testament of grace, 391. b. What is God's oath? II. 80. a.

units.la: Juramentum, ejus origo, I. 543. a. usus licitus, ib. contra Pelagium, Anabaptistas & Pontificios asseritur, ib. Legitimi conditiones, 544. a. leges ejus reliquæ, ib. b. Personæ, quibus Juramentum imponi potest, 545. a. Forma & ritus, quales esse debeant? ib. b. ejus vis ad obligandum jurantem, 546. a. ejusdem distinctiones variæ, ib. b. Idololatrarum admittenda cur? 539. b. de Juramento notatur Grotius, 546. b. Promissiorum an licitum sit? ib.
units.tr: The oath: its origin, I. 543. a. Its lawful use, ib.; asserted against Pelagius, the Anabaptists and the Papists, ib. The conditions of a lawful oath, 544. a. Its other laws, ib. b. The persons to whom an oath may be imposed, 545. a. Its form and rite: what should they be? ib. b. Its force to bind the one swearing, 546. a. Its various distinctions, ib. b. Why are idolaters admitted? 539. b. Grotius is noted concerning the oath, 546. b. Is it lawful to swear to promises? ib.

units.la: Jus naturale à Gentilibus & Grotio male describitur, I.309. a. quid sit? 310. b.
units.tr: Natural law is wrongly described by the Gentiles and by Grotius, I. 309. a. What is it? 310. b.

units.la: Jus vocandi Ministros toti Ecclesiæ & singulis ejus membris competit, II.568. a.
units.tr: The right to call ministers belongs to the whole Church and to each of its individual members, II. 568. a.

units.la: Jus Patronatus an, & quomodo in Nov. Test. tolerari possit? II.568. b.
units.tr: Whether, and how, the right of patronage can be tolerated in the New Testament, II. 568. b.

units.la: Justificatio. vide Breviar. ejus definitio, I.264. b. causa, 265. 266. divisio in primam & secundam rejicitur, 299. a. 301 b. finis, 302. a. est alia peccatoris, alia justi, 303. vide Breviar. S.Pauli & S. Jacobi conciliatio, ibid.304. b. effecta, 306. a. fructus, 309. b.
units.tr: Justification: see the Breviary. Its definition, I. 264. b. Its cause, 265. 266. The division into first and second justification is rejected, 299. a. 301. b. Its end, 302. a. There is one justification of the sinner, another of the righteous, 303. See the Breviary. The reconciliation of Paul and James, ibid. 304. b. Its effects, 306. a. Its fruit, 309. b.

units.la: Justificatio Legalis quid? I.,24. a. ex operibus cum foedere gratiæ non subsistit, 385. a.
units.tr: Justificatio Legalis: what is it? It does not stand with works under the covenant of grace, I.24 a; 385 a.

units.la: Justificatio Abrahami ex fide, I. 432. a.
units.tr: Justificatio of Abraham by faith, I.432 a.

units.la: Justificationis (sub Vet. & Nov.Test.discrimen, II, 173. b. justificandi hominis status internus vel externus, 265. a. Justificatio peccatoris irrevocabilis est, 397. in hac vita fit, 741. a.
units.tr: Justificationis difference under the Old and New Testament, II.173 b. The justified man's status, internal or external, 265 a. The justification of the sinner is irrevocable, 397. It takes place in this life, 741 a.

units.la: Justitia Dei, I.95. a. particularis, 97. b. judicialis, 98. a. punitiva, ibid. b. 99. gubernans, 100. b. Justitia Dei essentialis innocentem non punit, 321 b.
units.tr: Justitia of God, I.95 a. particular, 97 b. judicial, 98 a. punitive, ibid. b. 99. governing, 100 b. The essential justice of God does not punish the innocent, 321 b.

units.la: Justitia Christi tam activa, quam passiva nobis imputatur, I. 283. b seqq.
units.tr: Justitia of Christ, both active and passive, is imputed to us, I.283 b ff.

units.la: Justitia humana ultrix, I.583. a.
units.tr: Justitia human, avenging, I.583 a.

units.la: Justitia originalis primi hominis, 224. vide Rectitudo.
units.tr: Justitia original, of the first man, 224. See Rectitudo.

units.la: Justitia inhærens & infusa post lapsum nulla est, I.268, 269. 271. 273. sola illa Christi nos justificat, 274. a. quomodo nostra fiat; ibid. imputatione, 275. non essentialis, sed legalis Christi Mediatoris Justitia credentibus imputatur, 285. a. Legalis cur δικαιώμα dicatur? 316. a. ejus perfectio triplex explicatur, 316. b. quomodo ex Justitia vita æterna piis tribuatur? II.337. 338.
units.tr: Justitia inherent and infused, after the fall, is none; I.268, 269, 271, 273. Only that of Christ justifies us, 274 a. How it becomes ours, ibid.; by imputation, 275. The legal, not the essential, justice of Christ the Mediator is imputed to believers, 285 a. Why is legal justice called δικαίωμα [dikaioma]? 316 a. Its perfection is explained threefold, 316 b. How is eternal life granted to the pious from justice? II.337, 338.

units.la: Justitiam fidelium non ex operibus legis, sed ex fide Justitiam Christi apprehendente esse, ex Prophetarum consensu probatur, I. 478. b. ex Legis ritualis observantia frustra à Judæis quæsita, 648. b.
units.tr: Justitiam of the faithful is from faith laying hold of the justice of Christ, not from works of the law; this is proved from the agreement of the Prophets, I.478 b. Sought in vain by the Jews from observance of the ritual law, 648 b.

units.la: Justitia fidei per mortem Christi, II.173. a.
units.tr: Justitia of faith through the death of Christ, II.173 a.

units.la: Justitia simulata Pharisæorum à Christo arguitur, II, 91. a. b.
units.tr: Justitia feigned, of the Pharisees, is rebuked by Christ, II.91 a b.

units.la: Justus, Ezech.XVIII.24. qualis intelligatur? I. 403. a. justi & injusti quomodo sibi ipsis opponantur? II. 741. a. justi seu justificati an, & quomodo sint judicandi? 747. b.
units.tr: Justus, Ezek. 18.24: how is it to be understood? I.403 a. How are the just and the unjust opposed to one another? II.741 a. Are the just or the justified to be judged, and if so, how? 747 b.

units.la: Juvencus piacularis quando immolari consueverit? I. 658. b.
units.tr: Juvencus piacular: when was it customarily sacrificed? I.658 b.

units.la: Juventutis institutio in religione V.D.Ministris præcipue incumbit, II.597. b.
units.tr: Juventutis instruction in religion chiefly rests upon the ministers of the divine Word, II.597 b.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: Laborandum est cuique in sua vocatione, I. 607. a. Laborantes in sermone & doctrina quinam sint? II.579. a.
units.tr: Every person must labour in his own calling, I. 607. a. Who are those labouring in the word and doctrine? II. 579. a.

units.la: Labrum æneum in Templo Hierosol. quid significaverit? I.681.
units.tr: What did the bronze laver in the Temple at Jerusalem signify? I.681.

units.la: Lætitia spiritualis, I.521. a. fidelium, II.182. b. etiam in afflictionibus, 183.
units.tr: Spiritual joy, I.521. a. of the faithful, II.182. b. also in afflictions, 183.

units.la: Lætitia ineffabilis vitæ æternæ, II.778. b. eâque in solo Deo, 779. a.
units.tr: The ineffable joy of eternal life, II.778. b. and this is found in God alone, 779. a.

units.la: Laici calice in Eucharistia non sunt privandi, II. 468. fusius probatur, 470. b. 471. Pontificii refelluntur, ibid.
units.tr: The laity are not to be deprived of the cup in the Eucharist; II.468. More fully proved, 470. b. 471. The Papists are refuted, ibid.

units.la: Ἀμφιάραος, πυρρακαλυξάντων τὸν Χριστόν, quid? II.152. b.
units.tr: Amphiaraus [Ἀμφιάραος]; "those who set Christ on fire" [πυρρακαλυξάντων τὸν Χριστόν]: what is meant? II.152. b.

units.la: Laodicenum Concilium Nov. Test. Libros recenset, I. 39. b. ad Laodicenses Epistola nulla fuit, ibid. 40. a.
units.tr: The Council of Laodicea lists the books of the New Testament, I. 39. b. There was no epistle to the Laodiceans, ibid. 40. a.

units.la: Lapidatione quæ crimina expiabantur? I.711. b. quomodo facta fuerit? 712. a.
units.tr: By stoning, which crimes were expiated? I.711. b. How was it carried out? 712. a.

units.la: Lapsus Protoplastorum, vide Peccatum & Breviar. quomodo posteris imputatus sit, I.340. seq.
units.tr: The fall of the first parents: see Sin and Breviary. How was it imputed to their posterity? I.340 seq.

units.la: Lascivia in mente & corpore fœda est, I. 96.
units.tr: Lasciviousness is base in mind and body, I.96.

units.la: Λατρεία nomen omnium Paparum est, II.689. b.
units.tr: Latreia [Λατρεία] is the name of all the Popes, II.689. b.

units.la: Latinorum Symbolo Constantinopolitano addentium Filioque Elenchus, I. 139. a.
units.tr: A refutation of the Latins who add the Filioque to the Constantinopolitan Creed, I. 139. a.

units.la: Latinæ Linguæ in Cultu Divino usus quando cœperit? II. 433. a.
units.tr: When did the use of the Latin language in divine worship begin? II.433. a.

units.la: Λατρεύειν & δουλεύειν quomodo differant? I,514; b.
units.tr: How do λατρεύειν and δουλεύειν differ? I.514. b.

units.la: Latria in Imagine terminatur, I.536. a.
units.tr: Latria terminates in the image, I.536. a.

units.la: Latrones famosi Nephilim, Nimrod, Saraceni, Scythæ, Nomades, Cingari, Tartari, Arabes, &c. I. 609.
units.tr: Famous robbers: the Nephilim, Nimrod, the Saracens, Scythians, Nomads, Gypsies, Tartars, Arabs, etc. I.609.

units.la: Latrocinium quid? I.609. a. unde ortum? ib. b.
units.tr: What is robbery? I.609. a. Whence did it arise? ib. b.

units.la: Lectio. Lectiones variantes Script. Vet.Test. corruptionem non arguunt, I. 36. a. Scripturæ in vernacula lingua omnibus permittenda, 52. a. b.
units.tr: Reading. Variant readings of the Old Testament Scripture do not prove corruption, I.36. a. Scripture is to be permitted to everyone in the vernacular tongue, 52. a. b.

units.la: Lectores in Ecclesia Rom. quinam sint? II.663. b.
units.tr: Who are the readers in the Roman Church? II.663. b.

units.la: Lepra Hebraeorum, ejusque impuritas, I.672. a. Spiritualis, 690. b. purificatio leprosi, 691. a.
units.tr: The leprosy of the Hebrews, and its uncleanness, I.672. a. Spiritual leprosy, 690. b. The purification of the leper, 691. a.

units.la: Leviratus Hebraeorum jus explicatur, I.722. a.
units.tr: The Hebrew law of levirate marriage is explained, I.722. a.

units.la: Levita. Eorum tribes XLVIII. fuerunt, I.664. b. eorum munus quale? 670. consecratio, ibid. b, mysterium, 688. b.
units.tr: Levites. There were forty-eight Levitical cities, I.664. b. What was their office? 670. Consecration, ibid. b. Mystery, 688. b.

units.la: Levitici Sacerdotii à Christi differentia, II, 104. a.
units.tr: The difference between the Levitical priesthood and Christ's, II.104. a.

units.la: Lex oralis Judæorum quid? & unde orta? I.41. b. Legem Christus nostro loco implevit, 284. b. 285. Lex Divina boni operis norma esse debet, 328. b. Leges Vet. Test. quatenus fuerint carnales? 411. b. Lex Dei per Mosen lata quotuplex? 461. b. seq. non mera lex fidei, nec operum, nec utriusque mixtura, 462. ejus severitatis finis, 463. a. duplex χάρις, ibid. b. Lex carnalis præcepti cur data? 466. a. legales sententiæ, cur Israelitis obnuntiatæ? 467. Legis subintroductæ duplex facies, Legalis & Evang. ibid. quomodo pædagogus fuerit ad Christum, ibid. b. quomodo per Angelos data dicatur? 456. b. quomodo iram operetur? 469. b, Leges Mosaicæ quotuplices? 500. a. Legis naturalis, moralis & Decalogi distinctio, ibid. Leges Mosaicas mutabiles ab immutabilibus discernendi regulæ, 740. a. Legum immutabilium dignoscendarum certa criteria statuuntur, 741. a. Leges forenses immutabiles Mosaicæ, qua cum cautione sint servandæ? 742. Legi subjectus quomodo Christus fuerit? II.37. b. Lex non Evangelium litera occidens est, II. 185. a. justo non posita, I.308. b. spiritualis est, 313. b.
units.tr: What is the oral law of the Jews, and whence did it arise? I.41. b. Christ fulfilled the law in our place, 284. b. 285. The divine law ought to be the rule of good works, 328. b. In what respect were the Old Testament laws carnal? 411. b. How many kinds of the divine law were given through Moses? 461. b. seq. It is not a mere law of faith, nor of works, nor a mixture of both, 462. The end of its severity, 463. a. The twofold grace, ibid. b. Why was the carnal law of precept given? 466. a. Why were the legal sentences announced to the Israelites? 467. The twofold face of the introduced law, legal and evangelical, ibid. How was it a pedagogue to Christ? ibid. b. In what sense is it said to have been given through angels? 456. b. How does it work wrath? 469. b. How many kinds of Mosaic laws are there? 500. a. The distinction between natural law, moral law and the Decalogue, ibid. Rules for distinguishing the mutable Mosaic laws from the immutable, 740. a. Sure criteria for recognising immutable laws are laid down, 741. a. The immutable forensic Mosaic laws: with what caution are they to be observed? 742. How was Christ subject to the law? II.37. b. The law is not the Gospel; it is the letter that kills, II.185. a. Not laid down for the just, I.308. b. It is spiritual, 313. b.

units.la: Lex naturæ qualis sit, & quomodo vel accusetur vel defendat? I. 5. a.
units.tr: What is the law of nature, and how may it be either accused or defended? I.5. a.

units.la: Lex Dei naturalis homini concreata, I, 308. b. Lex unde dicta, 309. a. definitur & explicatur, 310. b. malè à veteribus gentilibus & Hobbesio, 311. est vel archetypa & æterna, vel ectypa & tradita in tempore, 310. a. a. vide Brev. ejus dictatum unde cognoscatur? 312. b. compendium ejus in Decalogo, 313. a. ejus præcipua capita in naturali Dei sanctitate fundantur, 314. immutabilis est, ibid. Lex positiva quid? 315. a.
units.tr: The law of God, naturally implanted in man, I.308. b. The word lex: whence it is named, 309. a. It is defined and explained, 310. b. Badly handled by the ancient heathens and by Hobbes, 311. It is either archetypal and eternal, or ectypal and delivered in time, 310. a. See Brev. Whence is its dictate known? 312. b. Its summary is in the Decalogue, 313. a. Its principal heads are grounded in God's natural holiness, 314. It is immutable, ibid. What is positive law? 315. a.

units.la: Legis Moralis præcipuus usus explicatur, I.643. b.
units.tr: The principal use of the moral law is explained, I.643. b.

units.la: Lex Ritualis seu rituum qualia præcepta continet? I.647. a. rationes ejus institutionis.647. b. Diversa ejus sub Patriarchis & Mose ratio, ib, 648. a. ejus evolvendæ regulæ, 649. a.
units.tr: What precepts does the ritual law, or the law of rites, contain? I.647. a. The reasons for its institution, 647. b. Its different arrangement under the patriarchs and under Moses, ib., 648. a. Rules for unfolding it, 649. a.

units.la: Legis Ceremonialis abolitio adversus Judæos demonstratur, I.692. b. variis argumentis evincitur, 693, 694. fusius, 695. b. 696. a. ejus finalis abolitio ostenditur, 697. 698. quando illa Lex viguerit, languere cœperit, cessaverit, ac denique antiquata de jure & de facto fuerit, 696.697. a. 698. a.
units.tr: The abolition of the ceremonial law is demonstrated against the Jews, I.692. b. It is proved by various arguments, 693, 694; more fully, 695. b. 696. a. Its final abolition is shown, 697, 698. When that law was in force, when it began to decline, when it ceased, and when at last it became obsolete both in law and in fact, 696, 697. a. 698. a.

units.la: Lex Mosis Judicialis definitur, I. 700. a. Deo authori accepta referitur, ib. b.
units.tr: The Mosaic judicial law is defined, I.700. a. It is referred to God as its author, ib. b.

units.la: Lex Politica an, & quando delicta fuere & abrogari debeat? II.666. a.
units.tr: Whether and when the political law of Moses dealt with crimes and ought to be abrogated, II.666. a.

units.la: Leges Mosis Politicæ tum pacis tum belli, I.732. b.
units.tr: The political laws of Moses, both of peace and of war, I.732. b.

units.la: Lex Christi in Nov. Test. an sit Legis Mosaicæ perfectio, correctio? I.411. a. qualis sit in Nov. Test? II. 161. a. non est lex operum, 162. b. uberius explicatur, 163. b.
units.tr: Is Christ's law in the New Testament the perfection or the correction of the Mosaic law? I.411. a. What kind of law is it in the New Testament? II.161. a. It is not a law of works, 162. b. More fully explained, 163. b.

units.la: Legum authoritas est vel latarum vel ferendarum, II; 644. b. 645.
units.tr: The authority of laws is either that of laws already enacted or of laws yet to be enacted, II.644. b. 645.

units.la: Legislationis Sinaiticæ historia, I.461. a.
units.tr: The history of the legislation at Sinai, I.461. a.

units.la: Legislatio ad summum Magistratum pertinet, II.623. a.
units.tr: Legislation belongs to the supreme magistrate, II.623. a.

units.la: Legislator, Christus quo sensu fuerit, II. 90. a. non nonnam
units.tr: Lawgiver: in what sense Christ was one, II.90. a.

units.la: vam tulit legem,91.92. nec mutavit,92. b. Legis-latoria potestas Principalis Papæ non competit, 644. a cum potestate dominante & principatu conjuncta non est,645. b.
units.tr: he did not bring a new law, 91, 92; nor did he change it, 92. b. The legislative power does not belong to the Pope as his principal power; it is not joined with ruling power and principality, 644. a. 645. b.

units.la: Legislatorum veterum astutia, quâ à Diis leges se accepisse finxerunt,1.700. b.
units.tr: The cunning of the ancient lawgivers, by which they pretended that they had received their laws from the gods, I.700. b.

units.la: Libamina Vet. Test. quomodo Typus fuerint passionum Christi & fidelium? I. 674. b.
units.tr: How were the libations of the Old Testament types of the sufferings of Christ and of the faithful? I.674. b.

units.la: Liber Legis Mosis aliquando totam Vet.Test.Scripturam notat, 1.35. b.
units.tr: The book of the law of Moses sometimes denotes the whole Scripture of the Old Testament, I.35. b.

units.la: Liber vitæ, quid sit deleri è Libro vitæ ? I.170. b.
units.tr: The book of life: what does it mean to be blotted out of the Book of Life? I.170. b.

units.la: Liberi, Eorum officium erga Parentes in quo consistat? 1.564. b. 570. parentibus contraria mandantibus quid faciendum ? 571. a. insciis & invitis parentibus nubere non debent, ibid. b.
units.tr: Children: in what does their duty towards their parents consist? I.564. b. 570. What is to be done when parents command contrary things? 571. a. They ought not to marry without, or against, the wishes of their parents, ibid. b.

units.la: Liberalitas qualis virtus ? 1.617. a. ejus officium declaratur,618. a. quid in ea spectandum? ibid. b.
units.tr: Liberality: what sort of virtue is it? I.617. a. Its duty is declared, 618. a. What is to be considered in it? ibid. b.

units.la: Libertas quid ? 227. b.
units.tr: What is liberty? 227. b.

units.la: Libertas Voluntatis Dei non in indifferentia consistit, I. 93. a. voluntatis creatæ non est independens à Dei determinatione, 166. b.
units.tr: The liberty of God's will does not consist in indifference, I.93. a. The liberty of the created will is not independent of God's determination, 166. b.

units.la: Libertas spiritualis quid? & quotuplex ? 1. 308. Christiana tribus regulis dirigitur, ibid. b. ea prudenter utendum, 563. a.
units.tr: Spiritual liberty: what is it, and how many kinds are there? I.308. Christian liberty is governed by three rules, ibid. b. It is to be used prudently, 563. a.

units.la: Libertas Nov. Test. II. 178. b. in quibus consistat? ib. 179. a. 180. a. à jugo Papalium decretorum nos liberavit,645. b. 646.
units.tr: Liberty in the New Testament, II.178. b. In what does it consist? ib. 179. a. 180. a. He freed us from the yoke of the papal decrees, 645. b. 646.

units.la: Libertinorum error, nihil suâ naturâ malum esse statuentium, I. 270. eorundem error, quo respicientiæ & pietatis studium ab Evangelio removent, II. 163. 164. Spiritum regenerantem in turbulentum phantasma commutantium, 234. a. ii libertatem Christianam in libidinem convertunt, 308. b. eorum error circa respicientiam, 325. b. operum bonorum studium contemnunt, 332. b. eorum contra Ministerium Ecclesiæ cavillationes refelluntur, 360. b.
units.tr: The error of the libertines, who hold that nothing is evil by its nature, I.270. Their error by which they remove the pursuit of contrition and piety from the Gospel, II.163, 164. Those who turn the regenerating Spirit into a turbulent phantasm, II.234. a. Those who turn Christian liberty into lust, II.308. b. Their error concerning contrition, II.325. b. They despise the pursuit of good works, II.332. b. Their cavils against the ministry of the Church are refuted, II.360. b.

units.la: Liberum Arbitrium primi hominis tantùm in bono fuit, I.2 7. a. non constitit in indifferentia ad bonum & malum, ib. b. quomodo libertas illa arbitrii Providentiæ Dei subsist,I.248.249.
units.tr: The free will of the first man was good only, I.27. a. It did not consist in indifference to good and evil, ib. b. How that freedom of the will subsists alongside the providence of God, I.248, 249.

units.la: Ligare & solvere est remittere & retinere peccata, II. 589. 590. a. 605.606.
units.tr: To bind and to loose is to remit and to retain sins, II.589, 590. a. 605, 606.

units.la: Limborchius in Articulo de Justitiæ Christi imputatione, erroris convincitur,I.180. b. refutatur,282. Tractatum Dei in hominis conversione extenuans perstringitur, II. 213. a. Arminianus ille professor de Sanctorum perseverantia perversè sentiens refelluitur,I I.404. a. 405. b. 407. b.
units.tr: Limborch, in the article on the imputation of Christ's righteousness, is convicted of error, I.180. b. Refuted, 282. His treatment of God's working in the conversion of man is disparaged, II.213. a. That Arminian professor, who holds perverse views on the perseverance of the saints, is refuted, II.404. a. 405. b. 407. b.

units.la: Limbus Patrum impugnatur, I. 413. seq. est utopia, II. 52. b.
units.tr: The limbus of the Fathers is attacked, I.413 seq. It is a utopia, II.52. b.

units.la: Lingua regimen præcepto I X. mandatur, I. 611. a. Linguæ usus, ib. b. in ejus moderamine perfectio viri consistit,612. a. ejus officium in studio veracitatis, ibid.
units.tr: Tongue: its government is commanded by the ninth precept, I. 611a. The use of the tongue, ib. b. A man's perfection consists in its control, 612a. Its office lies in the pursuit of truthfulness, ibid.

units.la: Linguæ ignotæ usus in cultu publico rejicitur, II.431. Linguarum inprimis Originalium peritiæ necessitas in Doctore Ecclesiæ,II.583. b. 585. a.
units.tr: Use of an unknown tongue in public worship is rejected, II. 431. The necessity of skill in the original languages is especially for a teacher of the Church, II. 583b, 585a.

units.la: Linteæ tria adhibebantur sepeliendis cadaveribus, II. 50. b.
units.tr: Linen cloths: three were used for burying corpses, II. 50b.

units.la: R. Lipman in explicando Jacobi vaticinio arguitur, I. 434. a.
units.tr: R. Lipman is refuted in his explanation of Jacob's prophecy, I. 434a.

units.la: Lipsanolatria Pontificiorum,I.538. b.
units.tr: Lipsanolatry of the Papists, I. 538b.

units.la: Litera occidens quid sit? I.44. b. non Evangelium sed Lex est, II.185 a.
units.tr: The letter that kills: what is it? I. 44b. It is not the Gospel but the Law, II. 185a.

units.la: Liturgiarum in cultu publico usus,I I.430. a.
units.tr: Liturgies: their use in public worship, II. 430a.

units.la: Locus quid? Cœlum an in loco? I.196. a. quomodo Angeli in loco sint definiri nequit,277. locus in Nov. Test. nullus alio sacratior,351. b. Locus sacrificandi varius fuit, 663. a.
units.tr: Place: what is it? Is heaven in a place? I. 196a. How angels are in a place cannot be defined, 277. No place in the New Testament is holier than another, 351b. The place of sacrifice varied, 663a.

units.la: Localis Christi descensus ad inferos impugnatur, II. 51. b.
units.tr: Local descent of Christ into hell is impugned, II. 51b.

units.la: Locutiones Sacramentales Tropicæ sunt,II.477. b.
units.tr: Sacramental locutions are tropical, II. 477b.

units.la: Λογίζεσθαι & λόγειν an & quomodo differant ? II. 275.
units.tr: Logizesthai [λογίζεσθαι] and legein [λέγειν]: do they differ, and if so how? II. 275.

units.la: Λόγος notio Christo tributa Divinitatem ejus probat, I.128. a. cur filium Dei notet ? I I.4. a. ejus Divinitatem notat,ib. λόγῳ quomodo caro factus, 18. a. 19. b. naturam humanam in hypostasi sua sustentat,II.20.a.λόγῳ an & quo sensu subsistentiam suam carni Christi communicaverit? 28. b. ubique carni unitus præsens est. ibid. 32. a.
units.tr: The name Logos (Word) ascribed to Christ proves his divinity, I. 128a. Why does it denote the Son of God? II. 4a. It denotes his divinity, ib. How was he made flesh by the Logos? 18a, 19b. He sustains the human nature in his own hypostasis, II. 20a. Did the Logos communicate his subsistence to the flesh of Christ, and in what sense? 28b. He is present everywhere, united to the flesh, ibid. 32a.

units.la: Lojolæ Socii blasphemè se locios Jesu jactant,II.75.b.
units.tr: Members of the Society of Loyola blasphemously boast that they are the companions of Jesus, II. 75b.

units.la: Lombardia quale usurarum genus fuerit? I. 615. a.
units.tr: Lombardy: what kind of usury was it? I. 615a.

units.la: Longævitas quâ conditione à Deo promittatur? I. 259.
units.tr: Length of life: on what condition is it promised by God? I. 259.

units.la: a. Quinto præcepto promissa qualis? 573. b. quale sit Dei beneficium,574. b.
units.tr: a. What kind of promise is attached to the fifth commandment? 573b. What kind of benefit of God is it? 574b.

units.la: Longanimitas quid? I. 578. a.
units.tr: Long-suffering: what is it? I. 578a.

units.la: Loquela summa cura habenda est,I.621. b.
units.tr: Speech must be taken with the utmost care, I. 621b.

units.la: Loqui debuit Christus ceu Propheta,II.87.88.
units.tr: Christ was obliged to speak as a Prophet, II. 87, 88.

units.la: Lucifer quis sit ? I.185. b. 287. a.
units.tr: Lucifer: who is he? I. 185b, 287a.

units.la: Luci Idolorum quales fuerint? 720. b.
units.tr: Lights of idols: what kind were they? 720b.

units.la: Luctta Spiritûs cum carne,I I.234. b. 236. a. b.
units.tr: Struggle of the Spirit with the flesh, II. 234b, 236a, b.

units.la: Lucta spiritualis definitur & explicatur,I.371. a. principalis luctator est Spiritus S. ib. b. minùs principales, regeniti, ib. cum Deo,372. cum Sathana,ib. 373. a. cum mundo,ib. cum carne, ib.
units.tr: Spiritual struggle is defined and explained, I. 371a. The principal combatant is the Holy Spirit, ib. b. Less principal combatants are the regenerate, ib.; with God, 372; with Satan, ib., 373a; with the world, ib.; with the flesh, ib.

units.la: Ludi & Joci qui & quatenus licitis sint? I.632. a.
units.tr: Games and jests: which are lawful, and how far? I. 632a.

units.la: Jobus Ludolphus laudatur, II. 674. b.
units.tr: Job Ludolf is praised, II. 674b.

units.la: Lumen Propheticum an nota sit verae Ecclesiæ ? II. 551. a.
units.tr: Prophetic light: is it a mark of the true Church? II. 551a.

units.la: Luminaria magna in Creatione sunt Sol & Luna,I. 209, b. quo sensu magna sint, ib. usus,210. a.
units.tr: The great lights at creation are the sun and the moon, I. 209b. In what sense are they great? ib. Their use, 210a.

units.la: Luna qualis stella ? I.209. b.
units.tr: The moon: what kind of star is it? I. 209b.

units.la: Lupanarium usus damnatus,I.598. a.
units.tr: Brothel: its use is condemned, I. 598a.

units.la: Lustrare urbem,est illam à poena liberare,II.110. a.
units.tr: To purify a city means to free it from punishment, II. 110a.

units.la: Lutherus. Ejus Liber de servo arbitrio laudatur? II. 217. b. prophetavit, 551. a. de tollendis vel tolerandis Tyrannis quid senserit ? 622. b.
units.tr: Luther: is his book On the Bondage of the Will praised? II. 217b. He prophesied, 551a. What did he think about removing or tolerating tyrants? 622b.

units.la: Lutheran. Eorum de Decreto prædestinationis sententia,I.165. a. eorum errores & exceptiones indogmatè de communicatione Idiomatum arguuntur, II. 17. b. de ubiquitate Naturæ Christi humanæ, 30. a. de gratia vocationis universali,217. b. fidei salvificæ objectum proprium gratiam universalem objectivam & subjectivam perperam statuunt,247. b. Electos & vocatos malè distinguunt in propriè & specificè, atque improprie & generaliter hie dictos, 508. b. Sanctorum Apostasiam totalem asserunt, 402. b. in quibus circa S. Cœnæ doctrinam cum Reformatis consentiant vel dissentiant,496. a.
units.tr: Lutherans: their view on the decree of predestination, I. 165a. Their errors and exceptions are argued dogmatically on the communication of idioms, II. 17b; on the ubiquity of Christ's human nature, 30a; on the grace of universal calling, 217b. They wrongly hold that the proper object of saving faith is universal grace, both objective and subjective, 247b. They wrongly distinguish the elect and the called, properly and specifically, from those called improperly and generally, 508b. They assert the total apostasy of the saints, 402b. In what they agree or disagree with the Reformed concerning the doctrine of the Holy Supper, 496a.

units.la: Lux primigenia qualis fuerit? I.202.b. in sydera translata est,203. a.
units.tr: Primeval light: what was it like? I. 202b. It was transferred into the stars, 203a.

units.la: Luxuria quid ? I. 595. b. ejus varii gradus ,ib. in vestitu,cibo & potu,596. a. in sermone, ibid. b. in operibus, 597.
units.tr: Luxury: what is it? I. 595b. Its various degrees, ib. In clothing, food and drink, 596a. In speech, ibid. b. In works, 597.

units.la: Lycanthropiæ figmentum refellitur, I. 291. a.
units.tr: The fiction of lycanthropy is refuted, I. 291a.

units.la: Lyserus Polygamiæ defensor,I.231.
units.tr: Lyserus, defender of polygamy, I. 231.

units.la: Λύτρον etiam in poenæ infictione locum habet,II. 110. a. Λυτρῶν & Lustrare iidem sunt, ibid.
units.tr: Lytron [λύτρον] also has a place in the infliction of punishment, II. 110a. Lytron and lustrare are the same, ibid. ## M.

units.la: M.
Macchabæus (Judas) non jussit sacrificari pro mortuis,II 702. a.
units.tr: Maccabeus (Judas) did not order sacrifice to be offered for the dead, II. 702a.

units.la: Machiavellus tyrannidem & cæcam obedientiam propugnans refellitur,I I. 620. b. argumenta ejus refutantur,621. a.
units.tr: Machiavelli, who defends tyranny and blind obedience, is refuted, II. 620b. His arguments are refuted, 621a.

units.la: Magi qui olim fuerint,qui postmodum,I.291. b. Magia quid.293. vide Breviar. converti posse,295. b. eorum poena Divinitus posita,qualis? 715.b.
units.tr: Magi: who they were formerly and who afterwards, I. 291b. Magic: what is it? 293. See Breviary. Can magi be converted? 295b. What kind of punishment did God appoint for them? 715b.

units.la: Magiam artesque magicas Christus vehementer detestatur,I I.98. a.
units.tr: Christ vehemently detests magic and magical arts, II. 98a.

units.la: Magistratus. Ejus origo Divina est, II. 616. b. omnis ejus potestas à Deo est,617. a. progressus illius potestatis inde à principio,ibid. b. ei non competit absoluta potestas quidvis faciendi,618. a. quatenus ei sit obediendum,ibid. Objectionibus Pontificiorum & Anabaptistarum occurritur, 619. b. Christianis Magistratu fungi licet, 620. a. ejus potestas in legibus ferendis,623. a.& in judiciis capitalibus administrandis, ibid. b. ei inprimis Ecclesiæ & religionis cura incumbit,I I.625, a. ejus potestas circa religionem difficulter definitur. ibid. 626. leq. Objectiones contrariæ diluuntur, 627. qualis ei potestas in Ecclesiam competat,ostenditur,628. b. in quæ eidem potestas nulla competat, ostenditur, 630. a. ejusdem partes præcipuæ edisseruntur,632. a. cuia Ecclesiæ magistratui incumbens generaliter exponitur,631. b. ejus officium circa conversionem errantium & prophetandi libertatem,634. a. quomodo in judicandis & corrigendis erantibus versari debeat ,635. a. Ejus officium duplex, 1.615. b. quatenus Ecclesiæ regimini subsit, ibid. seq. 595. b. Clavium potestas an , & quatenus ad eum pertineat? 606. b. Magistratuum, requisita, 704. a. primum requisitum est Timor Dei, ibid. patentum vicem sustinet,571. b.
units.tr: Magistrate. Its origin is divine, II. 616b. All its power is from God, 617a. The progress of that power from the beginning, ibid. b. It does not have absolute power to do whatever it likes, 618a. How far it is to be obeyed, ibid. Objections of the Papists and Anabaptists are met, 619b. Christians may hold the office of magistrate, 620a. Its power in enacting laws, 623a, and in administering capital judgments, ibid. b. Care of the Church and of religion rests above all with it, II. 625a. Its power in religious matters is hard to define, ibid., 626 seq. Contrary objections are answered, 627. What power it has over the Church is shown, 628b. Over what matters it has no power is shown, 630a. Its principal parts are set out, 632a. Its duty concerning the Church is set out in general terms, 631b. Its office regarding the conversion of those in error and the freedom to prophesy, 634a. How it should deal with judging and correcting those in error, 635a. Its office is twofold, I. 615b. How far it is subject to the government of the Church, ibid. seq., 595b. Whether and how far the power of the keys belongs to it, 606b. Requisites of magistrates, 704a. The first requisite is the fear of God, ibid. It takes the place of parents, 571b.

units.la: Magnanimitas qualis virtus ? I.566. a.
units.tr: Magnanimity: what kind of virtue is it? I. 566a.

units.la: Magnificentia non est virtus,I.620. a.
units.tr: Magnificence is not a virtue, I. 620a.

units.la: Majmonides in explicatione loci, Genes.4.26. notatur, I.437. I.437. a. alibi laudatur, II.145. b.
units.tr: Maimonides is noted in his explanation of Gen. 4.26, I. 437a. He is praised elsewhere, II. 145b.

units.la: Malachias Canonem V. T. clausit inde sigillum Prophetarum audit, I.35. a. 37. b.
units.tr: Malachi closed the canon of the Old Testament; hence he is called the seal of the prophets, I. 35a, 37b.

units.la: Maledictio, qui sub lege vixerunt, quomodo sub maledictione fuerint? I.469. b.
units.tr: Curse: how were those who lived under the law under the curse? I. 469b.

units.la: Mali & mala, boni & bona distinguenda, I.245. b. mali bonis mixti sunt in externa Ecclesia, II. 523. b.
units.tr: Evil and evils, good and goods must be distinguished, I. 245b. Evil people are mixed with good in the external Church, II. 523b.

units.la: Malum. Mali causa quaenam sit, I.133. a. quomodo Deus decreverit, I.154. a. quomodo regat & gubernet, 261. b. iis penitus carere aeternae felicitatis pars est, II.771. a.
units.tr: Evil: what is the cause of evil? I. 133a. How did God decree it? I. 154a. How does he govern and rule it? 261b. To be wholly free of it is part of eternal happiness, II. 771a.

units.la: Malus & capitalis hostis est Sathanas, I.359. a.
units.tr: The evil and chief enemy is Satan, I. 359a.

units.la: Mandata sua Deus ipse in nobis operatur, II.230. a. Christi qualia sint, & quomodo servanda? 91. a. a. Ecclesiae, quatenus obligent, 644. b. 645. a.
units.tr: Commandments: God himself works his own commandments in us, II. 230a. Of what kind are Christ's commandments, and how are they to be kept? 91a. The commandments of the Church, insofar as they bind, 644b, 645a.

units.la: Manducatio panis Eucharistici cur necessaria, II.466. b. Corporis Christi in S. Coena non corporalis, sed spiritualis est, 493. 494. a. indigne manducantium reatus, 495. b.
units.tr: Eating: why is eating the Eucharistic bread necessary? II. 466b. The eating of the body of Christ in the Lord's Supper is not bodily but spiritual, 493, 494a. The guilt of those who eat unworthily, 495b.

units.la: Manichaei liberum primi hominis arbitrium negarunt, I.227. b. Deum malum statuentes refelluntur, 269. 270. a. in S. Coenae usu an vino abstinuerint? II. 472. b.
units.tr: Manichaeans denied the free will of the first man, I. 227b. They are refuted for making God evil, 269, 270a. Did they abstain from wine in the use of the Supper? II. 472b.

units.la: Manifestatio Filii Dei in carne quomodo facta sit, II.4. b.
units.tr: Manifestation of the Son of God in the flesh: how was it made? II. 4b.

units.la: Manipuli spicarum oblatio quid significaverit, I. 632. a.
units.tr: Sheaves: the offering of a sheaf of ears signified what? I. 632a.

units.la: Manna in deserto typus fuit panis Eucharistici, I.491. b. de ea Judaeorum nugamenta, 192. a. typus fuit Christi, ibid. b.
units.tr: Manna in the desert was a type of the Eucharistic bread, I. 491b. The Jewish trifles about it, 192a. It was a type of Christ, ibid. b.

units.la: Mansiones in domo Patris quales Christus promiserit? II.66. a.
units.tr: Mansions in the Father's house: what did Christ promise? II. 66a.

units.la: Mansuetudo qualis virtus? I.578. a.
units.tr: Meekness: what kind of virtue is it? I. 578a.

units.la: Manum alicui implere est consecrare, I.667. b.
units.tr: To fill someone's hand is to consecrate, I. 667b.

units.la: Manuum impositio quando adhiberi, coeperit, II.571. b. a quibus fieri debeat? 572. a.
units.tr: Laying on of hands: when did it begin to be used? II. 571b. By whom should it be done? 572a.

units.la: Maria B. Virgo a peccato originali immunis non fuit, I.353. a. ejus Virginitas, II.9. b. 10. a. contra Judaeos vindicatur, 11. b. 12. a. Mater Christi ex tribu Juda & familia David, desponsata esse debuit, ib.10. a. ιχαιετηρον ib.non gratia iuhaerente plena fuit, ibid.
units.tr: Mary, the Blessed Virgin, was not free from original sin, I. 353a. Her virginity, II. 9b, 10a. Defended against the Jews, 11b, 12a. As mother of Christ from the tribe of Judah and the family of David, she had to be betrothed, ib., 10a. She was not full of inherent grace, ibid. The Greek word [ιχαιετηρον] is applied to her.

units.la: Mariti erga uxorem officium, & vicissim, I.570, a.
units.tr: Duties of a husband towards his wife, and of a wife towards her husband, I.570, a.

units.la: Marshamus Anglus notatur, II.142. a. ejus opinio de circumcisionis ritu ab Aegyptiis mutuato refellitur, I.450. a.
units.tr: Marshamus the Englishman is noted, II.142, a. His view about circumcision, supposedly borrowed from the Egyptians, is refuted, I.450, a.

units.la: Martyrium quid? I.369. b. Christi, II.101. b.
units.tr: What is martyrdom? I.369, b. Martyrdom of Christ, II.101, b.

units.la: Martyrum constantia S. Scripturae Divinitatem firmat. I.27. b.
units.tr: The steadfastness of the martyrs confirms the divinity of Holy Scripture. I.27, b.

units.la: Massaliani quinam fuerint? II.326.
units.tr: Who were the Massalians? II.326.

units.la: Massilienses seu Semipelagianorum de gratia conver-tente haeresis, I.164. b. II.215. b. de mortis Christi amplitudine error, 113. b.
units.tr: The heresy of the Massilians, or Semipelagians, concerning converting grace: I.164, b. II.215, b. Their error concerning the extent of Christ's death: II.113, b.

units.la: Masorethae puncta vocalia non invenerunt, I.36. eorum studium in Codice Hebraeo custodiendo diligentia, I.35.36. a.
units.tr: The Masorites did not invent the vowel points. I.36. Their careful labour in preserving the Hebrew codex: I.35, 36, a.

units.la: Materiarii veteres haeretici, I.186. b.
units.tr: The Materiarii, ancient heretics, I.186, b.

units.la: Materiae aeternitas contra Philosophos impugnatur, I.186. b. infoimis nulla datur, 187. a.
units.tr: The eternity of matter is attacked against the philosophers, I.186, b. No matter is given without form, I.187, a.

units.la: Μαθητής & μαθητεύειν quid sit? II.451. b.
units.tr: μαθητής and μαθητεύειν [μαθητής, μαθητεύειν]: what do they mean? II.451, b.

units.la: Matrimonii primaeva institutio, I.230. b. ei polygamia repugnat, 231. a. typus est foederis operum, 373. 374. a. fratrum & sororum Protoplastorum an incestum fuerit? 592. a. matrimonia cum gentilibus contrahere Lex vetuit, 723. a. cum Proselytis licita fuerunt, ibid. b. etiam extra tribus contrahere licuit, 724. a. Non est Sacramentum, II.502. b. quo respectu mysterium dicatur, ibid.
units.tr: The original institution of marriage, I.230, b. Polygamy is contrary to it, I.231, a. It is a type of the covenant of works, I.373, 374, a. Was the marriage of brothers and sisters among the first parents incest? I.592, a. The Law forbade marriage with Gentiles, I.723, a. Marriage with proselytes was lawful, ibid., b. It was also lawful to marry outside one's own tribe, I.724, a. It is not a sacrament, II.502, b. In what respect it is called a mystery, ibid.

units.la: Mater Christi, vid. Maria.
units.tr: Mother of Christ: see Mary.

units.la: Matris quale sit officium? I.570. b.
units.tr: What is the duty of a mother? I.570, b.

units.la: Matthaei Evangelium non fuit Hebraice a Matthaeo scriptum, I.39. a.
units.tr: The Gospel of Matthew was not written by Matthew in Hebrew, I.39, a.

units.la: Medi (Josephi) de Regno millenario opinio, I.726. refellitur, 727. a.
units.tr: The millennial kingdom: the opinion of Joseph Mede is refuted, I.726 and 727, a.

units.la: Mediator noster Christus solus est, II.79. a. secundum utramque Naturam, ibid. 80. b. non Sancti, 711. 712. a. qua talis est adorandus, 525. b. quando talis factus sit, I.379. a. Θεανθρωπος esse debuit, I.379. a. Vet. ac Novi Test. unicus est, 404. a. Foederis legalis mediator fuit tum verus, scil. Christus, tum typicus, Moses, 458. b. 459. a. Mediatoris nomen non est mediae alicujus Divinam inter & humanam naturae dignitas, II.82. a.
units.tr: Our Mediator is Christ alone, II.79, a. He is so according to both natures, ibid. and II.80, b. Not the saints, II.711, 712, a. As Mediator he is to be adored, II.525, b. When he became Mediator, I.379, a. He had to be God-man [θεάνθρωπος], I.379, a. He is the one Mediator of the Old and New Testaments, I.404, a. The Mediator of the legal covenant was both true, namely Christ, and typical, namely Moses, I.458, b. and 459, a. The name Mediator does not signify some intermediate dignity between the divine and human natures, II.82, a.

units.la: Mediatio in conciliatione partium dissidentium consistit, II.84. b.
units.tr: Mediation consists in reconciling parties who are at odds, II.84, b.

units.la: Melancholia atrae bilis cur viros magis quam foeminas corripiat? I.295. a.
units.tr: Why does black bile seize men more than women? I.295, a.

units.la: Melchisedecus quis fuerit? I.435. a. ejus sacrificium, 443. b. typus Christi fuit, 453. a. 686. a. in quibus typus Christi fuerit, II.102. seqq. 489. b.
units.tr: Who was Melchizedek? I.435, a. His sacrifice, I.443, b. He was a type of Christ, I.453, a. and 686, a. In what respects he was a type of Christ, II.102 ff. and 489, b.

units.la: Membra corporis Christi mystici qualia sint, II. 250. b.
units.tr: What are the members of the mystical body of Christ? II.250, b.

units.la: Mendacium quid? falsa ejus origo a Pseudo-Politicis ostenditur, I.622. a. cur vetitum Lege Divina, 623. a. 624. a. ejus foeditas graphice depingitur, 624. b. Historia mendacio patrocinantium, 625. b. Religiosum quale sit? II. 520. b.
units.tr: What is a lie? Its false origin is shown by the pseudo-politicians, I.622, a. Why it is forbidden by divine law, I.623, a. and 624, a. Its foulness is vividly depicted, I.624, b. History of those who defend lying, I.625, b. What is a religious lie? II.520, b.

units.la: Mendici quinam indigni, I.628. b.
units.tr: Who are the beggars who are unworthy? I.628, b.

units.la: Mens cujusvis hominis aliquam de Deo cogitationem habet, I 63. a.
units.tr: Every human mind has some thought of God, I.63, a.

units.la: Mensa non altare S. Coenae celebrandae adhibenda est, II. 473. a.
units.tr: A table, not an altar, is to be used for celebrating the Lord's Supper, II.473, a.

units.la: Mentalis reservatio Jesuitarum mendax, I.627. a. nulla in Scriptura praesidium habet, 628. b.
units.tr: The Jesuits' mental reservation is a lie, I.627, a. It has no support in Scripture, I.628, b.

units.la: Mentiri Deo quid? I. 141. b.
units.tr: What does it mean to lie to God? I.141, b.

units.la: Mercatura quid? I.611. a. Israelitis non prohibita fuit, ibid. b. ejus vitia, ibid. quomodo rite exercenda, 612. a.
units.tr: What is trade? I.611, a. It was not forbidden to the Israelites, ibid., b. Its vices, ibid. How it is to be carried on rightly, I.612, a.

units.la: Mercenarii merces prompte solvenda est, I.733. b. eorum officium, 616. a.
units.tr: Wages of hired workers must be paid promptly, I.733, b. Their duty, I.616, a.

units.la: Merces solvenda laborantibus, I.616. a. non semper praesupponit meritum, 337. a. vitae aeternae non meritoria, sed mere gratuita est, 389.
units.tr: Wages are to be paid to labourers, I.616, a. They do not always presuppose merit, I.337, a. Eternal life is not merited but is purely a gift of grace, I.389.

units.la: Mereri, Meritum, quid veteribus significent, I. 334. b. II.118. b. ejus requisita examinantur, 335. a. merita operum explodunrur, 336. a. non merentur nec ex condigno, 324. b. neque ex congruo, neque ex pacto, 336. b. ita ut vana sit omnis meriti opinio, 338.
units.tr: What do merit and to merit signify to the ancients? I.334, b. and II.118, b. Its requirements are examined, I.335, a. The merits of works are rejected, I.336, a. They merit neither by condignity, I.324, b., nor by congruity, nor by covenant, I.336, b., so that every opinion of merit is vain, I.338.

units.la: Meritum Christi immensi valoris, I.382. b. etiam sibi, ecu Ecclesiae capiti, Regi & summam meruit gloriam, 383. a. ejus efficacia tam in Veteri quam in N. Testamento, rationem suffitus habuit, 675. a. Angelis non applicatur, 279. b.
units.tr: Christ's merit is of immense value, I.382, b. He merited even for himself, as head of the Church, King, and the highest glory, I.383, a. Its efficacy in both the Old and New Testaments has taken account of the suffitus [incense]. I.675, a. It is not applied to angels, I.279, b.

units.la: Meruit Christus obedientia sua gloriam & nomen super omne nomen, II.119. b. fidelibus salutem, 120. seq. Pontificii vim ejus imminuunt, imo negant, II. 121. b.
units.tr: Christ merited by his obedience glory and the name above every name, II.119, b., and salvation for believers, II.120 ff. The Papists diminish its power, indeed deny it, II.121, b.

units.la: Messias. Ejus dignitas & Sacerdotium, quod non subest legibus Sacerdotii Aharonici, I. 695. Geminum Judaei comminiscuntur, II.138. ejus commenti absurditas demonstratur, ibid. 139. Verum Messiam jam venisse docetur, ibid. b. 140. a.
units.tr: The Messiah: his dignity and priesthood, which is not subject to the laws of the Aaronic priesthood, I.695. The Jews invent two Messiahs, II.138. The absurdity of this fiction is demonstrated, ibid. and II.139. It is taught that the true Messiah has already come, ibid., b. and II.140, a.

units.la: Μετάνοια & μετάμελεια quomodo differant, I.319. a.
units.tr: How repentance [μετάνοια] and regret [μεταμέλεια] differ, I.319, a.

units.la: Μετεμψύχωσις. Ejus origo, II.700. a. primi inventores Aegyptii, I.233. a. confutatur, II.700. a.
units.tr: Transmigration of souls [μετεμψύχωσις]: its origin, II.700, a. Its first inventors were the Egyptians, I.233, a. It is refuted, II.700, a.

units.la: Meteora etiam singulari Dei Providentiae subsunt, I. 260. a.
units.tr: Even meteors are subject to God's singular providence, I.260, a.

units.la: Methodista Pontificii consequentiarum usum in rebus sacris tollentes arguuntur, I. 13. a. b. eorum argumenta expenduntur, 14. a. articulorum fundamentalium numerum definitum requirunt, 17. a. eorum strophae circa S. Scripturae authentiam, 51. a.
units.tr: The Methodists: the Papists, who abolish the use of consequences in sacred matters, are charged, I.13, a. and b. Their arguments are weighed, I.14, a. They require a fixed number of fundamental articles, I.17, a. Their turns of argument concerning the authenticity of Holy Scripture, I.51, a.

units.la: Methodus, qua fideles de Gratia & salute certos se reddere possunt, I I.418. a.
units.tr: The method by which the faithful can make themselves certain of grace and salvation, II.418, a.

units.la: Metonymia in locutionibus Sacramentalibus usitata, I.398. b.
units.tr: Metonymy used in sacramental expressions, I.398, b.

units.la: Metropolitani quinam sint? II.671. b.
units.tr: Who are the metropolitans? II.671, b.

units.la: Meum & Tuum justitiae distributivae objectum, I.601. a. omnium fere bellorum causa est, 603. a.
units.tr: Mine and thine are the object of distributive justice, I.601, a. It is almost the cause of nearly all wars, I.603, a.

units.la: Michael Archangelus Christus est, I.282. b.
units.tr: Michael the archangel is Christ, I.282, b.

units.la: Milites quales ex Lege Divina legendi sint, I. 734. seq.
units.tr: What kind of soldiers should be read about according to divine law, I.734 ff.

units.la: Milnia non improbatur in N. T. II.633. b.
units.tr: The millennium is not disapproved in the New Testament, II.633, b.

units.la: Miltonus quid sentiat de divortiis, I.592. b. censetur, ibid.
units.tr: What Milton thinks about divorce, I.592, b. He is reckoned among..., ibid.

units.la: Mincha seu oblatio in V.T. quid significaverit? I.676. b. 677. b.
units.tr: The minchah, or offering, in the Old Testament: what did it signify? I.676, b. and 677, b.

units.la: Minimae aeque ac maximae res Providentiae Dei subsunt, 261. a.
units.tr: The smallest things as well as the greatest are subject to the providence of God, I.261, a.

units.la: Ministerium Angelorum quale sit, I.280. a. mortis quale fuerit. 460. b. Novi Test. spirituale est, II. 184. b. Spiritus & justitiae, 185. a. reconciliationis, ibid. b. quot annis Christus publicum egerit, disceptatur, 41. a. ejus historia usque ad primum Pascha, ibid. 41. b. Ministeriorum Ecclesiae juxta charismata distinctio, II. 558. b. ordinarii necessitas, 560. a.
units.tr: What kind of ministry the angels have, I.280, a. What the ministry of death was, I.460, b. The ministry of the New Testament is spiritual, II.184, b. It is a ministry of the Spirit and of righteousness, II.185, a. It is a ministry of reconciliation, ibid., b. How many years Christ carried on public ministry is disputed, II.41, a. His history up to the first Passover, ibid., b. The distinction of the ministries of the Church according to charisms, II.558, b. The necessity of an ordinary ministry, II.560, a.

units.la: Ministri Ecclesiae ordinarii Vet. Test. II, 562. a. Nov. Testam. ibid. b. eorundem officium, ibid. 563. a.
