I.615. b. officii partes, ibid. b. incentiva ad illud, 564. a. eorundem vocationis necessitas, 565. a. quotuplex, ibid. b. mediata fit ab Ecclesia, 566. 567. a. utpote cui vocandi jus competit, 568. a. Exercitium, ibid. b. Eorum inauguratio ubi & quando necessaria, 571. b. soli Sacramenta administrare debent, 461. b. iis in matrimonio vivere, 665. a. & praeter stipendia alia bona possidere licet, 577. b. Omnibus una & aequalis potestas a Christo data est, 590. a. 591. a. eorum munus tum circa doctrinam Verbi Dei, 594. seq. tum circa ceremonias explicatur, 599. a. iis stipendia solvi aequum est. I. 721. seq. Eorum electionis, ordinationis & missionis distinctio fictitia est, I I. 663. a.
units.tr: The ordinary ministers of the Church in the Old Testament, II.562, a.; in the New Testament, ibid., b. Their office, ibid. and II.563, a.; I.615, b. The parts of their office, ibid., b. Incentives to it, II.564, a. The necessity of their calling, II.565, a. How many kinds there are, ibid., b. A minister is made mediately by the Church, II.566, 567, a., since the Church has the right to call, II.568, a. The exercise of it, ibid., b. Where and when their inauguration is necessary, I.571, b. Only they ought to administer the sacraments, I.461, b. They may live in marriage, I.665, a., and may possess other goods besides their stipends, I.577, b. To all of them one and equal power has been given by Christ, I.590, a. and 591, a. Their function, both with regard to the doctrine of the Word of God, I.594 ff., and with regard to ceremonies, I.599, a., is explained. It is right that stipends be paid to them, I.721 ff. The distinction between their election, ordination and sending is fictitious, II.663, a.

units.la: Miracula vera solus Deus patrare potest, I. 133. b. 254. 255. a. notae quibus vera a falsis discernuntur, ibid. Christi veritas contra Judaeos asseritur, I I. 97. b. Divinitas, ibid. 98. a. ejus doctrinae mirificam lucem affuderunt, 96. ad triplex ejus munus firmandum pertinent, 95. b. eorum ordo, 96. b. hostium de iis testimonia, 97. a. per ea Deus populum non tentavit, 99. a. Josephi de iis testimonium, 97. a. ejus ψευδο defenditur, ib. a Mose patrata vera fuerunt, I. 481. b. Christi & Diaboli quantum distent. 298. b. Pontificiorum falsa & ficta non sunt nota verae Ecclesiae, II. 550. a.
units.tr: Only God can perform true miracles, I.133, b. and I.254, 255, a. The marks by which true miracles are distinguished from false ones, ibid. The truth of Christ's miracles is asserted against the Jews, II.97, b. Their divinity, ibid., 98, a. They shed a wonderful light on his doctrine, II.96. They serve to confirm his threefold office, II.95, b. Their order, II.96, b. The testimonies of enemies concerning them, II.97, a. God did not tempt the people through them, II.99, a. Josephus's testimony concerning them, II.97, a. Their pseudo- [ψευδο-] character is defended, ibid., a. The true miracles wrought by Moses, I.481, b. How far the miracles of Christ and of the Devil differ, I.298, b. The false and feigned miracles of the Papists are not marks of the true Church, II.550, a.

units.la: Miraculosa fides quid? II. 241. b.
units.tr: Miraculous faith: what is it? II. 241. b.

units.la: Miseria hominis naturalis exponitur, I. 161. b.
units.tr: Misery of natural man is set out, I. 161. b.

units.la: Misericordia qualis virtus, I. 616. 617. a. qualis erga bestias sit praestanda, 733. b. DEI. I. 97. a. non tollit ejus justitiam, I. 174. a.
units.tr: Mercy: what kind of virtue is it? I. 616. 617. a. What kind of mercy is to be shown to beasts, 733. b. Of God, I. 97. a. It does not take away his justice, I. 174. a.

units.la: Missa unde dicta? I I. 461. a. privatae usus exploditur, 466. a. centrum est mysterii iniquitatis. 482. a. non est sacrificium expiatorium, 487. b. 488. a. argumenta adversantia diluuntur, 489. a. pro defunctis habita refellitur, 491. b. Sacrificio & Sacerdotio Christi e diametro opposita est, 104. a. negat satisfactionem Christi, 121. b. cur non vulgari lingua celebretur, 431. a. defunctis nihil prodest, 491. b. Ejus Canon refutatur, ib. b.
units.tr: Mass: whence is the name derived? II. 461. a. Its private use is exploded, 466. a. It is the centre of the mystery of iniquity, 482. a. It is not an expiatory sacrifice, 487. b. 488. a. Opposing arguments are refuted, 489. a. Its use for the dead is refuted, 491. b. It is diametrically opposed to the sacrifice and priesthood of Christ, 104. a. It denies the satisfaction of Christ, 121. b. Why it is not celebrated in the vernacular, 431. a. It profits nothing for the dead, 491. b. Its Canon is refuted, ib. b.

units.la: Missio Filii Dei in carnem explicatur, I I. 3. b. Christi & Apostolorum ejus missio quomodo differat, 567. b.
units.tr: Mission of the Son of God into the flesh is explained, II. 3. b. How the mission of Christ differs from that of his Apostles, 567. b.

units.la: Mittere. Spiritus S. quomodo mittatur, I. 143. b.
units.tr: To send. How is the Holy Spirit sent? I. 143. b.

units.la: Mixtura zizaniorum cum tritico in Ecclesia visibili semper fuit, est & erit, II. 524. b. fusius explicatur parabola, 527. b. Antichristiani regni & verae Ecclesiae Christi, 539. a.
units.tr: Mixture of tares with wheat in the visible Church has always been, is and will be, II. 524. b. The parable is explained more fully, 527. b. The Antichristian kingdom and the true Church of Christ, 539. a.

units.la: Mobatra vel Barata quale usurae genus sit, I. 615. a.
units.tr: Mobatra or Barata: what kind of usury is it? I. 615. a.

units.la: Modestia qualis virtus? I. 566. a.
units.tr: Modesty: what kind of virtue? I. 566. a.

units.la: Modus rei licet ignoretur, res tamen negari non debet, I. 351. a.
units.tr: Manner of a thing: although it is unknown, the thing itself must not be denied, I. 351. a.

units.la: Moira fatum, seu Dea Parca fuit, I. 246. b.
units.tr: Moira was fate, or the goddess Parca, I. 246. b.

units.la: Molinos Quietismi author, I. 10. a.
units.tr: Molinos, author of Quietism, I. 10. a.

units.la: Molochi tentorium quomodo portarint veteres Judaei, 479. b.
units.tr: Tent of Moloch: how did the ancient Jews carry it? 479. b.

units.la: Monachi, Monachatus quid? II. 672. a. ex verbo Dei impugnatur, ibid. b. eorum varii ordines & nomina unde? ibid. Perfectio hypocritica, 673. b. Politicum Papae vaframentum est Monachatus, 674. a. ejus arcana, ibid. nullis aut saltem vaferrimis argumentis probatur, ib. b. Veterum & recentium Monachorum differentia, 675. a. Monachus eremita primus fuit Paulus Thebaeus, I I. 675. a. Monacho iudoctior, unde dictum? 582. a.
units.tr: Monks, monasticism: what is it? II. 672. a. It is attacked from the word of God, ibid. b. Their various orders and names: whence are they? ibid. Hypocritical perfection, 673. b. Monasticism is the Pope's political trick, 674. a. Its secrets, ibid. It is proved by no arguments, or at least only by the most cunning ones, ib. b. The difference between ancient and recent monks, 675. a. The first monk-hermit was Paul of Thebes, II. 675. a. Why is the saying "more ignorant than a monk" used? 582. a.

units.la: Monarcha Ecclesiae non Papa, sed solus Christus est, I I. 639. 640. a.
units.tr: Monarch of the Church is not the Pope but Christ alone, II. 639. 640. a.

units.la: Monarchia Papalis non est vera Ecclesia, II. 535. b. est Babylon magna illa, ib. 536. a. depingitur, 537. a. ejus objectum explicatur, 641. a.
units.tr: Papal monarchy is not the true Church, II. 535. b. It is that great Babylon, ib. 536. a. It is depicted, 537. a. Its object is explained, 641. a.

units.la: Monarchici veteres gradus inaequales in Deitate statuentes perstringuntur, I. 122. b.
units.tr: Monarchians: the ancient ones who posit unequal degrees in the Deity are censured, I. 122. b.

units.la: Monasteria quando & cur primitus instituta? II. 672. a.
units.tr: Monasteries: when and why were they first founded? II. 672. a.

units.la: Monopolia furta sunt, I. 612. a.
units.tr: Monopolies are thefts, I. 612. a.

units.la: Montanistarum error circa refispiscentiam, I. 326. a.
units.tr: Error of the Montanists concerning repentance, I. 326. a.

units.la: Montium existentia Providentiam Dei non tollit, I. 244. b. decorant mundi compagem, ibid.
units.tr: Mountains: their existence does not remove the providence of God, I. 244. b. They adorn the frame of the world, ibid.

units.la: Morinus Codicem Hebraeum V. T. corruptionis accusans arguitur, I. 36. a.
units.tr: Morinus is refuted for accusing the Hebrew text of the Old Testament of corruption, I. 36. a.

units.la: Mors non est naturae sequela, I. 223. a. temporalis fidelibus non est poena, 289. b. transgressori Legis Divinae intentata qualis fuerit? 322. a. Spiritualis quae? ibid. 337. b. I I. 221. b. Infernalis, ibid. b. 338. a. temporalis quae? 323. 338. 339. a. Est animae a corpore suo separatio, quae respectu fidelium describitur, I I. 694. non est poena, 695. a. ejus a morte profanorum differentia, ib. b. quatenus timenda, vel non timenda sit, ib. b. Ejus processus ex Ecclesiastis XII. 5. 6. 7. graphice describitur, 696. a.
units.tr: Death is not a consequence of nature, I. 223. a. Temporal death is not a punishment for believers, 289. b. What was threatened to the transgressor of the divine Law? 322. a. What is spiritual death? ibid. 337. b. II. 221. b. Infernal death, ibid. b. 338. a. What is temporal death? 323. 338. 339. a. It is the separation of the soul from its body, which is described with respect to believers, II. 694. It is not a punishment, 695. a. Its difference from the death of the profane, ib. b. Insofar as it is to be feared or not to be feared, ib. b. Its process is vividly described from Ecclesiastes 12:5–7, 696. a.

units.la: Mors Christi: ejus meritum explicatur, I. 382. b. vim expiandi peccata habuit, II. 106. a. 122. a. rationem poenae vicariae habuit, ib. b. sacrificiis piaculatibus Vet. Test. praefigurabatur, 677. a. ei expiatio peccatorum & satisfactio pro iis tribuitur, 107. a. 114. a. non tantum exemplar patientiae, ut Socinus voluit, sed etiam pro peccatis fuit, ib. 124. a. quibusnam prosit, 122. a. Ejus utilitas maxima, 122. b. Ejus sufficientia & efficacia quomodo a Remonstrantibus applicetur? II. 123. a. Distinctio haec examinatur & rejicitur, ib. ejus amplitudo ostenditur, ib. 122. 123. seqq. Ejus controversiae historia, 124. a. seq. Ejus efficaciam universalem propugnantium argumenta ad partes vocantur, 125. reprobis quid contulerit? 126. a. consolatio ex morte Christi praesentissima, II. 127. justitia fidei per illam, 173. a.
units.tr: Death of Christ: its merit is explained, I. 382. b. It had the power of expiating sins, II. 106. a. 122. a. It had the character of vicarious punishment, ib. b. It was prefigured by the sin-offerings of the Old Testament, 677. a. Expiation of sins and satisfaction for them are ascribed to it, 107. a. 114. a. It was not merely an example of patience, as Socinus wished, but was also for sins, ib. 124. a. To whom does it profit? 122. a. Its greatest usefulness, 122. b. How do the Remonstrants apply its sufficiency and efficacy? II. 123. a. This distinction is examined and rejected, ib. Its amplitude is shown, ib. 122. 123. following. History of its controversy, 124. a. following. The arguments of those defending its universal efficacy are called to account, 125. What did it contribute to the reprobate? 126. a. Consolation from the death of Christ most present, II. 127. The righteousness of faith through it, 173. a.

units.la: Mortis aeternae diritas, II. 759. b. ejus natura & indoles describitur, 763. 764.
units.tr: Eternal death: its harshness, II. 759. b. Its nature and character are described, 763. 764.

units.la: Morticini seu cadaveris contactus cur legaliter impurum reddiderit? 672. a.
units.tr: Contact with a corpse: why did it render a person legally unclean? 672. a.

units.la: Mortui non sunt baptizandi, I I. 452. b.
units.tr: The dead are not to be baptized, II. 452. b.

units.la: Moses, antiquissimus scriptor, I. 27. b. quinam Vet. T. libri ei tribuantur? 34. b. totum Pentateuchum scripsit, 35. a. omnis doctrinae & Prophetiae Canonem tradidit, 480. b. ejus authoritas contra Pseudo-Criticos asseritur, 481. a. Miraculis confirmata, ib. typicus foederis legalis mediator fuit, 458. 459. Cujus vita privata, 459. publica exponitur, 460. in utraque typus Christi fuit, ibid. a. in aliquibus tamen ei oppositus, 460. b. quomodo populum Israeliticum baptizaverit nube & mari, 491. a. II. 445. Ecclesiam & Rempublicam Israeliticam salutaribus institutis ordinavit, 700. a. tamen nec Rex neque Sacerdos Israelitarum fuit, 704. b. Messia longe inferior fuit, 695. a. quomodo populi λαος fuerit, II. 109. a. a promisso Propheta Christo quantum differat, I. 695. II. 156. a.
units.tr: Moses, the most ancient writer, I. 27. b. Which books of the Old Testament are attributed to him? 34. b. He wrote the whole Pentateuch, 35. a. He handed down the canon of all doctrine and prophecy, 480. b. His authority is asserted against the pseudo-critics, 481. a. Confirmed by miracles, ib. As a type, he was mediator of the legal covenant, 458. 459. His private life, 459. His public life is set out, 460. In both he was a type of Christ, ibid. a. Yet in some respects he was opposed to him, 460. b. How he baptized the Israelite people in the cloud and the sea, 491. a. II. 445. He ordered the Church and the Israelite commonwealth by salutary institutions, 700. a. Yet he was neither king nor priest of the Israelites, 704. b. He was far inferior to the Messiah, 695. a. How he was of the people (laos), II. 109. a. How far he differs from the promised Prophet, Christ, I. 695. II. 156. a.

units.la: Motus, quo Angeli de loco in locum moventur non est corporeus, I. 172. b. nec proprie dictus talis, 277. b.
units.tr: Motion by which angels move from place to place is not bodily, I. 172. b. Nor is it properly called motion, 277. b.

units.la: Muhammedani, eorum Alcoran & tota religio fabularum & superstitionum cento est, I. 6. b. αγνωσία veri Dei, 108. b. Naturalem religionem statuunt, 4. b. Eorum carnales de Filii Dei generatione conceptus, 125. a. Christum novum Deum vocant, 135. b. animalia castrata & in Paschate occisa, in suum Paradisum admittunt, 215. a. Adoptionem Christianorum subsannant, I I. 307. b.
units.tr: Muhammadans: their Alcoran and their whole religion is a patchwork of fables and superstitions, I. 6. b. Ignorance [ἀγνωσία] of the true God, 108. b. They posit a natural religion, 4. b. Their carnal conceptions of the generation of the Son of God, 125. a. They call Christ a new God, 135. b. They admit castrated animals and those killed at Passover into their Paradise, 215. a. They mock the adoption of Christians, II. 307. b.

units.la: Multa seu poenae pecuniariae apud Hebraeos quales fuerint; & quibus deliciis dictari fuerit, I. 713. a.
units.tr: Fines, or pecuniary penalties, among the Hebrews: what they were, and for what offences they were imposed, I. 713. a.

units.la: Mulier seducta a serpente prior peccavit, I. 332. b. cur Diabolus illam potius quam virum sit aggressus, 333. a. vid. Eva. Primae formatio non caruit mysterio, 230. a. ejusdem cum Adamo dignitatis fuit, 231. b.
units.tr: Woman, seduced by the serpent, sinned first, I. 332. b. Why did the devil attack her rather than the man, 333. a. See Eve. The formation of the first woman was not without mystery, 230. a. She had the same dignity as Adam, 231. b.

units.la: Mulier συνέουχτ@ subintroducta quaenam dicatur, I I. 667. b.
units.tr: Woman [συνείσακτος] subintroduced: who is meant by this? II. 667. b.

units.la: Mulieres etiam semen genitale habent, II. 15. a. earum baptismus rejicitur, I. 439. 440.
units.tr: Women also have generative seed, II. 15. a. Their baptism is rejected, I. 439. 440.

units.la: Multitudo credentium non est genuina nota verae Ecclesiae, I I. 546. a.
units.tr: The multitude of believers is not a genuine mark of the true Church, II. 546. a.

units.la: Mundus non est Deus, I. 106. b. nec ab aeterno exstitit, 185. b. 186. a. quomodo propter hominem conditus sit, 191. a. ejus creatio, ibid. b. vid. Brev. nonnisi unus est, 192. a. nullam habet animam, 193. non est ab aeterno, 194. nec defetiscit senescendo 195. b. ejus finitas tum extensionis, tum durationis, tum perfectionis, 194. 195. a. Dei domus est, in qua ille ceu Paterfamilias omnia gubernat, 249. b. Ejus renovatio ex certa siderum syzygia nulla fiet, II. 735. b. finis & consummatio quando futura sit, 750. a. etiam sana ratio ejus finem arguit, ib. b. ejus aeternitas impugnatur, 751. b. conflagrabit, ib. vide Conflagratio.
units.tr: The world is not God, I. 106. b. Nor has it existed from eternity, 185. b. 186. a. How it was created for the sake of man, 191. a. Its creation, ibid. b. See Brev. There is only one, 192. a. It has no soul, 193. It is not from eternity, 194. Nor does it wear out by growing old, 195. b. Its finitude in extension, duration and perfection, 194. 195. a. It is the house of God, in which he governs all things as a father governs his household, 249. b. Its renewal from a certain conjunction of the stars will never happen, II. 735. b. When its end and consummation will be, 750. a. Even sound reason proves its end, ib. b. Its eternity is attacked, 751. b. It will be burned up, ib. See Conflagration.

units.la: Mundi armatura & tentationes, I. 371. b.
units.tr: World: its armour and temptations, I. 371. b.

units.la: Mundus Joh. 14:17. quid significat? II. 215. b.
units.tr: World, John 14:17. What does it signify? II. 215. b.

units.la: Musica quatenus laudanda, I. 632. b. scenica & theatralis Pontificiorum perstringitur, 349. b.
units.tr: Music: how far it is to be commended, I. 632. b. The stage and theatrical music of the Papists is censured, 349. b.

units.la: Mutabilitas est propria rebus creatis, I. 196. b. hominis primi fuit conditio concreata, 228, b. Mutatio sacramentalis non substantialis, sed relativa tantum est, I.395. b. Superstitium in adventu Domini quomodo sit futura, I.743. b.
units.tr: Mutability is proper to created things, I. 196. b. It was the innate condition of the first man, 228, b. Change in the sacrament is not substantial but merely relative, I. 395. b. Superstition at the coming of the Lord: how it will arise, I. 743. b.

units.la: Mutuum quid sit, I.612. b. a commodato quomodo differat, 615. a.
units.tr: Loan for consumption (mutuum): what it is, I. 612. b. How it differs from a loan for use (commodatum), 615. a.

units.la: Mysterium. Mysteria fidei quænam sint? I.9. b. à solo Deo revelantur, ibid. rationi humanæ non patent, nec revelantur sapientibus hujus mundi, 10.a. S. Trinitatis in sola Scriptura panduntur, 110. a. vocum circa illa usus sobrius esse debet, ib. Philosophorum consensu etiam demonstratur, 112.b. vid Trinitas.
units.tr: Mystery. What are the mysteries of faith? I. 9. b. They are revealed by God alone, ibid. They are not open to human reason, nor revealed to the wise of this world, 10. a. The mysteries of the Holy Trinity are unfolded in Scripture alone, 110. a. The use of words about them ought to be sober, ib. They are also demonstrated by the consensus of the philosophers, 112. b. See Trinity.

units.la: Mysterii nomen cur Babylonis fronti inscriptum est? II. 641. Missa est centrum mysterii iniquitatis, 481. a.
units.tr: Mystery: why the name was inscribed on the forehead of Babylon, II. 641. The Mass is the centre of the mystery of iniquity, 481. a.

units.la: Mystici Pontificii sacra sua celant, II.433. a. refellunt eorum argumenta, 434. eorum de amando Deo & amore ejus insulsa opinio, 520. a. Theologiæ eorum à Scholastica discrimen; ejus item origo & crisis, I. 19, b.
units.tr: Mystics: the Papists conceal their sacred rites, II. 433. a. Their arguments are refuted, 434. Their insipid opinion about loving God and his love, 520. a. The difference between their theology and the Scholastic, and likewise its origin and crisis, I. 19. b.

units.la: N.
units.tr: N.

units.la: Natalis dies Christi certò definiri nequit, II. 25. a.
units.tr: The birthday of Christ cannot be fixed with certainty, II. 25. a.

units.la: Nativitas Christi à nativitate hominum aliorum quantum differat, II.5. b. adversus Judæorum blasphemias vindicatur, II.b. 12.a. ejus modus naturalis fuit, 14.a. tempus certò definiri nequit, ib. de die 15. Decemb. controvertitur, 25. a.
units.tr: How far the nativity of Christ differs from the birth of other men, II.5. b. Defended against the blasphemies of the Jews, II.b. 12.a. Its mode was natural, 14.a. The time cannot be fixed with certainty, ib. The question of 25 December is disputed, 25. a.

units.la: Natura rerum corporearum & spiritualium Dei existentiam docet, I.64. b. Non est Deus, 106. b. 107. seq. ejus vox quid sensu Scripturæ significet? 328. a.
units.tr: The nature of corporeal and spiritual things teaches the existence of God, I.64. b. Nature is not God, 106. b. 107 seq. What does the word "nature" signify in the sense of Scripture? 328. a.

units.la: Natura Dei providentiam ejus docet, I.241.b.
units.tr: The nature of God teaches his providence, I.241. b.

units.la: Natura Lex quid, I.310. b. vide Lex. ejus praxis in gentilibus qualis fuerit? I. 367.
units.tr: What is natural law? I.310. b. See Law. What was its practice among the Gentiles? I.367.

units.la: Natura humanæ communio in Christo, eum declarat caput Ecclesiæ, II.556. a.
units.tr: The communion of human nature in Christ: it declares him the head of the Church, II.556. a.

units.la: Naturalis Theologia asseritur & contra Socinum defenditur, I.3. a. non salutaris, 4. a. ejus usus respectu Dei & hominum, 5. a. vide Theologia, & Breviarium primum.
units.tr: Natural theology is asserted and defended against Socinus, I.3. a. It is not saving, 4. a. Its use with respect to God and men, 5. a. See Theology, and the Breviarium primum.

units.la: Nauta navi ignem ipsi subjicientes an ἀπτόχεσις? I. 577. a.
units.tr: Sailors who set fire to the ship under themselves: is this a case of [ἀπτόχεσις]? I.577. a.

units.la: Nazarenus cur Christus dictus fuerit? II.39. a.
units.tr: Why was Christ called a Nazarene? II.39. a.

units.la: Nazirai quinam fuerint? I. 670. a. eorum instituta, ibid. Votum, 367. b. mysterium illius voti, 689. a. Vinu usu sibi interdicentes, an in S. Coena vino abstinuerint? II. 472. a. nihil cum Monachis commune habuerunt, 674.
units.tr: Who were the Nazirites? I.670. a. Their rules, ibid. The vow, 367. b. The mystery of that vow, 689. a. Did those who abstained from wine by their own vow abstain from wine in the Holy Supper? II.472. a. They had nothing in common with monks, 674.

units.la: Nebucadnezaris metamorphosis explicatur, I. 291. a. Non in brutum animal conversus est, II.700.a.
units.tr: The metamorphosis of Nebuchadnezzar is explained, I.291. a. He was not turned into a brute animal, II.700. a.

units.la: Necessaria quænam? II. 644. a.
units.tr: What things are necessary? II.644. a.

units.la: Necessitas rerum quotuplex? I. 261. a. 263. a. fatalis quid? 146. b. inevitabilis reficitur, 247. a. durum telum est, 603. b. credendorum vel faciendorum ad salutem quotuplex? II. 454.a. absoluta Baptismi non est, 457. a.
units.tr: How many kinds of necessity are there in things? I.261. a. 263. a. What is fatal necessity? 146. b. Inevitable necessity is refuted, 247. a. It is a hard weapon, 603. b. How many kinds of necessity are there for things to be believed or done for salvation? II.454. a. Baptism is not absolutely necessary, 457. a.

units.la: Necessitates nostræ Deo licet notissimæ sint, tamen precandum est. I. 343. b.
units.tr: Although our needs are most well known to God, nonetheless we must pray. I.343. b.

units.la: Nekrosis seu Baptismus mortuorum cur improbanus? II. 452. b.
units.tr: Why is the [νέκρωσις] or baptism of the dead rejected? II.452. b.

units.la: Nephilim antediluviani non Angeli fuerunt, I.272. b. Nimrod, Saraceni, &c. latrones famosi fuerunt, 609. a.
units.tr: The antediluvian Nephilim were not angels, I.272. b. Nimrod, the Saracens, etc. were notorious robbers, 609. a.

units.la: Nestorii duas in Christo personas unitas fingentis hæresis refellitur, II.19. b.
units.tr: The heresy of Nestorius, who imagined two persons united in Christ, is refuted, II.19. b.

units.la: Nicænum Concilium II. imaginum cultum sanxit, I. 535. b.
units.tr: The Second Council of Nicaea sanctioned the veneration of images, I.535. b.

units.la: Nicolaus I. Papa Apollionem primus canonizavit, II.711. a.
units.tr: Pope Nicholas I was the first to canonize Apollonius, II.711. a.

units.la: Nihil. Quomodo juxta Aristotelem ex nihilo nihil fiat, I. 186. b.
units.tr: Nothing: how, according to Aristotle, nothing comes from nothing, I.186. b.

units.la: Nimrodus primus Tyrannus fuit, II.619. b. non verò Magistratus primus, ibid.
units.tr: Nimrod was the first tyrant, II.619. b. but not the first magistrate, ibid.

units.la: Noachi δικαιοσύνη, fides, justitiæ præconium, I.425. b. 426. a. fœderis Dei cum eo historia, 426. b. ejusdem Prophetia, ibid. b. sacrificium, 443. b. in arca servatus typus fuit Ecclesiæ in persecutionibus servandæ, 453. a.
units.tr: The righteousness, faith and proclamation of justice of Noah, I.425. b. 426. a. The history of God's covenant with him, 426. b. His prophecy, ibid. b. His sacrifice, 443. b. Preserved in the ark, he was a type of the Church to be preserved in persecutions, 453. a.

units.la: Nomen proprié Deus nullum habet, I.67. a. præcipua Dei Nomina, ibid. b. proprium nomen ejus Jah est, 69. a. Nomen Domini Dei quid, & quomodo in vanum sumatur? 541. a. 547. b. 548. a. Ejus san-
units.tr: Properly speaking, God has no name, I.67. a. The chief names of God, ibid. b. His proper name is Jah, 69. a. What is the name of the Lord God, and how is it taken in vain? 541. a. 547. b. 548. a. Its sanc-

units.la: ctificatio, I.355. b. 542.a. tetragrammati à Davide lapidi Templi insculpti fabula refutatur, II.98. b.
units.tr: tification, I.355. b. 542. a. The fable that David carved the tetragrammaton on a stone of the Temple is refuted, II.98. b.

units.la: Nomina Divina Christo in Veteri & in N.T. tribuuntur, I. 126.a. vel personam vel alteritatem Naturam notant, II. 22.a.
units.tr: Divine names are attributed to Christ in the Old and New Testaments, I.126. a. They denote either the person or the distinct nature, II.22. a.

units.la: Nomen super omne nomen quale Christo datum? II. 55.a. ejus causa meritoria Christi exinanitio & obedientia fuit, 56. a.
units.tr: What name above every name was given to Christ? II.55. a. Its meritorious cause was the self-emptying and obedience of Christ, 56. a.

units.la: Notæ, quibus verum Ecclesiam agnosci Pontificii asserunt, varia proponuntur, II.544.a. rejiciuntur, ibid. b. 545. seq.
units.tr: The marks by which the Papists assert the true Church may be recognised are variously proposed, II.544. a. They are rejected, ibid. b. 545 seq.

units.la: Notarii officium in judicio quale? I.636.b.
units.tr: What is the office of a notary in judgment? I.636. b.

units.la: Notitia Christi ejusque beneficiorum ad actus fidei salvificæ antecedentes pertinet, I.248. a.
units.tr: The knowledge of Christ and of his benefits pertains to the acts of saving faith that precede it, I.248. a.

units.la: Nova vita & novitas vitæ æterna est, II.399.a.
units.tr: New life and newness of life is eternal, II.399. a.

units.la: Novatianorum error circa refipiscentiam, I.326.a.
units.tr: The error of the Novatians concerning repentance, I.326. a.

units.la: Noviluniorum sacrificia V.T. quid significaverint, I. 677. b. Novilunia diversimodè constituta fuerunt apud Judæos, I.44.a.
units.tr: What did the new moon sacrifices of the Old Testament signify? I.677. b. New moons were fixed in various ways among the Jews, I.44. a.

units.la: Novissimum dicrum quid? II.144.b.
units.tr: What is the last day? II.144. b.

units.la: Novum cœlum & nova terra coeperunt Christo in cruce mortuo, II.753.755. a. quænam creaturæ sint renovandæ? 755. b. hujus considerationis usus, 757. a.
units.tr: The new heaven and new earth began with Christ dead on the cross, II.753. 755. a. Which creatures are to be renewed? 755. b. The use of this consideration, 757. a.

units.la: Nubere inscitis & invitis parentibus non licet, I.571.b.
units.tr: It is not lawful to marry without knowledge of, and against the will of, the parents, I.571. b.

units.la: Nubes quando creatæ fuerint, I.105. a. qua baptizati Israelitæ fuerunt, qualis? 491.a.
units.tr: When were the clouds created? I.105. a. What sort of clouds were those in which the Israelites were baptized? 491. a.

units.la: Nuditas Protoplastorum qualis fuerit, I.337. a. explicatur, ibid. b. mortis spiritualis argumentum est, ibid.
units.tr: What was the nakedness of the first parents like? I.337. a. It is explained, ibid. b. It is a proof of spiritual death, ibid.

units.la: Numerus articulorum fidei fundamentalium certus iniri nequit, I. 17. a.
units.tr: The number of the fundamental articles of faith cannot be determined with certainty, I.17. a.

units.la: Numerus denarius an sit mysticus, I. 512.a.
units.tr: Is the number ten mystical? I.512. a.

units.la: Numerus, 666. Apoc. 13 : 17.18. Bestiæ tributus explicatur, II.686. b.
units.tr: The number 666, Rev. 13:17-18. The tribute of the beast is explained, II.686. b.

units.la: Numinis reverenua quid? I.521.b.
units.tr: What is reverence of the divine majesty? I.521. b.

units.la: Nuptiæ clandestinæ rejiciuntur, I.571.a.
units.tr: Clandestine marriages are rejected, I.571. a.

units.la: Nuptiales ritus Hebræorum veterum describuntur, I.728.b.
units.tr: The nuptial rites of the ancient Hebrews are described, I.728. b.

units.tr: O.

units.la: Obedientiam Deus ab Adamo recens creato stipulatus est, I.308.a. eadem præstanda est Legi Naturæ etiam cum periculo vitæ, 314.b. in actibus imperatis consistit, 316.a. etiam post lapsum homo ad obedientiam Legi præstandam homo obligatur, 371. b. Hanc Christus in se suscepit & præstitit, 377.b. quæ non in pallionibus solis consistit, 284. a. 285. opus fuit, 286.a. est Regenerationis nostræ causa, II.121. a.
units.tr: Obedience God required from Adam, newly created, I.308.a. The same obedience is owed to the Law of Nature even at the risk of life, 314.b. It consists in commanded acts, 316.a. Even after the fall, man is bound to render obedience to the Law, 371.b. Christ took this upon himself and rendered it, 377.b. It does not consist in passive suffering alone, 284.a. 285. It was necessary, 286.a. It is the cause of our regeneration, II.121.a.

units.la: Obedientia Legi præstita efficit justitiam legalem, I. 316.a. quæ perfecta, 316.a. perseverans esse debuit, 318.a. fidei qualis esse debeat, I I.250.a. Nova exercetur per bona opera, I. 327, b. Cæcæ votum in Papatu rejicitur, II.166. b. Jesuitarum profligatur, 569.a. major Deo quàm hominibus debetur, 568.b.
units.tr: Obedience rendered to the Law produces legal righteousness, I.316.a. It ought to be perfect, 316.a., and to persevere, 318.a. What kind of faith it ought to be, II.250.a. The new obedience is exercised through good works, I.327.b. The vow of celibacy is rejected in Popery, II.166.b. It is refuted by the Jesuits, 569.a. It is owed more to God than to men, 568.b.

units.la: Oblatio Christi ad mortem voluntaria fuit, II. 105. b. ejus necessitas, 106.a.
units.tr: The offering of Christ to death was voluntary, II.105.b. Its necessity, 106.a.

units.la: Obsignatio fœderis Gratiæ in Veteri & Novo Test. eadem fuit, I. 415.a. Obsignatio & sanctificatio electorum per Spiritum S. eorum salutem certam reddit, I.394.a. efficit in illis perseverantiam, II.401. a.
units.tr: The sealing of the covenant of grace was the same in the Old and New Testaments, I.415.a. The sealing and sanctification of the elect through the Holy Spirit make their salvation certain, I.394.a. It produces perseverance in them, II.401.a.

units.la: Obtrectatio quale vitium? I. 566. a.
units.tr: Detraction: what kind of vice is it? I.566.a.

units.la: Obtrectator quis & qualis sit? I I.603. a.
units.tr: A detractor: who is he, and what is he like? II.603.a.

units.la: Oceanus quando coeperit, I. 205. b. est aquarum omnium locus & receptaculum, ibid.
units.tr: The ocean: when it began, I.205.b. It is the place and receptacle of all waters, ibid.

units.la: Oculorum concupiscentia peccaminosa, I.641. a.
units.tr: The lust of the eyes is sinful, I.641.a.

units.la: Odio habendi non sunt inimici, I. 504. b. quinam & quando odio habendi sint.505. a.
units.tr: Enemies are not to be hated, I.504.b. Who are to be hated, and when, 505.a.

units.la: Oeconomia Ecclesiæ quando & cur talis à Deo institua sit, I.7. a.
units.tr: The economy of the Church: when and why God instituted it in such a form, I.7.a.

units.la: Oeconomia Fœderis Gratiæ in Vet. & N. T. in quibus rebus differat, I. 415. b. sub Patriarchis qualis fuerit, 417. a. vide Breviar. Qualis sub Lege Mosis, 455.a. ejus definitio, 456. a. vide Breviar. Personarum S. Trinitatis tum inter se, I. 123. a. tum in negotio salutis hominum Patris, 124.a. Filii, ib.137.a. Spiritus S. 144. b.
units.tr: The economy of the covenant of grace in the Old and New Testaments: in what respects it differs, I.415.b. What it was under the Patriarchs, 417.a. See the Breviar. What it was under the Law of Moses, 455.a. Its definition, 456.a. See the Breviar. The persons of the Holy Trinity, both among themselves, I.123.a., and in the business of human salvation: the Father, 124.a.; the Son, ibid. 137.a.; the Holy Spirit, 144.b.

units.la: Omnes aliquando notat quosvis, II.125. b. alicubi de rebus contrariis usurpatur, ib. quomodo Deus salvari velit, I.173. a.
units.tr: All sometimes means any, II.125.b. Somewhere it is used of contrary things, ibid. How God wills all to be saved, I.173.a.

units.la: Omnia in omnibus quomodo Deus futurus sit, II. 137.a. b.
units.tr: Everything in everyone: how God will be in the future, II.137.a.b.

units.la: Omnipotentia Dei, I.101.b. Naturæ humanæ Christi non est communicata, II.29.a. 31.b.
units.tr: The omnipotence of God, I.101.b. It is not communicated to the human nature of Christ, II.29.a. 31.b.

units.la: Omnipræsentia Dei explicatur & asseritur, I.77.a. 78. b.
units.tr: The omnipresence of God is explained and asserted, I.77.a. 78.b.

units.la: f Naturæ humanæ Christi non est communicata, 11, 29.a. 30.a. 31.
units.tr: Not communicated to the human nature of Christ, II.29.a. 30.a. 31.

units.la: Omniscientia Naturæ humanæ Christi non est communicata, 11, 29.a. 31.b.
units.tr: The omniscience is not communicated to the human nature of Christ, II.29.a. 31.b.

units.la: Ὀμολογία seu astipulatio qualis actus fidei sit, II. 251. a. explicatur uberius, 256. a.
units.tr: Homologia [ὁμολογία], or assent: what kind of act of faith it is, II.251.a. It is explained more fully, 256.a.

units.la: Ὀμοούσιον in Concilio Nicaeno contra τὸ ὁμοιούσιον sancitur, I, 111. a.
units.tr: Homoousion [ὁμοούσιον] was established at the Council of Nicaea against homoiousion [ὁμοιούσιον], I.111.a.

units.la: Ὁμοιότης animalium ingentis Adami judicii testimonium fuit, I.230. a.
units.tr: Likeness [ὁμοιότης] of the animals was a testimony to Adam's great judgment, I.230.a.

units.la: Opera bona quænam sunt? I. 327. b. operis bonitas concursum omnium causarum requirit, ib. ejusdem conditiones, 328. 329. Pontificiorum perstringuntur, 331. fidelium imperfecta sunt, ib. eorum necessitas, 332. b. non merentur, 333. b. 335.a. eorum studium utile est, 338.b. gentilium bona opera peccatis polluta fuerunt, 330.a.
units.tr: Good works: what are they? I.327.b. The goodness of a work requires the concurrence of all causes, ibid. Its conditions, 328, 329. The views of the Papists are assailed, 331. The works of believers are imperfect, ibid. Their necessity, 332.b. They do not merit, 333.b. 335.a. Their study is useful, 338.b. The good works of the Gentiles were polluted by sins, 330.a.

units.la: Opera & fides in justificationis negotio quomodo sibi opponantur, II. 172. a. 231. b. 298. a. non justificant, ibid. 299. S, Pauli & S. Jacobi conciliatio, 304. b.
units.tr: Works and faith in the business of justification: how they are opposed to each other, II.172.a. 231.b. 298.a. Works do not justify, ibid. 299. The reconciliation of St Paul and St James, 304.b.

units.la: Opera Naturæ hominem ad quærendum Deum vocant & ducunt, I. 107. b. secundum Opera dare alicui quid significet, 337. b.
units.tr: The works of nature call and lead man to seek God, I.107.b. What it means to give something to someone according to works, 337.b.

units.la: Operari omnia, etiam malum, quomodo Deus dicatur, 275. b.
units.tr: Working all things, even evil: how God is said to do this, 275.b.

units.la: Operationes Dei immediatæ quot modis in creaturis fiant? I. 154. b. miraculosæ, ibid. Dei & Diaboli quibus characteribus dignoscantur? 294. a. Christi ad personam diversimodè referuntur, II.23.b.
units.tr: The operations of God: in how many ways are immediate operations produced in creatures? I.154.b. Miraculous ones, ibid. By what marks are the operations of God and of the Devil distinguished? 294.a. The operations of Christ are variously referred to his person, II.23.b.

units.la: Operum merita cum fœdere gratiæ non subsistunt, I. 385.a.
units.tr: The merits of works do not subsist together with the covenant of grace, I.385.a.

units.la: Oppignerntio qualis contractus sit, I. 612. a. mutua Deum inter & hominem fidelem certitudine nsalutis stabilit, II. 411. a.
units.tr: A pledge: what kind of contract is it? I.612.a. A mutual pledge between God and the believer establishes the certainty of salvation, II.411.a.

units.la: Oraculorum Divinorum infal'ibilitas, I.188. 289. Diabolicorum vanitas, ib. falsata ex veris hausta, ibid. Christo nato conticuerunt, 289. b.
units.tr: The oracles: the infallibility of divine oracles, I.188, 289. The vanity of diabolical oracles, ibid. They were falsified, drawn from true ones, ibid. They fell silent at the birth of Christ, 289.b.

units.la: Oratio Dominica precum formula accuratissima est, I. 353. ejus partes, ibid. sex petitiones, ib. b. alias etiam precum formulis uti licet, 354.a. Christi passionalis qualis fuerit, II.45.a. pro crucifigentibus ipsum indefinita est, 123. b. ex humano affectu profecta est, 128. a.
units.tr: The Lord's Prayer is the most exact formula of prayer, I.353. Its parts, ibid. Six petitions, ibid. b. Other formulas of prayer may also be used, 354.a. What the passion-prayer of Christ was like, II.45.a. For those who crucified him it is indefinite, 123.b. It proceeded from human feeling, 128.a.

units.la: Ordinationis ad Ecclesiæ ministerium tempus, II.571. Sacramentalis & ordinum Papalium vanitas, 663. a.
units.tr: The ordination to the ministry of the Church: its time, II.571. The vanity of sacramental ordination and of the Papal orders, 663.a.

units.la: Ordines Papales Ecclesiasticî varii, II.663. a. cum Judæorum & Gentilium ordinibus conveniunt, ib.
units.tr: The Papal ecclesiastical orders are various, II.663.a. They agree with the orders of the Jews and the Gentiles, ibid.

units.la: Ordo seu Ordinatio ad Ecclesiæ ministerium non est Sacramentum, I I.502.a.
units.tr: Order, or ordination to the ministry of the Church, is not a sacrament, II.502.a.

units.la: Ordo Decretorum Dei qualis? I.152.153.a.
units.tr: The order of God's decrees: what kind is it? I.152, 153.a.

units.la: Organorum musicorum in Ecclesia usus, I.349.a.
units.tr: The use of musical instruments in the Church, I.349.a.

units.la: Origenis error de pluribus mundis succedivis, I.192.b. hominis ... statuentis, II.213. a. de resurrectione, 738.a.
units.tr: Origen's error concerning many successive worlds, I.192.b. His statement about man, II.213.a. His view on the resurrection, 738.a.

units.la: Originale peccatum quid? I.340.a. Ejus imputatio posteris Adami facta, ibid. quod fusius diducitur. 341. a. ejus propagatio, 342. a. nomina, 344. vid. Breviar. non est hominis substantia, 346.b. Gentiles idem agnoverunt, ib. sed est corruptio tum potentiatum tum qualitatum naturalium, 347.b. inhæret, 349.a. non est mera justitiæ orig. carentia, 349. b. concupiscentia non exhaurit ejus naturam, ibid. Peccatum orig. negantium historia, 350. a. ejus propagatio defenditur, 351. propagationis modus ostenditur, ib. b. Pelagianorum peccatum orig. negantium error refutatur, 350. b. 353. b. In irregenitis nunquam, in regenitis demum post mortem penitus tollitur, 356.a. vide Peccatum.
units.tr: Original sin: what is it? I.340.a. Its imputation to the posterity of Adam, ibid. This is unfolded more fully, 341.a. Its propagation, 342.a. Its names, 344. See the Breviar. It is not the substance of man, 346.b. The Gentiles also acknowledged the same, ibid. But it is a corruption both of the faculties and of the natural qualities, 347.b. It adheres, 349.a. It is not merely the lack of original justice, 349.b. Concupiscence does not exhaust its nature, ibid. History of those who deny original sin, 350.a. Its propagation is defended, 351. The mode of propagation is shown, ibid. b. The error of the Pelagians, who deny original sin, is refuted, 350.b. 353.b. In the unregenerate it is never removed; in the regenerate it is finally removed completely only after death, 356.a. See Sin.

units.la: Ofiandri Filium Dei incarnatum imaginem Dei facientis error, I.263.b.
units.tr: The error of the Osiandrians, that the Son of God incarnate is the image of the God who makes, I.263.b.

units.la: Oves curiu victimis olim adhibitæ fuerint, I.675.b.
units.tr: Sheep: how they were formerly used as victims, I.675.b.

units.la: P.
units.tr: P.

units.la: Pacifica sacrificia quæ & qualia fuerint, I.655.a. eorum variæ species, ibid. b. noltri reconciliationem cum Deo per Christum significarunt, 676.a.
units.tr: Peace-offerings: what they were and of what kinds, I.655.a. Their various species, ibid. b. They signified the reconciliation of us with God through Christ, 676.a.

units.la: Pactum seu Consilium pacis singulare Deum Patrem inter & Filium, 376. a. in quo pater stipulatur à Filio obedientiam Legis hominis loco præstandam, 377. b. restipulatur Filius Sponsor obedientiæ suæ mercedem, 382.a.
units.tr: The covenant, or counsel, of peace that is unique between God the Father and the Son, 376.a. In it the Father stipulates from the Son the obedience of the Law to be rendered in place of man, 377.b. The Son, as surety, restipulates the reward of his obedience, 382.a.

units.la: Pactum vel Legale vel Evangelicum est, I I.337. a. ex neutro opera vitam æternam merentur, ib.
units.tr: A covenant is either legal or evangelical, I.II.337.a. By neither do works merit eternal life, ib.

units.la: Pactum sagarum cum Diabolo reale est, I.294.295.a.
units.tr: The pact of witches with the Devil is real, I.294.295.a.

units.la: Pædobaptismus demonstratur, I I.450.b.
units.tr: Infant baptism is demonstrated, II.450.b.

units.la: Panes Pentecostales & facierum Vet. Test. quid notaverint, I.652. b.
units.tr: What the Pentecostal loaves and the loaves of the Old Testament signified, I.652.b.

units.la: Panis azymus non necessario in S.Cœna adhibendus est, I I.463. a. cur Ecclesia Tigurina eo utatur, ib. ejus fractio necessaria est, 464. b. ratio in manus, non in os, 465.a. asservatio improbatur, 466.b. manducatio necessaria cur sit, ibid.
units.tr: Unleavened bread is not necessarily to be used in the Lord's Supper, II.463.a. Why the Tigurine Church uses it, ib. Its breaking is necessary, 464.b. The reason for placing it in the hand, not the mouth, 465.a. Reservation is disapproved, 466.b. Why eating it is necessary, ibid.

units.la: Panis ἀνώμαλος quis, & cur talis dicatur, I.156.355.
units.tr: Who is the "anomalous" bread [ἀνώμαλος], and why is it so called? I.156.355.

units.la: Panoplia spiritualis, 371. b.
units.tr: Spiritual armour, 371.b.

units.la: Pantheris filius cur Jesus à vereribus Judæis & Gentilibus blasphemetur, I I.12.a.
units.tr: Why is the Son of Panthera blasphemed by the old Jews and Gentiles? II.12.a.

units.la: Papa Rom. Ejus Spiritus privatus, I.44. a. Antichristianus est, 59.b. Quinam primùm ita dicti fuerint, 561.b. Hierarchiam suam falsò ab Apostolis derivat, II.198. a. Litem Prædicatores inter & Franciscanos de Gratia decidere hactenus non potuit, 216. 217. jus vota confirmandi aut relaxandi iniquè sibi tribuit, 370.b. impeccantia & infallibilitas sacrilegè ipsi tribuitur, 531. a. maximus ganeo est, 598. a. Monarcham Ecclesiæ se jactat, 639.640. potestatem suam ipse in Concilio Florentino definivit, 639.a. Caput Ecclesiæ esse vult, ib. b. potestatem suam supra omnem aliam temporalem extollit, 641. b. Non est universalis Ecclesiæ Episcopus, 642.a. Nullam potestatem temporalem habet nec jure Divino, nec humano, 642. b. seq. Argumenta contraria diluuntur, 643.a. Ecclesiæ leges imponere non potest, 646. b. 646.a. potestatem judicialem etiam sibi tribuit falsò, 647.a. Magistratus constituit, ibid. b. Concilia convocat, &c. illius potestatis iniquitas ostenditur, ib.d 648, a. Non est Christi vicarius, 649. b. Petri successor non est, 656. non est Caput Ecclesiæ, 660. b. errare potest, ibid. b. 661. rationes pro ejus suprematu elidiuntur, 661. b. jus supremum eligendi & ordinandi Ecclesiæ ministros non habet, 663. ejus ... per Concilia, 676.b. impugnatur, 677. a. advetsantia argumenta ventilantur, ib. b. argumenta pro ejus suprematu refelluntur, 678.b. qua Papa & papæ mu-nus gerens Antichristus est, 683.b.quod plurimis argumentis evincitur, ibid. & 684.a. Negat Jesum esse Christum & venisse in carne, 684. involat triplex Christi officium mediatorium, ibid. extollit se super omnem Augustum, ibid. Deum se esse demonstrat, ibid. Est homo peccati, 685.a. ἀντίχριστος, ibid. ei conveniunt flagitia, scortationum abominatio, blasphemandi cacoëthes, cyclopica tyrannis; Impietas magica, spiritualis nundinatio & avaritia, 685. b. Diltmotæ Periodi Antichristi Papæ congruunt, 686. corpus Antichristi cum corpore Papæ consonat, 687.b. Argumenta alia, Papam esse Antichristum proponuntur, 688.689. Argumenta contraria proponuntur, 690. a. dilunntur, ib. b. æmulus Christi Papa est, ib. a. Deum se facit, ib. b. Canonizatione sua alios Deificat, II.711. in ea Canonizatione sæpe errat, ibid. b.
units.tr: The Pope of Rome: his private spirit, I.44.a. He is Antichristian, 59.b. Who were the first so called, 561.b. He falsely derives his hierarchy from the Apostles, II.198.a. He has not hitherto been able to settle the dispute between the Preachers and the Franciscans about grace, 216, 217. He wrongly claims for himself the right to confirm or dispense vows, 370.b. Impeccability and infallibility are sacrilegiously attributed to him, 531.a. He is the greatest glutton, 598.a. He boasts himself the monarch of the Church, 639, 640. He himself defined his power at the Council of Florence, 639.a. He wishes to be the head of the Church, ib. b. He exalts his power above every other temporal power, 641.b. He is not the universal Bishop of the Church, 642.a. He has no temporal power, neither by divine nor by human right, 642.b ff. Arguments to the contrary are refuted, 643.a. He cannot impose laws on the Church, 646.b, 646.a. He also falsely claims judicial power for himself, 647.a. He appoints magistrates, ibid. b. He convokes councils, etc.; the wickedness of that power is shown, ib. d; 648.a. He is not Christ's vicar, 649.b. He is not the successor of Peter, 656. He is not the head of the Church, 660.b. He can err, ibid. b; 661. Arguments for his supremacy are overturned, 661.b. He does not have the supreme right of electing and ordaining ministers of the Church, 663. His ... through councils, 676.b. He is attacked, 677.a. Opposing arguments are debated, ib. b. Arguments for his supremacy are refuted, 678.b. In that the Pope, performing the office of the Pope, is Antichrist, 683.b, which is proved by very many arguments, ibid. and 684.a. He denies that Jesus is the Christ and has come in the flesh, 684. He usurps the threefold mediatorial office of Christ, ibid. He exalts himself above every Augustus, ibid. He shows himself to be God, ibid. He is the man of sin, 685.a. [ἀντίχριστος], ibid. The crimes that belong to him: the abomination of whoredoms, the itch for blasphemy, cyclopean tyranny; magical impiety, spiritual trafficking and avarice, 685.b. The periods of Antichrist distinguished by Daniel agree with the Pope, 686. The body of Antichrist accords with the body of the Pope, 687.b. Other arguments are put forward that the Pope is Antichrist, 688, 689. Arguments to the contrary are put forward, 690.a, and are answered, ib. b. The Pope is a rival of Christ, ib. a. He makes himself God, ib. b. By his canonization he deifies others, II.711. In that canonization he often errs, ibid. b.

units.la: Peccatum quoad vitiositatem actus Deo tribui non potest, I. 269. a. proin Deus nullo modo peccati author dici potest, ib. b. 270. a. units.tr: Sin, as regards the wickedness of the act, cannot be attributed to God, I. 269. a. Therefore God can in no way be called the author of sin, ibid. b. 270. a. How God decreed to permit sin, I. 151. a. 154. a. How he permits it, 265. b. In sin the act or motion of the sinner must be distinguished from the inherent wickedness, 269. a. How sins are subject to the Providence of God, 268. b.

units.la: Perseverantia Sanctorum: ejusdem ad salutem necessitas, 377. a. cum certitudine Gratiæ nexus, ibid. definitur, 378. a. Non quorumvis hominum nec quævis est, ibid. b. Dei donum est; non habitus moralis, 379. a. Fundamenta ejus sunt œconomicæ operationes trium S. Trinit. Personarum, 379. Dei Patris ad vitam æternam electio, 380. ejus cum cæteris gratiæ beneficiis nexus perseverantiam potenter evincit, 380. b. Dei Filii operatio œconomica fœdere gratiæ in se Mediatore initio redimentis, 381. a. Fœdus gratiæ in Christo initum fidem & obedientiam perseverantem promittit, ibid. b. Fœdus gratiæ æternum perseverantiam præsupponit, 382. a. Protectio fœderatorum adversus perseverantiæ hostes perseverantiam evincit, 382. b. nititur promissione Christi, 383. a. Promissionis illius confirmatio quoad modum comparativum eandem probat, 383. b. item Dei custodia fidelium ad salutem, ibid. nec non promissionum illarum confirmatio per facta & signa, ibid. 384. comparatio ne fœderis gratiæ cum conjugio, 384. a. cum Testamento, ib. b. cum statutis æternæ Providentiæ, 385. Confirmatione ex factis, ibid. Juramenta, quibus
units.tr: The perseverance of the saints: its necessity for salvation, 377. a. Its link with the certainty of grace, ibid. It is defined, 378. a. It belongs not to just any men, nor in every way, ibid. b. It is a gift of God, not a moral habit, 379. a. Its foundations are the economical operations of the three Persons of the Holy Trinity, 379. The election of God the Father to eternal life, 380. Its connection with the other benefits of grace powerfully proves perseverance, 380. b. The economical operation of God the Son, who as Mediator in the covenant of grace redeems at the beginning, 381. a. The covenant of grace entered into in Christ promises faith and persevering obedience, ibid. b. The eternal covenant of grace presupposes perseverance, 382. a. The protection of those in covenant against the enemies of perseverance proves perseverance, 382. b. It rests on the promise of Christ, 383. a. The confirmation of that promise, as to its comparative mode, proves the same, 383. b. Likewise God's keeping of the faithful unto salvation, ibid. And also the confirmation of those promises by deeds and signs, ibid. 384. Comparison of the covenant of grace with marriage, 384. a. With a testament, ibid. b. With the statutes of eternal Providence, 385. Confirmation from deeds, ibid. Oaths, by which

units.la: bus eædem confirmantur, 385. b. Earundem Testibus ex Cœlo & ex terra, 385. b. Sacrificio Christi, 386. Signis, ut sunt convivia spiritualia, arrhabo & sigillum Spiritus S.
