units.tr: they are confirmed, 385. b. Their witnesses from heaven and from earth, 385. b. The sacrifice of Christ, 386. By signs, such as spiritual feasts, the earnest and seal of the Holy Spirit. Sacraments as seals of grace, ibid. Prayers and thanksgiving confirm the same, 387. Likewise the impulsive cause of the covenant of grace, the highest love of God, and its final cause, the praise of glory, 388. a. Christ, the foundation of the covenant of grace, proves the same, 388. a. As servant, having become the reward of his work, he receives a people as inheritance, 388. As Mediator, the surety of believers, 389.

units.la: Perseverantiæ sanctorum doctrina in veteri Ecclesia illibata obtinuit, II.401. b. hostes Pelagiani, 401. b. Tridentini, 402. a. adversa argumenta diluuntur, ib. b. 403. a. ejus comes certitudo salutis, 409. a.
units.tr: The doctrine of the perseverance of the saints obtained unimpaired in the ancient Church, II. 401. b. Its enemies: the Pelagians, 401. b. The Tridentine (Council of Trent), 402. a. Adverse arguments are dissolved, ib. b. 403. a. Its companion is certainty of salvation, 409. a.

units.la: Personæ vocabulum quando in Divinis adhiberi cœperit, I.111. a. Personarum in S.S. Trinitate distinctio inter se, I.119. a. & ab essentia, 119. b. per proprietates personales, ibid. 120. a. Ordinis earum distinctio, 122. a. sed nulla ibi est subordinatio majoris & minorum, ibid. b.
units.tr: The word "person" when it began to be used in divine matters, I. 111. a. The distinction of the Persons in the Holy Trinity among themselves, I. 119. a. And from the essence, 119. b. Through personal properties, ibid. 120. a. The order of their distinction, 122. a. But there is no subordination of greater and lesser there, ibid. b.

units.la: Personarum sacrarum mystica significatio eruitur, I. 686. a.
units.tr: The mystical significance of the sacred Persons is brought out, I. 686. a.

units.la: Perspicuitas Scripturæ, I.46. a. variis argumentis probatur, 47. vide Scriptura & Breviar.
units.tr: Perspicuity of Scripture, I.46. a. is proved by various arguments, 47. See Scripture & Breviar.

units.la: Petiti error statuentis, esse quasdam naturales in homine ad prophetandum dispositiones, I. 441. b.
units.tr: Petitus's error, holding that there are certain natural dispositions in man for prophesying, I.441. b.

units.la: Petra spiritualis Vet.Test. Christus est, I.493. a. super qua Ecclesia ædificata est, 56. b.
units.tr: Spiritual rock in the Old Testament is Christ, I.493. a. the rock upon which the Church was built, 56. b.

units.la: Petrus non est Petra Ecclesiæ. I. 56. b. nullam præ reliquis Apostolis eminentiæ prærogativam habuit, 198. b. post abnegationem triplicem triplici confessione instauratur, II.63. a. qualis ipsi per claves regni cœlorum collata sit potestas? II.589. a. quæ in ejus persona toti Ecclesiæ collata est, ibid. b. Non est institutus vicarius Christi, II.650. a. ejus supra reliquos Apostolos prærogativa, 650. b. Primatus ejus variis argumentis refellitur, 651. Adversariorum objectiones diluuntur, 652. Petra & Petrus quantum differant, 652. b. Clavium potestas non soli Petro data est, 653. quæ non herilis aut dominica, sed ministerialis fuit, 654. a. Petrus suprematum nunquam usurpavit, 655. b. successorem nullum habuit, 656. b. an Romæ unquam fuerit, incertum est, 657. a. nec Adversarii evincere possunt, ibid. b. saltem Episcopatu Romæ non est functus, 658. a. Argumenta contraria refelluntur, ib. b.
units.tr: Peter is not the rock of the Church, I.56. b. He had no pre-eminent prerogative above the other apostles, 198. b. After his threefold denial he is restored by a threefold confession, II.63. a. What power was conferred on him through the keys of the kingdom of heaven? II.589. a. The power conferred on him was given to the whole Church, ibid. b. He was not instituted as Christ's vicar, II.650. a. His prerogative above the other apostles, 650. b. His primacy is refuted by various arguments, 651. The objections of the opponents are answered, 652. How far do Peter and the rock differ? 652. b. The power of the keys was not given to Peter alone, 653. It was not lordly or dominical but ministerial, 654. a. Peter never claimed supremacy, 655. b. He had no successor, 656. b. Whether he was ever at Rome is uncertain, 657. a. Nor can the opponents prove it, ibid. b. At least he did not hold the episcopate at Rome, 658. a. The contrary arguments are refuted, ib. b.

units.la: Petri Martyris Decalogi divisio notatur, I.513. a.
units.tr: The division of the Decalogue by Peter Martyr is noted, I.513. a.

units.la: Peyrerius Præadamitarum figmentum peperit, I.232. a.
units.tr: Peyrerius gave birth to the fiction of the Preadamites, I.232. a.

units.la: Pharisæi cur peccatum in Spiritum S. comisisse dicantur? I. 359. a. eorum justitia Legalis à Christo redarguitur, II.92. b.
units.tr: Pharisees: why are they said to have committed the sin against the Holy Spirit? I.359. a. Their legal righteousness is refuted by Christ, II.92. b.

units.la: Philautia quæ & quando licita sit? I. 505. b. recta & perversa capitaliter à se ipsis diffident, 506. a. 507. b. recta amicitiæ & civitatum principium fuit, ib. proximum sicut se ipsum amat, 508. a. Natura prior est, sed proximi dignior, 509. a.
units.tr: Self-love: what is it, and when is it lawful? I.505. b. Right and perverse self-love chiefly differ from each other, 506. a. 507. b. Right self-love was the beginning of friendship and of states, ib. Loving the neighbour as oneself, 508. a. Self-love is prior in nature, but the neighbour is more worthy, 509. a.

units.la: Philosophi gentiles Deum verum non cognoverunt, I. 4. a. Providentiam tamen Numinis agnoverunt, 243. b. de mundi creatione & æternitate vana cogitarunt, 186. a. nonnullorum stultus divitiarum contemptus, 605. b.
units.tr: The philosophers of the Gentiles did not know the true God, I.4. a. Yet they recognised the providence of the Deity, 243. b. They thought vainly about the creation and eternity of the world, 186. a. Some showed a foolish contempt for riches, 605. b.

units.la: Philosophia non est Scripturæ interpres, I. 49. a. Nihil in sana philosophia verum est, quod in Theologia falsum fit, I.49. b. Platonica & Pythagorica Theologiam mysticam peperit, I.19. b.
units.tr: Philosophy is not the interpreter of Scripture, I.49. a. Nothing is true in sound philosophy that is false in theology, I.49. b. Platonic and Pythagorean philosophy gave birth to mystical theology, I.19. b.

units.la: Philostratus Jesum inter & Apollonium Thyanæum comparationem instituens arguitur, I 65. a.
units.tr: Philostratus is charged with drawing a comparison between Jesus and Apollonius of Tyana, I.65. a.

units.la: Phœnicis longævitas fabulosa est, I.213. b.
units.tr: The longevity of the Phoenicians is fabulous, I.213. b.

units.la: Phraseologia sacramentalis duplex distinguenda, I. 398. a. ejus causa in Scriptura, ib.
units.tr: Sacramental phraseology is to be distinguished in two ways, I.398. a. Its cause lies in Scripture, ib.

units.la: Φυλακή, Matth. 5:25. non est Purgatorium, II.702. b.
units.tr: Phylake [Φυλακή], Matt. 5:25, is not Purgatory, II.702. b.

units.la: Φυλακτήρια Pharisæorum qualia fuerint? I.671. a.
units.tr: What were the phylacteries [Φυλακτήρια] of the Pharisees? I.671. a.

units.la: Φωναμός, Heb. 6:4. non est Baptismus, II.447. a.
units.tr: Photismos [φωτισμός], Heb. 6:4, is not Baptism, II.447. a.

units.la: Piacularia sacrificia quæ & qualia fuerint? I.656. a. iis id peculiare fuit, quod pœna vicaria illis irrogata fuit, 657. a. quid adumbraverint, 676. a. 679. a. Piacularia sacra non oblata quæ fuerint, 661. a.
units.tr: Expiatory sacrifices: what were they, and what were they like? I.656. a. What was peculiar to them was that a vicarious penalty was inflicted on them, 657. a. What they foreshadowed, 676. a. 679. a. What were the expiatory sacred things that were not offered? 661. a.

units.la: Pilati de Christi innocentia testimonium, II.101. b.
units.tr: Pilate's testimony to the innocence of Christ, II.101. b.

units.la: Piscatio Apostolorum post Christi resurrectionem, II. 63. a.
units.tr: The fishing of the apostles after Christ's resurrection, II.63. a.

units.la: Piscatoris (Joh.) de Christi justitia activa opinio, I. 183. b. refutatur, 185. a.
units.tr: The opinion of Piscator (John) on the active righteousness of Christ, I.183. b. is refuted, 185. a.

units.la: Piscium origo prima, I.212. b. 213. a.
units.tr: Fishes: their first origin, I.212. b. 213. a.

units.la: Pisis quæ sit hujus vocis vis & emphasis? I, 249. a,
units.tr: Pisis: what is the force and emphasis of this word? I.249. a.

units.la: Placabilitas qualis sit virtus, I.578. a. II.295. b.
units.tr: Placability: what kind of virtue is it? I.578. a. II.295. b.

units.la: Placandi Numen varii ritus unde? II.295. b.
units.tr: Whence come the various rites for placating the Deity? II.295. b.

units.la: Plagium qualis furti species? I.608. a.
units.tr: Kidnapping (plagium): what kind of theft is it? I.608. a.

units.la: Planetariorum vanitas arguitur, I.209. a. 210. seq.
units.tr: The vanity of the planets is exposed, I.209. a. 210. ff.

units.la: Plato Deum pro summo Bono agnovit, I. 774. a. ejus Hierarchia Angelorum ficta, I. 280. a. primus Angelos tutelares colere docuit, 284. b. ejus Philosophia Theologiam mysticam peperit, I.19. b. annus maximus inane figmentum est, I I.735. b. ejus & sequacium de spectris opinio, I.297. b.
units.tr: Plato acknowledged God as the highest Good, I.774. a. His hierarchy of angels is fictitious, I.280. a. He was the first to teach the worship of guardian angels, 284. b. His philosophy gave birth to mystical theology, I.19. b. The Great Year is an empty fiction, II.735. b. The opinion of him and his followers about spectres, I.297. b.

units.la: Plebs an potestatem habeat Ecclesiæ ministros vocandi & eligendi? II.568. a.
units.tr: The common people: do they have the power to call and elect the ministers of the Church? II.568. a.

units.la: Plenitudo temporis qualis œconomia fit, I I.3. a. Deitatis in Christo, II.6. b.
units.tr: The fullness of time: what kind of economy is it? II.3. a. The fullness of the Deity in Christ, II.6. b.

units.la: Πληροφορία fidei Spiritus S. causa est, I.59. b. fidei salvificæ propria est, II.251. b.
units.tr: Full assurance [plērophoria, πληροφορία] of faith is caused by the Holy Spirit, I.59. b. It is proper to saving faith, II.251. b.

units.la: Πνεῦμα quid? Deo, Angelis & animæ tributum immateriale est, I.272. a.
units.tr: Pneuma [πνεῦμα]: what is it? Ascribed to God, angels and the soul, it is immaterial, I.272. a.

units.la: Pneumatomachorum elenchus, I.140. b. Historia, 141, 143.
units.tr: Refutation of the Pneumatomachi, I.140. b. History, 141, 143.

units.la: Poculum, quod à se transferri Christus petiit, fuit intuitus iræ Divinæ contra peccatum, I 145. a.
units.tr: The cup from which Christ asked to be taken away was the sight of divine wrath against sin, I.145. a.

units.la: Pœna damni & sensus distinctio improbatur, I.361. a. una sine altera esse nequit, 323. b. 324. a. peccatidistinguenda, 289. a. ejus variæ differentiæ & species, 363. b. eam Deus in hac vita fidelibus variè temperat, 368. a. infidelibus non sunt satisfactiones pro peccato, ibid. b. quid sint, 369. b. æternam peccati pœnam quomodo Christus sustinuerit, II, 116. a. Vicaria sacrificiorum piacularium Christi vicariam satisfactionem notavit, 677. a. 657. a.
units.tr: Punishment: the distinction between punishment of loss and punishment of sense is rejected, I.361. a. Neither can exist without the other, 323. b. 324. a. Punishments are to be distinguished by sin, 289. a. Its various differences and kinds, 363. b. God variously tempers it for believers in this life, 368. a. For unbelievers there are no satisfactions for sin, ibid. b. What they are, 369. b. How Christ endured the eternal punishment of sin, II.116. a. Vicarious: the vicarious satisfaction of Christ was signified by the expiatory sacrifices, 677. a. 657. a.

units.la: Pœnarum infernalium atrocitas, II.759. b. differentia, 760. a. privativæ seu damni, 760. a. positivæ seu sensus, ibid. b. earundem ordo, 761. b. æternitas, 762. a. gradus, 763. a. elenchus æternitatem pœnarum infernalium negantium, ibid. b.
units.tr: Punishments of hell: their atrocity, II.759. b. Their difference, 760. a. Privative, or of loss, 760. a. Positive, or of sense, ibid. b. Their order, 761. b. Their eternity, 762. a. Their degrees, 763. a. Refutation of those who deny the eternity of the punishments of hell, ibid. b.

units.la: Pœnarum capitalium Hebræorum species, I. 711. b. Mosaicarum ἐπάνεσις, 715. b. illa בְּרֵת seu excidii qualis fuerit? 713. b.
units.tr: Punishments: the capital punishments of the Hebrews and their kinds, I.711. b. The Mosaic remission [epanesis, ἐπάνεσις], 715. b. What was karet [kareth, בְּרֵת], that is, excision? 713. b.

units.la: Pœnitentia non meretur salutem, I.324. a. ejus signa æterna, 325. b. vid. Resipiscentia, illa veteris Ecclesiæ non fuit sacramentum, I I.447. b. impugnatur, 500. a.
units.tr: Repentance does not merit salvation, I.324. a. Its marks are eternal, 325. b. See Repentance. The repentance of the early Church was not a sacrament, II.447. b. It is attacked, II.500. a.

units.la: Pœnitudo quomodo Deo tribuatur, I. 80. a.
units.tr: Regret: how is it ascribed to God? I.80. a.

units.la: Ποιμαίνειν pascere non regiam potestatem significat, II. 647. a. quod fusius explicatur, 654. b. 655. a.
units.tr: To shepherd [poimainein, ποιμαίνειν] does not signify royal power, II.647. a. This is explained more fully, 654. b. 655. a.

units.la: Pokoke Anglus laudatur, II.733. a.
units.tr: Pocock, the Englishman, is praised, II.733. a.

units.la: Politia Ecclesiæ qualis sit, II.557. b. 558. a. Mosaica externa typus fuit regni Christi spiritualis & æterni, 738. a. Christo in carne manifestato abolitanec amplius restituenda est, 738. b.
units.tr: Polity of the Church: what kind is it? II.557. b. 558. a. The external Mosaic polity was a type of the spiritual and eternal kingdom of Christ, 738. a. Abolished when Christ was manifested in the flesh, it is not to be restored again, 738. b.

units.la: Pollinctura cadaverum apud veteres, II. 50. b.
units.tr: Embalming of corpses among the ancients, II.50. b.

units.la: Pollutio legalis non caruit mysterio, I.690. a.
units.tr: Legal defilement was not without mystery, I.690. a.

units.la: Polygamia cum matrimonii prima institutione pugnat, I.231. a. ejus propugnatores fuit Lyterus, ib.
units.tr: Polygamy is at odds with the first institution of marriage, I.231. a. Its defender was Lyterus, ib.

units.la: Polytheismi origo ostenditur, I.112. b.
units.tr: The origin of polytheism is shown, I.112. b.

units.la: Pontifex noster quomodo Christus factus sit, I. 379. a. 380. a. Veteris Test. non Papæ, sed Christi typum gessit, I I.640. b. lacrificans cum Christo confertur, 678. b. ejus conditiones, dignitas, munus, vestitus, &c. 668. b.
units.tr: Our High Priest: how Christ was made one, I.379. a. 380. a. He bore the type of Christ, not of the Pope, in the Old Testament, II.640. b. The sacrificing priest is compared with Christ, 678. b. His qualifications, dignity, office, vestments, etc., 668. b.

units.la: Pontificii de usu rationis in Theologia, I.11. a. 12. a. eorum error circa articulos fundamentales, 17. a. de Theologiæ methodo, 21. a. de Scripturæ necessitate, 124. b. de Scripturæ Divinitate, ibid. 25. a. De Ecclesiæ testimonio, 28. 29. 30. de Scripturæ authoritate, ibid. 31. de Scripturæ fortuita occasione, 33. a. Scripturæ perfectionem se agnoscere simulant, 41. a. in dogmate de Traditionibus judaizant, 41. a. refutantur, ibid. 43. 44. de Scripturæ sensu, 45. b. de perspicuitate Scripturæ, 47. b. authentia Scripturæ, 50. 51. de Vulgatæ versionis authentia, ibid. 51. b. de Scripturæ Lectione in versionibus, ib. 52. b. de Scripturæ judicio, ib. 54. b. 55. a. eorum Polytheismus in Ἀπαθεία sua, I. 113. b. certitudinem salutis impugnant, 171. b. creatores sui creatoris esse impie volunt, 189. Fœdus operum duntaxat agnoscunt, 305. Scholastici reatum peccati formam faciunt, 338. Imaginem Dei in homine per lapsum amissam esse negant, 338. a. Concupiscentiam morbum corporis potius quàm mentis faciunt, 349. a. in quo natura peccati originalis confisstat Ecclesia Rom. hactenus non definivit. ibid. b. Concupiscentiam veri nominis peccatum esse Concil. Trident, negat, 351. a. de a. de poena peccati originalis in infantibus nihil certi definiverunt, 161. a. venialia peccata eorum, ibid. b. Foedus gratiae in novum foedus operum convertunt, 384. b. Sacramenta gratiam conferre ex opere operato, 396. 397. Legem & Evangelium confundunt, 402. a. Foederis gratiae unitatem in V. & Nov. Test. negant. 410. a. Patres V. T. salutem ante Christi in coelum ascensionem consecutos esse negant, 413. b. semen mulieris caput Serpentis contriturum B. Mariam faciunt, 413. b. ex operibus legis justitiam quaerentes refelluntur, 479. a. secundum Decalogi praeceptum cur eraserint? 512. a. idololatriam male defiiniunt, 530. a. multiplex eorum idololatria redarguitur, 538. b. Ecclesiasticos male a juramento eximunt, 545. a. Eorum errores, de conceptione B. Mariae utrum cum an sine peccato originali, 117. a. de nativitate Christi. Christum uterum matris aperuisse negantium, 24. a. per Transubstantiationem corpus Christi unicum multiplicant, 26. b. de locali Christi in infernum descensu ad liberandos Patres, 52. b. de Mediatore Christo tantum secundum humanam naturam, 81. a. abnegatae satisfactionis Christi rei peragantur, 121. b. Regnum Christi spirituale fere in terrestre commutant, 133. b. refutantur, 134. a. Regium Christi munus corrumpunt, 137. b. Consilia Evangelica obtrudunt, 164. b. Christum novam legem tulisse, 168. a. doctrinam Evangelii pervertunt, 187. a. b. Fidem historicam, miraculosam & justificantem eandem speciei esse asserunt, 241. a. fides eorum implicita, 249. b. charitatem propriam fidei formam faciunt, 255. b. remissionem peccatorum eorundem abolitionem explicant, 288. a. reatum tamen poenae superesse pertendunt, ib. Error satisfactionum humanarum, 290. sanctificationem & justificationem confundunt, 313. b. error circa poenitentiam, 327. a. eorum jactata bona opera perstringuntur, 331. b. Jejuna eorum de jejuniis doctrina nil pietatis vel religionis habet, 365. a. dies festi rejiciuntur, 366. 367. a. Vota perstringuntur, 368. b. oppugnant aperte gratiae certitudinem, 421. a. Lingua peregrina in cultu Dei publico utuntur, 431. a. sacra tua celant, 433. de Baptismo Johannis error, 438. de Baptismi ritibus superstitiosis, 460. a. Romanam Ecclesiam Catholicam faciunt, 514. b. invisibilem Ecclesiam tollunt, & visibilem Monarchiam Papalem faciunt, 534. a. eorum adversus Magistratus blasphemiae, 618. b. Magistratum a religionis negotio plane removent, 625. eorum circa statum animae separatae errores proponuntur, 709. confutantur, 710.
units.tr: Papists: on the use of reason in theology, I.11. a. 12. a. Their error concerning the fundamental articles, 17. a. On the method of theology, 21. a. On the necessity of Scripture, 124. b. On the divinity of Scripture, ibid. 25. a. On the testimony of the Church, 28. 29. 30. On the authority of Scripture, ibid. 31. On the chance occasion of Scripture, 33. a. They pretend to acknowledge the perfection of Scripture, 41. a. They judaize in the doctrine of traditions, 41. a. Refuted, ibid. 43. 44. On the sense of Scripture, 45. b. On the perspicuity of Scripture, 47. b. On the authenticity of Scripture, 50. 51. On the authenticity of the Vulgate version, ibid. 51. b. On the reading of Scripture in versions, ib. 52. b. On the judgment of Scripture, ib. 54. b. 55. a. Their polytheism in their apatheia, I.113. b. They attack the certainty of salvation, 171. b. They impiously wish creatures to be the creators of their Creator, 189. They acknowledge only a covenant of works, 305. The Scholastics make the guilt of sin its form, 338. They deny that the image of God in man was lost through the fall, 338. a. They make concupiscence a disease of the body rather than of the mind, 349. a. The Roman Church has not hitherto defined in what the nature of original sin consists, ibid. b. They deny that concupiscence is truly sin, Council of Trent, 351. a. They have defined nothing certain about the punishment of original sin in infants, 161. a. Their venial sins, ibid. b. They turn the covenant of grace into a new covenant of works, 384. b. They make sacraments confer grace ex opere operato, 396. 397. They confuse Law and Gospel, 402. a. They deny the unity of the covenant of grace in the Old and New Testaments, 410. a. They deny that the Fathers of the Old Testament obtained salvation before Christ's ascension into heaven, 413. b. They make the Blessed Virgin the one who will crush the serpent's head, 413. b. Those seeking righteousness from the works of the law are refuted, 479. a. Why did they erase the second commandment of the Decalogue? 512. a. They define idolatry badly, 530. a. Their manifold idolatry is rebuked, 538. b. They wrongly exempt ecclesiastics from oaths, 545. a. Their errors: whether the conception of the Blessed Virgin was with or without original sin, 117. a. On the nativity of Christ: those denying that Christ opened his mother's womb, 24. a. Through transubstantiation they multiply the one body of Christ, 26. b. On Christ's local descent into hell to free the Fathers, 52. b. On Christ as Mediator only according to his human nature, 81. a. They carry out in practice the denial of Christ's satisfaction, 121. b. They turn the spiritual kingdom of Christ almost into an earthly one, 133. b. Refuted, 134. a. They corrupt the kingly office of Christ, 137. b. They obtrude evangelical counsels, 164. b. That Christ gave a new law, 168. a. They pervert the doctrine of the Gospel, 187. a. b. They assert that historical, miraculous and justifying faith are of the same kind, 241. a. Their faith is implicit, 249. b. They make love the proper form of faith, 255. b. They explain the remission of sins as their abolition, 288. a. They nevertheless maintain that the guilt of punishment remains, ib. The error of human satisfactions, 290. They confuse sanctification and justification, 313. b. Error concerning repentance, 327. a. Their boasted good works are censured, 331. b. Their doctrine of fasts has nothing of piety or religion, 365. a. Feast days are rejected, 366. 367. a. Vows are censured, 368. b. They openly attack the certainty of grace, 421. a. They use a foreign tongue in the public worship of God, 431. a. They conceal the sacred things, 433. On the error about John's baptism, 438. On the superstitious rites of baptism, 460. a. They make the Roman Church the Catholic Church, 514. b. They abolish the invisible Church and make a visible Papal monarchy, 534. a. Their blasphemies against the magistrate, 618. b. They remove the magistrate altogether from the business of religion, 625. Their errors concerning the state of the separated soul are set out, 709. Refuted, 710.

units.la: Populus peculii Christi Regis haereditas est, II. 130. a. Papalis est illa bestia, quae Papam seu Pseudoprophetam portat, 688. a. Cui Papa dominatur, ib.
units.tr: The people is the inheritance of Christ the King, the peculiar people; II. 130. a. That beast is papal, which carries the Pope or the pseudo-prophet; 688. a. The Pope lords it over it, ib.

units.la: Πογεσίας λόγων quid significet, I. 592, 593.
units.tr: What does Πογεσίας λόγων [Πογεσίας λόγων] mean? I. 592, 593.

units.la: Porphyrius de sacrificiorum origine laudatur, I. 445. b.
units.tr: Porphyry is praised concerning the origin of sacrifices; I. 445. b.

units.la: Porta apud Veteres Hebraeos quid? I. 711. a. in illis jus dici consueverat, ibid.
units.tr: What was a gate among the ancient Hebrews? I. 711. a. Justice was customarily administered at the gates among them, ibid.

units.la: Possessionum vel communio vel proprietas quando coeperit, I. 235. Communio nulla universaliter obtinere potest, I I. 602. b. qualis in Ecclesia prima Hierosolymitana obtinuerit, 603. a. moderata cupiditas bona est, 605. a. duobus modis legitime comparantur, 607. a.
units.tr: When did possessions begin to be held in common or as private property? I. 235. Community of goods cannot be universally maintained; II. 602. b. What kind of community obtained in the first Church of Jerusalem; 603. a. Moderate desire is good; 605. a. Possessions are lawfully acquired in two ways; 607. a.

units.la: Possibile vel impossibile respectu Dei quid sit, I. 101. b.
units.tr: Possible or impossible with respect to God: what is it? I. 101. b.

units.la: Postillarum origo & primus author, I I. 595. a.
units.tr: The Postils: their origin and first author; II. 595. a.

units.la: Potentia Dei explicatur, I. 101. a. Omnipotentia, ibid. ejus objectum est possibile, ib. b. est vel absoluta vel ordinata, ibid. b. 102. a. Angelorum ingens est, 275. Dei in hominis conversione, I I. 222. a.
units.tr: The power of God is explained; I. 101. a. Omnipotence, ibid. Its object is the possible; ib. b. It is either absolute or ordained; ibid. b. 102. a. The power of the angels is great; 275. God's power in the conversion of man; II. 222. a.

units.la: Potentiae animi quae & quales sint, I. 347. a.
units.tr: The powers of the soul: what they are and of what kind; I. 347. a.

units.la: Potentia obedientialis creaturarum qualis sit, 252. b.
units.tr: The obediential power of creatures: what kind it is; 252. b.

units.la: Potestas & potentia differunt, II. 33. a. etiam in Christo Mediatore, ib.
units.tr: Power and potency differ; II. 33. a. This is so also in Christ the Mediator, ib.

units.la: Potestas Dei explicatur, I. 102. b. est vel absoluta vel ordinata, ibid. 103. a. docendi quam Christus habuit, II. 95. a. Clavium data Ecclesiae ministris, I. 321. in quo consistat, 587. b. distinguitur in minorem, magnam majorem & maximam, 587. 588. Herilis, ib. Ministerialis in quo consistat, 589. a. an & quatenus ad Magistratum pertineat, 605. 606. a. vid. Claves. Ecclesiae in dandis praeceptis quae sit, I I. 559. b. quatenus obligent, ib.
units.tr: The power of God is explained; I. 102. b. It is either absolute or ordained; ibid. 103. a. The teaching power which Christ had; II. 95. a. The power of the keys given to the ministers of the Church; I. 321. In what it consists; 587. b. It is distinguished into lesser, great, greater and greatest; 587, 588. Lordly; ib. Ministerial: in what it consists; 589. a. Whether and how far it pertains to the magistrate; 605, 606. a. See Keys. The power of the Church in giving precepts: what it is; II. 559. b. How far such precepts bind; ib.

units.la: Potestas Papalis supra omnem potestatem temporalem effertur, I I. 641. a. Solis & Lunae similitudine, ibid. quadruplex statuitur. ibid. Politica ejus potestas, Ecclesiasticae potestat non subordinatur, 641. b. seq. superior vel inferior quo sensu dicatur, 643. b.
units.tr: The power of the Papacy is exalted above all temporal power; II. 641. a. By the likeness of the sun and the moon, ibid. It is laid down as fourfold, ibid. Its political power is not subordinate to ecclesiastical power; 641. b. seq. In what sense it is called superior or inferior; 643. b.

units.la: Potus sacramentalis V. T. I. 492. b. seq. aqua exPetra fuit typus sanguinis Christi, ib. vide Petra.
units.tr: The sacramental drink in the Old Testament; I. 492. b. seq. The water from the rock was a type of Christ's blood; ib. See Rock.

units.la: Praeceptum Christi quo sensu vel vetus vel novum dicatur, I. 402. a.
units.tr: In what sense the precept of Christ is called old or new; I. 402. a.

units.la: Praecepta Decalogi. eorum tenor; Primi, I. 502. a. secundi, 523. b. tertii, 541. b. quarti, 551. a. sanctio ejus, 557. a. quinti, 563. est humanae societatis coagulum, 564. b. ejus sanctio, 573. a. sexti tenor, 575. a. septimi, 588. b. octavi scopus varius, 601. a. noni, 620. b. decimi, 638. b. ejus a caeteris distinctio, ib. vid. Breviar. item Decalogus.
units.tr: The precepts of the Decalogue: their tenor. Of the first, I. 502. a; of the second, 523. b; of the third, 541. b; of the fourth, 551. a; its sanction, 557. a. Of the fifth, 563, it is the cement of human society, 564. b; its sanction, 573. a. Tenor of the sixth, 575. a; of the seventh, 588. b; the eighth has a varied scope, 601. a; the ninth, 620. b; the tenth, 638. b; its distinction from the others, ib. See Breviary; likewise Decalogue.

units.la: Praeceptis Decalogi Christus nulla nova addidit, II. 168. 2.
units.tr: Christ added no new precepts to the precepts of the Decalogue; II. 168. 2.

units.la: Praecognitio Dei quid? I. 149. a.
units.tr: What is the foreknowledge of God? I. 149. a.

units.la: Praecones Verbi Dei quales esse debeant, I I. 594. b. eorum ante reformationem barbaries, 595. a. eorum proprium munus, ibid. b. missio jam in V. T. praedicta fuit, 188. b.
units.tr: The heralds of the Word of God: what sort they ought to be; II. 594. b. Their barbarism before the Reformation; 595. a. Their proper office; ibid. b. Their mission was already foretold in the Old Testament; 188. b.

units.la: Praeconium Evangelii cum praeconio Legis non semper ἀσυμπερ est, I. 644. b. praecipuum N. T. est, I I. 172. a.
units.tr: The preaching of the Gospel is not always in agreement with the preaching of the Law [ἀσυμπερ]; I. 644. b. The chief thing in the New Testament is this; II. 172. a.

units.la: Praeda ab hostibus devictis reportata quomodo fuerit dividenda, I. 737. a.
units.tr: How spoil taken from defeated enemies is to be divided; I. 737. a.

units.la: Praedestinatio Dei, I. 149. a.
units.tr: The predestination of God; I. 149. a.

units.la: Praedestinatio definitur, I. 154. b. vide Breviar. Electionis & Reprobationis decretum connotat, ibid. Non tantum circa hominum qualitates, sed circa ipsas singulas personas versatur, 155. b. Ejus doctrina in Ecclesia non dissimulari, sed tradi plebi Christianae debet, I. 181. a.
units.tr: Predestination is defined; I. 154. b. See Breviary. It implies the decree of election and reprobation, ibid. It concerns not only the qualities of men but the individual persons themselves; 155. b. Its doctrine ought not to be concealed in the Church but taught to the Christian people; I. 181. a.

units.la: Praedeterminantes quinam fuerint? II. 216. b.
units.tr: Who were the predeterminants? II. 216. b.

units.la: Praedicationis Evangelii efficacia admiranda, I. 27. a. Verbi promissionis viguit in familiis Patriarcharum, 436. 437. a.
units.tr: The efficacy of the preaching of the Gospel is admirable; I. 27. a. The power of the promise of the Word flourished in the families of the patriarchs; 436, 437. a.

units.la: Praedicatio Verbi Dei externa absque Spiritus S. interna operatione inutilis ad convertendum peccatorem, I I. 210. a. unde ejus diversus adeo apud auditores fructus, 212. a. 214. b. qualis esse debeat, 429. b. Ecclesiae ministris incumbit, 594. b. vide Brev.
units.tr: The external preaching of the Word of God, without the internal operation of the Holy Spirit, is useless for converting a sinner; II. 210. a. Whence its so varied fruit among hearers; 212. a. 214. b. What kind it ought to be; 429. b. It falls to the ministers of the Church; 594. b. See Breviary.

units.la: Praedictiones Divinarum in Scriptura contentarum eventus, ejus Divinitatem evincunt, I. 26, b.
units.tr: The predictions of divine things contained in Scripture, and the fulfilment of events, prove its divinity; I. 26. b.

units.la: Premium in foedere Legali promissum non ulloobedientiae merito, sed ex sola gratia credentibus collatum est, I. 477. b.
units.tr: The reward promised in the Legal covenant was bestowed not on the merit of any obedience but from grace alone on believers; I. 477. b.

units.la: Praeparatio ad S. Coenae usum in quibus consistat, II. 479. a.
units.tr: The preparation for the use of the Lord's Supper consists in what? II. 479. a.

units.la: Praescientia Dei, an ullam rebus necessitatem imponat? I. 264.
units.tr: Does God's foreknowledge impose any necessity on things? I. 264.

units.la: Praescientiste quinam fuerint, I I. 216. b. eorum & Praedeterminantium inter Pontificios dissensus, I. 277. b.
units.tr: Who were the prescientists? II. 216. b. Their dissension among the Papists, and that of the Predeterminants; I. 277. b.

units.la: Praesentia Dei cur in Scriptura de rebus nonnullis negetur, I. 73. b.
units.tr: Why is God's presence denied of certain things in Scripture? I. 73. b.

units.la: Praesentia corporis & sanguinis Christi in Eucharistia fusè explicatur, I I. 479. a. Modus ejus relativus, item spiritualis, 480. Corporalis rejicitur & refutatur, 483. seq.
units.tr: The presence of Christ's body and blood in the Eucharist is explained at length; II. 479. a. Its relative mode, likewise its spiritual mode; 480. The corporeal presence is rejected and refuted; 483. seq.

units.la: Praestigiatricis poena in V.T. qualis fuerit, I. 194. b. 715. b. vide Saga.
units.tr: The punishment of the sorceress in the Old Testament: what it was; I. 194. b; 715. b. See Witch.

units.la: Praevisionis fidei vel operum sententia infantes, surdos, amentes, &c. ab electione excludit, I. 167. b.
units.tr: The foreseen faith or works sentence excludes infants, the deaf, the insane, etc. from election; I. 167. b.

units.la: Praxis Theologiae qualis sit, I. 21. a.
units.tr: What kind of practice of theology; I. 21. a.

units.la: Precatio definitur ejusque necessitas explicatur, I. 343. b. 360. b. ejus requisita, 344. a. author in nobis Spiritus S. est, 345. (species, 346. a. formulae probantur, I I. 430. a. ejus efficacia certitudinem salutis confirmat, 416. b. Exauditio, 345. a.
units.tr: Prayer: defined, and its necessity explained; I. 343. b; 360. b. Its requisites; 344. a. The author of prayer in us is the Holy Spirit; 345. Its kinds; 346. a. Forms of prayer are approved; II. 430. a. Its efficacy confirms the certainty of salvation; 416. b. Answer to prayer; 345. a.

units.la: Precandi gestus, 352. a.
units.tr: Gestures in praying; 352. a.

units.la: Precum formulae, I. 350. a. I I. 430. a. ἡμιλέγεια, 675, a* exauditio, 345, a.
units.tr: Forms of prayer; I. 350. a; II. 430. a. ἡμιλέγεια [ἡμιλέγεια], 675. a*; answer to prayer, 345. a.

units.la: Presbyteri seu Seniores Ecclesiae an a Pastoribus docentibus peculiaris sint ordo, I I. 578. b. eorundem in Ecclesia functiones, ibid. duo eorum genera, 579. a. distinctio eorum vindicatur, ib. Seniores laici, quales olim fuerint & jam in Ecclesia sint, ib. b. quales Judaicae Ecclesiae olim Seniores fuerint, 580. b. Presbyteri jure divino Episcopis non sunt inferiores, II. 669. b. Adversariorum argumenta ad incudem revocantur. 670. a.
units.tr: Presbyters or elders: whether they are a distinct order from the teaching pastors; II. 578. b. Their functions in the Church, ibid. Two kinds of them; 579. a. Their distinction is vindicated; ib. Lay elders: what kind they once were and what they are now in the Church; ib. b. What kind the elders of the Jewish Church were; 580. b. Presbyters are by divine right not inferior to bishops; II. 669. b. The arguments of the opponents are brought to the anvil; 670. a.

units.la: Primatus in Ecclesia ad Christum pertinet, II. 557. a. Petri Papae potestatem non probat, 650. 651. vide Petrus,
units.tr: The primacy in the Church belongs to Christ; II. 557. a. It does not prove the power of Peter's Papacy; 650, 651. See Peter.
