units.tr: g

units.la: Petrus. de origine primatus Papæ Rom. luculentum est Guicciardini testimonium, I. 659. a.
units.tr: Peter: concerning the origin of the Roman Pope's primacy there is a clear testimony of Guicciardini; I. 659. a.

units.la: Primitiarum genera Deo sacrarum, I. 661. a. frugum & fructuum oblatio Minchæ vocabantur, licet integræ Sacerdotibus darentur, 653. a. earum oblatio mysticam significationem habuit, 679. a. 682. b.
units.tr: The kinds of firstfruits sacred to God; I. 661. a. The oblation of grain and fruits was called minchah, although the whole was given to the priests; 653. a. Their oblation had a mystical signification; 679. a; 682. b.

units.la: Primogenita cur Deus sibi sacra esse voluerit, I. 679. a.
units.tr: Why God wished the firstborn to be sacred to himself; I. 679. a.

units.la: Primogeniti primùm olim fungebantur Sacerdotio, I. 665. 667. a. mactabant agnum Paschalem, 487. a. in adeunda hæreditate paterna prærogativa singulari gaudebant, 729. b.
units.tr: The firstborn formerly served first as priests; I. 665, 667. a. They slaughtered the Paschal lamb; 487. a. In taking up their father's inheritance they enjoyed a singular prerogative; 729. b.

units.la: Principium quale Joh. 1:1. intelligatur? I. 132. a. In principio esse, & principium esse non est idem, 198. b.
units.tr: What is the principle in John 1:1 to be understood as? I. 132. a. To be in the beginning and to be the beginning are not the same; 198. b.

units.la: Priscillianistæ mentiri licitum esse docebant, I. 625. b.
units.tr: The Priscillianists taught that lying is lawful; I. 625. b.

units.la: Prius & posterius in Deo locum non habet, I. 150. b.
units.tr: Before and after have no place in God; I. 150. b.

units.la: Privativum & privatio quotuplex? I. 333. b. privativa quomodo à Deo cognoscantur, 83. a.
units.tr: How many kinds of privative and privation are there? I. 333. b. How privatives are known from God; 83. a.

units.la: Processio Spiritus S. à Patre & Filio, I. 138. a. 139.
units.tr: The procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son; I. 138. a; 139.

units.la: Prodigia mendacii Antichristi quænam sint, I I. 687. a.
units.tr: What are the portents of the lie of Antichrist? II. 687. a.

units.la: Προϊστάμενος in Ecclesia quis? II. 578. b.
units.tr: Who is a presiding officer [προϊστάμενος] in the Church? II. 578. b.

units.la: Prolabi quid & prolapsi, Heb. 6:4. qui sint, I I. 404. b.
units.tr: To fall away [prolabi] and the fallen, Heb. 6:4: who they are; II. 404. b.

units.la: Stoicorum quid? I. 328. a.
units.tr: What is the view of the Stoics? I. 328. a.

units.la: Promissio prima Protoplastis mysterium S. Trinitatis revelavit, I. 114. a. in fœdere operum fuit vita æterna, I. 318. b. in cœlo, 319. b. non ex sola Dei ... sed ex decentia virtutum ejus manavit, 321. a.
units.tr: The first promise to the protoplasts revealed the mystery of the Holy Trinity, I. 114. a. In the covenant of works eternal life was given, I. 318. b. In heaven, 319. b. It flowed not from God's bare will ... but from the fitness of his virtues, 321. a.

units.la: Promissiones Dei confirmantur per facta & signa, I. 384. a. comparatione cum conjugio, 384. a. cum Testamento æterno, ibid. cum statutis æternæ Providentiæ, 385. a. Factis, veluti juramento Dei, 385. b. earundem Testibus ex cœlo & ex terra, ib. continent justitiam Christi imputatam & vitam æternam, 386. a. illæ N.T. non sunt universales absolutè, sed omnium credentium, 391. a. fœderales conditionatæ sunt, 402. b. promissionum Vet. & Nov. Test. qualis sit differentia, 412. earum & comminationum differentia, 440. Abrahamo factæ spirituales fere sunt, 428. b. 430. Quinto Decalogi præcepto annexæ non tam temporales quàm spirituales sunt, 573. a. Promissiones gratiæ V. T. II. 157. b. Evangelii in N.T. 169. 170. a.
units.tr: God's promises are confirmed by deeds and signs, I. 384. a. Comparison with marriage, 384. a. With the eternal Testament, ibid. With the statutes of eternal Providence, 385. a. By deeds, as it were God's oath, 385. b. Their witnesses from heaven and from earth, ibid. They contain the imputed righteousness of Christ and eternal life, 386. a. The promises of the New Testament are not absolutely universal, but belong to all believers, 391. a. They are covenantal and conditional, 402. b. What is the difference between the promises of the Old and New Testaments? 412. The difference between promises and threats, 440. The promises made to Abraham are almost entirely spiritual, 428. b. 430. Those attached to the Fifth Commandment are spiritual rather than temporal, 573. a. The promises of grace in the Old Testament, II. 157. b. The promises of the Gospel in the New Testament, 169. 170. a.

units.la: Promissorium Juramentum an licitum sit? I. 546. b.
units.tr: Is a promissory oath lawful? I. 546. b.

units.la: Προορισμὸς seu prædefinitio quid? I. 166. a.
units.tr: What is proorismos, or predefinition? I. 166. a.

units.la: Prophetæ quinam fuerint? I. 666. b. eorum numerus, 484. a. scripta, ib. veri prophetæ proprietates, 438. a. eorum revelationis modi varii, ib. agitatio prophetica vel ad loquendum vel ad scribendum, ib. b. nec seducere neque seduci possunt, 439. a. Prophetica facultas non naturalis, sed Divina est, 440. b. eorum Scholæ quales fuerint? 442. a. Filii prophetarum seu discipuli, ibid. Triplex prophetandi periodus sub promissione, sub Lege & sub Evangelio, ibid. b. Falsus cur neci tradendus fuerit, 256. b. veri res futuras per præsens cur pronuntient, I I. 11. a.
units.tr: Who were the prophets? I. 666. b. Their number, 484. a. Their writings, ibid. The marks of a true prophet, 438. a. Their various modes of revelation, ibid. The prophetic impulse, whether to speak or to write, ibid. b. They can neither deceive nor be deceived, 439. a. The prophetic faculty is not natural but divine, 440. b. What were their schools? 442. a. The sons of the prophets, or disciples, ibid. The threefold period of prophesying: under promise, under the Law, and under the Gospel, ibid. b. Why was the false prophet to be put to death? 256. b. Why do true prophets state future things in the present tense? II. 11. a.

units.la: Prophetæ Nov. Test. quales Ecclesiæ ministri sint, I. 559. a. prophetandi libertas qualis esse debeat, I I. 634. a.
units.tr: What should the prophets of the New Testament be as ministers of the Church? I. 559. a. What freedom of prophesying ought there to be? II. 634. a.

units.la: Prophetia quid est? I. 437. b. seq. Novi Testamenti quid? I. 14. a. 200. a. Christi definitur, I I. 87. b. in carne eam potissimum obiit, 88. a. non didicit demum post baptismum in Cœlo, 89. a. sed post baptismum eam obire cœpit, 90. a. hinc in Vet. Test. הַמָּשִׁיחַ loquens dicitur, 87. b. vide Breviar. item Christus.
units.tr: What is prophecy? I. 437. b. ff. What is the New Testament? I. 14. a. 200. a. Its definition of Christ, II. 87. b. He especially discharged it in the flesh, 88. a. He did not learn it only after baptism in heaven, 89. a. But he began to discharge it after baptism, 90. a. Hence in the Old Testament he is called speaking as HaMashiach (the Messiah), 87. b. See the Breviary, and likewise Christ.

units.la: Prophetiarum & Doctrinæ Canonem Moses tradidit, I. 480. b.
units.tr: Moses handed down the canon of prophecies and of doctrine, I. 480. b.

units.la: Prophetica visio qualis fuerit, I. 480. a.
units.tr: What was prophetic vision like? I. 480. a.

units.la: Propheticum lumen an sit nota veræ Ecclesiæ? II. 551. a.
units.tr: Is the prophetic light a mark of the true Church? II. 551. a.

units.la: Propitiatorii Vet. Test. mystica significatio, I. 681. a. 683. b. 684. a.
units.tr: The mystical significance of the Old Testament mercy seat, I. 681. a. 683. b. 684. a.

units.la: Proprietas possessionum in Natura & Scriptura fundatur, I. 602.
units.tr: The ownership of property is founded in nature and in Scripture, I. 602.

units.la: Proprietates Divinæ naturæ non communicatæ sunt humanæ Christi naturæ, I I. 29. 30. &c.
units.tr: The properties of the divine nature are not communicated to the human nature of Christ, II. 29. 30. etc.

units.la: Proselyti apud Hebræos vel justitiæ vel domicilii dicebantur, I. 710. a.
units.tr: Among the Hebrews proselytes were called either of righteousness or of residence, I. 710. a.

units.la: Προσευχὴ seu petitio bonorum qualis precum species? I. 346. b.
units.tr: What kind of prayer is prosuchē, or petition for goods? I. 346. b.

units.la: Πρόσκαιρος quinam sint? II. 404. a.
units.tr: Who are the temporary (proskairoi)? II. 404. a.

units.la: Prosperi Aquitanici mortis Christi in sufficientem & efficacem distinctio examinatur, improbatur & rejicitur, I I. 123. seq.
units.tr: The distinction of Prosper of Aquitaine between a sufficient and an efficacious death of Christ is examined, disapproved and rejected, II. 123. ff.

units.la: Prostibula non esse toleranda, I. 727. a.
units.tr: Prostitutes are not to be tolerated, I. 727. a.

units.la: Περιστερὰ seu Persona notio in Divinis an probanda? I. III. a.
units.tr: Should the notion of person (persona) in the Divine be approved? I. III. a.

units.la: Προσωπολήπτης Deus non est, eò quòd hos præ illis elegerit, I. 167. a. 338. a.
units.tr: God is not a respecter of persons, in that he chose some rather than others, I. 167. a. 338. a.

units.la: Προσωπολημψία in pastorum Ecclesiæ electione vitanda est, I I. 474. a.
units.tr: Respect of persons is to be avoided in the election of the Church's ministers, II. 474. a.

units.la: Protoplasti lapsi licèt, converti tamen & salvati pièe credunt, I. 339. a. eorum fides, ibid. b.
units.tr: The fallen protoplasts, although lapsed, believe that they were converted and saved, I. 339. a. Their faith, ibid. b.

units.la: Providentia Dei quid? I. 240. argumenta eam astruentia, 242. seqq. Philosophi gentiles cum agnoverunt, 243. rerum creatarum conditio eam docet, ib. Objecta ejus, res omnes creatæ. 257. b. vide Breviar. Doctrinæ de Providentia salutaris usus, 277. a. abusus perstringitur, 278. a.
units.tr: What is the providence of God? I. 240. Arguments establishing it, 242. ff. When the Gentile philosophers recognised it, 243. The condition of created things teaches it, ibid. Its objects are all created things, 257. b. See the Breviary. The salutary use of the doctrine of providence, 277. a. Its abuse is censured, 278. a.

units.la: Proximus quis? I. 504. ejus diligendi præceptum, 508 a. modus, 509. a. dilectionis gradus, 510. a. qualis esse debeat, 561. a. quomodo singula Decalogi præcepta tabulæ secundæ ad eam concurrant, 563. b. in jure & Lege naturali fundatur, 312. a.
units.tr: Who is the neighbour? I. 504. The command to love him, 508. a. The manner, 509. a. Degrees of love, 510. a. What it ought to be like, 561. a. How each precept of the second table of the Decalogue bears on it, 563. b. It is founded in right and in the natural law, 312. a.

units.la: Proximus quomodo quisque sibi sit, I, 576. a.
units.tr: In what sense is each person his own neighbour? I. 576. a.

units.la: Psalmi quid sint? I. 349. a. Pœnitentiales quinam? 324. a.
units.tr: What are the Psalms? I. 349. a. Which are the penitential psalms? 324. a.

units.la: Pseudagorae, i.e. mendaciorum. patroni qui & quales? I. 627. a. eorum rationes diluuntur. 628. b.
units.tr: The defenders of falsehoods (pseudagorae, that is, of lies): who are they and what are they like? I. 627. a. Their arguments are refuted, 628. b.

units.la: Pseudochristiani animæ immortalitatem negant, I. 220. b.
units.tr: The pseudo-Christians deny the immortality of the soul, I. 220. b.

units.la: Pseudo-Messiæ Judæorum, II. 139. b.
units.tr: The pseudo-messiahs of the Jews, II. 139. b.

units.la: Pseudo-Politici remissionem peccatorum tident, II. 295. a. argumenta eorum absolutum magistratui quidvis faciendi potestatem tribuentia refutantur, 610. seqq. Magistratui in Republica & Ecclesia par jus & æqualem potestatem tribuunt, ib. resurrectionem mortuorum exibilant, 733. a. æternitatem pœnarum infernalium inficiantur, 763. b. eorum argumenta diluuntur, 764. a.
units.tr: The pseudo-politicians prate of remission of sins, II. 295. a. Their arguments that grant the magistrate an absolute power to do whatever he likes are refuted, 610. ff. They grant the magistrate equal right and power in the commonwealth and in the Church, ibid. They mock the resurrection of the dead, 733. a. They deny the eternity of infernal punishments, 763. b. Their arguments are answered, 764. a.

units.la: Pseudoprophetæ in V. T. qua pœna afficiendus fuerit, I. 715. b. Christus edens miracula sua Pseudoprophetæ neutiquam fuit, I I. 99. a.
units.tr: With what punishment the false prophet in the Old Testament ought to be visited, I. 715. b. Christ, when he worked his miracles, was by no means a pseudo-prophet, II. 99. a.

units.la: Ψυχὴ & Ψυχικὸς seu animalis homo quis & quid sit, I I. 739. a.
units.tr: Who and what is the psychē and the psychikos, that is, the natural man? II. 739. a.

units.la: Ψυχὴ Christi non notat ejus Divinitatem, I I. 8. b.
units.tr: The psychē of Christ does not denote his Divinity, II. 8. b.

units.la: Psychopannychitarum insulsum dogma proponitur, I I. 707. b. argumenta eorum refutantur, 708. b.
units.tr: The foolish dogma of the Psychopannychists is set forth, II. 707. b. Their arguments are refuted, 708. b.

units.la: Pudicitia tuendæ causa an liceat violentas sibi inferre manus, I. 577. b.
units.tr: Is it lawful to inflict violent hands on oneself for the sake of preserving chastity? I. 577. b.

units.la: Pueri Christi quinam sint, I I, 7. a.
units.tr: Who are the children of Christ? II. 7. a.

units.la: Pueritia Christi & adolescentia, in qua primum officii Propherici & Regii specimen anno ætatis, 12. exeruit I I. 39. a.
units.tr: The boyhood and youth of Christ, in which at the age of twelve he first displayed a specimen of his prophetic and kingly office, II. 39. a.

units.la: Puffendorfius de mendacii causa notatur, I. 622. b.
units.tr: Pufendorf is noted concerning the cause of lying, I. 622. b.

units.la: Pulveris seu cineris in caput inspersio quale signum fuerit? I. 361. b.
units.tr: What sign was the sprinkling of dust or ashes on the head? I. 361. b.

units.la: Punctorum vocalium Hebraeorum novitatem profitens Elias Levita refutatur, I. 36. a. b. Non sunt Masorethicarum, aut Ezrae inventum, sed Divinae originis, I. 36. b.
units.tr: Elias Levita, who professes that the Hebrew vowel points are a novelty, is refuted, I. 36. a. b. They are not the invention of the Masoretes or of Ezra, but of divine origin, I. 36. b.

units.la: Punire peccata non potest non Deus, I. 99. b.
units.tr: Only God can punish sins, I. 99. b.

units.la: Pupillorum qualis cura habenda sit, I. 616. a.
units.tr: What kind of care is to be had of orphans? I. 616. a.

units.la: Purgatorium Papale figmentum est, I I. 700. b. impugnatur, 701. a. Veteribus planè incognitum fuit, ib. b. argumentis Pontificiorum pro purgatorio occurritur, 702. a. Ejus vera origo ostenditur, 704. b.
units.tr: The Papal purgatory is a fiction, II. 700. b. It is assailed, 701. a. It was wholly unknown to the ancients, ibid. b. The arguments of the Papists for purgatory are met, 702. a. Its true origin is shown, 704. b.

units.la: Purificationes legales quales & quotuplices fuerint, I. 672. b. earum mystica significatio, 691. a.
units.tr: What and how many were the legal purifications? I. 672. b. Their mystical significance, 691. a.

units.la: Purim quale Judæorum festum, I. 364. b. 666. a.
units.tr: What kind of Jewish festival was Purim? I. 364. b. 666. a.

units.la: Pythagoras primus Dæmonum fecit mentionem, I. 171. a.
units.tr: Pythagoras was the first to make mention of demons, I. 171. a.

units.la: Q
units.tr: Q

units.la: Quadragesimalis jejunii Papalis origo, I. 364. b.
units.tr: The Papal origin of the Lenten fast, I. 364. b.

units.la: Qualitates creaturæ intelligentis bonas, quomodo Providentia Dei regat, I. 268. a.
units.tr: How does the providence of God govern the good qualities of an intelligent creature? I. 268. a.

units.la: Quasi-pœnæ apud Hebræos quænam & quales fuerint, I. 713. 714.
units.tr: What and what kind of quasi-punishments were there among the Hebrews? I. 713. 714.

units.la: Quietismus Theologiæ mysticæ proles est, I. 20. a. ejus author Molinos Hispanus, ibid.
units.tr: Quietism is an offspring of mystical theology, I. 20. a. Its author was the Spaniard Molinos, ibid.

units.la: Quintilliani Baptismum contempserunt, II. 453. b.
units.tr: The Quintillians despised baptism, II. 453. b.

units.la: R
units.tr: R

units.la: Rabbini quinam fuerint in V. Test. I. 582. a.
units.tr: Who were the rabbis in the Old Testament? I. 582. a.

units.la: Racematio vinearum pauperibus relinquenda, I, 733. b.
units.tr: Gleanings of the vineyard are to be left for the poor, I. 733. b.

units.la: Rapina quale furtum sit? 608. b.
units.tr: What kind of theft is robbery (rapina)? 608. b.

units.la: Raptus Christi in cœlum post baptismum Socini figmentum est, II. 88, 89.
units.tr: The rapture of Christ into heaven after baptism is a fiction of Socinus, II. 88, 89.

units.la: Ratio humana in rebus fidei quid valeat? I.9. a. nec corrupta nec sanata revelationis principium esse potest, 10.a. objectiones diluuntur, ib.b. 11.a. ejus usus quadruplex, I i.b. 12.a. ad ejus usum discretivum pertinent rectae consequentiae, ibid. b. Mysterium S. S. Trinitatis non assequitur, 119.a. b. creationem rerum ex nihilo assequitur, 185. a.
units.tr: Reason (ratio) in matters of faith: what can it do? I. 9. a. Neither corrupt nor healed reason can be a principle of revelation, 10. a. The objections are answered, ibid. b. 11. a. Its fourfold use, I. i. b. 12. a. To its discerning use belong right consequences, ibid. b. It does not attain the mystery of the Holy Trinity, 119. a. b. It does attain the creation of things out of nothing, 185. a.

units.la: Ratus non est forma peccati, I.138.b.
units.tr: Ratus is not the form of sin, I.138.b.

units.la: Rechabitarum origo & instituta, I.670.b. 689.b. Mysterium, 689. a.
units.tr: Rechabites: their origin and institutions, I.670.b. 689.b. Mystery, 689.a.

units.la: Reconciliatio nostri cum Deo explicatur, I 84. b. quod & quomodo facta sit? 117.b.
units.tr: Reconciliation of us with God is explained, I.84.b. What and how was it made? 117.b.

units.la: Recordatio mortis Christi qualis esse debeat? II.471.a.
units.tr: Remembrance of Christ's death: what should it be like? II.471.a.

units.la: Rectitudo. Dei, I.95.b. in dictis & factis, ibid.96.a. Hominis creati qualis fuerit? 224. b. mutabilis fuit, 226. 228. Socini contrariae cavillationes retunduntur, 226.b. 237.b.
units.tr: Rectitude. Of God, I.95.b. In words and deeds, ibid. 96.a. Of man as created: what was it like? 224.b. It was mutable, 226, 228. Socinus' contrary cavils are refuted, 226.b. 237.b.

units.la: Redemtio, ex peccatis est opus Divinum, I. 133. a. Redemtionis nostrae modus, 392.a. fructus; aeternitas, ibid. Redemtio Christi per mortem, II. 107. 108. explicatur & contra Socinianos vindicatur, ib. b. 109. seq. est causa meritoria Justificationis, 267. ejus necessitas, 268. Redemti a Christo certo perseverant, 400. b.
units.tr: Redemption from sins is a work of God, I.133.a. The mode of our redemption, 392.a. Its fruit and eternity, ibid. The redemption of Christ through death is explained and vindicated against the Socinians, II.107, 108, ib.b. 109 seq. It is the meritorious cause of justification, 267. Its necessity, 268. Those redeemed by Christ certainly persevere, 400.b.

units.la: Redemtio haereditatum & possessionum apud Hebraeos explicatur, I.731. b.
units.tr: Redemption of inheritances and possessions among the Hebrews is explained, I.731.b.

units.la: Reformatio Ecclesiae qualis & quando necessaria? II. 530.b. vel ordinaria, ib. vel extraordinaria, 531.a. diu expetita, 542. quomodo facta, 543. b.
units.tr: Reformation of the Church: what kind, and when is it necessary? II.530.b. Ordinary, ib.; or extraordinary, 531.a. Long desired, 542. How it was made, 543.b.

units.la: Reformatio vitae necessaria est, I 1.610.a. sed prudentiam Christianam requirit, ibid. b. collapsae Religionis, quatenus Magistratui Politico incumbat, 633.b.
units.tr: Reformation of life is necessary, I.610.a. but it requires Christian prudence, ibid. b. Of a corrupted religion, insofar as it falls to the political magistrate, I.633.b.

units.la: Reformatorum Ecclesiae, vocatio legitima fuit, II. 572. b.
units.tr: Reformed Church: its calling was lawful, II.572.b.

units.la: Regeneratio, ejus causa est Christi obedientia, II.121.a. est Divinae vocationis opus, 230.b. vide Breviar. ejus causae & principia, 231.b. imperfecta, 234. b. 235. 512. a. ejus causa & principium Spiritus S. est, 232. a.233.b. omnipotenti vi agens, ib. lucta cum carne, 234.b. ejus gradus, 236.a. non omnes baptizati ejus participes fiunt, 448. a. per aquam & spiritum quomodo fiat? 457.a. b. ejus gratia non ex lege, sed ex promissione data est, I. 478. a.
units.tr: Regeneration: its cause is the obedience of Christ, II.121.a. It is a work of divine calling, 230.b. See Breviary: its causes and principles, 231.b. Imperfect, 234.b. 235. 512.a. Its cause and principle is the Holy Spirit, 232.a. 233.b. It acts by omnipotent power, ib. It struggles with the flesh, 234.b. Its degrees, 236.a. Not all who are baptized become partakers of it, 448.a. How does it happen through water and the Spirit? 457.a.b. Its grace is given not by law but by promise, I.478.a.

units.la: Regeniti quatenus Legi non, & quatenus subsint, explicatur, I.642.b. 643.a.
units.tr: The regenerate: how far they are not under the Law, and how far they are subject to it, is explained, I.642.b. 643.a.

units.la: Reginem Ecclesiae Christianum, I I. 553. vide Breviar. Ministeriale describitur, 557.b. quale esse debeat, 591.b. vide Gubernatio. Item Breviar. externum non Monarchicum est, 639.a. vide Breviar. Antichristianum Hierarchia Romana exercet, 638.
units.tr: Government of the Christian Church, II.553. See Breviary. Its ministerial character is described, 557.b. What kind it ought to be, 591.b. See Government. Likewise the external Breviary is not monarchical, 639.a. See Breviary. The Antichristian Roman hierarchy exercises it, 638.

units.la: Regnum. singulorum Regnorum singuli Angeli protectores nulli sunt, I.283.a.
units.tr: Kingdom. Individual angels are not protectors of individual kingdoms, I.283.a.

units.la: Regnum. Dei universale in Mundo, I. 148. a. Regnum Dei quale? 354.a. vel gratiae, vel gloriae. Regnum Christi Spirituale, aeternum quale sit? 739.b. quomodo exhibuerit Israeli? II.64. a. Regnum Christi vel essentiale, vel personale & oeconomicum est, II.131. seq. non de hoc mundo, 132.a. ejus sceptrum & modus regnandi spiritualis, ib. b. spirituale non terrenum est, ibid. 133.a. seq. vide JESUS Christus, aeternum est, 135. b. 136.b. ejusdem alia in V. alia in N. Test, administratio fuit, 136.a. quomodo traditurus sit Patri. 137.a. Ejusdem Regni Christi & cum eodem regnaturae Ecclesiae profectus explicatur, 720. b. de eo Doctores discordant, 711. a. Regnum non particulare ex solis sanctis & martyribus resuscitatis per 1000. annos erit, 725. b. 726.
units.tr: Kingdom. The universal kingdom of God in the world, I.148.a. What is the kingdom of God? 354.a. Either of grace or of glory. What is the eternal, spiritual kingdom of Christ like? 739.b. How did it manifest itself to Israel? II.64.a. The kingdom of Christ is either essential, or personal and economical, II.131 seq. It is not of this world, 132.a. Its sceptre and mode of spiritual reigning, ib.b. It is spiritual, not earthly, ibid. 133.a. seq. See Jesus Christ. It is eternal, 135.b. 136.b. Its administration was one thing in the Old Testament and another in the New, 136.a. How will he hand it over to the Father? 137.a. The progress of this kingdom of Christ, and of the Church that will reign with him, is explained, 720.b. The teachers disagree about it, 711.a. A non-particular kingdom, of the saints and martyrs alone raised up, will last for a thousand years, 725.b. 726.

units.la: Regnum Coelorum quomodo appropinquaverit? II. 93. b.
units.tr: Kingdom of heaven: how did it draw near? II.93.b.

units.la: Regnum Antichristianum quale sit? 536. seq. perpetuum splendorem jactat, 537. 538. est Hierarchia Rom. 638. a.
units.tr: Antichristian kingdom: what is it like? 536 seq. It boasts of perpetual splendour, 537, 538. It is the Roman hierarchy, 638.a.

units.la: Regnum Diaboli, quale sit? I.287.a. miserrimum, 299.
units.tr: Kingdom of the devil: what is it like? I.287.a. Most wretched, 299.

units.la: Regula fidei & vitae, quomodo Scriptura sit? I.53. a.
units.tr: Rule of faith and life: how is Scripture such a rule? I.53.a.

units.la: Relationes, qualis earum vis in Sacramentis? II.479. b.
units.tr: Relations: what is their force in the sacraments? II.479.b.

units.la: Religio communis Naturae & rationis principiis nixa nulla salutaris datur, I. 4. b. Gentilium, Judaeorum, Muhamed. ad amussim orthodoxae exigenda est, ib.6. b. Christianae veritas, ib. 523. b. non vi & armis propaganda, 586.b. ejus persecutio, ib.
units.tr: Religion grounded on the principles of common nature and reason gives no saving religion, I.4.b. The religions of the Gentiles, Jews and Muhammadans must be measured by the exact standard of orthodoxy, ib. 6.b. The truth of the Christian religion, ib. 523.b. It is not to be propagated by force and arms, 586.b. Its persecution, ib.

units.la: Remissio peccatorum a Deo petenda, I.357. a. non nisi per mortem & sanguinem Christi obtinetur, II. 114-a. quomodo gratuita sit, 117.b. ea & adjudicatio vitae distinguenda, (sed non separanda sunt, 287.
units.tr: Remission of sins is to be sought from God, I.357.a. It is obtained only through the death and blood of Christ, II.114.a. How it is gratuitous, 117.b. It must be distinguished from the adjudication of life (but not separated from it), 287.

units.la: a. definitur, ibid. vide Breviar. non est conditionata, 397. per Baptismum non confertur, sed obsignatur, 447. a. etiam post baptismum commissorum peccatorum est, ibid.
units.tr: a. It is defined, ibid. See Breviary. It is not conditional, 397. It is not conferred through baptism but sealed by it, 447.a. Even after baptism it is of sins committed, ibid.

units.la: Remittere peccatum idem est quod non imputare, I.276.b. 287.b. est phrasis metaphorica, ib.
units.tr: To remit sin is the same as not to impute it, I.276.b. 287.b. It is a metaphorical expression, ib.

units.la: Remonstrantes Praedestinationem non ex Lege sed Evangelio cognoscendam esse docent, I.156.a. eorum de decreto reprobationis personali paratragoedia-tiones, ibid. b. eorum error circa decretum Electionis, 1,157.a. 165.b. per praevisionem fidei vel operum infantes, surdos, amentes, &c. ab electione excludunt, 167.b. absolutum reprobationis decretum rejiciunt, 174.a. mortem aeternam tantum poenam damni esse dicunt, 323. b. peccati primi imputationem negant, 343. a. hominem post lapsum vi foederis operum ad obedientiam tenere negant, 372. a. Foederis gratiae unitatem in Vet.& Nov.Testam. negant, 410.a.
units.tr: Remonstrants teach that predestination is to be known not from the Law but from the Gospel, I.156.a. Their tragic overstatements about the decree of personal reprobation, ibid. b. Their error concerning the decree of election, I.157.a. 165.b. Through foreseen faith or works they exclude infants, the deaf, the insane, etc. from election, 167.b. They reject the absolute decree of reprobation, 174.a. They say eternal death is only the penalty of loss, 323.b. They deny the imputation of the first sin, 343.a. They deny that man after the fall is held to obedience by the force of the covenant of works, 372.a. They deny the unity of the covenant of grace in the Old and New Testaments, 410.a.

units.la: Repraesentativa Ecclesia Pontificiorum ridicula, II. 604. a.
units.tr: Representative Church of the Papists is ridiculous, II.604.a.

units.la: Reprobatio quid? I.156.b. 172.a. vide Brev. ejus decretum absolutum ab Adversariis rejicitur, blasphematur, 174.a. non pietati repugnat, 177.a.
units.tr: Reprobation: what is it? I.156.b. 172.a. See Breviary. Its absolute decree is rejected and blasphemed by the adversaries, 174.a. It does not contradict piety, 177.a.

units.la: Reprobi. Eorum vocatio quomodo ab electorum differat? II. 206. b. Reprobi baptizati quomodo filii Regni sint? 448.b.
units.tr: Reprobates: how does their calling differ from that of the elect? II.206.b. How are baptized reprobates sons of the kingdom? 448.b.

units.la: Res negari non debet modo rei ignoto, I.351. a. Rerum creatarum conditio Providentiam Dei docet, 242. a. item earundem ordo & harmonia, ib. b.
units.tr: A thing must not be denied merely because it is unknown, I.351.a. The condition of created things teaches the providence of God, 242.a. Likewise their order and harmony, ib.b.

units.la: Resipiscentia quid? I.319.a. vid. Brev. non meretur salutem, 324. fera vera esse potest, 325. a. Novatianorum de illa error, 326. Montanistarum, ib. a. ejus necessitas ostenditur, 384. a. Pharisaeorum fide in Christum destituta, nulla est. 479. a. Resipiscentia & fides Evangelicae praedicationis summa, I.193.b.
units.tr: Repentance: what is it? I.319.a. See Breviary. It does not merit salvation, 324. It can be genuine, 325.a. The error of the Novatians concerning it, 326. Of the Montanists, ib.a. Its necessity is shown, 384.a. The repentance of the Pharisees, which lacked faith in Christ, is nothing, 479.a. Repentance and faith are the sum of evangelical preaching, I.193.b.

units.la: Resistere malo, quo senu vetuerit Christus? I.585.a. an vocationi Divinae resisti possit? 207.
units.tr: To resist evil: in what sense did Christ forbid it? I.585.a. Can the divine calling be resisted? 207.

units.la: Respublica. Judaicae Reipubl. status Theocraticus fuit, I.701.a. quod fuisse ostenditur, ibid.b. eidem religio innexa est, 703. b. Respubl. prima fuit Adami domus, I I.617.a. Reipubl. forma, modus, & personae ejus ab hominibus eliguntur, ib.b.
units.tr: Commonwealth. The state of the Jewish commonwealth was theocratic, I.701.a. That this was so is shown, ibid.b. Religion was bound up with it, 703.b. The first commonwealth was the household of Adam, II.617.a. The form and mode of the commonwealth, and its persons, are chosen by men, ib.b.

units.la: Restitutio ablati, I.616.b.
units.tr: Restitution of what was taken away, I.616.b.

units.la: Resurrectio Christi, ejus tempus, II.57. a. praedictum & Typis V. Test. praefiguratum fuit, ibid. b. ejus veritas. ibid. 59.b. multis argumentis demonstratur, ibid.60.a. testes varii, 60. a. b. plus quam quingenti, 63. b.
units.tr: Resurrection of Christ: its time, II.57.a. It was foretold and foreshadowed by types of the Old Testament, ibid.b. Its truth, ibid. 59.b. It is demonstrated by many arguments, ibid. 60.a. Various witnesses, 60.a.b. More than five hundred, 63.b.

units.la: Resurrectio mortuorum. ejus & vitae aeternae in V. Test. argumenta, I. 407. a. Resurgentium exempla inter gentiles nulla vera sunt, I I.60. a. erit universalis omnium hominum, 740.b. alia justorum, alia injustorum quomodo fit futura? 742. a. modus later, ibid. Locus resurgentium, ibid. b. eidem analogia erit viventium immutatio, 743.b. ejus finis, ib.
units.tr: Resurrection of the dead: arguments for it and for eternal life in the Old Testament, I.407.a. There are no true examples of the raised among the Gentiles, II.60.a. It will be universal for all men, 740.b. How will the resurrection of the just differ from that of the unjust? 742.a. The mode of the latter, ibid. The place of the risen, ibid.b. Its analogy is the transformation of the living, 743.b. Its end, ib.

units.la: Resuscitatio Mortuorum quid sit? II.719. a. fundamentum est fidei Christianae, ib. b. probatur Scripturae testimoniis, ibid. nec non rationibus ex Scriptura petitis, 731.a. ex lumine Naturae, quoad ejus possibilitatem, 732.a. gentiles crediderunt, ib.b. Resurrectionis Irrisores; inter veteres Judaei, gentiles Philosophi & Pseudo-Christiani fuerunt, 732. b. quorum argumenta refelluntur. 733.a. ejus causa efficiens solus Deus, tum singulariter Christus est, 734. non fit ex causis naturalibus, 735.
units.tr: Resurrection of the dead: what is it? II.719.a. It is the foundation of the Christian faith, ib.b. It is proved by testimonies of Scripture, ibid., and also by arguments drawn from Scripture, 731.a. From the light of nature, as to its possibility, 732.a. The Gentiles believed it, ib.b. Mockers of the resurrection: among the ancients were the Jews, the Gentile philosophers and the pseudo-Christians, 732.b. Their arguments are refuted, 733.a. Its efficient cause is God alone, and in particular Christ, 734. It does not arise from natural causes, 735.

units.la: Resuscitatorum cum Angelis similitudo in quibus constiftat? II.738.b.
units.tr: Likeness of the risen to the angels: in what does it consist? II.738.b.

units.la: Revelata quaedam explicitè, quaedam implicitè creduntur, I.15. b.
units.tr: Some things revealed are believed explicitly, and some implicitly, I.15.b.

units.la: Revelatio Divina. Ejus necessitas, I.5.a. diversa ejus oeconomia, ibid. 7. a. varii gradus, 7. b. Divinitatem suam non a modo traditionis, sed a re tradita obtinet, ib. 8.a. verae a falsa dijudicandae methodus, ib. & 25. b. Divinae centrum solus Christus est, 16. a. ab Adamo ad Mosen sola traditione sine Scriptura propagata est, 23.a. ejus traditionis modus, ibid. ea hominem ad veri Dei cognitionem ducit, 61.62.
units.tr: Divine revelation. Its necessity, I.5.a. Its diverse economy, ibid. 7.a. Its various degrees, 7.b. It derives its divinity not from the mode of transmission but from the thing transmitted, ib. 8.a. The method of distinguishing true revelation from false, ib. and 25.b. The centre of divine revelation is Christ alone, 16.a. From Adam to Moses it was propagated by tradition alone, without Scripture, 23.a. The mode of that tradition, ibid. It leads man to the knowledge of the true God, 61, 62.

units.la: Revelationes frequentes Patriarchis factae, I.437.b. quotuplices fuerint? ib. Divinarum characteres, 439. a. Revelationis. Prophetis factae modus, 480.a. ejus variae species, ibid. vid. Breviar.
units.tr: Revelations frequently made to the Patriarchs, I.437.b. How many kinds were there? ib. The marks of divine revelations, 439.a. The manner in which revelation was made to the Prophets, 480.a. Its various kinds, ibid. See Breviar.

units.la: Revelatio plenior N. Testam. II.175. b. ejus in V. & N. Test. oeconomia & differentia, 176.b,177.
units.tr: Fuller revelation in the New Testament, II.175.b. Its economy and difference in the Old and New Testaments, 176.b, 177.

units.la: Reverentia Numinis quid? I. 521. b.
units.tr: What is reverence for the Deity? I.521.b.

units.la: Revolutum iri corpora omnia hominum subtus terram in Canaan, ut ibi resurgant, Judæi nugantur, I I.742.b.
units.tr: The Jews idly maintain that all human bodies under the earth in Canaan will roll back there so as to rise again there, II.742.b.

units.la: Rex Deus est, cur & quomodo ? I. 301. b.
units.tr: God is King: why and how? I.301.b.

units.la: Rex populi sui Christus est, I.703. a. I I.93. b.
units.tr: Christ is King of his people, I.703.a; II.93.b.

units.la: Reges Israelitarum à Deo dati & constituti ? I.705. a eorum jus Regium Divinum, ibid. b. humanum, 706. a. Despoticum, 705 b. quorum potestas certis limitibus definita fuit, ibid. b.
units.tr: Were the kings of Israel given and appointed by God? I.705.a. Their royal right was divine, ibid.b; human, 706.a; despotic, 705.b. Their power was defined by certain limits, ibid.b.

units.la: Richardus Simon seu Pseudo-Criticus notatur, I. 34. b.; ejus commentum, quòd Scriptura V. Test. sit compendium è scribis quibusdam compilatum, refellitur, ibid. idem notatur, 42 .b. 43 .a. vid. Simon. item, 185. a.
units.tr: Richard Simon, or the Pseudo-Critic, is noted, I.34.b. His fiction that the Old Testament Scripture is a compendium compiled from certain scribes is refuted, ibid. The same man is noted, 42.b, 43.a; see Simon; likewise 185.a.

units.la: Ridicularii mimi quales sint ? I.655. a.
units.tr: What kind of ridiculous mimes were they? I.655.a.

units.la: Ritus. Rituum Paschalium mystica significatio, I.489. a. Judæorum nugæ, ib.
units.tr: Rites. The mystical signification of the Passover rites, I.489.a. Jewish trifles, ib.

units.la: Rituum Lex, qualia præcepta contineat? I.647. a. rationes ejus institutionis, ibid. b. diversa ejus sub Patriarchis & Mose ratio, ib.648. ejus evolvendæ regulæ, 649. a.
units.tr: The law of rites: what precepts does it contain? I.647.a. Reasons for its institution, ibid.b. Its different arrangement under the Patriarchs and under Moses, ib. 648. Rules for unfolding it, 649.a.

units.la: Rituum sacrificialium Mysterium, I.677. b.
units.tr: The mystery of the sacrificial rites, I.677.b.

units.la: Ritus Baptismales varii, I I.442.a. circa panem Eucharisticum à Christo adhibiti, 463. b. circa vinum, 465. a.
units.tr: Various baptismal rites, II.442.a. Rites used by Christ concerning the Eucharistic bread, 463.b; concerning the wine, 465.a.

units.la: Rituum diversitas non tollit fidei unitatem, I I.526. a. eorum harmonia exacta in Ecclesia obtineri nequit, 592. a.
units.tr: Diversity of rites does not remove unity of faith, II.526.a. Their exact harmony cannot be obtained in the Church, 592.a.

units.la: Roma tota emporium est, I I.459.a. est Babylon, 536. a. illa magna, 682. a.
units.tr: All Rome is a marketplace, II.459.a. It is Babylon, 536.a. That great city, 682.a.

units.la: S.
units.tr: S.

units.la: Sabbathum. Ejus primæva institutio, I. 238. a. quid sit? ejus Sanctificatio, 551. a. vel Divinum vel humanum est; illud vel Creationis vel Redemtionis, hoc vel ante vel post peccatum, ibid. b. morale quale sit? 552. a. Ceremoniale, ibid. b. spirituale, ibid. Morale in quarto præcepto quid? 553. a. tempus & locus, 554. a. sanctificatio moralis, ibid. Privativa, ibid. positiva in publico Dei cultu, ib. 555. a. ejus ceremoniale in quo consistat? 556. Spencerii de Sabbatho error, 552. b. 555. 556.
units.tr: Sabbath. Its primeval institution, I.238.a. What is it? Its sanctification, 551.a. It is either divine or human; the former is either of Creation or of Redemption, the latter either before or after sin, ibid.b. What is the moral sabbath? 552.a. The ceremonial, ibid.b. The spiritual, ibid. The moral element in the fourth commandment: what is it? 553.a. Time and place, 554.a. Moral sanctification, ibid. Privative, ibid. Positive, in the public worship of God, ib. 555.a. In what does its ceremonial consist? 556. Spencer's error about the Sabbath, 552.b, 555, 556.

units.la: Sabbathi Typici antiquatio adversus Judæos demonstratur, I. 558. a. ei spirituale N. Test. successit, ib. b. 559. cujus duplex sanctificatio, ib. b.
units.tr: The abolition of the typical Sabbath is demonstrated against the Jews, I.558.a. The spiritual Sabbath of the New Testament succeeded it, ib.b. 559. Its twofold sanctification, ib.b.

units.la: Σαββατον δ' ὑπερπέφυτον quale fuerit? I.665. b.
units.tr: What was the "Sabbath beyond the ordinary" [Σαββατον δ' ὑπερπέφυτον]? I.665.b.

units.la: Sabbathi profanationis qualis pœna fuerit? I.716. a.
units.tr: What was the punishment for profaning the Sabbath? I.716.a.

units.la: Sabbatha, prima Sabbathorum, in Historia Resurrectionis Christi quid notet? I I.57. a.
units.tr: What do the Sabbaths, the first of the Sabbaths, mean in the account of Christ's resurrection? II.57.a.

units.la: Sabbatharii olim qui dicti? I. 552. b. Veterum & recentiorum præcisitas taxatur, 555. a.
units.tr: Who were formerly called Sabbatarians? I.552.b. The excessive strictness of the ancients and of more recent writers is censured, 555.a.

units.la: Sacerdotes Vet. Test. qui fuerint? I. 666. b. eorum munus in quo constiterit? 667. a. eorum unctio, 669. a. Aharonidarum ordines non caruerunt Mysterio, 687 b. 688. a. eorum authoritas neutiquam probat Papæ potestatem, I I.646. b.
units.tr: Who were the priests of the Old Testament? I.666.b. In what did their office consist? 667.a. Their anointing, 669.a. The orders of the sons of Aaron were not without mystery, 687.b, 688.a. Their authority in no way proves the power of the Pope, II.646.b.

units.la: Sacerdotes & Sacrificium quomodo sinus? I I.429. a.
units.tr: How are priests and sacrifice related? II.429.a.

units.la: Sacerdotum Papalium locordia depicta, I I.434. a.
units.tr: The sloth of the Papal priests depicted, II.434.a.

units.la: Sacerdotium olim penes Patres familias fuit, I.445. b. antiquitus primogenitorum fuit, 666. 667. a. ad Aharonidas translatum est, ibid. b. Summum soli Aharoni & filiis cessit, 668. a.
units.tr: The priesthood was formerly in the hands of the heads of families, I.445.b. Anciently it belonged to the firstborn, 666, 667.a. It was transferred to the sons of Aaron, ibid.b. The high priesthood passed to Aaron and his sons alone, 668.a.

units.la: Sacerdotium Christi, I.380. a. cum Aharonis collatum, 686 b. eq. non subest legibus Sacerdotii Aharonici, 695. a. explicatur, I I.102. a. eodem qua Θεάρχης defunctus est, ib. b. ejus externa conditio, ib. interna, ib.103. b. à Levitico differentia, ib.104. a. partes, 105. a. ordo illarum ostenditur, ib. b. non demum post ingressum ejus in cœlum, sed jam in terra cœptum est, I 9. a. à Regno ejus differt, 129. b.
units.tr: The priesthood of Christ, I.380.a. Compared with the Aaronic, 686.b. Not subject to the laws of the Aaronic priesthood, 695.a. Explained, II.102.a. It was discharged in the same way as the Thearch's office [Θεάρχης], ib.b. Its external condition, ib.; its internal condition, ib.103.b. Its difference from the Levitical, ib.104.a. Its parts, 105.a. The order of those parts is shown, ib.b. It did not begin only after his ascension into heaven, but was already begun on earth, I.9.a. It differs from his Kingdom, 129.b.

units.la: Sacra celare non vera Ecclesiæ, sed hæreticorum mos est, I I. 433. b.
units.tr: To conceal sacred things is not the custom of the true Church but of heretics, II.433.b.

units.la: Sacramenta sunt sigilla fœderis gratiæ, I.392. a. b. 393. a. f sius asseritur, ib. b. 394. a. non nuda signa sunt, 396 a. nec conferunt gratiam ex opere operato, ib. b. a. ii solos credentes pertinent, 400. necessitas, 401. illa V. Test. quoad rem signatam, eadem cum illis Nov. Testam. 409. a. an, & in quibus differant? 415. a. extraordinaria Vet. Test. 491, a. quomodo à Sacramentis Nov. Test. discrepent. 494. a. eorum convenientia, 495.
units.tr: Sacraments are seals of the covenant of grace, I.392.a, b; 393.a. Their further assertion, ib.b; 394.a. They are not bare signs, 396.a; nor do they confer grace by the work worked, ib.b. They pertain only to believers, 400. Their necessity, 401. Those of the Old Testament, as to the thing signified, are the same as those of the New Testament, 409.a. Whether and in what respects they differ, 415.a. The extraordinary sacraments of the Old Testament, 491.a. How they differ from the sacraments of the New Testament, 494.a. Their agreement, 495.

units.la: Sacramenta Nov. Test. etiam ad Cultum Dei spiritualem pertinent, I I.184. a. duo sunt, 435. b. septenarius Sacramentorum numerus refellitur, 436. a. vim conferendi gratiam non habent, 445. b. non sunt causæ salutis, ib.
units.tr: The sacraments of the New Testament also pertain to the spiritual worship of God, II.184.a. There are two, 435.b. The septenary number of sacraments is refuted, 436.a. They have no power to confer grace, 445.b. They are not causes of salvation, ib.

units.la: Sacrificia Vet. Test. reatum peccati expiobrihant, I. 421. a. eorum à Sacramentis discrimen, 443. a. ea post lapsum cœperunt, ib. b. non naturæ inlinctu, sed præcepto Dei, ib.445. eorum locus & tempus ante Mosen, 446. a. non abstulerunt reatum peccati, 478. a. non sunt media remissionis peccatorum, 479. b. temporibus statis offerri solita, 653. ritus sacrificandi, 659. a. locus, 663. a. omnia Christum adumbrarunt, 673. b.
units.tr: The sacrifices of the Old Testament expiated the guilt of sin, I.421.a. Their distinction from the sacraments, 443.a. They began after the fall, ib.b. They were instituted not by the impulse of nature but by the command of God, ib. 445. Their place and time before Moses, 446.a. They did not remove the guilt of sin, 478.a. They are not means of remission of sins, 479.b. They were customarily offered at fixed times, 653. The rite of sacrificing, 659.a. The place, 663.a. All of them foreshadowed Christ, 673.b.

units.la: Sacrificium Christi in cruce peractum oppositum Sacrificio Missæ, I I.491.a.
units.tr: Christ's sacrifice accomplished on the cross, opposed to the sacrifice of the Mass, II.491.a.

units.la: Sacrificium illud Juge Dan. V I I I, 11. non est missa, I I. 689. b.
units.tr: That continual sacrifice, Dan. 8:11, is not the Mass, II.689.b.

units.la: Sacrilegium maximum quale? I.523.a. quid sit? 608.b.
units.tr: What is the greatest sacrilege? I.523.a. What is it? 608.b.

units.la: Sadducæi Resurrectionis impugnatores, I I.732. b. eorum error unde ortus? ib.b.
units.tr: The Sadducees, opponents of the resurrection, II.732.b. From what source did their error arise? ib.b.

units.la: Saga & striges quâ pœna afficiendæ? I.194. b. earum pactum cum Diabolo, & stigmata, 195.
units.tr: With what punishment are witches and sorceresses to be afflicted? I.194.b. Their pact with the Devil, and their marks, 195.

units.la: Salmasius laudatur, I I.50.b. 51.a.
units.tr: Salmasius is praised, II.50.b, 51.a.

units.la: Salvare homines quomodo præter Christum res aliæ dicantur? I I.76. b.
units.tr: In what sense are other things said to save men besides Christ? II.76.b.

units.la: Salus. Salutem æternam Patres V. Test. consecuti sunt, etiam ante Christi in cœlum ascensionem, I.413. b. ejus certitudo perseverantiæ comes est, I I.409. a. definitur, 410. a. ejus causæ non sunt Sacramenta, 445. b.
units.tr: Salvation. The Fathers of the Old Testament obtained eternal salvation, even before Christ's ascension into heaven, I.413.b. Its certainty accompanies perseverance, II.409.a. It is defined, 410.a. The Sacraments are not its causes, 445.b.

units.la: Salutare illud quod exspectavit Jacob, quale fuerit? I.435.
units.tr: What was that salvation which Jacob awaited? I.435.

units.la: Salutare quo ritu fiebat? 524. b.
units.tr: By what rite was salvation effected? I.524.b.

units.la: Samuelis Ipectrum, I.Sam. X X V I I I.8. Diabolus ipse fuit, I.297. b. ejus anima Sauli noa apparuit, I I. 715. a.
units.tr: The spectre of Samuel, 1 Sam. 28:8. The Devil himself was it, I.297.b. His soul did not appear to Saul, II.715.a.

units.la: Sanctum Sanctorum Templi Hierosolymitani emblema fuit Ecclesiæ, I.680. b.
units.tr: The Holy of Holies of the Temple at Jerusalem was an emblem of the Church, I.680.b.

units.la: Sancta cur & quomodo Ecclesia dicatur? I I.544. b. quomodo sit? 511. b.
units.tr: Why and how is the Church called holy? II.544.b. How is it so? II.511.b.

units.la: Sancti. In eorum honorem missæ non celebrandæ, I I. 491.b. cœlites non iciunt quid in terris sigillatim à quovis agatur, 709.a. secreta cogitationum in terris viventium ignorant, ib.710.a. quomodo Angelis similes, ib.a. iis Regimen m ndi & Ecclesiæ non est commissum, ib. eorum canonisatio Pap.lis refellitur, 711. a. eorum cultus religiosus juramento à Papa mandatur, I I.711. b. variis argumentis impugnatur, 712. non sunt nostri mediatores, ibid. b. Sancti quomodo mundum sint judicaturi, 746. b.
units.tr: Saints. Masses are not to be celebrated in their honour, II.491.b. The inhabitants of heaven do not know what is done by each individual on earth, II.709.a. They do not know the secret thoughts of those living on earth, ib.710.a. How they are like the angels, ib.a. The government of the world and of the Church has not been committed to them, ib. Their canonization by the Papists is refuted, 711.a. Their religious worship is enjoined by the Pope under oath, II.711.b. It is attacked by various arguments, 712. They are not our mediators, ibid.b. How the saints will judge the world, 746.b.

units.la: Sanctitas Dei, I. 95.a. exemplar nostræ Sanctitatis est, 316. b. ejusdem norma Verbum Dei, ibid. Sanctitas in cordibus fidelium per Spiritum sanctificantem perpetuitatem sanctificationis arguit, I I. 399.a.
units.tr: The holiness of God, I.95.a. It is the pattern of our holiness, 316.b. Its rule is the Word of God, ibid. Holiness in the hearts of the faithful, through the sanctifying Spirit, argues the perpetuity of sanctification, II.399.a.

units.la: Sanctitas vitæ, auctorum & Patrum religionis, an sit nota veræ Ecclesiæ, I I.550.a.
units.tr: Holiness of life among the authors and Fathers of the religion: is it a mark of the true Church? II.550.a.

units.la: Sanctificatio Nominis Dei in genere, I. 541.b.
units.tr: Sanctification of the Name of God in general, I. 541.b.

units.la: Sanctificari Dies Sabbathi quomodo dicatur, I.551.a.
units.tr: How the Sabbath Day is said to be sanctified, I. 551.a.

units.la: Sanctificatio Humanæ Christi Naturæ qualis? I I.17.a. ejus modus, ibid. causæ, proxima & remota, ib.b.
units.tr: What is the sanctification of the human nature of Christ? II. 17.a. Its mode, ibid. Its causes, proximate and remote, ib. b.

units.la: Sanctificatio hominis prævisa electionis causa non est, I. 166. a. quid? I I.313.a. vide Breviar, ejus necessitas & utilitas, 315. subjectum, 316. ex illa affictorum consolatio, 315. b. in hac vita est imperfecta, 370. b. immota & stabilis est, 398. b. triga virtutum, fide, spe & charitate absolvitur, 399.a.
units.tr: The sanctification of man is not the cause of foreseen election, I. 166.a. What it is, II. 313.a. See Breviar. Its necessity and usefulness, 315. Its subject, 316. The consolation of the afflicted that arises from it, 315.b. In this life it is imperfect, 370.b. It is unmoved and stable, 398.b. It is completed by the triad of virtues, faith, hope and charity, 399.a.

units.la: Sanguis. Ejus interdictum post diluvium, I.747.a. ejus ratio moralis & ceremonialis, ibid. b. ejus eius interdictus Hebraeis, 671. b. victimarum V. Test. quid significarit? 676. b. interdicti Mysterium, 690. a. illud comedentis qualis pœna fuerit? 717.a.
units.tr: Blood. Its prohibition after the flood, I. 747.a. Its moral and ceremonial reason, ibid. b. Its prohibition for the Hebrews, 671.b. What did the victims of the Old Testament signify? 676.b. The mystery of the prohibition, 690.a. What punishment fell on one who ate it? 717.a.

units.la: Sanguis Christi causa est remissionis peccatorum, I I. 114. a. ejus gutta una non sufficit redemtioni, 294. b.
units.tr: The blood of Christ is the cause of the remission of sins, II. 114.a. One drop of it does not suffice for redemption, 294.b.

units.la: Sapientia. ejus nomine in Sacris Theologia venit, I.3. a. naturalis Deum non cognoscit ut debet, ib,4.a.
units.tr: Wisdom. By this name it is called in Sacred Theology, I. 3.a. Natural wisdom does not know God as it ought, ib. 4.a.

units.la: Sapientia Dei explicatur, I.87. b. vid. Brev. item. 151.a.
units.tr: The wisdom of God is explained, I. 87.b. See Brev., also 151.a.

units.la: Sapientia personalis Christus est, I.120. b. cujus sapientia tanquam hominis incrementa sua habuit, I I. 21. a.
units.tr: Personal Wisdom is Christ, I. 120.b. Whose wisdom, as of a man, had its growth, II. 21.a.

units.la: Sarabaitæ Monachi hodiernis similes fuerunt, I I. 675. b.
units.tr: The Sarabaites were similar to the monks of today, II. 675.b.

units.la: Saravia notatus ob assertam Apostolatus in Ecclesia durationem, I.199. a.
units.tr: Saravia, noted for asserting the duration of the apostolate in the Church, I. 199.a.

units.la: Sathanas, ejus ligatio qualis? I.299. a. est malus ille à quo liberari petimus, 359.a. ejus arma & Tyrannis, 373.a.b.
units.tr: Satan. What is his binding? I. 299.a. Is he the evil one from whom we ask to be delivered? 359.a. His weapons and tyranny, 373.a.b.

units.la: Sathanæ tradere peccantem quid? I I. 606. a. quando liga-
units.tr: What does it mean to deliver the sinner to Satan? II. 606.a. When he is bound-

units.la: ligatus & denuò solutus fuerit? 728.b. die novissi-mo judicabitur, 747. b.
units.tr: bound, and when he is loosed again? 728.b. He will be judged on the last day, 747.b.

units.la: Satisfactiones humanæ pro peccatis radarguuntur, I. 190. Christo injuriæ sunt, 291.
units.tr: Human satisfactions for sins are refuted, I. 190. They are injuries to Christ, 291.

units.la: Satisfactio Christi pro electis contra Socinianos asseri-tur, I I. 109. seqq. ejus veritas ex eo, quòd pro nobis execratio factus est, 112. a. ex typis sa-crificiorum Vet. Test. probatur, ib. b. quâ sublatâ syrma absurditatum sequitur, 113. a. eandem ne-gantium historia, ib. refutantur, 114. a. 115. Satis-factionis vox non simpliciter ἀνταπόδοσις est, 115. a. non est impossibilis, 116. a. b. non est superva-canea, 116. a. per eam Lex non relaxatur sed imple-tur, 116. b. non repugnat voluntati Dei, 117. a. non gratuitæ peccatorum remissioni, 117. b. Patres Vet. Test. non sine ea salvati sunt, 117. a. ejus negatæ rei peraguntur Pontificii & Remonstrantes. 121. b. non efficit ut fides nobis in justitiam imputetur, 301. b.
units.tr: Christ's satisfaction for the elect is asserted against the Socinians, II. 109 ff. Its truth follows from the fact that he was made a curse for us, 112.a. It is proved from the types of the Old Testament sacrifices, ib. b. With it removed, a train of absurdities follows, 113.a. The history of those who deny it, ib. Refuted, 114.a. 115. The word satisfaction is not simply ἀνταπόδοσις (repayment), 115.a. It is not impossible, 116.a.b. It is not superfluous, 116.a. Through it the Law is not relaxed but fulfilled, 116.b. It does not conflict with the will of God, 117.a. It does not conflict with the free remission of sins, 117.b. The fathers of the Old Testament were not saved without it, 117.a. The Papists and Remonstrants deny this, 121.b. It does not bring about that faith is imputed to us for righteousness, 301.b.

units.la: Savanarola Prophetiæ dono instructus fuit, I. 551. a.
units.tr: Savonarola was endowed with the gift of prophecy, I. 551.a.

units.la: Scaliger (Julius Cæsar) laudatur, I. 177. b.
units.tr: Scaliger (Julius Caesar) is praised, I. 177.b.

units.la: Scandalum explicatur & distinguitur, I. 562. a.
units.tr: Scandal is explained and distinguished, I. 562.a.

units.la: Scelerum apud quascunque gentes una eadémque ratio semper est, I. 741.
units.tr: Crimes among all peoples always have one and the same reason, I. 741.

units.la: Sceptrum Juda quid? & quando ab eo ablatum? 434. a. b. 435. a.
units.tr: The sceptre of Judah: what is it, and when was it taken away from him? 434.a.b. 435.a.

units.la: R. Schanai Leviratus explicatio falsa, I. 722. b.
units.tr: R. Schanai's explanation of levirate marriage is false, I. 722.b.

units.la: Schisma duplex est, I I. 526. b. variæ ejus causæ, ib. 517. a. quando justum & necessarium sit? ib.
units.tr: Schism is of two kinds, II. 526.b. Its various causes, ib. 517.a. When is it just and necessary? ib.

units.la: Schlichtingius notatus, I I. 6. b. 7. a. pervertens locum, Col. I. 19. de plenitudine Deitatis in Christo.
units.tr: Schlichting is noted, II. 6.b. 7.a., for distorting the passage Col. 1.19 on the fullness of the Deity in Christ.

units.la: Scholæ Prophetarum quales fuerint? I. 441. a.
units.tr: The schools of the Prophets: what were they like? I. 441.a.

units.la: Scholastica Theologiæ historia, origo & vitia, I. 18. a. ejus à mystica discrimen, ib, 19. a.
units.tr: The history, origin and vices of scholastic theology, I. 18.a. Its distinction from mystical theology, ib. 19.a.

units.la: Scholastici Pelagianizantes, I. 366. a. refutantur, ib. b. semipelagianismum foverunt, II. 216. b.
units.tr: The Scholastics who favour Pelagianism, I. 366.a. Refuted, ib. b. They fostered semi-Pelagianism, II. 216.b.

units.la: Scholarum cura Magistratui incumbit, I I. 632. b.
units.tr: The care of schools rests with the magistrate, II. 632.b.

units.la: Scientia Dei, I. 81. a. a. ejus in simplicis intelligentiæ & visionis distinctio expenditur, 85. a. Media, Jesuitarum sensu, refutatur, 85. b.
units.tr: The knowledge of God, I. 81.a. Its distinction into simple intelligence and vision is examined, 85.a. Middle knowledge, in the Jesuits' sense, is refuted, 85.b.

units.la: Scortatio grande peccatum est, I. 356. a. quale scelus, 589. a. 592. 593. a. Scortatio quid & עריות דבר λόγῳ πνευματ, 592. 593. cujus fœditas describitur, 597. b. ejus incommoda, ibid.
units.tr: Fornication is a great sin, I. 356.a. What kind of crime is it? 589.a. 592. 593.a. Fornication, what is it, and "nakedness of a thing" [עריות דבר] by the word, spiritually [λόγῳ πνευματ]? 592, 593. Its foulness is described, 597.b. Its disadvantages, ibid.

units.la: Scotista Semi-Pelagiani sunt, I I. 216. b.
units.tr: The Scotists are semi-Pelagians, II. 216.b.

units.la: Scribæ Mosis tempore nondum exiterunt, I. 34. b. quale fuerit illorum munus? ib. qui & quales fuerint? 709. b.
units.tr: The Scribes did not yet exist in the time of Moses, I. 34.b. What was their office? ib. Who were they and what were they like? 709.b.

units.la: Scriptura S. Ejus origo, I. 7. b. necessitas, ibid. ejus primordia, 23. b. vid. Breviar. Loc. II. necessitas, ibid. 24. a. definitio, ib. b. Divinitas adversus Pontificios aliosque asseritur, ib. 25. a. Sanctitas, styli sublimitas, simplicitas, &c. aliaque ejus Divinitatem arguunt, ib. 27. a. de se testari potest, ibid. 30. b. in Testamentum Vetus & Novum distribuitur, 34. a. perfectio essentialis & integralis, 40. a. vid. Breviar.
units.tr: Holy Scripture. Its origin, I. 7.b. Its necessity, ibid. Its beginnings, 23.b. See Breviar., Loc. II. Its necessity, ibid. 24.a. Its definition, ib. b. Its divinity is asserted against the Papists and others, ib. 25.a. Its holiness, the sublimity and simplicity of its style, etc., and other things argue for its divinity, ib. 27.a. It can testify of itself, ibid. 30.b. It is divided into Old and New Testament, 34.a. Its essential and integral perfection, 40.a. See Breviar.

units.la: S. Scripturæ authentia definitur, & quo sensu fontibus & versionibus competat? 51. a. credendorum & faciendorum regula est, 53. nec partialis, nec plumbea, ibid. b. judex est, ibid. 54. 55. Ejus in vernaculas linguas versio cur à Papis prohibeatur? II. 433. b. ejus lectio in linguis notis ante Reformationem nondum prohibita fuit, 541. b.
units.tr: The authenticity of Holy Scripture is defined, and in what sense does it belong to the sources and to the versions? 51.a. It is the rule of what is to be believed and done, 53. It is neither partial nor leaden, ibid. b. It is judge, ibid. 54, 55. Why is its translation into the vernacular tongues forbidden by the Papists? II. 433.b. Its reading in known languages was not yet forbidden before the Reformation, 541.b.

units.la: Scriptores Sacri. Eorum in Jolcs, & sanctitas & ingenuitas, I. 26. b. Prophetæ & Apostoli, 32. a. non fortuitâ occasione; sed vocati & justi scripserunt 32. a. Θεοπνευστοι fuerunt, ibid. b. 33. a. infallibiles, ibid. b.

units.la: Socinus, Socinians. Socini argumenta contra Theolog. naturalem, I. 3. b. diluuntur, ibid. 4. eorum error, Religionem naturalem salutiferam statuentium, 4. b. rationem humanam fidei principium statuunt, 9. a. b. eorum perversa Theologia, ibid. 10. b. Infinitatem essentiæ Dei negant, 75. a. æternitatem Dei temporum differentiis subjiciunt, 76. b. Christum non ut primam sed ut secundam causam invocari debere, 134. a. Decreta in Deo mutationem arguere, 150. a. eorum perversa Decretorum constructio, 153. Decreta necessitatem hominibus inferre, 156. a. Materiæ æternitatem asserunt, 188. a. animæ immortalitatem negant, 220. b. mortem esse naturæ sequelam, 223. a. refutantur, 224. a. Justitiam originalem negant, 225. a. eorum cavillamenta retunduntur, 226. a. Imaginem Dei in homine in dominio ipsi concesso constituunt, 236. a. ejus argumenta confutantur, 237. b. Angelos ab æterno fuisse, 271. b. Fœdus Dei cum homine operum duntaxat agnoscunt, 305. b. primo homini vitam æternam cœlestem promissam fuisse negant, 320. b. mortis comminationem peccatori intentatæ non nisi vitæ hujus dolorem & perpetuam damnatorum dissolutionem fuisse, 323. b. Socini error de Arbore vitæ, 326. a. & danda vita æterna intercedente ramen morte, ibid. b. lapsu Imaginem Dei in homine amissam esse negant, 338. b. peccatum primum posteris imputatum esse negant, 343. a. 350. a. eorum de pœna peccati error, 363, a. Pelagianizant, 366. a. Sacerdotium Christi pervertunt, 380, a. Fœdus gratiæ in novum fœdus operum convertunt, 384. b. Sacramenta esse sigilla gratiæ ad remissionem peccatorum, negant, 393. a. Legem & Evangelium confundunt, 402. a. Fœderis gratiæ unitatem V. & N. Testam. negant, 410. Patres V. Testam. salutem ante consummationem seculi consequi negant, 413. b. Promissionem illam de semine caput serpentis contrituro non de Christo diei asserunt, 423. b. Promissionem Abrahamo factam terreoam tantum fuisse dicunt, 430. a. Patriarchas non nisi naturalem habuisse Religionem, 437. b. Angelum cum Mose in monte Sinai loquentem, angelum creatum fuisse, 456. b. Promissiones legis ad terrena tantum restringunt, 473. b. per proximum tantum amicos, qui soli amandi sint, intelligunt, 504. a. tantum sacrificia statis temporibus & prototo cœtu oblata, Christum adumbrasse, 674. a. Leges Mosaicas quasi in N. T. abrogatas esse contenduni, 739, b.
units.tr: Socinus, Socinians. The arguments of Socinus against natural theology are refuted, I. 3. b.; ibid. 4. His error, which holds natural religion to be saving, 4. b. They make human reason the principle of faith, 9. a. b. Their perverse theology, ibid. 10. b. They restrict the fundamental articles too narrowly, 17. a. They assert that the books of the Old Testament have no use in the New, 38. a. They deny that the name יהוה is proper to God, 68. b. They deny the infinity of God's essence, 75. a. They subject the eternity of God to differences of time, 76. b. They attack the immensity of God, 78. a. They deny God's foreknowledge of future contingents, 87. a. Their polytheism is exposed, 113. b. Those who deny that Christ is the eternal Son of the eternal Father are refuted, 125. b. They falsely claim that the word Θεὸς signifies power and office, not essence, 727. b. They interpret John 1.1 as referring to the beginning of the world, 132. a. They hold that Christ ought to be invoked not as the first cause but as a second cause, 134. a. They argue that decrees imply change in God, 150. a. Their perverse construction of the decrees, 153. They hold that decrees bring necessity upon men, 156. a. They assert the eternity of matter, 188. a. They deny the immortality of the soul, 220. b. They hold that death is a consequence of nature, 223. a. Refuted, 224. a. They deny original righteousness, 225. a. Their cavils are repelled, 226. a. They place the image of God in man in the dominion granted to him, 236. a. His arguments are refuted, 237. b. They hold that the angels existed from eternity, 271. b. They acknowledge only a covenant of works between God and man, 305. b. They deny that eternal heavenly life was promised to the first man, 320. b. They hold that the threatened penalty of death was only the pain of this life and the perpetual dissolution of the damned, 323. b. Socinus's error concerning the tree of life, 326. a. They hold that eternal life was to be given, death intervening, ibid. b. They deny that the image of God in man was lost by the Fall, 338. b. They deny that the first sin was imputed to posterity, 343. a.; 350. a. Their error concerning the punishment of sin, 363. a. They Pelagianize, 366. a. They pervert the priesthood of Christ, 380. a. They turn the covenant of grace into a new covenant of works, 384. b. They deny that the sacraments are seals of grace for the remission of sins, 393. a. They confound Law and Gospel, 402. a. They deny the unity of the covenant of grace in the Old and New Testaments, 410. They deny that the fathers of the Old Testament obtained salvation before the consummation of the age, 413. b. They assert that the promise concerning the seed who would crush the serpent's head does not refer to Christ, 423. b. They say the promise made to Abraham was merely earthly, 430. a. They say the patriarchs had only natural religion, 437. b. They hold that the angel speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai was a created angel, 456. b. They restrict the promises of the law to earthly things, 473. b. They understand "neighbour" only of friends, the only ones to be loved, 504. a. They hold that only the sacrifices offered at fixed times and by the whole assembly foreshadowed Christ, 674. a. They contend that the Mosaic laws have been abrogated in the New Testament, 739. b.

units.la: Eorum error de Raptu Christi post Baptismum in Cœlum, I. 3. b. 89. a. πάλιν ἀγαπώντας ad Rom. I. 3. perquem Christus Deus definitus est, cum Spiritum Dei, quo Christus homo sanctificatus in Filii Dei dignitatem sublatus sit, esse pertend. int, 5. b. Plenitudinem Deitatis in Christo de notitia voluntatis Dei explicant, 6. b. Naturarum in persona Christi unionem impossibilem asserunt, 17. a. Christum propter exaltationem & dominium tantum Deum esse, ibid. b. Christum post Baptismum in cœlum profectum docendi munere institutum fuisse, 41. b. in Christi collocatione ad dextram Patris primum Regni ejus initium statuunt, 68. b. de corpore Christi ad dextram Patris novo, 69. b vim nominis JESU abnegant, dum eum, ne unus quidem hominis peccatum expiavisse asserunt, 76. a. Reconciliationem nostram nisi nisi adductionem ad amorem Dei esse fingunt, 84. b. Christum novum Legislatorem facientes, hominem lege Christi præstita propria justitia salvari pertendunt, 90. b, 91. a. eorum contra Christi satisfactionem objectiones diluuntur, 108. seqq. metaphoricam redemptionem statuunt, 110. a. satisfactionem Christi negant, 113. 114. refutantur, 114. 115. Mentum Christi negant, 119. a. seq. Intercessionis sacerdotalis Christi vim abnegant, dum in cœlo demum sacerdotem factum esse dicunt, 129. a. Regium Christi munus corrumpunt, 137. b. Fidem & resipiscentiam, conditionem Evangelii propriè dictam, viribus nostris præstandam faciunt, 164. a. Christum novam perfectionemque Legem tulisse, 168. a. Pelagianismi & Sadducæismi recodores, 214. b. erant circa fidei salvificæ objectum 246. b. Fidei naturam definitione ejusdem subvertunt, 258. a. Deum justificare peccatorem ex sola misericordia, citra ullam satisfactionem, 269. Fidem gratuitam Dei acceptilationem interpretantur, 296. Sanctificationem in sola actuum emendatione collocant, 317. b, eorum circa pœnitentiam hæreses, 317. a. Sanctos deficere posse, 402. a. errores de Baptismo, 441. a. Pædobaptismum negant, 450. b. eorum de S. Cœna error, 461. b. S. Cœnam in fidei & obedientiæ tesseram convertunt, 497. a. verborum: Hoc est corpus meum, falsa explicatio, ib. manducationem spiritualem negant, 498. a. Ecclesiam penitus deficere posse, 515. b. Ecclesiam visibilem esse negant, 533. a. animas piorum post mortem ante resurrectionem beatitudine frui negant, 707. b. resurrectionem malorum negant, 733. eorundem argumenta refellun-tur, 741. a. Justificationem demum post mortem hominis peragi pertendunt, 741. a. Judicium ultimum indirecte negant, 745. b. Poenarum rufernalium æternitatem negant, 765. a. Justitiæ Divinæ repugnare dicunt, quod Deus delicta finita infinitis pœnis puniat, 765.
units.tr: Their error concerning Christ's ascension into heaven after baptism, I. 3. b.; 89. a. Romans 1.3, by which Christ was defined as God, they explain as meaning that the Spirit of God, by whom Christ as man was sanctified and raised to the dignity of the Son of God, is ... (they contend), 5. b. They explain the fullness of the Godhead in Christ as the knowledge of the will of God, 6. b. They assert that the union of natures in the person of Christ is impossible, 17. a. They hold that Christ is God only because of his exaltation and dominion, ibid. b. They hold that Christ, after baptism, went up into heaven and was appointed to the office of teaching, 41. b. They place the first beginning of his kingdom in Christ's being seated at the right hand of the Father, 68. b. Concerning a new body of Christ at the right hand of the Father, 69. b. They deny the force of the name JESUS, since they assert that he did not expiate even the sin of one man, 76. a. They feign that our reconciliation is nothing but a bringing of us to the love of God, 84. b. Making Christ a new Lawgiver, they contend that man is saved by his own righteousness by performing the law of Christ, 90. b.; 91. a. Their objections against the satisfaction of Christ are refuted, 108 ff. They posit a metaphorical redemption, 110. a. They deny the satisfaction of Christ, 113, 114. Refuted, 114, 115. They deny the merit of Christ, 119. a. ff. They deny the force of Christ's priestly intercession, since they say he became priest only in heaven, 129. a. They corrupt the kingly office of Christ, 137. b. They make faith and repentance, which are properly the condition of the Gospel, something to be performed by our own powers, 164. a. They hold that Christ gave a new and more perfect law, 168. a. Revivers of Pelagianism and Sadduceeism, 214. b. They differed concerning the object of saving faith, 246. b. They subvert the nature of faith by its definition, 258. a. They hold that God justifies a sinner from mercy alone, without any satisfaction, 269. They interpret the free gift of God's faith as an acceptilation, 296. They place sanctification solely in the amendment of actions, 317. b. Their heresies concerning repentance, 317. a. They hold that the saints can fall away, 402. a. Errors concerning baptism, 441. a. They deny infant baptism, 450. b. Their error concerning the Lord's Supper, 461. b. They turn the Lord's Supper into a token of faith and obedience, 497. a. A false explanation of the words "This is my body," ib. They deny spiritual manducation, 498. a. They hold that the Church can wholly fail, 515. b. They deny that the Church is visible, 533. a. They deny that the souls of the pious enjoy blessedness after death and before the resurrection, 707. b. They deny the resurrection of the wicked, 733. Their arguments are refuted, 741. a. They contend that justification is completed only after the death of a man, 741. a. They indirectly deny the last judgment, 745. b. They deny the eternity of infernal punishments, 765. a. They say it is contrary to divine justice that God should punish finite offences with infinite punishments, 765.

units.la: Socinianismi origo & progressus ostenditur, I. 135. b.
units.tr: The origin and progress of Socinianism is shown, I. 135. b.

units.la: Sol, qualis stella; I. 209, b. ejus motus & terræ quies temere non vellicari debent, 211. b.

units.la: Sol & Luna Ecclesiæ & Politiæ antecessores notant, II. 719. b.
units.tr: Sun and moon note the forerunners of the Church and of the state, II. 719. b.

units.la: Soliciudo, pro bonorum & possessionum acquisitione, nimia est in vitio, I. 605. b.
units.tr: Solicitude for the acquisition of goods and possessions is excessive and a vice, I. 605. b.

units.tr: Solomon did not fall away totally and finally from the grace of God, II. 406. b. Ecclesiastes is a witness of his repentance, ibid.

units.la: Solus. quomodo sola fides justificet? II. 300, a.
units.tr: Alone: how does faith alone justify? II. 300. a.

units.la: Somnia Prophetica revelationis genus, 480. a.
units.tr: Prophetic dreams are a kind of revelation, 480. a.

units.la: Σώφρων Episcopus quomodo Tit. I. 8. dicatur? II, 666. b.

units.la: Sors quid? ejus abusus, I. 548. a. in N. Test. licita sors est, ib. b. Dei Providentiæ subest, 263. a.
units.tr: Lot: what is it? Its abuse, I. 548. a. In the New Testament the lot is lawful, ib. b. It is subject to the providence of God, 263. a.

units.la: Sortitionis veritæ species, I. 548. b. licitæ in divisione, quæ divisoria dicitur, 549. a. alcares veritæ, ib.
units.tr: Species of the truth of the lot, I. 548. b. Lawful in division, which is called "divisory," 549. a. Other kinds of truth, ib.

units.la: Sparthani & Ægyptii furta permiserunt, I. 610. b.
units.tr: The Spartans and the Egyptians permitted theft, I. 610. b.

units.la: Spectra. Dæmonum apparitiones dari probatur, I. 297. a. quid sint? ibid. b. spectrum Samuelis, 1. Sam. XXVIII. 8. Diabolus ipse fuit, ibid.
units.tr: Apparitions. That the appearances of demons occur is proved, I. 297. a. What are they? ibid. b. The spectre of Samuel, 1 Sam. 28.8. It was the devil himself, ibid.

units.la: Speculum S. Trinitatis confutatur, I 709. b. fundamentum ἀρχολαπτέας est, 710.
units.tr: The speculum of the Holy Trinity is refuted, I. 709. b. It is the foundation of [ἀρχολαπτέας] , 710.

units.la: Spencerus. ejus de sacrificiorum origine error refellitur, I. 445. a. de circumcisionis institutione, 450. a, ejus commentum de Urim & Tummim rejicitur, 482. b. præceptum de Sabbatho mere ceremoniale, Christianos non obligare asserit, 552. b. examinatur, 555. b. & ejus argumenta refelluntur, 556. Cer-emoremonias legales non à Deo institutas, sed ab Ægyptiis mutuatas esse, statuens arguitur,649. b. argumenta ejus refelluntur, 650. b. laudatur,702. b. notatur,715. a.
units.tr: Spencer. His error concerning the origin of sacrifices is refuted, I. 445. a.; concerning the institution of circumcision, 450. a.; his fiction concerning the Urim and Thummim is rejected, 482. b.; he asserts that the precept concerning the Sabbath is purely ceremonial and does not bind Christians, 552. b.; examined, 555. b.; and his arguments are refuted, 556. He is argued against for holding that the legal ceremonies were not instituted by God but borrowed from the Egyptians, 649. b.; his arguments are refuted, 650. b.; praised, 702. b.; censured, 715. a.

units.la: Spes in Deo quid? I. 519. a. fidelium perseverat in æternum, II.400. a. Spei natura salutis certitudinem confirmat, 415. a. ejus certitudo contra Bellarminum asseritur, ib. b.
units.tr: Hope in God: what is it? I. 519a. The hope of believers endures forever, II. 400a. The nature of hope confirms the certainty of salvation, 415a. Its certainty is asserted against Bellarmine, ib. b.

units.la: Spicilegium pauperibus relinquendum,I.733.b.
units.tr: Gleaning is to be left for the poor, I. 733b.

units.la: Spinoza Apostolis humanam in plurib[?]us sapientiam fuisse pertendit,I. 33. a. ejus enthusiasmus detegitur, 45. a. ejus de interpretatione Scripturæ per lumen rationis, hæresis,49. a. extensionem Dei attributum statuens refutatur,73.b. creaturarum perfectiones secundum formam suam Deo inesse docet,ib.75.a. Naturam Deum faciens refutatur, 107. a. 108. ejus nexus rerum æternus arguitur, 185. b. ejus fatalis causarum necessitas refellitur, 247. a. ejus in Sacris impiæ assertiones, 247. b. miraculis omnibus fidem detrahit,258. a. angelos negat esse substantias spirituales,271.b. spectra ridet, 297. Legem naturalem primo homini inditam negat, 308. b. ejus impietas, Prophetiam nil aliud olim quàm delirantium phantasmata fuisse, statuentis, 441. a. Promissiones legis ad sola terrena restringit, 473. b.
units.tr: Spinoza contends that the Apostles had human wisdom in many matters, I. 33a. His enthusiasm is exposed, 45a. His heresy concerning the interpretation of Scripture by the light of reason, 49a. He is refuted for asserting that extension is an attribute of God, 73b. He teaches that the perfections of creatures are in God according to their form, ib. 75a. He is refuted for making God Nature, 107a, 108. His eternal connection of things is shown to be false, 185b. His fatalistic necessity of causes is refuted, 247a. His impious assertions in sacred matters, 247b. He strips all miracles of credibility, 258a. He denies that angels are spiritual substances, 271b. He mocks apparitions, 297. He denies that the natural law was implanted in the first man, 308b. His impiety, in holding that prophecy was once nothing but the phantasms of deranged people, 441a. He restricts the promises of the law to earthly things alone, 473b.

units.la: Spiritus vox est homonyma, I. 137. b. Simplicissimus Deus est,I. 73. a. Spiritualitas est Dei attributum, ibid. contra Anthropomorphitas Veteres & Novos asseritur,ibid.b.
units.tr: Spirit is a homonymous word, I. 137b. God is most simple Spirit, I. 73a. Spirituality is an attribute of God, ibid. It is asserted against the ancient and the new Anthropomorphites, ibid. b.

units.la: Spiritus S. Persona,I.137.b. character, 138. Personalitas asserta, 139. vid. Brev. Deitas variis argumentis probatur, vid. Brev. contra adversarios asseritur, 143.b. Spiritus mundum creans & regens idem est, 193.a. incubans aquis idem Dei fuit, 201. a. Spiritum S. habere quid? 215.b. Spiritus S. operatio, obsignatio & sanctificatio electorum, perseverantiæ sanctorum basis est,394. a. credentium sigillum & arrhabo est, ib. b. ejus dona ... sunt, 394. a. perennant,395.b. è Spiritu S. Christus conceptus est,II.112.b. ejus ἐπισκίασις super beatam Virginem explicatur,I 2.b. non idèo ejus Pater est, 13.b. ejus operatio in B. Virgine, 13. b. quomodo Paracletus noster sit? & pro nobis intercedat? 128.b. 119. a. ejus operatio,per Verbum foris prædicatum, & intus cordi inscriptum, efficacissima est,211. b. Regenerationis causa & principium est,232.a.233.b.omnipotentivi agens, ibid. operatur in nobis fidem, 244. b. Sanctificationis author est,315.316. Ejus operatio in fidelibus eos de salute certos reddit,411. b. fidelibus datur ut sigillum,arrhabo, primitiæ, ibid. b. consecrificatur nobis quòd filii Dei simus, 411. a. est Spiritus precum. 430. b. quodmodo in omnem veritatem ducere dicatur? 513.b. quomodo sit causa vitæ æternæ? 769.b.
units.tr: Holy Spirit, a Person, I. 137b. Character, 138. Personality asserted, 139; see Brev. Deity is proved by various arguments; see Brev. Asserted against adversaries, 143b. The Spirit who creates and governs the world is the same, 193a. Brooding over the waters was the Spirit of God, 201a. What is it to have the Holy Spirit? 215b. The operation, sealing and sanctification of the Holy Spirit in the elect is the basis of the perseverance of the saints, 394a. He is the seal and earnest of believers, ib. b. His gifts are ... , 394a. They abide, 395b. Christ was conceived of the Holy Spirit, II. 112b. His overshadowing (ἐπισκίασις) upon the Blessed Virgin is explained [ἐπισκίασις], I. 2b. He is therefore not the Father of Christ, 13b. His operation in the Blessed Virgin, 13b. How is our Paraclete, and how does he intercede for us? 128b, 119a. His operation, through the Word preached outwardly and written on the heart within, is most effective, 211b. He is the cause and principle of regeneration, 232a, 233b. He is the omnipotent agent, ibid. He works faith in us, 244b. He is the author of sanctification, 315, 316. His operation in believers makes them certain of salvation, 411b. He is given to believers as seal, earnest and firstfruits, ibid. b. He consecrates us, so that we are sons of God, 411a. He is the Spirit of prayer, 430b. In what way is he said to lead us into all truth? 513b. How is he the cause of eternal life? 769b.

units.la: Spiritus privatus Enthusiastarum,I.44.a. rejicitur, ib. b. judicans privatus Antichristianus vel Enthusiasticus est,59.b. vel Christianus est,ib. b.
units.tr: Private spirit of the Enthusiasts, I. 44a. Rejected, ib. b. Judging by a private spirit is either Antichristian or enthusiastic, 59b, or Christian, ib. b.
